entries.zh: 累擢寧夏副都統。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to vice commander at Ningxia.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commander at Ningxia.

entries.zh: 乾隆十九年，命與侍衛海福將千人佐定西將軍永常討達瓦齊，遷寧夏將軍。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of the Qianlong reign he was ordered, together with imperial bodyguard Haifu, to lead a thousand men in support of Pacification-of-the-West General Yongchang's campaign against Dawachi, and was promoted to general at Ningxia.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he was ordered, together with Bodyguard Haifu, to lead a thousand men to assist Pacification-of-the-West General Yongchang in campaigning against Dawachi, and was transferred to be general at Ningxia.

entries.zh: 永常劾和起兵不及額，而和起先疏言將九百人以往，留百人護輜重，上得永常疏，不之罪也。
entries.en: Yongchang impeached He Qi for bringing fewer troops than required, but He Qi had already reported that he would advance with nine hundred men and leave a hundred to guard the baggage train. When the emperor read Yongchang's memorial, he declined to punish He Qi.
entries.literal: Yongchang impeached He Qi for falling short of the allotted troop strength, but He Qi had earlier memorialized that he would take nine hundred men forward and leave a hundred to guard the baggage; when the emperor received Yongchang's memorial, he did not punish him.

entries.zh: 尋又命偕提督豆斌為巴里坤辦事大臣，策楞代永常為定西將軍，复劾和起送兵馬遲誤，當奪官，留任。
entries.en: He was soon appointed, together with provincial commander Dou Bin, minister resident at Barkul. When Celeng replaced Yongchang as Pacification-of-the-West General, he impeached He Qi again for tardiness in moving troops and horses. He Qi should have been dismissed, but was allowed to remain in office.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was again ordered, together with Provincial Commander Dou Bin, to serve as Grand Minister Resident at Barkul; Celeng replaced Yongchang as Pacification-of-the-West General and again impeached He Qi for delay in dispatching troops and horses, for which he ought to have been stripped of office but was kept in his post.

entries.zh: 旋复官，授欽差大臣關防，召詣京師諮軍事。
entries.en: His rank was soon restored, he received the seal of an imperial commissioner, and he was summoned to the capital for consultation on military affairs.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward his office was restored; he was given the seal of an imperial commissioner and summoned to the capital to consult on military affairs.

entries.zh: 達什達瓦所屬宰桑訥默庫、曼集、烏達瑚們都等在軍私還游牧，命和起嚴鞫得實，以降人請予寬典，上不許，命正軍法。
entries.en: The zaisangs Nemuku, Manji, Udahundu, and others under Dashdawa had slipped away from the army to return to their pastures. He Qi was ordered to investigate the matter rigorously and established the facts beyond dispute. Surrendered tribesmen pleaded for leniency, but the emperor refused and ordered them dealt with under military law.
entries.literal: The zaisangs Nemuku, Manji, Udahundu, and others under Dashdawa had privately returned to their pastures while still in the army; He Qi was ordered to investigate strictly and established the facts; surrendered men asked that leniency be shown, but the emperor would not permit it and ordered military law enforced.

entries.zh: 唐喀祿，他塔喇氏，蒙古正藍旗人。
entries.en: Tang Kalu, of the Tatara clan, belonged to the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Tang Kalu, of the Tatara clan, was a man of the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 自筆帖式再遷理籓院員外郎。
entries.en: Starting as a clerk, he was promoted twice to vice director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
entries.literal: From the post of clerk he was twice promoted to vice director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

entries.zh: 乾隆十九年，賜副都統銜，命赴北路軍董理新降輝特台吉阿睦爾撒納、班珠爾等游牧地。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of the Qianlong reign he received the brevet rank of vice commander and was sent to the northern army to oversee the pastures of the newly surrendered Khoyit taijis Amursana, Banzhur, and others.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he was granted the brevet rank of vice commander and ordered to the northern-route army to supervise the pastures of the newly surrendered Khoyit taijis Amursana, Banzhur, and others.

entries.zh: 唐喀祿疏言：「班珠爾所屬多老稚不能耕，慮飢餒。」
entries.en: Tang Kalu memorialized, "Many of those under Banzhur are old or young and cannot farm; I fear they will go hungry."
entries.literal: Tang Kalu memorialized: "Among those under Banzhur many are old and young and cannot farm; I fear hunger."

entries.zh: 上以距耕時尚遠，責其瑣屑，命撤還。
entries.en: The emperor replied that the planting season was still far off, rebuked him for fussing over trifles, and ordered him recalled.
entries.literal: The emperor said that the planting season was still far off, rebuked him for triviality, and ordered him recalled.

entries.zh: 扎薩克林丕勒多爾濟初命同董理游牧，將軍別有指揮，唐喀祿疏請留。
entries.en: The jasak Lambeldorji had originally been ordered to oversee the pastures jointly with him, but when the general issued separate instructions Tang Kalu memorialized asking to stay on.
entries.literal: The jasak Lambeldorji had at first been ordered to supervise the pastures jointly; the general had separate instructions, but Tang Kalu memorialized asking to remain.

entries.zh: 上責其不當，左遷理籓院筆帖式。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him for overstepping his authority and demoted him to clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him for impropriety and demoted him to clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

entries.zh: 尋复授員外郎，命送濟隆呼圖克圖自巴林赴伊犁，董理定邊右副將軍薩喇爾游牧。
entries.en: He was soon reappointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jilong Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to oversee the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jilong Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to supervise the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.

entries.zh: 复賜副都統銜，授領隊大臣，將駐防扎布堪兵千人，從定邊右副將軍哈達哈赴哈薩克，逐捕阿睦爾撒納。
entries.en: He received the brevet rank of vice commander again, was appointed a leading-column grand minister, and led a thousand garrison troops from Zhabukan in support of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Hadaha's march into Kazakhstan to hunt down Amursana.
entries.literal: He was again granted the brevet rank of vice commander, appointed a leading-column grand minister, and ordered to lead a thousand garrison troops from Zhabukan to follow Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Hadaha into Kazakhstan in pursuit of Amursana.

entries.zh: 賊渠固爾班和卓遁入烏梁海，唐喀祿報哈達哈督兵擒之，賜孔雀翎。
entries.en: The rebel leader Gurbankhoja fled into Uriankhai. Tang Kalu urged Hadaha to press the pursuit and capture him, and was rewarded with a peacock feather.
entries.literal: The rebel leader Gurbankhoja fled into Uriankhai; Tang Kalu reported to Hadaha to supervise the troops in capturing him, and was granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 阿睦爾撒納令其徒達瓦藏布入掠，唐喀祿令索倫總管鄂博什將五百人御之，降其眾三百。
entries.en: Amursana sent his follower Davazangbu on a raiding incursion. Tang Kalu ordered Solon commander Eboshi to meet him with five hundred men and accepted the surrender of three hundred of his followers.
entries.literal: Amursana ordered his follower Davazangbu to raid inward; Tang Kalu ordered Solon commander Eboshi to lead five hundred men against him and accepted the surrender of three hundred of his followers.

entries.zh: 尋命屯科布多。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to establish a garrison at Kobdo.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to garrison Kobdo.

entries.zh: 授理籓院侍郎、鑲藍旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He was appointed vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: He was appointed vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 唐喀祿行按諸部，輝特降人屯紮克賽，每自相劫奪，請移屯呼倫貝爾、齊齊哈爾諸地；
entries.en: While touring the tribes, Tang Kalu found that Khoyit who had surrendered and been settled at Zakasai were constantly raiding one another. He asked that they be relocated to Hulunbuir, Qiqihar, and other districts;
entries.literal: As Tang Kalu toured the various tribes, the surrendered Khoyit who were settled at Zakasai constantly plundered one another; he requested that they be moved to garrison Hulunbuir, Qiqihar, and other places;

entries.zh: 喀爾喀俘獲扎哈沁、特楞古特、奇爾吉斯、烏爾罕濟蘭諸部人萬餘，請以扎哈沁人移駐卡倫內；
entries.en: more than ten thousand captives from the Zhahakin, Terengut, Kirghiz, and Urhanjilan tribes taken by the Khalkha—he proposed moving the Zhahakin inside the border posts;
entries.literal: more than ten thousand people of the Zhahakin, Terengut, Kirghiz, and Urhanjilan tribes captured by the Khalkha he asked to have the Zhahakin moved to garrison inside the border posts;

entries.zh: 特楞古特、奇爾吉斯、烏爾罕濟蘭人給東三省兵丁為奴；
entries.en: assigning the Terengut, Kirghiz, and Urhanjilan as bond servants to troops in the Three Eastern Provinces;
entries.literal: the Terengut, Kirghiz, and Urhanjilan he asked to be given as slaves to the troops of the Three Eastern Provinces;

entries.zh: 杜爾伯特游牧請移烏蘭固木：上並從其請。
entries.en: and relocating Durbot pastures to Ulan Gom—the emperor approved every request.
entries.literal: and for the Durbot pastures he requested removal to Ulan Gom: the emperor approved all his requests.

entries.zh: 師出西路擊哈薩克錫喇，命唐喀祿屯額爾齊斯為聲援。
entries.en: When the army marched on the western route against Kazakh Xila, Tang Kalu was ordered to hold the Irtysh line as a supporting force.
entries.literal: When the army marched out on the western route to attack Kazakh Xila, Tang Kalu was ordered to garrison the Irtysh as a supporting force.

entries.zh: 阿睦爾撒納敗走，唐喀祿诇知杜爾伯特貝勒巴圖博羅特、台吉阿喇善等潛與相結；
entries.en: After Amursana was defeated and fled, Tang Kalu learned through intelligence that the Durbot beile Batuborot, the taiji Alashan, and others were secretly in league with him;
entries.literal: Amursana was defeated and fled; Tang Kalu learned through reconnaissance that the Durbot beile Batuborot, the taiji Alashan, and others were secretly in league with him;

entries.zh: 遣兵攻之輝巴朗山，擒阿喇善等，並戮烏梁海五十餘戶，遂赴塔爾巴哈台逐捕阿睦爾撒納及哈薩克錫喇，賜御用荷包、鼻煙壺。
entries.en: He sent troops against them at Huibolang Mountain, captured Alashan and others, and executed more than fifty Uriankhai households besides. He then pressed on to Tarbagatai in pursuit of Amursana and Kazakh Xila and was rewarded with an imperial purse and snuff bottle from the emperor's own hand.
entries.literal: he sent troops to attack them at Huibolang Mountain, captured Alashan and others, and also executed more than fifty Uriankhai households; he then went to Tarbagatai in pursuit of Amursana and Kazakh Xila, and was granted an imperial purse and snuff bottle.

entries.zh: 師至塔爾巴哈台，糧罄馬乏，唐喀祿引師退，疏言遵旨撤兵，上怒，左授藍翎侍衛，佐定邊左副將軍納穆扎爾出北路。
entries.en: When the army reached Tarbagatai, provisions ran out and the horses were exhausted. Tang Kalu withdrew the force and memorialized that he was obeying orders to pull back. The emperor was furious, demoted him to blue-plume imperial bodyguard, and sent him to assist Pacification Left Deputy General-in-Chief Namuzhar on the northern route.
entries.literal: When the army reached Tarbagatai, provisions were exhausted and the horses worn out; Tang Kalu led the army back and memorialized that he was withdrawing troops in obedience to orders; the emperor was angry, demoted him to blue-plume imperial bodyguard, and had him assist Pacification Left Deputy General-in-Chief Namuzhar on the northern route.

entries.zh: 降人和碩齊，上擢用至散秩大臣，至是令護哈薩克來使入邊，上命納穆扎爾遣唐喀祿將二百人迎之。
entries.en: Among the surrendered leaders was Khoshuuchi, whom the emperor had promoted as far as minister without portfolio. He was now ordered to escort the Kazakh envoy across the border, and the emperor directed Namuzhar to send Tang Kalu with two hundred men to meet him.
entries.literal: Among the surrendered men was Khoshuuchi, whom the emperor had promoted all the way to minister without specific portfolio; at this time he was ordered to escort the Kazakh envoy into the border, and the emperor ordered Namuzhar to send Tang Kalu with two hundred men to receive him.

entries.zh: 阿睦爾撒納竄俄羅斯，上命唐喀祿偕和碩齊駐額爾齊斯偵禦。
entries.en: When Amursana fled into Russia, the emperor ordered Tang Kalu and Khoshuuchi to hold the Irtysh line on reconnaissance and defense.
entries.literal: Amursana fled into Russia; the emperor ordered Tang Kalu, together with Khoshuuchi, to garrison the Irtysh on reconnaissance and defense.

entries.zh: 二十三年三月，土爾扈特舍棱等謀走俄羅斯，上命偕和碩齊逐捕。
entries.en: In the third month of the twenty-third year, when the Torghut Shelen and others plotted to flee to Russia, the emperor ordered Tang Kalu and Khoshuuchi to pursue and capture them.
entries.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year, the Torghut Shelen and others plotted to flee to Russia; the emperor ordered him, together with Khoshuuchi, to pursue and capture them.

entries.zh: 四月，師次佈固圖河，獲舍棱弟勞章扎卜。
entries.en: In the fourth month the army halted on the Bugutu River and captured Shelen's younger brother Laochangzhab.
entries.literal: In the fourth month the army halted at Bugutu River and captured Shelen's younger brother Laochangzhab.

entries.zh: 勞章扎卜詭為兄乞降，唐喀祿未敢信，和碩齊遽縱之還。
entries.en: Laochangzhab falsely offered surrender on his brother's behalf. Tang Kalu was unwilling to trust him, but Khoshuuchi promptly sent him back.
entries.literal: Laochangzhab falsely pleaded surrender on his brother's behalf; Tang Kalu did not dare believe him, but Khoshuuchi promptly released him to return.

entries.zh: 越日，舍棱詭約降，獻酒，和碩齊飲之，邀唐喀祿過其營，賊噪而起。
entries.en: The next day Shelen feigned agreement to surrender and offered wine. Khoshuuchi drank it and invited Tang Kalu to his camp, where the rebels suddenly rose in uproar.
entries.literal: The next day Shelen falsely agreed to surrender, offered wine, and Khoshuuchi drank it; he invited Tang Kalu to his camp, and the rebels rose with a clamor.

entries.zh: 唐喀祿及侍衛富錫爾、穆倫保、佛爾慶額力戰，均遇害，和碩齊更衣降。
entries.en: Tang Kalu and the bodyguards Fuxier, Mulunbao, and Fo'erqing'e fought to the last and were all killed. Khoshuuchi changed clothes and went over to the enemy.
entries.literal: Tang Kalu and the bodyguards Fuxier, Mulunbao, and Fo'erqing'e fought fiercely and were all killed; Khoshuuchi changed clothes and surrendered.

entries.zh: 事聞，賜騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。
entries.en: When word reached the court, he was granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry and enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
entries.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry and enshrined in the Zhaozhong Shrine.

entries.zh: 富錫爾、佛爾慶額，皆滿洲鑲黃旗人；
entries.en: Fuxier and Fo'erqing'e both belonged to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner;
entries.literal: Fuxier and Fo'erqing'e were both men of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner;

entries.zh: 穆倫保，滿洲正白旗人：皆賜雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: Mulunbao belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner. All three were granted the hereditary rank of commandant of the cloud cavalry.
entries.literal: Mulunbao was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner: all were granted the hereditary office of commandant of the cloud cavalry.

entries.zh: 阿敏道，襲職。
entries.en: A Mindao inherited the rank.
entries.literal: A Mindao inherited the office.

entries.zh: 雍正初，累遷二等侍衛。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he rose through successive promotions to second-rank imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was repeatedly promoted to second-rank imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 九年，命將巴里呼兵百人自固爾班塞堪赴巴爾坤佐軍，又命偕侍讀學士查克丹調喀爾喀兵三千率之往。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was ordered to lead a hundred Barghu troops from Gurbansaihan to Barkul to support the campaign, and was also directed, together with Hanlin reader Zhakedan, to mobilize three thousand Khalkha troops and lead them there.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to lead a hundred Barghu troops from Gurbansaihan to Barkul to assist the army, and was also ordered, together with Hanlin Reader Zhakedan, to mobilize three thousand Khalkha troops and lead them thither.

entries.zh: 尋复偕護軍統領費雅思哈赴烏爾輝音扎罕練兵。
entries.en: He soon joined garrison commander Feiyasaha at Wuerhuiyinzhahan to drill troops.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he again accompanied Garrison Commander Feiyasaha to Wuerhuiyinzhahan to drill troops.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，準噶爾乞和，撤軍，阿敏道還京，授鑲藍旗察哈爾總管。
entries.en: In the first year of the Qianlong reign the Zunghars sued for peace and the army withdrew. A Mindao returned to the capital and was appointed commander of the Chahar Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Zunghars sued for peace and the army was withdrawn; A Mindao returned to the capital and was appointed commander of the Chahar Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 十九年，師收烏梁海，將察哈爾兵以從，加副都統銜。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year, when the army recovered Uriankhai, he led Chahar troops on the campaign and received the brevet rank of vice commander.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the army recovered Uriankhai, he led Chahar troops in the campaign and was given the brevet rank of vice commander.

entries.zh: 二十年，遷所獲巴爾沁人等於齊拉罕。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he relocated the captured Barghin and others to Qilahan.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he moved the captured Barghin and others to Qilahan.

entries.zh: 師定伊犁，定北將軍班第奏以阿敏道督台站。
entries.en: After the army pacified Ili, Pacification-of-the-North General Bandi recommended A Mindao to supervise the courier stations.
entries.literal: When the army pacified Ili, Pacification-of-the-North General Bandi memorialized that A Mindao should supervise the courier stations.

entries.zh: 是年，阿睦爾撒納叛，班第陷賊。
entries.en: That same year Amursana rebelled and Bandi was trapped by the enemy.
entries.literal: That year Amursana rebelled and Bandi fell into the rebels' hands.

entries.zh: 阿巴噶斯、哈丹附逆肆掠，台站中斷。
entries.en: Abaghas and Hadan joined the rebellion and raided freely, severing the courier lines.
entries.literal: Abaghas and Hadan joined the rebellion and plundered wantonly, and the courier stations were cut off.

entries.zh: 阿敏道輒督兵巡徼，使驛遞恆得相續。
entries.en: A Mindao repeatedly led patrols so that the relay posts could stay in contact.
entries.literal: A Mindao repeatedly supervised troops on patrol so that relay communications could be kept unbroken.

entries.zh: 會定西將軍永常自木壘退駐烏爾圖布拉克，撤阿敏道還。
entries.en: Pacification-of-the-West General Yongchang had meanwhile withdrawn from Mulei to Wuerhtubulake and recalled A Mindao.
entries.literal: At that time Pacification-of-the-West General Yongchang had withdrawn from Mulei to garrison Wuerhtubulake and recalled A Mindao.

entries.zh: 上奪永常官，以策楞代將。
entries.en: The emperor removed Yongchang from office and put Celeng in command.
entries.literal: The emperor stripped Yongchang of office and replaced him with Celeng as commander.

entries.zh: 命阿敏道將精騎詣伊犁求班第消息。
entries.en: He ordered A Mindao to take picked cavalry to Ili to learn Bandi's fate.
entries.literal: He ordered A Mindao to lead picked cavalry to Ili to seek news of Bandi.

entries.zh: 策楞不即遣，上詰責之。
entries.en: Celeng did not send him at once, and the emperor rebuked him for the delay.
entries.literal: Celeng did not dispatch him at once; the emperor rebuked him.

entries.zh: 尋將千人捕阿巴噶斯、哈丹賊眾。
entries.en: He soon led a thousand men against the rebel bands of Abaghas and Hadan and captured them.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he led a thousand men to capture the rebel bands of Abaghas and Hadan.

entries.zh: 二十二年，上諭諸將檄霍集占送阿敏道還，不從，謀加害。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year the emperor ordered the generals to demand Khojijaha's return of A Mindao. Khojijaha refused and plotted to kill him.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year the emperor ordered the generals to send a summons to Khojijaha to return A Mindao; he refused and plotted to harm him.

entries.zh: 庫車伯克呼岱巴爾以告，阿敏道謀脫歸，不克，死之。
entries.en: The Kucha beg Hudaibar warned him. A Mindao tried to escape but failed and was killed.
entries.literal: The Kucha beg Hudaibar informed him; A Mindao plotted to escape and return but could not succeed and was killed.

entries.zh: 二等男署察哈爾營總旺扎勒及諸裨將繃科、耨金吹、扎木蘇
entries.en: The acting second-class baron and Chahar camp commander Wangzhale, together with staff officers Bengke, Noujinchui, Zhamusu,
entries.literal: The acting second-class baron and Chahar camp commander Wangzhale, together with the staff officers Bengke, Noujinchui, Zhamusu,

entries.zh: 滿福，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。
entries.en: Man Fu, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Man Fu, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 自世管佐領累擢拉林副都統。
entries.en: Starting as a hereditary company commander, he rose through successive promotions to vice commander at Lalin.
entries.literal: From hereditary company commander he was repeatedly promoted to vice commander at Lalin.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十二年，遷都統，駐巴里坤。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year of the Qianlong reign he was promoted to commander-in-chief and stationed at Barkul.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he was transferred to be commander-in-chief and garrisoned at Barkul.

entries.zh: 命將吉林兵千人屯吐魯番，尋授領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was ordered to lead a thousand Jilin troops to garrison Turfan and was soon appointed a leading-column grand minister.
entries.literal: He was ordered to lead a thousand Jilin troops to garrison Turfan and was soon appointed a leading-column grand minister.

entries.zh: 定邊將軍成袞扎佈出珠勒都斯，令滿福將三百人巡視阿勒輝至烏納哈特十三台站，搜剿嗎哈沁。
entries.en: When Pacification General Cheng'enjab marched out of Zhuledusi, he ordered Man Fu to lead three hundred men along the thirteen courier stations from Alehui to Wuna'hate to hunt down the Mahajin.
entries.literal: Pacification General Cheng'enjab marched out of Zhuledusi; he ordered Man Fu to lead three hundred men to patrol the thirteen courier stations from Alehui to Wuna'hate and search out and suppress the Mahajin.

entries.zh: 沙拉斯、嗎唬斯既降复叛，掠台站，上命滿福自阿勒輝往剿，又令巴里坤辦事大臣阿里袞帥師與會。
entries.en: Shalasi and Mahusi had surrendered but rebelled again and raided the courier stations. The emperor ordered Man Fu to move from Alehui against them and directed minister resident at Barkul Arigun to bring troops to join the operation.
entries.literal: Shalasi and Mahusi, having surrendered, rebelled again and plundered the courier stations; the emperor ordered Man Fu to proceed from Alehui to suppress them and also ordered Grand Minister Resident at Barkul Arigun to lead troops to join him.

entries.zh: 阿里袞未至，滿福師次肯色嶺，與賊遇，擊之，賊敗走，偽遣人乞降，且言賊渠已就縛，請除道迎。
entries.en: Before Arigun arrived, Man Fu's force halted at Kense Ridge, met the rebels, and drove them off. The enemy then sent men with a false offer of surrender, claiming their leader was already bound and asking that the road be cleared to receive them.
entries.literal: Before Arigun arrived, Man Fu's army halted at Kense Ridge, encountered the rebels, attacked them, and the rebels fled in defeat; they falsely sent men to beg surrender and also said the rebel leader had already been bound, asking that the road be cleared to receive them.

entries.zh: 滿福信之，行次哈喇和落，徑險林密，下臨深溝。
entries.en: Man Fu believed them. At Halaholuo the path ran through dense forest along the edge of a deep ravine.
entries.literal: Man Fu believed them; marching to Halaholuo, the path was narrow, the forest dense, and a deep ravine lay below.

entries.zh: 滿福悟為賊所紿，急麾前隊返。
entries.en: Man Fu realized the rebels had deceived him and urgently ordered the vanguard to turn back.
entries.literal: Man Fu realized he had been deceived by the rebels and urgently ordered the vanguard to turn back.

entries.zh: 賊千餘突自林中出，圍我師。
entries.en: More than a thousand rebels burst from the forest and surrounded his force.
entries.literal: More than a thousand rebels suddenly burst from the forest and surrounded our army.

entries.zh: 滿福厲聲督兵力戰，被創墜溝，死之。
entries.en: Man Fu shouted orders and fought on fiercely until, wounded, he fell into the ravine and died.
entries.literal: Man Fu shouted loudly as he urged the troops to fight fiercely; wounded, he fell into the ravine and died.

entries.zh: 上以滿福雖為賊所愚，愍其捐軀，命如陣亡例議卹，諡武毅，祀昭忠祠，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: Though Man Fu had been fooled by the rebels, the emperor pitied his sacrifice and ordered condolence grants on the same terms as for death in battle. He was posthumously honored with the title Wuyi, enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: The emperor, though Man Fu had been fooled by the rebels, pitied his sacrifice of life and ordered condolence grants according to the precedent for death in battle; he was given the posthumous title Wuyi, enshrined in the Zhaozhong Shrine, and portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 豆斌，陝西固原人。
entries.en: Dou Bin was a native of Guyuan in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Dou Bin was a man of Guyuan in Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 初以馬兵入提標，累遷肅州鎮標中營守備。
entries.en: He began as a cavalry soldier in the provincial commander's establishment and rose through successive promotions to defender of the central battalion of the Suzhou garrison.
entries.literal: At first he entered the provincial commander's establishment as a cavalry soldier and was repeatedly promoted to defender of the central battalion of the Suzhou garrison.

entries.zh: 雍正間，從征準噶爾。
entries.en: During the Yongzheng reign he served on the campaign against the Zunghars.
entries.literal: During Yongzheng he followed the campaign against the Zunghars.

entries.zh: 力戰受創，賜白金四百。
entries.en: He fought fiercely, was wounded, and was rewarded with four hundred taels of silver.
entries.literal: He fought fiercely and was wounded, and was granted four hundred taels of silver.

entries.zh: 遷川陝督標前營游擊。
entries.en: He was promoted to brigade commander of the vanguard battalion under the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be brigade commander of the vanguard battalion of the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general's command.

entries.zh: 準噶爾犯科舍圖，率兵擊走之。
entries.en: When the Zunghars invaded Keshetu, he led troops and drove them off.
entries.literal: When the Zunghars invaded Keshetu he led troops and drove them off.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，累遷提督，自廣東移廣西。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he rose to provincial commander, transferring from Guangdong to Guangxi.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was repeatedly promoted to provincial commander, moving from Guangdong to Guangxi.

entries.zh: 疏言：「各營鳥槍，舊式大小參差，坐臥倚伏，不能應手；
entries.en: He memorialized, "In the various battalions the old-pattern muskets vary greatly in size. Whether troops sit, lie, lean, or crouch, the weapons cannot be handled readily;
entries.literal: He memorialized: "In the various battalions the muskets of the old pattern vary greatly in size; whether sitting, lying, leaning, or crouching, they cannot be handled readily;

entries.zh: 又質薄易熱，難收實用。
entries.en: moreover the metal is thin and overheats easily, so they are of little practical use.
entries.literal: moreover their metal is thin and heats easily, so they are hard to use effectively.

entries.zh: 請照陝西威字號纏絲槍式改制。」
entries.en: Please have them remade according to the Shaanxi Wei-series wrapped-silk musket pattern."
entries.literal: I request that they be remade according to the Shaanxi Wei-series wrapped-silk musket pattern."

entries.zh: 下兩廣總督議行。
entries.en: The matter was referred to the governor-general of the Two Guangs for implementation.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the governor-general of the Two Guangs for deliberation and implementation.

entries.zh: 俄，調還固原。
entries.en: He was soon transferred back to Guyuan.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred back to Guyuan.

entries.zh: 又命以提督銜領湖北宜昌鎮總兵事。
entries.en: He was then ordered to hold the brevet rank of provincial commander while directing the Yichang garrison in Hubei.
entries.literal: He was again ordered to hold the brevet rank of provincial commander while directing the affairs of the commander at Yichang in Hubei.

entries.zh: 尋复歷甘肅、安西提督。
entries.en: He soon served again in succession as provincial commander of Gansu and Anxi.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he again served in succession as provincial commander of Gansu and Anxi.

entries.zh: 命討準噶爾，帥將標兵出駐巴里坤，以輸軍馬後時，下吏議。
entries.en: Ordered to campaign against the Zunghars, he led his troops to garrison Barkul. Because he delivered army horses late, the case was referred to the judicial authorities.
entries.literal: He was ordered to campaign against the Zunghars and led his command's troops to garrison Barkul; because he delivered army horses late, the case was referred to the judicial authorities.

entries.zh: 旋乞病，罷。
entries.en: He soon pleaded illness and was dismissed.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he pleaded illness and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 居數月，复授安西提督，仍令赴巴里坤兆惠師。
entries.en: After several months he was reappointed provincial commander of Anxi and again ordered to join Zhaohui's army at Barkul.
entries.literal: After several months he was again appointed provincial commander of Anxi and still ordered to proceed to Barkul to Zhaohui's army.

entries.zh: 師攻霍集占於庫車，命斌將所部從，充領隊大臣，徼巡魯克察克、闢展、庫車諸地驛路。
entries.en: When the army attacked Khojijaha at Kucha, Bin was ordered to lead his troops, appointed a leading-column grand minister, and assigned to patrol the courier roads around Lukchak, Buzhan, Kucha, and neighboring districts.
entries.literal: When the army attacked Khojijaha at Kucha, Bin was ordered to lead his troops in the campaign, appointed a leading-column grand minister, and patrolled the courier roads of Lukchak, Buzhan, Kucha, and other places.

entries.zh: 兆惠被圍黑水，斌從副將軍富德自阿克蘇兼程赴援。
entries.en: When Zhaohui was trapped at the Black River, Bin followed Deputy General-in-Chief Fude from Aksu on forced marches to relieve him.
entries.literal: When Zhaohui was besieged at the Black River, Bin followed Deputy General-in-Chief Fude from Aksu by forced marches to the relief.

entries.zh: 師次呼爾璊，霍集占以五千人迎戰，我師分兩翼，賊據高岡，斌率中軍火器進攻。
entries.en: At Khur the army met Khojijaha with five thousand men. The Qing forces divided into two wings while the rebels held the high ground. Bin led the central column's firearms troops in the assault.
entries.literal: The army halted at Khur; Khojijaha met them with five thousand men; our army divided into two wings; the rebels held the high ground; Bin led the central army's firearms troops in the attack.

entries.zh: 賊知我師馬力乏，擁眾相偪。
entries.en: Seeing that the Qing horses were exhausted, the rebels pressed forward in dense masses.
entries.literal: The rebels, knowing our army's horses were exhausted, pressed forward in massed numbers.

entries.zh: 阿里袞解馬至，斌偕眾將夾擊，脅中創，仍力戰，賊大敗。
entries.en: Arigun sent up fresh horses. Bin and the other generals attacked from both sides. Though wounded in the flank, he kept fighting until the rebels were routed.
entries.literal: Arigun sent horses; Bin, together with the other generals, attacked from both sides; he was wounded in the flank but still fought fiercely, and the rebels were utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 創甚遂卒，諡壯節，祀昭忠祠，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉。
entries.en: His wounds proved fatal. He was posthumously honored with the title Zhuangjie, enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and granted the combined ranks of commandant of cavalry and commandant of the cloud cavalry.
entries.literal: His wounds were severe and he soon died; he was given the posthumous title Zhuangjie, enshrined in the Zhaozhong Shrine, and granted commandant of cavalry combined with commandant of the cloud cavalry.

entries.zh: 上製詩惜之。
entries.en: The emperor composed a poem lamenting his death.
entries.literal: The emperor composed a poem to mourn him.

entries.zh: 回部平，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: After the Muslim regions were pacified, his portrait was hung in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: When the Muslim regions were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 孫{澍}，襲世職，官至山東登州鎮總兵。
entries.en: His grandson Shu inherited the hereditary rank and rose to commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
entries.literal: His grandson Shu inherited the hereditary office and rose to be commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.

entries.zh: 端濟布，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Duanjibu, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Duanjibu, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 自前鋒累遷頭等侍衛、鑲黃旗察哈爾總管。
entries.en: Starting in the vanguard, he rose through successive promotions to first-rank imperial bodyguard and commander of the Chahar Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: From the vanguard he was repeatedly promoted to first-rank imperial bodyguard and commander of the Chahar Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十二年，上令選兵千佐定邊將軍兆惠出西路。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year of the Qianlong reign the emperor ordered a thousand picked troops to assist Pacification General Zhaohui on the western route.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong the emperor ordered a thousand picked troops selected to assist Pacification General Zhaohui on the western route.

entries.zh: 自硃爾圖斯赴瑪納斯，獲得木齊鄂羅斯，並所部三百人、馬駝牛羊二千餘。
entries.en: Marching from Zhuerutusi to Manas, he captured Demuchi Eluosi together with three hundred followers and more than two thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
entries.literal: From Zhuerutusi he went to Manas, captured Demuchi Eluosi, and also took three hundred of his followers and more than two thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

entries.zh: 扎哈沁頭人巴哈曼集叛走，端濟布偕侍衛奎瑪岱追捕，至小衛和勒津，降所部二百戶，又得掠台站賊札木布。
entries.en: When the Zhahakin leader Bahamanji rebelled and fled, Duanjibu and bodyguard Kuimadai pursued him to Xiaoweihelejin, accepted the surrender of two hundred households, and also captured the bandit Zhamubu, who had been raiding courier stations.
entries.literal: The Zhahakin leader Bahamanji rebelled and fled; Duanjibu, together with Bodyguard Kuimadai, pursued him to Xiaoweihelejin, accepted the surrender of two hundred of his households, and also captured the bandit Zhamubu who had plundered courier stations.

entries.zh: 師捕治厄魯特頭人噶爾藏多爾濟、扎那噶爾布等，布魯古特台吉琿齊、呼爾璊台吉達瓦斬扎那噶爾布，詣端濟布軍請降。
entries.en: While the army was pursuing the Oirat leaders Galdan Dorji, Zanagarbu, and others, the Burut taiji Hunqi and the Khurlet taiji Dawa killed Zanagarbu and came to Duanjibu's camp to offer surrender.
entries.literal: When the army pursued and punished the Oirat leaders Galdan Dorji, Zanagarbu, and others, the Burut taiji Hunqi and the Khurlet taiji Dawa killed Zanagarbu and came to Duanjibu's army to offer surrender.

entries.zh: 端濟布遽引師還，琿齊、達瓦复叛去。
entries.en: Duanjibu abruptly withdrew the army, and Hunqi and Dawa rebelled and fled again.
entries.literal: Duanjibu abruptly led the army back, and Hunqi and Dawa rebelled again and fled.

entries.zh: 上懲端濟布惟事姑息，命靖逆將軍雅爾哈善按治。
entries.en: The emperor, angered that Duanjibu had been too indulgent, ordered Pacification General Yarghashi to investigate and discipline him.
entries.literal: The emperor, punishing Duanjibu for dealing only in indulgence, ordered Pacification General Yarghashi to investigate and punish him.

entries.zh: 師至羅克倫孟古圖嶺，獲噶爾藏多爾濟宰桑羅卜札尼瑪、得木齊敦多克，檻送巴里坤。
entries.en: At Luokelunmengutuling the army captured Galdan Dorji's zaisang Luobuzhanima and Demuchi Dunduoke and sent them in cages to Barkul.
entries.literal: When the army reached Luokelunmengutuling, it captured Galdan Dorji's zaisang Luobuzhanima and Demuchi Dunduoke and sent them in cages to Barkul.

entries.zh: 上聞，命貸端濟布罪。
entries.en: When word reached the court, the emperor ordered Duanjibu's offense pardoned.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he ordered Duanjibu's offense pardoned.

entries.zh: 諾爾本，吳機格忒氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
entries.en: Nuoerben, of the Ujigit clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Nuoerben, of the Ujigit clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 以前鋒從軍。
entries.en: He served on campaign as a vanguard soldier.
entries.literal: He followed the army as a vanguard soldier.

entries.zh: 富德獲宰桑烏巴什，遣諾爾本送兆惠軍。
entries.en: Fude captured the zaisang Ubashi and sent Nuoerben to deliver him to Zhaohui's army.
entries.literal: Fude captured the zaisang Ubashi and sent Nuoerben to deliver him to Zhaohui's army.

entries.zh: 道遇賊，力戰，賜號克籌巴圖魯。
entries.en: On the march he met rebels and fought fiercely, for which he was granted the title Kechoubatur.
entries.literal: On the road he encountered rebels and fought fiercely; he was granted the title Kechoubatur.

entries.zh: 師圍庫車，霍集占來援。
entries.en: When the army besieged Kucha, Khojijaha marched to relieve the city.
entries.literal: When the army besieged Kucha, Khojijaha came to reinforce.

entries.zh: 諾爾本偕公袞楚克，侍衛齊凌札卜、齊努渾等擊賊右翼，賊敗走，逐之六十餘裡，至鄂根河口，斬獲甚眾；
entries.en: Nuoerben, together with Gonggunchuke and bodyguards Qilingzhab, Qinuhun, and others, struck the enemy's right wing. The rebels broke and fled, and the pursuers drove them more than sixty li to the mouth of the Egen River, killing and capturing a great number;
entries.literal: Nuoerben, together with Gonggunchuke, Bodyguards Qilingzhab, Qinuhun, and others, attacked the rebels' right wing; the rebels fled in defeat and were pursued more than sixty li to the mouth of the Egen River, where many were killed and captured;

entries.zh: 賊逃入蘇巴什山，复偕齊努渾入山搜戮：溫詔嘉焉。
entries.en: the survivors fled into Subashi Mountain. He entered the mountains again with Qinuhun to hunt them down, and the emperor warmly praised him in an edict.
entries.literal: the rebels fled into Subashi Mountain; he again entered the mountain with Qinuhun to search them out and kill them: the emperor warmly praised him in an edict.

entries.zh: 師攻葉爾羌，偕端濟布戰城東，敗賊。
entries.en: During the attack on Yarkand he fought alongside Duanjibu east of the city and routed the rebels.
entries.literal: When the army attacked Yarkand, he fought with Duanjibu east of the city and defeated the rebels.

entries.zh: 師還，命在乾清門行走，賚銀帛，賜騎都尉加一云騎尉世職，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: After the army returned, he was ordered to serve at the Qianqing Gate, rewarded with silver and silks, granted the hereditary ranks of commandant of cavalry with an additional commandant of the cloud cavalry, and portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered to serve at the Qianqing Gate, was rewarded with silver and silks, granted commandant of cavalry with an additional commandant of the cloud cavalry as hereditary office, and portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 擢頭等侍衛，從明瑞徵緬甸，擊賊被創。
entries.en: He was promoted to first-rank imperial bodyguard and followed Mingrui on the Burma campaign, where he was wounded in action.
entries.literal: He was promoted to first-rank imperial bodyguard and followed Mingrui on the Burma campaign; attacking the enemy he was wounded.

entries.zh: 尋令將兵屯騰越。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to lead a garrison at Tengyue.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Tengyue.

entries.zh: 還京，擢圍場總管，加副都統銜。
entries.en: On returning to the capital he was promoted to director of the imperial hunting grounds and given the brevet rank of vice commander.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, he was promoted to director of the hunting grounds and given the brevet rank of vice commander.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 列傳一百二
entries.en: Biographies 102
entries.literal: Biographies 102

entries.zh: 列傳一百三 瑚爾起愛隆阿弟巴靈阿舒明福祿齊里克齊 閻相師伊柱努三烏勒登 瑚爾起，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。
entries.en: Biographies 103: Hu Erqi, Ai Long'a, his younger brother Ba Ling'a, Shu Ming, Fu Lu, Qilikeqi, Yan Xiangshi, Yizhu, Nusan, and Wuleideng. Hu Erqi, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Biographies 103: Hu Erqi, Ai Long'a, [his] younger brother Ba Ling'a, Shu Ming, Fu Lu, Qilikeqi, Yan Xiangshi, Yizhu, Nusan, Wuleideng. Hu Erqi, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 自筆帖式累遷協領。
entries.en: He rose from clerk through successive promotions to assistant commander.
entries.literal: From clerk he was promoted in succession to assistant commander.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年，從征金川。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of the Qianlong reign he took part in the campaign against Jinchuan.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, he accompanied the campaign against Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 遷呼倫貝爾總管。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as commander of Hulun Buir.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be commander of Hulun Buir.

entries.zh: 二十年，從征準噶爾，加副都統銜。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he joined the Dzungar campaign and was granted the rank of vice commandant.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, he joined the campaign against the Dzungars and was given the rank of vice commandant.

entries.zh: 二十一年，從參贊大臣達爾黨阿自珠爾都斯逐捕阿睦爾撒納，诇知阿睦爾撒納竄哈薩克，從定邊左副將軍哈達哈以師臨之。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he followed campaign counselor Da Erdang'a from Zhuerduosi in pursuit of Amursana; when scouts reported that Amursana had fled into Kazakh lands, he marched with Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Ha Daha to bring the army up against him.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, he followed the campaign counselor Da Erdang'a from Zhuerduosi in pursuit of Amursana; learning that Amursana had fled into Kazakh territory, he marched with the Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Ha Daha to bring troops against him.

entries.zh: 哈薩克汗阿布賚拒戰，擊敗之，斬百餘級，得馬二百餘。
entries.en: When the Kazakh khan Abulai gave battle, they defeated him, took more than a hundred heads, and seized over two hundred horses.
entries.literal: The Kazakh khan Abulai resisted in battle; they defeated him, beheaded more than a hundred men, and captured more than two hundred horses.

entries.zh: 獲其頭人，言阿睦爾撒納方在泥雅斯圖山，檄阿布賚擒獻。
entries.en: They captured a Kazakh leader who reported that Amursana was then on Niyasitu Mountain, and issued a dispatch ordering Abulai to seize him and send him in.
entries.literal: They captured a Kazakh leader, who said Amursana was then on Niyasitu Mountain; they sent a dispatch ordering Abulai to seize and deliver him.

entries.zh: 杜爾默特貝勒巴圖、伯羅特等潛通阿睦爾撒納，瑚爾起與戰輝巴朗山，執伯羅特，盡殲其部眾，及阿睦爾撒納所留烏梁海五十餘戶。
entries.en: The Durbet prince Batu, Berote, and others had been in secret contact with Amursana; Hu Erqi fought them at Huibolang Mountain, captured Berote, and wiped out their entire following along with the more than fifty Urianghai households Amursana had left behind.
entries.literal: The Durbet prince Batu, Berote, and others had secretly communicated with Amursana; Hu Erqi fought them at Huibolang Mountain, seized Berote, and annihilated their entire following, as well as more than fifty Urianghai households left behind by Amursana.

entries.zh: 沙喇斯、瑪呼斯既降复叛，掠台站，而布魯古特台吉琿齊等戕察哈爾總管巴寧阿以叛。
entries.en: Shalasi and Mahusi had surrendered but rebelled again and raided courier stations, while the Burut taiji Hunchi and others killed Chahar commander Baning'a and rose in revolt.
entries.literal: Shalasi and Mahusi had submitted but rebelled again, plundering courier stations; meanwhile the Burut taiji Hunchi and others killed the Chahar commander Baning'a in revolt.

entries.zh: 上命瑚爾起偕鄂實、三格副哈寧阿，將千人駐濟爾哈朗、巴里坤適中地，捕琿齊及沙喇斯、瑪呼斯部眾。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Hu Erqi, together with Eshi and Sange assisting Haning'a, to take a thousand men and garrison the midpoint between Jierhalang and Barkol to capture Hunchi and the bands of Shalasi and Mahusi.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Hu Erqi, together with Eshi and Sange assisting Haning'a, to lead a thousand men and garrison the midpoint between Jierhalang and Barkol to capture Hunchi and the followers of Shalasi and Mahusi.

entries.zh: 瑚爾起偕鄂實追剿扎哈沁逃賊，又偕副都統巴圖濟爾噶勒自呼斯坦至尼勒喀河，偵琿齊等百餘戶游牧，突擊，執之。
entries.en: Hu Erqi joined Eshi in pursuing Zahachin fugitives, then marched with Vice Commandant Batujiergale from Hustan to the Nileka River, located more than a hundred households of Hunchi and his people at pasture, struck by surprise, and captured them.
entries.literal: Hu Erqi, with Eshi, pursued and attacked fleeing Zahachin bandits; he also joined Vice Commandant Batujiergale from Hustan to the Nileka River, reconnoitered more than a hundred households of Hunchi and others at pasture, made a surprise attack, and seized them.

entries.zh: 尋從師自伊犁逐剿諸回部，至善塔斯巔，招降布魯特頭人圖魯啟拜、鄂庫及其部眾，搜捕阿里瑪圖河逸賊。
entries.en: He soon followed the army from Ili in the pursuit and suppression of the Muslim districts as far as Shantasi Peak, induced the Burut leaders Turuqibai and Eku and their people to surrender, and hunted down fugitive bandits along the Alimatu River.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he followed the army from Ili in pursuing and suppressing the various Muslim districts, reaching Shantasi Peak; he induced the Burut leaders Turuqibai and Eku and their followers to submit, and searched out fugitive bandits along the Alimatu River.

entries.zh: 上以索倫兵從征久，召瑚爾起及副都統鄂博什率以還，瑚爾起等仍請從軍。
entries.en: Because the Solon troops had been on campaign so long, the emperor recalled Hu Erqi and Vice Commandant Eboshi to lead them home, but Hu Erqi and his men still asked to stay with the army.
entries.literal: Because the Solon troops had campaigned for a long time, the emperor summoned Hu Erqi and Vice Commandant Eboshi to lead them back; Hu Erqi and the others still asked to remain with the army.

entries.zh: 將軍兆惠攻霍集占於葉爾羌，被圍，定邊右副將軍富德檄瑚爾起及巴圖濟爾噶勒率索倫兵自伊拉里克赴援，以馬駝未至，負糧械步行戈壁中。
entries.en: When General Zhao Hui attacked Huojizhan at Yarkand and found himself besieged, Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De ordered Hu Erqi and Batujiergale to lead Solon troops from Ilirik to his relief; with horses and camels not yet arrived, they shouldered grain and arms and marched on foot across the Gobi.
entries.literal: General Zhao Hui attacked Huojizhan at Yarkand and was besieged; the Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De dispatched Hu Erqi and Batujiergale to lead Solon troops from Ilirik to the relief; as horses and camels had not yet arrived, they carried grain and weapons on foot across the Gobi.

entries.zh: 上獎諭，即授正白旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: The emperor praised him in edict and at once appointed him Mongol vice commandant of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: The emperor issued commendatory edicts and immediately appointed him Mongol vice commandant of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 師至巴爾楚克，兆惠圍已解，與富德軍合。
entries.en: By the time the army reached Barcuk, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they united with Fu De's army.
entries.literal: When the army reached Barcuk, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they joined Fu De's forces.

entries.zh: 霍集占之徒阿卜都克勒木等侵和闐，攻哈拉哈什，侍衛齊凌扎卜請援，兆惠令瑚爾起與巴圖濟爾噶勒督兵赴援。
entries.en: Huojizhan's follower Abudukelimu and others invaded Khotan and attacked Karakash; bodyguard Qilingzhabu called for help, and Zhao Hui ordered Hu Erqi and Batujiergale to take troops to their relief.
entries.literal: Huojizhan's follower Abudukelimu and others invaded Khotan and attacked Karakash; bodyguard Qilingzhabu requested aid, and Zhao Hui ordered Hu Erqi and Batujiergale to lead troops to the relief.

entries.zh: 齊凌扎卜馳告，夜行至伊立齊，賊聞兵至，引退。
entries.en: Qilingzhabu rode in haste with word of the attack; they marched by night to Yiliqi, and when the rebels heard troops were coming, they pulled back.
entries.literal: Qilingzhabu rode in haste to report; they marched by night to Yiliqi, and when the bandits heard troops had arrived, they withdrew.

entries.zh: 诇知賊騎七百餘屯博爾齊，天大霧，瑚爾起督兵突擊，賊潰走，退至皁窪勒河，斬百餘級，收回人四千餘戶，和闐遂平。
entries.en: Scouts reported that more than seven hundred rebel horsemen were encamped at Bo'erqi; in a thick fog Hu Erqi led a surprise attack, the rebels broke and fled to Zaowale River, more than a hundred were killed, more than four thousand households were recovered, and Khotan was pacified.
entries.literal: Scouts learned that more than seven hundred rebel horsemen were encamped at Bo'erqi; a heavy fog blanketed the sky, and Hu Erqi directed a surprise attack; the bandits broke and fled, retreating to Zaowale River; more than a hundred were beheaded, and more than four thousand households were recovered; Khotan was then pacified.

entries.zh: 上賦博羅齊行紀事，賜瑚爾起雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: The emperor composed a narrative poem on the Bo'erqi campaign and granted Hu Erqi a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: The emperor composed a narrative poem on the Bo'erqi campaign and granted Hu Erqi a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 師自喀喇烏蘇逐捕霍集占，至阿爾楚爾。
entries.en: The army pursued Huojizhan from Karasu as far as Altur.
entries.literal: The army pursued Huojizhan from Karasu to Altur.

entries.zh: 賊設伏兩山間，我軍張兩翼擊之，賊敗走三十里，負山而屯。
entries.en: The rebels laid an ambush between two mountains; our army struck with both wings, routed them for thirty li, and they made camp with the mountain at their backs.
entries.literal: The bandits set an ambush between two mountains; our army deployed both wings to attack them; the bandits were defeated and fled thirty li, then encamped with the mountain at their backs.

entries.zh: 瑚爾起等自山麓橫衝入陣，師夾擊，賊大敗，越山遁，師從之，至伊西洱庫爾淖爾。
entries.en: Hu Erqi and others charged into the line from the mountain foot while the army struck from both sides; the rebels were routed, fled over the mountains, and the army pursued them to Lake Yixihuku'er.
entries.literal: Hu Erqi and others charged horizontally into the battle line from the foot of the mountain; the army attacked from both sides; the bandits were utterly defeated, fled over the mountain, and the army pursued them to Lake Yixihuku'er.

entries.zh: 瑚爾起等為伏東山，側擊，賊復大敗，霍集占竄入巴達克山。
entries.en: Hu Erqi and others lay in ambush on the eastern mountain and struck from the flank; the rebels were routed again, and Huojizhan fled into Badakhshan.
entries.literal: Hu Erqi and others lay in ambush on the eastern mountain and struck from the flank; the bandits were again utterly defeated, and Huojizhan fled into Badakhshan.

entries.zh: 巴達克山汗素勒坦沙獻霍集占首。
entries.en: The khan of Badakhshan, Sultan Shah, sent in Huojizhan's head.
entries.literal: The Badakhshan khan Sultan Shah presented Huojizhan's head.

entries.zh: 瑚爾起將索倫兵還，賚銀幣，圖形紫光閣，列前五十功臣。
entries.en: Hu Erqi led the Solon troops home, was rewarded with silver and coins, had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and was ranked among the first fifty meritorious officials.
entries.literal: Hu Erqi led the Solon troops back; he was rewarded with silver and coins, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first fifty meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 瑚爾起疏言：「呼倫貝爾多水泉，可耕。
entries.en: Hu Erqi memorialized: "Hulun Buir has abundant springs and land fit for cultivation.
entries.literal: Hu Erqi memorialized: "Hulun Buir has many springs and can be cultivated.

entries.zh: 請選塔里雅沁降回百戶往耕。」
entries.en: I ask that a hundred households of surrendered Taliyachin Muslims be chosen to settle and farm there."
entries.literal: I request that a hundred households of surrendered Muslims from Taliyachin be selected to go and farm there."

entries.zh: 上命瑚爾起以副都統為呼倫貝爾總管，董其事。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Hu Erqi, while retaining his vice commandant rank, to serve as commander of Hulun Buir and oversee the project.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Hu Erqi, with his vice commandant rank, to serve as commander of Hulun Buir and supervise the matter.

entries.zh: 移黑龍江副都統。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice commandant of Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be vice commandant of Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 從征緬甸，收猛拱、猛養諸地。
entries.en: He joined the Burma campaign and recovered Menggong, Mengyang, and other districts.
entries.literal: He joined the campaign against Burma and recovered Menggong, Mengyang, and other districts.

entries.zh: 卒於軍。
entries.en: He died on campaign.
entries.literal: He died in the army.

entries.zh: 賜騎都尉，並前世職為一等輕車都尉，祀昭忠祠。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Cavalry Captain, and together with his earlier hereditary rank was raised to first-class Commandant of Light Chariots; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Cavalry Captain, and together with his previous hereditary office was raised to a first-class Commandant of Light Chariots; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

entries.zh: 愛隆阿，覺爾察氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Ai Long'a, of the Jerci clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Ai Long'a, of the Jerci clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 自前鋒侍衛累遷齊齊哈爾副都統。
entries.en: He rose from vanguard guardsman through successive posts to vice commandant of Qiqihar.
entries.literal: From vanguard guardsman he was promoted in succession to vice commandant of Qiqihar.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十一年，授領隊大臣，赴巴里坤軍營。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year of the Qianlong reign he was appointed column commander and went to the Barkol army camp.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Qianlong he was appointed column commander and went to the Barkol army camp.

entries.zh: 偕參贊大臣富德逐捕巴雅爾，至愛登蘇，遇阿布賚部眾突出，數與戰，卻之。
entries.en: With campaign counselor Fu De he pursued Bayar to Aidengsu, met Abulai's followers in a sudden attack, fought them several times, and drove them off.
entries.literal: Together with campaign counselor Fu De he pursued Bayar to Aidengsu; they encountered Abulai's followers making a sudden appearance, fought them several times, and drove them back.

entries.zh: 自巴爾楚克至濟爾哈朗置台站，逐賊沙喇博和什嶺，遇都爾伯特納木奇游牧，乞降，旋遁去，愛隆阿追及之，殺千餘人，納木奇遂納款。
entries.en: They set up courier stations from Barcuk to Jierhalang and pursued bandits at Shalabohuoshi Ridge; they met the Dorbet Namuchi at pasture, who begged to surrender but soon fled; Ai Long'a caught up with him, killed more than a thousand men, and Namuchi then submitted.
entries.literal: From Barkul to Jierhalang they established courier stations; pursuing bandits at Shalabohuoshi Ridge, they encountered the Dorbet Namuchi at pasture, who begged to submit but soon fled; Ai Long'a overtook him, killed more than a thousand men, and Namuchi then tendered allegiance.

entries.zh: 師至察罕烏蘇，收厄魯特宰桑烏魯木游牧百餘戶。
entries.en: When the army reached Chahan Usu, they took in more than a hundred households of the Oirat zaisang Ulumu at pasture.
entries.literal: When the army reached Chahan Usu, they received more than a hundred households of the Oirat zaisang Ulumu at pasture.

entries.zh: 師屯濟爾哈朗，命愛隆阿駐守濟爾哈朗、巴里坤適中地。
entries.en: The army encamped at Jierhalang, and Ai Long'a was ordered to garrison the midpoint between Jierhalang and Barkol.
entries.literal: The army encamped at Jierhalang; Ai Long'a was ordered to garrison the midpoint between Jierhalang and Barkol.

entries.zh: 尋從靖逆將軍雅爾哈善討霍集占。
entries.en: He soon followed Pacification General Ya Erhashan in the campaign against Huojizhan.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he followed the Pacification General Ya Erhashan in campaigning against Huojizhan.

entries.zh: 先是愛登甦之戰，侍衛奇徹布戰沒，至是愛隆阿上言：「前擒巴雅爾，奪還奇徹布屍，富德未及疏列。」
entries.en: Earlier, at the battle of Aidengsu, bodyguard Qichebu had been killed in action; now Ai Long'a submitted: "When Bayar was captured earlier, we recovered Qichebu's body, but Fu De had not yet reported it in a memorial."
entries.literal: Earlier, in the battle at Aidengsu, bodyguard Qichebu had been killed in action; now Ai Long'a submitted: "When Bayar was captured earlier, Qichebu's corpse was recovered, but Fu De had not yet reported it in a memorial."

entries.zh: 定邊將軍兆惠疏言：「愛隆阿原報所無，事後追論，顯為爭功，請嚴議。」
entries.en: Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui memorialized: "What Ai Long'a now claims was absent from his original report; raising it afterward is clearly an attempt to claim credit—please subject him to strict review."
entries.literal: Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui memorialized: "What Ai Long'a now claims was not in his original report; raising it afterward is clearly striving for merit—please subject him to strict deliberation."

entries.zh: 詔原之。
entries.en: An edict pardoned him.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned him.

entries.zh: 師圍庫車，賊來援，愛隆阿等與戰於戈壁，殲賊甚眾。
entries.en: When the army besieged Kuche and rebels came to relieve the city, Ai Long'a and others fought them on the Gobi and killed a great many.
entries.literal: The army besieged Kuche; bandits came to relieve it; Ai Long'a and others fought them on the Gobi and destroyed a great many of the enemy.

entries.zh: 霍集占將五千人續至，愛隆阿等率吉林及索倫兵千騎逐賊至鄂根河側，與戰，迫賊入水，死者三千餘人。
entries.en: When Huojizhan brought five thousand more men to relieve the city, Ai Long'a and others led a thousand Jilin and Solon horsemen in pursuit to the Egen River, fought them, drove them into the water, and more than three thousand drowned or were killed.
entries.literal: Huojizhan brought five thousand men in continued relief; Ai Long'a and others led a thousand Jilin and Solon horsemen in pursuit to the bank of the Egen River, fought them, drove the bandits into the water, and more than three thousand died.

entries.zh: 拔其纛，驛致京師。
entries.en: They captured the enemy standard and sent it by courier to the capital.
entries.literal: They seized the enemy standard and sent it by courier post to the capital.

entries.zh: 上為賦回纛行，獎其能戰。
entries.en: The emperor composed a poem on the return of the standard and praised their prowess in battle.
entries.literal: The emperor composed a poem on the return of the standard and praised their fighting ability.

entries.zh: 旋從將軍兆惠至葉爾羌，與霍集占部眾戰，當左翼。
entries.en: He soon followed General Zhao Hui to Yarkand, fought Huojizhan's followers, and held the left wing.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he followed General Zhao Hui to Yarkand, fought Huojizhan's followers, and held the left wing.

entries.zh: 兆惠被困，靖逆將軍納穆札爾赴援，愛隆阿將兵截喀什噶爾賊援路。
entries.en: When Zhao Hui was besieged, Pacification General Namuzha'er went to relieve him, and Ai Long'a led troops to cut off the Kashgar rebel relief route.
entries.literal: Zhao Hui was besieged; Pacification General Namuzha'er went to his relief; Ai Long'a led troops to cut off the Kashgar rebel relief route.

entries.zh: 徼巡台站，至托罕塔罕，遇賊，剿殺百餘人。
entries.en: While patrolling courier stations he reached Tohantahan, met rebels, and killed more than a hundred in action.
entries.literal: Patrolling courier stations, he reached Tohantahan, encountered bandits, and killed more than a hundred in suppression.

entries.zh: 上授愛隆阿參贊大臣，令與定邊右副將軍富德援兆惠。
entries.en: The emperor appointed Ai Long'a campaign counselor and ordered him, with Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De, to relieve Zhao Hui.
entries.literal: The emperor appointed Ai Long'a campaign counselor and ordered him, together with Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De, to relieve Zhao Hui.

entries.zh: 愛隆阿戰呼爾璊，再戰葉爾羌河，遂與兆惠軍合。
entries.en: Ai Long'a fought at Hu'erlan and again at the Yarkand River, then united with Zhao Hui's army.
entries.literal: Ai Long'a fought at Hu'erlan, fought again at the Yarkand River, and then joined Zhao Hui's army.

entries.zh: 尋引兵駐烏什，兼防喀什噶爾，予雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: He soon led troops to garrison Ushi while also guarding Kashgar, and was granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he led troops to garrison Ushi and also guard Kashgar; he was granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 復從富德逐霍集占，戰於伊西洱庫爾淖爾。
entries.en: He again followed Fu De in pursuit of Huojizhan and fought at Lake Yixihuku'er.
entries.literal: He again followed Fu De in pursuing Huojizhan and fought at Lake Yixihuku'er.

entries.zh: 徼巡台站，值嗎唬斯、賓巴等謀劫察罕烏蘇台站，以兵追襲，斬獲殆盡，進騎都尉世職。
entries.en: While patrolling courier stations he found Mahusi, Binba, and others plotting to raid the Chahan Usu station, pursued them with troops, and killed or captured nearly all; he was advanced to a hereditary Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: While patrolling courier stations, he found Mahusi, Binba, and others plotting to raid the Chahan Usu station; he pursued with troops and killed or captured nearly all of them; he was advanced to a hereditary Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 師還，授正白旗護軍統領，兼鑲白旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was appointed commander of the guards of the Plain White Banner and concurrently Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed commander of the guards of the Plain White Banner and concurrently Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner.

entries.zh: 圖形紫光閣，列前五十功臣。
entries.en: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first fifty meritorious officials.
entries.literal: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first fifty meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 再進一等輕車都尉兼一云騎尉世職。
entries.en: He was further advanced to first-class Commandant of Light Chariots with an additional hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: He was further advanced to first-class Commandant of Light Chariots with an additional hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 授伊犁參贊大臣。
entries.en: He was appointed campaign counselor of Ili.
entries.literal: He was appointed campaign counselor of Ili.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 弟巴靈阿，自親軍校累遷二等侍衛，授察哈爾總管。
entries.en: His younger brother Ba Ling'a rose from imperial guards corporal to second-class bodyguard and was appointed Chahar commander.
entries.literal: His younger brother Ba Ling'a rose from imperial guards corporal through successive promotions to second-class bodyguard and was appointed Chahar commander.

entries.zh: 賜坤都爾巴圖魯名號，授領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was granted the title Kundul Baturu and appointed column commander.
entries.literal: He was granted the title Kundul Baturu and appointed column commander.

entries.zh: 在博羅齊搜捕厄魯特部眾，遇伏戰死，賜雲騎尉世職，圖形紫光閣，列後五十功臣。
entries.en: At Bo'erqi, while hunting down Oirat followers, he was ambushed and killed in battle; he was posthumously granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the latter fifty meritorious officials.
entries.literal: At Bo'erqi, while searching out Oirat followers, he met an ambush and died in battle; he was posthumously granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the latter fifty meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 舒明，烏梁海濟勒莫特氏，蒙古正黃旗人。
entries.en: Shu Ming, of the Urianghai Jilemote clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Shu Ming, of the Urianghai Jilemote clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 自二等侍衛累遷都察院左副都御史、正黃旗護軍統領。
entries.en: He rose from second-class bodyguard to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and commander of the guards of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: From second-class bodyguard he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and commander of the guards of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 命赴北路軍，為諸部降人董理游牧。
entries.en: He was ordered to the Northern Route army to oversee the pastoral settlement of surrendered peoples from the various tribes.
entries.literal: He was ordered to the Northern Route army to supervise the pastoral arrangements of surrendered peoples from the various tribes.

entries.zh: 旋授吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 诇知降人訥默庫戕台站侍衛，謀以所部叛，馳奏。
entries.en: When he learned that the surrendered man Nemuku had killed a courier-station bodyguard and planned to rebel with his following, he rode in haste to report it.
entries.literal: Learning that the surrendered man Nemuku had killed a courier-station bodyguard and planned to rebel with his following, he rode in haste to report.

entries.zh: 敕參贊大臣阿蘭泰往捕治，阿蘭泰請益兵，上責其紛擾。
entries.en: The emperor ordered campaign counselor Alantai to go and capture him; when Alantai asked for more troops, the emperor rebuked him for stirring up trouble.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered campaign counselor Alantai to go and capture him; Alantai requested additional troops, and the emperor rebuked him for causing confusion.

entries.zh: 訥默庫就擒，上以舒明籌策得宜，而阿蘭泰推諉遲誤，奪阿蘭泰三等男爵畀舒明。
entries.en: When Nemuku was captured, the emperor found Shu Ming's planning sound but Alantai evasive and dilatory; he stripped Alantai of his third-class baronage and gave it to Shu Ming.
entries.literal: Nemuku was captured; because Shu Ming's planning had been appropriate while Alantai had shirked and delayed, the emperor stripped Alantai of his third-class baronage and gave it to Shu Ming.

entries.zh: 舒明在邊，諸部降人至者，為之拊循。
entries.en: On the frontier Shu Ming comforted and guided all surrendered peoples from the various tribes who came in.
entries.literal: While Shu Ming was on the frontier, he comforted and guided all surrendered peoples from the various tribes who arrived.

entries.zh: 噶勒雜特宰桑根敦降，上授佐領，使與丹畢游牧同處。
entries.en: When the Galazat zaisang Genden submitted, the emperor made him assistant banner commander and had him pasture together with Danbi.
entries.literal: The Galazat zaisang Genden submitted; the emperor appointed him assistant banner commander and had him pasture together with Danbi.

entries.zh: 都爾伯特台吉伯什阿噶什、烏巴什降，上授伯什阿噶什親王、烏巴什貝子，游牧額爾齊斯，舒明為陳請留屯哈達青吉勒。
entries.en: When the Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted, the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beise, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.
entries.literal: The Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted; the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beise, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.

entries.zh: 達什達瓦部降，編為三旗，移阿爾台；
entries.en: When Dashidawa's following submitted, they were organized into three banners and moved to Altai;
entries.literal: Dashidawa's following submitted and was organized into three banners and moved to Altai;

entries.zh: 其續至者，使處扎哈沁舊游牧地。
entries.en: those who continued to arrive were settled on the former Zahachin pastures.
entries.literal: those who continued to arrive were settled on the former Zahachin pastures.

entries.zh: 策淩烏巴什、巴圖博羅特及達瑪林等部眾貧甚，疏請賑，上為發米六百石。
entries.en: The followers of Tsewang Ubashi, Batubolot, Damalin, and others were desperately poor; he memorialized for relief, and the emperor issued six hundred piculs of grain.
entries.literal: The followers of Tsewang Ubashi, Batubolot, and Damalin and others were extremely poor; he memorialized requesting relief, and the emperor issued six hundred piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 上聞和托輝特青滾雜卜將叛，命舒明诇之。
entries.en: When the emperor heard that the Khotogoid Chinggunjab was about to rebel, he ordered Shu Ming to investigate.
entries.literal: The emperor heard that the Khotogoid Chinggunjab was about to rebel and ordered Shu Ming to reconnoiter.

entries.zh: 舒明言叛已著，命會將軍成袞札布等捕治。
entries.en: Shu Ming reported that the rebellion was already evident; he was ordered to join General Chenggunjab and others in capturing and punishing him.
entries.literal: Shu Ming reported that the rebellion was already manifest; he was ordered to join General Chenggunjab and others in capturing and punishing him.

entries.zh: 授參贊大臣，成袞札布令將科布多兵二百以往。
entries.en: He was appointed campaign counselor, and Chenggunjab ordered two hundred Kobdo troops to accompany him.
entries.literal: He was appointed campaign counselor; Chenggunjab ordered two hundred troops from Kobdo to go with him.

entries.zh: 上命侍衛巴寧阿勒泰將三百人為舒明佐。
entries.en: The emperor ordered bodyguard Baning'altai to lead three hundred men to assist Shu Ming.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered bodyguard Baning'altai to lead three hundred men to assist Shu Ming.

entries.zh: 旋命偕成袞札布駐烏里雅蘇台。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to join Chenggunjab in garrisoning Uliastai.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to join Chenggunjab in garrisoning Uliastai.

entries.zh: 授理籓部侍郎。
entries.en: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
entries.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

entries.zh: 再遷綏遠城將軍，兼領歸化城都統。
entries.en: He was again transferred to General of Suiyuan and concurrently commander of Guihuacheng.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to be General of Suiyuan and concurrently commander of Guihuacheng.

entries.zh: 二十七年，卒。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year he died.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died.

entries.zh: 子雅滿泰，襲三等男。
entries.en: His son Yamantai inherited the third-class baronage.
entries.literal: His son Yamantai inherited the third-class baronage.

entries.zh: 累遷正白旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to Mongol vice commandant of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Mongol vice commandant of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 坐事左授頭等侍衛。
entries.en: For an offense he was demoted to first-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: For an offense he was demoted to first-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 與保泰同充駐藏大臣。
entries.en: He served together with Baotai as Resident Minister in Tibet.
entries.literal: Together with Baotai he served as Resident Minister in Tibet.

entries.zh: 廓爾喀侵後藏，與保泰同得罪，荷校被杖。
entries.en: When the Gurkhas invaded Rear Tibet, he and Baotai were both punished, placed in the cangue, and flogged.
entries.literal: When the Gurkhas invaded Rear Tibet, he and Baotai were both found guilty, placed in the cangue, and flogged.

entries.zh: 復起至頭等侍衛。
entries.en: He was later restored and rose again to first-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: He was later restored and rose again to first-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 福祿，旺察氏，蒙古正白旗人。
entries.en: Fu Lu, of the Wangcha clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Fu Lu, of the Wangcha clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 自護軍校累遷福建建寧鎮總兵。
entries.en: He rose from guards corporal to regional commander of Jianning in Fujian.
entries.literal: From guards corporal he was promoted in succession to regional commander of Jianning in Fujian.

entries.zh: 內移正藍旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He was transferred within the capital to Mongol vice commandant of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: He was transferred within the capital to Mongol vice commandant of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 外授直隸宣化、廣東右翼諸鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was posted outside the capital as regional commander of Xuanhua in Zhili and of the Right Wing in Guangdong.
entries.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as regional commander of Xuanhua in Zhili and of the Right Wing in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 又內移正紅旗漢軍副都統。
entries.en: He was again transferred within the capital to Chinese Banner vice commandant of the Plain Red Banner.
entries.literal: He was again transferred within the capital to Chinese Banner vice commandant of the Plain Red Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十三年，授參贊大臣，駐烏里雅蘇台。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year of the Qianlong reign he was appointed campaign counselor and garrisoned at Uliastai.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Qianlong he was appointed campaign counselor and garrisoned at Uliastai.

entries.zh: 旋命將索倫兵二千人赴巴里坤。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to lead two thousand Solon troops to Barkol.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to lead two thousand Solon troops to Barkol.

entries.zh: 時定邊左副將軍成袞札布與參贊大臣阿桂會討舍楞，福祿請具三月糧，自科布多輸送，從之。
entries.en: At that time Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Chenggunjab and campaign counselor Agui were jointly campaigning against Seleng; Fu Lu asked for three months' provisions to be shipped from Kobdo, and the request was approved.
entries.literal: At that time Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Chenggunjab and campaign counselor Agui were jointly campaigning against Seleng; Fu Lu requested three months' provisions to be transported from Kobdo, and this was approved.

entries.zh: 至海拉爾，與御前侍衛敦察會師進。
entries.en: At Hailar they joined the imperial bodyguard Duncha and marched forward together.
entries.literal: When they reached Hailar, they joined the imperial bodyguard Duncha and advanced together.

entries.zh: 旋佐將軍兆惠討霍集占，偕定邊右副將軍富德帥師次呼爾璊。
entries.en: He soon assisted General Zhao Hui against Huojizhan and, with Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De, led the army to encamp at Hu'erlan.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he assisted General Zhao Hui in campaigning against Huojizhan and, together with Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De, led troops encamped at Hu'erlan.

entries.zh: 霍集占以五千餘人來犯，福祿偕領隊大臣永慶率索倫、察哈爾兵擊之，自巳至申，與賊戰十餘次，賊潰去。
entries.en: When Huojizhan attacked with more than five thousand men, Fu Lu and column commander Yongqing led Solon and Chahar troops against them; from mid-morning to mid-afternoon they fought more than ten engagements, and the rebels broke and withdrew.
entries.literal: Huojizhan came to attack with more than five thousand men; Fu Lu, together with column commander Yongqing, led Solon and Chahar troops to strike them; from the si hour to the shen hour they fought the bandits more than ten times, and the bandits broke and withdrew.

entries.zh: 進次葉爾羌河岸，城賊突圍出，富德與福祿等領中軍自右進，追賊渡河，賊屢敗。
entries.en: Advancing to the Yarkand River, garrison rebels broke out in a sortie; Fu De and Fu Lu led the center from the right, pursued them across the river, and routed them again and again.
entries.literal: Advancing to the bank of the Yarkand River, garrison bandits broke out in a sortie; Fu De and Fu Lu and others led the center army from the right, pursued the bandits across the river, and the bandits were repeatedly defeated.

entries.zh: 兆惠自葉爾羌出，至阿爾吉什，偵鄂斯璊方侵和闐，疏請富德、福祿帥師策應。
entries.en: Zhao Hui marched out from Yarkand to Arjish; when scouts reported that Esijian was invading Khotan, he memorialized asking Fu De and Fu Lu to bring troops to support him.
entries.literal: Zhao Hui came out from Yarkand to Arjish; scouts reported that Esijian was then invading Khotan; he memorialized requesting Fu De and Fu Lu to lead troops in support.

entries.zh: 上命福祿偕策布登札布以兵堵霍集占竄俄羅斯路。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Fu Lu, together with Tsebudunjab, to block Huojizhan's escape route into Russia.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Fu Lu, together with Tsebudunjab, to block with troops Huojizhan's route of flight into Russia.

entries.zh: 旋命駐軍和闐，予雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to garrison Khotan and granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to garrison Khotan and was granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 遷杭州將軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to General of Hangzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be General of Hangzhou.

entries.zh: 準噶爾平，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: After the Dzungars were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: When the Dzungars were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 上巡浙江，福祿督駐防兵肄武，制閱武詩獎之。
entries.en: During the emperor's tour of Zhejiang, Fu Lu supervised the garrison in military drill, and the emperor composed an inspection poem to reward him.
entries.literal: When the emperor toured Zhejiang, Fu Lu supervised the garrison troops in military drill; the emperor composed an inspection poem to reward him.

entries.zh: 調西安將軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to General of Xi'an.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be General of Xi'an.

entries.zh: 授領侍衛內大臣。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard.

entries.zh: 以老乞休。
entries.en: On grounds of old age he asked to retire.
entries.literal: On grounds of old age he requested retirement.

entries.zh: 卒 齊里克齊，蒙古鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: He died. Qilikeqi was a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: He died. Qilikeqi was a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 初為額魯特人，以地為氏。
entries.en: Originally an Oirat, he took his territory as his clan name.
entries.literal: Originally he was an Oirat; he took his territory as his clan name.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十年，師徵準噶爾，來降。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of the Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he came over and submitted.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Qianlong, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he came to submit.

entries.zh: 準噶爾平，從定邊將軍兆惠擊霍集占，戰於霍爾果斯。
entries.en: After the Dzungars were pacified, he followed Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui against Huojizhan and fought at Khorgos.
entries.literal: When the Dzungars were pacified, he followed Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui in attacking Huojizhan and fought at Khorgos.

entries.zh: 霍集占敗走，降頭人圖魯啟拜等，授藍翎侍衛。
entries.en: When Huojizhan was defeated and fled, he induced the headmen Turuqibai and others to surrender and was appointed Blue Plume Bodyguard.
entries.literal: When Huojizhan was defeated and fled, he induced the headmen Turuqibai and others to submit; he was appointed Blue Plume Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 護哈薩克使臣詣京師，遷三等侍衛。
entries.en: He escorted a Kazakh envoy to the capital and was promoted to third-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: He escorted a Kazakh envoy to the capital and was transferred to third-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 復從定邊右副將軍富德擊霍集占，至色勒庫爾，敵踞山以拒。
entries.en: He again followed Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De against Huojizhan; at Sarikul the enemy held the heights and resisted.
entries.literal: He again followed Pacification of the Frontier Right Vice General Fu De in attacking Huojizhan; reaching Sarikul, the enemy held the mountains to resist.

entries.zh: 齊里克齊偕前鋒參領喀木齊布督健銳營兵自山陰攀登仰擊，霍集占敗遁。
entries.en: Qilikeqi and vanguard adjutant Khamuqibu led the Vanguard Camp up the northern slope in an uphill attack; Huojizhan was defeated and fled.
entries.literal: Qilikeqi, together with vanguard adjutant Khamuqibu, directed the Vanguard Camp troops to climb from the northern slope of the mountain and attack upward; Huojizhan was defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 降所部二千餘人，獲軍器、駝騾，賜布哈巴圖魯勇號。
entries.en: More than two thousand of his followers surrendered; arms and camels were captured; and he was granted the courageous title Buhu Baturu.
entries.literal: More than two thousand of his followers submitted; military equipment and camels were captured; he was granted the courageous title Buhu Baturu.

entries.zh: 師還，命在乾清門行走，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 再遷頭等侍衛，予雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: He was again promoted to first-class bodyguard and granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to first-class bodyguard and granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 三十二年，從將軍明瑞徵緬甸，遇賊於底麻，敗之。
entries.en: In the thirty-second year he followed General Mingrui against Burma, met rebels at Dima, and defeated them.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year, he followed General Mingrui in the Burma campaign; at Dima he encountered bandits and defeated them.

entries.zh: 賜副都統銜。
entries.en: He was granted the rank of vice commandant.
entries.literal: He was granted the rank of vice commandant.

entries.zh: 召回京，再遷鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。
