entries.en: Recalled to the capital, he was again promoted to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was again promoted to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 三十七年，師徵金川，命督健銳營從參贊大臣阿桂出南路。
entries.en: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, he was ordered to lead the Vanguard Camp with campaign counselor Agui on the southern route.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, he was ordered to supervise the Vanguard Camp in following campaign counselor Agui on the southern route.

entries.zh: 授領隊大臣，攻美諾，克之。
entries.en: He was appointed column commander, attacked Meinuo, and took it.
entries.literal: He was appointed column commander, attacked Meinuo, and captured it.

entries.zh: 金川平，師還，領健銳營。
entries.en: After Jinchuan was pacified and the army returned, he commanded the Vanguard Camp.
entries.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified and the army returned, he commanded the Vanguard Camp.

entries.zh: 嘉慶初，教匪起，送察哈爾馬如湖北軍，事竟即還。
entries.en: Early in the Jiaqing reign, when sect rebels rose, he sent Chahar horses to the Hubei army and returned as soon as the affair was over.
entries.literal: Early in the Jiaqing reign, when the sect rebels rose, he sent Chahar horses to the Hubei army; when the affair was over he returned at once.

entries.zh: 上以未請從軍，詔詰責，奪官，削世職。
entries.en: Because he had not asked to join the campaign, the emperor rebuked him in edict, stripped him of office, and removed his hereditary rank.
entries.literal: Because he had not requested to join the campaign, the emperor issued an edict of reproof, stripped him of office, and removed his hereditary rank.

entries.zh: 尋授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 閻相師，字渭陽，陝西高台人。
entries.en: Yan Xiangshi, style Weiyang, was a native of Gaotai in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Yan Xiangshi, style Weiyang, was a native of Gaotai in Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 入伍。
entries.en: He enlisted.
entries.literal: He enlisted.

entries.zh: 累遷安西前營游擊。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to mobile-force commander of the front camp of Anxi.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to mobile-force commander of the front camp of Anxi.

entries.zh: 雅爾哈善謀誅厄魯特降人沙克都爾曼吉。
entries.en: Ya Erhashan plotted to execute the surrendered Oirat Shakeduer Mangji.
entries.literal: Ya Erhashan plotted to execute the surrendered Oirat Shakeduer Mangji.

entries.zh: 天大雪，相師將五百人，偽為失道，求寄宿其壘。
entries.en: In heavy snow Xiangshi led five hundred men, pretending they had lost their way, and asked to lodge in their camp.
entries.literal: Heavy snow fell; Xiangshi led five hundred men, feigning that they had lost their way, and sought lodging in their camp.

entries.zh: 夜分，鳴笳驟起，殺沙克都爾曼吉，殲其部眾四千餘人。
entries.en: At midnight they sounded horns and struck suddenly, killed Shakeduer Mangji, and wiped out more than four thousand of his followers.
entries.literal: At midnight they sounded horns and suddenly rose, killed Shakeduer Mangji, and annihilated more than four thousand of his followers.

entries.zh: 尋偕副將醜達將千人赴魯克察克同額敏和卓逐回酋莽阿里克。
entries.en: Soon after, with vice general Chouda, he led a thousand men to Lukchak to join Emin Hezhuo in driving out the Muslim chief Mang'aliq.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter, together with vice general Chouda, he led a thousand men to Lukchak to join Emin Hezhuo in driving out the Muslim chief Mang'aliq.

entries.zh: 錄功，遷金塔寺營副將。
entries.en: His merit was recorded, and he was transferred to vice general of Jinta Temple Camp.
entries.literal: His merit was recorded; he was transferred to be vice general of Jinta Temple Camp.

entries.zh: 屯田吐魯番。
entries.en: He conducted garrison farming at Turfan.
entries.literal: He conducted garrison farming at Turfan.

entries.zh: 擢甘肅肅州鎮總兵，賜花翎。
entries.en: He was promoted to regional commander of Suzhou in Gansu and granted the peacock feather.
entries.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of Suzhou in Gansu and granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 從雅爾哈善討霍集占，授領隊大臣。
entries.en: He followed Ya Erhashan against Huojizhan and was appointed column commander.
entries.literal: He followed Ya Erhashan in campaigning against Huojizhan and was appointed column commander.

entries.zh: 圍庫車，力戰被創。
entries.en: At the siege of Kuche he fought fiercely and was wounded.
entries.literal: Besieging Kuche, he fought fiercely and was wounded.

entries.zh: 師克阿克蘇，以相師駐守。
entries.en: When the army took Aksu, Xiangshi was left to garrison the city.
entries.literal: When the army captured Aksu, Xiangshi was stationed there to garrison it.

entries.zh: 已，复隨剿霍集占於葉爾羌。
entries.en: He then joined again in suppressing Huojizhan at Yarkand.
entries.literal: Thereafter he again followed in suppressing Huojizhan at Yarkand.

entries.zh: 授安西提督，駐喀什噶爾。
entries.en: He was appointed Military Governor of Anxi and garrisoned Kashgar.
entries.literal: He was appointed Military Governor of Anxi and garrisoned Kashgar.

entries.zh: 未幾，改甘肅提督，移駐庫車。
entries.en: Before long he was reassigned as Military Governor of Gansu and moved his headquarters to Kuche.
entries.literal: Before long he was changed to Military Governor of Gansu and moved his garrison to Kuche.

entries.zh: 上命屯田烏魯木齊。
entries.en: The emperor ordered garrison farming at Urumqi.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered garrison farming at Urumqi.

entries.zh: 凱旋，入覲，賚銀幣，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: On his triumphal return he was received in audience, rewarded with silver and coins, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: On the triumphal return he was received in audience, rewarded with silver and coins, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 引疾罷，予食全俸。
entries.en: He resigned citing illness and was granted full salary.
entries.literal: Citing illness he resigned; he was granted full salary.

entries.zh: 旋卒，贈太子太保，諡桓肅。
entries.en: He soon died and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Huansu.
entries.literal: He soon died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Huansu.

entries.zh: 相師軀幹修偉，有至性。
entries.en: Xiangshi was tall and imposing, with a deeply filial nature.
entries.literal: Xiangshi was tall and imposing in stature and possessed utmost filial devotion.

entries.zh: 既貴，念親不逮養，每食泣下。
entries.en: After he rose to eminence, remembering that he could no longer care for his parents in life, he wept at every meal.
entries.literal: After he rose to eminence, thinking that he could no longer care for his parents in life, he wept at every meal.

entries.zh: 得俸與兄弟，不問出入。
entries.en: He gave his salary to his brothers without keeping track of what came in or went out.
entries.literal: He gave his salary to his brothers without asking about income or expenditure.

entries.zh: 所居鎮夷堡地萬畝，為濬渠灌溉，數百家利賴之。
entries.en: At Zhenyi Fort, where he lived, he dredged canals to irrigate ten thousand mu of land, to the lasting benefit of several hundred households.
entries.literal: At Zhenyi Fort where he lived, ten thousand mu of land were irrigated by canals he dredged, to the benefit of several hundred households.

entries.zh: 伊柱，薩克達氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Yizhu, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Yizhu, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 父塔勒馬善，雍正間，以副都統將歸化城兵從征噶爾丹策淩。
entries.en: His father Tale'mashan, in the Yongzheng reign, led Guihuacheng troops as vice commandant against Galdan Tsewang.
entries.literal: His father Tale'mashan, in the Yongzheng reign, as vice commandant led Guihuacheng troops in campaigning against Galdan Tsewang.

entries.zh: 將軍達爾濟駐伯格爾，世宗命塔勒馬善參贊軍務。
entries.en: General Da'erji was garrisoned at Bo'erge, and the Shizong ordered Tale'mashan to assist in military affairs.
entries.literal: General Da'erji was garrisoned at Bo'erge; the Shizong ordered Tale'mashan to assist in military affairs.

entries.zh: 署前鋒統領，逐賊至額得爾河源，駐軍烏里雅蘇台。
entries.en: As acting vanguard commander he pursued bandits to the source of the Eder River and garrisoned Uliastai.
entries.literal: Acting as vanguard commander, he pursued bandits to the source of the Eder River and garrisoned Uliastai.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，權定邊左副將軍，召還。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he served as acting Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General and was recalled.
entries.literal: Early in Qianlong he acted as Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General and was recalled.

entries.zh: 師复徵準噶爾，命赴額爾齊斯屯田。
entries.en: When the army campaigned against the Dzungars again, he was ordered to the Irtysh for garrison farming.
entries.literal: When the army again campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to go to the Irtysh for garrison farming.

entries.zh: 二十一年，授北路參贊大臣。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Northern Route campaign counselor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Northern Route campaign counselor.

entries.zh: 復召還，授護軍統領。
entries.en: He was recalled again and appointed commander of the guards.
entries.literal: He was again recalled and appointed commander of the guards.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 伊柱，自佐領再遷索倫總管。
entries.en: Yizhu rose from assistant banner commander to Solon commander.
entries.literal: Yizhu, from assistant banner commander was again promoted to Solon commander.

entries.zh: 偕副都統濟福、侍衛德爾森保赴喀爾喀車臣部捕盜，得逋賊。
entries.en: With Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Setsen department to capture bandits and took several fugitives.
entries.literal: Together with Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Setsen department to capture bandits and obtained fugitive bandits.

entries.zh: 二十四年，從將軍兆惠討霍集占。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he followed General Zhao Hui against Huojizhan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed General Zhao Hui in campaigning against Huojizhan.

entries.zh: 霍集占之棄葉爾羌走也，副將軍富德等逐之，至阿爾楚爾。
entries.en: When Huojizhan abandoned Yarkand and fled, Vice General Fu De and others pursued him as far as Altur.
entries.literal: When Huojizhan abandoned Yarkand and fled, Vice General Fu De and others pursued him to Altur.

entries.zh: 賊設伏兩山間，師分三隊奮擊，伊柱領右翼，戰自辰至午，賊大潰。
entries.en: The rebels laid an ambush between two mountains; the army struck in three columns; Yizhu led the right wing; from morning until noon the rebels were utterly routed.
entries.literal: The bandits set an ambush between two mountains; the army divided into three columns and struck fiercely; Yizhu led the right wing; fighting from the chen hour to the wu hour, the bandits were utterly routed.

entries.zh: 翌日，至巴達克山界伊西洱庫爾淖爾，賊據險守。
entries.en: The next day they reached the Badakhshan border at Lake Yixihuku'er, where the rebels held the difficult ground and defended.
entries.literal: The next day they reached the Badakhshan border at Lake Yixihuku'er; the bandits held the terrain and defended.

entries.zh: 師分道進攻，樹白纛，降賊萬餘。
entries.en: The army attacked from several directions, raised white standards, and more than ten thousand rebels surrendered.
entries.literal: The army attacked from several routes, raised white standards, and more than ten thousand bandits submitted.

entries.zh: 伊柱偕巴圖濟爾噶勒等堵山後策應。
entries.en: Yizhu, with Batujiergale and others, blocked the mountain rear in support.
entries.literal: Yizhu, together with Batujiergale and others, blocked the rear of the mountains in support.

entries.zh: 富德遣侍衛賽音圖等諭巴達克山汗，使擒霍集占以獻。
entries.en: Fu De sent bodyguard Saiyintu and others to tell the khan of Badakhshan to seize Huojizhan and hand him over.
entries.literal: Fu De dispatched bodyguard Saiyintu and others to instruct the Badakhshan khan to seize Huojizhan and deliver him.

entries.zh: 伊柱駐兵卡倫為聲援。
entries.en: Yizhu garrisoned troops at the pass to lend support.
entries.literal: Yizhu garrisoned troops at the pass as reinforcement.

entries.zh: 瓦罕伯克率所部降。
entries.en: The beg of Wakhan led his following in submission.
entries.literal: The beg of Wakhan led his following to submit.

entries.zh: 尋，巴達克山汗素勒坦沙函獻霍集占首。
entries.en: Soon after, the khan of Badakhshan, Sultan Shah, sent Huojizhan's head in a dispatch.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter the Badakhshan khan Sultan Shah sent Huojizhan's head in a letter.

entries.zh: 回部平。
entries.en: The Muslim districts were pacified.
entries.literal: The Muslim districts were pacified.

entries.zh: 伊柱將千人駐喀什噶爾，護諸降人屯田伊犁。
entries.en: Yizhu led a thousand men to garrison Kashgar and protect the surrendered peoples farming at Ili.
entries.literal: Yizhu led a thousand men to garrison Kashgar and protect the various surrendered peoples in garrison farming at Ili.

entries.zh: 師還，上御豐澤園宴勞，賜伊柱緞十二、白金五百。
entries.en: When the army returned, the emperor feasted the troops at Fengze Garden and granted Yizhu twelve bolts of silk and five hundred taels of white silver.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the emperor feasted them at Fengze Garden; Yizhu was granted twelve bolts of silk and five hundred taels of white silver.

entries.zh: 伊柱復出領屯田，為置台守望，疏渠灌溉，農隙督佃伐木作屋以居，上諭令加意開拓。
entries.en: Yizhu went out again to lead garrison farming, set up courier stations for guard duty, dredged irrigation canals, and in farming intervals had tenants cut timber and build houses; the emperor instructed him to press on with development.
entries.literal: Yizhu again went out to lead garrison farming, established courier stations for guard and watch, dredged canals for irrigation, and in farming intervals supervised tenants in felling timber to build houses for dwelling; the emperor instructed him to devote himself to development.

entries.zh: 遷鑲藍旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He was transferred to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 從將軍明瑞徵緬甸，擊賊老官屯。
entries.en: He followed General Mingrui against Burma and attacked rebels at Laoguantun.
entries.literal: He followed General Mingrui in the Burma campaign and attacked bandits at Laoguantun.

entries.zh: 卒於軍，進三等輕車都尉世職。
entries.en: He died on campaign and was advanced to a hereditary third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
entries.literal: He died in the army and was advanced to a hereditary third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

entries.zh: 努三，瓜爾佳氏，吉林滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Nusan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Jilin Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Nusan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Jilin Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 自前鋒再遷頭等侍衛、御前行走。
entries.en: He rose from vanguard to first-class bodyguard and served in the imperial presence.
entries.literal: From vanguard he was again promoted to first-class bodyguard and served in the imperial presence.

entries.zh: 乾隆十一年，四川總督慶復剿下瞻對頭人班滾，命努三如慶復軍。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of the Qianlong reign, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zhandui chief Banbo, and Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Qianlong, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zhandui chief Banbo; Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.

entries.zh: 慶復疏報班滾焚死，罷兵。
entries.en: Qingfu reported that Banbo had burned himself to death, and the troops were withdrawn.
entries.literal: Qingfu memorialized that Banbo had burned himself to death and the troops were withdrawn.

entries.zh: 張廣泗代慶復，言班滾現在。
entries.en: Zhang Guangsi replaced Qingfu and reported that Banbo was still alive.
entries.literal: Zhang Guangsi replaced Qingfu and reported that Banbo was still alive.

entries.zh: 慶復坐得罪，努三罷御前行走。
entries.en: Qingfu was punished; Nusan was dismissed from service in the imperial presence.
entries.literal: Qingfu was found guilty; Nusan was dismissed from service in the imperial presence.

entries.zh: 尋授鑲白旗蒙古副都統、正藍旗護軍統領。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner and commander of the guards of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner and commander of the guards of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 十八年，師徵準噶爾，命從湖廣總督永常籌軍事。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to assist Huguang governor-general Yongchang in military preparations.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to join Huguang governor-general Yongchang in preparing military affairs.

entries.zh: 旋帥師駐鄂爾坤。
entries.en: He soon led troops to garrison the Orkhon.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he led troops to garrison the Orkhon.

entries.zh: 準噶爾宰桑瑪木特闌入卡倫。
entries.en: The Dzungar zaisang Mamut broke through the border pass.
entries.literal: The Dzungar zaisang Mamut broke through the pass.

entries.zh: 授參贊大臣，命會將軍成袞札布逐捕。
entries.en: He was appointed campaign counselor and ordered to join General Chenggunjab in pursuit and capture.
entries.literal: He was appointed campaign counselor and ordered to join General Chenggunjab in pursuit and capture.

entries.zh: 努三與參贊大臣薩賴爾、護軍統領烏勒登合軍，軍不戢，雜取牲畜。
entries.en: Nusan joined campaign counselor Salai'er and guards commander Wuleideng; their combined troops were undisciplined and seized livestock indiscriminately.
entries.literal: Nusan joined campaign counselor Salai'er and guards commander Wuleideng in combining armies; the troops were undisciplined and indiscriminately took livestock.

entries.zh: 努三獲逃人特赫拜哈都，未聞上。
entries.en: Nusan captured the fugitive Tekebai Hadu but did not report it to the emperor.
entries.literal: Nusan captured the fugitive Tekebai Hadu but did not report it to the emperor.

entries.zh: 烏勒登收烏梁海，縱逃人巴朗。
entries.en: Wuleideng took in the Urianghai but released the fugitive Balang.
entries.literal: Wuleideng received the Urianghai but released the fugitive Balang.

entries.zh: 上詰責努三、烏勒登，下定北將軍班第等按治。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked Nusan and Wuleideng and ordered Pacification of the North General Bandi and others to investigate and punish them.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Nusan and Wuleideng and ordered Pacification of the North General Bandi and others to investigate and punish them.

entries.zh: 努三、烏勒登自陳收牲畜匿以自私事始薩賴爾，上以薩賴爾新降，不知法度，責努三等不得以此諉過。
entries.en: Nusan and Wuleideng admitted that the seizure and concealment of livestock for private gain had begun with Salai'er; the emperor held that Salai'er had only recently submitted and did not know the regulations, and rebuked Nusan and the others for trying to shift the blame onto him.
entries.literal: Nusan and Wuleideng themselves stated that the matter of seizing livestock and concealing them for private gain had begun with Salai'er; the emperor held that Salai'er had only recently submitted and did not know the law, and rebuked Nusan and the others for shifting the blame onto him.

entries.zh: 尋讞上，坐失巴朗，罪當斬。
entries.en: When the case was submitted, losing Balang was judged a capital offense.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter the judgment was submitted; for losing Balang the offense warranted execution.

entries.zh: 詔錄其前勞，恕死，留軍，仍籍其家。
entries.en: An edict took account of their earlier merit, spared their lives, kept them with the army, but still registered their households for punishment.
entries.literal: An edict recorded their former merit, pardoned death, kept them with the army, but still registered their households for punishment.

entries.zh: 旋授藍翎侍衛。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Blue Plume Bodyguard.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Blue Plume Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 再遷頭等侍衛，命與左都御史何國宗赴伊犁，測天度，繪地圖。
entries.en: He was again promoted to first-class bodyguard and ordered, with Left Censor-in-Chief He Guozong, to go to Ili to measure celestial degrees and draw maps.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to first-class bodyguard and ordered, together with Left Censor-in-Chief He Guozong, to go to Ili to measure celestial degrees and draw maps.

entries.zh: 送兵詣巴里坤，請回京。
entries.en: After escorting troops to Barkol, he asked to return to the capital.
entries.literal: He escorted troops to Barkol and requested to return to the capital.

entries.zh: 左授藍翎侍衛，留巴里坤差遣。
entries.en: He was demoted to Blue Plume Bodyguard and left at Barkol on assignment.
entries.literal: He was demoted to Blue Plume Bodyguard and left at Barkol on assignment.

entries.zh: 招撫巴爾達穆特各鄂拓克有勞，三遷鑲藍旗護軍統領，督巴里坤屯田。
entries.en: For merit in pacifying the various otoks of the Bardanmut, he was promoted three ranks to commander of the guards of the Bordered Blue Banner and supervised garrison farming at Barkol.
entries.literal: For merit in inducing and comforting the various otoks of the Bardanmut, he was promoted three ranks to commander of the guards of the Bordered Blue Banner and supervised garrison farming at Barkol.

entries.zh: 兆惠被圍黑水，努三從定邊左副將軍富德往援，至呼爾璊，分兩翼擊賊，與兆惠軍會，賜騎都尉世職。
entries.en: When Zhao Hui was besieged at Black Water, Nusan followed Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Fu De to his relief; at Hu'erlan they struck the rebels in two wings, united with Zhao Hui's army, and Nusan was granted a hereditary Cavalry Captaincy.
entries.literal: When Zhao Hui was besieged at Black Water, Nusan followed Pacification of the Frontier Left Vice General Fu De to the relief; reaching Hu'erlan, they divided into two wings to attack the bandits, joined Zhao Hui's army, and he was granted a hereditary Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 師還，賜銀幣。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was rewarded with silver and coins.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was rewarded with silver and coins.

entries.zh: 累遷領侍衛內大臣、正藍旗滿洲都統。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard and Manchu commander of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard and Manchu commander of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 卒，諡恪靖。
entries.en: He died and was given the posthumous title Kejing.
entries.literal: He died; he was given the posthumous title Kejing.

entries.zh: 烏勒登，烏禮蘇氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Wuleideng, of the Ulisu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Wuleideng, of the Ulisu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 自前鋒累遷鑲黃旗蒙古副都統、護軍統​​領。
entries.en: He rose from vanguard to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner and commander of the guards.
entries.literal: From vanguard he was promoted in succession to Mongol vice commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner and commander of the guards.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年，從征金川。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of the Qianlong reign he took part in the campaign against Jinchuan.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, he accompanied the campaign against Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 經略大學士傅恆至軍，令駐軍馬奈。
entries.en: When Grand Secretary and Pacification Commissioner Fu Heng reached the army, he ordered troops garrisoned at Manai.
entries.literal: When Grand Secretary and Pacification Commissioner Fu Heng reached the army, he ordered troops garrisoned at Manai.

entries.zh: 十八年，師徵準噶爾，授參贊大臣，駐烏里雅蘇台。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was appointed campaign counselor and garrisoned at Uliastai.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was appointed campaign counselor and garrisoned at Uliastai.

entries.zh: 扎哈沁宰桑瑪木特等闌入卡倫，烏勒登偕喀爾喀副都統策登扎卜將五百人，與參贊大臣努三分道捕治。
entries.en: When the Zahachin zaisang Mamut and others broke through the pass, Wuleideng and Khalkha Vice Commandant Tserengjab led five hundred men and, with campaign counselor Nusan, pursued them by separate routes.
entries.literal: The Zahachin zaisang Mamut and others broke through the pass; Wuleideng, together with Khalkha Vice Commandant Tserengjab, led five hundred men and, with campaign counselor Nusan, pursued and punished them by separate routes.

entries.zh: 參贊大臣薩賴爾收烏梁海，烏勒登自索郭克策應，俘獲甚眾。
entries.en: When campaign counselor Salai'er took in the Urianghai, Wuleideng supported him from Suogoke and captured a great many.
entries.literal: Campaign counselor Salai'er received the Urianghai; Wuleideng supported him from Suogoke and captured a great many.

entries.zh: 尋坐縱逃人巴朗，並與努三匿所獲烏梁海牲畜，罪當斬，貸死從軍。
entries.en: Soon after, for releasing the fugitive Balang and, with Nusan, concealing Urianghai livestock they had seized, he was sentenced to death; the sentence was commuted and he remained with the army.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter, for releasing the fugitive Balang and, together with Nusan, concealing Urianghai livestock they had obtained, the offense warranted execution; death was commuted and he remained with the army.

entries.zh: 尋授頭等侍衛，命選厄魯特宰桑厄勒錐音等兵赴伊犁討賊。
entries.en: He was soon appointed first-class bodyguard and ordered to select Oirat zaisang Elechuin and other troops for the campaign against bandits at Ili.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed first-class bodyguard and ordered to select Oirat zaisang Elechuin and other troops to go to Ili to suppress bandits.

entries.zh: 加副都統銜，授領隊大臣，進剿阿巴噶斯、哈丹等游牧。
entries.en: He was granted the rank of vice commandant, appointed column commander, and advanced against the pastures of Abagasi, Hadan, and others.
entries.literal: He was given the rank of vice commandant, appointed column commander, and advanced to suppress the pastures of Abagasi, Hadan, and others.

entries.zh: 阿睦爾撒納竄哈薩克，定西將軍策楞遣烏勒登將千人從參贊大臣玉保逐捕，玉保中道引還。
entries.en: When Amursana fled into Kazakh lands, Pacification of the West General Celeng sent Wuleideng with a thousand men to join campaign counselor Yubao in pursuit; Yubao turned back halfway.
entries.literal: Amursana fled into Kazakh territory; Pacification of the West General Celeng dispatched Wuleideng to lead a thousand men with campaign counselor Yubao in pursuit; Yubao turned back midway.

entries.zh: 烏勒登師至庫隴癸嶺，阿睦爾撒納脫走。
entries.en: When Wuleideng's army reached Kulungui Ridge, Amursana got away.
entries.literal: When Wuleideng's army reached Kulungui Ridge, Amursana escaped.

entries.zh: 逮詣京師，廷鞫，言：「初聞阿睦爾撒納遁，請發兵速追之。
entries.en: Brought to the capital and tried at court, he said: "When I first heard that Amursana had fled, I asked that troops be sent at once in rapid pursuit.
entries.literal: He was brought to the capital and tried at court, where he said: "When I first heard that Amursana had fled, I requested troops be sent at once in rapid pursuit.

entries.zh: 策楞、玉保俱不允。
entries.en: Celeng and Yubao both refused.
entries.literal: Celeng and Yubao both refused.

entries.zh: 後從玉保往，復請追擊。
entries.en: Later, when I followed Yubao, I again asked to pursue.
entries.literal: Later, when I followed Yubao, I again requested pursuit.

entries.zh: 玉保止發兵五十，至庫隴癸嶺，僅餘二十人，駝复乏。
entries.en: Yubao sent only fifty men; by the time we reached Kulungui Ridge only twenty remained, and camels were again in short supply.
entries.literal: Yubao sent only fifty troops; when we reached Kulungui Ridge, only twenty men remained, and camels were again scarce.

entries.zh: 阿睦爾撒納於師行日已過嶺竄哈薩克。」
entries.en: Amursana had already crossed the ridge and fled into Kazakh territory on the day our army marched."
entries.literal: Amursana had already crossed the ridge and fled into Kazakh territory on the day our army marched."

entries.zh: 上以其言實，貸死，授三等侍衛，在乾清門行走。
entries.en: The emperor found his account truthful, commuted the death sentence, appointed him third-class bodyguard, and ordered him to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
entries.literal: The emperor held his account to be true, commuted death, appointed him third-class bodyguard, and ordered him to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

entries.zh: 尋仍遣赴軍。
entries.en: He was soon sent back to the army.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was again sent to the army.

entries.zh: 定邊將軍兆惠招降布勒特部頭目圖魯啟拜，令烏勒登自珠木罕至圖固斯塔老宣詔，護降人入覲。
entries.en: Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui induced the Burut leader Turuqibai to submit and ordered Wuleideng from Zhumuhan to Tugustalao to proclaim the edict and escort the surrendered people to audience.
entries.literal: Pacification of the Frontier General Zhao Hui induced the Burut leader Turuqibai to submit; he ordered Wuleideng from Zhumuhan to Tugustalao to proclaim the edict and escort the surrendered people to audience.

entries.zh: 擢頭等侍衛，授參贊大臣。
entries.en: He was promoted to first-class bodyguard and appointed campaign counselor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to first-class bodyguard and appointed campaign counselor.

entries.zh: 令捕瑪哈沁，並截霍集占逃路。
entries.en: He was ordered to capture Mahaqin and cut off Huojizhan's escape route.
entries.literal: He was ordered to capture Mahaqin and also cut off Huojizhan's escape route.

entries.zh: 尋以捕瑪哈沁不力，令在領隊大臣上行走。
entries.en: Soon after, for failing to capture Mahaqin effectively, he was ordered to serve in the capacity of a column commander.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter, for ineffective pursuit of Mahaqin, he was ordered to serve in the capacity of column commander.

entries.zh: 師還，累遷鑲黃旗蒙古都統、左翼前鋒統領。
entries.en: When the army returned, he rose to Mongol commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted in succession to Mongol commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 論曰：從兆惠、富德討霍集占有功諸將校，若瑚爾起、愛隆阿殲敵搴旗，見於詠歌，厥績懋焉。
entries.en: The historian remarks: Among the officers who followed Zhao Hui and Fu De against Huojizhan and distinguished themselves—men such as Hu Erqi and Ai Long'a, who destroyed the enemy and seized standards, celebrated in song—their achievements were truly great.
entries.literal: The historian remarks: Among the officers who followed Zhao Hui and Fu De in campaigning against Huojizhan and won merit, such as Hu Erqi and Ai Long'a, who destroyed the enemy and seized standards—celebrated in song—their achievements were truly great.

entries.zh: 舒明逐叛拊降，以勞受爵。
entries.en: Shu Ming pursued rebels and comforted those who surrendered, and was ennobled for his labors.
entries.literal: Shu Ming pursued rebels and comforted those who submitted, and received a noble rank for his labors.

entries.zh: 福祿、努三與呼爾璊之役，齊里克齊佐色勒庫爾之戰，相師助庫車之圍，伊柱收伊西洱之降，錄功皆居最，抑亦其次也。
entries.en: Fu Lu and Nusan at Hu'erlan, Qilikeqi at Sarikul, Xiangshi at the siege of Kuche, Yizhu at the surrender at Yixihuer—in the recording of merit they all ranked at the top, yet they were still second to those named above.
entries.literal: Fu Lu and Nusan at the battle of Hu'erlan, Qilikeqi assisting at the battle of Sarikul, Xiangshi aiding the siege of Kuche, Yizhu receiving the submission at Yixihuer—in recording merit they all ranked foremost, yet they were still second in rank.

entries.zh: 范毓皛，山西介休人。
entries.en: Fan Yuxiao was a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Fan Yuxiao, a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 范氏故巨富。
entries.en: The Fan clan had long been immensely wealthy.
entries.literal: The Fan clan was formerly immensely wealthy.

entries.zh: 康熙中，師徵準噶爾，輸米餽軍，率以百二十金致一石。
entries.en: Under Kangxi, when armies campaigned against the Dzungars, the family supplied grain to the troops, generally at a cost of one hundred and twenty taels of silver per picul.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi period, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, they supplied grain to feed the troops, generally at a cost of one hundred and twenty taels per picul.

entries.zh: 六十年，再出師，毓皛兄毓馪請以家財轉餉，受運值視官運三之一。
entries.en: In the sixtieth year, when troops marched out again, Yuxiao's elder brother Yushen offered family wealth to transport provisions and was paid carriage fees at one-third of the official rate.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year, when the army marched out again, Yuxiao's elder brother Yushen asked to transport provisions with family wealth and received transport fees at one-third of official rates.

entries.zh: 雍正間，師出西北二路，怡親王允祥薦毓馪主餉，計穀多寡，程道路遠近，以次受值，凡石米自十一兩五錢至二十五兩有差，累年運米百餘萬石。
entries.en: In the Yongzheng reign, when armies marched by the two northwest routes, Prince Yi Yinxiang recommended Yushen to manage supplies; fees were set by grain volume and distance, ranging from eleven taels five mace to twenty-five taels per picul, and over the years he transported more than a million piculs of grain.
entries.literal: In the Yongzheng period, when armies took the two northwest routes, Prince Yi Yinxiang recommended Yushen to manage provisions; grain amounts and distances were calculated and fees taken in order—from eleven taels five mace to twenty-five taels per picul—and over successive years more than a million piculs of grain were transported.

entries.zh: 世宗特賜太僕寺卿銜，章服同二品。
entries.en: The Yongzheng Emperor specially granted him the rank of Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with insignia and dress of the second rank.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor specially granted him the rank of Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with insignia and dress equal to the second rank.

entries.zh: 寇犯北路，失米十三萬餘石，毓馪斥私財補運，凡白金百四十四萬。
entries.en: When raiders struck the northern route and more than one hundred thirty thousand piculs of grain were lost, Yushen spent private funds to make up the shipments, totaling one million four hundred forty thousand taels of silver.
entries.literal: When the enemy invaded the northern route and more than one hundred thirty thousand piculs of grain were lost, Yushen spent private wealth to make up the transport, altogether one million four hundred forty thousand taels of silver.

entries.zh: 師既罷，米轉運近地，戶部按近值核銷，故所受遠值，責毓馪追繳，凡白金二百六十二萬，復出私財採蓡，市銅供鑄錢以償。
entries.en: After the campaign ended, grain was moved to nearby depots and the Board of Revenue settled accounts at local rates; Yushen was therefore ordered to repay the difference on distant hauls—two million six hundred twenty thousand taels in all—and again spent private funds gathering ginseng and buying copper for minting to meet the debt.
entries.literal: After the campaign ended, grain was transported to nearby places and the Board of Revenue audited payment at nearby rates; therefore the higher fees received for distant transport were charged back to Yushen for recovery—two million six hundred twenty thousand taels of silver in all—and he again spent private wealth gathering ginseng and buying copper to supply coinage for repayment.

entries.zh: 譚行義，四川三台人。
entries.en: Tan Xingyi was a native of Santai in Sichuan.
entries.literal: Tan Xingyi, a native of Santai in Sichuan.

entries.zh: 康熙時，以武舉授陝西西寧衛千總。
entries.en: Under Kangxi, as a military licentiate he was appointed company captain of the Xining guard in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi period, as a military licentiate he was appointed company captain of the Xining guard in Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 雍正初，從軍平青海，再遷河南城守營參將。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he campaigned in Qinghai and was promoted to colonel of the Henan garrison battalion.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he followed the army to pacify Qinghai and was again promoted to colonel of the Henan garrison battalion.

entries.zh: 河東總督田文鏡劾行義送陝西軍馬疲瘦，奪官，上令來京引見，召對稱旨，賜編刻上諭、貂皮、香珠，復原官。
entries.en: Hedong Governor-General Tian Wenjing impeached him for delivering worn and emaciated Shaanxi army horses; he was dismissed, but the emperor summoned him to the capital. His answers in audience pleased the throne, and he received engraved imperial pronouncements, sable fur, and fragrant pearls; his rank was restored.
entries.literal: Hedong Governor-General Tian Wenjing impeached Xingyi for delivering Shaanxi army horses worn and thin; his office was taken, but the emperor ordered him to the capital for audience; his responses pleased the throne, and he was given engraved imperial pronouncements, sable fur, and fragrant pearls, and his post was restored.

entries.zh: 再遷廣東高雷廉總兵。
entries.en: He was promoted again to regional commander of the Gaolei and Lian garrisons in Guangdong.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to regional commander of Gaolei and Lian in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 總督鄂彌達檄行義將五千人協剿貴州亂苗，進擊滾縱、高表諸寨。
entries.en: Governor-General E'ermida ordered Xingyi to lead five thousand men against rebellious Miao in Guizhou and to assault the stockades of Gunzong, Gaobiao, and others.
entries.literal: Governor-General E'ermida ordered Xingyi to lead five thousand men in joint suppression of rebellious Miao in Guizhou and advance against the stockades of Gunzong, Gaobiao, and others.

entries.zh: 經略張廣泗令赴援上江，攻烏婆、擺吊諸險要地，搜牛皮大箐，獲其魁。
entries.en: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi sent him to reinforce the upper river, storm the strongpoints of Wupo and Baidiao, comb Niupi Daqing, and capture the rebel leader.
entries.literal: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi ordered him to reinforce the upper river, attack the strategic places of Wupo and Baidiao, search Niupi Daqing, and capture their chieftain.

entries.zh: 歷福建漳州、湖南鎮筸諸鎮。
entries.en: He served in turn as commander at Zhangzhou in Fujian and at Zhenbian in Hunan.
entries.literal: He served in turn at the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian and the Zhenbian garrison in Hunan.

entries.zh: 毓皛以武舉授衛千總，以駝佐軍，擢守備。
entries.en: Yuxiao entered service as a military licentiate appointed company captain of a guard; he supplied camels to the army and was promoted to garrison commander.
entries.literal: Yuxiao, as a military licentiate, was appointed company captain of a guard; he assisted the army with camels and was promoted to garrison commander.

entries.zh: 累遷直隸天津鎮總兵。
entries.en: He rose through several posts to regional commander of the Tianjin garrison in Zhili.
entries.literal: He was promoted through several posts to regional commander of the Tianjin garrison in Zhili.

entries.zh: 自河南河北鎮移廣東潮州，疏請令潮州營兵如河北例，兼習長槍、短棍、連接棍諸藝。
entries.en: Transferred from the Henan–Hebei garrison to Chaozhou in Guangdong, he memorialized asking that Chaozhou troops, following the Hebei precedent, also drill in long spear, short staff, and linked staff.
entries.literal: Transferred from the Henan–Hebei garrison to Chaozhou in Guangdong, he memorialized asking that Chaozhou garrison troops, following the Hebei precedent, also train in long spear, short staff, and linked staff.

entries.zh: 世宗命與總督鄂彌達、提督張溥商榷。
entries.en: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered him to consult Governor-General E'ermida and Provincial Commander Zhang Pu.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor ordered consultation with Governor-General E'ermida and Provincial Commander Zhang Pu.

entries.zh: 鄂彌達等上言：「廣東山海交錯，軍械惟鳥槍最宜，次則弓箭、藤牌、挑刀、大砲。
entries.en: E'ermida and others reported: "Guangdong's terrain mixes mountain and sea; muskets suit it best, followed by bows, rattan shields, pole blades, and cannon.
entries.literal: E'ermida and others reported: "Guangdong's mountains and sea interweave; among arms the musket is most suitable, next bows and arrows, rattan shields, pole blades, and cannon.

entries.zh: 毓皛所議與廣東不甚宜。」
entries.en: Yuxiao's proposal is not well suited to Guangdong."
entries.literal: What Yuxiao proposed is not very suitable for Guangdong."

entries.zh: 上韙鄂彌達等議，仍諭毓皛初至，當嘉其肯言。
entries.en: The emperor sided with E'ermida but still told Yuxiao that, as a newcomer, his willingness to speak out deserved praise.
entries.literal: The emperor approved E'ermida's view but still instructed that since Yuxiao had just arrived, his willingness to speak should be commended.

entries.zh: 嘉應、潮陽遇颶，海岸決。
entries.en: Jiaying and Chaoyang were struck by typhoons and the sea walls gave way.
entries.literal: Jiaying and Chaoyang were struck by typhoons and the coast broke.

entries.zh: 毓皛以聞，命加意撫綏。
entries.en: Yuxiao reported the disaster and was ordered to give special attention to relief and pacification.
entries.literal: Yuxiao reported it and was ordered to give special care to relief and pacification.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，署廣東提督。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he served as acting provincial military commander of Guangdong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he acted as provincial military commander of Guangdong.

entries.zh: 故事，市舶至，詣海關納稅。
entries.en: By precedent, trading ships paid duties at the customs house on arrival.
entries.literal: By precedent, when trading ships arrived they went to the customs house to pay tax.

entries.zh: 或遇風未至所往地，中道暫泊，亦論稅如例。
entries.en: If storms kept them from their destination and they anchored en route, duties were still assessed as usual.
entries.literal: If wind held them from their destination and they anchored midway, tax was still assessed as usual.

entries.zh: 毓皛慮民避屢稅，遇風不敢泊，致傾覆，疏請商舟寄泊，非即地市易不徵稅，上命待審察。
entries.en: Yuxiao feared merchants would avoid repeated duties, refuse to anchor in storms, and capsize; he memorialized that temporary anchorage should be tax-free unless goods were sold on the spot, and the emperor ordered the proposal held for review.
entries.literal: Yuxiao feared that people would avoid repeated taxation and, meeting wind, dare not anchor and so capsize; he memorialized asking that merchant vessels be allowed to anchor temporarily without tax unless they traded on the spot, and the emperor ordered the matter held for review.

entries.zh: 毓皛以憂歸，服終，授直隸正定鎮總兵。
entries.en: Yuxiao returned home to mourn; after the mourning period he was appointed regional commander of the Zhengding garrison in Zhili.
entries.literal: Yuxiao returned home for mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed regional commander of the Zhengding garrison in Zhili.

entries.zh: 湖廣總督阿爾賽請移任苗疆，上不允，諭以「毓皛富家子弟，謹慎無過。
entries.en: Huguang Governor-General A'ersai asked that he be transferred to the Miao frontier; the emperor refused, saying: "Yuxiao is a wealthy man's son—careful and without fault.
entries.literal: Huguang Governor-General A'ersai asked that he be transferred to the Miao frontier; the emperor did not agree and instructed: "Yuxiao is the son of a wealthy family, cautious and without fault.

entries.zh: 苗疆事重，不能勝也」。
entries.en: Miao frontier affairs are too weighty for him to bear."
entries.literal: Miao frontier affairs are weighty; he cannot bear the burden."

entries.zh: 上巡五台，毓皛言兄毓馪子清注具羊千、馬十備賞賚，上卻之。
entries.en: During the emperor's tour of Wutai, Yuxiao reported that his brother Yushen's son Qingzhu had prepared a thousand sheep and ten horses as gifts; the emperor declined them.
entries.literal: When the emperor toured Wutai, Yuxiao said that his brother Yushen's son Qingzhu had prepared a thousand sheep and ten horses as gifts for bestowal; the emperor declined them.

entries.zh: 尋以老罷。
entries.en: He soon retired on account of age.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he retired because of age.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 范毓皛
entries.en: Fan Yuxiao
entries.literal: Fan Yuxiao

entries.zh: 于敏中，字叔子，江蘇金壇人。
entries.en: Yu Minzhong, whose style name was Shuzi, was a native of Jintan in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong, style name Shuzi, was a native of Jintan in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 乾隆三年一甲一名進士，授翰林院修撰。
entries.en: In Qianlong 3 he placed first in the palace examination and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he passed the palace examination as first in the first rank and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

entries.zh: 以文翰受高宗知，直懋勤殿，敕書華嚴、楞嚴兩經。
entries.en: His literary ability won the Gaozong Emperor's notice; he served at the Maoqin Hall and was ordered to copy the Avatamsaka and Surangama Sutras.
entries.literal: Through his literary skill he won the Gaozong Emperor's notice, served duty at the Maoqin Hall, and was ordered to copy the Avatamsaka and Surangama Sutras.

entries.zh: 累遷侍講，典山西鄉試，督山東、浙江學政。
entries.en: He rose to reader-in-waiting, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, and served as educational commissioner of Shandong and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to reader-in-waiting, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, and served as educational commissioner of Shandong and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 十五年，直上書房。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was assigned to the Upper Study.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he entered the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 累遷內閣學士。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat bachelor.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat bachelor.

entries.zh: 十八年，复督山東學政。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he again served as educational commissioner of Shandong.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he again served as educational commissioner of Shandong.

entries.zh: 擢兵部侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice minister of War.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of War.

entries.zh: 二十一年，丁本生父憂，歸宗持服。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he mourned his biological father's death and returned to his clan to observe mourning.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he mourned the death of his biological father and returned to his clan to observe mourning.

entries.zh: 逾年，起署刑部侍郎。
entries.en: After a year he was recalled to serve as acting vice minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: After a year he was recalled to serve in an acting capacity as vice minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 二十三年，嗣父枋歿，回籍治喪。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year his adoptive father Fang died, and he returned home to manage the funeral.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year his adoptive father Fang died, and he returned home to manage the funeral.

entries.zh: 未幾，丁本生母憂，未以上聞。
entries.en: Before long he mourned his biological mother's death but did not report it to the throne.
entries.literal: Before long he mourned the death of his biological mother but did not report it to the throne.

entries.zh: 御史朱嵇疏劾敏中「兩次親喪，蒙混為一，恝然赴官」。
entries.en: Censor Zhu Ji memorialized to impeach Minzhong, saying, "Having twice suffered parental bereavement, he conflated the two cases and callously took office."
entries.literal: Censor Zhu Ji memorialized impeaching Minzhong: "Having twice suffered parental bereavement, he conflated the two cases and callously took office."

entries.zh: 並言：「部臣與疆臣異，不宜奪情任事。」
entries.en: He also said, "Ministers at court differ from frontier officials; it is improper to set aside mourning and take office."
entries.literal: He also said: "Ministers at court differ from frontier officials; it is improper to set aside mourning and take office."

entries.zh: 詔原之。
entries.en: An edict pardoned him.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned him.

entries.zh: 尋實授。
entries.en: He soon received formal appointment.
entries.literal: Soon he received formal appointment.

entries.zh: 調戶部，管錢法堂事。
entries.en: He was transferred to the Board of Revenue and managed affairs of the Money Standards Office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Revenue and managed affairs of the Money Standards Office.

entries.zh: 二十五年，命為軍機大臣。
entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed a Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed a Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 敏中敏捷過人，承旨得上意。
entries.en: Minzhong was exceptionally quick-witted and, in drafting edicts, won the emperor's approval.
entries.literal: Minzhong was exceptionally quick-witted and, in drafting edicts, won the emperor's approval.

entries.zh: 三十年，擢戶部尚書。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 子齊賢，鄉試未中式。
entries.en: His son Qixian failed to pass the provincial examination.
entries.literal: His son Qixian failed to pass the provincial examination.

entries.zh: 詔以敏中久直內廷，僅一子年已及壯，加恩依尚書品級予廕生。
entries.en: An edict stated that because Minzhong had long served in the inner court and had only one grown son, he was granted the privilege of yinsheng appointment according to a minister's rank.
entries.literal: An edict stated that because Minzhong had long served in the inner court and had only one son already grown, grace was granted to award him a yinsheng privilege according to a minister's rank.

entries.zh: 又以敏中正室前卒，特封其妾張為淑人。
entries.en: Because Minzhong's principal wife had died earlier, his concubine Zhang was specially ennobled as Lady Shuren.
entries.literal: Because Minzhong's principal wife had died earlier, his concubine Zhang was specially ennobled as Lady Shuren.

entries.zh: 三十三年，加太子太保。
entries.en: In the thirty-third year he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 三十六年，協辦大學士。
entries.en: In the thirty-sixth year he became associate grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he became associate grand secretary.

entries.zh: 三十八年，晉文華殿大學士，兼戶部尚書如故。
entries.en: In the thirty-eighth year he was advanced to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall while continuing as minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was advanced to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall while continuing as minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 時下詔徵遺書，安徽學政朱筠請開局搜輯永樂大典中古書。
entries.en: At that time an edict called for collecting lost books; Zhu Yun, educational commissioner of Anhui, requested that a bureau be opened to search out and compile ancient books from the Yongle Encyclopedia.
entries.literal: At that time an edict called for collecting lost books; Zhu Yun, educational commissioner of Anhui, requested that a bureau be opened to search out and compile ancient books from the Yongle Encyclopedia.

entries.zh: 大學士劉統勳謂非政要，欲寢其議。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun said it was not a governmental priority and wished to shelve the proposal.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun said it was not a matter of governmental priority and wished to shelve the proposal.

entries.zh: 敏中善筠奏，與統勳力爭，於是特開四庫全書館，命敏中為正總裁，主其事。
entries.en: Minzhong approved Zhu Yun's memorial and argued strenuously with Tongxun; the Siku Quanshu Bureau was then specially opened, and Minzhong was appointed chief director to preside over the project.
entries.literal: Minzhong approved Zhu Yun's memorial and argued strenuously with Tongxun; thereupon the Siku Quanshu Bureau was specially opened, and Minzhong was appointed chief director to preside over the project.

entries.zh: 又充國史館、三通館正總裁。
entries.en: He also served as chief director of the State Historiography Bureau and the Santong Bureau.
entries.literal: He also served as chief director of the State Historiography Bureau and the Santong Bureau.

entries.zh: 屢典會試，命為上書房總師傅，兼翰林院掌院學士。
entries.en: He repeatedly presided over the metropolitan examination and was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, while also serving as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: He repeatedly presided over the metropolitan examination and was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, while also serving as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 敏中為軍機大臣久，頗接外吏，通聲氣。
entries.en: Minzhong had long been a Grand Councilor and frequently received outside officials, maintaining channels of communication.
entries.literal: Minzhong had long been a Grand Councilor and frequently received outside officials, maintaining channels of communication.

entries.zh: 三十九年，內監高雲從漏洩硃批道府記載，下廷臣鞫治。
entries.en: In the thirty-ninth year the eunuch Gao Yuncong leaked vermilion-annotated records of prefectural and circuit appointments, and court ministers were ordered to investigate.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year the eunuch Gao Yuncong leaked vermilion-annotated records of prefectural and circuit appointments, and court ministers were ordered to investigate.

entries.zh: 雲從言敏中嘗向詢問記載，及雲從買地涉訟，嘗乞敏中囑託府尹蔣賜棨。
entries.en: Yuncong said Minzhong had once asked him about the records, and that when Yuncong became involved in a lawsuit over a land purchase he had begged Minzhong to entreat Prefect Jiang Ciqi on his behalf.
entries.literal: Yuncong said Minzhong had once asked him about the records, and that when Yuncong became involved in a lawsuit over land purchase he had begged Minzhong to entreat the prefect Jiang Ciqi on his behalf.

entries.zh: 上面詰，敏中引罪，詔切責之曰：「內廷諸臣與內監交涉，一言及私，即當據實奏聞。
entries.en: The emperor questioned him in person; Minzhong confessed guilt, and an edict sternly rebuked him, saying, "When inner-court ministers deal with eunuchs, if a single word touches private affairs, they must report it truthfully to the throne.
entries.literal: The emperor questioned him in person; Minzhong confessed guilt, and an edict sternly rebuked him, saying: "When inner-court ministers deal with eunuchs, if a single word touches private affairs, they must report it truthfully to the throne.

entries.zh: 朕方嘉其持正，重治若輩之罪，豈肯轉咎奏參者？
entries.en: I would praise such uprightness and severely punish those offenders—how could I turn and blame the one who memorialized?
entries.literal: I would praise such uprightness and severely punish those offenders—how could I turn and blame the one who memorialized?

entries.zh: 於敏中侍朕左右有年，豈尚不知朕而為此隱忍耶？
entries.en: Yu Minzhong has attended at my side for years—can he still not know me and yet practice such concealment?
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong has attended at my side for years—can he still not know me and yet practice such concealment?

entries.zh: 於敏中日蒙召對，朕何所不言？
entries.en: Yu Minzhong is summoned to audience daily—what do I not speak of?
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong is summoned to audience daily—what do I not speak of?

entries.zh: 何至轉向內監探詢消息？
entries.en: Why turn instead to eunuchs to probe for news?
entries.literal: Why turn instead to eunuchs to probe for news?

entries.zh: 自川省用兵以來，敏中承旨有勞。
entries.en: Since military operations began in Sichuan, Minzhong has had merit in drafting edicts.
entries.literal: Since military operations began in Sichuan, Minzhong has had merit in drafting edicts.

entries.zh: 大功告竣，朕欲如張廷玉例，領以世職。
entries.en: With the great achievement completed, I intended, following the precedent of Zhang Tingyu, to grant him a hereditary office.
entries.literal: With the great achievement completed, I intended, following the precedent of Zhang Tingyu, to grant him a hereditary office.

entries.zh: 今事垂成，敏中乃有此事，是其福澤有限，不能受朕深恩，寧不痛自愧悔？
entries.en: Now, just as the matter neared completion, Minzhong has done this—his blessings are limited and he cannot receive my deep grace; should he not bitterly repent?
entries.literal: Now, just as the matter neared completion, Minzhong has done this—his blessings are limited and he cannot receive my deep grace; should he not bitterly repent?

entries.zh: 免其治罪，嚴加議處。」
entries.en: He is exempted from criminal punishment but is to be severely dealt with by deliberation."
entries.literal: He is exempted from criminal punishment but is to be severely dealt with by deliberation."

entries.zh: 部議革職，詔從寬留任。
entries.en: The ministry deliberated dismissal from office, but an edict leniently allowed him to remain in post.
entries.literal: The ministry deliberated dismissal from office, but an edict leniently allowed him to remain in post.

entries.zh: 四十一年，金川平，詔嘉其勞勚，過失可原，仍列功臣，給一等輕車都尉，世襲罔替。
entries.en: In the forty-first year, when Jinchuan was pacified, an edict praised his labor, held his faults forgivable, still listed him among meritorious officials, and granted a first-rank Light Chariot Commandant, hereditary in perpetuity.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year, when Jinchuan was pacified, an edict praised his labor and toil, held his faults forgivable, still listed him among meritorious officials, and granted a first-rank Light Chariot Commandant, hereditary in perpetuity.

entries.zh: 四十四年，病喘，遣醫視，賜人蓡。
entries.en: In the forty-fourth year he fell ill with asthma; physicians were sent to attend him and ginseng was bestowed.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he fell ill with asthma; physicians were sent to attend him and ginseng was bestowed.

entries.zh: 卒，優詔賜卹，祭葬如例，祀賢良祠，諡文襄。
entries.en: He died; a favorable edict granted condolence payments, sacrifices and burial followed precedent, he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and was given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
entries.literal: He died; a favorable edict granted condolence payments, sacrifices and burial followed precedent, he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and was given the posthumous title Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 子齊賢，前卒。
entries.en: His son Qixian had died earlier.
entries.literal: His son Qixian had died earlier.

entries.zh: 孫德裕，襲世職，以主事用。
entries.en: His grandson Deyu inherited the hereditary office and was employed as a secretary.
entries.literal: His grandson Deyu inherited the hereditary office and was employed as a secretary.

entries.zh: 敏中從侄時和，擁其貲回籍，德裕訟之。
entries.en: Minzhong's younger cousin's son Shihe seized his wealth and returned home; Deyu sued him.
entries.literal: Minzhong's younger cousin's son Shihe seized his wealth and returned home; Deyu sued him.

entries.zh: 江蘇巡撫吳壇察治，罪時和，戍伊犁。
entries.en: Jiangsu Governor Wu Tan investigated and punished Shihe, banishing him to Yili.
entries.literal: Jiangsu governor Wu Tan investigated and punished Shihe, banishing him to Yili.

entries.zh: 所侵奪者，還德裕三萬兩，馀充金壇開河用。
entries.en: What had been seized was returned to Deyu in the amount of thirty thousand taels; the remainder was used for river works at Jintan.
entries.literal: What had been seized was returned to Deyu in the amount of thirty thousand taels; the remainder was used for river works at Jintan.

entries.zh: 蘇松糧道章攀桂為敏中營造花園，事覺，褫攀桂職。
entries.en: Zhang Pan'gui, grain intendant of Su-Song, built a garden for Minzhong; when the matter came to light, Pan'gui was stripped of office.
entries.literal: Zhang Pan'gui, grain intendant of Su-Song, built a garden for Minzhong; when the matter came to light, Pan'gui was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 敏中受地方官逢迎，以已卒置不論。
entries.en: Minzhong had accepted the flattery of local officials; because he was already dead, the matter was set aside.
entries.literal: Minzhong had accepted the flattery of local officials; because he was already dead, the matter was set aside.

entries.zh: 既而浙江巡撫王亶望以貪敗，上追咎敏中。
entries.en: Later Zhejiang Governor Wang Tanwang was ruined by corruption, and the emperor traced blame back to Minzhong.
entries.literal: Later Zhejiang governor Wang Tanwang was ruined by corruption, and the emperor traced blame back to Minzhong.

entries.zh: 五十一年，詔曰：「朕幾馀詠物，有嘉靖年間器皿，念及嚴嵩專權煬蔽，以致國是日非，朝多稗政。
entries.en: In the fifty-first year an edict said, "While at leisure composing poems on objects, I came upon vessels from the Jiajing reign and thought of Yan Song's monopoly of power and concealment of truth, which caused the affairs of state daily to go astray and the court to abound in harmful policies.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year an edict said: "While at leisure composing poems on objects, I came upon vessels from the Jiajing reign and thought of Yan Song's monopoly of power and concealment of truth, which caused the affairs of state daily to go astray and the court to abound in harmful policies.

entries.zh: 取閱嚴嵩傳，見其賄賂公行，生死予奪，潛竊威柄，實為前明奸佞之尤。
entries.en: I took up and read the biography of Yan Song and saw how bribery was openly practiced, life and death were arbitrarily dispensed, and authority was secretly usurped—he was truly the worst villain of the former Ming.
entries.literal: I took up and read the biography of Yan Song and saw how bribery was openly practiced, life and death were arbitrarily dispensed, and authority was secretly usurped—he was truly the worst villain of the former Ming.

entries.zh: 本朝家法相承，紀綱整肅，太阿從不下移，本無大臣專權之事。
entries.en: Our dynasty's household laws have been handed down in succession, discipline is strict, and the sword of authority has never shifted downward—there is fundamentally no matter of ministers monopolizing power.
entries.literal: Our dynasty's household laws have been handed down in succession, discipline is strict, and the sword of authority has never shifted downward—there is fundamentally no matter of ministers monopolizing power.

entries.zh: 原任大學士於敏中因任用日久，恩眷稍優。
entries.en: The former grand secretary Yu Minzhong, because he had long been in office, enjoyed somewhat greater imperial favor.
entries.literal: The former grand secretary Yu Minzhong, because he had long been in office, enjoyed somewhat greater imperial favor.

entries.zh: 無識之徒，心存依附，敏中亦遂時相招引，潛受苞苴。
entries.en: Men without judgment sought to attach themselves, and Minzhong in turn occasionally drew them in and secretly accepted gifts.
entries.literal: Men without judgment sought to attach themselves, and Minzhong in turn occasionally drew them in and secretly accepted gifts.

entries.zh: 其時軍機大臣中無老成更事之人，福康安年輕，未能歷練，以致敏中聲勢略張。
entries.en: At that time among the Grand Councilors there was no seasoned and experienced man; Fukang'an was young and had not yet been tempered by experience, so Minzhong's influence expanded somewhat.
entries.literal: At that time among the Grand Councilors there was no seasoned and experienced man; Fukang'an was young and had not yet been tempered by experience, so Minzhong's influence expanded somewhat.

entries.zh: 究之亦止侍直承旨，不特非前朝嚴嵩可比，並不能如康熙年間明珠、徐乾學、高士奇等；
entries.en: In the end he only attended duty and drafted edicts; he was not only incomparable to Yan Song of the previous dynasty, but also could not match such men as Nalan Mingzhu, Xu Qianxue, and Gao Shiqi in the Kangxi reign;
entries.literal: In the end he only attended duty and drafted edicts; he was not only incomparable to Yan Song of the previous dynasty, but also could not match such men as Nalan Mingzhu, Xu Qianxue, and Gao Shiqi in the Kangxi reign;

entries.zh: 即寵眷亦尚不及鄂爾泰、張廷玉，安能於朕前竊弄威福、淆亂是非耶？
entries.en: even his favor still fell short of Oertai and Zhang Tingyu—how could he secretly wield authority and confuse right and wrong before me?
entries.literal: even his favor still fell short of Oertai and Zhang Tingyu—how could he secretly wield authority and confuse right and wrong before me?

entries.zh: 朕因其宣力年久，身故仍加恩飾終，准入賢良祠。
entries.en: Because he had long served with effort, after his death I still bestowed grace in honoring his end and allowed him entry into the Shrine of Worthies.
entries.literal: Because he had long served with effort, after his death I still bestowed grace in honoring his end and allowed him entry into the Shrine of Worthies.

entries.zh: 迨四十六年甘肅捐監折收之事敗露，王亶望等侵欺貪黷，罪不容誅。
entries.en: When in the forty-sixth year the Gansu practice of selling supervisory student status and collecting grain in lieu of silver was exposed, Wang Tanwang and others were guilty of embezzlement and corruption beyond what execution could expiate.
entries.literal: When in the forty-sixth year the Gansu practice of selling supervisory student status and collecting grain in lieu of silver was exposed, Wang Tanwang and others were guilty of embezzlement and corruption beyond what execution could expiate.

entries.zh: 因憶此事前經舒赫德奏請停止，於敏中於朕前力言甘肅捐監應開，部中免撥解之煩，閭閻有糶販之利，一舉兩得，是以準行。
entries.en: Recalling that Shuhede had earlier memorialized requesting its cessation, Yu Minzhong had strongly urged before me that Gansu sales of supervisory student status should be opened, sparing the ministry the trouble of forwarding grain and giving common people the profit of selling grain—two gains at once—and therefore it was approved.
entries.literal: Recalling that this matter had earlier been memorialized by Shuhede requesting its cessation, Yu Minzhong had strongly urged before me that Gansu sales of supervisory student status should be opened, sparing the ministry the trouble of forwarding grain and giving common people the profit of selling grain—two gains at once—and therefore it was approved.

entries.zh: 詎知勒爾謹為王亶望所愚，通同一氣，肥橐殃民。
entries.en: Who knew that Le'erjin would be deceived by Wang Tanwang, act in collusion, fatten their purses, and harm the people?
entries.literal: Who knew that Le'erjin would be deceived by Wang Tanwang, act in collusion, fatten their purses, and harm the people?

entries.zh: 非於敏中為之主持，勒爾謹豈敢遽行奏請？
entries.en: Had Yu Minzhong not backed it, how would Le'erjin have dared to memorialize so hastily?
entries.literal: Had Yu Minzhong not backed it, how would Le'erjin have dared to memorialize so hastily?

entries.zh: 王亶望豈敢肆無忌憚？
entries.en: How would Wang Tanwang have dared to act so brazenly?
entries.literal: How would Wang Tanwang have dared to act so brazenly?

entries.zh: 於敏中擁有厚貲，必出王亶望等賄求酬謝。
entries.en: Yu Minzhong's possession of great wealth must have come from bribes and rewards sought by Wang Tanwang and others.
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong's possession of great wealth must have come from bribes and rewards sought by Wang Tanwang and others.

entries.zh: 使於敏中尚在，朕必嚴加懲治。
entries.en: Had Yu Minzhong still been alive, I would certainly have punished him severely.
entries.literal: Had Yu Minzhong still been alive, I would certainly have punished him severely.

entries.zh: 今不將其子孫治罪，已為從寬；
entries.en: That I do not now punish his descendants is already leniency;
entries.literal: That I do not now punish his descendants is already leniency;

entries.zh: 賢良祠為國家風勵有位盛典，豈可以不慎廉隅之人濫行列入？
entries.en: the Shrine of Worthies is a great state ceremony for encouraging those in office—how can men who do not guard their integrity be recklessly listed therein?
entries.literal: the Shrine of Worthies is a great state ceremony for encouraging those in office—how can men who do not guard their integrity be recklessly listed therein?

entries.zh: 朕久有此心，因覽嚴嵩傳，觸動鑑戒。
entries.en: I have long had this thought; reading the biography of Yan Song stirred my sense of warning.
entries.literal: I have long had this thought; reading the biography of Yan Song stirred my sense of warning.

entries.zh: 恐無知之人，將以明世宗比朕，朕不受也。
entries.en: I fear ignorant men may compare me to the Jiajing Emperor of the Ming—I do not accept that.
entries.literal: I fear ignorant men may compare me to the Jiajing Emperor of the Ming—I do not accept that.

entries.zh: 於敏中著撤出賢良祠，以昭儆戒。」
entries.en: Yu Minzhong is to be removed from the Shrine of Worthies, to serve as a warning."
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong is to be removed from the Shrine of Worthies, to serve as a warning."

entries.zh: 六十年，國史館進呈敏中列傳，詔曰：「於敏中簡任綸扉，不自檢束，既向宦寺交接，復與外省官吏夤緣舞弊。
entries.en: In the sixtieth year the State Historiography Bureau submitted Minzhong's biography; an edict said, "Yu Minzhong was simply appointed to the Grand Secretariat but did not restrain himself; he not only associated with eunuchs but also colluded in corruption with officials from outside provinces.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year the State Historiography Bureau submitted Minzhong's biography; an edict said: "Yu Minzhong was simply appointed to the Grand Secretariat but did not restrain himself; he not only associated with eunuchs but also colluded in corruption with officials from outside provinces.

entries.zh: 即此二節，實屬辜恩，非大臣所應有。
entries.en: These two points alone truly betrayed grace and are not what a great minister should do.
entries.literal: These two points alone truly betrayed grace and are not what a great minister should do.

entries.zh: 若仍令濫邀世職，何以示懲？
entries.en: If he were still allowed to claim a hereditary office in vain, how would punishment be shown?
entries.literal: If he were still allowed to claim a hereditary office in vain, how would punishment be shown?

entries.zh: 其孫於德裕現官直隸知府，已屬格外恩施，所襲輕車都尉世職即撤革，以為大臣營私玷職者戒。」
entries.en: His grandson Yu Deyu now serves as prefect of Zhili, which is already extraordinary grace; the inherited Light Chariot Commandant hereditary office is forthwith revoked, as a warning to great ministers who pursue private gain and stain their office."
entries.literal: His grandson Yu Deyu now serves as prefect of Zhili, which is already extraordinary grace; the inherited Light Chariot Commandant hereditary office is forthwith revoked, as a warning to great ministers who pursue private gain and stain their office."

entries.zh: 四十七年，御史錢灃劾山東巡撫國泰、布政使於易簡貪縱營私，命和珅偕都御史劉墉按鞫，灃從往。
entries.en: In the forty-seventh year Censor Qian Feng impeached Shandong Governor Guo Tai and Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yijian for greed, indulgence, and private profit. He Shen was ordered to join Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong in the investigation, and Qian Feng went along.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year, Censor Qian Feng impeached Shandong Governor Guo Tai and Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yijian for greedy indulgence and private profit; He Shen was ordered to join Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong in investigation; Qian Feng accompanied them.

entries.zh: 和珅陰袒國泰，即至，盤庫，令抽視銀數十封無缺，即起還行館。
entries.en: He Shen secretly favored Guo Tai. As soon as he arrived he inspected the treasury, had several dozen sealed silver packets drawn at random and found no shortage, then immediately returned to his lodging.
entries.literal: He Shen secretly favored Guo Tai; upon arrival he inspected the treasury, had several dozen sealed silver packets drawn at random and found no shortage, then left immediately for his lodging.

entries.zh: 灃請封庫，明日盡發視庫銀，得借市銀充抵狀，國泰等罪皆鞫實。
entries.en: Qian Feng requested that the treasury be sealed. The next day all the silver was examined, and evidence was found that market silver had been borrowed to cover shortfalls. The crimes of Guo Tai and the others were all verified.
entries.literal: Qian Feng requested the treasury be sealed; the next day all silver was examined and evidence was found of borrowed market silver used to fill deficits; the crimes of Guo Tai and others were all verified.

entries.zh: 會加恩中外大臣，加太子太保，充經筵講官。
entries.en: At the time the emperor was extending favor to ministers at court and abroad. He Shen was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed lecturer at the imperial lectures.
entries.literal: At the time favor was extended to ministers at court and in the provinces; He Shen was given the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed lecturer at the imperial lectures.

entries.zh: 四十八年，賜雙眼花翎，充國史館正總裁、文淵閣提舉閣事、清字經館總裁。
entries.en: In the forty-eighth year he was granted double peacock feathers and made chief director of the National History Bureau, superintendent of the Wenyuan Pavilion, and director of the Manchu Classics project.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he was granted double peacock feathers, made chief director of the National History Bureau, superintendent of the Wenyuan Pavilion, and director of the Manchu Classics project.

entries.zh: 甘肅石峰堡回匪平，以承旨論功，再予輕車都尉世職，並前職授一等男爵。
entries.en: When the Muslim rebels at Shi Feng Fort in Gansu were pacified, he was rewarded for carrying out the imperial will. He was again granted the hereditary Light Chariot Commandant, and together with his previous post was made a first-rank baron.
entries.literal: When the Shi Feng Fort Muslim rebels in Gansu were pacified, based on carrying out the imperial will he was rewarded; he was again granted the hereditary Light Chariot Commandant, and with his previous post was given the first-rank baron.

entries.zh: 調吏部尚書、協辦大學士，管理戶部如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to minister of Personnel and associate grand secretary, while continuing to manage the Ministry of Revenue as before.
entries.literal: He was transferred to minister of Personnel and associate grand secretary, continuing to manage Revenue as before.

entries.zh: 五十一年，御史曹錫寶劾和珅家奴劉全奢僭，造屋踰制，帝察其欲劾和珅，不敢明言，故以家人為由。
entries.en: In the fifty-first year Censor Cao Xibao impeached He Shen's household slave Liu Quan for arrogating prerogatives and building houses in violation of regulations. The emperor saw that Cao really wished to impeach He Shen himself but dared not say so openly, and so used the household member as his pretext.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year, Censor Cao Xibao impeached He Shen's household slave Liu Quan for arrogating prerogatives and building houses in violation of regulations; the emperor saw he wished to impeach He Shen himself but dared not say so openly, hence used the household member as pretext.

entries.zh: 命王大臣會同都察院傳問錫寶，使直陳和珅私弊，卒不能指實。
entries.en: Imperial princes and ministers together with the Censorate were ordered to summon Cao Xibao and have him speak directly of He Shen's private abuses, but he ultimately could not substantiate any charge.
entries.literal: Imperial princes and ministers together with the Censorate were ordered to summon Cao Xibao and have him speak directly of He Shen's private abuses; he ultimately could not substantiate his claims.

entries.zh: 和珅亦預使劉全毀屋更造，察勘不得直，錫寶因獲譴。
entries.en: He Shen had also beforehand had Liu Quan demolish and rebuild the house. Inspection could not verify the charge, and Cao Xibao was punished.
entries.literal: He Shen also beforehand had Liu Quan demolish and rebuild the house; inspection could not verify the charge, and Cao Xibao was punished.

entries.zh: 踰月，授和珅文華殿大學士。
entries.en: A month later He Shen was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
entries.literal: A month later He Shen was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

entries.zh: 詔以其管崇文門監督已閱八年，大學士不宜兼榷務，且錫寶劾其家人，未必不因此，遂罷其監督。
entries.en: An edict stated that he had managed the Chongwen Gate superintendency for eight years, that a grand secretary should not also hold revenue-collection duties, and that Cao Xibao's impeachment of his household member may not have been unrelated to the matter. His superintendency was therefore removed.
entries.literal: An edict stated that he had managed the Chongwen Gate superintendency for eight years; a Grand Secretary should not also hold revenue collection duties; and since Cao Xibao had impeached his household member, the post may not have been unrelated; so his superintendency was removed.

entries.zh: 部員湛露擢廣信知府，上見其年幼，不勝方面，斥和珅濫保。
entries.en: Ministry clerk Zhan Lu was promoted to prefect of Guangxin. The emperor saw that he was young and unfit for a regional post and rebuked He Shen for reckless recommendation.
entries.literal: Ministry clerk Zhan Lu was promoted to prefect of Guangxin; the emperor saw he was young and unfit for a regional post, and rebuked He Shen for reckless recommendation.

entries.zh: 又兩廣總督富勒渾縱容家人婪索，和珅請調回富勒渾，不興大獄。
entries.en: Also, Governor-General Fu Lehun of Guangdong and Guangxi had indulged his household in extortion. He Shen requested that Fu Lehun be transferred back without launching a major prosecution.
entries.literal: Also Governor-General Fu Lehun of Guangdong and Guangxi indulged his household in extortion; He Shen requested Fu Lehun be transferred back without launching a major prosecution.

entries.zh: 京師米貴，和珅請禁囤積，逾五十石者交廠減糶，商民以為不便。
entries.en: Rice in the capital was dear. He Shen requested a ban on hoarding: anyone holding more than fifty shi would have to surrender the surplus to government granaries for sale at reduced price. Merchants and commoners found the measure inconvenient.
entries.literal: Rice in the capital was dear; He Shen requested a ban on hoarding—those exceeding fifty shi must surrender grain to the government for sale at reduced price; merchants and commoners found it inconvenient.

entries.zh: 廷臣遷就原議，上並切責之。
entries.en: Court ministers went along with the original proposal, and the emperor sharply rebuked them all.
entries.literal: Court ministers accommodated the original proposal; the emperor sharply rebuked them all.

entries.zh: 五十三年，以台灣逆匪林爽文平，晉封三等忠襄伯，賜紫韁。
entries.en: In the fifty-third year, with the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen pacified, he was promoted to third-rank Loyal and Assisting Count and granted a purple bridle.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year, with the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen pacified, he was promoted to third-rank Loyal and Assisting Count and granted a purple bridle.

entries.zh: 五十五年，賜黃帶、四開褉袍。
entries.en: In the fifty-fifth year he was granted the yellow belt and a four-panel patched robe.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was granted the yellow belt and four-panel patched robe.

entries.zh: 上八旬萬壽，命和珅偕尚書金簡專司慶典事。
entries.en: For the emperor's eightieth birthday, He Shen and Minister Jin Jian were ordered to manage the celebration affairs exclusively.
entries.literal: For the emperor's eightieth birthday, He Shen and Minister Jin Jian were ordered exclusively to manage celebration affairs.

entries.zh: 內閣學士尹壯圖疏論各省庫藏空虛，上為動色，和珅請即命壯圖往勘各省庫，以侍郎慶成監之。
entries.en: Academician Yin Zhuangtu memorialized that the provincial treasuries were empty. The emperor was visibly moved. He Shen requested that Yin Zhuangtu be sent at once to inspect the treasuries of every province, with Vice Minister Qing Cheng supervising.
entries.literal: Academician Yin Zhuangtu memorialized on the emptiness of provincial treasuries; the emperor was visibly moved; He Shen requested Yin Zhuangtu be immediately sent to inspect all provincial treasuries, with Vice Minister Qing Cheng supervising.

entries.zh: 慶成每至一省輒掣肘，待挪移既足，然後啟榷，迄無虧絀，壯圖以妄言坐黜。
entries.en: At each province Qing Cheng obstructed the inspection, waiting until funds had been shifted to cover the gaps before the treasury was opened. No shortfalls were found anywhere, and Yin Zhuangtu was dismissed for false statements.
entries.literal: Qing Cheng at each province obstructed matters, waiting until funds had been transferred to fill gaps, then opened the treasury; throughout no shortfalls were found; Yin Zhuangtu was dismissed for false statements.

entries.zh: 五十六年，刻石經於辟雍，命為正總裁。
entries.en: In the fifty-sixth year stone classics were carved at the Piyong, and He Shen was appointed chief director.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, stone classics were carved at the Piyong; He Shen was appointed chief director.

entries.zh: 時總裁八人，尚書彭元瑞獨任校勘，敕編石經考文提要，事竣，元瑞被優賚。
entries.en: At the time there were eight directors. Minister Peng Yuanrui alone undertook the collation and was ordered to compile the Collected Emendations to the Stone Classics. When the work was finished Yuanrui received special rewards.
entries.literal: At the time there were eight directors; Minister Peng Yuanrui alone undertook collation; he was ordered to compile Collected Emendations to the Stone Classics; when completed Yuanrui received special rewards.

entries.zh: 和珅嫉之，毀元瑞所編不善，且言非天子不考文。
entries.en: He Shen envied this. He slandered Yuanrui's compilation as poor and further said that only the Son of Heaven may emend texts.
entries.literal: He Shen envied this; he slandered Yuanrui's compilation as poor and further said that only the Son of Heaven may emend texts.

entries.zh: 上曰：「書為御定，何得目為私書耶？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "The book was imperially approved—how can it be called a private work?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "The book was imperially approved—how can it be called a private work?"

entries.zh: 和珅乃使人撰考文提要舉正以攻之，冒為己作進上，訾提要不便士子，請銷毀，上不許。
entries.en: He Shen then had others compose emendations against the Collected Emendations, passed them off as his own work and presented them to the throne, criticized the Collected Emendations as inconvenient for students, and requested their destruction. The emperor did not permit it.
entries.literal: He Shen then had others compose emendations against the Collected Emendations, passed them off as his own work and presented them, criticizing the Collected Emendations as inconvenient for students and requesting destruction; the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 館臣疏請頒行，為和珅所阻，中止，复私使人磨碑字，凡從古者盡改之。
