entries.en: The academy officials memorialized requesting publication, but He Shen blocked it and the plan was halted. He also secretly had men grind down characters on the stone tablets, altering every reading that followed antiquity.
entries.literal: The academy officials memorialized requesting publication; He Shen blocked it and stopped it; he also secretly had men grind down characters on the stone tablets, altering all that followed antiquity.

entries.zh: 五十七年，廓爾喀平，予議敘，兼翰林院掌院學士。
entries.en: In the fifty-seventh year, with Gorkha pacified, he received merit evaluation and was also made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, with Gorkha pacified, he received merit evaluation and concurrently served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 六十年，充殿試讀卷官，教習庶吉士。
entries.en: In the sixtieth year he served as reader at the palace examination and as instructor to the newly passed jinshi.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year, he served as reader at the palace examination and instructor to passed jinshi.

entries.zh: 時朝審停勾，情重者請旨裁定。
entries.en: At the time the annual capital review had suspended executions; only the most serious cases required an imperial decision.
entries.literal: At the time the annual capital review had suspended executions; severe cases required imperial decision.

entries.zh: 和珅管理籓院，於蒙古重獄置未奏，鐫級留任。
entries.en: While managing the Court of Colonial Affairs, He Shen left a memorial on a serious Mongol case unsent. He was demoted one rank but kept in office.
entries.literal: He Shen managed the Court of Colonial Affairs; in a serious Mongol case he left a memorial unsent and was demoted one rank but kept in office.

entries.zh: 又廷試武舉發策，上命檢實錄。
entries.en: Also, at the military metropolitan examination he drafted the policy questions, and the emperor ordered verification against the Veritable Records.
entries.literal: Also at the military metropolitan examination he drafted policy questions; the emperor ordered verification in the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 故事，實錄不載武試策問，和珅率對不以實，詔斥護過飾非，革職留任。
entries.en: By precedent the Veritable Records do not record military examination policy questions. He Shen answered casually and not in accord with fact. An edict rebuked him for shielding faults and concealing errors, and he was dismissed from office but retained to serve.
entries.literal: By precedent the Veritable Records do not record military examination policy questions; He Shen casually answered contrary to fact; an edict rebuked him for shielding faults and concealing errors; he was dismissed from office but retained to serve.

entries.zh: 先是京察屢邀議敘，是年特停罷之。
entries.en: Previously he had repeatedly been nominated for merit evaluation at the capital inspection, but that year the nomination was specially suspended.
entries.literal: Previously he had repeatedly been nominated for merit evaluation at the capital inspection; that year it was specially suspended.

entries.zh: 嘉慶二年，調管刑部。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 2 he was transferred to manage the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing, he was transferred to manage the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 尋以軍需報銷，仍兼管戶部。
entries.en: Soon afterward, because of military supply accounting, he again concurrently managed the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: Soon due to military supply accounting he again concurrently managed Revenue.

entries.zh: 三年，教匪王三槐就擒，以襄贊功晉公爵。
entries.en: In the third year, with the teaching-bandit Wang Sanhuai captured, he was promoted to duke for his supporting merit.
entries.literal: In the third year, with the teaching-bandit Wang Sanhuai captured, he was promoted to duke for supporting merit.

entries.zh: 于敏中和珅弟和琳蘇凌阿
entries.en: Yu Minzhong; He Shen; his younger brother He Lin; and Su Linga.
entries.literal: Yu Minzhong, He Shen, younger brother He Lin, Su Linga.

entries.zh: 三寶，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人。
entries.en: San Bao, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.
entries.literal: San Bao, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆四年繙譯進士，授內閣中書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 4 (1739) he earned jinshi through the translation examination and was appointed a drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the translator jinshi examination and was appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter.

entries.zh: 襲世管佐領。
entries.en: He succeeded to a hereditary company commandership.
entries.literal: He inherited a hereditary company commander's post.

entries.zh: 遷內閣侍讀。
entries.en: He was promoted to a reader in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be a reader in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 出為湖北驛鹽道。
entries.en: He was posted as intendant of the Hubei Post and Salt Circuit.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as Hubei Post and Salt Circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 入補戶部郎中。
entries.en: He was recalled to the capital to fill a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: He returned to fill a vacancy as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 師徵準噶爾，命赴北路董達什達瓦游牧。
entries.en: During the Dzungar campaign he was ordered to the northern front to oversee pastoral herds at Dongdashidawa.
entries.literal: When the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to go to the northern route to supervise herds at Dongdashidawa.

entries.zh: 擢直隸布政使。
entries.en: He was elevated to Zhili provincial administration commissioner.
entries.literal: He was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili.

entries.zh: 二十六年，上幸熱河，坐蹕路不修，命以道銜駐哈密。
entries.en: In Qianlong 26, while the emperor was at Rehe, San Bao was punished for neglecting repairs along the imperial route and was sent to Hami with intendant's rank.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the emperor visited Rehe, for failure to maintain the imperial procession route he was ordered to remain at Hami with intendant's rank.

entries.zh: 二十九年，起四川布政使，更湖北、湖南、貴州諸省。
entries.en: In Qianlong 29 he was reappointed Sichuan administration commissioner and subsequently served in Hubei, Hunan, and Guizhou in turn.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was recalled as Sichuan administration commissioner, then moved through Hubei, Hunan, and Guizhou provinces.

entries.zh: 三十七年，擢山西巡撫。
entries.en: In Qianlong 37 he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Shanxi.

entries.zh: 明年，移浙江。
entries.en: The following year he was moved to Zhejiang.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 四十二年，擢湖廣總督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 he was made governor-general of Huguang.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

entries.zh: 閱兵，衡州協副將海福、沅州協副將洪昌運皆衰老，三寶請以海福內授旗員，昌運令休致。
entries.en: On troop inspection he found the Hengzhou and Yuanzhou garrison deputy commanders, Haifu and Hong Changyun, both too old for duty; he asked that Haifu be reassigned within the banners and that Changyun be retired.
entries.literal: When reviewing troops, he found that Hengzhou garrison deputy commander Haifu and Yuanzhou garrison deputy commander Hong Changyun were both aged; San Bao requested that Haifu be given an internal banner appointment and that Changyun be ordered to retire.

entries.zh: 上以偏護滿洲，顯分軒輊，拒不允。
entries.en: The emperor judged that he was favoring Manchus and showing clear partiality, and refused.
entries.literal: The emperor, holding that he was partial to Manchus and showed obvious favoritism, refused to approve.

entries.zh: 四十四年，授東閣大學士，兼禮部尚書，督湖廣如故。
entries.en: In Qianlong 44 he was made Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Rites while retaining the Huguang governor-generalship.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Rites, continuing as governor-general of Huguang as before.

entries.zh: 旋移閩浙總督。
entries.en: He was soon moved to the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-generalship.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 浙江海塘自老鹽倉以上皆柴塘，上南巡，諭改築石塘。
entries.en: Above Laoyancang the Zhejiang coast was protected by wattled seawalls; during his southern tour the emperor ordered them replaced with stone dikes.
entries.literal: The Zhejiang seawalls above Laoyancang were all wattled embankments; on the southern tour the emperor ordered them rebuilt as stone dikes.

entries.zh: 三寶疏言：「時方大汛，未宜更動。
entries.en: San Bao memorialized: "The great flood season is upon us; this is no time for major works.
entries.literal: San Bao memorialized: "At present the great flood season is at hand; it is not suitable to make changes.

entries.zh: 當於柴塘內下椿築石，而以柴塘為外護。」
entries.en: Stone piles should be driven inside the wattled embankments, leaving the wattled works as an outer barrier."
entries.literal: Stone should be piled within the wattled dikes, using the wattled dikes as an outer shield."

entries.zh: 會上亦降旨令留柴塘為重關保障，與三寶議合。
entries.en: The emperor then ordered that the wattled dikes be retained as a second line of defense, in agreement with San Bao's plan.
entries.literal: The emperor also issued an edict ordering the wattled dikes kept as a major line of defense, which accorded with San Bao's proposal.

entries.zh: 旋命入閣治事。
entries.en: He was soon summoned into the Grand Secretariat to conduct state business.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to enter the Grand Council and handle affairs.

entries.zh: 巡撫王亶望以贓敗，三寶坐未舉劾，部議當奪職，上命留任。
entries.en: When Governor Wang Tanwang fell in a corruption scandal, San Bao was faulted for not having impeached him; although the ministry recommended dismissal, the emperor kept him in office.
entries.literal: When Governor Wang Tanwang was ruined by corruption, San Bao was held culpable for failing to impeach him; the ministry proposed dismissal, but the emperor ordered him retained.

entries.zh: 尋復令在上書房總師傅上行走。
entries.en: He was soon assigned again to serve as chief tutor of the Upper Study.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to serve on duty as chief tutor of the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 四十九年，扈蹕熱河，以疾還京師。
entries.en: In Qianlong 49 he escorted the emperor to Rehe, then returned to Beijing because of illness.
entries.literal: In the forty-ninth year he accompanied the emperor to Rehe, then returned to the capital on account of illness.

entries.zh: 卒，諡文敬。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously titled Wénjìng (Cultivated and Reverent).
entries.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Wénjìng.

entries.zh: 三寶喜讀宋諸儒書，大節不苟。
entries.en: San Bao loved the Song Neo-Confucian masters and would not compromise on matters of principle.
entries.literal: San Bao delighted in reading the Song Neo-Confucians and was unbending in major principles.

entries.zh: 為直隸布政使時，高宗幸熱河，至密雲，值大霖雨，水盛漲。
entries.en: While he was Zhili administration commissioner, the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Rehe; at Miyun torrential rain had swollen the rivers.
entries.literal: When he was Zhili administration commissioner, the Gaozong Emperor visited Rehe; reaching Miyun, they encountered heavy rains and greatly swollen waters.

entries.zh: 上欲策騎亂流渡，三寶諫曰：「千金之子，坐不垂堂。
entries.en: The emperor meant to ride through the churning current; San Bao remonstrated: "A man of priceless worth does not court danger under a crumbling eave.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to spur his horse through the turbulent current to cross; San Bao remonstrated: "The son worth a thousand in gold does not sit beneath the eaves of a low hall.

entries.zh: 今以萬乘輕狎波濤，使禦駟有失，臣等雖萬段，何可追悔？」
entries.en: If Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, treats the flood lightly and the imperial horses come to grief, though we servants be torn limb from limb, what remedy would there be?"
entries.literal: Now, with the ten-thousand-chariot ruler lightly treating the billows, if the imperial steeds should come to harm, though your servants be torn in ten thousand pieces, how could regret be undone?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「滿洲舊俗宜親習勞勚，顧不可耶？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Manchu custom calls for sharing hardship firsthand—surely that is fitting?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "By Manchu custom one should personally accustom oneself to toil—may that not be done?"

entries.zh: 三寶復曰：「上方奉太后乘輿同臨幸，即上渡河安便，不識奉太后何所？」
entries.en: San Bao replied: "Your Majesty is traveling with the empress dowager's carriage; even if the crossing is safe for you, how is the empress dowager to cross?"
entries.literal: San Bao replied again: "Your Majesty is now accompanying the empress dowager's carriage on this tour; even if crossing the river is convenient for Your Majesty, where would the empress dowager be placed?"

entries.zh: 上動容，為之回轡。
entries.en: The emperor was moved and turned his horse back.
entries.literal: The emperor was moved and turned his horse back for him.

entries.zh: 其為上書房總師傅，輯古今儲貳事曰春華日覽，授諸皇子，論者謂其得師保之體云。
entries.en: As chief tutor of the Upper Study he compiled a digest of crown-prince affairs through the ages, entitled Spring Splendor Daily Perusal, for the imperial sons; critics said he embodied the true role of tutor and guardian.
entries.literal: As chief tutor of the Upper Study he compiled affairs of heirs apparent ancient and modern into Spring Splendor Daily Perusal and presented it to the princes; commentators said he had grasped the substance of a tutor and guardian.

entries.zh: 永貴，字心齋，拜都氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Yong Gui, styled Xinzhaī, of the Baidu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Yong Gui, style Xinzhaī, of the Baidu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 父布蘭泰，自云騎尉世職授理籓院員外郎。
entries.en: His father Bulantai entered service from a hereditary yunqiwei post as an assistant director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
entries.literal: His father Bulantai, from a hereditary yunqiwei post, was appointed an assistant department director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

entries.zh: 雍正間，為江西巡撫，治嚴刻，世宗召還京師面詰之，對曰：「臣治事從嚴，待上改正，俾恩出自上。」
entries.en: Under Yongzheng, as Jiangxi governor he ruled harshly; the Yongzheng Emperor recalled him to Beijing and questioned him in person. He answered: "I govern strictly so that Your Majesty may temper my excesses and bestow mercy yourself."
entries.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, as Jiangxi governor his rule was harsh; the Shizong Emperor summoned him back to the capital to question him face to face, and he replied: "Your servant governs strictly, awaiting Your Majesty's correction so that grace may issue from above."

entries.zh: 世宗不懌，奪職。
entries.en: Yongzheng was displeased and dismissed him.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor was displeased and stripped him of office.

entries.zh: 尋復起，至古北口提督。
entries.en: He was soon reinstated and eventually became provincial military commander at Gubeikou.
entries.literal: He was soon reappointed and rose to provincial military commander at Gubeikou.

entries.zh: 卒，諡愨僖。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously titled Mìnxī (Sincere and Joyful).
entries.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Mìnxī.

entries.zh: 永貴，自筆帖式授戶部主事。
entries.en: Yong Gui rose from a clerkship to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: Yong Gui, from a clerk's post, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，累遷郎中。
entries.en: Early in Qianlong he was promoted through several ranks to director.
entries.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign he was promoted step by step to director.

entries.zh: 出為湖南辰沅永靖道。
entries.en: He was posted as intendant of the Hunan Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as Hunan Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 擢雲南布政使。
entries.en: He was elevated to Yunnan provincial administration commissioner.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Yunnan provincial administration commissioner.

entries.zh: 移浙江，署巡撫。
entries.en: He was moved to Zhejiang as acting governor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang and served as acting governor.

entries.zh: 前總督李衛領鹽政，發帑收馀鹽，名曰「帑鹽」；
entries.en: Former governor-general Li Wei had run the salt monopoly, using treasury funds to buy surplus salt under the name "treasury salt";
entries.literal: The former governor-general Li Wei had overseen the salt administration, disbursing treasury funds to purchase surplus salt, called "treasury salt";

entries.zh: 令武職任緝私，其制未善。
entries.en: military officers were assigned to suppress smuggling—a system that had proved unsatisfactory.
entries.literal: military officers were charged with suppressing smuggling, and the system was not sound.

entries.zh: 永貴條上八事，俾文武互任其責，下部議行。
entries.en: Yong Gui submitted eight reform articles dividing duties between civil and military officials; the ministries approved and enacted them.
entries.literal: Yong Gui submitted eight detailed proposals so that civil and military officials would share responsibilities; the ministry deliberated and implemented them.

entries.zh: 居三年，命真除。
entries.en: After three years he received a regular appointment.
entries.literal: After three years he was ordered to receive formal appointment.

entries.zh: 溫、台諸縣旱，永貴令知府金洪銓治賑，不稱職。
entries.en: When drought struck Wenzhou, Taizhou, and neighboring counties, Yong Gui put Prefect Jin Hongquan in charge of relief, but Jin proved inadequate.
entries.literal: Wenzhou, Taizhou, and other counties suffered drought; Yong Gui ordered Prefect Jin Hongquan to manage relief, but he was incompetent.

entries.zh: 永貴論劾，請休致。
entries.en: Yong Gui impeached him and requested that he be retired.
entries.literal: Yong Gui memorialized in impeachment and requested retirement.

entries.zh: 總督喀爾吉善再劾，上為奪洪銓職。
entries.en: Governor-General Ka'erjishan joined the impeachment, and the emperor dismissed Hongquan.
entries.literal: Governor-General Ka'erjishan impeached again; the emperor thereupon stripped Hongquan of office.

entries.zh: 御史範廷楷因劾永貴瞻徇，上難其代，命寬之。
entries.en: Censor Fan Tingkai then impeached Yong Gui for partiality; the emperor was reluctant to replace him and ordered the matter set aside.
entries.literal: Censor Fan Tingkai thereupon impeached Yong Gui for favoritism; the emperor found it hard to replace him and ordered leniency.

entries.zh: 永貴請留本省及江蘇漕八十萬，借撥江蘇等省米五十五萬，又請開事例，補倉儲。
entries.en: Yong Gui asked to retain eight hundred thousand piculs of local and Jiangsu tribute grain, borrow five hundred fifty thousand piculs from Jiangsu and other provinces, and open a sale-of-offices drive to refill the granaries.
entries.literal: Yong Gui requested retaining eight hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute in the province and Jiangsu, borrowing and allocating five hundred fifty thousand piculs of grain from Jiangsu and other provinces, and also requested opening a sale of offices to replenish granaries.

entries.zh: 上責其張皇，既又聞永貴陳災狀有所諱飾，乃命奪職，赴北路軍董理糧餉。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him for exaggeration; learning later that Yong Gui had glossed over the disaster reports, he stripped him of office and sent him to manage provisions on the northern campaign.
entries.literal: The emperor reproached him for alarmism; then, hearing that Yong Gui's reports on the disaster had been concealed and embellished, he ordered dismissal and sent him to the northern-route army to oversee grain and pay.

entries.zh: 居三年，賜按察使銜，署甘肅臨洮道，仍赴巴里坤主餉。
entries.en: After three years he was given surveillance-commissioner rank, acted as Gansu Lintao intendant, and continued to manage supplies at Barkol.
entries.literal: After three years he was granted the rank of provincial surveillance commissioner and acted as Gansu Lintao Circuit intendant, still going to Barkol to oversee provisions.

entries.zh: 二十一年，加副都統銜，兼參贊大臣。
entries.en: In Qianlong 21 he received vice commander's rank and was made an assisting grand minister.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given vice commander's rank and served concurrently as assisting grand minister.

entries.zh: 是歲冬，厄魯特宰桑達什策淩等為亂，定邊右副將軍兆惠駐伊犁辦賊。
entries.en: That winter the Oirat chief Dashiceling and others rose in revolt; Deputy General Zhaohui was posted at Ili to suppress them.
entries.literal: That winter the Oirat zaisang Dashiceling and others rebelled; the Pacification Commissioner on the Right, Deputy General Zhaohui, was stationed at Ili to handle the bandits.

entries.zh: 永貴既抵巴里坤，具以軍事上聞，上嘉其奮勉，予三等輕車都尉世職，令從兆惠自額林沁畢爾罕進兵。
entries.en: On reaching Barkol Yong Gui reported fully on the campaign; the emperor commended his zeal, granted a hereditary third-rank commandery chariot captaincy, and ordered him to advance with Zhaohui from Elinqin Bi'erhan.
entries.literal: When Yong Gui reached Barkol he reported fully on military affairs; the emperor praised his exertions, granted a hereditary third-rank commandery chariot captaincy, and ordered him to follow Zhaohui in advancing from Elinqin Bi'erhan.

entries.zh: 命署西安巡撫，未之任，令赴魯克察克屯田。
entries.en: He was named acting Xi'an governor but never assumed the post and was sent to establish military farms at Lukchak.
entries.literal: He was ordered to act as Xi'an governor but did not take up the post and was sent to Lukchak to open military colonies.

entries.zh: 二十三年，以侍郎銜留軍，因授刑部侍郎，董屯田。
entries.en: In Qianlong 23 he stayed with the army as a vice-minister and was appointed Vice Minister of Justice to oversee the colony program.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, with vice-minister's rank he remained with the army; he was then appointed Vice Minister of Justice and supervised military colonies.

entries.zh: 烏魯木齊、闢展、托克三、哈喇沙爾、昌吉、羅克倫皆駐兵營墾，秋穫得穀三萬五千八百馀石。
entries.en: Garrison colonies were opened at Urumqi, Piqan (Pichan), Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun, yielding over thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs in the autumn harvest.
entries.literal: At Urumqi, Piqan (Pichan), Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun garrison farms were all established; the autumn harvest yielded more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 是時兆惠兵次葉爾羌，命永貴駐阿克蘇主餽軍。
entries.en: Zhaohui's forces were then at Yarkand; Yong Gui was stationed at Aksu to provision the campaign.
entries.literal: At that time Zhaohui's army was at Yarkand; Yong Gui was ordered to remain at Aksu to supply the army.

entries.zh: 二十四年，還至庫車，布政使德舒為嗎哈沁所戕。
entries.en: In Qianlong 24 he returned to Kucha, where administration commissioner Deshu was murdered by Mahakin rebels.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he returned to Kucha; the administration commissioner Deshu was killed by Mahakin.

entries.zh: 永貴與護軍統領努三協殲逆眾，回部平。
entries.en: Yong Gui and garrison commander Nu San jointly destroyed the rebels, pacifying the Muslim territories.
entries.literal: Yong Gui, together with garrison commander Nu San, jointly exterminated the rebels, and the Muslim regions were pacified.

entries.zh: 移倉場侍郎。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice minister of the Granary Directorate.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Granary Directorate.

entries.zh: 擢左都御史。
entries.en: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 二十六年，命赴克什噶爾辦事。
entries.en: In Qianlong 26 he was sent to serve as Kashgar commissioner.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was ordered to go to Kashgar to handle affairs.

entries.zh: 旋授禮部尚書、鑲紅旗漢軍都統，仍駐克什噶爾。
entries.en: He was soon made Minister of Rites and commander of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Martial Force while remaining at Kashgar.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of Rites and commander of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Martial Force, still stationed at Kashgar.

entries.zh: 疏請疏溝渠，興耕稼，議自赫色勒河東南浚渠四十馀裡，引水入赫色勒布伊，材托庸河湍急，宜增堤壩，鑿山石，弱水勢。
entries.en: He memorialized for canal dredging and expanded farming, proposing a canal of over forty li southeast from the Hesele River to irrigate Hesele Buyi; where the swift Caituoyong River ran steep, he urged higher dikes, stone cutting, and measures to reduce the current.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting dredging of canals and promotion of agriculture, proposing to dredge a canal of more than forty li southeast from the Hesele River to draw water into Hesele Buyi; the Caituoyong River ran swift and steep, where dikes and dams should be increased, mountain stone cut, and the water's force weakened.

entries.zh: 召還京師。
entries.en: He was recalled to Beijing.
entries.literal: He was recalled to the capital.

entries.zh: 三十年，烏什回人為亂，復命赴哈什哈爾。
entries.en: In Qianlong 30, when the Muslims of Ush rebelled, he was again sent to Kashgar.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year the Ush Muslims rebelled; he was again ordered to go to Kashgar.

entries.zh: 事平，移駐烏什。
entries.en: After the rebellion was suppressed he was stationed at Ush.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled he moved his station to Ush.

entries.zh: 三十三年，署伊犁將軍。
entries.en: In Qianlong 33 he served as acting Ili general.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he acted as Ili general.

entries.zh: 移吏部，再移禮部。
entries.en: He was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and then back to the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, then again to the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 坐厄魯特兵盜哈薩克馬轉誣哈薩克，辦事大臣巴爾品斷獄未得其實，永貴論劾，語有所諉飾。
entries.en: He was faulted when Oirat troops stole Kazakh horses and shifted blame to the Kazakhs; frontier commissioner Ba'erpin's ruling missed the truth, and Yong Gui's impeachment used evasive language.
entries.literal: He was implicated because Oirat soldiers stole Kazakh horses and then falsely accused the Kazakhs; the frontier commissioner Ba'erpin's judgment did not get at the facts, and Yong Gui's impeachment memorial contained language of evasion and embellishment.

entries.zh: 又以涼州、莊浪滿洲兵損馬當償，誤扣熱河兵餉，召還京師，命授左都御史，命不得用翎頂。
entries.en: He also wrongly docked Rehe troop pay to cover horse losses among Liangzhou and Zhuanglang Manchu garrisons; recalled to Beijing, he was made Left Censor-in-Chief but stripped of peacock feather and finial privileges.
entries.literal: Also, because Liangzhou and Zhuanglang Manchu troops' lost horses were to be compensated, he mistakenly withheld Rehe troops' pay; recalled to the capital, he was ordered appointed Left Censor-in-Chief but forbidden to wear the peacock feather and ruby finial.

entries.zh: 旋移禮部尚書，得用頂帶，仍不得戴翎。
entries.en: He was soon moved to Minister of Rites, allowed his finial cap again, but still denied the peacock feather.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of Rites, permitted to use the finial cap, but still not allowed to wear the feather.

entries.zh: 四十二年，命署大學士，題孝聖憲皇后神主。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 he was named acting Grand Secretary and charged with inscribing the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaoshengxian.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year he was ordered to act as Grand Secretary and to inscribe the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaoshengxian.

entries.zh: 尋補吏部尚書，在阿哥總諳達處行走，賜花翎。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Minister of Personnel, assigned to the princes' chief instructorship, and awarded the peacock feather.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was made Minister of Personnel, served on duty in the princes' chief instructorship, and was granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 初，山東民王倫為亂，給事中李漱芳陳奏饑民釀釁，坐妄言，左授禮部主事。
entries.en: Earlier, when Wang Lun of Shandong rose in rebellion, Supervising Secretary Li Shufang had warned that famine victims were brewing unrest; he was demoted to a Rites Ministry secretary for what was judged reckless speech.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Shandong commoner Wang Lun rebelled, Supervising Secretary Li Shufang memorialized that famine victims were brewing trouble; for reckless speech he was demoted to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 及是，吏部請以漱芳升授員外郎。
entries.en: Now the Ministry of Personnel proposed promoting Shufang to assistant department director.
entries.literal: At this time the Ministry of Personnel requested promoting Shufang to assistant department director.

entries.zh: 上責永貴市恩，削職奪花翎，令以三品頂帶赴烏什辦事。
entries.en: The emperor accused Yong Gui of trading favors, stripped his rank and peacock feather, and sent him to Ush with a third-rank cap.
entries.literal: The emperor reproached Yong Gui for currying favor, stripped his office and took back the peacock feather, and ordered him to go to Ush to handle affairs with a third-rank finial cap.

entries.zh: 詔詰責甚至，且言：「永貴回烏什，如不實心任事，必在彼處正法。」
entries.en: The edict rebuked him harshly, declaring: "If Yong Gui returns to Ush and does not serve wholeheartedly, he will be executed there."
entries.literal: The edict rebuked him severely, saying: "If Yong Gui returns to Ush and does not serve in earnest, he will certainly be executed on the spot there."

entries.zh: 先是葉爾羌辦事大臣侍郎高樸役回民采玉，並婪取金珠，為諸伯克所訟。
entries.en: Earlier, Yarkand commissioner Gao Pu had forced Muslim subjects to mine jade and extorted gold and gems, provoking lawsuits from the local begs.
entries.literal: Earlier the Yarkand frontier commissioner, Vice Minister Gao Pu, had forced Muslim commoners to gather jade and had greedily taken gold and gems, and was sued by the begs.

entries.zh: 永貴如葉爾羌，訊得實，聞上。
entries.en: Yong Gui went to Yarkand, confirmed the charges, and reported to the throne.
entries.literal: Yong Gui went to Yarkand, investigated and found the facts true, and reported to the emperor.

entries.zh: 上為誅高樸，手詔嘉永貴持正，並謂：「永貴罪不至貶。
entries.en: The emperor executed Gao Pu and wrote personally to praise Yong Gui's integrity, adding: "Yong Gui's offense did not warrant demotion.
entries.literal: The emperor had Gao Pu executed, and in a personal edict praised Yong Gui for uprightness, also saying: "Yong Gui's offense did not warrant demotion.

entries.zh: 今命西行，適以發高樸之姦，潛銷禍萌，此天啟朕衷也！」
entries.en: Sending him west now exposed Gao Pu's crimes and quietly removed a growing threat—Heaven has guided My purpose!"
entries.literal: Now, ordering him westward, it happened to expose Gao Pu's wickedness and quietly remove the sprout of disaster—this is Heaven opening My mind!"

entries.zh: 仍授吏部尚書，賜花翎。
entries.en: He was reappointed Minister of Personnel and given back the peacock feather.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Minister of Personnel and granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 尋授參贊大臣。
entries.en: He was soon made an assisting grand minister.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed assisting grand minister.

entries.zh: 四十四年，召還京師，授鑲藍旗滿洲都統。
entries.en: In Qianlong 44 he was recalled to Beijing and made commander of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchus.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was recalled to the capital and appointed commander of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchu force.

entries.zh: 四十五年，協辦大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 45 he became associate Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was made associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 四十八年，卒，諡文勤。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48 he died and was posthumously titled Wénqín (Cultivated and Diligent).
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wénqín.

entries.zh: 永貴端謹。
entries.en: Yong Gui was upright and conscientious.
entries.literal: Yong Gui was upright and cautious.

entries.zh: 初直軍機處，與阿桂齊名，時稱「二桂」。
entries.en: Early in his career he served in the Grand Council alongside Agui; the pair were known as "the two Guis."
entries.literal: Early on he served in the Grand Council and was as famous as Agui; at the time they were called "the two Guis."

entries.zh: 其撫浙江，有廉聲。
entries.en: As Zhejiang governor he earned a reputation for integrity.
entries.literal: In governing Zhejiang he had a reputation for integrity.

entries.zh: 子 伊江阿 子伊江阿，官至山東巡撫。
entries.en: Son: Yijiang'a. His son Yijiang'a rose to governor of Shandong.
entries.literal: Son: Yijiang'a. His son Yijiang'a rose to governor of Shandong.

entries.zh: 高宗崩，伊江阿因奏事附書和珅勸節哀。
entries.en: After the Qianlong Emperor's death, Yijiang'a attached to a routine memorial a note urging Heshen to moderate his mourning.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor died, Yijiang'a, in a routine memorial, enclosed a letter urging Heshen to moderate his grief.

entries.zh: 和□申已下獄，仁宗得其書，詔詰責，奪職。
entries.en: Heshen was already in prison; the Jiaqing Emperor obtained the letter, rebuked him by edict, and dismissed him.
entries.literal: Heshen was already imprisoned; the Renzong Emperor obtained the letter, issued an edict of stern rebuke, and stripped him of office.

entries.zh: 既，又追論在山東日佞佛寬盜，命戍伊犁。
entries.en: He was later prosecuted for promoting Buddhism and being lenient toward bandits while in Shandong and was banished to Ili.
entries.literal: Afterward he was again prosecuted for flattering Buddhism and being lenient toward bandits during his days in Shandong, and was ordered exiled to Ili.

entries.zh: 尋授藍翎侍衛、古城領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was soon made a blue-lance guardsman and frontier commandant at Gucheng.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed a blue-lance guardsman and commandant at Gucheng.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 蔡新，字次明，福建漳浦人，贈尚書世遠族子。
entries.en: Cai Xin, styled Ciming, came from Zhangpu in Fujian and was a kinsman of the posthumously honored Minister Shi Yuan.
entries.literal: Cai Xin, style Ciming, was a native of Zhangpu, Fujian, and a clansman of the posthumously honored Minister Shi Yuan.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 1 (1736), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 入直上書房。
entries.en: He was assigned to the Upper Study.
entries.literal: He entered service in the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 試御史第一，辭，授侍講。
entries.en: He topped the censor examination but declined the post and was made an expositor.
entries.literal: He ranked first in the censor examination but declined and was appointed expositor.

entries.zh: 累遷工部侍郎，移刑部。
entries.en: He rose through several ranks to Vice Minister of Works and was then moved to the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: He was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 十八年，以母老請歸省，賜其母貂緞；
entries.en: In Qianlong 18 he asked leave to visit his elderly mother and the court bestowed sable fur on her;
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, because his mother was aged he requested leave to return home to visit her, and sable fur was bestowed on his mother;

entries.zh: 旋乞終養，允之。
entries.en: he then asked to retire permanently to care for her, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: he then begged to retire permanently to care for her, and this was granted.

entries.zh: 即家命為上書房總師傅，辭，高宗諭之曰：「非令汝即來供職，待後日耳。」
entries.en: At home he was named chief tutor of the Upper Study but declined; the Qianlong Emperor told him: "I am not asking you to take up duty at once—only for some later day."
entries.literal: While at home he was ordered to be chief tutor of the Upper Study; he declined, and the Gaozong Emperor instructed him: "This is not ordering you to come immediately to serve; it is for a later day."

entries.zh: 二十五年，上五十壽，入京師祝嘏。
entries.en: In Qianlong 25, for the emperor's fiftieth birthday, he went to Beijing to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when the emperor reached fifty, he entered the capital to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 二十六年，南巡，覲行在。
entries.en: In Qianlong 26 he had an audience with the emperor during the southern tour.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, on the southern tour, he had an audience at the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 母喪終，授刑部侍郎。
entries.en: After his mother's mourning period he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: When his mourning for his mother ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 三十二年，擢工部尚書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 32 he was made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 三十八年，移禮部。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38 he was moved to the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 四十五年，命以吏部尚書協辦大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 45 he was made associate Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was ordered to serve as associate Grand Secretary while Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 四十六年，乞假修墓。
entries.en: In Qianlong 46 he took leave to repair family tombs.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year he begged leave to repair tombs.

entries.zh: 四十八年，還朝。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48 he returned to court.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he returned to court.

entries.zh: 拜文華殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was appointed Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was appointed Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 五十年，與千叟宴。
entries.en: In Qianlong 50 he attended the banquet of a thousand elders.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year he attended the banquet of a thousand elders.

entries.zh: 上臨雍講學，新以大學士領國子監，講易「天行健，君子以自強不息」，賜茶並文綺。
entries.en: When the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Xin, as Grand Secretary and head of the Directorate of Education, expounded the line "Heaven moves with strength; the noble man strengthens himself without ceasing" and received tea and brocade.
entries.literal: When the emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Xin, as Grand Secretary heading the Directorate of Education, lectured on the Changes: "Heaven moves with strength; the noble man thereby strengthens himself without ceasing," and was granted tea and patterned silks.

entries.zh: 新操履端謹，言行必衷於禮法。
entries.en: Xin was upright and cautious, and his words and deeds always conformed to ritual propriety.
entries.literal: Xin's conduct was upright and cautious; in word and deed he always adhered to ritual and law.

entries.zh: 上眷之厚，賦臨雍詩，注謂：「今群臣孰可當三老五更？
entries.en: The emperor favored him deeply; in a poem on the Academy lecture he wrote: "Which minister today could serve as the Three Elders and Five Geng?
entries.literal: The emperor favored him deeply; in a poem on lecturing at the Academy he noted: "Among the ministers today, who could serve as the Three Elders and Five Geng?

entries.zh: 獨新長朕四歲，或可居兄事。
entries.en: Only Xin is four years my senior and might be treated as an elder brother.
entries.literal: Only Xin is four years older than I and might be treated as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 然恐其局促勿敢當，舉王導對晉元帝語以謝耳。」
entries.en: Yet I fear he would be too modest to accept and would cite Wang Dao's reply to Emperor Yuan of Jin in declining."
entries.literal: Yet I fear he would be constrained and not dare accept, and would cite Wang Dao's reply to Emperor Yuan of Jin in declining."

entries.zh: 新上疏乞致仕，語切至，上許其歸，加太子太師，三賦詩以餞。
entries.en: Xin memorialized to retire in earnest terms; the emperor allowed him to go home, made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and composed three farewell poems.
entries.literal: Xin memorialized begging to retire; his words were earnest, and the emperor permitted his return, adding the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and composing three poems to see him off.

entries.zh: 既歸，上每製文，屢以寄新，且曰：「在朝無可與言古文者。
entries.en: After he retired, the emperor often sent him new compositions, saying: "At court there is no one with whom I can discuss classical prose.
entries.literal: After his return, whenever the emperor composed writings he often sent them to Xin, saying: "At court there is no one with whom to discuss ancient-style prose.

entries.zh: 不可阿好徒稱頌。」
entries.en: Do not flatter me with empty praise."
entries.literal: You must not flatter me with empty praise."

entries.zh: 五十五年，上八十壽，詣京師祝嘏，賜宴同樂園，賜人葠一斤。
entries.en: In Qianlong 55, for the emperor's eightieth birthday, he went to Beijing to congratulate him, was feasted at the Garden of Shared Joy, and received one jin of ginseng.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, when the emperor reached eighty, he went to the capital to offer congratulations, was feasted at the Garden of Shared Joy, and granted one jin of ginseng.

entries.zh: 及歸，命歸途所經，有司具舟車護行。
entries.en: On his return journey local officials along the route were ordered to provide boats and carriages as an escort.
entries.literal: On his return he was ordered that along the route local officials should provide boats and carriages to escort him.

entries.zh: 上仍以詩文寄新，諭將以驗學詣，戒詩毋和韻。
entries.en: The emperor continued sending him poems and essays, telling him that when he came to demonstrate his learning he should not write matching-rhyme verse.
entries.literal: The emperor still sent poems and essays to Xin, instructing that when he came to test his learning he should not compose matching-rhyme poems.

entries.zh: 五十七年，重赴鹿鳴宴。
entries.en: In Qianlong 57 he again attended the Deer Call banquet.
entries.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he again attended the Deer Call banquet.

entries.zh: 六十年，上御極六十載，諭新不必入賀。
entries.en: In Qianlong 60, when the emperor marked sixty years on the throne, he told Xin he need not come to court to congratulate him.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year, when the emperor had reigned sixty years, he instructed Xin that he need not come to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 新奏言上九旬萬壽，冀再詣闕祝嘏。
entries.en: Xin memorialized that he hoped to come to court again when the emperor reached ninety.
entries.literal: Xin memorialized that when the emperor reached ninety he hoped to come again to the palace to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 上諭之曰：「覽奏，字字出誠心，我君臣共勉之。
entries.en: The emperor replied: "Every word of your memorial speaks from the heart; let us encourage one another as ruler and minister.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Having read your memorial, every word comes from sincerity; let us ruler and minister encourage one another.

entries.zh: 若天恩得符所原，實佳話也！」
entries.en: If Heaven grants your wish, it will be a fine story indeed!"
entries.literal: If Heaven's grace fulfills your wish, it will truly be a fine story!"

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，新年九十，賜額曰「綠野恆春」​​，侑以諸珍物。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 1, when Xin turned ninety, the court bestowed the plaque "Evergreen in the Green Fields" along with many precious gifts.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when Xin reached ninety, he was granted an inscription reading "Evergreen in the Green Fields," together with many precious objects.

entries.zh: 四年，高宗崩，奔赴，至福州，病不能進。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 4, when the Qianlong Emperor died, he set out to attend the mourning but fell ill at Fuzhou and could go no farther.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, when the Gaozong Emperor died, he hurried to attend but reached Fuzhou and, ill, could not proceed.

entries.zh: 巡撫汪志伊以聞，溫詔止其行。
entries.en: Governor Wang Zhiyi reported his condition, and a gracious edict told him to turn back.
entries.literal: Governor Wang Zhiyi reported this, and a warm edict ordered him to stop his journey.

entries.zh: 是冬，卒，贈太傅，諡文端。
entries.en: That winter he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wénduān (Cultivated and Steady).
entries.literal: That winter he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the title Wénduān.

entries.zh: 新學以求仁為宗，以不動心為要。
entries.en: Xin's learning aimed at benevolence and prized an unmoved mind.
entries.literal: Xin's learning took seeking benevolence as its aim and an unmoved mind as its essential point.

entries.zh: 嘗輯先儒操心、養心、存心、求放心諸語，曰事心錄。
entries.en: He compiled earlier Confucian teachings on mind-cultivation into Records of Mind-Cultivation.
entries.literal: He once compiled sayings of earlier Confucians on tending the mind, nourishing the mind, preserving the mind, and recovering the lost mind, entitled Records of Mind-Cultivation.

entries.zh: 直上書房四十二年，培養啟迪，動必稱儒先。
entries.en: For forty-two years in the Upper Study he nurtured the princes, always invoking the sages of old.
entries.literal: In the Upper Study for forty-two years he nurtured and enlightened, always invoking the sages of old in his teaching.

entries.zh: 高宗以新究心根柢，守世遠家法，深敬禮之。
entries.en: Qianlong deeply honored him for his mastery of moral foundations and for upholding the family tradition of Shi Yuan.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor, because Xin had penetrated the roots of the mind and kept the family tradition of Shi Yuan, deeply honored him.

entries.zh: 既歸，福建督撫坐貪黷、虧倉庫得重譴，上責「新知而不言，自比寒蟬，無體國公忠之意」。
entries.en: After he retired, Fujian's top officials were heavily punished for corruption and granary shortfalls; the emperor rebuked Xin: "You knew but kept silent, like a winter cicada—where was your loyalty to the state?"
entries.literal: After his return, the Fujian governor-general and governor were heavily punished for corruption and granary deficits; the emperor reproached Xin: "You knew but did not speak, likening yourself to a winter cicada, without the spirit of serving the state with public loyalty."

entries.zh: 新上疏請下吏議，卒以篤老寬之。
entries.en: Xin asked to be handed over for official judgment; in the end his great age won him leniency.
entries.literal: Xin memorialized asking to be handed over to the officials for judgment; in the end he was leniently treated on account of his great age.

entries.zh: 嘉慶初，海盜方肆，新子本俊官京師，御史宋樹疏言新家書及海盜事，不以聞。
entries.en: Early in Jiaqing, when pirates were rampant, Xin's son Benjun served in Beijing; Censor Song Shu charged that family letters from Xin about piracy had not been reported to the throne.
entries.literal: Early in Jiaqing, when pirates were rampant, Xin's son Benjun held office in the capital; Censor Song Shu memorialized that family letters from Xin concerning pirates had not been reported.

entries.zh: 上為詰本俊，本俊言新已具疏令謄真入奏，上亦不之責，仍諭新毋畏。
entries.en: The emperor questioned Benjun, who said Xin had already drafted a memorial for submission; the emperor did not blame him and told Xin not to be afraid.
entries.literal: The emperor questioned Benjun; Benjun said Xin had already prepared a memorial and ordered a fair copy for submission; the emperor did not blame him and still instructed Xin not to fear.

entries.zh: 新家居謙慎，遇丞尉執禮必恭。
entries.en: In retirement he was humble; he always treated local magistrates and constables with full courtesy.
entries.literal: At home Xin was humble and cautious; when he met assistant magistrates and constables he always observed ritual with respect.

entries.zh: 或問之，曰：「欲使鄉人知位至宰相，亦必敬本籍官吏，庶心有所不敢，犯法者鮮耳。」
entries.en: When asked why, he said: "I want my neighbors to see that even a chief minister must respect local officials, so they will think twice before breaking the law."
entries.literal: When asked, he said: "I wish the people of my district to know that even one who reaches the rank of chief minister must still respect the officials of his native place, so that in their hearts they will not dare, and lawbreakers will be few."

entries.zh: 著有緝齋詩文集。
entries.en: He left the Jizhai collected poems and essays.
entries.literal: He authored the Jizhai collected poems and essays.

entries.zh: 程景伊，字聘三，江南武進人。
entries.en: Cheng Jingyi, styled Pingsan, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Cheng Jingyi, style Pingsan, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 乾隆四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 4 (1739), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 再遷侍讀學士，命在上書房行走。
entries.en: He was promoted to Hanlin reader and assigned to the Upper Study.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to reader of the Hanlin Academy and ordered to serve on duty in the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 復三遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: After three further promotions he became Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: After three more promotions he became Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 景伊致人書，言：「承乏中樞，晨夕內廷多曠廢。
entries.en: Jingyi wrote to an acquaintance: "Holding a central post, I neglect my duties morning and evening in the inner court.
entries.literal: Jingyi sent someone a letter saying: "Holding a post at the center, morning and evening in the inner court much is neglected.

entries.zh: 今秋未與木蘭之役，稍得專心職業。」
entries.en: This autumn I missed the Mulan hunt and can finally focus on my work."
entries.literal: This autumn I did not join the Mulan hunt and can somewhat concentrate on my duties."

entries.zh: 為上聞，責其躭逸，解上書房行走。
entries.en: The emperor heard of it, rebuked him for idleness, and removed him from the Upper Study.
entries.literal: This came to the emperor's ears; he reproached him for indulgence in ease and relieved him of duty in the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 歷禮、工諸部。
entries.en: He served in the Ministries of Rites and Works among others.
entries.literal: He served in the Ministries of Rites and Works among others.

entries.zh: 三十四年，擢工部尚書，歷刑、吏諸部。
entries.en: In Qianlong 34 he was made Minister of Works and later served in the Ministries of Justice and Personnel.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Works and passed through the Ministries of Justice and Personnel.

entries.zh: 三十八年，協辦大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38 he became associate Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was made associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 四十一年，上東巡迴鑾，駐蹕黃新莊。
entries.en: In Qianlong 41, on the emperor's return from an eastern tour, the court halted at Huangxinzhuang.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year the emperor made an eastern tour and returned; halting at Huangxinzhuang,

entries.zh: 景伊與在京王大臣迎駕，未召見即退班，命奪職，仍留任。
entries.en: Jingyi joined the Beijing princes and ministers in welcoming the emperor but left before being received; he was stripped of rank but kept in office.
entries.literal: Jingyi, together with princes and grand ministers in the capital who welcomed the imperial carriage, withdrew from attendance before being summoned; he was ordered stripped of office but still retained in his post.

entries.zh: 四十四年，授文淵閣大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 44 he was made Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 四十五年，上南巡，命景伊留京治事。
entries.en: In Qianlong 45, during the southern tour, he was left in Beijing to manage affairs.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year, on the southern tour, he was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.

entries.zh: 上還京師，入對，以景伊病後衰弱，命安心調理，勿勉強行走。
entries.en: When the emperor returned, Jingyi had an audience; finding him weak after illness, the emperor told him to rest and not force himself to attend duty.
entries.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital and Jingyi had an audience, because Jingyi was weak after illness he was ordered to rest and recuperate in peace and not force himself to attend duty.

entries.zh: 七月，卒，諡文恭。
entries.en: He died in the seventh month and was posthumously titled Wéngōng (Cultivated and Respectful).
entries.literal: In the seventh month he died and was given the posthumous title Wéngōng.

entries.zh: 梁國治，字階平，浙江會稽人。
entries.en: Liang Guozhi, styled Jieping, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Liang Guozhi, style Jieping, was a native of Kuaiji, Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。
entries.en: In Qianlong 13 (1748) he took first place in the jinshi examination and was appointed a reviser.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination as top graduate of the first class and was appointed reviser.

entries.zh: 遷國子監司業。
entries.en: He was made vice director of the Directorate of Education.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be vice director of the Directorate of Education.

entries.zh: 充廣東鄉試正考官。
entries.en: He served as chief examiner of the Guangdong provincial examination.
entries.literal: He served as chief examiner of the Guangdong provincial examination.

entries.zh: 復命，奏對稱旨，命以道員發廣東待缺。
entries.en: On reporting back, his audience pleased the emperor, who sent him to Guangdong as a circuit intendant awaiting appointment.
entries.literal: On reporting back, his audience responses pleased the emperor, and he was ordered dispatched to Guangdong as a circuit intendant awaiting a vacancy.

entries.zh: 旋除惠嘉潮道，移署糧驛道。
entries.en: He was soon appointed to the Huizhou-Jiaying-Chaozhou Circuit and then acted as grain and courier intendant.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed to the Huizhou-Jiaying-Chaozhou Circuit and then transferred to act as grain and courier intendant.

entries.zh: 卓異引見，擢署左副都御史。
entries.en: Cited for outstanding merit, he was promoted to acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Cited for outstanding merit and presented to the throne, he was promoted to act as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was made Vice Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 廣東總督楊廷璋等追論國治署糧驛道時失察家人舞弊，讞實，奪職。
entries.en: Guangdong Governor-General Yang Tingzhang prosecuted him for failing to detect household fraud while acting as grain intendant; the charge was sustained and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: Guangdong Governor-General Yang Tingzhang and others pursued the case that when Guozhi acted as grain and courier intendant he failed to detect household servants' fraud; the judgment was confirmed and he was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 起授山西冀寧道。
entries.en: He was reinstated as Shanxi Jining Circuit intendant.
entries.literal: He was reappointed and made Shanxi Jining Circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 三遷湖北巡撫。
entries.en: After three promotions he became governor of Hubei.
entries.literal: After three promotions he became governor of Hubei.

entries.zh: 三十四年，命署湖廣總督，兼荊州將軍。
entries.en: In Qianlong 34 he was named acting Huguang governor-general and concurrent Jingzhou general.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered to act as governor-general of Huguang and concurrently as Jingzhou general.

entries.zh: 時湖北頻歲水旱，治賑，缺倉穀四十八萬馀石。
entries.en: Hubei had suffered repeated floods and droughts; relief efforts left granaries short by over four hundred eighty thousand piculs.
entries.literal: At that time Hubei had floods and droughts in successive years; in managing relief the granaries were short by more than four hundred eighty thousand piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 國治議發司庫白金二十萬，俟秋穫易穀，來歲春夏間出糶，石溢銀一錢。
entries.en: Guozhi proposed releasing two hundred thousand taels from the provincial treasury to buy grain after the autumn harvest and sell it the following spring and summer at one tael profit per picul.
entries.literal: Guozhi proposed disbursing two hundred thousand taels of treasury silver from the provincial treasury, waiting until the autumn harvest to exchange for grain, then in the spring and summer of the coming year selling grain, with one tael profit per picul.

entries.zh: 行之數年，倉穀得無缺。
entries.en: After several years the granaries were kept full.
entries.literal: Carried out for several years, the granaries were kept without shortage.

entries.zh: 三十六年，移湖南巡撫。
entries.en: In Qianlong 36 he was moved to Hunan governor.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to governor of Hunan.

entries.zh: 師徵金川，治軍械，造藥彈，費不給。
entries.en: During the Jinchuan campaign he supplied arms and ammunition, but funds ran short.
entries.literal: When the army campaigned against Jinchuan, he managed military equipment and manufactured gunpowder and shells, but funds were insufficient.

entries.zh: 國治請以司庫儲備軍興白金十馀萬，照一年應扣各糧通行借給，仍分三年扣還歸款。
entries.en: Guozhi asked to lend over one hundred thousand taels from military reserves, advancing it against annual grain quotas to be repaid over three years.
entries.literal: Guozhi requested using more than one hundred thousand taels of treasury silver reserved for military expenses, lending it broadly according to each year's grain deductions, to be repaid in installments over three years.

entries.zh: 國治又以出征將弁，例軍中升用，本營缺出，仍系照常拔補。
entries.en: Guozhi also noted that officers on campaign were promoted in the field while home-camp vacancies were filled by routine seniority.
entries.literal: Guozhi also noted that for officers on campaign, promotion was customarily made in the army, while vacancies in their home camps were still filled by routine selection.

entries.zh: 循資按格者，轉得坐致升遷；
entries.en: Those who advanced by seniority could gain promotion without fighting;
entries.literal: those who advanced by seniority and qualification could sit and obtain promotion;

entries.zh: 冒敵衝鋒者，專待軍營缺出，無以鼓勵戎行。
entries.en: while men who charged the enemy had to wait for field vacancies—giving little incentive to valor.
entries.literal: while those who braved the enemy in the charge had only to wait for army vacancies, giving no encouragement to military service.

entries.zh: 請嗣後本營缺出，與出征將弁一體論升。
entries.en: He asked that home-camp vacancies and campaign officers be considered together for promotion.
entries.literal: He requested that thereafter home-camp vacancies and officers on campaign be considered together for promotion.

entries.zh: 皆從其請。
entries.en: All his proposals were approved.
entries.literal: All his requests were granted.

entries.zh: 三十八年，召還京師，命在軍機處行走，並直南書房。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38 he was recalled to Beijing, assigned to the Grand Council, and also to the Southern Study.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was recalled to the capital, ordered to serve on duty in the Grand Council, and also assigned to the Southern Study.

entries.zh: 三十九年，授戶部右侍郎。
entries.en: In Qianlong 39 he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 四十二年，遷尚書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 he was promoted to minister.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year he was transferred to minister.

entries.zh: 四十七年，加太子少傅。
entries.en: In Qianlong 47 he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 四十八年，命協辦大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48 he was made associate Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was ordered to serve as associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 五十年，晉授東閣大學士，兼戶部尚書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 50 he was promoted to Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrent Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year he was advanced to Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 五十一年，卒，加太子太保，諡文定。
entries.en: In Qianlong 51 he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the title Wéndìng (Cultivated and Settled).
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year he died; he was given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wéndìng.

entries.zh: 國治父文標，官刑部司獄，卹囚有惠政。
entries.en: Guozhi's father Wenbiao was a jailer in the Ministry of Justice known for humane treatment of prisoners.
entries.literal: Guozhi's father Wenbiao served as a jailer in the Ministry of Justice and showed compassionate policy toward prisoners.

entries.zh: 國治篤孝友，與兄孿生，兄蚤卒，終生不稱壽，事嫂如母。
entries.en: Guozhi was deeply filial; his twin brother died young, and he never celebrated his own birthday, treating his sister-in-law as his mother.
entries.literal: Guozhi was deeply filial and brotherly; he and his elder brother were twins; the brother died early, and all his life he never spoke of longevity, treating his sister-in-law as a mother.

entries.zh: 治事敬慎縝密。
entries.en: In office he was reverent, cautious, and meticulous.
entries.literal: In handling affairs he was reverent, cautious, and meticulous.

entries.zh: 生平無疾言遽色，然不可以私幹。
entries.en: He was never harsh or abrupt in manner, yet would not be moved by private appeals.
entries.literal: Throughout his life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger, yet private requests could not sway him.

entries.zh: 門下士有求入按察使幕主刑名者，戒之曰：「心術不可不慎！」
entries.en: When a follower sought a post on a surveillance commissioner's staff handling criminal law, he warned: "You must be scrupulous in your principles!"
entries.literal: A follower asked to enter a surveillance commissioner's staff to handle criminal law; he warned him: "One's inner principles must not be treated carelessly!"

entries.zh: 其人請改治錢穀，則曰：「刑名不慎，不過殺一人，所殺必有數，且為人所共知。
entries.en: The man asked to handle revenue and grain instead; he said: "Carelessness in criminal law kills at most one person—the toll is finite and public.
entries.literal: The man asked instead to handle revenue and grain accounts; he said: "If criminal law is handled carelessly, at most one person is killed; the number killed is definite and known to all.

entries.zh: 錢穀厲人，十倍刑名，當時不覺。
entries.en: Revenue and grain work harms people ten times more than criminal law, though the harm is not felt at once.
entries.literal: Revenue and grain harm people tenfold over criminal law, though at the time one does not notice.

entries.zh: 近數十年，遠或數百年，流毒至於無窮，且未有已！」
entries.en: Within decades, or centuries hence, the poison spreads without end and never stops!"
entries.literal: In the near term decades, in the far term perhaps centuries, the poison spreads without end and has not ceased!"

entries.zh: 卒不許。
entries.en: In the end he refused.
entries.literal: In the end he did not permit it.

entries.zh: 著有敬思堂集。
entries.en: He left the Jingsi Hall collected works.
entries.literal: He authored the Jingsi Hall collected works.

entries.zh: 英廉，字計六，馮氏，內務府漢軍鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Ying Lian, styled Jiliu, of the Feng clan, was a Chinese Martial Force bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: Ying Lian, style Jiliu, of the Feng clan, was a Chinese Martial Force bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 雍正十年舉人。
entries.en: He passed the provincial examination in Yongzheng 10 (1732).
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he passed the provincial examination.

entries.zh: 自筆帖式授內務府主事。
entries.en: He rose from a clerkship to a secretaryship in the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: From a clerk's post he was appointed a secretary in the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，命往江南河工學習，補淮安府外河同知。
entries.en: At the start of the Qianlong reign he was sent to Jiangnan to train in river engineering, then appointed sub-prefect for outer-river works in Huaian Prefecture.
entries.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign he was ordered to go to Jiangnan to study river works, and was appointed sub-prefect in charge of outer-river works in Huaian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 累遷永定河道。
entries.en: He rose through successive postings to commissioner of the Yongding River.
entries.literal: Through repeated promotions he became commissioner of the Yongding River.

entries.zh: 河決，總督方觀承劾英廉淤溝鑲埽，衝陷水上月堤，匿不以聞，遂誤要工。
entries.en: When the river breached, Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian for silt-choked ditches and inset revetments that had burst and collapsed a moon-shaped dike above the water; Ying Lian had kept silent about it, delaying essential repairs.
entries.literal: The river breached; Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian, charging that silted ditches and inset revetments had burst and collapsed the above-water moon-shaped dike; he concealed this without reporting it, thereby delaying urgent repair work.

entries.zh: 奪職，逮治，英廉抗辨。
entries.en: Stripped of office and taken into custody, Ying Lian contested the charges.
entries.literal: His post was stripped, he was arrested for trial, and Ying Lian argued in his defense.

entries.zh: 逾年讞未決，觀承請遣大臣蒞其事。
entries.en: After more than a year without a verdict, Guancheng asked that a senior minister be dispatched to try the case.
entries.literal: More than a year passed without a verdict; Guancheng requested that a high minister be sent to preside over the case.

entries.zh: 上命尚書舒赫德會鞫，言英廉申報不以實，且未將淤溝先事預防，堵築經費，當責出私財以償。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Minister Shu Hede to sit jointly in judgment. The court found that Ying Lian had filed false reports and failed to guard against the silted ditches beforehand; he was to make restitution for blocking and construction costs from his own purse.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister Shu Hede to join in the trial; the finding was that Ying Lian's reports had not been truthful, and that he had not taken preventive measures against the silted ditches in advance; the costs of blocking and building works should be recovered from his private funds.

entries.zh: 上諭言：「英廉上官未及兩月，淤溝失防，咎實在前政。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Ying Lian had been in office less than two months; the breach at the silted ditch was really the fault of his predecessor.
entries.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Ying Lian had held office less than two months; the failure to guard the silted ditch—the blame truly lies with the previous administration.

entries.zh: 然觀承以總督劾屬吏，不敢率意入罪，讞逾年未定，請遣大臣蒞其事。
entries.en: Still, as governor-general prosecuting a subordinate, Guancheng would not convict lightly; the case dragged on for over a year before he asked for a senior minister to take it over.
entries.literal: Yet Guancheng, as governor-general impeaching a subordinate, did not dare to convict rashly; the case remained undecided for more than a year, and he requested that a high minister be sent to preside over it.

entries.zh: 是其心有所警畏，亦朕明慎庶政之效。
entries.en: That shows a salutary fear in his heart—and also the fruit of My own careful stewardship of public affairs.
entries.literal: This shows his mind holds some caution and awe; it is also the effect of My clear and careful governance of common affairs.

entries.zh: 仍從其請。」
entries.en: The request was granted."
entries.literal: His request was still granted."

entries.zh: 未幾，命在高樑橋迤西稻田廠效力。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was ordered to perform menial duty at the Daotian Farm west of Gaoliang Bridge.
entries.literal: Not long after, he was ordered to serve at the Daotian Farm west of Gaoliang Bridge.

entries.zh: 尋復自筆帖式授內務府主事。
entries.en: He was soon restored from clerk to secretary in the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: Soon he was again appointed a secretary in the Imperial Household Department from the rank of clerk.

entries.zh: 累遷內務府正黃旗護軍統領。
entries.en: He rose to commander of the Plain Yellow Banner guard corps in the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: Through repeated promotions he became commander of the guards of the Plain Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 外授江寧布政使，兼織造。
entries.en: Posted outside the capital as Jiangning financial commissioner, he also supervised imperial textile production.
entries.literal: He was assigned to an external post as financial commissioner of Jiangning, concurrently overseeing textile manufacture.

entries.zh: 英廉以父老，乞留京師，賜二品銜，授內務府大臣、戶部侍郎。
entries.en: Citing his father's age, Ying Lian asked to stay in Beijing; he was given second-rank honors and made Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department and Vice Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: Ying Lian, because his father was old, begged to remain in the capital; he was granted second-rank status and appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department and Vice Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 三十四年，徵緬甸，師行，命與尚書托庸等董其事。
entries.en: In Qianlong 34 (1769), when troops marched against Burma, he was ordered to manage logistics alongside Minister Tuoyong and others.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when an expedition was launched against Burma and the army marched, he was ordered together with Minister Tuoyong and others to oversee the matter.

entries.zh: 遷刑部尚書，仍兼戶部侍郎、正黃旗滿洲都統。
entries.en: He became Minister of Punishments while retaining his posts as Vice Minister of Revenue and Manchu commander of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, still concurrently holding the posts of Vice Minister of Revenue and commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 三十九年，侍郎高樸劾左都御史觀保，侍郎申保、倪承寬、吳壇交內監高雲從，洩道府記載。
entries.en: In Qianlong 39 (1774), Vice Minister Gao Pu impeached Censor-in-Chief Guan Bao, charging that Vice Ministers Shen Bao, Ni Chengkuan, and Wu Tan had dealings with the eunuch Gao Yuncong and leaked provincial inspection records.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Vice Minister Gao Pu impeached Censor-in-Chief Guan Bao; Vice Ministers Shen Bao, Ni Chengkuan, and Wu Tan associated with the eunuch Gao Yuncong and leaked circuit and prefectural inspection records.

entries.zh: 上問英廉，英廉謝不知。
entries.en: When the Emperor questioned Ying Lian, he claimed not to know.
entries.literal: The Emperor questioned Ying Lian; Ying Lian pleaded ignorance.

entries.zh: 詔詰責，命奪職，從寬留任。
entries.en: An edict rebuked him and ordered his dismissal, but he was leniently permitted to keep serving.
entries.literal: An edict reprimanded him; he was ordered stripped of office, but leniently allowed to remain at his post.

entries.zh: 京師商人投呈皇六子，有所陳請，事下內務府。
entries.en: When a Beijing merchant petitioned the Sixth Imperial Son with a request, the case was sent down to the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: A Beijing merchant submitted a petition to the Sixth Imperial Son with certain requests; the matter was referred to the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 上召內務府諸大臣，問：「收呈者誰也？」
entries.en: The Emperor summoned the department's senior ministers and asked, "Who accepted the petition?"
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned all grand ministers of the Imperial Household Department and asked: "Who received the petition?"

entries.zh: 英廉、金簡皆謝不知。
entries.en: Both Ying Lian and Jin Jian claimed ignorance.
entries.literal: Ying Lian and Jin Jian both pleaded ignorance.

entries.zh: 邁拉遜乃言「六阿哥收呈」。
entries.en: Maila Sun then said, "The Sixth Prince took it in."
entries.literal: Maila Sun then said, "The Sixth Prince received the petition."

entries.zh: 上責英廉、金簡隱諱，下部議，命寬之，仍註冊。
entries.en: The Emperor censured Ying Lian and Jin Jian for suppressing the truth; after ministry review they were treated leniently, but the offense was recorded.
entries.literal: The Emperor rebuked Ying Lian and Jin Jian for concealment; the matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation; they were ordered leniency, but the offense was still entered in the register.

entries.zh: 四十二年，協辦大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 (1777) he became Assistant Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year he was made Assistant Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 四十四年，暫署直隸總督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 44 (1779) he acted temporarily as Governor-General of Zhili.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he temporarily served as acting Governor-General of Zhili.

entries.zh: 四十五年，大學士於敏中卒，上以英廉本漢軍，協辦有年，特授漢大學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 45 (1780), after Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong died, the Emperor— noting that Ying Lian was Chinese Martial Force and had long served as assistant grand secretary— made him a Han-rank Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong died; because Ying Lian was originally Chinese Martial Force and had served as assistant grand secretary for years, the Emperor specially appointed him Grand Secretary of Han rank.

entries.zh: 漢軍授漢大學士自英廉始。
entries.en: Ying Lian was the first Chinese Martial Force bannerman raised to Han Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: Appointment of a Chinese Martial Force bannerman as Han Grand Secretary began with Ying Lian.

entries.zh: 尋授東閣大學士，仍領戶部。
entries.en: He was soon made Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary while continuing to head the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, still heading the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 四十六年，复署直隸總督，疏請清州縣虧帑。
entries.en: In Qianlong 46 (1781) he again acted as Governor-General of Zhili and petitioned to settle shortfalls in prefectural and county treasuries.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year he again served as acting Governor-General of Zhili and memorialized asking to clear county and prefectural treasury deficits.

entries.zh: 四十七年，加太子太保。
entries.en: In Qianlong 47 (1782) he received the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 复署直隸總督。
entries.en: He again acted as Governor-General of Zhili.
entries.literal: Again he served as acting Governor-General of Zhili.

entries.zh: 直隸災，治賑，疏請以截存漕米補各倉儲穀，又疏請蠲未完耗羨三萬馀兩，皆從其請。
entries.en: During a Zhili famine he directed relief efforts, petitioning to divert stored tribute rice to refill granaries and to waive more than thirty thousand taels in outstanding surplus fees—all approved.
entries.literal: When Zhili suffered disaster he managed relief; he memorialized to use withheld stored tribute grain to replenish granary reserves, and also memorialized to remit unpaid surplus levies of more than thirty thousand taels; all requests were granted.

entries.zh: 尋以病乞罷，命以大學士還京師養疴。
entries.en: He soon asked to step down for illness and was ordered home to Beijing to recuperate in his capacity as Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: Soon, on grounds of illness, he begged to retire; he was ordered to return to the capital as Grand Secretary to convalesce.

entries.zh: 卒，賜白金五千治喪，祀賢良祠，諡文肅。
entries.en: At his death he received five thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses, entry into the Worthy Officials Shrine, and the posthumous name Wensu (Literary Solemn).
entries.literal: He died; five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral; he was enshrined in the Worthy Officials Shrine; his posthumous name was Wensu.

entries.zh: 彭元瑞，字芸楣，江西南昌人。
entries.en: Peng Yuanrui, styled Yunmei, was from Nanchang in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Peng Yuanrui, style Yunmei, was a native of Nanchang, Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十二年進士，改庶吉士。
entries.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 22 (1757), he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination as jinshi and became a Hanlin bachelor.

entries.zh: 散館授編修，直懋勤殿。
entries.en: After completing Hanlin service he was made Compiler and attached to the Maoqin Hall.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was appointed Compiler and served at the Maoqin Hall.

entries.zh: 大考，以內直不與。
entries.en: Exempted from the triennial evaluation because he served on the inner staff.
entries.literal: At the grand examination he was excused from participation because of inner-court service.

entries.zh: 遷侍講。
entries.en: He was promoted to Lecturer.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Lecturer.

entries.zh: 擢詹事府少詹事。
entries.en: He rose to Junior Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
entries.literal: He was elevated to Junior Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

entries.zh: 直南書房。
entries.en: He was posted to the Southern Library.
entries.literal: He served at the Southern Library.

entries.zh: 遷侍郎，歷工、戶、兵、吏諸部。
entries.en: He became Vice Minister, serving in turn in Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister, serving in succession in the Ministries of Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.

entries.zh: 高宗六十壽，次聖教序為贊以進，上嘉之。
entries.en: For the Qianlong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he wrote a hymn modeled on the Preface to the Sacred Teachings and presented it to the throne; the Emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: On the Gaozong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he composed a laudatory piece in the style of the Preface to the Sacred Teachings and presented it; the Emperor commended it.

entries.zh: 上製全韻詩，元瑞重次周興嗣千字文為跋。
entries.en: When the Emperor wrote a fully rhymed poem, Yuanrui reworked Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Classic into a colophon.
entries.literal: The Emperor composed a poem in full rhyme; Yuanrui rearranged Zhou Xingsi's Thousand-Character Classic as a postscript.

entries.zh: 上手詔獎諭，稱為「異想逸材」，賜貂裘、硯、墨。
entries.en: The Emperor wrote him a letter of praise in his own hand, dubbing him "a mind of rare invention," and sent a sable coat, inkstone, and ink.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally issued an edict of commendation, calling him "a talent of extraordinary imagination," and bestowed a sable fur coat, inkstone, and ink.

entries.zh: 敕撰寧壽宮、皇極殿鐙聯，稱旨，賜以詩。
entries.en: Ordered to write lantern-scroll couplets for Ningshou Palace and Huangji Hall, he pleased the court and received an imperial poem in return.
entries.literal: By imperial command he composed lantern couplets for Ningshou Palace and Huangji Hall; they met with approval, and he was granted a poem.

entries.zh: 辟雍成，釋奠講學，又繼以耕耤。
entries.en: After the Imperial Academy opened, he took part in the sacrifice and lecture rites and then the ceremonial plowing.
entries.literal: When the Imperial Academy was completed, the sacrifice and lecture ceremony was held, followed in turn by the plowing ceremony.

entries.zh: 上三大禮賦。
entries.en: He submitted three fu celebrating the great rites to the throne.
entries.literal: He presented three great ceremonial fu to the Emperor.

entries.zh: 擢尚書，歷禮、兵、吏三部。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister and served in turn at Rites, War, and Personnel.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister and served successively in the Rites, War, and Personnel ministries.

entries.zh: 五十五年，上八十壽，以歲陽在庚，進八庚全韻詩。
entries.en: In Qianlong 55 (1790), for the Emperor's eightieth birthday, he submitted an eight-geng complete-rhyme poem, the year's stem being geng.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, when the Emperor reached his eightieth birthday, because the year's celestial stem was geng, he submitted an eight-geng complete-rhyme poem.

entries.zh: 上以庚立字數奇，易首句用韻去一聯，末句乃諧律，親為裁定。
entries.en: The Emperor found the geng-based character count awkward, revised the opening rhyme and cut a couplet so only the closing line met the meter, and settled the poem himself.
entries.literal: The Emperor held that counting characters by geng yielded an odd number; he changed the rhyme use in the opening line and removed one couplet, and only the final line conformed to meter—the Emperor personally settled it.

entries.zh: 尋加太子少保、協辦大學士。
entries.en: He was soon made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and Associate Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and Associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 五十六年，以從孫冒入官，御史初彭齡論劾，左授禮部侍郎，命仍直南書房。
entries.en: In Qianlong 56 (1791), after a grand-nephew gained office by fraud drew a memorial from Censor Chu Pengling, he was demoted to Vice Minister of Rites but kept on duty in the Southern Imperial Library.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, because a grand-nephew had fraudulently entered official service, Censor Chu Pengling memorialized in accusation; he was demoted to Vice Minister of Rites, but was ordered to continue serving in the Southern Imperial Library.

entries.zh: 尋复授工部尚書。
entries.en: He was soon restored as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Soon he was again appointed Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年，高宗奉安禮成，元瑞撰祝文，仁宗嘉其得體，加太子太保。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 4 (1799), when Gaozong's interment rites were complete, Yuanrui's prayer text pleased Renzong, who made him Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when the rites for Gaozong's interment were completed, Yuanrui drafted the prayer text; Renzong praised its appropriateness and added him as Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 元瑞子翼蒙，官江南鹽巡道，坐事免，元瑞自劾，又坐誤舉編修繆晉，下吏議，上皆寬之。
