entries.en: Yuanrui's son Yimeng, intendant of the Jiangnan Salt Circuit, was dismissed for misconduct; Yuanrui impeached himself and was also charged with wrongly recommending Compiler Miu Jin—both cases went to the judicial officials, and the Emperor showed lenience in each.
entries.literal: Yuanrui's son Yimeng served as Jiangnan Salt Circuit intendant; he was dismissed for an offense. Yuanrui impeached himself, and was again charged with wrongly recommending Compiler Miu Jin; the matter was referred to judicial officials for deliberation, but the Emperor pardoned him in both cases.

entries.zh: 修高宗實錄，命充總裁。
entries.en: He was appointed chief editor of the Veritable Record of Gaozong.
entries.literal: When the Veritable Record of Gaozong was being compiled, he was appointed chief editor.

entries.zh: 八年，以疾乞罷，慰留，久之乃許。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 8 (1803) he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the Emperor pressed him to remain, and only after long delay assented.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he pleaded illness to resign; the Emperor urged him to stay, and only after a long while permitted it.

entries.zh: 命仍領實錄總裁。
entries.en: He was still ordered to head the Veritable Record as chief editor.
entries.literal: He was ordered to continue leading the Veritable Record as chief editor.

entries.zh: 旋卒，贈協辦大學士，諡文勤。
entries.en: He died soon after, and was posthumously made Associate Grand Secretary with the posthumous name Wenqin.
entries.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously granted the title Associate Grand Secretary, with the posthumous name Wenqin.

entries.zh: 元瑞以文學被知遇。
entries.en: Yuanrui owed his rise to imperial favor won by his literary gifts.
entries.literal: Yuanrui won imperial favor through his literary accomplishments.

entries.zh: 內廷著錄藏書及書畫、彝鼎，輯秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈、西清古鑑、寧壽鑑古、天祿琳瑯諸書，元瑞無役不與。
entries.en: Whether the Inner Court was cataloguing books, paintings, or bronzes, or compiling works such as Secret Hall Pearl Forest, Stone Canal Treasure Collection, Western Purification Antique Mirror, Ningshou Antique Mirror, and Tianlu Linlang, Yuanrui had a hand in every project.
entries.literal: For the Inner Court cataloguing of books, calligraphy and paintings, and ritual vessels, and for the compilation of such works as Secret Hall Pearl Forest, Stone Canal Treasure Collection, Western Purification Antique Mirror, Ningshou Antique Mirror, and Tianlu Linlang, Yuanrui took part in every undertaking.

entries.zh: 和章獻頌，屢荷褒嘉。
entries.en: His responsive verses to the Zhangxian eulogy won repeated praise and rewards.
entries.literal: He composed matching stanzas for the Zhangxian eulogy and repeatedly received praise and rewards.

entries.zh: 所著有經進藁、知聖道齋跋尾諸書。
entries.en: Among his writings are Court Memorials and Postscripts from the Studio of Knowing the Sage's Way.
entries.literal: His writings include Court Memorials, Postscripts from the Studio of Knowing the Sage's Way, and other works.

entries.zh: 高宗實錄成，推恩賜祭，並祀賢良祠，官翼蒙員外郎。
entries.en: When Gaozong's Veritable Record was finished, imperial grace brought sacrificial honors and enshrinement in the Worthies' Shrine, and Yimeng was given the rank of secretary.
entries.literal: When the Veritable Record of Gaozong was completed, grace was extended in bestowing sacrificial offerings, and he was also enshrined in the Worthies' Shrine; Yimeng was appointed a secretary of the sixth rank.

entries.zh: 紀昀 紀昀，字曉嵐，直隸獻縣人。
entries.en: Ji Yun, styled Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.
entries.literal: Ji Yun, style Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.

entries.zh: 乾隆十九年進士，改庶吉士。
entries.en: He passed the metropolitan examination in Qianlong 19 (1754) and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

entries.zh: 散館授編修。
entries.en: After completing Hanlin probation he was made a compiler.
entries.literal: Upon completing his Hanlin probation he was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 再遷左春坊左庶子。
entries.en: He was transferred again to Left Sub-Reader in the Left Spring Palace.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Left Sub-Reader in the Left Spring Palace.

entries.zh: 京察，授貴州都勻府知府。
entries.en: At the capital inspection he was named prefect of Duyun in Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the capital inspection he was appointed prefect of Duyun Prefecture in Guizhou.

entries.zh: 高宗以昀學問優，加四品銜，留庶子。
entries.en: Gaozong judged Yun's learning outstanding, gave him fourth-rank insignia, and kept him as sub-reader.
entries.literal: Gaozong, holding that Yun's learning was superior, granted him fourth-rank insignia and kept him at his post as sub-reader.

entries.zh: 尋擢翰林院侍讀學士。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 前兩淮鹽運使盧見曾得罪，昀為姻家，漏言奪職，戍烏魯木齊，釋還。
entries.en: When the former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng fell from favor, Yun—his kinsman by marriage—was stripped of office for leaking word, exiled to Urumqi, and later released.
entries.literal: The former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng had fallen afoul of the throne; Yun was related by marriage and was dismissed for leaking information, exiled to Urumqi, then released and returned.

entries.zh: 上幸熱河，迎鑾密雲，試詩，以土爾扈特全部歸順為題，稱旨，复授編修。
entries.en: When the Emperor went to Rehe, Yun met the procession at Miyun and was tested in verse on the Torghuts' complete submission; his poem pleased the throne, and he was restored as compiler.
entries.literal: When the Emperor traveled to Rehe, Yun met the imperial procession at Miyun and was examined in poetry on the topic of the complete submission of the Torghut; his work pleased the Emperor, and he was again appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 三十八年，開四庫全書館，大學士劉統勳舉昀及郎中陸錫熊為總纂。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38 (1773), when the Siku Quanshu project opened, Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun recommended Yun and Department Director Lu Xixiong as chief compilers.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the Siku Quanshu project was inaugurated; Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun recommended Yun and Department Director Lu Xixiong as chief compilers.

entries.zh: 從永樂大典中搜輯散逸，盡讀諸行省所進書，論次為提要上之，擢侍讀。
entries.en: He recovered lost texts from the Yongle Encyclopaedia, read every book the provinces sent in, arranged synopses for submission, and was promoted to reader.
entries.literal: He searched out scattered and lost texts from the Yongle Encyclopaedia, read through all books submitted from the provinces, arranged them into synopses and submitted them upward, and was promoted to reader.

entries.zh: 上復命輯簡明書目。
entries.en: The Emperor also ordered him to compile a concise catalogue.
entries.literal: The Emperor further ordered him to compile a concise catalogue.

entries.zh: 坐子汝傳積逋被訟，下吏議，上寬之。
entries.en: When his son Ruchuan was sued over accumulated tax arrears, the case went to the judicial officials, but the Emperor showed leniency.
entries.literal: Because his son Ruchuan's accumulated tax arrears were subject to lawsuit, the matter was referred to judicial officials for deliberation, but the Emperor showed leniency.

entries.zh: 旋遷翰林院侍讀學士。
entries.en: He was soon made Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 建文淵閣藏書，命充直閣事。
entries.en: When the Wenyuan Pavilion library was built, he was appointed a pavilion attendant.
entries.literal: When the Wenyuan Pavilion library was built, he was appointed to serve as a pavilion attendant.

entries.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 四庫全書成，表上。
entries.en: When the Siku Quanshu was finished, the completion memorial was submitted.
entries.literal: When the Siku Quanshu was completed, the memorial of completion was submitted.

entries.zh: 上曰：「表必出昀手！」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "This memorial must be Yun's work!"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "This memorial must have come from Yun's hand!"

entries.zh: 命加賚。
entries.en: He ordered additional rewards.
entries.literal: He ordered additional gifts.

entries.zh: 遷左都御史。
entries.en: He was made Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 再遷禮部尚書。
entries.en: He was transferred again to Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 復為左都御史。
entries.en: He again became Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He again became Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 畿輔災，饑民多就食京師。
entries.en: When disaster struck the capital region, hungry refugees flooded into Beijing.
entries.literal: Disaster struck the capital region, and many famine victims came to the capital seeking food.

entries.zh: 故事，五城設飯廠，自十月至三月。
entries.en: By longstanding practice, Beijing's Five Cities ran soup kitchens from the tenth month through the third month.
entries.literal: By precedent, the Five Cities established soup kitchens, operating from the tenth month through the third month.

entries.zh: 昀疏請自六月中旬始，廠日煮米三石，十月加煮米二石，仍以三月止，從之。
entries.en: Yun memorialized that the kitchens should open from mid-sixth month, cooking three piculs of rice daily and adding two more from the tenth month, with operations still ending in the third month; the court approved.
entries.literal: Yun submitted a memorial requesting that the kitchens begin from mid-sixth month, cooking three piculs of rice per day; from the tenth month add two piculs; still ending in the third month—the request was approved.

entries.zh: 复遷禮部尚書，仍署左都御史。
entries.en: He was again made Minister of Rites while continuing to serve as acting Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Rites, still acting as Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 疏請鄉會試春秋罷胡安國傳，以左傳本事為文，參用公、穀，從之。
entries.en: He memorialized that provincial and metropolitan candidates in the Spring and Autumn Annals should set aside Hu Anguo's commentary, write essays grounded in the Zuo Tradition's narrative, and may also draw on the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries; the court approved.
entries.literal: He memorialized that in the provincial and metropolitan examinations the Spring and Autumn Annals should abandon Hu Anguo's commentary, take the Zuo Tradition's original events as the basis for essays, and draw also on the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries—the request was approved.

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，移兵部尚書。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 1 (1796) he was transferred to Minister of War.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was transferred to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 复移左都御史。
entries.en: He was again made Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 二年，复遷禮部尚書。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 2 (1797) he was again made Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the second year he was again transferred to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 疏請婦女遇強暴，雖受污，仍量予旌表。
entries.en: He memorialized that women assaulted by force, though violated, should still be granted commemorative honors according to their merit.
entries.literal: He memorialized that women who met with violent assault, though defiled, should still receive commemorative honors as appropriate.

entries.zh: 十年，協辦大學士，加太子少保。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 10 (1805) he was made Associate Grand Secretary and Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was made Associate Grand Secretary and granted the title Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 卒，賜白金五百治喪，諡文達。
entries.en: He died; the court granted five hundred taels of silver for his funeral and posthumously titled him Wenda (Literary Accomplishment).
entries.literal: He died; five hundred taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Wenda.

entries.zh: 昀學問淵通。
entries.en: Yun's scholarship was deep and far-reaching.
entries.literal: Yun's learning was profound and comprehensive.

entries.zh: 撰四庫全書提要，進退百家，鉤深摘隱，各得其要指，始終條理，蔚為巨觀。
entries.en: In writing the Siku Quanshu synopses he weighed the hundred schools with discriminating judgment, probing deep and drawing out what was hidden until each work yielded its essential point; the whole, ordered from start to finish, formed a monumental achievement.
entries.literal: In composing the synopses for the Siku Quanshu, he advanced and retreated among the hundred schools, probing deep and plucking hidden points; each work obtained its essential meaning, consistently ordered throughout—a grand spectacle.

entries.zh: 懲明季講學之習，宋五子書功令所重，不敢顯立異同；
entries.en: Wary of the late-Ming passion for public lecturing and of the examination system's esteem for the Five Song Masters, he dared not openly take sides;
entries.literal: Taking warning from the late-Ming habit of public lecturing, and with the books of the Five Song Masters being what the examination system prized, he dared not openly declare agreement or disagreement;

entries.zh: 而於南宋以後諸儒，深文詆諆，不無門戶出入之見云。
entries.en: Yet in treating Southern Song and later scholars, he often wrote in harshly denunciatory tones—not without partisan favor in deciding who belonged and who did not.
entries.literal: Yet toward Confucians after the Southern Song, he used harsh language of denunciation, not without partisan bias in choosing whom to admit or exclude.

entries.zh: 陸錫熊，字健男，江蘇上海人。
entries.en: Lu Xixiong, styled Jiannan, came from Shanghai in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Lu Xixiong, style Jiannan, was a native of Shanghai, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十六年進士。
entries.en: He earned jinshi in Qianlong 26 (1761).
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 召試，授內閣中書。
entries.en: Summoned to an imperial examination, he was appointed a drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: Called to examination, he was appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter.

entries.zh: 累遷刑部郎中。
entries.en: He rose by stages to department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 與昀同司總纂，旋並授翰林院侍讀。
entries.en: He served with Yun as chief compiler, and both were soon appointed Hanlin readers.
entries.literal: He served with Yun as chief compiler; soon both were appointed Hanlin Academy readers.

entries.zh: 五遷左副都御史。
entries.en: After five promotions he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: After five promotions he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 旋以書有譌謬，令重為校正，寫官所費，責錫熊與昀分任。
entries.en: When errors were found in the books, he was ordered to recorrect them, and the copyists' costs were split between Xixiong and Yun.
entries.literal: Soon, because the books contained errors, he was ordered to recorrect them; the copyists' expenses were charged to Xixiong and Yun to share.

entries.zh: 又令詣奉天校正文溯閣藏書，卒於奉天。
entries.en: He was then sent to Mukden to collate the Wensu Pavilion collection and died there.
entries.literal: He was further ordered to go to Mukden to collate the books stored in the Wensu Pavilion, and died in Mukden.

entries.zh: 陸費墀，字丹叔，浙江桐鄉人。
entries.en: Lu Feichi, styled Danshu, came from Tongxiang in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Lu Feichi, style Danshu, was a native of Tongxiang, Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 陸費為複姓。
entries.en: Lu Fei is a compound surname.
entries.literal: Lu Fei is a compound surname.

entries.zh: 墀，乾隆三十一年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: Feichi earned jinshi in Qianlong 31 (1766), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: Feichi passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-first year of Qianlong, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 充四庫全書館總校，用昀、錫熊例，擢侍讀。
entries.en: As chief proofreader of the Siku Quanshu project, he was promoted to reader on the same terms as Yun and Xixiong.
entries.literal: He served as chief proofreader of the Siku Quanshu project; following the precedent of Yun and Xixiong, he was promoted to reader.

entries.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。
entries.en: He rose by stages to Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 書有譌謬，上謂昀、錫熊、墀專司其事，而墀咎尤重。
entries.en: When errors were found in the books, the Emperor held that Yun, Xixiong, and Feichi were specially responsible, but Feichi bore the heaviest blame.
entries.literal: When the books contained errors, the Emperor said Yun, Xixiong, and Feichi were specially charged with the matter, but Feichi bore the heavier blame.

entries.zh: 文瀾、文匯、文宗三閣書面葉木匣，責墀出資裝治。
entries.en: Feichi was ordered to pay for the wooden cases and binding of the books at the Wenlan, Wenhui, and Wenzong pavilions.
entries.literal: The wooden cases for the page leaves of the books in the Wenlan, Wenhui, and Wenzong pavilions—Feichi was charged to fund their binding and repair.

entries.zh: 仍下吏議，奪職。
entries.en: The case was still sent to the judicial officials for review, and he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: The matter was still referred to the judicial officials for deliberation, and he was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 旋卒。
entries.en: He soon died.
entries.literal: Soon after he died.

entries.zh: 上命籍墀家，留千金贍其孥，馀充三閣裝治之用。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Feichi's estate confiscated, kept one thousand taels to support his wife and children, and applied the rest to binding the books at the three pavilions.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Feichi's household goods confiscated; one thousand taels were kept to support his wife and children, and the remainder applied to binding the three pavilions' books.

entries.zh: 論曰：乾隆中年後，多以武功致台鼎。
entries.en: The commentators observe: After mid-Qianlong, many men reached the highest offices through military achievement.
entries.literal: The commentary says: After the middle years of Qianlong, many reached the highest ministerial offices through military merit.

entries.zh: 若三寶、永貴、國治、英廉，皆先陟外台，敭歷著聲績。
entries.en: Men such as San Bao, Yong Gui, Guozhi, and Ying Lian all first rose through provincial service, repeatedly passing through posts and achieving renown.
entries.literal: Such men as San Bao, Yong Gui, Guozhi, and Ying Lian all first rose through provincial posts, repeatedly passing through offices and achieving renown.

entries.zh: 國治直樞廷十馀年，先後與於敏中、和珅未嘗有所阿。
entries.en: Guozhi served at the inner court for more than ten years; whether alongside Yu Minzhong or Heshen, he never showed favoritism.
entries.literal: Guozhi served directly at the inner court for more than ten years; serving in succession with Yu Minzhong and Heshen, he never showed partiality.

entries.zh: 新、元瑞、昀起侍從，文學負時望。
entries.en: Xin, Yuanrui, and Yun rose from service at court; their literary gifts commanded the age's respect.
entries.literal: Xin, Yuanrui, and Yun rose from attendant service; their literary attainments commanded contemporary esteem.

entries.zh: 新謹厚承世遠之教。
entries.en: Xin was careful and steadfast, carrying on the teachings of Shi Yuan.
entries.literal: Xin was cautious and sincere, inheriting Shi Yuan's teachings.

entries.zh: 昀校定四庫書，成一代文治，允哉，稱其位矣！
entries.en: Yun collated the Siku collection and brought about an age of literary governance—truly, he was worthy of his place!
entries.literal: Yun collated the Siku books and achieved an age of literary governance—indeed, his title matched his station!

entries.zh: 開泰，烏雅氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Kai Tai, of the Uya clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Kai Tai, of the Uya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 雍正二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He took his jinshi in Yongzheng 2, entered the Hanlin as a probationer, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In Yongzheng 2 he passed the metropolitan examination, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 九年，遷侍講。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was promoted to expositor.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to expositor.

entries.zh: 上御門，開泰未入侍班，黜令乾清門行走。
entries.en: When the emperor held audience at the Gate, Kai Tai had failed to take his place in the attendance roster and was demoted to duty at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
entries.literal: When the emperor held court at the Gate, Kai Tai had not entered the attendance roster and was dismissed to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

entries.zh: 十三年，复編修。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was reappointed compiler.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was restored as compiler.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，遷國子監司業。
entries.en: In Qianlong 1 he was promoted to vice-director of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to vice-director of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 八年，遷祭酒。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to chancellor of the Academy.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to chancellor.

entries.zh: 督江蘇學政。
entries.en: He served as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
entries.literal: He supervised the educational administration of Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 再遷內閣學士。
entries.en: He was next promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 三遷兵部侍郎，仍留學政任。
entries.en: He was then promoted to vice minister of War but kept his educational commission.
entries.literal: A third transfer made him vice minister of War, while he retained his post as educational commissioner.

entries.zh: 十年，授湖北巡撫。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed governor of Hubei.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed governor of Hubei.

entries.zh: 疏言：「社倉較常平尤近於民，而弊亦易滋。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial stating: "Community granaries lie even closer to the people than ever-normal granaries, but malfeasance also spreads more easily.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "Community granaries are even closer to the people than ever-normal granaries, yet abuses also arise more easily.

entries.zh: 湖北社倉穀麥五十二萬石有奇，散在諸鄉，恐多虧缺。
entries.en: Hubei's community granaries hold over five hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain and wheat, dispersed among the townships, and I fear many shortfalls.
entries.literal: Hubei's community granaries hold more than five hundred twenty thousand piculs of grain, scattered through the townships, and I fear much may be deficient.

entries.zh: 應飭道府按部所至，便宜抽驗。」
entries.en: Circuit and prefectural officials should be instructed to conduct spot checks wherever their inspections take them."
entries.literal: Circuit intendants and prefects should be ordered to conduct spot inspections wherever their tours take them."

entries.zh: 調江西。
entries.en: He was then transferred to Jiangxi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 十三年，又調湖南。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Hunan.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred again to Hunan.

entries.zh: 疏言：「戶部諮各省常平倉穀，以雍正舊額為準。
entries.en: He memorialized: "The Board of Revenue has asked each province to report on ever-normal granary stocks, using the Yongzheng quota as the standard.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "The Board of Revenue has inquired of each province regarding ever-normal granary grain, taking the Yongzheng quota as the standard.

entries.zh: 湖南溢額穀五十五萬餘石，令糶價儲庫。
entries.en: Hunan's surplus exceeds five hundred fifty thousand piculs, and the province has been ordered to sell it and deposit the proceeds in the treasury.
entries.literal: Hunan has a surplus of more than five hundred fifty thousand piculs and has been ordered to sell the surplus and deposit the proceeds in the treasury.

entries.zh: 臣維雍正舊額七十餘萬石。
entries.en: I maintain that the Yongzheng quota was over seven hundred thousand piculs.
entries.literal: Your servant maintains that the Yongzheng quota was more than seven hundred thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 湖南夙稱產米，乾隆二年至八年，諸省赴湖南購米，先後計百七十五萬有奇。
entries.en: Hunan has long been known as a rice-producing region; from Qianlong 2 through 8 other provinces purchased rice there, totaling more than one million seven hundred fifty thousand piculs.
entries.literal: Hunan has long been famed for rice production; from Qianlong 2 to 8 other provinces came to Hunan to purchase rice, totaling in all more than one million seven hundred fifty thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 中間又撥運福建、江蘇。
entries.en: In the meantime grain was also requisitioned and shipped to Fujian and Jiangsu.
entries.literal: In between, grain was also allocated and shipped to Fujian and Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 若盡糶溢額之穀，遇本省需用或鄰疆告糴，必致倉儲缺額，買補不易。」
entries.en: If all surplus grain is sold, whenever the province itself needs grain or neighboring regions request relief, stores will fall below quota and be hard to replenish."
entries.literal: If all the surplus grain is sold off, when this province needs grain or neighboring regions request relief, granary quotas will fall short and replenishment will be difficult."

entries.zh: 疏上，以留心積貯嘉之。
entries.en: The emperor commended him for his care in maintaining grain reserves.
entries.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, he was praised for his attention to accumulation and storage.

entries.zh: 十五年，有壽掄元者，自言南河同知，赴湖南採木，布政使孫灝諭永州府為料理。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year a man named Shou Lunyuan claimed to be sub-prefect of the Southern Rivers and came to Hunan to procure timber; provincial treasurer Sun Hao instructed Yongzhou prefecture to assist him.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year a man named Shou Lunyuan claimed to be sub-prefect of the Southern Rivers, came to Hunan to procure timber, and the provincial treasurer Sun Hao instructed Yongzhou prefecture to arrange matters for him.

entries.zh: 尋得其詐偽狀，開泰以聞，但言灝殊為未諳。
entries.en: His imposture was soon uncovered; Kai Tai reported it to the throne but merely said that Hao had been quite naive.
entries.literal: Soon his fraud was discovered; Kai Tai reported it but only said that Hao had been quite uninformed.

entries.zh: 上以灝瞻徇，何得但言未諳，知為開泰門生，斥其徇庇，下吏部嚴議，議奪官，命留任。
entries.en: The emperor said Hao had shown favoritism and asked how Kai Tai could dismiss it as mere ignorance; learning that Hao was Kai Tai's protégé, he rebuked Kai Tai for shielding him. The Board of Civil Appointments recommended stripping his rank, but the emperor allowed him to remain in office.
entries.literal: The emperor said Hao had shown favoritism—how could one merely say he was uninformed?—and knowing him to be Kai Tai's protégé, rebuked Kai Tai for partiality, referred the case to the Board of Civil Appointments for severe deliberation, which recommended dismissal from office, but the emperor ordered him retained in his post.

entries.zh: 尋調貴州。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Guizhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guizhou.

entries.zh: 十八年，疏言：「古州募軍屯田，戶上田六畝，中田八畝，下田十畝。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he memorialized: "At Guzhou recruited soldiers farm garrison lands on a graded basis—six mu per household on top-grade fields, eight on middle-grade, ten on lower-grade.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he memorialized: "At Guzhou recruited soldiers farm garrison lands: six mu per household on upper fields, eight on middle fields, ten on lower fields.

entries.zh: 今食指日多，生計艱難，請準屯戶入伍充兵。」
entries.en: As dependents multiply and livelihoods grow harder, I ask that garrison households be allowed to enlist as regular troops."
entries.literal: Now mouths to feed grow daily and livelihoods are hard; I request permission for garrison households to enlist as soldiers."

entries.zh: 許之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: Permission was granted.

entries.zh: 擢湖廣總督，加太子少傅。
entries.en: He was promoted to governor-general of Huguang and given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was promoted governor-general of Huguang and given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 二十年，調四川。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Sichuan.

entries.zh: 金川土司莎羅奔與革布什咱土司色楞敦多布初為婚媾，繼乃相怨構兵。
entries.en: Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon and Gebushizan chieftain Selenduobu were initially linked by marriage, but later fell out and went to war.
entries.literal: Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon and Gebushizan chieftain Selenduobu were at first allied by marriage, but later bore grudges and raised troops against each other.

entries.zh: 旁近綽斯甲布、鄂克什、雜穀、巴旺、丹壩、明正、章谷、小金川諸土司皆不直莎羅奔。
entries.en: Neighboring chieftains of Zhuosijia, Eke Shi, Zagu, Bawang, Danba, Mingzheng, Zhanggu, and Lesser Jinchuan all took sides against Slob Dpon.
entries.literal: Neighboring chieftains of Zhuosijia, Eke Shi, Zagu, Bawang, Danba, Mingzheng, Zhanggu, and Lesser Jinchuan all sided against Slob Dpon.

entries.zh: 二十三年，莎羅奔攻吉地。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year Slob Dpon attacked Jidi.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year Slob Dpon attacked Jidi.

entries.zh: 吉地，色楞敦多布所居寨也。
entries.en: Jidi was the stockade where Selenduobu lived.
entries.literal: Jidi was the stockade where Selenduobu resided.

entries.zh: 開泰與提督岳鍾琪檄游擊楊青、都司夏尚德等率兵分屯章谷、泰宁，令鄂克什、雜穀援革布什咱，攻金川，莎羅奔引退。
entries.en: Kai Tai and provincial commander Yue Zhongqi ordered battalion commander Yang Qing, brigade commander Xia Shangde, and others to station troops at Zhanggu and Taining, sent Eke Shi and Zagu to aid Gebushizan against Jinchuan, and Slob Dpon retreated.
entries.literal: Kai Tai and provincial commander-in-chief Yue Zhongqi ordered battalion commander Yang Qing, brigade commander Xia Shangde, and others to lead troops and garrison separately at Zhanggu and Taining, directed Eke Shi and Zagu to aid Gebushizan and attack Jinchuan, and Slob Dpon withdrew.

entries.zh: 尋復攻破吉地，色楞敦多布走泰宁求援，開泰复檄諸土司出兵助之，調雜穀土練千人分屯丹壩、章谷、泰宁，發黎、雅、峨邊兵屯打箭爐，諭郎卡撤兵。
entries.en: Jidi fell again soon afterward; Selenduobu fled to Taining for help. Kai Tai again ordered the chieftains to send troops, deployed a thousand Zagu militiamen at Danba, Zhanggu, and Taining, posted troops from Li, Ya, and Ebian at Dajianlu, and instructed Lang Ka to withdraw.
entries.literal: Soon Jidi was again taken; Selenduobu fled to Taining to seek aid. Kai Tai again ordered the chieftains to send troops to help, mobilized a thousand Zagu native militia to garrison separately at Danba, Zhanggu, and Taining, sent troops from Li, Ya, and Ebian to garrison Dajianlu, and instructed Lang Ka to withdraw his forces.

entries.zh: 郎卡，莎羅奔從子，為副酋，主兵事者也。
entries.en: Lang Ka was Slob Dpon's nephew, served as deputy chieftain, and directed military affairs.
entries.literal: Lang Ka was Slob Dpon's nephew, served as deputy chieftain, and directed military affairs.

entries.zh: 事聞，上謂：「番目相攻，於打箭爐何與？」
entries.en: When word reached the throne, the emperor said: "When native chiefs fight among themselves, what business is that of Dajianlu?"
entries.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor said: "When native chiefs fight one another, what has that to do with Dajianlu?"

entries.zh: 疑郎卡擾邊，命開泰具實覆奏。
entries.en: Suspecting Lang Ka of harassing the frontier, he ordered Kai Tai to submit a full factual report.
entries.literal: Suspecting Lang Ka of disturbing the border, he ordered Kai Tai to report the facts in full.

entries.zh: 開泰尋疏報章谷、巴旺土兵擊敗金川，莎羅奔焚吉地走，盡复革布什咱境，留綽斯甲布、明正兩土司兵分守之，使色楞敦多布歸寨。
entries.en: Kai Tai soon reported that Zhanggu and Bawang forces had defeated Jinchuan; Slob Dpon burned Jidi and fled; Gebushizan territory was fully recovered; Zhuosijia and Mingzheng troops were left to garrison it; and Selenduobu was restored to his stockade.
entries.literal: Kai Tai soon memorialized that Zhanggu and Bawang native troops had defeated Jinchuan; Slob Dpon burned Jidi and fled; Gebushizan territory was fully recovered; troops of the Zhuosijia and Mingzheng chieftains were left to garrison it in separate detachments; and Selenduobu was restored to his stockade.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「番民挾仇攻擊，不必繩以內地官法。
entries.en: The emperor instructed: "When native tribesmen attack one another over old grudges, there is no need to apply the laws of the interior provinces.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: "When native tribesmen attack one another out of vendetta, there is no need to bind them with the statutes of the interior.

entries.zh: 宜以番攻番，處以靜鎮。」
entries.en: Let natives fight natives and handle the matter with calm restraint."
entries.literal: It is fitting to let natives fight natives and handle matters with quiet restraint."

entries.zh: 旋加太子太保。
entries.en: He was soon given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was soon given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 二十四年，松潘鎮總兵楊朝棟入覲，開泰與鍾琪奏朝棟衰老，難期勝任。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year Songpan garrison commander Yang Chaodong came to court; Kai Tai and Zhongqi reported that he was too old to be relied upon for duty.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Songpan garrison commander Yang Chaodong came to audience; Kai Tai and Zhongqi memorialized that Chaodong was aged and could hardly be expected to perform his duties.

entries.zh: 上責開泰何以不先奏，下吏部議，奪官，命仍留任。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked Kai Tai for not having reported this sooner; the Board recommended stripping his rank, but the emperor allowed him to remain in office.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Kai Tai for not having reported this earlier, referred the case to the Board of Civil Appointments, which recommended stripping his rank, but the emperor ordered him retained in his post.

entries.zh: 二十七年，莎羅奔死，郎卡應襲。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year Slob Dpon died and Lang Ka was due to inherit the chieftaincy.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Slob Dpon died and Lang Ka was due to succeed.

entries.zh: 例，土司承襲，鄰封諸土司具結。
entries.en: By precedent, when a native chieftain succeeds, neighboring chieftains must submit joint attestations.
entries.literal: By precedent, when a native chieftain succeeds, neighboring chieftains submit joint attestations.

entries.zh: 開泰以郎卡與諸土司皆不協，令毋取結，疏聞，上許之，命嚴諭郎卡知恩守法。
entries.en: Because Lang Ka was at odds with all the neighboring chieftains, Kai Tai waived the attestations; the emperor approved and ordered Lang Ka sternly reminded to show gratitude and obey the law.
entries.literal: Kai Tai, because Lang Ka was at odds with all the chieftains, ordered that no attestations be taken; when he reported this, the emperor approved and ordered Lang Ka sternly instructed to know gratitude and obey the law.

entries.zh: 未幾，郎卡侵丹壩，取所屬瑪讓，開泰檄綽斯甲布往援，使守備溫欽等赴金川詰責。
entries.en: Before long Lang Ka invaded Danba and seized its dependency Marang; Kai Tai ordered Zhuosijia to relieve Danba and sent garrison commandant Wen Qin and others to Jinchuan to rebuke him.
entries.literal: Before long Lang Ka invaded Danba and seized its dependency Marang; Kai Tai ordered Zhuosijia to go to its aid and sent garrison commandant Wen Qin and others to Jinchuan to reprimand him.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「郎卡狼子野心，即使詰責伏罪，豈肯永守約束？
entries.en: The emperor instructed: "Lang Ka is treacherous by nature; even if rebuked into submission, how could he be trusted to keep his word forever?
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: "Lang Ka has the heart of a wolf cub; even if rebuked and made to submit, how could he forever keep to his bonds?

entries.zh: 諸土司援兵既集，能協力剿除，分據其地，轉可相安；
entries.en: If the chieftains' relief forces are already assembled and can join to destroy him and divide his territory among themselves, the region may yet be pacified;
entries.literal: If the chieftains' relief forces are already assembled and can join in exterminating him and divide his lands among themselves, peace may yet be secured;

entries.zh: 若諸部不能並力剿除，而郎卡怙惡不悛，亦非開泰、岳鍾琪四川綠營兵能任其事，應臨時奏請進止。」
entries.en: if the tribes cannot combine to destroy him and Lang Ka persists in his wickedness, neither Kai Tai nor Yue Zhongqi's Sichuan Green Standard troops can handle the matter—you should memorialize when the time comes for instructions on how to proceed."
entries.literal: if the tribes cannot combine to exterminate him and Lang Ka persists in his evil without reform, neither Kai Tai nor Yue Zhongqi's Sichuan Green Standard troops can undertake the task—you should memorialize at the time for instructions on advancing or halting."

entries.zh: 二十八年六月，開泰奏九土司大舉擊破金川。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year Kai Tai reported that nine chieftains had launched a major campaign and defeated Jinchuan.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year Kai Tai memorialized that nine chieftains had launched a major campaign and broken Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 上聞郎卡使人詣成都，開泰許進謁，撫慰之，而陰令九土司進兵，諭曰：「郎卡於綽斯甲布等屢肆欺凌，眾土司合力報復。
entries.en: The emperor learned that Lang Ka had sent envoys to Chengdu; Kai Tai received them and offered reassurance while secretly ordering the nine chieftains to advance. He instructed: "Lang Ka has repeatedly bullied Zhuosijia and others; the chieftains are joining forces to retaliate.
entries.literal: The emperor learned that Lang Ka had sent envoys to Chengdu; Kai Tai allowed them audience and comforted them, while secretly ordering the nine chieftains to advance. He instructed: "Lang Ka has repeatedly bullied Zhuosijia and the others; the chieftains are joining forces in reprisal.

entries.zh: 開泰既聞其事，惟應明白宣示，諭令悉銳往攻；
entries.en: Once Kai Tai heard of this, he should have declared openly and ordered them to attack with full force;
entries.literal: Now that Kai Tai has heard of this, he should only declare openly and order them to attack with full force;

entries.zh: 而於郎卡來人嚴為拒絕，且諭以爾結怨鄰境，誰肯甘心？
entries.en: and toward Lang Ka's envoys he should have refused them firmly, saying: You have made enemies of your neighbors—who will bear that gladly?
entries.literal: and toward Lang Ka's envoys he should have been stern in refusal, telling them: You have made enemies of your neighbors—who will bear this gladly?

entries.zh: 斷不能曲為庇護。
entries.en: I certainly cannot bend the rules to shield you.
entries.literal: I certainly cannot bend the rules to shield you.

entries.zh: 如此，則郎卡既不敢逞強，綽斯甲布等亦可洩忿。
entries.en: That way Lang Ka would not dare act aggressively, and Zhuosijia and the others could also vent their grievances.
entries.literal: In this way Lang Ka would not dare show his strength, and Zhuosijia and the others could also vent their anger.

entries.zh: 乃既用譎以籠絡郎卡，又隱為各土司援助，郎卡素狡黠，豈能掩其耳目？
entries.en: Instead he used deceit to win Lang Ka over while secretly aiding the chieftains—Lang Ka has always been cunning; how could he fail to see through it?
entries.literal: Yet he used deceit to win Lang Ka over while secretly aiding the chieftains—Lang Ka has always been cunning; how could his eyes and ears be hoodwinked?

entries.zh: 殊非駕馭邊夷之道。」
entries.en: This is far from the proper way to manage frontier tribes."
entries.literal: This is far from the way to manage frontier tribes."

entries.zh: 命奪官，以頭等侍衛赴伊犁辦事。
entries.en: He was stripped of rank and sent to Yili as a first-class imperial bodyguard on assignment.
entries.literal: He was ordered stripped of rank and sent to Yili as a first-class bodyguard on assignment.

entries.zh: 尋卒。
entries.en: He died soon afterward.
entries.literal: He soon died.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰至四川，議平治道路：陸道北訖廣元，西達松潘，東抵夔州，護其傾欹，補其缺落，兼葺大渡河瀘定橋；
entries.en: On reaching Sichuan, Aertai proposed repairing the road network: overland routes north to Guangyuan, west to Songpan, and east to Kuizhou, shoring up tilting sections and filling gaps, and also repairing the Luding Bridge on the Dadu River;
entries.literal: When Aertai reached Sichuan he proposed leveling and repairing roads: overland routes north to Guangyuan, west to Songpan, and east to Kuizhou, shoring up tilting sections and filling gaps, and also repairing the Luding Bridge on the Dadu River;

entries.zh: 水道自萬縣入湖廣境，鑿治險灘凡一百有奇。
entries.en: along the water route from Wan County into Huguang, more than a hundred dangerous shoals were cleared.
entries.literal: the water route from Wan County into Huguang territory had more than a hundred dangerous shoals cut and cleared.

entries.zh: 議以牧廠餘地招佃為田。
entries.en: He proposed recruiting tenants to farm unused pasture lands.
entries.literal: He proposed recruiting tenants to farm leftover pasture lands.

entries.zh: 議置義倉，捐穀千餘石以倡。
entries.en: He proposed establishing charity granaries and donated more than a thousand piculs of grain to lead by example.
entries.literal: He proposed establishing charity granaries and donated more than a thousand piculs of grain to set an example.

entries.zh: 議開南川金佛山磺礦。
entries.en: He proposed opening the sulfur mines at Jinfo Mountain in Nanchuan.
entries.literal: He proposed opening the sulfur mines at Jinfo Mountain in Nanchuan.

entries.zh: 議築都江大堰。
entries.en: He proposed repairing the great Dujiangyan irrigation works.
entries.literal: He proposed building the great Dujiangyan irrigation works.

entries.zh: 議松潘、雜穀、打箭爐三廳置倉儲麥稞，備邊儲。
entries.en: He proposed that the frontier offices of Songpan, Zagu, and Dajianlu establish granaries for barley and grain as border reserves.
entries.literal: He proposed that the three frontier offices of Songpan, Zagu, and Dajianlu establish granaries for barley and grain to prepare border reserves.

entries.zh: 上皆從其請。
entries.en: The emperor approved all his proposals.
entries.literal: The emperor approved all his requests.

entries.zh: 初，徵金川，以頭人郎卡出降，罷兵。
entries.en: Earlier, during the campaign against Jinchuan, when chieftain Lang Ka surrendered, the army was withdrawn.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the campaign against Jinchuan, when chieftain Lang Ka submitted, troops were withdrawn.

entries.zh: 三十一年，復為亂，掠丹壩、巴旺。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year he rebelled again and raided Danba and Bawang.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he rebelled again and raided Danba and Bawang.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰策以番攻番，令旁近綽斯甲布諸土司攻之。
entries.en: Aertai adopted the strategy of letting natives fight natives and ordered neighboring Zhuosijia and other chieftains to attack him.
entries.literal: Aertai planned to let natives fight natives and ordered neighboring Zhuosijia and other chieftains to attack him.

entries.zh: 秋出行邊，至雜穀腦。
entries.en: That autumn he toured the frontier as far as Zagunao.
entries.literal: In autumn he went on a frontier tour as far as Zagunao.

entries.zh: 郎卡使請還所侵丹壩碉卡。
entries.en: Lang Ka sent envoys asking that the Danba blockhouses he had seized be returned.
entries.literal: Lang Ka sent envoys requesting return of the Danba blockhouses he had seized.

entries.zh: 復與提督董天弼進至康巴達，郎卡出謁，阿爾泰許如所請，並畀以新印。
entries.en: He advanced again with provincial commander Dong Tianbi to Kangbada; Lang Ka came out to pay his respects; Aertai granted his request and presented him with a new seal.
entries.literal: He advanced again with provincial commander Dong Tianbi to Kangbada; Lang Ka came out to pay his respects; Aertai granted his request and also gave him a new seal.

entries.zh: 疏聞，上戒毋遷就苟安。
entries.en: When he reported this, the emperor warned him not to settle for a temporary peace at the cost of principle.
entries.literal: When he reported this, the emperor warned him not to compromise for the sake of temporary peace.

entries.zh: 三十五年，小金川頭人僧格桑掠鄂克什，阿爾泰赴達木巴宗，僧格桑出謁，還侵地。
entries.en: In the thirty-fifth year Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Senggesang raided Eke Shi; Aertai went to Damubazong; Senggesang came out to pay his respects and returned the seized lands.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Senggesang raided Eke Shi; Aertai went to Damubazong; Senggesang came out to pay his respects and returned the seized territory.

entries.zh: 尋授武英殿大學士，仍領總督。
entries.en: He was soon appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory while continuing as governor-general.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory while still retaining the governorship.

entries.zh: 三十六年，召還京，入閣治事。
entries.en: In the thirty-sixth year he was recalled to the capital to serve in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was recalled to the capital to conduct affairs in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 既，復令出領總督。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was again sent out to resume the governorship.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered out to resume the governorship.

entries.zh: 金川頭人索諾木攻革布什咱，僧格桑亦圍達木巴宗，侵明正土司。
entries.en: Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu attacked Gebushizan; Senggesang also besieged Damubazong and invaded the Mingzheng chieftaincy.
entries.literal: Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu attacked Gebushizan; Senggesang also besieged Damubazong and invaded the Mingzheng chieftaincy.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰疏言：「兩金川相比，如議出師，需兵既多，糜餉亦鉅。
entries.en: Aertai memorialized: "The two Jinchuans border each other; if a campaign is proposed, it will require large forces and enormous supplies.
entries.literal: Aertai memorialized: "The two Jinchuans adjoin one another; if a campaign is proposed, many troops will be needed and provisions will be enormous.

entries.zh: 茲令董天弼臨之以兵，仍使游擊宋元俊宣諭索諾木。」
entries.en: I now order Dong Tianbi to press him with troops while battalion commander Song Yuanjun is sent to proclaim the imperial will to Suonuomu."
entries.literal: Now order Dong Tianbi to press him with troops, and still send battalion commander Song Yuanjun to proclaim and instruct Suonuomu."

entries.zh: 上責阿爾泰議非是，決策用兵，令定邊右副將軍溫福視師，佐以侍郎桂林，諭斥阿爾泰掩飾偷安，奪大學士、總督，留軍治餉，以桂林代為總督。
entries.en: The emperor rejected Aertai's proposal, decided to use force, appointed Pacification Commissioner on the Right Wen Fu to command the campaign with Vice Minister Guilin as his deputy, rebuked Aertai for covering up problems and seeking an easy peace, stripped him of his grand secretary and governor-general posts, kept him with the army to manage supplies, and replaced him with Guilin as governor-general.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Aertai's proposal as wrong, decided on military action, ordered Pacification Commissioner on the Right Wen Fu to oversee the army with Vice Minister Guilin as assistant, rebuked Aertai for concealment and seeking ease, stripped him of grand secretary and governor-general, kept him with the army to manage supplies, and made Guilin governor in his place.

entries.zh: 師克約咱，上以阿爾泰鑄大砲利軍行，予散秩大臣銜。
entries.en: When the army captured Yozai, the emperor credited Aertai's cast cannon with aiding the campaign and granted him minister-without-portfolio rank.
entries.literal: When the army took Yozai, the emperor, because Aertai's cast cannon had aided the march, granted him the rank of minister without portfolio.

entries.zh: 三十七年，與總兵宋元俊劾桂林覆軍諱敗，上為罷桂林，即命阿爾泰攝總督。
entries.en: In the thirty-seventh year he and regional commander Song Yuanjun impeached Guilin for annihilating his force and concealing defeat; the emperor dismissed Guilin and immediately had Aertai act as governor.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he and regional commander Song Yuanjun impeached Guilin for destroying the army and concealing defeat; the emperor dismissed Guilin and immediately ordered Aertai to act as governor.

entries.zh: 俄移督湖廣。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to govern Huguang.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to govern Huguang.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰疏言：「各路轉餉，當招商承運。
entries.en: Aertai memorialized: "Supply transport on all routes should be contracted to merchants.
entries.literal: Aertai memorialized: "For supply transport on all routes, merchants should be recruited to undertake carriage.

entries.zh: 西路去內地近，南路山險途長，商不肯應募，當增運值。
entries.en: The western route lies close to the interior, but the southern route is mountainous, dangerous, and long, and merchants will not volunteer—transport fees must be raised.
entries.literal: The western route is close to the interior; the southern route is mountainous, dangerous, and long, and merchants will not answer the call—transport fees should be increased.

entries.zh: 火藥已運罄，當令雲南、陝西協助。」
entries.en: Gunpowder supplies have run out in transit; Yunnan and Shaanxi should be ordered to assist."
entries.literal: Gunpowder has already been exhausted in transport; Yunnan and Shaanxi should be ordered to assist."

entries.zh: 上謂：「阿爾泰專領轉餉，何不早籌畫？
entries.en: The emperor said: "Aertai was put solely in charge of supply transport—why did he not plan ahead?
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Aertai was put solely in charge of supply transport—why did he not plan early?

entries.zh: 今福隆安、阿桂皆至南路，始以一奏塞責。」
entries.en: Only now that Fulunga and Agui have both reached the southern route does he submit a memorial merely to cover himself."
entries.literal: Now that Fulunga and Agui have both reached the southern route, he submits one memorial merely to fulfill obligation."

entries.zh: 命毋往湖廣，仍以散秩大臣留軍督餉。
entries.en: He was ordered not to proceed to Huguang but to remain with the army as minister without portfolio supervising supplies.
entries.literal: He was ordered not to go to Huguang but to remain with the army as minister without portfolio supervising supplies.

entries.zh: 未幾，阿桂疏言軍至卡丫，無五日之糧；
entries.en: Before long Agui reported that when the army reached Kayia it had less than five days' grain;
entries.literal: Before long Agui memorialized that when the army reached Kayia it had less than five days' grain;

entries.zh: 又言綽斯甲布轉餉將一月猶未至。
entries.en: he also reported that Zhuosijia's supply transport had been underway for nearly a month without arriving.
entries.literal: he also said Zhuosijia's supply transport had been nearly a month and still had not arrived.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰亦自陳請奪職從軍。
entries.en: Aertai also volunteered to be stripped of rank and serve with the army.
entries.literal: Aertai also volunteered to be stripped of rank and join the campaign.

entries.zh: 上責其倚老負恩，始終不肯以國事為念，命逮問。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him for relying on his age and betraying imperial favor, never putting state affairs first, and ordered his arrest.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him for relying on age and betraying favor, never willing to think of state affairs, and ordered his arrest for interrogation.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰初至四川，上以天壇立燈竿，下四川求楠木。
entries.en: When Aertai first reached Sichuan, the emperor had lamp poles erected at the Temple of Heaven and ordered Sichuan to supply nanmu timber.
entries.literal: When Aertai first reached Sichuan, the emperor had lamp poles erected at the Temple of Heaven and ordered Sichuan to supply nanmu timber.

entries.zh: 阿爾泰附運木材以進，言出養廉採獻。
entries.en: Aertai forwarded timber with his transport and said it had been procured from his integrity stipend for presentation.
entries.literal: Aertai sent timber along with his transport and said it was procured from his integrity stipend for presentation.

entries.zh: 既乃私語人，謂他日且以此負累。
entries.en: Afterward he privately told others that one day this would come back to haunt him.
entries.literal: Afterward he privately told others that one day this would become a burden on him.

entries.zh: 語聞上，上心慊之。
entries.en: When word reached the emperor, he took offense.
entries.literal: When the words reached the emperor, his heart turned against him.

entries.zh: 至是，詔罪狀阿爾泰，猶及此事，斥為昧良飾詐。
entries.en: At this point the edict listing Aertai's crimes still cited this incident and denounced him as ungrateful and deceitful.
entries.literal: At this time the edict listing Aertai's crimes still mentioned this matter and denounced him as ungrateful and deceitful.

entries.zh: 川東道托隆入見，發阿爾泰贓私，下繼任總督富勒渾嚴鞫。
entries.en: Eastern Sichuan circuit intendant Tuo Long came to court and exposed Aertai's corruption; succeeding governor Fulehun was ordered to conduct a strict investigation.
entries.literal: Eastern Sichuan circuit intendant Tuo Long came to audience and exposed Aertai's corruption; the case was referred to succeeding governor Fulehun for strict interrogation.

entries.zh: 三十八年，獄具，擬斬，上命賜自盡。
entries.en: In the thirty-eighth year the case was concluded; decapitation was recommended, but the emperor ordered him granted suicide.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the case was complete; decapitation was recommended, but the emperor ordered him granted suicide.

entries.zh: 桂林，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人，兩廣總督鶴年子。
entries.en: Guilin, of the Irgen Gioro clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was the son of Liangguang governor-general Henian.
entries.literal: Guilin, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner and son of Liangguang governor-general Henian.

entries.zh: 桂林自廩生入貲為工部主事。
entries.en: Guilin purchased office as a secretary in the Ministry of Works from his status as a granary student.
entries.literal: Guilin entered the Ministry of Works as a secretary by purchasing office from his status as a granary student.

entries.zh: 累遷山西按察使。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions until he became provincial judge of Shanxi.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he became Shanxi provincial judge.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十六年三月，擢戶部侍郎、軍機處行走。
entries.en: In the third month of Qianlong 36 he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue and assigned to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the third month of Qianlong 36 he was promoted vice minister of Revenue and assigned to the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 九月，命佐定邊右副將軍溫福討金川。
entries.en: In the ninth month he was ordered to assist Pacification Commissioner on the Right Wen Fu against Jinchuan.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to assist Pacification Commissioner on the Right Wen Fu in campaigning against Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 十一月，授四川總督。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 小金川頭人在卡外投文餽土宜，桂林卻不受，檄罪狀其酋僧格桑。
entries.en: A Lesser Jinchuan chieftain outside the pass submitted a letter and local tribute; Guilin refused them and issued a proclamation listing chieftain Senggesang's crimes.
entries.literal: A Lesser Jinchuan chieftain outside the pass submitted a document and presented local products; Guilin refused them and issued a proclamation listing the crimes of chieftain Senggesang.

entries.zh: 旋督兵收約咱，進克其東山梁大小碉五、石卡二十餘。
entries.en: He soon directed troops to recover Yozai and advanced to capture five blockhouses and more than twenty stone forts on its eastern ridge.
entries.literal: He soon directed troops to recover Yozai and advanced to take five large and small blockhouses and more than twenty stone forts on its eastern ridge.

entries.zh: 疏請添調黔、陝兵五千益師，上許益陝、甘兵三千。
entries.en: He memorialized requesting five thousand additional troops from Guizhou and Shaanxi; the emperor approved three thousand from Shaanxi and Gansu.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting five thousand additional troops from Guizhou and Shaanxi to reinforce the army; the emperor approved three thousand from Shaanxi and Gansu.

entries.zh: 桂林旋督總兵宋元俊攻卡丫，進據墨爾多山梁。
entries.en: Guilin soon directed regional commander Song Yuanjun to attack Kayia and advanced to occupy the Moerduo ridge.
entries.literal: Guilin soon directed regional commander Song Yuanjun to attack Kayia and advanced to occupy the Moerduo ridge.

entries.zh: 上嘉其措置合宜，手詔謂：「無意中用汝，竟能得力。
entries.en: The emperor praised his arrangements and wrote in his own hand: "I appointed you almost by chance, yet you have proved effective.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his arrangements as fitting and wrote in his own hand: "I used you without intending to, yet you have proved effective.

entries.zh: 亦賴在軍機處半年，日耹朕訓也。」
entries.en: That also owes to half a year in the Grand Council, hearing my instruction every day."
entries.literal: This also owes to half a year in the Grand Council, daily hearing my instruction."

entries.zh: 三十七年，克卡丫，复破克郭松、甲木、噶爾金。
entries.en: In the thirty-seventh year Kayia was captured and Guosong, Jiamu, and Ga'erjin were recovered.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year Kayia was taken and Guosong, Jiamu, and Ga'erjin were recovered.

entries.zh: 進克噶爾金後山梁，分兵攻東山梁，襲阿仰，自墨壟溝進取達烏圍。
entries.en: He advanced to take the rear ridge of Ga'erjin, divided his forces to attack the eastern ridge, raided Ayang, and advanced from Molong Gully to take Dawuwei.
entries.literal: He advanced to take the rear ridge of Ga'erjin, divided troops to attack the eastern ridge, raided Ayang, and from Molong Gully advanced to take Dawuwei.

entries.zh: 是時大金川酋索諾木攻陷革布什咱，屯兵其地。
entries.en: At this time Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu had overrun Gebushizan and stationed troops there.
entries.literal: At this time Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu had taken Gebushizan and stationed troops there.

entries.zh: 桂林議乘索諾木兵力未備、革布什咱人心未定，與元俊分兵五道並進，並約將軍溫福合擊，密令革布什咱降酋旺勒丹等約其戚加琿爾為內應，遂收革布什咱寨落七十餘裡。
entries.en: Guilin proposed striking while Suonuomu's forces were unprepared and Gebushizan loyalties unsettled; he and Yuanjun advanced in five columns, coordinated with General Wen Fu for a joint attack, and secretly ordered surrendered chieftain Wangleidan to arrange inside support through his kinsman Jiahuer, recovering more than seventy li of Gebushizan stockades.
entries.literal: Guilin proposed that while Suonuomu's forces were unprepared and Gebushizan loyalties unsettled, he and Yuanjun should advance in five columns together, coordinate a joint strike with General Wen Fu, and secretly order surrendered Gebushizan chieftain Wangleidan and others to arrange with his kinsman Jiahuer as inside support; thus more than seventy li of Gebushizan stockades were recovered.

entries.zh: 旋令元俊及守備陳定國率綽斯甲布土兵屯甲爾壟壩，進攻默資溝、吉地，斷其水道，進攻丹東。
entries.en: He soon ordered Yuanjun and garrison commandant Chen Dingguo to lead Zhuosijia troops to garrison at Jia'erlongba, attack Mozigou and Jidi, cut enemy water supplies, and advance on Dandong.
entries.literal: He soon ordered Yuanjun and garrison commandant Chen Dingguo to lead Zhuosijia native troops to garrison at Jia'erlongba, attack Mozigou and Jidi, cut their water supply, and advance against Dandong.

entries.zh: 上獎桂林甚合機宜，促元俊乘勝深入取索諾木。
entries.en: The emperor praised Guilin's timing and urged Yuanjun to press the victory and capture Suonuomu.
entries.literal: The emperor praised Guilin as very well timed and urged Yuanjun to press the victory deep and capture Suonuomu.

entries.zh: 桂林遣裨將自東山梁墨壟溝越嶺進攻，別遣兵出間道，自札哇窠山梁縋崖設伏師。
entries.en: Guilin sent a deputy general from the eastern ridge over Molong Gully to attack across the pass, and separately sent troops by a hidden route to lower ropes from Zhawake Ridge and set an ambush.
entries.literal: Guilin sent a deputy general from the eastern ridge over Molong Gully to attack across the pass, and separately sent troops by a hidden route to lower ropes from Zhawake Ridge and set an ambush.

entries.zh: 既度東山梁墨壟溝，札哇窠伏兵亦起，賊敗竄，克大碉一、石卡二十一。
entries.en: Once they crossed the eastern ridge and Molong Gully, the Zhawake ambush struck as well; the rebels were routed; one large blockhouse and twenty-one stone forts were captured.
entries.literal: Once they crossed the eastern ridge and Molong Gully, the Zhawake ambush also rose; the rebels were defeated and fled; one large blockhouse and twenty-one stone forts were taken.

entries.zh: 別遣參將常泰環攻黨哩，都司李天貴等攻沙沖，革布什咱頭人為內應，賊盡殲。
entries.en: He separately sent colonel Chang Tai to encircle Dangli and brigade commander Li Tiangui and others to attack Shachong; Gebushizan chieftains served as inside allies and the rebels were annihilated.
entries.literal: He separately sent colonel Chang Tai to encircle Dangli and brigade commander Li Tiangui and others to attack Shachong; Gebushizan chieftains served as inside support and the rebels were annihilated.

entries.zh: 黨哩、沙沖地並復。
entries.en: The territories of Dangli and Shachong were also recovered.
entries.literal: The territories of Dangli and Shachong were also recovered.

entries.zh: 總兵英泰等復攻克達烏官寨。
entries.en: Regional commander Ying Tai and others again captured the Dawu official stockade.
entries.literal: Regional commander Ying Tai and others again took the Dawu official stockade.

entries.zh: 上嘉其功，賜御用玉韘。
entries.en: The emperor praised his achievement and bestowed an imperial jade archer's ring.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his achievement and bestowed an imperial jade archer's ring.

entries.zh: 再進攻克格烏巴桑及那隆山嶺。
entries.en: Advancing again, he captured Gewubasang and the Nalong ridge.
entries.literal: Advancing again, he took Gewubasang and the Nalong mountain ridge.

entries.zh: 元俊別攻克丹東及覺拉喇嘛寺，誅賊渠三百、番眾百三十餘。
entries.en: Yuanjun separately captured Dandong and the Juela Lama Temple, executing three hundred rebel leaders and more than one hundred thirty tribesmen.
entries.literal: Yuanjun separately took Dandong and the Juela Lama Temple, executing three hundred rebel leaders and more than one hundred thirty tribesmen.

entries.zh: 革布什咱地盡复，桂林檄定國將所調綽斯甲布兵駐界上聽調。
entries.en: Gebushizan territory was fully recovered; Guilin ordered Dingguo to station the Zhuosijia troops he had mobilized on the border awaiting orders.
entries.literal: Gebushizan territory was fully recovered; Guilin ordered Dingguo to station the Zhuosijia troops he had mobilized on the border awaiting orders.

entries.zh: 上以革布什咱既复，正當乘勝進剿金川，攻其無備，責桂林失算。
entries.en: The emperor said that with Gebushizan recovered, Guilin should have pressed the victory against Jinchuan while the enemy was unprepared, and rebuked him for poor judgment.
entries.literal: The emperor said that with Gebushizan recovered, this was the moment to press the victory against Jinchuan and strike while they were unprepared, and rebuked Guilin for poor judgment.

entries.zh: 桂林复督兵攻達烏東岸山梁，參將薛琮戰沒，琮驍將，深入糧盡。
entries.en: Guilin again directed troops against the eastern bank ridge of Dawu; colonel Xue Cong was killed in battle—a fierce commander who had advanced deep and run out of supplies.
entries.literal: Guilin again directed troops to attack the eastern bank ridge of Dawu; colonel Xue Cong was killed in battle—Cong was a fierce commander who had advanced deep and exhausted his grain.

entries.zh: 桂林既失期不會師，又不以時遣援，軍盡覆，疏請治罪，述戰狀不敢盡。
entries.en: Guilin had missed the rendezvous and failed to send relief in time; the army was annihilated; he memorialized requesting punishment and did not dare report the full extent of the defeat.
entries.literal: Guilin had missed the rendezvous and failed to send relief in time; the army was annihilated; he memorialized requesting punishment and dared not report the battle in full.

entries.zh: 元俊與散秩大臣阿爾泰劾其虛誑，並言桂林在卡丫建屋宇以居，迫屬僚供應，與副都統鐵保、提督汪騰龍等終日酣飲，諸將罕得見；
entries.en: Yuanjun and minister without portfolio Aertai impeached him for false reporting, also alleging that Guilin had built houses at Kayia for his residence, compelled subordinates to supply him, and with vice commander Tie Bao, provincial commander Wang Tenglong, and others drank all day while his generals rarely saw him;
entries.literal: Yuanjun and minister without portfolio Aertai impeached him for falsehood, also saying Guilin had built houses at Kayia to live in, compelled subordinates to supply him, and with vice commander Tie Bao, provincial commander Wang Tenglong, and others drank all day while generals rarely saw him;

entries.zh: 密令騰龍畀總兵王萬邦白金五百，贖被掠官兵，希圖掩飾。
entries.en: he secretly ordered Tenglong to give regional commander Wang Wanbang five hundred taels of silver to ransom captured officers and men, hoping to cover up the defeat.
entries.literal: he secretly ordered Tenglong to give regional commander Wang Wanbang five hundred taels of silver to ransom captured officers and soldiers, hoping to cover up the matter.

entries.zh: 上奪桂林職，命額駙、尚書、公福隆安馳往按治，尋奏所劾皆虛，惟官兵傷損不即察奏屬實；
entries.en: The emperor stripped Guilin of office and ordered imperial son-in-law, minister, and duke Fulunga to investigate on the spot; Fulunga soon reported that the charges were largely false, except that Guilin had failed to report promptly on casualties among officers and soldiers;
entries.literal: The emperor stripped Guilin of office and ordered imperial son-in-law, minister, and duke Fulunga to hurry there to investigate; he soon reported that the impeachments were all false, except that failure to report promptly on casualties among officers and soldiers was true;

entries.zh: 至贖被掠官兵，乃在軍戶部郎中汪承霈聞巴旺、布拉克底土兵歸失道，官兵告桂林，發白金五百交騰龍備賞，事為元俊構陷，請分別治罪。
entries.en: as for ransoming captured troops, Revenue Bureau director Wang Chengpei with the army learned that Bawang and Bulakedi native troops had lost their way on return; officers and soldiers informed Guilin, who issued five hundred taels of silver to Tenglong for rewards—this was a frame-up by Yuanjun; he requested that punishments be assigned separately.
entries.literal: as for ransoming captured troops, Revenue Bureau director Wang Chengpei with the army, learning that Bawang and Bulakedi native troops had lost their way on return, had officers and soldiers inform Guilin, who issued five hundred taels of silver to Tenglong for rewards—the matter was framed by Yuanjun; he requested separate punishments.

entries.zh: 上以桂林在軍日親曲糱，止圖安逸，不能與士卒同甘苦，致北山梁傷損多兵，不得為無罪，命戍伊犁。
entries.en: The emperor said that in camp Guilin personally attended to brewing, sought only comfort, could not share hardship with his soldiers, and caused heavy casualties on the northern ridge—he could not be held guiltless—and ordered him exiled to Yili.
entries.literal: The emperor said that in camp Guilin personally attended to brewing, sought only ease, could not share hardship with the soldiers, and caused heavy casualties on the northern ridge—he could not be held guiltless—and ordered him exiled to Yili.

entries.zh: 三十八年七月，予三等侍衛銜，仍詣軍前督糧運。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the thirty-eighth year he was given third-class bodyguard rank and again sent to the front to supervise grain transport.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-eighth year he was given third-class bodyguard rank and again sent to the front to supervise grain transport.

entries.zh: 四十年，授頭等侍衛。
entries.en: In the fortieth year he was appointed first-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he was appointed first-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 尋授四川提督，遷兩廣總督。
entries.en: He was soon appointed provincial commander of Sichuan and then governor-general of Liangguang.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed provincial commander of Sichuan and transferred to governor-general of Liangguang.

entries.zh: 卒，加太子太保銜，諡壯敏。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent rank and the posthumous name Zhuangmin.
entries.literal: He died and was given the posthumous rank Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Zhuangmin.

entries.zh: 三十六年，師徵金川，授定邊右副將軍，以侍郎桂林佐之，共討賊。
entries.en: In the thirty-sixth year the army campaigned against Jinchuan; he was appointed Pacification Commissioner on the Right with Vice Minister Guilin as his deputy to campaign against the rebels.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year troops campaigned against Jinchuan; he was appointed Pacification Commissioner on the Right with Vice Minister Guilin as assistant to campaign against the rebels together.

entries.zh: 溫福自汶川出西路，桂林自打箭爐出南路。
entries.en: Wen Fu advanced by the western route from Wenchuan; Guilin advanced by the southern route from Dajianlu.
entries.literal: Wen Fu marched out by the western route from Wenchuan; Guilin marched out by the southern route from Dajianlu.

entries.zh: 時小金川頭人澤旺子僧格桑割地乞援於大金川頭人索諾木，索諾木潛遣兵助之。
entries.en: At this time Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's son Senggesang ceded territory to beg aid from Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu, who secretly sent troops to assist him.
entries.literal: At this time Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's son Senggesang ceded territory to beg aid from Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suonuomu, who secretly sent troops to help him.

entries.zh: 上命先剿小金​​川，且勿聲大金川罪。
entries.en: The emperor ordered that Lesser Jinchuan be suppressed first and that Greater Jinchuan's complicity not be proclaimed.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered that Lesser Jinchuan be suppressed first and that Greater Jinchuan's guilt not be proclaimed.

entries.zh: 溫福至打箭爐，分兵三道入：溫福出巴朗拉，提督董天弼自甲金達援達木巴宗，總督阿爾泰自約咱攻僧格桑。
entries.en: Wen Fu reached Dajianlu and divided his forces into three columns: Wen Fu advanced by Balang La, provincial commander Dong Tianbi from Jajianda to relieve Damubazong, and governor Aertai from Yozai against Senggesang.
entries.literal: Wen Fu reached Dajianlu and divided the army into three columns: Wen Fu advanced by Balang La, provincial commander Dong Tianbi from Jajianda to relieve Damubazong, and governor Aertai from Yozai against Senggesang.

entries.zh: 十一月，擢武英殿大學士。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he was promoted grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he was promoted grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

entries.zh: 十二月，至巴朗拉，戰三晝夜，賊敗去。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he reached Balang La, fought for three days and nights, and the rebels were defeated and withdrew.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he reached Balang La, fought three days and nights, and the rebels were defeated and withdrew.

entries.zh: 三十七年正月，取達木巴宗。
entries.en: In the first month of the thirty-seventh year Damubazong was captured.
entries.literal: In the first month of the thirty-seventh year Damubazong was taken.

entries.zh: 進攻斯底葉安，而分軍出別斯滿、瑪爾瓦爾濟，兩路夾擊，進克資哩。
entries.en: He advanced against Sidiye'an while dividing troops through Biesiman and Ma'erwa'erji for a pincer attack and captured Zili.
entries.literal: He advanced against Sidiye'an while dividing troops out by Biesiman and Ma'erwa'erji for a two-pronged attack and took Zili.

entries.zh: 再進克東瑪，再進克路頂宗及喀木色爾，取諸碉寨。
entries.en: Advancing again he captured Dongma, then Ludingzong and Kamuse'er, and seized the blockhouses and stockades.
entries.literal: Advancing again he took Dongma, then Ludingzong and Kamuse'er, and seized the blockhouses and stockades.

entries.zh: 再進得博爾根山梁，並攻克得瑪覺烏寨落，攻公雅山。
entries.en: Advancing again he took the Bo'ergen ridge, also captured the Demajuewu stockades, and attacked Gongya Mountain.
entries.literal: Advancing again he gained the Bo'ergen ridge, also took the Demajuewu stockades, and attacked Gongya Mountain.

entries.zh: 十二月，授定邊將軍，以阿桂、豐升額副之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he was appointed Pacification General with Agui and Fengsheng'e as deputies.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed Pacification General with Agui and Fengsheng'e as deputies.

entries.zh: 進克明郭宗，再進克底木達。
entries.en: He advanced to capture Mingguozong and then Dimuda.
entries.literal: He advanced to take Mingguozong and again took Dimuda.

entries.zh: 底木達者，僧格桑父澤旺所居寨也。
entries.en: Dimuda was the stockade where Senggesang's father Zewang had lived.
entries.literal: Dimuda was the stockade where Senggesang's father Zewang had resided.

entries.zh: 師至，俘澤旺，檻致京師，誅於市，而僧格桑奔大金川。
entries.en: When the army arrived, Zewang was captured, sent to the capital in a cage, and executed in the marketplace, while Senggesang fled to Greater Jinchuan.
entries.literal: When the army arrived, Zewang was captured, sent to the capital in a cage, and executed in the marketplace, while Senggesang fled to Greater Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 溫福檄索諾木令縛獻僧格桑，不應。
entries.en: Wen Fu ordered Suonuomu by proclamation to bind and deliver Senggesang; he refused.
entries.literal: Wen Fu ordered Suonuomu by proclamation to bind and deliver Senggesang; he did not comply.

entries.zh: 上將進討大金川，溫福等疏言：「前此張廣泗徵金川，十路、七路分合不常，實祗有六路，皆以抵勒烏圍、噶爾依為主。
entries.en: The emperor was preparing to advance against Greater Jinchuan; Wen Fu and others memorialized: "When Zhang Guangsi campaigned against Jinchuan before, accounts spoke of ten or seven routes with shifting combinations—in fact there were only six routes, all aimed chiefly at Lewuwei and Ga'eryi.
entries.literal: The emperor was about to advance against Greater Jinchuan; Wen Fu and others memorialized: "When Zhang Guangsi campaigned against Jinchuan before, ten routes or seven routes were spoken of with shifting combinations—in fact there were only six routes, all aimed chiefly at reaching Lewuwei and Ga'eryi.

entries.zh: 一為卡撒正路，自美諾至噶爾依，約五程，為傅恆進兵路；
entries.en: One was the main Kasai route from Meinuo to Ga'eryi, about five stages—the route Fu Heng had used;
entries.literal: One was the main Kasai route from Meinuo to Ga'eryi, about five stages, the route by which Fu Heng advanced;

entries.zh: 一為丹壩，自維州橋經番地抵勒烏圍，約二十餘程，中有穆津岡天險，為岳鍾琪進兵路；
entries.en: one was Danba, from Weizhou Bridge through native territory to Lewuwei, about twenty stages, with the natural barrier of Mujingang in between—the route Yue Zhongqi had used;
entries.literal: one was Danba, from Weizhou Bridge through native territory to Lewuwei, about twenty-odd stages, with the heavenly barrier of Mujingang in between, the route by which Yue Zhongqi advanced;

entries.zh: 一地名僧格桑，自美諾抵噶爾依，六七程，即總兵馬良柱所行路；
entries.en: one route passed through a place named Senggesang, from Meinuo to Ga'eryi in six or seven stages—the route regional commander Ma Liangzhu had taken;
entries.literal: one place was named Senggesang, from Meinuo to Ga'eryi, six or seven stages, the route taken by regional commander Ma Liangzhu;

entries.zh: 一為革布什咱，一為馬爾邦，皆距噶爾依六七程，險狹難行；
entries.en: one was Gebushizan and one Ma'erbang, each six or seven stages from Ga'eryi, narrow, dangerous, and hard to travel;
entries.literal: one was Gebushizan and one Ma'erbang, each six or seven stages from Ga'eryi, narrow and dangerous and hard to travel;

entries.zh: 一為綽斯甲布寨至勒烏圍三程，至噶爾依亦三程，均隔大河，碉寨林立，難攻。
entries.en: one ran from Zhuosijia stockade to Lewuwei in three stages and to Ga'eryi in another three, all separated by great rivers with dense blockhouses and stockades that were hard to attack.
entries.literal: one was from Zhuosijia stockade to Lewuwei in three stages and to Ga'eryi also three stages, all separated by great rivers with blockhouses and stockades standing thick and hard to attack.

entries.zh: 此外又有俄坡一路，從綽斯甲布寨至勒烏圍，僅二程，路較平。
entries.en: Besides these there was also the Epo route from Zhuosijia stockade to Lewuwei, only two stages, with a comparatively level road.
entries.literal: Besides these there was also the Epo route from Zhuosijia stockade to Lewuwei, only two stages, with a comparatively level road.

entries.zh: 今當由卡撒正路進兵，其俄坡一路，既有綽斯甲布土司原出兵復其侵地，可為犄角。
entries.en: Now the army should advance by the main Kasai route; on the Epo route the Zhuosijia chieftain is already sending troops to recover seized territory and can serve as a supporting force.
entries.literal: Now the army should advance by the main Kasai route; on the Epo route the Zhuosijia chieftain is already sending troops to recover seized territory and can serve as a pincer.

entries.zh: 其餘各路，分兵牽制，使不能兼顧。」
entries.en: On the remaining routes troops should be divided to pin down the enemy so they cannot defend everywhere at once."
entries.literal: On the remaining routes troops should be divided to pin down the enemy so they cannot attend to everything."

entries.zh: 於是溫福自功噶爾拉入，阿桂自當噶爾拉入，豐升額自綽斯甲布入。
entries.en: Thereupon Wen Fu entered by Gongga'er La, Agui by Dangga'er La, and Fengsheng'e by Zhuosijia.
entries.literal: Thereupon Wen Fu entered by Gongga'er La, Agui by Dangga'er La, and Fengsheng'e by Zhuosijia.

entries.zh: 溫福性剛愎，不廣諮方略，惟襲訥親、張廣泗故事，以碉卡攻碉卡，修築千計。
entries.en: Wen Fu was stubborn by nature, did not widely consult on strategy, and only followed the precedents of Neqin and Zhang Guangsi—attacking blockhouses with blockhouses and building thousands of fortifications.
entries.literal: Wen Fu was stubborn by nature, did not widely consult on strategy, and only followed the precedents of Neqin and Zhang Guangsi—attacking blockhouses with blockhouses and building by the thousands.

entries.zh: 所將兵二萬餘，強半散在各碉卡。
entries.en: The troops under his command numbered more than twenty thousand, more than half scattered among the various blockhouses.
entries.literal: The troops he commanded numbered more than twenty thousand, more than half scattered among the various blockhouses.

entries.zh: 每逾數日當奏事，即督兵攻碉。
entries.en: Every few days when he should have reported to the throne, he instead directed troops to attack blockhouses.
entries.literal: Every few days when he should have reported affairs, he instead directed troops to attack blockhouses.

entries.zh: 士卒多傷亡，諮怨無鬥志。
entries.en: The soldiers suffered heavy casualties, complained bitterly, and lost all fighting spirit.
entries.literal: Soldiers suffered many casualties, complained bitterly, and had no fighting spirit.

entries.zh: 溫福日置酒高會，參贊伍岱歎曰：「焉有為帥若此而能制勝者？」
entries.en: Wen Fu held grand banquets every day; staff officer Wu Dai sighed and said: "How can a commander like this ever win a victory?"
entries.literal: Wen Fu daily held grand banquets; staff officer Wu Dai sighed and said: "How can a commander like this ever win victory?"

entries.zh: 因密疏聞上，溫福亦疏劾伍岱。
entries.en: He therefore sent a secret memorial to the emperor; Wen Fu also memorialized to impeach Wu Dai.
entries.literal: He therefore memorialized the emperor in secret; Wen Fu also memorialized to impeach Wu Dai.

entries.zh: 上命豐升額及額駙色布騰巴勒珠爾按治。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Fengsheng'e and imperial son-in-law Sebuteng Balzhu'er to investigate the matter.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Fengsheng'e and imperial son-in-law Sebuteng Balzhu'er to investigate.

entries.zh: 溫福又言色布騰巴勒珠爾朋比傾陷，上為奪伍岱職，令色布騰巴勒珠爾逮詣熱河行在，獄成，戍伍岱伊犁。
entries.en: Wen Fu also claimed that Sebuteng Balzhu'er had formed a faction to frame him; the emperor stripped Wu Dai of office, ordered Sebuteng Balzhu'er arrested and sent to the Rehe traveling palace; when the case was concluded, Wu Dai was exiled to Yili.
entries.literal: Wen Fu also said Sebuteng Balzhu'er had formed a faction to frame him; the emperor stripped Wu Dai of office, ordered Sebuteng Balzhu'er arrested and sent to the Rehe traveling palace; when the case was complete, Wu Dai was exiled to Yili.

entries.zh: 三十八年春，溫福師至功噶爾拉，賊阻險，不得進，別取道攻昔嶺，駐軍木果木；
entries.en: In the spring of the thirty-eighth year Wen Fu's army reached Gongga'er La; the rebels held the dangerous passes and he could not advance, so he took another route to attack Xiling and encamped at Muguo Wood;
entries.literal: In the spring of the thirty-eighth year Wen Fu's army reached Gongga'er La; the rebels blocked the dangerous passes and he could not advance, so he took another route to attack Xiling and stationed troops at Muguo Wood;

entries.zh: 令提督董天弼分軍屯底木達。
entries.en: he ordered provincial commander Dong Tianbi to divide his forces and garrison Dimuda.
entries.literal: he ordered provincial commander Dong Tianbi to divide troops and garrison Dimuda.

entries.zh: 木果木、底木達皆故小金川地，索諾木陰使小金川頭人煽諸降番使復叛。
entries.en: Muguo Wood and Dimuda were both former Lesser Jinchuan territory; Suonuomu secretly had Lesser Jinchuan chieftains incite the surrendered tribes to rebel again.
entries.literal: Muguo Wood and Dimuda were both former Lesser Jinchuan territory; Suonuomu secretly had Lesser Jinchuan chieftains incite the surrendered tribes to rebel again.

entries.zh: 諸降番以師久頓不進，遂蜂起應之。
entries.en: The surrendered tribes, seeing the army stalled for so long without advancing, rose in swarms to join the rebellion.
entries.literal: The surrendered tribes, because the army had long halted without advancing, rose in swarms to answer the call.

entries.zh: 先攻底木達，天弼死之，次劫糧台，潛襲木果木。
entries.en: They first attacked Dimuda and Tianbi was killed; next they raided the grain depots and launched a surprise attack on Muguo Wood.
entries.literal: They first attacked Dimuda and Tianbi was killed; next they raided the grain depots and secretly struck Muguo Wood.

entries.zh: 溫福不嚴備山後要隘，賊突薄大營，奪砲局，斷汲道。
entries.en: Wen Fu failed to guard the vital passes in the rear; the rebels suddenly pressed the main camp, seized the artillery park, and cut off the water supply.
