entries.literal: Wen Fu did not strictly guard the vital passes behind the mountains; the rebels suddenly pressed the great camp, seized the artillery park, and cut off the water route.

entries.zh: 時大營兵尚萬餘，運糧役數千，爭避入大營，溫福堅閉壘門不納，轟而潰，聲如壞堤，於是軍心益震。
entries.en: The main camp still held more than ten thousand troops and several thousand transport laborers, all scrambling to flee inside; Wen Fu firmly closed the stockade gates and refused them entry; they collapsed in a roar like a broken dike, and army morale collapsed with them.
entries.literal: At the time the great camp still had more than ten thousand troops and several thousand transport laborers, all scrambling to flee into the camp; Wen Fu firmly closed the stockade gates and would not admit them; they collapsed in a roar like a broken dike, and army morale was shaken all the more.

entries.zh: 賊四面蹂入，溫福中槍死，各卡兵望風潰散。
entries.en: The rebels overran the camp from all sides; Wen Fu was shot and killed; troops at every post fled at the mere sight of the enemy.
entries.literal: The rebels trampled in from all sides; Wen Fu was shot and died; troops at every post fled at the mere sight of them.

entries.zh: 參贊海蘭察聞警赴援，殿餘兵自間道出。
entries.en: Staff officer Hailancha, hearing the alarm, rushed to their aid and covered the retreat of the surviving troops along a hidden route.
entries.literal: Staff officer Hailancha, hearing the alarm, went to relieve them and covered the retreat of the remaining troops out by a hidden route.

entries.zh: 小金川地盡陷。
entries.en: All of Lesser Jinchuan territory was lost.
entries.literal: Lesser Jinchuan territory fell entirely.

entries.zh: 上初聞溫福死，詔予一等伯爵，世襲罔替，祀昭忠祠。
entries.en: When the emperor first heard of Wen Fu's death, he decreed him a first-class earl with perpetual hereditary succession and enshrinement in the Temple of Loyalty.
entries.literal: When the emperor first heard of Wen Fu's death, he decreed him a first-class earl with perpetual hereditary succession and enshrinement in the Temple of Loyalty.

entries.zh: 既，劉秉恬、海蘭察、富勒渾各疏言溫福僨事狀，命奪伯爵，予三等輕車都尉世職。
entries.en: Afterward Liu Bingtian, Hailancha, and Fulehun each memorialized on Wen Fu's disastrous conduct; he was stripped of the earldom and given the hereditary rank of third-class commandant of light chariots.
entries.literal: Afterward Liu Bingtian, Hailancha, and Fulehun each memorialized on Wen Fu's ruinous conduct; he was ordered stripped of the earldom and given the hereditary rank of third-class commandant of light chariots.

entries.zh: 四十一年，命並罷之。
entries.en: In the forty-first year all honors were revoked.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year he was ordered stripped of all honors.

entries.zh: 子勒保、永保，皆有傳。
entries.en: His sons Lebao and Yongbao each have biographies of their own.
entries.literal: His sons Lebao and Yongbao each have biographies.

entries.zh: 楊應琚，字佩之，漢軍正白旗人，廣東巡撫文乾子。
entries.en: Yang Yingju, styled Peizhi, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Banner of the Han Army and the son of Wen Qian, Governor of Guangdong.
entries.literal: Yang Yingju, styled Peizhi, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Banner of the Han Army; son of Wen Qian, Governor of Guangdong.

entries.zh: 應琚起家任子。
entries.en: Yingju began his career through the hereditary privilege of an official's son.
entries.literal: Yingju began his career as an hereditary official's son.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，自員外郎出為河東道，調西寧道。
entries.en: In the early Qianlong years he left his post as Bureau Director to serve as Intendant of Hedong, and was later transferred to Xining Circuit.
entries.literal: In early Qianlong, from Bureau Director he went out as Intendant of Hedong, then was transferred to Xining Circuit.

entries.zh: 巡撫黃廷桂薦其才，高宗曰：「若能進於誠而擴充之，正未可量也。」
entries.en: Governor Huang Tinggui recommended his talent; the Gaozong said, "If he can advance in sincerity and build upon it, his future is indeed hard to measure."
entries.literal: Governor Huang Tinggui recommended his talent; the Gaozong said: "If he can advance in sincerity and expand upon it, his future is indeed hard to measure."

entries.zh: 累遷至兩廣總督。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor-General of Liang-Guang.

entries.zh: 先後疏請練水師，籌軍食，修漓水、陡河堤壩，貯柳、桂、慶、梧餘鹽，皆如所請行。
entries.en: He successively memorialized to train naval forces, provision the army, repair the dikes on the Li and Dou Rivers, and store surplus salt from Liu, Gui, Qing, and Wu; all his requests were approved and carried out.
entries.literal: He successively memorialized to train naval forces, provision the army, repair dikes on the Li and Dou Rivers, and store surplus salt from Liu, Gui, Qing, and Wu—all were approved and carried out.

entries.zh: 暹羅貢使毆傷通事，其國王鞫實，擬罰鍰，遣使牒禮部。
entries.en: A Siamese tribute envoy beat a court attendant; the king of that country investigated the facts, proposed a fine, and sent a messenger to lodge a memorial with the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: A Siam tribute envoy beat a court attendant; the king of that country investigated, proposed a fine, and sent a messenger to memorialize the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 應琚曰：「屬國陪臣無上交。」
entries.en: Yingju said, "Attendant ministers of a tributary state have no presentation to make to the superior court."
entries.literal: Yingju said: "A tributary state's attendant ministers have no presentation to the superior court."

entries.zh: 好語諭遣之，稱旨。
entries.en: He received them with kind words of instruction and sent them on their way; this pleased the Emperor.
entries.literal: He received them with kind words of instruction and sent them off; this pleased the Emperor.

entries.zh: 二十二年，移閩浙總督。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Governor-General of Fujian-Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 二十三年，加太子太保。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year he was given the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he was given the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 劉藻，字素存，山東菏澤人。
entries.en: Liu Zao, styled Sucun, was a native of Heze in Shandong.
entries.literal: Liu Zao, styled Sucun, was a native of Heze, Shandong.

entries.zh: 初名玉麟，以舉人授觀城教諭，乾隆元年，薦舉博學鴻詞，試一等，授檢討，更名。
entries.en: Originally named Yulin, he received appointment as instructor at Guancheng on the strength of his juren degree. In the first year of the Qianlong reign he was recommended for the special examination in erudite learning and polished composition, ranked in the first class, appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy, and given his present name.
entries.literal: His original name was Yulin. As a juren he was appointed instructor at Guancheng. In the first year of Qianlong he was recommended for the Boxue Hongci examination, placed in the first class, appointed reviser, and renamed.

entries.zh: 累遷左僉都御史。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 圓明園工興，疏言：「園工不過少加補葺，視前代飾臺榭之觀者度越何啻萬萬？
entries.en: When construction at the Yuanming Garden began, he submitted a memorial: "The work on the garden amounts to little more than patching and repair—how can it be compared, by countless degrees, with the lavish pavilions and terraces of earlier dynasties?
entries.literal: When work on the Yuanming Garden began, he memorialized: "The garden work is no more than minor repairs and patching—how can it compare, by countless degrees, with the pavilions and terraces ornamented by previous dynasties?

entries.zh: 臣愚以為奢靡之漸，不可稍開。
entries.en: Your servant is convinced that the first steps toward extravagance must not be opened even slightly.
entries.literal: This humble subject believes that the first steps toward extravagance must not be opened even slightly.

entries.zh: 乞皇上慎始慮終，為天地惜物力，為國家培元氣，來歲諸工酌量停減。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to be careful at the outset and thoughtful to the end, to spare material resources for Heaven and Earth, to nurture the vital energy of the state, and to suspend or scale back the various works next year as appropriate."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to be careful at the beginning and thoughtful to the end, to spare material resources for Heaven and Earth, to nurture the vital energy of the state, and to suspend or reduce various projects next year as appropriate."

entries.zh: 上嘉納。
entries.en: The Emperor praised and accepted the memorial.
entries.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.

entries.zh: 遷通政使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

entries.zh: 六年，擢內閣學士。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the reign he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 督江蘇學政。
entries.en: He served as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
entries.literal: He supervised the educational administration of Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 尋以高郵諸生求賑而閧，左授宗人府府丞。
entries.en: Soon afterward, because students from Gaoyou had rioted while petitioning for relief grain, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: Soon, because students from Gaoyou rioted while seeking relief grain, he was demoted on the left to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 藻居揚州候代，有吳之黼者，以文求教，藻行，饋糟魚，受之，中途發視，得白金四百，藻畀兩淮運使硃續晫還之黼。
entries.en: While Zao was staying in Yangzhou awaiting reassignment, a man named Wu Zhifu sought his instruction in literature. When Zao set out on his journey, Zhifu presented pickled fish as a gift; he accepted it, but on the road opened it and found four hundred taels of silver inside. Zao entrusted the money to the Lianghuai grain transport commissioner Zhu Xuzhe to return it to Zhifu.
entries.literal: Zao was staying in Yangzhou awaiting reassignment. A certain Wu Zhifu sought instruction in literature. When Zao departed, Zhifu presented pickled fish; he accepted it, and midway opened it to look inside, finding four hundred taels of silver. Zao handed it to the Lianghuai grain transport commissioner Zhu Xuzhe to return to Zhifu.

entries.zh: 上聞，諭曰：「如此方不愧四知！」
entries.en: When the Emperor heard of it, he remarked, "Only in this way is one worthy of the Four Knowings!"
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he instructed: "Only thus is one worthy of the Four Knowings!"

entries.zh: 旋乞養歸。
entries.en: He soon requested leave to return home and care for his mother.
entries.literal: He soon requested leave to return home to care for his mother.

entries.zh: 孝賢皇后及長皇子定安親王喪，藻詣闕入見。
entries.en: During the mourning for Empress Xiaoxian and for the Prince of Ding'an, the eldest imperial son, Zao came to the capital for an audience.
entries.literal: At the mourning for Empress Xiaoxian and for the Prince of Ding'an, the eldest imperial son, Zao came to the capital for an audience.

entries.zh: 會大學士張廷玉乞歸失上指，因獎藻，謂其知君臣休戚相關大義，以媿廷玉，加藻內閣學士銜，賜人葠二斤，命歸養母。
entries.en: At the time Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu's request to retire had displeased the Emperor; the Emperor therefore praised Zao, saying that he understood the great principle that ruler and minister share weal and woe alike, so as to shame Zhang Tingyu. He granted Zao the title of Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, bestowed two jin of ginseng, and ordered him home to care for his mother.
entries.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu's request to retire had missed the Emperor's intent; the Emperor therefore praised Zao, saying he understood the great principle that ruler and minister share weal and woe, to shame Zhang Tingyu; he added to Zao the title of Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, bestowed two jin of ginseng, and ordered him to return home to support his mother.

entries.zh: 母喪終，二十一年，授陝西布政使。
entries.en: When his period of mourning for his mother ended, in the twenty-first year of the reign he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi.
entries.literal: When his mother's mourning ended, in the twenty-first year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 二十二年，擢雲南巡撫。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Governor of Yunnan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Governor of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 加太子少保，兼領貴州巡撫。
entries.en: He was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrently served as Governor of Guizhou.
entries.literal: He was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrently governed Guizhou as governor.

entries.zh: 二十九年，例行大計，巡撫圖爾炳阿未至，藻疏請先期舉行，上嘉之，旋授雲貴總督。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year, at the regular grand evaluation of officials, Governor Tu Erbing'a had not yet arrived; Zao memorialized asking that it be held early. The Emperor commended this, and soon afterward appointed him Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at the regular grand evaluation, Governor Tu Erbing'a had not yet arrived; Zao memorialized asking to hold it early; the Emperor praised this, and soon appointed him Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou.

entries.zh: 三十年，疏言：「年來木梳野匪與緬甸所屬木邦構釁，又與耿馬土司毗連。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year he memorialized: "In recent years the Musuo bandits have clashed with Mohang, which is subject to Burma, and their territory also adjoins the Gengma native office.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he memorialized: "In recent years the Musuo bandits have provoked trouble with Mohang, subject to Burma, and also border on the Gengma native office.

entries.zh: 自木邦至滾弄江，應設卡防守，請於各土司就近派撥。」
entries.en: From Mohang to the Gunong River, guard posts ought to be established for defense; he asked that men be assigned from the nearest native offices."
entries.literal: From Mohang to the Gunong River, guard posts should be set up for defense; he requested that troops be assigned from nearby native offices."

entries.zh: 詔如所請。
entries.en: An imperial decree approved his request.
entries.literal: The imperial decree approved as requested.

entries.zh: 三十一年，移湖廣總督，未行，尋奏：「副將趙宏榜等赴孟連、耿馬剿逐莽匪，鎮臣烏爾登額赴滾弄江口。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to Governor-General of Huguang but had not yet set out when he soon memorialized: "Brigadier Zhao Hongbang and others have gone to Menglian and Gengma to pursue and drive off the Mang bandits, while Commander Wu Erden'e has gone to the mouth of the Gunong River.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to Governor-General of Huguang but had not yet departed when he soon memorialized: "Brigadier Zhao Hongbang and others went to Menglian and Gengma to pursue and drive off the Mang bandits; Commander Wu Erden'e went to the Gunong River mouth.

entries.zh: 臣於普洱、思茅各隘調度。」
entries.en: Your servant will coordinate affairs at the various passes of Pu'er and Simao."
entries.literal: Your subject will coordinate at the various passes of Pu'er and Simao."

entries.zh: 又奏言：「由小猛崙進攻九龍江、橄欖壩諸寨，多斬獲。
entries.en: He also reported: "Advancing from Xiaomenglun against the stockades at Jiulong River, Ganlanba, and elsewhere, our forces killed and captured many of the enemy.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "Advancing from Xiaomenglun to attack the stockades at Jiulong River, Ganlanba, and elsewhere, many were killed and captured.

entries.zh: 惟參將何瓊詔、游擊明浩派赴整控江防禦，冒昧渡江，遇賊敗沒。」
entries.en: Only Regiment Commander He Qiongshao and Guerrilla Officer Ming Hao, whom I had sent to defend the Zhengkong River, rashly crossed the river, met the rebels, and were reported lost in battle."
entries.literal: Only Regiment Commander He Qiongshao and Guerrilla Officer Ming Hao, sent to defend at Zhengkong River, rashly crossed the river, encountered the rebels, and were reported lost."

entries.zh: 尋奏瓊詔等未死，請治貪功輕進之罪，上以「瓊詔、明浩等遇賊敗逃，又復妄言敗沒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he memorialized that Qiongshao and the others were not dead and asked that they be punished for greed for merit and rash advance. The Emperor said, "Qiongshao, Ming Hao, and the others met the rebels and fled in defeat, yet falsely reported themselves lost in battle.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized that Qiongshao and others were not dead and requested punishment for greed for merit and rash advance; the Emperor said: "Qiongshao, Ming Hao, and others met the rebels, fled in defeat, yet falsely reported themselves lost.

entries.zh: 此法所難宥，藻反稱冒昧貪功輕進，何憒憒乃爾」？
entries.en: This is unpardonable by law, yet Zao instead calls it rashness and greed for merit. How muddled can he be"?
entries.literal: This is unpardonable by law, yet Zao instead calls it rashness and greed for merit—how muddled can he be"?

entries.zh: 詔言：「藻本書生，軍行機宜，非其所習，朕不責以所不能。
entries.en: An edict stated: "Zao was originally a scholar; the conduct of military affairs is not what he has practiced, and We do not blame him for what he cannot do.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Zao was originally a scholar; military affairs are not what he is practiced in, and We do not blame him for what he cannot do.

entries.zh: 至調度賞罰，並可力為籌辦，乃舛謬若此，豈堪复勝總督之任？」
entries.en: Yet in dispatching troops and in rewards and punishments he could have exerted himself fully—instead he has been so wrong-headed. How can he again be fit to hold the post of governor-general?"
entries.literal: Yet in dispatch, rewards, and punishments he could have exerted himself fully—instead he is so wrong-headed; how can he again be fit to hold the post of governor-general?"

entries.zh: 因左授湖北巡撫，命楊應琚往代。
entries.en: He was therefore demoted to Governor of Hubei, and Yang Yingju was ordered to replace him.
entries.literal: He was therefore demoted on the left to Governor of Hubei, and Yang Yingju was ordered to replace him.

entries.zh: 复諭：「應琚未至，藻當實力經理。
entries.en: Another edict instructed: "Before Yingju arrives, Zao must manage affairs in earnest.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "Before Yingju arrives, Zao must manage affairs in earnest.

entries.zh: 若自以為五日京兆，致誤事機，必重治其罪！」
entries.en: If he treats himself as a short-term official with no stake in the outcome and thereby causes military affairs to miscarry, he will surely be severely punished!"
entries.literal: If he thinks himself a five-day capital official and causes military affairs to miscarry, he will surely be severely punished!"

entries.zh: 部議奪職，留雲南效力。
entries.en: The Board recommended stripping him of office, but he was retained in Yunnan to serve.
entries.literal: The Board recommended stripping his office; he was retained in Yunnan to serve.

entries.zh: 藻聞上怒，惶迫自殺，巡撫常鈞疏報。
entries.en: When Zao heard of the Emperor's anger, he killed himself in panic; Governor Chang Jun memorialized to report it.
entries.literal: Hearing the Emperor's anger, Zao in panic killed himself; Governor Chang Jun memorialized to report it.

entries.zh: 上令應琚至普洱，為求醫治療，傷平，傳旨逮問。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Yingju to go to Pu'er to seek medical treatment for him; when his wounds healed, an edict was sent to arrest and interrogate him.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Yingju to go to Pu'er to seek medical treatment; when his wounds healed, an edict was sent to arrest and interrogate him.

entries.zh: 常鈞旋奏藻死，上复詔責其張皇畏葸，旅襯歸葬，不得聽其家立碑書歷官事實。
entries.en: Chang Jun soon memorialized that Zao was dead. The Emperor again issued an edict reproaching his alarm and timidity, ordered his coffin sent home for burial, and forbade his family to erect a stele recording his official career.
entries.literal: Chang Jun soon memorialized that Zao was dead; the Emperor again issued an edict reproaching his alarm and timidity; his coffin was sent home for burial, and his family was not allowed to erect a stele recording his official career.

entries.zh: 三十一年，緬甸大入邊，滇事棘。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year Burma invaded the border on a large scale, and affairs in Yunnan became critical.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year, Burma invaded the border on a large scale and Yunnan affairs became critical.

entries.zh: 緬酋莽達拉自為木梳長所篡，擊敗貴家木邦，貴酋宮裹雁奔孟連。
entries.en: The Burmese chief Mang Dala had been usurped by the Musuo chief; he defeated the Gui Family of Mohang, and the Gui chief Gong Guyan fled to Menglian.
entries.literal: The Burmese chief Mang Dala had been usurped by the Musuo chief; he defeated the Gui Family Mohang; the Gui chief Gong Guyan fled to Menglian.

entries.zh: 時應琚子重穀為永昌知府，誘殺之，木酋亦走。
entries.en: At that time Yingju's son Chonggu was prefect of Yongchang; he lured Gong Guyan and killed him, and the Mohang chief also fled.
entries.literal: At that time Yingju's son Chonggu was prefect of Yongchang; he lured and killed him, and the Mohang chief also fled.

entries.zh: 緬益橫，入犯思茅。
entries.en: Burma grew more overbearing and invaded Simao.
entries.literal: Burma grew more overbearing and invaded Simao.

entries.zh: 上移應珺雲貴總督視師。
entries.en: The Emperor transferred Yang Yingju to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou to take command of the army.
entries.literal: The Emperor transferred Yang Yingju to Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou to take command.

entries.zh: 應琚至楚雄，緬人漸退，師乘間收復。
entries.en: When Yingju reached Chuxiong, the Burmese gradually withdrew, and the army seized the opportunity to recover lost ground.
entries.literal: When Yingju reached Chuxiong, the Burmese gradually retreated, and the army seized the opportunity to recover territory.

entries.zh: 應琚往孟良、整賣正經界，集流亡，釐戶口，定賦稅，而令召丙、叭先俸分據之，請賞給三品指揮使。
entries.en: Yingju went to Mengliang and Zhenmai to rectify the border, gathered refugees, sorted household registers, fixed tax levies, and had Zhao Bing and Baxianfeng hold portions of the territory, requesting that they be granted the rank of third-grade battalion commander.
entries.literal: Yingju went to Mengliang and Zhenmai to rectify the border, gathered refugees, sorted household registers, fixed tax levies, and had Zhao Bing and Baxianfeng hold portions, requesting grants of third-rank battalion commanders.

entries.zh: 上以為能，賜珍物，官其孫茂齡藍翎侍衛。
entries.en: The Emperor considered him capable, bestowed precious objects, and appointed his grandson Maoling a Blue Plume Imperial Bodyguard.
entries.literal: The Emperor considered him capable, bestowed treasures, and appointed his grandson Maoling a Blue Plume Imperial Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 又使人誘致孟密、孟養、蠻暮令獻地，實則地懸緬境，內附特空言。
entries.en: He also sent men to induce Mengmi, Mengyang, and Manmu to offer territory, but in fact the land lay within Burma's borders, and their submission was merely empty talk.
entries.literal: He also sent men to induce Mengmi, Mengyang, and Manmu to offer territory—but in fact the land lay within Burma's borders, and submission was merely empty talk.

entries.zh: 諸將希應琚指，爭謂緬勢孤，易攻取。
entries.en: The generals, hoping to please Yingju, all contended that Burma was isolated and easy to attack.
entries.literal: The generals, hoping to please Yingju, all contended that Burma was isolated and easy to attack.

entries.zh: 應琚初猶弗聽，曰：「吾官至一品，年逾七十，復何所求，而以貪功開邊釁乎？」
entries.en: At first Yingju would not listen, saying, "My rank has reached the first grade and I am over seventy—what more do I seek, that I should open border war through greed for merit?"
entries.literal: At first Yingju would not listen, saying: "My rank has reached the first grade, I am over seventy—what more do I seek, that I should open border war through greed for merit?"

entries.zh: 副將趙宏榜慫恿之，遂下道、鎮、府、州合議，亦謂寇勢大，邊釁不可開，總兵烏爾登額阻尤力，應琚滋不懌。
entries.en: Brigadier Zhao Hongbang urged him on; he then convened a joint consultation of circuits, commands, prefectures, and departments. They too said the enemy force was large and border war must not be opened; Regional Commander Wu Erden'e opposed most strongly, and Yingju grew increasingly displeased.
entries.literal: Brigadier Zhao Hongbang urged him on; he then convened a joint consultation of circuits, commands, prefectures, and departments—they too said the enemy force was large and border war must not be opened; Regional Commander Wu Erden'e opposed most strongly, and Yingju grew increasingly displeased.

entries.zh: 重英初至雲南，隱以監軍自居，嗣為鄂寧所劾，命以知府從軍。
entries.en: When Chongying first came to Yunnan, he quietly acted as military overseer; later impeached by E'ning, he was ordered to follow the army in the capacity of prefect.
entries.literal: Chongying had first come to Yunnan, quietly acting as military overseer; later impeached by E'ning, he was ordered to follow the army as prefect.

entries.zh: 明年，軍士患飢，緬嗛詐媾和，參贊珠魯訥遣重英往報，被執。
entries.en: The next year the soldiers suffered famine; Burma used the famine to feign negotiating peace; Coordinator Zhulun'e sent Chongying to report back and he was captured.
entries.literal: The next year the soldiers suffered famine; Burma used famine to feign negotiating peace; Coordinator Zhulun'e sent Chongying to report back and he was captured.

entries.zh: 上以重英且降緬，下其子長齡獄。
entries.en: The Emperor thought Chongying was about to surrender to Burma and imprisoned his son Changling.
entries.literal: The Emperor thought Chongying was about to surrender to Burma and imprisoned his son Changling.

entries.zh: 已，緬歸俘卒，賚貝葉書，附重英書乞罷兵，拒弗納。
entries.en: Later Burma returned captive soldiers and sent a palm-leaf letter with Chongying's letter begging that troops be withdrawn; this was refused.
entries.literal: Later Burma returned captive soldiers, sent a palm-leaf letter with Chongying's letter begging to cease troops; this was refused.

entries.zh: 四十一年，緬出都司蘇爾相議和，仍弗許。
entries.en: In the forty-first year Burma sent Metropolitan Commander Su Erxiang to negotiate peace; this was still not permitted.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year Burma sent Metropolitan Commander Su Erxiang to negotiate peace; this was still not permitted.

entries.zh: 五十三年，緬聞暹羅受封，乃款關求貢，並還重英。
entries.en: In the fifty-third year, hearing that Siam had received investiture, Burma opened the border pass to seek tribute and also returned Chongying.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year, Burma heard that Siam had received investiture, and then opened the border pass to seek tribute, also returning Chongying.

entries.zh: 重英陷緬後，獨居佛寺逾二十年，未改中國衣冠。
entries.en: After Chongying fell into Burmese hands, he lived alone in a Buddhist temple for more than twenty years without changing his Chinese dress.
entries.literal: After Chongying fell into Burmese hands, he lived alone in a Buddhist temple for more than twenty years without changing his Chinese dress.

entries.zh: 上大悅，進道員，釋長齡出獄，比以蘇武之節，御製蘇楊論旌之。
entries.en: The Emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to circuit intendant, released Changling from prison, compared him to the integrity of Su Wu, and composed the Discourse on Su and Yang to honor him.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to circuit intendant, released Changling from prison, compared him to Su Wu's integrity, and composed the Discourse on Su and Yang to honor him.

entries.zh: 俄，病卒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he died of illness.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.

entries.zh: 二十四年，移陝甘總督。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Governor-General of Shaanxi-Gansu.

entries.zh: 疏言伊犁底定，宜先屯田，留兵五千墾特諾果爾、長吉、羅克倫。
entries.en: He memorialized that with Yili pacified, colonization should come first, and that five thousand troops should remain to open fields at Tenoguo'er, Changji, and Luokelun.
entries.literal: He memorialized that with Yili pacified, colonization should come first; five thousand troops should remain to cultivate Tenoguo'er, Changji, and Luokelun.

entries.zh: 復以陝、甘非一督能治，請更西安總督為川陝總督，四川總督為巡撫，甘肅巡撫為總督，上遂命應琚督甘肅，陝西提鎮受節制，進太子太師。
entries.en: He further argued that Shaanxi and Gansu were beyond the capacity of a single governor-general to govern, and requested that the Xi'an governor-general be renamed Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, the Sichuan governor-general be reduced to provincial governor, and the Gansu governor be promoted to governor-general. The Emperor then ordered Yingju to govern Gansu with Shaanxi's commanders and brigades under his command, and promoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He further held that Shaanxi and Gansu were beyond one governor-general's capacity, and requested changing the Xi'an governor-general to Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, the Sichuan governor-general to provincial governor, and the Gansu governor to governor-general; the Emperor then ordered Yingju to govern Gansu with Shaanxi's commanders and brigades under his command, promoting him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 嘗募巴爾楚克回戶治多蘭溝渠，墾喀喇沙爾以西各台，又增置兵備道、總兵，分駐阿克蘇、葉爾羌二城，逐為重鎮。
entries.en: He once recruited Balchuk Muslim households to work the Duolan canal, opened farming terraces west of Karashahr, and added military preparedness circuits and regional commanders stationed at Aksu and Yarkand, thereby turning them into key garrisons.
entries.literal: He once recruited Balchuk Muslim households to work the Duolan canal, opened terraces west of Karashahr, and added military preparedness circuits and regional commanders stationed at Aksu and Yarkand—thereby forming key garrisons.

entries.zh: 應琚奏辦屯墾，遣兵購畜，部署紛煩；
entries.en: Yingju had memorialized on organizing colonization, dispatching troops to purchase livestock, and making arrangements that were numerous and vexatious;
entries.literal: Yingju memorialized on organizing colonization, dispatching troops to purchase livestock—arrangements were numerous and vexatious;

entries.zh: 至是，疏自言其非，請因利乘便規久遠。
entries.en: at this point he memorialized acknowledging his errors and asked to take advantage of circumstances and plan for the long term.
entries.literal: at this point he memorialized acknowledging his errors, asking to take advantage of circumstances and plan for the long term.

entries.zh: 帝嘉納，下其疏示中外。
entries.en: The Emperor praised and accepted the memorial, and circulated it throughout the court and the provinces.
entries.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted, and circulated his memorial inside and outside the court.

entries.zh: 二十九年，移駐肅州，拜東閣大學士。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year he moved his headquarters to Suzhou and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he moved his headquarters to Suzhou and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

entries.zh: 永昌知府陳大呂懼更初議，應琚乃往永昌受降，並為文檄緬，侈言水陸軍五十萬陳境上，不降即進討。
entries.en: Yongchang Prefect Chen Dalv feared a reversal of the earlier plan; Yingju therefore went to Yongchang to accept surrender and also drafted a proclamation to Burma exaggerating that five hundred thousand land and water troops were arrayed on the border—if they did not submit, he would advance to chastise them.
entries.literal: Yongchang Prefect Chen Dalv feared a reversal of the earlier plan; Yingju therefore went to Yongchang to accept surrender, and also drafted a proclamation to Burma exaggerating that five hundred thousand land and water troops were arrayed on the border—if they did not submit he would advance to chastise them.

entries.zh: 緬遂大發兵溯金沙江而上。
entries.en: Burma then sent a large army up the Jinsha River.
entries.literal: Burma then sent a large army up the Jinsha River.

entries.zh: 其時宏榜頓新街，卻走。
entries.en: At that time Hongbang was stationed at Xinjie and retreated.
entries.literal: At that time Hongbang was stationed at Xinjie and retreated.

entries.zh: 應琚聞警即遘疾，上命楊廷璋往代，遣侍衛福靈安攜御醫往診；
entries.en: When Yingju heard the alarm he immediately fell ill; the Emperor ordered Yang Tingzhang to replace him and sent Bodyguard Fuling'an with imperial physicians to examine him;
entries.literal: When Yingju heard the alarm he immediately fell ill; the Emperor ordered Yang Tingzhang to replace him and sent Bodyguard Fuling'an with imperial physicians to examine him;

entries.zh: 並諭其子江蘇按察使重英、寶慶知府重穀省視。
entries.en: he also instructed his sons, Jiangsu Surveillance Commissioner Chongying and Baqing Prefect Chonggu, to visit and look after him.
entries.literal: he also instructed his sons, Jiangsu Surveillance Commissioner Chongying and Baqing Prefect Chonggu, to visit and look after him.

entries.zh: 比廷璋至而疾已愈，乃令諸軍進擊，總兵硃崙出鐵壁關，攻楞木，不克，寇勢益張。
entries.en: By the time Tingzhang arrived the illness had already passed; he then ordered the armies to advance. Regional Commander Zhu Lun went out through Tiewu Pass to attack Lengmu without success, and the rebels grew bolder.
entries.literal: By the time Tingzhang arrived the illness had already recovered; he then ordered the armies to advance; Regional Commander Zhu Lun went out through Tiewu Pass to attack Lengmu without success, and the rebels grew bolder.

entries.zh: 提督李時升告急，應琚不報。
entries.en: Regional Commander-in-Chief Li Shisheng reported urgency, but Yingju did not respond.
entries.literal: Regional Commander-in-Chief Li Shisheng reported urgency; Yingju did not answer.

entries.zh: 緬陽議款，遂以楞木大捷入告，而緬已漸入戶臘撒。
entries.en: Burma feigned willingness to negotiate peace; he therefore reported a great victory at Lengmu, while Burma had already gradually penetrated Huluosa.
entries.literal: Burma feigned talks of peace; he therefore reported a great victory at Lengmu, while Burma had already gradually entered Huluosa.

entries.zh: 時總兵劉德成擁兵幹崖，飲酒高會，時升屢趣罔應。
entries.en: At that time Regional Commander Liu Decheng held troops at Ganya, drinking and feasting at leisure; Shisheng repeatedly urged him but received no response.
entries.literal: At that time Regional Commander Liu Decheng held troops at Ganya, drinking and feasting; Shisheng repeatedly urged him but got no response.

entries.zh: 應琚遣緬寧通判富森持令箭督戰，德成始抵盞達。
entries.en: Yingju dispatched Dianning Subprefect Fu Sen with a command arrow to supervise the battle; only then did Decheng reach Zhanda.
entries.literal: Yingju dispatched Dianning Subprefect Fu Sen with a command arrow to supervise the battle; Decheng only then reached Zhanda.

entries.zh: 緬懼擊其後，潛引去，應琚仍以捷聞。
entries.en: Burma feared an attack from the rear and quietly withdrew; Yingju still reported victory.
entries.literal: Burma feared attack from the rear and quietly withdrew; Yingju still reported victory.

entries.zh: 緬甸復入猛卯，參將哈國興等引還，砲械多遺失，應琚又報捷；
entries.en: Burma again entered Mengmao; Regiment Commander Ha Guoxing and others led the troops back, and much artillery was lost; Yingju again reported victory;
entries.literal: Burma again entered Mengmao; Regiment Commander Ha Guoxing and others led troops back; much artillery was lost; Yingju again reported victory;

entries.zh: 並傳令硃崙兼剿撫，陰示以和蕆事，緬果累乞和。
entries.en: and transmitted orders for Zhu Lun to combine suppression and appeasement, secretly indicating that peace was to be concluded; Burma indeed repeatedly begged for peace.
entries.literal: and transmitted orders for Zhu Lun to combine suppression and appeasement, secretly indicating that peace affairs were to be concluded—Burma indeed repeatedly begged for peace.

entries.zh: 逾歲，奏言：「緬甸酋弟卜坑率聶渺遮乞款附，懇予蠻暮、新街互市。」
entries.en: After a year he memorialized: "Burma's chief's younger brother Bokeng led Ni Miaozhe to beg to submit, earnestly requesting permission to trade at Manmu and Xinjie."
entries.literal: After a year he memorialized: "Burma's chief's younger brother Bokeng led Ni Miaozhe to beg to submit, earnestly requesting trade at Manmu and Xinjie."

entries.zh: 上察其偽，數訶責。
entries.en: The Emperor perceived the deceit and reprimanded him repeatedly.
entries.literal: The Emperor perceived the deceit and reprimanded him repeatedly.

entries.zh: 嗣木邦告警，國興軍抵蠻暮，寇★K4退，應琚又以復新街奏。
entries.en: Then Mohang sounded the alarm; Guoxing's army reached Manmu and the bandits retreated; Yingju again memorialized that Xinjie had been recovered.
entries.literal: Then Mohang sounded the alarm; Guoxing's army reached Manmu and the bandits retreated; Yingju again memorialized recovering Xinjie.

entries.zh: 上視所進地圖，疑寇既屢敗，何以尚據內地土司境，降旨駁詰。
entries.en: The Emperor examined the map submitted and wondered how, if the rebels had suffered repeated defeats, they could still hold territory within the domains of interior native offices; he issued an edict to refute and question the report.
entries.literal: The Emperor examined the map submitted and doubted how, if the rebels had suffered repeated defeats, they still held territory within interior native offices; he issued an edict to refute and question.

entries.zh: 會福靈安先被命廉軍事，具言宏榜諸人失守狀，應琚亦劾德成等遲留不進，於是俱逮問，而以楊寧為提督，且以應琚不勝任，召明瑞代統其軍。
entries.en: At the time Fuling'an had already been ordered to investigate military affairs in detail; he reported how Hongbang and others had lost their posts. Yingju also impeached Decheng and others for delay in advancing; they were all arrested and brought up for interrogation. Yang Ning was made Regional Commander-in-Chief, and because Yingju was unfit for his post, Ming Rui was summoned to take command of the army.
entries.literal: At the time Fuling'an had already been ordered to investigate military affairs in detail; he stated how Hongbang and others had lost their posts; Yingju also impeached Decheng and others for delay—they were all arrested; Yang Ning was made Regional Commander-in-Chief; and because Yingju was unfit, Ming Rui was summoned to take command.

entries.zh: 明瑞至，首發其欺罔罪，謂誤木緬別為一事尤妄誕，鄂寧亦糾其掩敗為勝。
entries.en: When Ming Rui arrived he first exposed his deceit, saying that treating Musuo and Burma as separate matters was especially absurd; E'ning also impeached him for masking defeat as victory.
entries.literal: When Ming Rui arrived he first exposed his deceit, saying that treating Musuo and Burma as separate matters was especially absurd; E'ning also impeached him for masking defeat as victory.

entries.zh: 應琚恐，乃上言大舉徵緬，調湖廣、川、滇軍五萬，五路並進，請敕暹羅夾攻，朝論皆斥之。
entries.en: Yingju in fear then memorialized proposing a great campaign against Burma, mobilizing fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Sichuan, and Yunnan to advance in five columns, and requesting orders to Siam for a pincer attack—all were denounced at court.
entries.literal: Yingju in fear then memorialized proposing a great campaign against Burma, mobilizing fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Sichuan, and Yunnan in five columns advancing together, and requesting orders to Siam for a pincer attack—all were denounced at court.

entries.zh: 未幾，詔逮問，賜死。
entries.en: Before long an edict ordered his arrest and interrogation; he was granted death.
entries.literal: Before long an edict ordered his arrest; he was granted death.

entries.zh: 重穀亦坐笞殺人，棄市。
entries.en: Chonggu was also punished for beating a man to death and was executed in the market.
entries.literal: Chonggu was also punished for beating a man to death and executed in the market.

entries.zh: 蘇爾相，甘肅靈州人。
entries.en: Su Erxiang was a native of Lingzhou in Gansu.
entries.literal: Su Erxiang was a native of Lingzhou, Gansu.

entries.zh: 自行伍從征緬甸、金川有勞，累遷雲南奇兵營都司。
entries.en: Rising from the ranks, he took part in campaigns against Burma and Jinchuan with distinction and was repeatedly promoted to Metropolitan Commander of the Yunnan Irregular Forces Battalion.
entries.literal: From the ranks he followed campaigns against Burma and Jinchuan with merit, and was repeatedly promoted to Metropolitan Commander of the Yunnan Irregular Forces Battalion.

entries.zh: 三十五年，雲貴總督彰寶以緬甸表貢久不至，遣爾相齎檄往諭，被留，迫使上書阿桂申表貢之議。
entries.en: In the thirty-fifth year, because Burma's tribute memorial had long failed to arrive, Governor-General Zhang Bao of Yunnan and Guizhou sent Erxiang bearing a proclamation to instruct them; he was detained and forced to write to Agui proposing the restoration of tribute.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Governor-General Zhang Bao of Yunnan-Guizhou, because Burma's tribute memorial had long failed to arrive, sent Erxiang bearing a proclamation to instruct them; he was detained and forced to write to Agui proposing tribute.

entries.zh: 上謂爾相且降緬，命甘肅疆吏執爾相妻孥致京師，子一、女二死於獄，妻死於道。
entries.en: The Emperor thought Erxiang was about to surrender to Burma and ordered the border officials of Gansu to seize his wife and children and bring them to the capital; one son and two daughters died in prison, and his wife died on the road.
entries.literal: The Emperor thought Erxiang was about to surrender to Burma and ordered Gansu border officials to seize his wife and children and bring them to the capital; one son and two daughters died in prison, and his wife died on the road.

entries.zh: 四十一年，緬始送爾相還。
entries.en: In the forty-first year Burma at last sent Erxiang back.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year Burma at last sent Erxiang back.

entries.zh: 上命阿桂傳諭，令其詣京師，引見，授游擊，賜詩亦比以蘇武。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Agui to instruct him to come to the capital, granted him an audience, appointed him guerrilla officer, and in bestowing a poem also compared him to Su Wu.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Agui to transmit instructions for him to go to the capital, granted him an audience, appointed him guerrilla officer, and in bestowing a poem also compared him to Su Wu.

entries.zh: 累遷騰越鎮總兵，兼署雲南提督。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to Regional Commander of Tengyue Garrison and concurrently served as acting Regional Commander-in-Chief of Yunnan.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Tengyue Garrison and concurrently acted as Regional Commander-in-Chief of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 三十年二月，烏什回為亂，駐烏什副都統素誠自戕，亂回推小伯克賴黑木圖拉為渠，拒守。
entries.en: In the second month of the thirtieth year the Muslims of Ush rebelled; the Vice Commander-in-Chief stationed there, Sucheng, killed himself; the rebels made the petty beg Lai Heimutula their leader and held out behind the walls.
entries.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year the Muslims of Ush rebelled; the Vice Commander-in-Chief stationed at Ush, Sucheng, killed himself; the rebels made the petty beg Lai Heimutula their leader and held out in defense.

entries.zh: 明瑞遣副都統觀音保往討，而帥師繼其後。
entries.en: Ming Rui sent Vice Commander-in-Chief Guanyinbao to attack, while he himself led the main army in support.
entries.literal: Ming Rui sent Vice Commander-in-Chief Guanyinbao to attack, while he himself led the army after him.

entries.zh: 烏什回二千餘出禦，明瑞與觀音保力戰破之，奪砲台七。
entries.en: More than two thousand Ush Muslims came out to resist; Ming Rui and Guanyinbao fought fiercely and routed them, capturing seven batteries.
entries.literal: More than two thousand Ush Muslims came out to resist; Ming Rui and Guanyinbao fought fiercely and defeated them, capturing seven batteries.

entries.zh: 賊入城，師合圍。
entries.en: The rebels withdrew into the city, and the army closed in around them.
entries.literal: The rebels entered the city; the army surrounded them.

entries.zh: 明瑞疏陳素誠狂縱激變，及參贊納世通虐回民，阻援師，副都統弁塔哈掩敗妄奏諸狀，上令尚書阿桂至軍，按誅納世通、弁塔哈。
entries.en: Ming Rui memorialized that Such eng's arrogance and license had provoked the uprising, that Coordinator Nashitong had abused the Muslims and blocked relief troops, and that Vice Commander-in-Chief Biantaha had concealed defeats and filed false reports; the Emperor ordered Minister Agui to the army to investigate and execute Nashitong and Biantaha.
entries.literal: Ming Rui memorialized stating Such eng's arrogance and license had provoked the uprising, and that Coordinator Nashitong had abused the Muslims, blocked relief troops, and Vice Commander-in-Chief Biantaha had concealed defeats and falsely reported—all these matters; the Emperor ordered Minister Agui to the army to investigate and execute Nashitong and Biantaha.

entries.zh: 賊夜襲我軍，我軍诇知之，預為備，射賴黑木圖拉殪，賊擁其父額色木圖拉為渠。
entries.en: The rebels attacked the army by night; scouts detected them and preparations were made in advance; Lai Heimutula was shot dead, and the rebels made his father Eseimutula their leader.
entries.literal: The rebels attacked our army by night; our army learned of it through scouts and made preparations beforehand, shooting Lai Heimutula dead; the rebels made his father Eseimutula their leader.

entries.zh: 明瑞以兵六百餘夜攜雲梯薄其城，不克，則毀其堞，且斷汲道。
entries.en: Ming Rui led more than six hundred men with scaling ladders in a night approach to the wall; when he failed to take the city, he destroyed the parapets and cut off the water supply.
entries.literal: Ming Rui with more than six hundred men carried scaling ladders by night to approach the city wall; failing to take it, he destroyed the parapets and cut off the water supply route.

entries.zh: 賊待阿富汗援不至，乃縛獻額色木圖拉等四十二人降，明瑞悉斬之，其脅從及婦稚萬餘送伊犁。
entries.en: When Afghan aid failed to arrive, the rebels bound and presented Eseimutula and forty-one others in surrender; Ming Rui executed them all and sent more than ten thousand coerced followers, women, and children to Yili.
entries.literal: The rebels, waiting for Afghan aid that did not arrive, then bound and presented Eseimutula and forty-one others in surrender; Ming Rui executed them all, and sent more than ten thousand coerced followers, women, and children to Yili.

entries.zh: 烏什平。
entries.en: Ush was pacified.
entries.literal: Ush was pacified.

entries.zh: 上以明瑞得渠魁，未詳鞫為亂狀，亂回至圍急始縛獻首惡，不可輕宥，所措置皆不當，與阿桂同下部議，奪職，命留任。
entries.en: The Emperor held that although Ming Rui had obtained the ringleader, he had not thoroughly investigated the facts of the rebellion; the rebel Muslims had only bound and presented the chief culprit when the siege grew desperate and could not be lightly pardoned; all his dispositions were improper. He and Agui were both referred to the Board, stripped of office, and ordered to remain at their posts.
entries.literal: The Emperor held that although Ming Rui had obtained the ringleader, he had not thoroughly tried the facts of the rebellion; the rebel Muslims had only bound and presented the chief culprit when the siege grew desperate—they could not be lightly pardoned; all his dispositions were improper; he and Agui were both referred to the Board, stripped of office, and ordered to remain at their posts.

entries.zh: 旋條上善後事，如所請。
entries.en: Soon afterward he submitted a detailed plan for post-pacification measures, and it was approved as requested.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a detailed plan for post-pacification measures, and it was approved as requested.

entries.zh: 是時緬甸為亂犯邊，總督劉藻戰屢敗，自殺。
entries.en: At that time Burma was in rebellion and invading the border; Governor Liu Zao was repeatedly defeated in battle and killed himself.
entries.literal: At that time Burma was in rebellion and invading the border; Governor Liu Zao was repeatedly defeated in battle and killed himself.

entries.zh: 大學士楊應琚代為總督，師久無功，賜死。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Yang Yingju replaced him as governor; the army achieved nothing for a long time, and he was granted death.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yingju replaced him as governor; the army was long without success, and he was granted death.

entries.zh: 三十二年二月，命明瑞以雲貴總督兼兵部尚書，經略軍務。
entries.en: In the second month of the thirty-second year Ming Rui was ordered to serve as Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently Minister of War, with overall direction of military affairs.
entries.literal: In the second month of the thirty-second year Ming Rui was ordered to serve as Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou and concurrently Minister of War, directing military affairs.

entries.zh: 明瑞議大軍出永昌、騰越攻宛頂、木邦為正兵，遣參贊額爾登額出北路，自猛密攻老官屯，會於阿瓦。
entries.en: Ming Rui proposed that the main army advance from Yongchang and Tengyue against Wanding and Mohang as the principal force, while Coordinator E'erdeng'e would take the northern route from Mengmi against Laoguantun, the two columns to meet at Ava.
entries.literal: Ming Rui proposed that the main army advance from Yongchang and Tengyue to attack Wanding and Mohang as the principal force, while Coordinator E'erdeng'e would go by the northern route from Mengmi to attack Laoguantun, meeting at Ava.

entries.zh: 十一月，至宛頂，進攻木邦，賊遁，留參贊珠魯訥、按察使楊重英守之，率兵萬餘渡錫箔江攻蠻結。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he reached Wanding and advanced against Mohang; the rebels fled. He left Coordinator Zhulun'e and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Chongying to hold the place, then led more than ten thousand men across the Xibo River to attack Manjie.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he reached Wanding and advanced to attack Mohang; the rebels fled; he left Coordinator Zhulun'e and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Zhongying to guard it, and led more than ten thousand men across the Xibo River to attack Manjie.

entries.zh: 寇二萬，立十六寨，寨外浚溝，溝外又環以木柵，列象陣為伏兵。
entries.en: The enemy numbered twenty thousand. They established sixteen stockades, dug trenches outside them, ringed the trenches with wooden palisades, and arrayed elephant formations as ambush troops.
entries.literal: The enemy numbered twenty thousand, established sixteen stockades, dug trenches outside the stockades, and ringed the trenches with wooden palisades, arraying elephant formations as ambush troops.

entries.zh: 明瑞統兵居中，領隊大臣扎拉豐阿、李全據東山梁，觀音保、長青據西山梁。
entries.en: Ming Rui commanded the center; Leading Commanders Zhala Feng'a and Li Quan held the eastern hill ridge, while Guanyinbao and Chang Qing held the western hill ridge.
entries.literal: Ming Rui commanded the center; leading commanders Zhala Feng'a and Li Quan held the eastern hill ridge; Guanyinbao and Chang Qing held the western hill ridge.

entries.zh: 賊突陣西出，觀音保、長青力戰，明瑞督中軍進，殺賊二百餘，賊退保柵。
entries.en: The rebels burst out of the formation on the west; Guanyinbao and Chang Qing fought fiercely while Ming Rui directed the central army forward, killing more than two hundred rebels before the enemy withdrew behind the palisades.
entries.literal: The rebels burst out of the formation on the west; Guanyinbao and Chang Qing fought fiercely; Ming Rui directed the central army forward, killing more than two hundred rebels; the rebels withdrew to hold the palisades.

entries.zh: 明瑞令分兵為十二隊，身先陷陣，目傷，猶指揮不少挫。
entries.en: Ming Rui divided the army into twelve companies and himself led the charge into the enemy lines; though wounded in the eye, he continued to command without faltering.
entries.literal: Ming Rui ordered the army divided into twelve companies, himself leading the charge into the formation; though wounded in the eye, he continued to command without faltering.

entries.zh: 賊陣中群象反奔，我兵毀柵進，無不一當百。
entries.en: Within the rebel formation the elephants in a body turned and fled; our troops destroyed the palisades and advanced, each man fighting as if he were a hundred.
entries.literal: In the rebel formation the elephants in a body turned and fled; our troops destroyed the palisades and advanced, each fighting as if a hundred.

entries.zh: 有貴州兵王連者，舞藤牌躍入陣，眾從之，縱橫擊殺，馘二十餘，俘三十有四，賊遁走。
entries.en: A Guizhou soldier named Wang Lian, brandishing a rattan shield, leaped into the enemy formation; the troops followed him, striking and killing at will. They took more than twenty heads and thirty-four prisoners, and the rebels fled.
entries.literal: A Guizhou soldier named Wang Lian, brandishing a rattan shield, leaped into the formation; the troops followed him, striking and killing at will; they took more than twenty heads and thirty-four prisoners; the rebels fled.

entries.zh: 捷聞，上大悅，封一等誠嘉毅勇公，賜黃帶、寶石頂、四團龍補服，原襲承恩公畀其弟奎林。
entries.en: When news of the victory arrived the Emperor was greatly pleased. He enfeoffed Ming Rui as Duke of the First Rank, Sincere and Commendable, Resolute and Brave, granted him a yellow belt, jeweled finial, and surcoat with four-dragon roundels, and transferred the original inheritance of Duke of Enfeoffment to his younger brother Kuilin.
entries.literal: When news of the victory arrived the Emperor was greatly pleased, enfeoffed him as Duke of the First Rank, Sincere and Commendable, Resolute and Brave, granted a yellow belt, jeweled finial, and four-dragon roundels on his surcoat, and transferred the original inheritance of Duke of Enfeoffment to his younger brother Kuilin.

entries.zh: 扎拉豐阿、觀音保勸明瑞乘勝罷兵，明瑞不可。
entries.en: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao urged Ming Rui to halt the campaign while victory was at hand; Ming Rui would not agree.
entries.literal: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao urged Ming Rui to cease fighting while victory was at hand; Ming Rui would not agree.

entries.zh: 師復進，十二月，次革龍，地逼天生橋渡口，賊踞山巔立柵。
entries.en: The army advanced again. In the twelfth month it halted at Gelong, where the terrain pressed upon the Tiansheng Bridge crossing; the rebels held the mountain summit and erected palisades.
entries.literal: The army advanced again; in the twelfth month it halted at Gelong, where the terrain pressed upon the Tiansheng Bridge crossing; the rebels held the mountain summit and erected palisades.

entries.zh: 明瑞令別軍出大道，若將奪渡口，而督軍從間道繞至天生橋上游，乘霧徑渡，進據山梁。
entries.en: Ming Rui sent a separate force out on the main road as if to seize the crossing, while he himself led the army by a hidden path around to the upper reaches of Tiansheng Bridge, crossed directly through the fog, and seized the hill ridge.
entries.literal: Ming Rui ordered a separate force out on the main road as if to seize the crossing, while he himself directed the army by a hidden path around to the upper reaches of Tiansheng Bridge, crossed directly through the fog, and advanced to seize the hill ridge.

entries.zh: 賊驚潰，浮馘二千餘。
entries.en: The rebels fled in alarm; more than two thousand enemy dead were counted.
entries.literal: The rebels fled in alarm; more than two thousand heads were counted floating on the water.

entries.zh: 復進至象孔，糧垂罄，欲退，慮額爾登額師已入，聞猛籠土司糧富，且地近猛密，冀通北路軍消息，乃移軍猛籠。
entries.en: Advancing again to Xiangkong, grain was nearly exhausted and he wished to withdraw, but feared E'erdeng'e's column had already entered. Hearing that the Menglong native chieftain had abundant grain and that the place lay near Mengmi, where he hoped to establish contact with the northern-route army, he moved his forces to Menglong.
entries.literal: Advancing again to Xiangkong, grain was nearly exhausted and he wished to withdraw, but feared E'erdeng'e's army had already entered; hearing that the Menglong native chieftain had abundant grain, and that the place was near Mengmi, hoping to communicate with the northern-route army, he moved the army to Menglong.

entries.zh: 賊尾我軍後，至章子壩，我軍且戰且行。
entries.en: The rebels followed close behind; at Zhangziba the army fought as it marched.
entries.literal: The rebels followed behind our army; reaching Zhangziba, our army fought as it marched.

entries.zh: 明瑞及觀音保等殿，日行不三十里，至猛籠已歲除，土司避匿，發窖粟二萬餘石。
entries.en: Ming Rui, Guanyinbao, and others brought up the rear; each day they marched no more than thirty li. By the time they reached Menglong it was already New Year's Eve; the native chieftain had hidden away, but they opened stored grain amounting to more than twenty thousand piculs.
entries.literal: Ming Rui and Guanyinbao and others brought up the rear; each day they marched no more than thirty li; reaching Menglong it was already New Year's Eve; the native chieftain had hidden away; they opened stored grain of more than twenty thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 駐三日，復引軍趨猛密，人持數升粟，焚其餘積。
entries.en: After encamping for three days, he again led the army toward Mengmi; each man carried only a few sheng of grain, and the remaining stores were burned.
entries.literal: After encamping three days, he again led the army toward Mengmi; each man carried a few sheng of grain and burned the remaining stores.

entries.zh: 賊躡我軍行，至夕駐營，初相距十餘裡。
entries.en: The rebels tracked the army's march; when the troops encamped at evening the enemy was at first still more than ten li away.
entries.literal: The rebels tracked our army's march; when we encamped at evening they were at first more than ten li distant.

entries.zh: 賊诇我軍飢疲，經蠻化，我軍屯山巔，賊即營山半。
entries.en: The rebels learned that the army was hungry and weary. Passing through Manhua, the army encamped on the mountain summit while the rebels immediately pitched camp halfway up the slope.
entries.literal: The rebels learned that our army was hungry and weary; passing through Manhua, our army encamped on the mountain summit and the rebels immediately encamped halfway up the slope.

entries.zh: 明瑞謂諸將曰：「賊輕我甚，不一死戰，無焦類矣！
entries.en: Ming Rui said to the generals, "The rebels despise us utterly; if we do not fight to the death, none of us will survive!
entries.literal: Ming Rui said to the generals: "The rebels despise us greatly; if we do not fight to the death, none of us will survive!

entries.zh: 賊識我軍號。
entries.en: The rebels know our army's signals.
entries.literal: The rebels know our army's signals.

entries.zh: 明旦我軍傳號，若將起行，則盡出營伏箐待。」
entries.en: At dawn tomorrow, when our army sounds the signals as if about to break camp and march, they will all leave camp and lie in ambush in the ravines to wait."
entries.literal: At dawn tomorrow, when our army sounds the signals as if about to break camp and march, they will all leave camp and lie in ambush in the ravines to wait."

entries.zh: 明旦賊聞聲，蟻附上山。
entries.en: At dawn the rebels heard the signals and swarmed up the mountain like ants.
entries.literal: At dawn the rebels heard the sounds and swarmed up the mountain like ants.

entries.zh: 我軍突出發槍砲，賊反走，乘之，斬四千有奇。
entries.en: The army burst forth and opened fire with muskets and cannon; the rebels turned and fled, and in pursuit more than four thousand were beheaded.
entries.literal: Our army burst forth and opened fire with muskets and cannon; the rebels turned and fled; pursuing them, we beheaded more than four thousand.

entries.zh: 自此每夜遙屯二十里外，明瑞令休兵六日。
entries.en: From this point they encamped each night at a distance of twenty li; Ming Rui ordered the troops to rest for six days.
entries.literal: From this point they encamped each night at a distance of twenty li; Ming Rui ordered the troops to rest for six days.

entries.zh: 賊柵於要道，我軍攻之不能拔，得波霙人引自桂家銀廠舊址出。
entries.en: The rebels had palisaded the vital pass; the army attacked but could not break through until a Bo'ing tribesman guided them out by the old site of the Gui Family silver mine.
entries.literal: The rebels palisaded the vital pass; our army attacked but could not take it; a Bo'ing tribesman guided them out by the old site of the Gui Family silver mine.

entries.zh: 上聞明瑞深入，命全師速出。
entries.en: When the Emperor heard that Ming Rui had penetrated deeply, he ordered the entire army to withdraw quickly.
entries.literal: The Emperor heard that Ming Rui had penetrated deeply and ordered the entire army to withdraw quickly.

entries.zh: 詔未達，三十三年正月，賊攻木邦，副都統珠魯訥師潰自戕，執重英以去。
entries.en: Before the edict arrived, in the first month of the thirty-third year the rebels attacked Mohang; Vice Commander-in-Chief Zhulun'e's army collapsed and he killed himself, and Yang Chongying was seized and taken away.
entries.literal: Before the edict arrived, in the first month of the thirty-third year the rebels attacked Mohang; Vice Commander-in-Chief Zhulun'e's army collapsed and he killed himself; Yang Zhongying was seized and taken away.

entries.zh: 額爾登額出猛密，阻於老官屯，月餘引還。
entries.en: E'erdeng'e advanced from Mengmi but was blocked at Laoguantun; after more than a month he withdrew.
entries.literal: E'erdeng'e advanced from Mengmi but was blocked at Laoguantun; after more than a month he withdrew.

entries.zh: 繞從小隴川緩行，巡撫鄂寧檄援，不應，於是明瑞軍援絕，而賊自木邦、老官屯兩道並集。
entries.en: He made a detour by way of Xiaolongchuan and marched slowly; Governor E'ning sent orders calling for aid, but he did not respond. Thus Ming Rui's army was cut off from relief while the rebels converged from Mohang and Laoguantun along two routes.
entries.literal: He made a detour by way of Xiaolongchuan and marched slowly; Governor E'ning sent orders for aid, but he did not respond; thus Ming Rui's army was cut off from relief, while the rebels converged from Mohang and Laoguantun in two columns.

entries.zh: 二月，至小猛育，賊麕聚五萬餘。
entries.en: In the second month they reached Xiaomengyu, where more than fifty thousand rebels had gathered.
entries.literal: In the second month they reached Xiaomengyu; the rebels gathered in a herd of more than fifty thousand.

entries.zh: 我軍食罄，殺馬騾以食；
entries.en: The army's food was exhausted, and horses and mules were killed for food;
entries.literal: Our army's food was exhausted; they killed horses and mules for food;

entries.zh: 火藥亦竭，槍砲不能發。
entries.en: gunpowder was also exhausted, and muskets and cannon could no longer be fired.
entries.literal: gunpowder was also exhausted, and muskets and cannon could not be fired.

entries.zh: 明瑞令諸將達興阿、本進忠分隊潰圍出，而自為殿，血戰萬寇中。
entries.en: Ming Rui ordered the generals Da Xing'a and Ben Jinzhong to divide their companies and break out of the encirclement, while he himself brought up the rear, fighting in bloody combat amid tens of thousands of rebels.
entries.literal: Ming Rui ordered the generals Da Xing'a and Ben Jinzhong to divide their companies and break out of the encirclement, while he himself brought up the rear, fighting in bloody combat amid tens of thousands of rebels.

entries.zh: 扎拉豐阿、觀音保皆死。
entries.en: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao both fell in battle.
entries.literal: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao both died.

entries.zh: 明瑞負創行二十餘裡，手截辮髮授其僕歸報，而縊於樹下，其僕以木葉掩屍去。
entries.en: Wounded, Ming Rui went on for more than twenty li, cut off his own queue with his own hand and gave it to his servant to return and report, then hanged himself beneath a tree; his servant covered the body with leaves and departed.
entries.literal: Ming Rui, wounded, went more than twenty li; with his own hand he cut off his queue and gave it to his servant to return and report, then hanged himself beneath a tree; his servant covered the corpse with leaves and departed.

entries.zh: 事聞，上震悼，賜祭葬，諡果烈。
entries.en: When word arrived the Emperor was shaken with grief, granted sacrificial funeral rites, and gave him the posthumous title Guolie.
entries.literal: When word arrived the Emperor was shaken with grief, granted sacrificial funeral rites, and gave the posthumous title Guolie.

entries.zh: 建旌勇祠京師，諸將死事者扎拉豐阿、觀音保、李全、王廷玉，命並祀，珠魯訥以自戕不與。
entries.en: The Jingyong Shrine was built in the capital; the generals who died in service—Zhala Feng'a, Guanyinbao, Li Quan, and Wang Tingyu—were ordered to be worshiped together, while Zhulun'e was excluded for having killed himself.
entries.literal: The Jingyong Shrine was built in the capital; the generals who died in service—Zhala Feng'a, Guanyinbao, Li Quan, and Wang Tingyu—were ordered to be worshiped together; Zhulun'e was excluded for having killed himself.

entries.zh: 額爾登額及提督譚五格坐失機陷帥，逮詣京師，上廷鞫，用大逆律磔額爾登額，囚其父及女，並族屬戍新疆；
entries.en: E'erdeng'e and Regional Commander-in-Chief Tan Wuge were punished for missing their opportunity and causing the commander's destruction; they were arrested and brought to the capital. The Emperor tried them at court, had E'erdeng'e dismembered under the law of great treason, imprisoned his father and daughter, and exiled his clansmen to Xinjiang;
entries.literal: E'erdeng'e and Regional Commander-in-Chief Tan Wuge were punished for missing their opportunity and causing the commander's destruction; they were arrested and brought to the capital; the Emperor tried them at court; E'erdeng'e was dismembered under the law of great treason; his father and daughter were imprisoned, and his clansmen were exiled to guard Xinjiang;

entries.zh: 譚五格亦棄市，而以其明日祭明瑞及扎拉豐阿、觀音保，上親臨奠。
entries.en: Tan Wuge was also executed in the market. On the following day, when sacrifices were offered to Ming Rui, Zhala Feng'a, and Guanyinbao, the Emperor personally attended.
entries.literal: Tan Wuge was also executed in the market; and on the following day, when Ming Rui and Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao were sacrificed to, the Emperor personally attended the offering.

entries.zh: 常青，佟佳氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
entries.en: Chang Qing, of the Tunggiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Chang Qing, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 父安圖，官至江西巡撫。
entries.en: His father Antu had served as governor of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: His father Antu reached the office of Governor of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 常青自寧郡王府長史累遷察哈爾都統，杭州、福州將軍。
entries.en: Chang Qing advanced step by step from chief steward in the Ning commandery prince's household to commander-in-chief of Chahar and then to general at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Chang Qing rose in succession from Chief steward of the Ning Commandery Prince's establishment to Commander-in-chief of Chahar, and to General at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十一年，署閩浙總督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 51 (1786), he was appointed acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong, he acted as Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 諸羅縣民楊光勳與其弟爭家業，糾眾立會，縣吏捕治不服，常青令按察使李永祺往按。
entries.en: A Zhuluo county man named Yang Guangxun feuded with his brother over family property, rallied supporters into a sworn association, and resisted arrest when county officials moved against them; Chang Qing dispatched surveillance commissioner Li Yongqi to investigate.
entries.literal: Yang Guangxun, a commoner of Zhuluo County, disputed the family estate with his younger brother, gathered a crowd to form a secret society, and when county officials arrested and punished them they would not submit; Chang Qing ordered Surveillance Commissioner Li Yongqi to go investigate.

entries.zh: 上以台灣在海外，不可輕縱，諭勿使蔓延疏脫。
entries.en: The emperor considered Taiwan distant and unstable territory that could not be treated lightly, and ordered that the affair must not be allowed to spread or escape control through negligence.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Taiwan was beyond the sea, said it could not be lightly indulged, and instructed that it must not be allowed to spread or slip through lax handling.

entries.zh: 尋實授閩浙總督。
entries.en: He was soon confirmed in the post of governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Soon he was formally appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 十二月，林爽文亂起，陷彰化，知縣俞峻死之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the Lin Shuangwen uprising broke out; Zhanghua was taken and magistrate Yu Jun was killed.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the rebellion of Lin Shuangwen arose; Zhanghua fell, and Magistrate Yu Jun died in the fighting.

entries.zh: 常青檄水師提督黃仕簡自鹿耳門進，副將丁朝雄從海壇鎮總兵郝壯猷自淡水進，都司馬元勳屯鹿仔港，分道部署；
entries.en: Chang Qing directed naval commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to enter from Luerhmen, vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to move with Haitan garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou from Tamsui, and department commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lugang, dividing his forces along several axes.
entries.literal: Chang Qing ordered Naval Commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to advance from Luerhmen, Vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to accompany Haitan garrison commander-in-chief Hao Zhuangyou advancing from Tamsui, and Department Commander Ma Yuanxun to encamp at Lugang, deploying forces along separate routes;

entries.zh: 復如泉州會陸路提督任承恩調度，令金門鎮總兵羅英笈詣廈門彈壓。
entries.en: He then went to Quanzhou to coordinate with land-forces commander Ren Chengen and ordered Kinmen garrison commander Luo Yingji to Xiamen to keep order.
entries.literal: He then went to Quanzhou to confer with Land Forces Commander-in-chief Ren Chengen on deployment, and ordered Kinmen garrison commander-in-chief Luo Yingji to proceed to Xiamen to suppress unrest.

entries.zh: 尋復令承恩自鹿耳門繼進。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he ordered Chengen to press forward again from Luerhmen.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he again ordered Chengen to follow up by advancing from Luerhmen.

entries.zh: 五十二年，奏賊陷諸羅。
entries.en: In Qianlong 52 (1787) he reported that the rebels had captured Zhuluo.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year, he memorialized that the rebels had taken Zhuluo.

entries.zh: 台灣鎮總兵柴大紀堵剿，賊勢稍沮。
entries.en: Taiwan garrison commander Chai Daji held them in check, and rebel strength began to falter.
entries.literal: Taiwan garrison commander-in-chief Chai Daji blocked and suppressed them, and the rebel momentum slackened somewhat.

entries.zh: 爽文漳州人，其徒率漳籍。
entries.en: Shuangwen was from Zhangzhou, and most of his followers were Zhangzhou men.
entries.literal: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou, and his followers were mostly men of Zhangzhou registration.

entries.zh: 移會兩廣督臣防範，上責其張皇。
entries.en: He notified the governors of the two Guang provinces to guard against spillover, and the emperor criticized him for overstating the danger.
entries.literal: He forwarded a joint notice to the governors of Guangdong and Guangxi to take precautions, and the emperor rebuked him for alarmism.

entries.zh: 授李侍堯閩浙總督，而移常青湖廣。
entries.en: Li Shiyao was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, and Chang Qing was reassigned to Huguang.
entries.literal: Li Shiyao was appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, while Chang Qing was transferred to Huguang.

entries.zh: 既又命常青渡台視師，四月，至台灣。
entries.en: He was soon ordered back to cross to Taiwan and take command of the campaign; in the fourth month he arrived on the island.
entries.literal: Thereafter he was again ordered to cross to Taiwan to oversee the army; in the fourth month he reached Taiwan.

entries.zh: 劾仕簡、承恩遷延觀望，擁兵自衛；
entries.en: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for dragging their feet, holding back while hoarding troops for self-protection;
entries.literal: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for delay and watching from the sidelines while holding troops for their own protection;

entries.zh: 壯猷守鳳山，賊至，棄城走。
entries.en: Zhuangyou was holding Fengshan; when rebels came he abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: Zhuangyou was defending Fengshan; when the rebels arrived, he abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 諭逮承恩，罷仕簡候命，而誅壯猷，遂授常青為將軍。
entries.en: The court ordered Chengen arrested, relieved Shijian pending further orders, and executed Zhuangyou; Chang Qing was then appointed general.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Chengen arrested, Shijian dismissed pending orders, and Zhuangyou executed; then Chang Qing was appointed General.

entries.zh: 賊攻府城，常青督諸軍禦戰，有所俘馘；
entries.en: When rebels assaulted the prefectural seat, Chang Qing led the troops in defense and won some captives and heads;
entries.literal: The rebels attacked the prefectural city; Chang Qing directed the armies in defense and took some captives and heads;

entries.zh: 賊攻桶盤棧，令游擊蔡攀龍等分駐力禦。
entries.en: When rebels attacked Tongpanzhan, he posted guerrilla commander Cai Panlong and others at separate points to hold the line.
entries.literal: When the rebels attacked Tongpanzhan, he ordered Guerrilla Commander Cai Panlong and others to station forces separately and resist with all their strength.

entries.zh: 奏入，上以常青年逾七十，能如此勇往督戰，手詔嘉獎，授其子刑部筆帖式喜明三等侍衛，馳驛往省，並賜御用搬指。
entries.en: When the memorial reached court, the emperor praised Chang Qing in a personal edict for pressing the fight at over seventy, made his son Ximing—a Ministry of Punishments clerk—a third-rank bodyguard, sent him post-haste to visit his father, and granted an imperial thumb ring.
entries.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor, because Chang Qing was over seventy yet could press forward so boldly in directing battle, personally wrote an edict of praise, appointed his son Ximing, a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, as a third-rank bodyguard, sent him post-haste to visit his father, and also bestowed an imperial thumb ring.

entries.zh: 旋奏爽文還大里杙舊巢，其徒莊大田等萬餘人分擾南路，擬先南剿大田，乃北取爽文。
entries.en: He soon reported that Shuangwen had withdrawn to his old base at Daliyi while followers such as Zhuang Datian, numbering more than ten thousand, were harrying the south; he planned to crush Datian in the south first, then move north against Shuangwen.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized that Shuangwen had returned to his old lair at Daliyi, while his followers Zhuang Datian and others, more than ten thousand men, were raiding the southern route in separate bands; he proposed first to suppress Datian in the south, then to strike north and take Shuangwen.

entries.zh: 上韙之，下部優敘。
entries.en: The emperor approved the plan and ordered a favorable record of merit in the ministries.
entries.literal: The emperor approved it and ordered the ministries to record meritorious service favorably.

entries.zh: 旋奏勦賊南潭，殲賊六百餘；
entries.en: He soon reported a campaign at Nantan in which more than six hundred rebels were killed;
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized on suppressing rebels at Nantan, annihilating more than six hundred rebels;

entries.zh: 爽文之徒莊錫舍出降，擒偽軍師番婦金孃，請檻車送京師，上命授錫舍守備。
entries.en: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe defected, and the rebels' female aboriginal strategist Jin Niang was taken; he asked to send her to the capital in a prison cart, and the emperor made Xishe a garrison commander.
entries.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe came over in surrender; the false strategist, the aboriginal woman Jin Niang, was captured; he requested sending her to the capital in a caged cart; the emperor ordered Xishe appointed garrison commander.

entries.zh: 又奏進剿鳳山，出城未十里，賊三面並進，官兵奮勇擊退；
entries.en: He reported another advance on Fengshan; less than ten li from the city rebels closed in from three directions, and government troops drove them back;
entries.literal: He again memorialized on advancing to suppress Fengshan; not ten li outside the city, rebels pressed in from three sides, and government troops fought them off with spirit;

entries.zh: 賊勢蔓延，請厚集兵力，遣大臣督戰。
entries.en: With rebel strength spreading, he asked for heavier reinforcements and a senior minister to take command.
entries.literal: As rebel strength spread, he requested concentrating more troops and dispatching a high minister to direct the campaign.

entries.zh: 上命陝甘總督福康安往視師。
entries.en: The emperor sent Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Fuk'anggan to take command of the campaign.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Fuk'anggan to go oversee the army.

entries.zh: 旋奏：「賊犯府城，為丁朝雄擊退。
entries.en: He soon reported: "Rebels assaulted the prefectural seat and were repulsed by Ding Chaoxiong.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized: "The rebels attacked the prefectural city and were beaten back by Ding Chaoxiong.

entries.zh: 官軍攻莊大田於南潭，殺賊二百餘。
entries.en: Government forces attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.
entries.literal: Government troops attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.

entries.zh: 大營距府城未遠，勢相犄角，無後顧之虞。」
entries.en: The main camp lay close enough to the prefectural seat to support it in mutual defense, with no concern for the rear."
entries.literal: The main camp was not far from the prefectural city, the positions mutually supporting like horn and corner, with no worry for the rear."

entries.zh: 得旨嘉獎，賜雙眼孔雀翎。
entries.en: The court praised him in an edict and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.
entries.literal: He received an edict of praise and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

entries.zh: 旋迭奏鹽水港、笨港均為賊據，糧道既斷，諸羅勢甚危；
entries.en: He soon sent repeated reports that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang had fallen to rebels, supply lines were cut, and Zhuluo was in dire straits;
entries.literal: Soon he repeatedly memorialized that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang were both held by rebels, the grain route was cut, and Zhuluo was in grave peril;

entries.zh: 令總兵魏大斌赴援，戰賊失利，又令游擊田藍玉援大斌。
entries.en: He sent commander Wei Dabin to relieve the city, but Dabin was beaten in action; he then ordered guerrilla commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce him.
entries.literal: He ordered Commander-in-chief Wei Dabin to go to the relief; in fighting the rebels he was defeated, and he then ordered Guerrilla Commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce Dabin.

entries.zh: 上以兵分力薄，飭常青調度失當。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked Chang Qing for poor coordination, saying his forces were spread too thin.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the forces were divided and too thin, rebuked Chang Qing for faulty deployment.

entries.zh: 又諭：「常青駐軍桶盤棧，距南潭不過五里，不將賊目莊大田先行剿除，乃結營自守。
entries.en: The court also said: "Chang Qing held Tongpanzhan only five li from Nantan yet failed to destroy the rebel chief Zhuang Datian first, instead digging in on the defensive.
entries.literal: He further instructed: "Chang Qing encamped at Tongpanzhan, no more than five li from Nantan, yet did not first wipe out the rebel leader Zhuang Datian, but instead entrenched himself in self-defense.

entries.zh: 肘腋之間，任其逼處。」
entries.en: He let the enemy press in at his very side."
entries.literal: At his very armpit he allowed the enemy to press close."

entries.zh: 八月，命福康安為將軍，督諸將海蘭察、普爾普等大出師討爽文。
entries.en: In the eighth month Fuk'anggan was made general and led Hailancha, Pulupu, and other commanders in a full-scale campaign against Shuangwen.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Fuk'anggan was appointed General and directed the generals Hailancha, Pulupu, and others in a major expedition against Shuangwen.

entries.zh: 諭常青，謂：「非責其師無功，特以年已七十，軍旅非所素習。
entries.en: Chang Qing was told: "This is not to reproach you for failure in command, but at seventy you are not seasoned in field warfare.
entries.literal: Chang Qing was instructed: "This is not to blame you for achieving nothing as commander, but simply that you are already seventy, and military affairs are not what you have long practiced.

entries.zh: 福康安未至，仍當相機進​​剿。」
entries.en: Until Fuk'anggan arrives, you should still press the attack whenever conditions allow."
entries.literal: Before Fuk'anggan arrives, you should still advance to suppress as opportunity permits."

entries.zh: 旋奏：「賊自南潭來攻，侍衛烏什哈達等擊敗之。
entries.en: He soon reported: "Rebels came from Nantan and were beaten back by bodyguard Ushihada and others.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized: "Rebels attacked from Nantan and were defeated by Bodyguard Ushihada and others.

entries.zh: 因雨後路滑，收兵；
entries.en: After rain made the roads treacherous, the troops were pulled back;
entries.literal: Because the roads were slippery after rain, the troops were withdrawn;

entries.zh: 又進攻南潭，焚草藔數百間，以天晚，山徑偪仄，不便深入。」
entries.en: they advanced again on Nantan and burned several hundred rebel huts; at dusk the mountain trails were too narrow for a deep pursuit."
entries.literal: they again advanced on Nantan and burned several hundred thatched huts; as night fell, the mountain paths were narrow and cramped, making deep pursuit inconvenient."

entries.zh: 藔謂賊所居草屋也。
entries.en: Liao here means the grass huts in which the rebels dwelt.
entries.literal: Liao means the grass huts where the rebels lived.

entries.zh: 上以其屢稱遇雨路仄收兵，傳旨嚴飭。
entries.en: The emperor, weary of repeated excuses about rain, mud, and narrow trails, sent a stern rebuke.
entries.literal: The emperor, because he repeatedly cited rain, bad roads, and narrow paths as reasons for withdrawing troops, sent an edict sternly rebuking him.

entries.zh: 上又聞賊诇知軍中暑濕多病，常青機事不密，又不督兵深入，屢詰責。
entries.en: The court also learned that rebels had spied out the army's heat-sickness and that Chang Qing's plans leaked and he would not drive troops forward; he was rebuked again and again.
entries.literal: The emperor also heard that the rebels had learned by espionage that the army suffered much from heat, damp, and disease; that Chang Qing was not discreet in his plans; and that he again failed to drive the troops deep—he was repeatedly questioned and rebuked.

entries.zh: 旋奏總兵梁朝桂勦賊多斬獲，提督柴大紀報諸羅圍急，令副將蔡攀龍赴援。
entries.en: He reported commander Liang Chaogui's heavy kills in action and commander Chai Daji's urgent plea from the Zhuluo siege, and sent vice-general Cai Panlong to relieve the city.
