entries.literal: Soon he memorialized that Commander-in-chief Liang Chaogui had suppressed rebels with many kills and captures; Commander-in-chief Chai Daji reported that the siege of Zhuluo was urgent; he ordered Vice-general Cai Panlong to go to the relief.

entries.zh: 上諭令親援大紀，待福康安至，合軍進攻。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him to relieve Daji in person and, once Fuk'anggan arrived, to combine forces for a general assault.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him to go in person to relieve Daji, and when Fuk'anggan arrived to join forces and attack.

entries.zh: 旋奏同江寧將軍永慶等在竹篙厝等處殲賊甚眾；
entries.en: He soon reported that with Jiangning general Yongqing and others he had destroyed large rebel forces at Zhugaocuo and elsewhere;
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized that together with Jiangning General Yongqing and others he had annihilated very many rebels at Zhugaocuo and other places;

entries.zh: 山豬毛社義民尤趫捷，獲砲一，生擒賊目張招。
entries.en: loyal militia from the Shanzhumao community fought with exceptional speed; one cannon was taken and rebel leader Zhang Zhao captured alive.
entries.literal: the loyal militia of the Shanzhumao community were especially swift and agile; one cannon was captured and the rebel leader Zhang Zhao was taken alive.

entries.zh: 又奏總兵普吉保克月眉莊，距諸羅五里，令與大紀並力固守；
entries.en: He reported that commander Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and ordered him to hold the line with Daji;
entries.literal: He again memorialized that Commander-in-chief Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and he ordered him to hold fast together with Daji;

entries.zh: 又令諸生劉宗榮等給番社土目札諭防賊竄匿。
entries.en: and had students Liu Zongrong and others deliver written orders to aboriginal headmen to block rebel escape routes.
entries.literal: he also ordered the students Liu Zongrong and others to issue written notices to aboriginal community headmen to guard against rebels slipping into hiding.

entries.zh: 屢得旨嘉許。
entries.en: The court praised these reports repeatedly.
entries.literal: He repeatedly received edicts of approval.

entries.zh: 普吉保，札庫塔氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Pu Jibao, of the Jakuta clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Pu Jibao, of the Jakuta clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十年，以藍翎侍衛從軍徵烏什，有功，補三等侍衛。
entries.en: In Qianlong 30 he went to war against Ush as a blue-insignia bodyguard, distinguished himself, and was made a third-rank bodyguard.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong, as a bodyguard with the blue insignia he joined the army to campaign against Ush, performed meritorious service, and was appointed third-rank bodyguard.

entries.zh: 三十七年，從參贊大臣舒常攻日旁，有功。
entries.en: In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Minister Consultant Shu Chang against Ripang and earned credit.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Minister Consultant Shu Chang in attacking Ripang, with merit.

entries.zh: 三十九年，從副將軍豐升額攻凱立葉山，進抵迪噶拉穆札山。
entries.en: In the thirty-ninth year he served under Deputy Commander Feng Sheng'e at Kailiye Mountain and pushed on to Digalamuzha Mountain.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he followed Deputy Commander-in-chief Feng Sheng'e in attacking Kailiye Mountain, advancing to Digalamuzha Mountain.

entries.zh: 賊分三隊，普吉保偕侍衛瑪爾占等夾攻，斃賊無算，賜衝捷巴圖魯名號。
entries.en: When the enemy split into three bodies, Pu Jibao and bodyguard Ma'erzhan and others struck from both flanks and killed without number; he received the title Chongjie Batulu.
entries.literal: The rebels divided into three columns; Pu Jibao together with bodyguards Ma'erzhan and others attacked from both flanks, killing countless rebels, and was granted the title Chongjie Batulu.

entries.zh: 四十年，攻噶爾丹寺諸地，連破木城、石碉。
entries.en: In the fortieth year he fought at Ga'erdan Monastery and elsewhere, breaking wooden walls and stone blockhouses in succession.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he attacked Ga'erdan Monastery and other places, successively breaking wooden palisades and stone blockhouses.

entries.zh: 上獎普吉保勇往，累擢福建汀州鎮總兵。
entries.en: The emperor praised Pu Jibao's bold advance and raised him by stages to garrison commander of Tingzhou in Fujian.
entries.literal: The emperor commended Pu Jibao's daring advance and repeatedly promoted him to garrison commander of Tingzhou in Fujian.

entries.zh: 林爽文為亂，總督常青檄普吉保會剿，五十二年，率水師渡台灣，迭破賊鹿仔港、八卦山，上嘉其奮勉。
entries.en: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor-General Chang Qing summoned Pu Jibao to the joint campaign; in Qianlong 52 he crossed to Taiwan at the head of the fleet, took Lugang and Baguashan in turn, and won the emperor's praise for his zeal.
entries.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor-General Chang Qing ordered Pu Jibao to join the suppression; in the fifty-second year he led the naval forces across to Taiwan, repeatedly defeating the rebels at Lugang and Baguashan; the emperor praised his zeal.

entries.zh: 爽文見師至，退守鬥六門、大里杙。
entries.en: Seeing the imperial host arrive, Shuangwen withdrew to hold Douliumen and Daliyi.
entries.literal: Shuangwen, seeing the army arrive, fell back to defend Douliumen and Daliyi.

entries.zh: 普吉保以師進，爽文攻諸羅，赴援，抵笨港，率游擊海亮等殲賊數百，毀賊莊七，得旨嘉獎，賜玉搬指、荷包、蟒袍。
entries.en: Pu Jibao pressed forward; when Shuangwen struck Zhuluo, he hurried to the relief, reached Bengang, and with guerrilla commander Hailiang and others killed hundreds of rebels and destroyed seven rebel villages. An imperial commendation followed, with a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.
entries.literal: Pu Jibao advanced with his army; Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo; he went to the rescue, reaching Bengang, leading Guerrilla Commander Hailiang and others to destroy several hundred rebels, destroying seven rebel villages; he received an imperial commendation and was granted a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.

entries.zh: 笨港潰賊糾眾截我兵，普吉保擊斬甚眾。
entries.en: Routed rebels at Bengang rallied to cut off the government column; Pu Jibao struck and slew a great many.
entries.literal: Routed rebels at Bengang gathered a mob to intercept government troops; Pu Jibao struck and beheaded very many.

entries.zh: 嗣以駐兵元長莊、月眉莊不進，旨嚴飭。
entries.en: Later, because he sat idle at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang, the court sent a stern rebuke.
entries.literal: Subsequently because he stationed troops at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang without advancing, he received a stern imperial reprimand.

entries.zh: 尋攻大埔林，收復鬥六門。
entries.en: He soon attacked Dapulin and retook Douliumen.
entries.literal: Soon he attacked Dapulin and recovered Douliumen.

entries.zh: 爽文竄內山，普吉保從諸將徒步陟山搜捕。
entries.en: Shuangwen fled into the interior hills; Pu Jibao joined the other commanders in climbing the mountains on foot to hunt him down.
entries.literal: Shuangwen fled into the inner mountains; Pu Jibao followed the various generals on foot up the mountains to search and capture.

entries.zh: 五十三年，以兵扼科仔坑口，合圍，俘爽文。
entries.en: In Qianlong 53 he blocked Kezikeng Pass with his men, helped close the net, and took Shuangwen alive.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year, with troops he held Kezikeng Pass, joined the encirclement, and captured Shuangwen alive.

entries.zh: 南路莊大田亦就擒。
entries.en: Zhuang Datian of the southern front was captured as well.
entries.literal: The southern-route rebel Zhuang Datian was also captured.

entries.zh: 台灣平，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: When Taiwan was pacified, his likeness was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.
entries.literal: Taiwan was pacified; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.

entries.zh: 普吉保初克鹿仔港，以福康安疏薦，授台灣總兵。
entries.en: After Pu Jibao's first victory at Lugang, Fuk'anggan recommended him and he was made garrison commander of Taiwan.
entries.literal: When Pu Jibao first captured Lugang, on Fuk'anggan's memorial recommendation he was appointed Taiwan garrison commander.

entries.zh: 明年，上念台灣初定，慮普吉保不能勝，命解任。
entries.en: The next year, mindful that Taiwan had only just been settled and doubting Pu Jibao was equal to the post, the emperor ordered him removed.
entries.literal: The next year the emperor, reflecting that Taiwan had only just been pacified and fearing Pu Jibao could not fill the post, ordered him relieved of duty.

entries.zh: 尋授廣西左江鎮，坐責把總黎振乾投水死，戍伊犁。
entries.en: He was soon given the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi, but was convicted after platoon commander Li Zhenqian drowned himself on his watch and was sent to exile in Yili.
entries.literal: Soon appointed to the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi; convicted for holding a platoon commander Li Zhenqian responsible when he drowned himself, and exiled to Yili.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 五十三年春，復攻東港，仍遣諜以水注賊砲，督兵攻渡口，賊驚竄，逐三十餘裡，乃倚山而軍。
entries.en: In the spring of Qianlong 53 he attacked Donggang again, again flooding the enemy guns by stratagem, stormed the ford, and chased the fleeing rebels more than thirty li before making camp against the hills.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year he again attacked Donggang, again sending spies to flood the rebels' cannon with water, directing troops to attack the crossing; rebels fled in alarm; he pursued over thirty li, then encamped backed by mountains.

entries.zh: 賊夜來犯，朝雄戒勿動；
entries.en: The rebels came by night; Chaoxiong ordered his men to hold still.
entries.literal: Rebels came to attack by night; Chaoxiong warned troops not to move.

entries.zh: 及曉，賊倦，掩擊，大破之。
entries.en: At daybreak, when the enemy was spent, he fell on them from cover and broke them utterly.
entries.literal: At dawn, when the rebels were weary, he made a surprise attack and routed them decisively.

entries.zh: 爽文遣其徒來援，朝雄築壘困之。
entries.en: Shuangwen sent men to relieve them; Chaoxiong threw up stockades to pin them down.
entries.literal: Shuangwen sent his followers to reinforce; Chaoxiong built stockades to hem them in.

entries.zh: 賊潰圍出，設伏斷其歸路，而自將追之，大破賊，遂復東港。
entries.en: When the rebels burst out, he laid an ambush across their retreat and led the pursuit himself, shattering them and retaking Donggang.
entries.literal: Rebels broke out of the encirclement; he set an ambush to cut their return route and himself led the pursuit, routing the rebels decisively, and thus recovered Donggang.

entries.zh: 福康安上其功，授海壇鎮總兵。
entries.en: Fuk'anggan memorialized his merit, and he was made garrison commander of Haitan.
entries.literal: Fuk'anggan reported his merit; he was appointed garrison commander of Haitan.

entries.zh: 既，福康安劾柴大紀受陋規，言朝雄為安平協副將時亦有此，當奪職戍軍台，上以朝雄攻東港戰有功，命留任。
entries.en: Later Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for taking mean bribes and said Chaoxiong had done the same as Anping's deputy commander and should be dismissed and sent to the military penal colony; the emperor, weighing his service at Donggang, let him keep his post.
entries.literal: Subsequently Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for accepting shabby bribes, saying Chaoxiong when deputy commander at Anping had done the same and ought to be stripped of office and exiled to the military penal colony; the emperor, because Chaoxiong's fighting at Donggang had merit, ordered him to remain in post.

entries.zh: 林鬎舵、林明灼者，海盜渠也，五十四年，朝雄巡洋至汜澳，破盜巢，得鬎舵等；
entries.en: The pirate chiefs Lin Liguduo and Lin Mingzhuo were broken when Chaoxiong, patrolling in Qianlong 54, raided their nest at Fan'ao and took Liguduo and his fellows.
entries.literal: Lin Liguduo and Lin Mingzhuo were pirate chieftains; in the fifty-fourth year Chaoxiong on patrol reached Fan'ao, broke their pirate nest and captured Liguduo and others.

entries.zh: 而明灼拒殺參將張殿魁。
entries.en: Mingzhuo, however, resisted and killed lieutenant commander Zhang Diankui.
entries.literal: But Mingzhuo resisted and killed Lieutenant Commander Zhang Diankui.

entries.zh: 上責總督伍拉納，伍拉納以屬朝雄，督舟師出海，遇諸大麥洋，俟其近，發大砲，斃數酋，明灼窮蹙，躍入海，官軍鉤致，俘以歸。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked Governor-General Wulana, who handed the hunt to Chaoxiong; Chaoxiong put the fleet to sea, met the pirates at Zhudamaiyang, waited until they were close, and opened with heavy guns, killing several chiefs; Mingzhuo, trapped, leapt into the water, was gaffed up by government sailors, and brought in alive.
entries.literal: The emperor reprimanded Governor-General Wulana; Wulana turned the matter over to Chaoxiong, who directed the naval force to sea; encountering them at Zhudamaiyang, he waited until they drew near, fired great cannon, killed several chieftains; Mingzhuo, cornered, leaped into the sea; government troops hooked him up and brought him back prisoner.

entries.zh: 五十五年，追論朝雄在台灣失察天地會邪教，當奪職；
entries.en: In Qianlong 55 he was judged retrospectively for failing in Taiwan to detect the Heaven and Earth Society secret society and was to be dismissed from office.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, retrospectively it was adjudged that Chaoxiong in Taiwan had failed to detect the Heaven and Earth Society heterodox cult and ought to be stripped of office.

entries.zh: 上諮伍拉納朝雄在官狀，伍拉納言朝雄督水師捕盜有勞，命還任。
entries.en: The emperor asked Governor-General Wulana about Ding Chaoxiong's performance in office. Wulana reported that Chaoxiong had distinguished himself directing the navy in the pursuit of pirates, and the court ordered him restored to his post.
entries.literal: The emperor inquired of Wulana about Chaoxiong's conduct in office; Wulana said Chaoxiong had merit in supervising the naval forces to capture bandits, and he was ordered to return to his post.

entries.zh: 五十八年，攝水師提督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 58 he served as acting naval commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he acted as naval commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 五十九年，入覲，至清江浦，病篤。
entries.en: In Qianlong 59 he traveled to court for audience, but upon reaching Qingjiangpu his illness turned critical.
entries.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he came to audience; reaching Qingjiangpu, his illness became grave.

entries.zh: 乞罷歸，卒於上海舟中。
entries.en: He petitioned to resign and return home, and died aboard his boat at Shanghai.
entries.literal: He begged to resign and return; he died in a boat at Shanghai.

entries.zh: 鄂輝，碧魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 自前鋒分發四川試用守備。
entries.en: Posted from the Vanguard, he was sent to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commander.
entries.literal: From the Vanguard he was assigned to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commander.

entries.zh: 七遷建昌鎮總兵。
entries.en: After seven promotions he rose to commander of the Jianchang garrison.
entries.literal: After seven promotions he became commander of the Jianchang garrison.

entries.zh: 從大學士阿桂定蘭州回亂，予法什尚阿巴圖魯名號。
entries.en: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in suppressing the Muslim uprising at Lanzhou and was granted the honorific title Fashishang'a Batulu.
entries.literal: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in pacifying the Lanzhou Muslim rebellion and was given the title Fashishang'a Batulu.

entries.zh: 再遷成都將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted again to general at Chengdu.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to general at Chengdu.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十二年，署四川總督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 52 he served as acting governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong he acted as Governor-General of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 將軍福康安討台灣亂民林爽文，上命鄂輝率四川屯練降番濟師。
entries.en: When General Fuk'anggan marched against the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen, the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan militia, trained levies, and surrendered tribal auxiliaries to reinforce the campaign.
entries.literal: When General Fuk'anggan campaigned against the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen, the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan militia, trained troops, and surrendered tribesmen to reinforce the army.

entries.zh: 尋授參贊，從渡海援嘉義。
entries.en: He was soon appointed campaign deputy and crossed the strait to relieve Jiayi.
entries.literal: Soon he was made a staff deputy and crossed the sea to relieve Jiayi.

entries.zh: 鄂輝屯東莊溪橋，攻克牛稠山竹柵，嘉義圍解。
entries.en: E Hui encamped at Dongzhuangxi Bridge, stormed the bamboo stockade at Niuchoushan, and the siege of Jiayi was broken.
entries.literal: E Hui encamped at Dongzhuangxi Bridge, captured the bamboo stockade at Niuchoushan, and the siege of Jiayi was lifted.

entries.zh: 逐賊至大排竹，殲之。
entries.en: He drove the rebels to Dapaizhu and destroyed them there.
entries.literal: He pursued the rebels to Dapaizhu and annihilated them.

entries.zh: 師攻鬥六門，賊自山下撲，鄂輝督兵衝截，賊奔逸，攻克大埔林、大埔尾二莊，賊潰。
entries.en: At the assault on Douliumen the rebels charged down from the hills; E Hui led his men in a countercharge, broke their attack, and seized the villages of Dapulin and Dapowei as the enemy scattered in rout.
entries.literal: When the army attacked Douliumen the rebels rushed down from the hills; E Hui directed troops to charge and intercept, the rebels fled, and Dapulin and Dapowei were taken and the rebels collapsed.

entries.zh: 爽文自所居大里杙奔內山番界，鄂輝逐之至集埔。
entries.en: Shuangwen fled his stronghold at Daliyi into the inner mountain aboriginal lands, and E Hui pursued him as far as Jipu.
entries.literal: Shuangwen fled from his residence at Daliyi into the mountain aborigine territory; E Hui pursued him to Jipu.

entries.zh: 五十三年春，诇知爽文所匿地曰東勢角，福康安督鄂輝及舒亮追捕，自歸仔頭至麻著社，分軍，鄂輝自撲仔離東山路進，舒亮直取東勢角。
entries.en: In the spring of Qianlong 53, intelligence placed Shuangwen at Dongshijiao. Fuk'anggan directed E Hui and Shu Liang in pursuit from Guizaitou to Mazheshe, splitting their forces: E Hui would advance along the eastern road from Puzaili, while Shu Liang would strike Dongshijiao head-on.
entries.literal: In spring of the fifty-third year scouts learned Shuangwen was hiding at Dongshijiao; Fuk'anggan directed E Hui and Shu Liang in pursuit from Guizaitou to Mazheshe, dividing the army—E Hui advanced by the eastern route from Puzaili, Shu Liang struck directly for Dongshijiao.

entries.zh: 是役遂俘爽文，亂乃定。
entries.en: In that operation Shuangwen was taken prisoner, and the rebellion was finally brought to an end.
entries.literal: In this campaign Shuangwen was captured and the rebellion was settled.

entries.zh: 上命台灣嘉義立諸將帥生祠，鄂輝與焉。
entries.en: The emperor ordered living shrines erected at Jiayi in Taiwan to honor the commanding generals, and E Hui was numbered among them.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered living shrines erected at Jiayi in Taiwan to the generals, and E Hui was among them.

entries.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣，賜雙眼孔雀翎、雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: On the army's return his portrait was hung in the Hall of Purple Glories, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather together with a hereditary Cloud Cavalry captaincy.
entries.literal: When the army returned, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.

entries.zh: 鄂輝朝熱河行在。
entries.en: E Hui presented himself to the emperor at the traveling palace in Rehe.
entries.literal: E Hui attended the emperor at the Rehe traveling palace.

entries.zh: 廓爾喀侵西藏，據濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。
entries.en: The Gurkhas invaded Tibet and occupied Gyirong, Nyalam, and neighboring districts.
entries.literal: The Gurkhas invaded Tibet and seized Gyirong, Nyalam, and other places.

entries.zh: 上促鄂輝還四川，與提督成德帥師赴援，又命侍郎巴忠往按。
entries.en: The emperor pressed E Hui to return to Sichuan and, together with commander Cheng De, lead a relief force into Tibet, while also dispatching Vice Minister Ba Zhong to conduct an on-site investigation.
entries.literal: The emperor urged E Hui back to Sichuan to join Commander-in-chief Cheng De in leading relief forces, and also sent Vice Minister Ba Zhong to investigate on site.

entries.zh: 巴忠先嘗為駐藏大臣，習藏事，示意噶布倫，令賂廓爾喀返侵地。
entries.en: Ba Zhong had once served as the Qing resident commissioner in Tibet and knew Tibetan affairs well; he quietly instructed the kalöns to buy off the Gurkhas and recover the lost territory.
entries.literal: Ba Zhong had previously served as Resident Commissioner in Tibet and knew Tibetan affairs; he signaled the kalöns to bribe the Gurkhas to return the seized territory.

entries.zh: 鄂輝等遂與議和，疏陳善後事。
entries.en: E Hui and his colleagues thereupon negotiated a settlement and submitted a memorial outlining measures for the aftermath.
entries.literal: E Hui and others thereupon made peace and memorialized on measures for aftermath.

entries.zh: 尋授四川總督。
entries.en: He was soon appointed governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed Governor-General of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 五十六年，廓爾喀渝盟，复侵濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。
entries.en: In Qianlong 56 the Gurkhas violated the agreement and again invaded Gyirong, Nyalam, and the surrounding region.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year the Gurkhas broke the treaty and again invaded Gyirong, Nyalam, and neighboring areas.

entries.zh: 上命將軍福康安督師討廓爾喀，責鄂輝誤用巴忠議致復生事，奪官，予副都統銜駐藏，聽福康安指揮，福康安令督餉。
entries.en: The emperor placed General Fuk'anggan in overall command of the campaign against the Gurkhas, held E Hui responsible for having followed Ba Zhong's counsel and thereby inviting a renewed crisis, stripped him of office, and assigned him to Tibet with the rank of vice banner commander under Fuk'anggan's command; Fuk'anggan then put him in charge of provisioning the army.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered General Fuk'anggan to command the campaign against the Gurkhas, blamed E Hui for wrongly adopting Ba Zhong's plan and causing renewed trouble, stripped his office, gave him vice banner commander rank to remain in Tibet under Fuk'anggan's orders, and Fuk'anggan put him in charge of supplies.

entries.zh: 工部尚書和琳劾鄂輝得廓爾喀貢表不以上聞，命奪副都統銜，逮赴前藏荷校示罰。
entries.en: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for having received Gurkha tribute memorials without reporting them to the throne. He was stripped of his vice banner commander rank, arrested, and sent to front Tibet to bear the cangue as a public punishment.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for receiving Gurkha tribute memorials without reporting them; he was stripped of vice banner commander rank and arrested to front Tibet to bear the cangue as punishment.

entries.zh: 五十八年，命還京師，授拜唐阿。
entries.en: In Qianlong 58 he was recalled to the capital and appointed a Baitangga guardsman.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was ordered back to the capital and appointed a Baitangga guard.

entries.zh: 加員外郎銜，遷熱河總管。
entries.en: He was given the additional rank of vice director and transferred to superintendent of Rehe.
entries.literal: He received the additional title of vice director and was transferred to superintendent of Rehe.

entries.zh: 列傳一百十五
entries.en: Biography 115
entries.literal: Biographies 115

entries.zh: 桂林遣陳定國調綽斯甲布兵駐軍界上，備調遣。
entries.en: Guilin sent Chen Dingguo to muster Zhuosijia troops and hold them on the frontier, ready for deployment.
entries.literal: Guilin dispatched Chen Dingguo to mobilize Zhuosijia troops and station them on the border, ready for deployment.

entries.zh: 上責桂林不令元俊乘勝取金川。
entries.en: The emperor censured Guilin for failing to let Yuanjun press the victory and seize Jinchuan.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Guilin for not ordering Yuanjun to take advantage of the victory to seize Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 元俊旋與散秩大臣阿爾泰劾桂林欺誑及諸罪狀，上為奪桂林職，令阿爾泰署四川總督，命額駙、尚書、公福隆安按治。
entries.en: Yuanjun then joined Minister Without Portfolio Altai in impeaching Guilin for deceit and other offenses. The emperor removed Guilin from office, appointed Altai acting Governor-General of Sichuan, and sent Imperial Son-in-Law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to conduct an inquiry.
entries.literal: Yuanjun then joined Minister Without Portfolio Altai in impeaching Guilin for deception and various offenses. The emperor stripped Guilin of his office, ordered Altai to serve as acting Governor-General of Sichuan, and dispatched Imperial Son-in-Law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to investigate.

entries.zh: 未至，詔元俊督兵赴綽斯甲布率土兵進攻金川。
entries.en: Before the investigators arrived, an edict ordered Yuanjun to take command at Zhuosijia and lead native troops in an assault on Jinchuan.
entries.literal: Before they arrived, an edict ordered Yuanjun to supervise troops and proceed to Zhuosijia to lead native soldiers in an attack on Jinchuan.

entries.zh: 元俊奏：「自戰失利，士氣消沮，現在兵力不足並按兩金川。
entries.en: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since our recent defeat, morale has collapsed. Our present strength is insufficient to subdue both Jinchuans simultaneously.
entries.literal: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since the defeat in battle, morale has collapsed. Present forces are insufficient to suppress both Jinchuans at once.

entries.zh: 請敕調湖南、湖北、山西、甘肅兵二萬，分三道進軍，計兩月可竟事。」
entries.en: I request orders to mobilize twenty thousand troops from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu for a three-column advance; the campaign should be finished within two months."
entries.literal: I request an edict to mobilize twenty thousand troops from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu, advancing in three columns; I estimate the affair can be concluded within two months."

entries.zh: 上以元俊請益師，未免張皇，令福隆安會阿爾泰、阿桂與元俊詳悉覈計。
entries.en: The emperor regarded Yuanjun's request for reinforcements as unduly alarmist and ordered Fu Long'an to confer with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun on a full reassessment.
entries.literal: The emperor considered Yuanjun's request for additional troops unduly alarmist and ordered Fu Long'an to meet with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun for a thorough review and calculation.

entries.zh: 上諭軍機大臣，謂：「元俊能治事，熟番情；
entries.en: The emperor told the Grand Council: "Yuanjun is capable and knows the frontier tribes well;
entries.literal: The emperor instructed the Grand Council, saying: "Yuanjun can manage affairs and understands tribal conditions;

entries.zh: 但其人似狡猾好事，當留意駕馭。」
entries.en: but he seems crafty and prone to stirring trouble—keep a firm hand on him."
entries.literal: but the man seems crafty and eager for trouble; care should be taken in controlling him."

entries.zh: 尋，福隆安疏陳所劾桂林狀不實，上以方進兵，元俊熟番情，諸事不必窮究；
entries.en: Soon afterward Fu Long'an reported that the charges against Guilin did not hold up. With the campaign underway and Yuanjun's expertise on the frontier indispensable, the emperor said not every accusation need be pursued to the end;
entries.literal: Soon afterward, Fu Long'an memorialized that the charges against Guilin were unfounded. Since troops were advancing, and Yuanjun understood tribal conditions, the emperor said there was no need to pursue every matter to the end;

entries.zh: 惟言：「桂林以白金畀金川贖被掠官兵罪最重，今汪承霈自承出其意。
entries.en: but noted: "Guilin's gravest offense was paying Jinchuan silver to ransom captured officers and men. Wang Chengpei has now admitted the scheme was his.
entries.literal: but stated: "Guilin's gravest offense was giving silver to Jinchuan to ransom captured officers and soldiers. Now Wang Chengpei has admitted the idea came from him.

entries.zh: 承霈以曹司從軍，不當與其事。
entries.en: As a Board secretary attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.
entries.literal: Chengpei, as a Board secretary accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.

entries.zh: 當詰汪騰龍，成信讞。」
entries.en: Wang Tenglong must be questioned so the truth can be established."
entries.literal: Wang Tenglong should be interrogated to establish a credible finding."

entries.zh: 福隆安复疏言：「騰龍以金囑王萬邦待巴旺、布拉底克歸迷道官兵予金為賞，元俊誘萬邦令具札言桂林使贖被掠官兵。
entries.en: Fu Long'an reported further: "Tenglong had entrusted Wang Wanbang with silver to reward officers and men from Bawang and Buladike who had lost their way and returned. Yuanjun coerced Wanbang into writing a letter claiming Guilin had paid silver to ransom captured troops.
entries.literal: Fu Long'an memorialized again: "Tenglong entrusted Wang Wanbang with silver to reward officers and soldiers from Bawang and Buladike who had strayed and returned. Yuanjun induced Wanbang to write a letter stating that Guilin had sent silver to ransom captured officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 事為元俊陷。」
entries.en: The whole affair was a frame-up engineered by Yuanjun."
entries.literal: The affair was a frame-up by Yuanjun."

entries.zh: 上乃怒，責元俊奸狡負恩，命奪職逮問，籍其家。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, denounced Yuanjun for treachery and ingratitude, stripped him of rank, ordered his arrest, and confiscated his property.
entries.literal: The emperor grew angry, rebuked Yuanjun for treachery and ingratitude, ordered his dismissal and arrest for interrogation, and confiscated his household property.

entries.zh: 參贊阿桂疏言：「元俊在川日久，熟番情，為近邊土司所信服。
entries.en: Campaign Adviser Agui memorialized: "Yuanjun has served in Sichuan for years, knows the tribes intimately, and enjoys the trust of the frontier chieftains.
entries.literal: Campaign Adviser Agui memorialized: "Yuanjun has been in Sichuan for many years, understands tribal conditions, and is trusted by the frontier chieftains.

entries.zh: 諸將能馭番無出其右。
entries.en: No other general matches him in handling tribal affairs.
entries.literal: Among the generals, none surpasses him in managing the tribes.

entries.zh: 臣遇事多與詢商，冀收指臂之效。
entries.en: I consult him on nearly every decision, hoping to make our efforts work as one coordinated force.
entries.literal: Your servant consults with him on many matters, hoping to achieve the effect of moving finger and arm as one.

entries.zh: 乞恩仍留軍中，倘奮勉出力，使詐使貪，原所不廢；
entries.en: I beg that he be kept with the army. If he fights hard, his skill in deception—or even his appetite for gain—need not count against him;
entries.literal: I beg grace to keep him in the army. If he exerts himself diligently, the use of stratagem or even greed need not be discarded;

entries.zh: 如剛愎逞私，即據實嚴劾。」
entries.en: but if he turns obstinate or self-serving, I shall impeach him without mercy."
entries.literal: but if he is obstinate and pursues private ends, I shall impeach him strictly according to the facts."

entries.zh: 上命留總兵，還所籍財產。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Yuanjun kept on as regional commander and his confiscated property returned.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him retained as regional commander and his confiscated property restored.

entries.zh: 元俊同副都統永平、博靈阿等潛赴墨壟溝，進至郡崢。
entries.en: Yuanjun joined Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others in a stealthy advance to Molonggou and on to Junzheng.
entries.literal: Yuanjun, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others, secretly proceeded to Molonggou and advanced to Junzheng.

entries.zh: 乘月督軍登山薄賊卡，正大霧，我師騰躍入卡，克山樑三道、碉卡二十有四，進克格魯克石。
entries.en: Under cover of moonlight he led the troops up the mountain against the rebel blockhouses. A thick fog hung over the field; our men vaulted into the positions, took three ridges and twenty-four watchtower blockhouses, and pressed on to capture Gelukeshi.
entries.literal: Taking advantage of moonlight, he directed the army up the mountain to press against the rebel blockhouses. A heavy fog had set in; our troops leapt into the blockhouses, captured three mountain ridges and twenty-four watchtower blockhouses, and advanced to take Gelukeshi.

entries.zh: 金川酋圖佔丹壩官寨，綽斯甲布土司發兵往助，阿桂奏令元俊增兵往剿，未行，卒於軍。
entries.en: When the Jinchuan chieftain tried to seize the Danba chieftain's stockade, the Zhuosijia chieftain sent troops to help. Agui memorialized ordering Yuanjun to reinforce and move against them, but before he could march, he died in camp.
entries.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain plotted to seize the Danba official stockade. The Zhuosijia chieftain dispatched troops to assist. Agui memorialized ordering Yuanjun to add troops and proceed to suppress them, but before he could march, he died in camp.

entries.zh: 元俊在邊久，善馭諸土司。
entries.en: Yuanjun had spent years on the frontier and knew how to manage the chieftains.
entries.literal: Yuanjun had been on the frontier for a long time and was skilled at managing the various chieftains.

entries.zh: 往時賚諸土司繒帛輒窳敝，元俊必以善者，諸土司皆喜。
entries.en: Imperial gifts of silk to the chieftains had often been shoddy; Yuanjun always saw that they received good cloth, and the chieftains were grateful.
entries.literal: In former times the silk bestowed on the chieftains was often shoddy; Yuanjun always gave them good quality, and all the chieftains were pleased.

entries.zh: 元俊出行邊，諸土司率妻子出謁，畀以茶、菸、簪珥，視若家人。
entries.en: When Yuanjun toured the frontier, chieftains would bring their wives and children to greet him. He shared tea, tobacco, hairpins, and earrings with them and treated them like kin.
entries.literal: When Yuanjun traveled the frontier, the chieftains would bring their wives and children out to pay respects. He would give them tea, tobacco, hairpins, and earrings, treating them like family.

entries.zh: 稍不循法度，即訶譴，皆悚息聽命。
entries.en: Step out of line even slightly and he would rebuke you—everyone trembled and obeyed.
entries.literal: If they strayed even slightly from proper conduct, he would rebuke them, and all would tremble and obey.

entries.zh: 打箭爐徼外夾壩出沒，元俊至，無敢犯行李者。
entries.en: Bandits prowled beyond the Dartsedo frontier, yet when Yuanjun passed through, no one dared lay a hand on his baggage.
entries.literal: Bandits lurked beyond the Dartsedo frontier passes, but when Yuanjun arrived, none dared touch his baggage.

entries.zh: 諸番小有動靜，爭來告，以故元俊諸所措置皆中窾要。
entries.en: The tribes reported even the smallest stir, which is why Yuanjun's every move hit the mark.
entries.literal: Whenever the tribes showed the slightest movement, they vied to report it. For this reason, Yuanjun's every measure hit the vital point.

entries.zh: 其得罪，上亦知其枉。
entries.en: When he fell from favor, the emperor knew the punishment was unjust.
entries.literal: When he fell into disgrace, the emperor also knew he had been wronged.

entries.zh: 既卒，其子猶戍邊。
entries.en: After his death, his son remained on frontier garrison duty.
entries.literal: After he died, his son remained in frontier garrison service.

entries.zh: 四十一年，金川平。
entries.en: In Qianlong 41 (1776), Jinchuan was pacified.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year, Jinchuan was pacified.

entries.zh: 元俊部將張芝元請於阿桂，謂元俊有功無罪，徒以忤專閫被羅織，語甚切。
entries.en: Yuanjun's subordinate Zhang Zhiyuan pleaded with Agui that Yuanjun had served with distinction and committed no crime, having been framed only for crossing the supreme commander. His appeal was passionate.
entries.literal: Yuanjun's subordinate general Zhang Zhiyuan appealed to Agui, saying Yuanjun had merit and no guilt, and had been framed only because he had offended the supreme commander. His words were very forceful.

entries.zh: 阿桂為疏請，赦其子還。
entries.en: Agui memorialized on his behalf, and the emperor pardoned his son and allowed him to come home.
entries.literal: Agui memorialized on his behalf, and the emperor pardoned his son and allowed him to return.

entries.zh: 三十七年，師攻革布​​什咱，元俊請於桂林，分兵為五道：一自郭宗濟野宗攻木巴拉博租；
entries.en: In Qianlong 37 (1772), during the campaign against Gepusizhai, Yuanjun proposed to Guilin a five-pronged plan: one column from Guozongjiyezong against Mubalabozu;
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, as the army attacked Gepusizhai, Yuanjun requested of Guilin to divide the forces into five routes: one from Guozongjiyezong to attack Mubalabozu;

entries.zh: 一自章谷渡河夾攻，俾賊前後受敵，兩軍既合，先據默資溝，截金川來路，進取吉地官寨；
entries.en: one to cross the river at Zhanggu and pinch the enemy from both sides, then unite, seize Mozigou to sever Jinchuan's supply line, and advance on the Jidi chieftain's stockade;
entries.literal: one to cross the river from Zhanggu and attack from both sides, so that the rebels would be caught between enemies front and rear; once the two armies joined, they would first occupy Mozigou, cut off the route from Jinchuan, and advance to take the Jidi official stockade;

entries.zh: 一自巴旺之高石、嘉舉諸山，分道攻薩瑪多監藏布覺，取吉地；
entries.en: one from the Gaoshi and Jiaju heights in Bawang, splitting to strike Samaduojianzangbujue and capture Jidi;
entries.literal: one from the mountains of Gaoshi and Jiaju in Bawang, dividing into routes to attack Samaduojianzangbujue and take Jidi;

entries.zh: 一自茂紐攻沙沖；
entries.en: one from Maoniu against Shachong;
entries.literal: one from Maoniu to attack Shachong;

entries.zh: 一自喀勒塔爾攻黨哩，會兵取丹東。
entries.en: one from Kaleta'er against Dangli, then converging to take Dandong.
entries.literal: one from Kaleta'er to attack Dangli, then combining forces to take Dandong.

entries.zh: 策定，元俊及游擊吳錦江等自章谷渡河據格藏橋，哈青阿、天佑出郭宗濟野宗，兩隊軍夾攻，賊驚潰，遂克木巴拉博租、薩瑪多監藏布覺諸地。
entries.en: The plan adopted, Yuanjun and Brigade Commander Wu Jinjiang forded the river at Zhanggu and seized Gezang Bridge while Ha Qing'a and Tianyou advanced from Guozongjiyezong. The two columns caught the rebels in a pincer; the enemy broke and fled, and Mubalabozu, Samaduojianzangbujue, and neighboring positions were taken.
entries.literal: Once the plan was settled, Yuanjun and Brigade Commander Wu Jinjiang and others crossed the river from Zhanggu and occupied Gezang Bridge. Ha Qing'a and Tianyou marched out from Guozongjiyezong. The two columns attacked from both sides; the rebels panicked and fled, and Mubalabozu, Samaduojianzangbujue, and other places were captured.

entries.zh: 進克吉地官寨及默資溝。
entries.en: They went on to capture the Jidi chieftain's stockade and Mozigou.
entries.literal: They advanced and captured the Jidi official stockade and Mozigou.

entries.zh: 參將常泰等克黨哩，都司李天貴等克沙沖，元俊复克丹東。
entries.en: Regimental Commander Chang Tai took Dangli, Company Commander Li Tiangui seized Shachong, and Yuanjun captured Dandong as well.
entries.literal: Regimental Commander Chang Tai and others captured Dangli; Company Commander Li Tiangui and others captured Shachong; Yuanjun again captured Dandong.

entries.zh: 复革布什咱地三百餘裡，民戶二千餘。
entries.en: More than three hundred li of Gepusizhai territory and over two thousand households were restored.
entries.literal: More than three hundred li of Gepusizhai territory and more than two thousand households were recovered.

entries.zh: 張芝元，四川清溪人。
entries.en: Zhang Zhiyuan came from Qingxi in Sichuan.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan was a native of Qingxi in Sichuan.

entries.zh: 以千總從副將軍明亮徵金川有功，積官至越巂營參將。
entries.en: Serving as a company commander (qianzong) under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
entries.literal: As a company commander (qianzong) he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.

entries.zh: 金川酋以番僧诇軍事，芝元言於明亮曰：「軍事每為賊知，非去其諜，滅賊無日矣。」
entries.en: The Jinchuan chieftain used tribal monks to spy on the army. Zhiyuan told Mingliang: "The enemy always knows our moves. Unless we cut off their intelligence, we will never defeat them."
entries.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain used tribal monks to spy on military affairs. Zhiyuan said to Mingliang: "Our operations are always known to the enemy. Unless we eliminate their spies, there will be no day of victory over the rebels."

entries.zh: 會大風雪，明亮命芝元率數十人偽若以他事出者，宿番僧寺中。
entries.en: During a blizzard, Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to take several dozen men, pretending to be out on other business, and lodge at the tribal monks' temple.
entries.literal: A great wind and snowstorm came. Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to lead several dozen men, pretending to go out on other business, and lodge in the tribal monks' temple.

entries.zh: 芝元故通番語，與僧飲甚歡，僧醉眠，芝元出寺聚柴焚之，僧皆死。
entries.en: Zhiyuan already spoke the tribal tongue. He drank freely with the monks; when they passed out, he slipped outside, piled firewood against the temple, and set it ablaze. Every monk inside died.
entries.literal: Zhiyuan already knew the tribal language. He drank merrily with the monks; when they fell drunk asleep, he went out of the temple, gathered firewood, and burned it. All the monks died.

entries.zh: 賊諜斷，因招降其眾。
entries.en: With the enemy's spy network broken, he was able to induce many rebels to surrender.
entries.literal: The rebels' intelligence network was severed, and he was thus able to induce their followers to surrender.

entries.zh: 尋從成都將軍特成額駐兵江卡，捕夾壩，圍本肯賊寨，焚其碉，斃賊甚眾，擢懋功協副將。
entries.en: He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.

entries.zh: 台灣林爽文為亂，芝元率屯練降番佐軍。
entries.en: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen in support of the campaign.
entries.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to assist the army.

entries.zh: 參贊海蘭察等分攻大埔林、中林、大埔尾三莊，芝元為策應。
entries.en: Campaign Adviser Hailancha and others split forces against the three villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei while Zhiyuan provided supporting action.
entries.literal: Campaign Adviser Hailancha and others divided forces to attack the three villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei; Zhiyuan served as supporting force.

entries.zh: 賊據小半天山，將軍福康安等自前山進，芝元與領隊大臣普爾普領兵別為一隊，夜半先發，繞大山夾攻賊後。
entries.en: The rebels held Xiaobantian Hill. General Fukang'an advanced from the front while Zhiyuan and Lead Commissioner Pu'erpu led a separate column that set out at midnight, swung around the mountain, and struck the enemy from the rear.
entries.literal: The rebels held Xiaobantian Hill. General Fukang'an and others advanced from the front hills. Zhiyuan and Lead Commissioner Pu'erpu led a separate column, setting out first at midnight and circling the great mountain to attack the rebels from the rear in a pincer.

entries.zh: 黎明，諸軍同抵山麓，攀援上，賊力拒，芝元先登，拔其柵，斬獲無算，並堵賊去路。
entries.en: At dawn the columns converged at the foot of the hill and climbed under fire. Zhiyuan was first over the top, tore down the palisade, killed and captured without number, and sealed off the enemy's escape route.
entries.literal: At dawn all the armies reached the foot of the hill together, climbed up, and the rebels resisted fiercely. Zhiyuan was first to ascend, pulled up their palisade, killed and captured beyond counting, and also blocked the rebels' escape route.

entries.zh: 未幾，爽文就擒。
entries.en: Before long, Shuangwen was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: Before long, Shuangwen was captured.

entries.zh: 台灣平，擢建昌鎮總兵，圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣。
entries.en: After Taiwan was pacified, he was promoted to regional commander of Jianchang, his portrait was enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was numbered among the first twenty meritorious officials.
entries.literal: When Taiwan was pacified, he was promoted to regional commander of Jianchang, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first twenty meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 尋調松潘鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to regional commander of Songpan.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.

entries.zh: 廓爾喀掠西藏濟嚨、聶拉木，上命芝元率屯練降番往討之。
entries.en: When Gurkhas raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet, the emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen against them.
entries.literal: Gurkhas raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet. The emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to attack them.

entries.zh: 芝元至，值大雪，山谷皆滿。
entries.en: Zhiyuan arrived in the midst of a blizzard that had buried the valleys in snow.
entries.literal: When Zhiyuan arrived, a heavy snowfall had filled the valleys.

entries.zh: 芝元手大刀指揮，士卒皆感激用命，賊敗走。
entries.en: Zhiyuan led from the front with a broadsword in hand; his men, stirred to gratitude, fought with all they had, and the enemy broke and fled.
entries.literal: Zhiyuan wielded a broadsword in hand to direct operations; the soldiers, moved with gratitude, obeyed with all their strength, and the enemy fled in defeat.

entries.zh: 廓爾喀再叛，芝元偕提督成德督兵攻聶拉木，守拍甲嶺隘口斷賊援，聶拉木遂下；
entries.en: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan and Regional Commander Chengde assaulted Nyalam, held the pass at Paijialing to sever enemy reinforcements, and Nyalam fell;
entries.literal: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan together with Regional Commander Chengde directed troops to attack Nyalam, held the pass at Paijialing to cut off enemy reinforcements, and Nyalam was taken;

entries.zh: 乘勝攻濟嚨，复克之，賊懼，乞降。
entries.en: then pressed the attack to Jilong and retook it as well. The enemy, terrified, sued for peace.
entries.literal: pressing the victory to attack Jilong, recapturing it as well; the enemy grew fearful and begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒。
entries.en: He died soon afterward.
entries.literal: Before long, he died.

entries.zh: 五十八年，論平定廓爾喀功，再圖形紫光閣，列後十五功臣。
entries.en: In Qianlong 58 (1793), when honors were awarded for pacifying the Gurkhas, his portrait was again enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor and he was numbered among the later fifteen meritorious officials.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when the merit of pacifying the Gurkhas was assessed, his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the later fifteen meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 董天弼，字霖蒼，順天大興人。
entries.en: Dong Tianbi, styled Lincang, came from Daxing in Shuntian.
entries.literal: Dong Tianbi, courtesy name Lincang, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.

entries.zh: 自武進士授四川提標前營守備。
entries.en: Having passed the military jinshi examination, he was appointed garrison commander of the Forward Battalion of the Sichuan Provincial Standard.
entries.literal: As a military jinshi he was appointed garrison commander of the Forward Battalion of the Sichuan Provincial Standard.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，師徵金川，天弼在軍有功。
entries.en: In the early Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Tianbi distinguished himself in the field.
entries.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Tianbi served with merit.

entries.zh: 累遷維​​州協副將。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to deputy vice general of the Weizhou Brigade.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy vice general of the Weizhou Brigade.

entries.zh: 金川酋郎卡攻丹壩土司，天弼偕游擊宋元俊諭郎卡歸所掠，毀所築碉，兵罷，遷松潘鎮總兵。
entries.en: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Danba chieftain, Tianbi and Brigade Commander Song Yuanjun ordered Langka to restore what he had seized and demolish the watchtowers he had built. After the campaign, Tianbi was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.
entries.literal: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Danba chieftain, Tianbi together with Brigade Commander Song Yuanjun instructed Langka to return what he had seized and destroy the watchtowers he had built. When the campaign ended, Tianbi was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.

entries.zh: 旋擢四川提督。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
entries.literal: He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 郭羅克部劫西藏入貢喇嘛，上命天弼按治，未得其渠，詔責其苟且。
entries.en: When Golok tribesmen robbed Tibetan tribute-bearing lamas, the emperor ordered Tianbi to investigate and punish them. He failed to capture the ringleaders, and an edict censured his half-hearted effort.
entries.literal: The Golok tribes robbed Tibetan tribute-bearing lamas. The emperor ordered Tianbi to investigate and punish them, but he failed to capture the ringleaders, and an edict rebuked his perfunctory effort.

entries.zh: 三十五年，小金川土司澤旺子僧格桑為亂，攻鄂克什土司色達克拉，圍其寨。
entries.en: In Qianlong 35 (1770), Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rebelled, attacked the Ekezhi chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his stockade.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rebelled, attacked the Ekezhi chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his stockade.

entries.zh: 天弼督兵駐達木巴宗，檄僧格桑斂兵退色達克拉，以其寨糧盡，乞徙達木巴宗。
entries.en: Tianbi stationed troops at Damubazong and ordered Senggesang to withdraw from Sedakela. With the stockade's provisions exhausted, Sedakela pleaded to relocate to Damubazong.
entries.literal: Tianbi directed troops stationed at Damubazong and ordered Senggesang to withdraw from Sedakela. Because the stockade's provisions were exhausted, Sedakela begged to relocate to Damubazong.

entries.zh: 天弼與總督阿爾泰議留兵戍焉。
entries.en: Tianbi and Governor-General Altai agreed to leave a garrison there.
entries.literal: Tianbi and Governor-General Altai agreed to leave troops to garrison the place.

entries.zh: 三十六年，僧格桑复圍達木巴宗，並略木耳宗、巴朗拉諸地。
entries.en: In Qianlong 36 (1771), Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and overran Mu'erzong, Balangla, and other positions.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and also seized Mu'erzong, Balangla, and other places.

entries.zh: 天弼自打箭爐出邊，徵省標及松潘、維州諸鎮協兵，行至眠龍岡，賊已得巴朗拉，築碉卡為久守計，且斷我兵路。
entries.en: Tianbi marched out from Dartsedo, mobilizing provincial standard troops and forces from Songpan and Weizhou. At Mianlonggang he found the rebels already holding Balangla, fortifying watchtowers and blockhouses for a long defense, and severing his line of advance.
entries.literal: Tianbi marched out from the frontier at Dartsedo, mobilizing provincial standard troops and forces from the Songpan and Weizhou garrisons. When he reached Mianlonggang, the rebels had already taken Balangla, built watchtowers and blockhouses for a prolonged defense, and cut off our army's route.

entries.zh: 天弼議襲山神溝以解達木巴宗圍，尋將四百人自山神溝至德爾密，克碉七，賊竄走；
entries.en: Tianbi proposed a raid through Shanshengou to break the siege of Damubazong. He soon led four hundred men through Shanshengou to De'ermi, took seven watchtowers, and the rebels fled;
entries.literal: Tianbi proposed a raid through Shanshengou to relieve the siege of Damubazong. He soon led four hundred men from Shanshengou to De'ermi, captured seven watchtowers, and the rebels fled;

entries.zh: 再進取畢旺拉，賊乘霧來犯，土兵驚潰，德爾密、畢旺拉皆陷。
entries.en: then advanced on Biwangla. The rebels struck through the fog; the native troops panicked and broke, and both De'ermi and Biwangla were lost.
entries.literal: advancing again to take Biwangla. The rebels took advantage of fog to attack; the native soldiers panicked and fled, and both De'ermi and Biwangla fell.

entries.zh: 天弼疏請罪，上以天弼所將兵本少，總督阿爾泰不預策應援，宥其罪，諭以「當奪勉。
entries.en: Tianbi memorialized asking to be punished. The emperor noted that Tianbi's force had been small to begin with and that Governor-General Altai had failed to plan supporting relief, and pardoned him with the admonition: "You must strive to redeem yourself.
entries.literal: Tianbi memorialized requesting punishment. The emperor considered that Tianbi's force had originally been small and that Governor-General Altai had failed to plan supporting relief, and pardoned his offense, instructing him: "You must strive to redeem yourself.

entries.zh: 再不努力，獲罪滋重矣」。
entries.en: Fail again, and your guilt will only deepen."
entries.literal: If you fail to exert yourself again, your guilt will grow all the heavier."

entries.zh: 天弼復將五百人自木坪陟堯磧，順山攻甲金達對面山梁，取碉二。
entries.en: Tianbi again led five hundred men from Muping up Yaoji and along the ridge opposite Jajianda, taking two watchtowers.
entries.literal: Tianbi again led five hundred men from Muping up Yaoji, and along the mountain attacked the ridge opposite Jajianda, capturing two watchtowers.

entries.zh: 天弼以鄂克什牛廠當要道，分兵殲守廠賊，駐軍其地；
entries.en: Seeing that the Ekezhi cattle station lay on a vital route, Tianbi detached troops to wipe out the rebels holding it and stationed his force there;
entries.literal: Tianbi considered the Ekezhi cattle station to lie on a vital route, divided his force to annihilate the rebels guarding the station, and stationed troops there;

entries.zh: 乘勝上下截擊，木坪、鄂克什諸土司錯壤，要隘皆為我軍有。
entries.en: then pressed the advantage with strikes from above and below. With the Muping and Ekezhi chieftains' territories interlocking, every strategic pass fell to our forces.
entries.literal: pressing the victory to strike from above and below. The chieftains of Muping, Ekezhi, and neighboring territories interlocked in their domains, and all the strategic passes came into our army's possession.

entries.zh: 未幾，賊复襲據牛廠。
entries.en: Before long the rebels raided and retook the cattle station.
entries.literal: Before long, the rebels again raided and seized the cattle station.

entries.zh: 上以阿爾泰師久無功，奪官。
entries.en: The emperor stripped Altai of rank for his army's prolonged failure.
entries.literal: The emperor stripped Altai of his office because his army had long achieved no success.

entries.zh: 因責：「天弼始終貽誤，與阿爾泰同罪，奪官，留軍中充伍。
entries.en: He also decreed: "Tianbi has bungled from start to finish and shares Altai's guilt. Strip him of rank and keep him in the ranks as a common soldier.
entries.literal: He also rebuked: "Tianbi has from first to last caused delay and error, and shares Altai's guilt. Strip him of office and keep him in the army as a common soldier.

entries.zh: 如更退縮，正軍法。」
entries.en: Retreat again, and military law will be applied."
entries.literal: If he retreats again, apply military law."

entries.zh: 尋命下成都獄。
entries.en: He was soon ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.

entries.zh: 詔未至，天弼以甲金達山峻不可上，求間道，得溝在兩崖間。
entries.en: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi found Jajianda Hill too steep to climb and searched for a hidden route, discovering a ravine between two cliffs.
entries.literal: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi found Jajianda Hill too steep to ascend and sought a hidden route, discovering a ravine between two cliffs.

entries.zh: 會大風雪，天弼率兵自溝中潛度，遂至達木巴宗，擊僧格桑色達克拉；
entries.en: During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;
entries.literal: A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;

entries.zh: 潰圍出，並克木耳宗，迎溫福師與會。
entries.en: broke out of the encirclement, also captured Mu'erzong, and linked up with Wenfu's army.
entries.literal: breaking out of the encirclement, also captured Mu'erzong, and joined Wenfu's army.

entries.zh: 上聞，命貸死，留軍中。
entries.en: When word reached the emperor, he commuted the death sentence and kept Tianbi with the army.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard this, he ordered his death sentence commuted and kept him in the army.

entries.zh: 阿桂令天弼監火藥軍械。
entries.en: Agui put Tianbi in charge of gunpowder and ordnance.
entries.literal: Agui ordered Tianbi to supervise gunpowder and military equipment.

entries.zh: 三十七年，師克資哩，阿桂令天弼將五百人駐焉。
entries.en: In Qianlong 37 (1772), after the army captured Zili, Agui ordered Tianbi to garrison the place with five hundred men.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army captured Zili, Agui ordered Tianbi to lead five hundred men to garrison it.

entries.zh: 尋予副將銜，授重慶鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was soon granted vice general's rank and appointed regional commander of Chongqing.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was granted the rank of vice general and appointed regional commander of Chongqing.

entries.zh: 命督兵赴曾頭溝，進至梭磨，梭磨土婦請以千人從。
entries.en: He was ordered to lead troops to Zengtougou and on to Suomo, where the Suomo chieftainess offered a thousand warriors to follow him.
entries.literal: He was ordered to direct troops to Zengtougou and advance to Suomo. The Suomo tribal chieftainess requested to follow with a thousand men.

entries.zh: 事聞，賜花翎。
entries.en: When this was reported, the emperor awarded him a peacock feather.
entries.literal: When this was reported, he was granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 天弼督兵攻堪卓溝，自間道出納云達，深入賊境五十餘裡，克山樑三，破碉卡三十餘、木城三。
entries.en: Tianbi assaulted Kanzhuogou, emerging by a hidden route at Nayunda and penetrating more than fifty li into enemy territory. He took three ridges and destroyed over thirty watchtower blockhouses and three wooden forts.
entries.literal: Tianbi directed troops to attack Kanzhuogou, emerging by a hidden route at Nayunda, penetrating more than fifty li into enemy territory, capturing three mountain ridges, and breaking more than thirty watchtower blockhouses and three wooden forts.

entries.zh: 迎溫福師會於布朗郭宗，克大板昭、木丫寨，得碉三十六、卡十六。
entries.en: He linked up with Wenfu at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhai and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six watchtowers and sixteen blockhouses.
entries.literal: He joined Wenfu's army at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhai and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six watchtowers and sixteen blockhouses.

entries.zh: 上以溫福已得布朗郭宗進克底木達，天弼所克不過空寨，疏語頗鋪張，手敕戒之。
entries.en: The emperor noted that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced to capture Dimuda, while Tianbi had seized only empty stockades; his memorial overstated the achievement, and the emperor personally admonished him.
entries.literal: The emperor considered that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced to capture Dimuda, while what Tianbi had captured were only empty stockades; his memorial language was rather inflated, and the emperor personally wrote an edict admonishing him.

entries.zh: 尋授領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Lead Commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Lead Commissioner.

entries.zh: 三十八年，復為四川提督。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 時小金川已定，溫福督師進討大金川，令天弼以五百人守底木達。
entries.en: Lesser Jinchuan had by then been pacified. Wenfu led the advance against Greater Jinchuan and ordered Tianbi to hold Dimuda with five hundred men.
entries.literal: Lesser Jinchuan had by then been pacified. Wenfu supervised the army in advancing against Greater Jinchuan and ordered Tianbi to hold Dimuda with five hundred men.

entries.zh: 溫福進駐木果木，號大營；
entries.en: Wenfu advanced to Muguomu, designated the Great Camp;
entries.literal: Wenfu advanced to station at Muguomu, which was called the Great Camp;

entries.zh: 底木達當賊來路，為要隘。
entries.en: Dimuda lay on the enemy's line of approach and was a vital pass.
entries.literal: Dimuda lay on the enemy's line of approach and was a strategic pass.

entries.zh: 溫福檄三百人益大營，又去其後援。
entries.en: Wenfu requisitioned three hundred of Tianbi's men for the Great Camp, stripping him of his rear support.
entries.literal: Wenfu requisitioned three hundred men to reinforce the Great Camp, thereby removing Tianbi's rear support.

entries.zh: 時溫福以軍屢勝，不以賊為意。
entries.en: Wenfu, flush with repeated victories, paid the enemy little heed.
entries.literal: At the time Wenfu, because the army had won repeated victories, paid the enemy little heed.

entries.zh: 金川頭人七圖葛拉爾思甲布等以千餘人詐降，溫福使與廝養雜處，因誘諸降人為變，諗底木達兵弱無後援，六月乙丑朔，潛自山後擁眾攻底木達，天弼率所部二百人抽刀力戰，至夜半，賊以鳥槍數百環擊，殺之。
entries.en: The Jinchuan headmen Qitu Gela'ersijia and others feigned surrender with over a thousand men. Wenfu quartered them among the servants, then incited the surrendered men to revolt. Learning that Dimuda was thinly held and unsupported, on the first day of the sixth month they secretly massed behind the hills and struck Dimuda. Tianbi led his two hundred men in a desperate blade fight. By midnight the rebels ringed them with hundreds of muskets and killed him.
entries.literal: The Jinchuan headmen Qitu Gela'ersijia and others feigned surrender with more than a thousand men. Wenfu had them mixed among the servants and attendants, then incited the surrendered men to revolt. Learning that Dimuda was weakly garrisoned and without rear support, on the first day of the sixth month they secretly gathered a force from behind the hills to attack Dimuda. Tianbi led his two hundred men, drawing blades to fight with all their strength. By midnight the rebels surrounded them with several hundred muskets and killed him.

entries.zh: 越九日，劫大營，溫福亦死焉。
entries.en: Nine days later they overran the Great Camp, and Wenfu was killed as well.
entries.literal: Nine days later they raided the Great Camp, and Wenfu also died.

entries.zh: 上先命天弼駐丹壩，旋命移駐布朗郭宗，軍中傳賊來犯。
entries.en: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to garrison Danba, then to move to Bulangguozong. Rumors spread through camp that the enemy was coming.
entries.literal: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to garrison Danba, then ordered him to move to Bulangguozong. In camp it was rumored that the enemy was coming to attack.

entries.zh: 時天弼方屯美諾，上命奪官逮治。
entries.en: Tianbi was then encamped at Meinuo. The emperor ordered him stripped of rank and arrested.
entries.literal: At the time Tianbi was encamped at Meinuo. The emperor ordered his dismissal and arrest.

entries.zh: 總督劉秉恬疏言：「天弼自美諾馳赴底木達，途遇賊，右脅中槍死。」
entries.en: Governor-General Liu Bingtian reported: "Tianbi galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, met the enemy on the road, took a musket ball in the right side, and died."
entries.literal: Governor-General Liu Bingtian memorialized: "Tianbi galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, encountered the enemy on the way, was struck by a musket ball in the right side, and died."

entries.zh: 仍以貽誤軍事籍其家，戍其子舉人聯伊犁。
entries.en: Nevertheless, for military negligence his property was confiscated and his son, the juren Lian, was exiled to Yili.
entries.literal: Nevertheless, for having caused military delay and error, his household property was confiscated and his son, the juren Lian, was exiled to Yili.

entries.zh: 五十二年春，水師提督黃仕簡、陸路提督任承恩先後赴援。
entries.en: In the spring of Qianlong 52 (1787), Naval Regional Commander Huang Shijian and Army Regional Commander Ren Chengen arrived in succession to reinforce.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fifty-second year, Naval Regional Commander Huang Shijian and Army Regional Commander Ren Chengen successively came to reinforce.

entries.zh: 大紀出攻諸羅，克之，即移軍守諸羅。
entries.en: Daji marched out against Zhuluo, captured it, and immediately shifted his army to hold the city.
entries.literal: Daji marched out to attack Zhuluo, captured it, and immediately moved his army to defend Zhuluo.

entries.zh: 旋以守府城功，賜花翎。
entries.en: For his defense of the prefectural city, he was soon awarded a peacock feather.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, for his merit in defending the prefectural city, he was granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 上以仕簡、承恩師久無功，授總督常青將軍，渡台灣視師。
entries.en: With Shijian's and Chengen's forces stalled, the emperor appointed Governor-General Chang Qing as commanding general and sent him to Taiwan to take charge.
entries.literal: Because Shijian's and Chengen's armies had long achieved no success, the emperor appointed Governor-General Chang Qing general and sent him across to Taiwan to supervise the campaign.

entries.zh: 爽文攻諸羅，自二月至四月凡十至，大紀督游擊楊起麟、守備邱能成等出戰，殺賊數千。
entries.en: Shuangwen assaulted Zhuluo ten times between the second and fourth months. Daji led Brigade Commander Yang Qilin, Garrison Commander Qiu Nengcheng, and others in sorties that killed several thousand rebels.
entries.literal: Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo ten times from the second to the fourth month. Daji directed Brigade Commander Yang Qilin, Garrison Commander Qiu Nengcheng, and others to go out and fight, killing several thousand rebels.

entries.zh: 爽文之徒張慎徽偽降，大紀察其詐，置諸法。
entries.en: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender; Daji saw through the ruse and had him executed.
entries.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender; Daji detected the deception and punished him by law.

entries.zh: 台灣諸府縣皆編竹為城，不耐攻，大紀以忠義率兵民誓堅守。
entries.en: Taiwan's prefectures and districts all had bamboo-woven walls that could not withstand assault. Daji rallied soldiers and civilians with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, swearing to hold firm.
entries.literal: The prefectures and districts of Taiwan all had walls woven of bamboo that could not withstand assault. Daji led soldiers and civilians with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, swearing to hold firm.

entries.zh: 上嘉大紀勞，賜荷包、奶餅，下部議敘。
entries.en: The emperor praised Daji's exertions, sent him a purse and milk cakes, and referred his merits to the ministries for commendation.
entries.literal: The emperor praised Daji's exertions, granted him a purse and milk cakes, and referred the matter to the ministries for commendation.

entries.zh: 六月，授福建陸路提督，仍兼領台灣總兵。
entries.en: In the sixth month he was appointed Army Regional Commander of Fujian while retaining his post as regional commander of Taiwan.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Army Regional Commander of Fujian while still concurrently holding the post of regional commander of Taiwan.

entries.zh: 鹽水港者，諸羅通府城糧道也，賊來攻，大紀力御之。
entries.en: Yanshui Harbor was the grain route linking Zhuluo to the prefectural city. When the rebels attacked it, Daji fought them off with all his strength.
entries.literal: Yanshui Harbor was the grain route connecting Zhuluo to the prefectural city. When the rebels came to attack, Daji resisted them with all his strength.

entries.zh: 上促常青赴援，予大紀壯健巴圖魯名號，參贊軍務。
entries.en: The emperor pressed Chang Qing to march to the relief, granted Daji the title of Brave and Strong Batur, and appointed him campaign adviser.
entries.literal: The emperor urged Chang Qing to go to the relief, granted Daji the title of Brave and Strong Batur, and made him campaign adviser.

entries.zh: 八月，上以常青衰老不能辦賊，命福康安為將軍，仍令大紀參贊；
entries.en: In the eighth month, finding Chang Qing too aged to suppress the rebels, the emperor appointed Fukang'an as general while keeping Daji as campaign adviser;
entries.literal: In the eighth month, because Chang Qing was aged and unable to deal with the rebels, the emperor appointed Fukang'an as general and still ordered Daji to serve as campaign adviser;

entries.zh: 而常青令總兵魏大斌援諸羅，賊邀諸途，退駐鹿仔草；
entries.en: meanwhile Chang Qing ordered Regional Commander Wei Dabin to reinforce Zhuluo; the rebels blocked him at every turn, and he fell back to Luzicao;
entries.literal: but Chang Qing ordered Regional Commander Wei Dabin to reinforce Zhuluo; the rebels intercepted him at every turn, and he withdrew to station at Luzicao;

entries.zh: 復令總兵蔡攀龍援諸羅，大紀出戰，迎入城共守。
entries.en: Chang Qing then ordered Regional Commander Cai Panlong to reinforce Zhuluo. Daji fought his way out and escorted him into the city to defend it together.
entries.literal: Chang Qing again ordered Regional Commander Cai Panlong to reinforce Zhuluo. Daji went out to fight and welcomed him into the city to defend together.

entries.zh: 上移大紀水師提督，而以陸路提督授攀龍。
entries.en: The emperor promoted Daji to Naval Regional Commander and gave the Army Regional Commander post to Panlong.
entries.literal: The emperor transferred Daji to Naval Regional Commander and gave the Army Regional Commander post to Panlong.

entries.zh: 十一月，加大紀太子少保。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Daji was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Daji was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 上以諸羅被圍久，縣民困守，奮力向義，更縣名為嘉義。
entries.en: Because Zhuluo had endured a long siege and its people had fought with loyal resolve, the emperor renamed the county Jiayi, "Praise of Righteousness."
entries.literal: Because Zhuluo had been besieged for a long time and the county people had endured the siege and exerted themselves in loyalty and righteousness, the emperor changed the county name to Jiayi.

entries.zh: 賊攻城益急，上密諭大紀：「不必堅執與城存亡，如遇事急，可率兵力戰，出城再圖進取。」
entries.en: As the siege intensified, the emperor secretly told Daji: "You need not die with the city. If matters grow desperate, lead your troops in a fighting breakout and plan your next move from outside."
entries.literal: As the rebels pressed the siege ever harder, the emperor secretly instructed Daji: "You need not insist on perishing with the city. If matters grow urgent, you may lead your troops in fierce battle, leave the city, and plan a renewed advance."

entries.zh: 大紀疏言：「諸羅居台灣南北之中，縣城四周積土植竹，環以深壕，壕上為短垣，置砲，防衛堅固。
entries.en: Daji replied: "Zhuluo lies at the heart of Taiwan between north and south. The county seat is ringed with earthen ramparts and bamboo palisades, a deep moat, and a low wall mounted with cannon—the defenses are formidable.
entries.literal: Daji memorialized: "Zhuluo lies at the center between north and south Taiwan. The county city is surrounded by piled earth and planted bamboo, encircled by a deep moat; atop the moat is a low wall with cannon emplaced—the defenses are solid.

entries.zh: 一旦棄之而去，為賊所得，慮賊勢益張，鹽水港運道亦不能守。
entries.en: Abandon it now and the rebels will take it, their power will swell, and we will lose the supply route through Yanshui Harbor as well.
entries.literal: If we abandon it in a moment and it falls to the rebels, I fear the rebel power will grow all the stronger and the supply route through Yanshui Harbor also cannot be held.

entries.zh: 且城廂內外居民及各莊避難入城者共四萬餘人，助餉協守，以至於今。
entries.en: Moreover, more than forty thousand residents and refugees from surrounding villages have helped supply the garrison and fought alongside us until now.
entries.literal: Moreover, residents inside and outside the city walls and refugees from the various villages who entered the city total more than forty thousand. They have helped supply provisions and joined in the defense down to this day.

entries.zh: 不忍將此數万生靈付逆賊毒手！
entries.en: I cannot abandon these tens of thousands of lives to the rebels!
entries.literal: I cannot bear to deliver these tens of thousands of lives into the murderous hands of the rebel bandits!

entries.zh: 惟有竭力保守，以待援兵。」
entries.en: I can only hold on with all my strength and await relief."
entries.literal: I can only exert all my strength to hold and defend, awaiting relief troops."

entries.zh: 上手詔謂：「所奏忠肝義，披覽為之墮淚！
entries.en: The emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears!
entries.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict saying: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears as I read it!

entries.zh: 大紀被圍日久，心志益堅，勉勵兵民，忍飢固守，惟知以國事民生為重。
entries.en: Besieged for so long, Daji's resolve has only hardened. He rallies soldiers and civilians, endures hunger, and holds firm—thinking only of the state and the people's welfare.
entries.literal: Daji has been besieged for a long time, yet his resolve grows ever firmer. He encourages soldiers and civilians, enduring hunger to hold firm, knowing only to place state affairs and the people's livelihood above all.

entries.zh: 古之名將，何以加之？」
entries.en: What general of old could surpass this?"
entries.literal: What ancient famous general could surpass this?"

entries.zh: 因封為一等義勇伯，世襲罔替，並命浙江巡撫琅玕予其家白金萬，促福康安赴援。
entries.en: He ennobled Daji as Baron of First Rank Yiyong with perpetual hereditary succession, ordered Zhejiang Governor Langgan to grant his family ten thousand taels of silver, and pressed Fukang'an to march to the relief.
entries.literal: He therefore ennobled him as Baron of First Rank Yiyong, with perpetual hereditary succession, and also ordered Zhejiang Governor Langgan to grant his family ten thousand taels of silver and urged Fukang'an to hurry to the relief.

entries.zh: 柴大紀，浙江江山人。
entries.en: Chai Daji came from Jiangshan in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Chai Daji was a native of Jiangshan in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 自武進士授福建守備。
entries.en: Having passed the military jinshi examination, he was appointed garrison commander in Fujian.
entries.literal: As a military jinshi he was appointed garrison commander in Fujian.

entries.zh: 累擢至海壇鎮總兵，移台灣鎮。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to regional commander of Haitan and was then transferred to Taiwan.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Haitan and then transferred to Taiwan.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十一年十一月，林爽文亂起。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Qianlong 51 (1786), the Lin Shuangwen rebellion broke out.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign, the Lin Shuangwen rebellion broke out.

entries.zh: 爽文漳州人，徙彰化，所居村曰大里杙。
entries.en: Shuangwen was from Zhangzhou and had moved to Zhanghua; he lived in the village of Daliyi.
entries.literal: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou who had moved to Zhanghua; the village where he lived was called Daliyi.

entries.zh: 時奸民相聚，號天地會，漳州人莊煙為之魁，爽文與相結，謀為變。
entries.en: Wicked men had gathered in a secret society called the Heaven and Earth Society, led by Zhuang Yan of Zhangzhou. Shuangwen joined them and plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: At the time wicked men gathered together under the name Heaven and Earth Society; Zhuang Yan of Zhangzhou was their leader, and Shuangwen joined with them to plot rebellion.

entries.zh: 台灣知府孫景燧馳詣彰化，督知縣俞峻、副將赫生額、游擊耿世文捕治，焚數小村以怵之。
entries.en: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui rushed to Zhanghua and directed District Magistrate Yu Jun, Vice General He Sheng'e, and Brigade Commander Geng Shiwen to arrest the rebels, burning several villages to intimidate them.
entries.literal: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui hurried to Zhanghua and supervised District Magistrate Yu Jun, Vice General He Sheng'e, and Brigade Commander Geng Shiwen in arresting and punishing them, burning several small villages to intimidate them.

entries.zh: 爽文因民怨，夜糾其徒來襲，赫生額等皆戰死。
entries.en: Exploiting popular resentment, Shuangwen rallied his followers by night and struck; He Sheng'e and the others all fell in battle.
entries.literal: Shuangwen, exploiting popular resentment, gathered his followers by night to attack; He Sheng'e and the others all died in battle.

entries.zh: 明日，遂破彰化，景燧亦殉焉。
entries.en: The next day they overran Zhanghua, and Jingsui died defending it.
entries.literal: The next day they broke Zhanghua, and Jingsui also died for the cause.

entries.zh: 傍攻諸羅、鳳山，皆陷。
entries.en: They also struck Zhuluo and Fengshan on the flanks, and both cities fell.
entries.literal: They also attacked Zhuluo and Fengshan on the flanks, and both fell.

entries.zh: 大紀時以總兵守府城，賊分道來攻，大紀出駐鹽埕橋御之，擊沉賊舟數十，馘千餘。
entries.en: Daji was then regional commander defending the prefectural city. When the rebels attacked from several directions, he took position at Yancheng Bridge, sank dozens of rebel boats, and killed more than a thousand.
entries.literal: Daji was then regional commander defending the prefectural city. The rebels came to attack by separate routes. Daji went out to station at Yancheng Bridge to resist them, sinking several dozen rebel boats and beheading more than a thousand.

entries.zh: 列傳一百十六
entries.en: Biographies 116
entries.literal: Biographies 116

entries.zh: 伊勒圖，納喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Yi Leitu, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Yi Leitu, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，以世管佐領授三等侍衛，累遷鑲紅旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he entered service as Third Class Bodyguard through his hereditary company captaincy and rose to deputy military governor of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, by hereditary company captain he was appointed Third Class Bodyguard and was repeatedly promoted to deputy military governor of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.

entries.zh: 出駐烏魯木齊，移阿克蘇。
entries.en: Posted to the northwest, he garrisoned Urumqi and was later transferred to Aksu.
entries.literal: He went out to garrison Urumqi and was transferred to Aksu.

entries.zh: 三十二年，授伊犁參贊大臣，移喀什噶爾。
entries.en: In the thirty-second year of Qianlong he became assistant military governor at Ili and was moved to Kashgar.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Ili assistant military governor and transferred to Kashgar.

entries.zh: 內擢理籓院尚書，外授伊犁將軍。
entries.en: Promoted to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs at court, he was simultaneously appointed Ili general on the frontier.
entries.literal: He was promoted within to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and appointed without to Ili general.

entries.zh: 三十四年，師徵緬甸，授副將軍，從經略大學士傅恆分道進軍，緬甸人拒戛鳩江，築寨。
entries.en: In the thirty-fourth year, during the Burma campaign, he was made deputy commander and marched with Grand Secretary Fu Heng along a separate route; the Burmese held the Jiayu River line behind fortified stockades.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when the army campaigned against Burma, he was appointed deputy general; following Grand Secretary Fu Heng he advanced by separate routes; the Burmese blocked the Jiayu River and built stockades.

entries.zh: 伊勒圖偕參贊大臣阿里袞與戰，奪寨三，殺賊五千餘。
entries.en: Yi Leitu fought alongside Assistant Military Governor Aligun, took three stockades, and killed more than five thousand of the enemy.
entries.literal: Yi Leitu together with Assistant Military Governor Agui fought, captured three stockades, and killed more than five thousand rebels.

entries.zh: 師還，授兵部尚書。
entries.en: After the campaign he was appointed minister of war.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed minister of war.

entries.zh: 复外授伊犁將軍。
entries.en: He was again posted as Ili general on the frontier.
entries.literal: Again he was appointed without to Ili general.

entries.zh: 土爾扈特汗渥巴錫、台吉策伯克多爾濟等率所部三萬餘戶來歸，先期使至伊犁，具書通款。
entries.en: Torghut Khan Ubashi, Taiji Cebeke Duolji, and others led more than thirty thousand households of their people back to allegiance, having sent envoys ahead to Ili with letters of submission.
entries.literal: The Torghut khan Oboi, the taiji Cebeke Duolji, and others led more than thirty thousand households of their tribes to submit; beforehand envoys reached Ili with letters expressing goodwill.

entries.zh: 伊勒圖以聞，高宗命加意撫綏，俾得所。
entries.en: Yi Leitu reported the arrival to the throne, and the Qianlong Emperor ordered that they be settled with particular care.
entries.literal: Yi Leitu reported it; the Gaozong emperor ordered special care in pacification so they might find their place.

entries.zh: 於是土爾扈特部悉內附，哈薩克、布魯特兩​​部厄魯特降者日眾。
entries.en: The Torghuts were thus fully brought within the empire, and Oirats of the Kazakh and Burut tribes came over in growing numbers day by day.
entries.literal: Thereupon the entire Torghut tribe submitted within; among the Kazakh and Burut two tribes, Oirat submitters daily grew numerous.

entries.zh: 伊勒圖請增置佐領，俾領其眾，從之。
entries.en: Yi Leitu asked that additional company captaincies be created to command the new tribesmen, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: Yi Leitu requested additional company captains to lead their masses; it was approved.

entries.zh: 三十六年，左授參贊大臣，駐烏什，移塔爾巴哈台。
entries.en: In the thirty-sixth year he was reassigned as assistant military governor, first at Ushi and then at Tarbagatai.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred left to assistant military governor, garrisoned at Ushi, transferred to Tarbagatai.

entries.zh: 三十八年，复授伊犁將軍。
entries.en: In the thirty-eighth year he was again made Ili general.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was again appointed Ili general.

entries.zh: 兵部議禁鳥槍，伊勒圖以土爾扈特部新歸附，牧馬禦豺虎恃鳥槍，不當一體收禁。
entries.en: When the Ministry of War proposed a general ban on firearms, Yi Leitu argued that the newly submitted Torghuts relied on muskets to herd their horses and drive off predators, and should not be disarmed wholesale.
entries.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated prohibiting muskets; Yi Leitu argued that the Torghut tribe had newly submitted, herding horses and defending against jackals and tigers relied on muskets, and they should not all be confiscated alike.

entries.zh: 四十八年，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎。
entries.en: In the forty-eighth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
