entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

entries.zh: 五十年七月，卒，諡襄武，封一等伯，祀賢良祠。
entries.en: He died in the seventh month of the fiftieth year and was posthumously titled Xiangwu, created a first-class baron, and entered for worship in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fiftieth year he died; posthumous title Xiangwu, enfeoffed as first-class baron, worshipped in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.

entries.zh: 發帑金千，遣侍衛豐伸濟倫如伊犁賜奠。
entries.en: The court issued a thousand taels from the treasury and sent Bodyguard Fengshen Jilun to Ili to offer libations on the emperor's behalf.
entries.literal: A thousand taels from the treasury were issued; Bodyguard Fengshen Jilun was dispatched to Ili to confer funeral offerings.

entries.zh: 胡貴，字爾恆，福建同安人。
entries.en: Hu Gui, styled Erheng, came from Tong'an in Fujian.
entries.literal: Hu Gui, style name Erheng, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

entries.zh: 少有智略。
entries.en: Even as a young man he showed keen judgment and resourcefulness.
entries.literal: From youth he had intelligence and stratagem.

entries.zh: 入伍，稍遷水師提標右營千總。
entries.en: He enlisted and rose in due course to company commander in the Right Battalion of the naval commander's brigade.
entries.literal: He entered the army and was gradually promoted to company commander of the Right Battalion of the naval commander's standard.

entries.zh: 雍正六年，齎奏入都，世宗召入見。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he brought a memorial to the capital and was received in audience by the Yongzheng Emperor.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he carried a memorial to the capital; the Shizong emperor summoned him for an audience.

entries.zh: 再遷後營游擊。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to battalion commander of the Rear Battalion.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to battalion commander of the Rear Battalion.

entries.zh: 監修戰艦，出巡海，坐誤工，吏議當左授，上特宥之。
entries.en: While supervising warship repairs and patrolling at sea he was found negligent; the personnel office recommended demotion, but the emperor pardoned him.
entries.literal: Supervising repair of warships, on a sea patrol he was charged with delay in work; clerks judged he should be demoted; the emperor specially pardoned him.

entries.zh: 累遷江南蘇松鎮總兵。
entries.en: He rose in due course to regional commander of the Susong Garrison in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Susong Garrison in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 督運漕糧十萬轉海賑福建，道溫州鳳凰洋，颶作，損米五百餘，請出私財以償。
entries.en: Ordered to ship one hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute by sea to relieve famine in Fujian, he was caught in a typhoon off Wenzhou's Fenghuang Sea and lost more than five hundred piculs; he offered to make good the loss from his own purse.
entries.literal: Supervising transport of one hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute by sea to relieve Fujian, passing Fenghuang Sea off Wenzhou, a typhoon arose and more than five hundred piculs of grain were lost; he requested to pay compensation from private wealth.

entries.zh: 高宗諭曰：「冒險已可嘉，豈有復令出私財償米之理？」
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor replied: "Your willingness to brave the seas is praise enough—how could I ask you to make good the grain from your own funds?"
entries.literal: The Gaozong emperor instructed: "Taking risks is already praiseworthy—how could there be reason further to make him pay grain from private wealth?"

entries.zh: 命罷勿償。
entries.en: He ordered that the offer be declined and the matter closed.
entries.literal: He ordered the matter dropped and no compensation.

entries.zh: 旋坐廢弛當奪職，复特宥之。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was again found remiss in duty and liable to dismissal, and again the emperor spared him.
entries.literal: Soon after, charged with lax administration deserving dismissal from office, he was again specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 疏言：「本鎮春、秋兩哨，中營游擊司糧餉，奇兵營游擊職城守，例不出巡。
entries.en: He memorialized: "In this command's spring and autumn patrol seasons the Middle Battalion commander handles rations while the Odd Troops Battalion commander holds the city; by custom neither leaves post for sea patrol.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "This garrison's spring and autumn patrol seasons—the Middle Battalion battalion commander manages provisions, the Odd Troops Battalion battalion commander's duty is city defense; by precedent they do not go on patrol.

entries.zh: 惟既任水師，​​當知海道，應從眾出巡。
entries.en: Yet as naval officers they ought to know the sea lanes and should take part in the general patrols.
entries.literal: Yet having been assigned to the navy, they ought to know sea routes and should join the general patrol.

entries.zh: 陸路將士原改水師者，先令出海演試，如有膽略，量為改補。」
entries.en: Soldiers transferred from the army to the navy should first be sent to sea for trial; those who prove steady and bold may be confirmed in naval posts according to merit."
entries.literal: Land-force officers and soldiers originally transferred to the navy should first be ordered to go to sea for trial exercises; if they have courage and resource, appoint them to posts as appropriate."

entries.zh: 並從所請。
entries.en: The court approved every point.
entries.literal: All was granted as requested.

entries.zh: 崇明海漲，沒民廬。
entries.en: A tidal surge at Chongming drowned countless homes.
entries.literal: At Chongming the sea surged and submerged commoners' dwellings.

entries.zh: 召縣吏議賑，吏言當待請。
entries.en: He summoned the county officials to plan relief, but they said they must await imperial authorization.
entries.literal: He summoned county clerks to discuss relief; the clerks said they should wait for a request.

entries.zh: 貴曰：「民死在頃刻，豈能俟報？
entries.en: Hu said: "People are dying this very hour—how can we wait on paperwork?
entries.literal: Gui said: "The people die in an instant—how can we wait for a report?

entries.zh: 有譴吾任之。」
entries.en: If punishment follows, I alone will answer for it."
entries.literal: If there is punishment, I will bear it."

entries.zh: 即發倉以賑，令所屬為助，眾有難色，貴曰：「設官非以衛民乎？
entries.en: He opened the granaries at once and ordered his subordinates to help; when they hesitated he said, "Are we not put in office precisely to protect the people?
entries.literal: He immediately opened the granary for relief and ordered subordinates to assist; the crowd showed reluctance; Gui said: "Are offices not established to protect the people?

entries.zh: 賑不週，生它變，豈能免患？」
entries.en: If relief falls short and unrest follows, who among us will escape blame?"
entries.literal: If relief is not thorough, other troubles arise—how can we escape calamity?"

entries.zh: 疏請發帑金十八萬、倉穀二十八萬，並留漕米續賑，上深嘉之。
entries.en: He then memorialized for 180,000 taels from the treasury, 280,000 piculs from the public granaries, and retention of grain-transport rice for further relief; the emperor commended him warmly.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting disbursement of 180,000 taels from the treasury and 280,000 piculs from the granary, and also retaining grain tribute transport grain for continued relief; the emperor deeply praised it.

entries.zh: 歷廣東潮州、瓊州諸鎮，擢提督。
entries.en: After serving at the Chaozhou and Qiongzhou garrisons in Guangdong he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: He served successively at the garrisons of Chaozhou and Qiongzhou in Guangdong and was promoted to provincial naval commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 增城民王亮臣為亂，貴勒兵馳赴，分遣所屬防隘，扼賊走路。
entries.en: When Wang Liangchen of Zengcheng rose in revolt, Hu led his troops posthaste, posted detachments at the passes, and cut off the rebels' lines of retreat.
entries.literal: The commoner Wang Liangchen of Zengcheng raised a rebellion; Gui urged troops to rush there, dispatched subordinates to guard passes, and blocked the rebels' escape routes.

entries.zh: 總督阿里袞軍亦至，分道捕治，諸賊皆就擒。
entries.en: Governor-General Aligun's force arrived as well; operating on separate lines they rounded up the rebels until every band was taken.
entries.literal: Governor-General Agui's army also arrived; by separate routes they pursued and suppressed, and all rebels were captured.

entries.zh: 以失察自劾，貸勿問，仍敘勞。
entries.en: He impeached himself for having failed to detect the plot in time; the court waived punishment and still recorded his merit.
entries.literal: For failure of oversight he impeached himself; he was pardoned without inquiry and still given merit recognition.

entries.zh: 入覲，賜花翎。
entries.en: At court audience he was granted the peacock feather.
entries.literal: On entering audience he was awarded the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 移福建水師提督，復自浙江還廣東。
entries.en: He was transferred to command the Fujian naval forces, then returned to Guangdong by way of Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Transferred to Fujian naval commander-in-chief, again from Zhejiang back to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十五年，卒，諡勤愨。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong and was posthumously titled Qinque.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Qinmin.

entries.zh: 子振聲，附李長庚傳。
entries.en: His son Zhensheng is treated in the biography of Li Changgeng.
entries.literal: His son Zhensheng is appended to the biography of Li Changgeng.

entries.zh: 金鼇嘗預千叟宴，高宗賜之酒，命賦詩記事，金鼇辭不能詩。
entries.en: Jin'ao once attended the Banquet for a Thousand Elders; the Qianlong Emperor offered him wine and asked him to compose a commemorative poem, but Jin'ao begged off, saying he was no poet.
entries.literal: Jin'ao once attended the Banquet for a Thousand Elders; the Gaozong emperor bestowed wine on him and ordered him to compose a poem recording the event; Jin'ao declined, saying he could not write poetry.

entries.zh: 上顧笑曰：「汝為香樹妻弟，又從受業，豈不能詩者？」
entries.en: The emperor turned with a smile and said, "You are the brother-in-law of Xiangshu and studied under him as well—how can you claim you cannot write verse?"
entries.literal: The emperor looked back smiling and said: "You are the wife's younger brother of Xiangshu and also studied under him—how could you be unable to write poetry?"

entries.zh: 香樹，錢陳群字也。
entries.en: Xiangshu was the style name of the scholar Qian Chenqun.
entries.literal: Xiangshu was the style name of Qian Chenqun.

entries.zh: 官湖廣，和珅已柄政，欲納交焉。
entries.en: While serving in Huguang, when Heshen already dominated the government, Heshen sought his friendship.
entries.literal: When he held office in Huguang, Heshen already wielded power and wished to win his friendship.

entries.zh: 金鼇謝不可。
entries.en: Jin'ao politely refused.
entries.literal: Jin'ao declined and would not agree.

entries.zh: 富僧阿，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Fu Senga, of the Sumulu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Fu Senga, of the Sumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 雍正初，授拜唐阿，累遷頭等侍衛。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was made a palace attendant and rose in due course to First Class Bodyguard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign he was appointed a baitangga and was repeatedly promoted to First Class Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 出為副都統，歷成都、三姓、寧古塔諸地。
entries.en: He was then posted as deputy military governor, serving in turn at Chengdu, Sanxing, Ningguta, and elsewhere.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as deputy military governor, successively at Chengdu, Sanxing, Ningguta, and other posts.

entries.zh: 擢將軍，自荊州移黑龍江。
entries.en: Promoted to frontier general, he was moved from Jingzhou to Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: He was promoted to general and transferred from Jingzhou to Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 黑龍江北鄰俄羅斯，康熙二十九年與定界。
entries.en: Heilongjiang's northern frontier adjoins Russia; the border had been delimited in the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign.
entries.literal: Heilongjiang on the north borders Russia; in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi the boundary was fixed.

entries.zh: 歲久，將吏憚行邊，道裡不能詳。
entries.en: Over time the garrison officers grew reluctant to patrol the frontier, and the routes and distances were no longer known with precision.
entries.literal: As years passed, officers and clerks feared traveling the border, and the routes and distances could not be known in detail.

entries.zh: 富僧阿遣副都統瑚爾起等分探諸水源，皆至興堪山還報。
entries.en: Fu Senga dispatched Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi and others to reconnoiter the various headwaters in separate parties; each party reached Xingkan Mountain and returned with its report.
entries.literal: Fu Senga sent the deputy military governor Hu'erqi and others to explore the various river sources separately; all reached Xingkanshan and returned to report.

entries.zh: 乃上疏言：「副都統瑚爾起探格爾畢齊河源，自黑龍江至格爾畢齊河口，水程一千六百九十七里；
entries.en: He then memorialized the throne, reporting: "Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi traced the Ge'erbiji River to its source: from the Heilongjiang to the Ge'erbiji estuary the water route measures 1,697 li;
entries.literal: He then submitted a memorial stating: "Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi explored the source of the Ge'erbiji River; from the Heilongjiang to the mouth of the Ge'erbiji, the water route is 1,697 li;

entries.zh: 自河口行陸路二百四十七里，至興堪山：其間無人跡。
entries.en: from the estuary a land march of 247 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; the country between is utterly uninhabited.
entries.literal: from the mouth by land route 247 li to Xingkanshan: in between there are no human traces.

entries.zh: 協領納林布探精奇哩江源，自黑龍江入精奇哩江，北行至托克河口，水程一千五百八十七里；
entries.en: Assistant Commandant Nalinbu reconnoitered the Jingqiri headwaters: entering the Jingqiri from the Heilongjiang and sailing north to the Tuo estuary, the water route is 1,587 li;
entries.literal: Assistant Commandant Nalinbu explored the source of the Jingqiri River; entering the Jingqiri from the Heilongjiang and proceeding north to the mouth of the Tuo River, the water route is 1,587 li;

entries.zh: 自河口行陸路二百四十里至興堪山：地苦寒，無水草禽獸。
entries.en: from the estuary a land march of 240 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; the region is bitterly cold and devoid of pasture, waterfowl, or game.
entries.literal: from the mouth by land route 240 li to Xingkanshan: the land is bitterly cold, without water, grass, birds, or beasts.

entries.zh: 協領偉保探西里木第河源，自黑龍江經精奇哩江入西里木第河口，復過英肯河，水程一千三百五里；
entries.en: Assistant Commandant Weibao traced the Xilimudi headwaters: from the Heilongjiang through the Jingqiri into the Xilimudi estuary, then past the Yingken River, the water route is 1,305 li;
entries.literal: Assistant Commandant Weibao explored the source of the Xilimudi River; from the Heilongjiang via the Jingqiri into the mouth of the Xilimudi, then crossing the Yingken River, the water route is 1,305 li;

entries.zh: 自英肯河口行陸路一百八十里至興堪山：地苦寒，無水草禽獸。
entries.en: from the Yingken estuary a land march of 180 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; there too the country is bitterly cold and without pasture or wildlife.
entries.literal: from the mouth of the Yingken by land route 180 li to Xingkanshan: the land is bitterly cold, without water, grass, birds, or beasts.

entries.zh: 協領阿迪木保探鈕曼河源，自黑龍江入鈕曼河，復經西里木第河入烏默勒河口，水程一千六百十五里；
entries.en: Assistant Commandant Adimubao reconnoitered the Niuman headwaters: entering the Niuman from the Heilongjiang, then via the Xilimudi to the Wumole estuary, the water route is 1,615 li;
entries.literal: Assistant Commandant Adimubao explored the source of the Niuman River; entering the Niuman from the Heilongjiang, then via the Xilimudi into the mouth of the Wumole, the water route is 1,615 li;

entries.zh: 自河口行陸路四百五十六里至興堪山。
entries.en: from the estuary a land march of 456 li reaches Xingkan Mountain.
entries.literal: from the mouth by land route 456 li to Xingkanshan.

entries.zh: 諸地俱無俄羅斯偷越。
entries.en: Along all these routes there was no sign of Russians crossing the border illicitly.
entries.literal: In all these regions there was no Russian trespass.

entries.zh: 臣按呼倫貝爾有額爾古訥河，西為俄羅斯界，東屬我國。
entries.en: Your subject observes that in Hulunbuir the Ergun River marks the frontier: its west bank is Russian territory, its east bank our own.
entries.literal: Your subject notes that in Hulunbuir there is the Ergun River; to the west is the Russian border, to the east it belongs to our state.

entries.zh: 自此至珠爾特，處處設卡。
entries.en: From that point to Zhu'erte, guard posts have been established at intervals throughout.
entries.literal: From there to Zhu'erte, checkpoints are set everywhere.

entries.zh: 今復自珠爾特至莫哩勒克河口，設卡二，索博爾罕增立鄂博，逐日巡查。
entries.en: It is now proposed to add two more posts between Zhu'erte and the Molileke estuary, to erect additional border cairns in Sobo'erhan, and to inspect the line daily.
entries.literal: Now again from Zhu'erte to the mouth of the Molileke, two checkpoints are set; in Sobo'erhan additional obos are erected, with daily patrols.

entries.zh: 俄羅斯、鼐瑪爾斷難偷越。
entries.en: Russians and Naimar tribesmen will scarcely be able to slip across undetected.
entries.literal: Russians and Naimar will certainly find it difficult to cross secretly.

entries.zh: 黑龍江與俄羅斯接壤，興堪山延亙至海。
entries.en: Along the Heilongjiang our territory adjoins Russia, and Xingkan Mountain runs in an unbroken line to the coast.
entries.literal: Heilongjiang borders Russia; Xingkanshan extends continuously to the sea.

entries.zh: 嗣後請飭打牲總管每歲六月遣章京、驍騎校、兵丁，自水路與捕貂人同至托克、英肯兩河口，及鄂勒希、西里木第兩河間，巡察還報；
entries.en: Henceforth the Fur Tribute superintendent should each year in the sixth month dispatch clerks, cavalry officers, and troops by boat, together with sable hunters, to the Tuo and Yingken estuaries and to the stretch between the E'lexi and Xilimudi rivers, patrol the ground, and report back;
entries.literal: Hereafter it is requested to order the Fur Tribute superintendent each year in the sixth month to dispatch zhangjing, darti-achas, and soldiers, by water route together with sable hunters to the two river mouths of Tuo and Yingken, and between the two rivers E'lexi and Xilimudi, to patrol and return to report;

entries.zh: 三年遣副總管、佐領、驍騎校於冰解後，自水路至興堪山巡察還報；
entries.en: every three years, after the ice breaks, deputy superintendents, company captains, and cavalry officers should travel by water to Xingkan Mountain, patrol, and return with their reports;
entries.literal: every three years dispatch deputy superintendents, zuolings, and darti-achas after the ice breaks, by water route to Xingkanshan to patrol and return to report;

entries.zh: 黑龍江官兵每歲巡察格爾畢齊河口，三年亦至興堪山巡察還報：歲終報部。」
entries.en: Heilongjiang troops should inspect the Ge'erbiji estuary annually and reach Xingkan Mountain on the triennial circuit; all findings are to be reported to the Board at year's end."
entries.literal: Heilongjiang officers and soldiers each year patrol the mouth of the Ge'erbiji, and every three years also patrol to Xingkanshan and return to report: at year's end report to the ministry."

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The emperor approved these proposals.
entries.literal: The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 富僧阿治事嚴，嘗疏請罪人予官兵為奴，併其妻子皆令為奴；
entries.en: Fu Senga ran a tight administration. He once asked that convicted offenders be assigned as bondsmen to troops, together with their wives and children;
entries.literal: Fu Senga was strict in administration; he once memorialized requesting that criminals be given to officers and soldiers as slaves, and that their wives and children likewise be made slaves;

entries.zh: 又以遣犯脫走，出巡並將校婪索，皆請逮送刑部：上不許。
entries.en: and when exiled convicts escaped or officers on tour were caught extorting bribes, he asked that they be sent to the Ministry of Justice for punishment—the emperor declined each request.
entries.literal: also because exiled convicts escaped, and on inspection tours commanders and officers extorted greedily, all requested to be arrested and sent to the Ministry of Justice: the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 移西安將軍，西安、寧夏移駐滿洲兵，復分駐巴里坤，富僧阿議定規制，皆如所請。
entries.en: Transferred to Xi'an as frontier general, he drew up the regulations for redeploying Manchu garrisons from Xi'an and Ningxia and posting detachments at Barkol; the court adopted his plans in full.
entries.literal: Transferred to general at Xi'an; Manchu troops relocated from Xi'an and Ningxia, again distributed to garrison at Barkol—Fu Senga's proposed regulations were all granted as requested.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十年三月，卒官。
entries.en: He died in office in the third month of the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fortieth year of Qianlong, he died in office.

entries.zh: 剛塔，烏濟克忒氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
entries.en: Gangta, of the Ujikete clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Gangta, of the Ujikete clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 初充前鋒，從征準噶爾，授雲騎尉世職。
entries.en: He began as a vanguard on the Dzungar campaigns and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
entries.literal: At first he served as a vanguard, followed the campaign against the Dzungars, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

entries.zh: 三遷直隸泰宁鎮中營游擊。
entries.en: After three promotions he became battalion commander of the Middle Battalion at the Taining Garrison in Zhili.
entries.literal: After three promotions he became battalion commander of the Middle Battalion of the Taining Garrison in Zhili.

entries.zh: 從克臨清，山東巡撫楊景素奏留山東。
entries.en: He took part in the capture of Linqing, and Shandong Governor Yang Jingsu asked that he be kept in Shandong.
entries.literal: He followed in the capture of Linqing; Shandong Governor Yang Jingsu memorialized to retain him in Shandong.

entries.zh: 四遷直隸提督，兼領馬蘭鎮總兵。
entries.en: Four further promotions brought him to provincial commander-in-chief of Zhili, while he also commanded the Malan Garrison.
entries.literal: After four more promotions he became Zhili commander-in-chief, concurrently holding regional command of the Malan Garrison.

entries.zh: 移陝西固原提督。
entries.en: He was transferred to command the Guyuan garrison in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi Guyuan commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十九年，鹽茶廳小山回田五糾眾為亂，攻破安西州。
entries.en: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong the Xiaoshan Muslim Tian Wu of Yancha ting raised followers, rebelled, and overran Anxi Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong, the Xiaoshan Hui Tian Wu of Yancha ting gathered crowds in rebellion and stormed Anxi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 剛塔督兵逐賊，殺賊數十，射殪乘馬賊渠，賜上用玉韘、大小荷包。
entries.en: Gangta led the pursuit, killed dozens of rebels, and shot down the mounted rebel chief; the emperor rewarded him with an imperial jade thumb-ring and large and small purses.
entries.literal: Gangta supervised troops pursuing the rebels, killed several tens of rebels, shot dead the mounted rebel chieftain, and was awarded the emperor's jade thumb-ring and large and small purses.

entries.zh: 复逐賊至浪山，田五戰被創，自殺。
entries.en: Pressing on to Lang Mountain, he wounded Tian Wu in battle; Tian Wu then took his own life.
entries.literal: Again pursuing the rebels to Lang Mountain, Tian Wu was wounded in battle and killed himself.

entries.zh: 其徒竄據馬家堡，剛塔督兵合圍，賊夜出堡逾山遁，環壘樹木桿，懸衣帽其上，紿官軍，官軍逼壘，乃知賊已走。
entries.en: The survivors seized Majia Fort; Gangta invested it, but the rebels slipped out by night over the hills, left poles and clothing on the walls to deceive the besiegers, and were long gone before the troops discovered the ruse.
entries.literal: His followers fled and seized Majia Fort; Gangta supervised troops in combined encirclement; the rebels by night left the fort and escaped over the mountains; they ringed the ramparts with wooden poles and hung clothes and hats on them to deceive the government army; when the government army pressed the ramparts, only then did they know the rebels had already fled.

entries.zh: 剛塔督兵逐賊，戰於馬家灣，剛塔中矢。
entries.en: Gangta continued the pursuit and fought at Majia Bay, where he was wounded by an arrow.
entries.literal: Gangta supervised troops pursuing the rebels, fought at Majia Bay, and Gangta was struck by an arrow.

entries.zh: 復進至馬營街，殺賊數十，得級二十五。
entries.en: Advancing again to Maying Street, he killed dozens of rebels and took twenty-five heads.
entries.literal: Advancing again to Maying Street, he killed several tens of rebels and obtained twenty-five heads.

entries.zh: 賊攻陷通渭，其徒分據石峰堡。
entries.en: The rebels then overran Tongwei while their bands occupied Shifeng Fort.
entries.literal: The rebels stormed and took Tongwei; their followers separately held Shifeng Fort.

entries.zh: 西安副都統明善攻之，沒於陣。
entries.en: Xi'an Deputy Military Governor Mingshan assaulted the fort and was killed in action.
entries.literal: Xi'an Deputy Military Governor Mingshan attacked it and perished in battle.

entries.zh: 上以師無功，令大學士阿桂、尚書福康安出視師。
entries.en: Because the campaign stalled, the emperor sent Grand Secretary Agui and Minister Fuk'anggan to take command in the field.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the army had no success, ordered Grand Secretary Agui and Minister Fuk'anggan to go out and inspect the army.

entries.zh: 上謂馬營街、石峰堡皆通渭地，剛塔方逐賊馬營街，通渭陷不赴援，明善又以攻石峰堡戰死，詔詰責。
entries.en: The emperor observed that Maying Street and Shifeng Fort lay within Tongwei: Gangta had been chasing rebels at Maying Street when Tongwei fell yet he did not march to its relief, and Mingshan had died assaulting Shifeng Fort—an edict censured him sharply.
entries.literal: The emperor said Maying Street and Shifeng Fort are both in Tongwei territory; Gangta was just pursuing rebels at Maying Street when Tongwei fell and he did not go to relieve it; Mingshan also died attacking Shifeng Fort; an edict rebuked and held him accountable.

entries.zh: 剛塔疏言：「獲賊言將自通渭道伏羌、秦州天潼關。」
entries.en: Gangta memorialized, "Prisoners said the rebels would march from Tongwei through Fuxiang and Qinzhou toward Tiantong Pass."
entries.literal: Gangta memorialized: "Capturing rebels, they said they would go from Tongwei by way of Fuxiang and Qinzhou to Tiantong Pass."

entries.zh: 上責剛塔信賊妄語搖軍心，令福康安傳諭，奪剛塔職，逮送京師。
entries.en: The emperor accused him of crediting rebel bluster and unsettling the troops, had Fuk'anggan relay the edict, stripped him of rank, and sent him under arrest to the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Gangta for believing the rebels' false words and shaking army morale, ordered Fuk'anggan to transmit the edict, stripped Gangta of office, and had him arrested and sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 上方幸熱河，留京王大臣等讞當斬，上以剛塔殲賊渠田五，戰馬家灣身被創，貸死，戍伊犁。
entries.en: The emperor was at Rehe; the princes and ministers in Beijing recommended execution, but noting that Gangta had destroyed the rebel chief Tian Wu and been wounded at Majia Bay, the emperor spared his life and banished him to Ili.
entries.literal: The emperor was then visiting Rehe; the princes and grand ministers left in the capital judged death by decapitation; the emperor, because Gangta had destroyed the rebel chieftain Tian Wu and at Majia Bay was wounded in battle, commuted death and exiled him to garrison duty at Ili.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died there in exile.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 列傳一百二十二
entries.en: Biographies 122
entries.literal: Biographies, Number 122

entries.zh: 陳夢說，字曉岩，山西絳縣人。
entries.en: Chen Mengshuo, whose courtesy name was Xiaoyan, came from Jiang County in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Chen Mengshuo, styled Xiaoyan, was a man of Jiang County, Shanxi.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年進士，授刑部主事。
entries.en: He received his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of the Qianlong reign and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 讞決，執法不阿上官；
entries.en: When adjudicating cases he held to the law and would not defer to his superiors.
entries.literal: In deciding cases he enforced the law without currying favor with superiors.

entries.zh: 兼提牢，役不能為奸。
entries.en: While also serving as prison superintendent, he kept the underlings from any misconduct.
entries.literal: He also supervised the prison; the runners could not practice deceit.

entries.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to director in the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 出為浙江寧紹台道。
entries.en: He left the capital to serve as intendant of the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as intendant of the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 台州素獷悍，寧海梅村民拒捕，提督將以兵往，旁村皆驚竄。
entries.en: Taizhou had long been known for its fierce and unruly populace. When villagers at Mei in Ninghai resisted arrest, the provincial commander prepared to march troops against them, and neighboring hamlets scattered in panic.
entries.literal: Taizhou had always been fierce and unruly; villagers of Mei in Ninghai resisted arrest, and the provincial military commander was about to send troops; neighboring villages all fled in alarm.

entries.zh: 夢說輕騎臨縣，縣令已纟累系竄者數十人，盡釋之，曰：「吾來捕梅姓數人而已。」
entries.en: Mengshuo rode to the county seat with only a light escort. The magistrate had already bound dozens of people from the surrounding villages, and Mengshuo released them all, saying, "I have come to arrest only a handful of men from the Mei clan."
entries.literal: Mengshuo came lightly mounted to the county; the magistrate had already bound and detained several dozen who had fled, and he released them all, saying: "I have come to seize only a few men of the Mei surname."

entries.zh: 獲誅拒捕者，而釋其少子一人。
entries.en: He captured and executed those who had resisted arrest, but spared one younger son.
entries.literal: He seized and executed those who resisted arrest, but released one younger son.

entries.zh: 台人感之，謠其事為存孤記。
entries.en: The people of Taizhou were deeply moved and spread a ballad about the affair, calling it the Tale of the Spared Orphan.
entries.literal: The people of Taizhou were moved and balladed the affair as the Record of Preserving the Orphan.

entries.zh: 修鄞縣錢湖徬。
entries.en: He repaired the Qian Lake embankment in Yin County.
entries.literal: He repaired the Qian Lake embankment in Yin County.

entries.zh: 值上南巡，召見，素知其在刑部有能名，賜綺貂。
entries.en: During the emperor's southern tour he was summoned to audience. The emperor, who had long known his reputation for competence at the Ministry of Punishments, rewarded him with a fur robe of fine sable.
entries.literal: When the emperor made his southern tour he was summoned for audience; the emperor had long known his reputation for ability in the Ministry of Punishments and bestowed upon him fine sable.

entries.zh: 尋以失察屬吏不職罣議，仍以道員用。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was censured for failing to detect misconduct by a subordinate, yet was retained in service at the circuit level.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, for failure to detect dereliction by a subordinate official, he was censured but still employed as a circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 授督糧道，卻餽金，漕政肅然。
entries.en: Appointed grain-transport intendant, he refused bribes of gold and brought order to the grain-shipping administration.
entries.literal: He was appointed grain-transport intendant, refused gifts of gold, and grain transport administration became orderly.

entries.zh: 時訛言妖人翦發，蕭山捕僧了凡等四人，誣服，夢說平反之。
entries.en: At the time a rumor spread that sorcerers were clipping people's hair. Xiaoshan arrested the monk Liaofan and three others, who confessed under coercion, and Mengshuo overturned the convictions.
entries.literal: At the time a rumor spread that sorcerers were cutting people's hair; Xiaoshan arrested the monk Liaofan and three others, who confessed under false coercion, and Mengshuo reversed the verdict.

entries.zh: 後或言事由浙見，解京訊治無驗，抵妄捕者罪，以夢說輕比，降秩。
entries.en: Later it was reported that the affair had first appeared in Zhejiang. The case was sent to the capital for investigation, but no evidence was found. Those who had made wrongful arrests were punished, while Mengshuo was demoted for having treated the matter too leniently.
entries.literal: Later someone said the affair had originated in Zhejiang; the case was sent to the capital for investigation and nothing was verified; those who had made false arrests were punished, but because Mengshuo had treated the offense too lightly, he was demoted in rank.

entries.zh: 修餘杭南湖堤。
entries.en: He repaired the South Lake embankment in Yuhang.
entries.literal: He repaired the South Lake embankment in Yuhang.

entries.zh: 署嘉興、嚴州、處州、湖州諸府，復原官。
entries.en: After serving in acting posts at Jiaxing, Yanzhou, Chuzhou, and Huzhou, he was restored to his former rank.
entries.literal: He acted in the prefectures of Jiaxing, Yanzhou, Chuzhou, and Huzhou, and was restored to his original rank.

entries.zh: 夢說官浙十二年，所至有聲。
entries.en: Mengshuo served in Zhejiang for twelve years and won renown wherever he was posted.
entries.literal: Mengshuo held office in Zhejiang for twelve years and wherever he went left a reputation.

entries.zh: 尋乞歸。
entries.en: He soon petitioned to retire.
entries.literal: Soon he requested to retire.

entries.zh: 顧光旭，字晴沙，江蘇無錫人。
entries.en: Gu Guangxu, whose courtesy name was Qingsha, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Gu Guangxu, styled Qingsha, was a man of Wuxi, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 乾隆十八年進士，授戶部主事。
entries.en: He received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of the Qianlong reign and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the eighteenth year of Qianlong, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 晉員外郎，主鹽筴，兩淮解銀，輒掛欠百之十五。
entries.en: Promoted to vice director, he oversaw salt affairs; Lianghuai remittances routinely showed a fifteen-percent shortfall.
entries.literal: He was advanced to vice director, in charge of salt policy; when the Lianghuai circuit forwarded silver, it always showed a shortfall of fifteen per hundred.

entries.zh: 光旭謂：「各省庫平皆部較頒，何獨兩淮歷久如是？
entries.en: Guangxu said, "Every province's treasury scale-weights are set by the ministry—why has Lianghuai alone suffered this chronic shortfall?
entries.literal: Guangxu said: "Every province's treasury scale-weights are issued after comparison by the ministry—why alone has Lianghuai been thus for so long?

entries.zh: 是銀庫多索也。」
entries.en: The silver vault is exacting too much."
entries.literal: This is the silver treasury demanding too much."

entries.zh: 白於長官除免之。
entries.en: He reported to his superiors and had the excess levy abolished.
entries.literal: He reported to his superiors and had it abolished.

entries.zh: 擢御史。
entries.en: He was promoted to supervising censor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to censor.

entries.zh: 二十四年，直隸、山東大水。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of the reign, Zhili and Shandong were struck by severe floods.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Zhili and Shandong suffered great floods.

entries.zh: 次年春，疏曰：「上年兩省災，截漕發帑加賑。
entries.en: The following spring he memorialized: "Last year both provinces suffered disaster; the Court diverted grain tribute and opened the treasury for extra relief.
entries.literal: The next spring he memorialized, saying: "Last year the two provinces suffered disaster; grain transport was diverted and treasury funds issued for added relief.

entries.zh: 近見流民扶老攜幼入京，春來尤甚。
entries.en: Yet I now see refugees entering the capital supporting the elderly and leading children, and since spring the influx has grown worse.
entries.literal: Recently I have seen vagrant people supporting the old and leading the young into the capital; since spring it has been especially severe.

entries.zh: 五城米廠飯廠人倍增，詢之，近京數百里，毀屋伐樹，賣男鬻女，老弱踣頓，不可勝計。
entries.en: Crowds at the Five Cities grain and soup kitchens have doubled; inquiry shows that for hundreds of li around the capital people are tearing down houses, felling trees, selling sons and daughters, and the old and weak are collapsing in the roads beyond count.
entries.literal: The Five Cities grain depots and soup kitchens have doubled their people; on inquiry, for several hundred li near the capital, houses are destroyed and trees felled, sons sold and daughters trafficked, old and weak collapsed in exhaustion beyond counting.

entries.zh: 耳目所及如此，其外可知。
entries.en: If conditions within sight are this dire, the suffering farther afield may be imagined.
entries.literal: What ears and eyes reach is thus; what lies beyond can be known.

entries.zh: 伏思救荒無奇策，惟督撫及有司親民之官實心實力方克有濟。
entries.en: I submit that famine relief has no miracle cure: only when governors-general, governors, and magistrates who truly care for the people work with genuine devotion can relief succeed.
entries.literal: I humbly consider that in famine relief there are no marvelous stratagems; only when governor-generals, governors, and local officials who are close to the people exert sincere heart and sincere strength can there be success.

entries.zh: 各州縣未嘗不施賑，或委任佐貳，或假手胥吏，或設廠遠離村鎮，窮民奔走待食，或得或不得。
entries.en: Every county distributes relief in name, yet some delegate to deputies, some leave it to clerks, some open kitchens far from villages; the poor rush about for food and may or may not be fed.
entries.literal: Every prefecture and county has not failed to distribute relief, yet some delegate to deputies, some lend the matter to clerks, some set up depots far from villages and towns; the destitute run about waiting for food, sometimes obtaining it and sometimes not.

entries.zh: 良法美意，一入俗吏之手，沾實惠者十不及五。
entries.en: Once a good policy reaches a corrupt clerk, fewer than half those in need receive real help.
entries.literal: Good laws and fine intentions, once they enter vulgar clerks' hands—those who receive real benefit are fewer than five in ten.

entries.zh: 一二賢有司撫循周至，則他境流民聞風畢集，轉難措手。
entries.en: Where one capable magistrate administers relief well, refugees from neighboring districts flock in, making his task harder still.
entries.literal: When one or two worthy local officials comfort and follow through thoroughly, then vagrant people from other districts hear the wind and all gather, making it harder to handle.

entries.zh: 此督撫不能真實愛民，下亦以應付塞責，一切皆屬具文。
entries.en: This shows governors-general and governors do not truly care for the people; subordinates merely go through the motions, and every measure becomes paperwork.
entries.literal: This is because governor-generals and governors cannot truly love the people; below them officials also treat it as perfunctory duty to fill obligations—everything becomes empty documents.

entries.zh: 請敕下隨地撫綏，毋致流移失所。
entries.en: I ask that the throne order local comforting so people are not driven from their homes.
entries.literal: I request an imperial command sent down to comfort and pacify according to locality, and not allow drifting displacement and loss of home.

entries.zh: 疏導積水，以工代賑，借給牛種，以資耕作。
entries.en: Drain standing water, employ work-for-relief projects, and lend oxen and seed so fields can be planted.
entries.literal: Drain accumulated water, use labor in place of relief grain, lend oxen and seed, to supply cultivation.

entries.zh: 有流民有礦土，尉即重治督撫州縣之罪。
entries.en: Wherever vagrants appear or land is left waste, the Court should immediately hold the responsible governor-general, governor, prefect, and magistrate to stern account.
entries.literal: When there are vagrant people or wasteland, the authorities should immediately heavily punish the offenses of governors-general, governors, and prefectural and county officials.

entries.zh: 來京饑民，已領廠賑。
entries.en: Refugees who reached the capital have already received kitchen relief.
entries.literal: Starving people who came to the capital have already received depot relief.

entries.zh: 一年之計，在於東作。
entries.en: The year's livelihood depends on the spring planting.
entries.literal: The year's plan lies in the eastern plowing.

entries.zh: 無力自回者給貲遣送，其本籍無倚賴者歸大興、宛平安輯，勿令棲流無著。
entries.en: Those too poor to return home should receive travel funds; those with no kin in their native districts should be settled in Daxing and Wanping, not left homeless wanderers.
entries.literal: Those unable to return on their own should be given funds and sent back; those with no support in their native place should be settled in Daxing and Wanping in peace, and not allowed to lodge drifting without fixed abode.

entries.zh: 又每遇水旱，司、道、府親勘，先以供應煩州縣，所委佐貳，亦滋擾累，請嚴參重處。」
entries.en: Moreover, whenever flood or drought strikes, intendants and prefects tour the scene in person, burdening counties with hosting their entourages; the deputies they send add further harassment. I ask that such officials be impeached and punished severely."
entries.literal: Moreover, whenever flood or drought occurs, circuit, route, and prefectural officials personally survey—first they trouble prefectures and counties with provisions for their retinue; the deputies they delegate also increase harassment; I request severe impeachment and heavy punishment."

entries.zh: 奏入，上善之。
entries.en: The emperor received the memorial and commended it.
entries.literal: The memorial entered; the emperor approved it.

entries.zh: 命赴京畿察勘，疏消文安、大城積水。
entries.en: He was ordered to inspect the capital region and drained the standing water at Wen'an and Dacheng.
entries.literal: He was ordered to go to the capital region to inspect and survey, and drained accumulated water in Wen'an and Dacheng.

entries.zh: 樂亭民擁閧縣門，撫定之，馳章請加賑。
entries.en: When Leting townsfolk stormed the county yamen, he calmed them and urgently memorialized for additional relief.
entries.literal: The people of Leting crowded and stormed the county gate; he pacified and settled them, galloped a memorial requesting added relief.

entries.zh: 歷寶坻、灤州，盧龍，兩月竣事。
entries.en: He worked through Baodi, Luanzhou, and Lulong and finished in two months.
entries.literal: He passed through Baodi, Luanzhou, and Lulong; in two months the work was completed.

entries.zh: 遷給事中。
entries.en: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 列傳一百二十三
entries.en: Biography 123
entries.literal: Biographies 123

entries.zh: 盧焯，字光植，漢軍鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Lu Chao, styled Guangzhi, was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Lu Chao, courtesy name Guangzhi, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 入貲授直隸武邑知縣。
entries.en: He bought his way into office as magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.
entries.literal: By purchase of office he was appointed magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.

entries.zh: 縣舊有均徭錢供差費，遇差仍按裡派夫，焯革除之，又歸火耗於公，捕盜尤力。
entries.en: The county had long collected equalized corvée funds for official errands, yet whenever a duty arose corvée labor was still levied by neighborhood; Chao abolished the practice. He also turned surplus grain fees over to the public treasury and was notably zealous in catching thieves.
entries.literal: The county had long levied equalized corvée money for dispatch expenses, yet when duties arose labor was still apportioned by li; Chao abolished this. He also remitted surplus grain fees to the public account and was especially vigorous in apprehending bandits.

entries.zh: 雍正六年，解餉詣京師，世宗特召對。
entries.en: In 1728, while delivering tribute silver to the capital, he was granted a special audience by the Yongzheng Emperor.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, while escorting tribute funds to the capital, he received a special audience from the Yongzheng Emperor.

entries.zh: 遷江南亳州知州，禁械鬥。
entries.en: He was promoted to prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan, where he banned factional armed fights.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan and prohibited armed brawls.

entries.zh: 再遷山東東昌知府，總督田文鏡遣官弁四出訪事，東昌民逮下獄甚眾，焯至，悉判遣之。
entries.en: He was next made prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor-general Tian Wenjing had sent officers far and wide to investigate cases, and a great many Dongchang residents had been thrown into jail; on taking office, Chao reviewed the cases and released them all.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to be prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor-general Tian Wenjing had sent officials in all directions to investigate matters, and very many people of Dongchang had been arrested and imprisoned; when Chao arrived, he judged and released them all.

entries.zh: 會有水災，焯疏運河，築護城長堤，動帑賑恤。
entries.en: When floods struck, he dredged the Grand Canal, built a long embankment around the city walls, and spent state funds on relief.
entries.literal: When flooding occurred, Chao dredged the Grand Canal, built a long protective dike around the city wall, and drew on the treasury for relief.

entries.zh: 上遣大臣閱視，獨東昌得完。
entries.en: The throne dispatched high officials to inspect the damage; only Dongchang emerged unscathed.
entries.literal: The emperor sent grand ministers to inspect; Dongchang alone remained intact.

entries.zh: 九年，遷督糧道，移河南南汝道。
entries.en: In 1731 he was moved to grain transport intendant, then to the Nannu circuit in Henan.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to grain transport intendant and then to the Nannu Circuit in Henan.

entries.zh: 十年，授按察使。
entries.en: In 1732 he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 十一年，遷布政使。
entries.en: In 1733 he was promoted to provincial treasurer.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to provincial treasurer.

entries.zh: 十二年，擢福建巡撫，賜孔雀翎。
entries.en: In 1734 he was elevated to governor of Fujian and awarded a peacock feather.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian and granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，焯疏言被水州縣不成災，上諭曰：「被水雖不成災，仍須加意賑恤，毋使小民失所。」
entries.en: In 1735, when the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Chao reported that flood-hit districts had not technically qualified as disaster areas. The emperor replied: 'Even if the floods have not risen to the level of a declared disaster, you must still relieve the people with special care and keep the poor from losing their livelihoods.'
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the Gaozong Emperor acceded; Chao memorialized that flooded prefectures and counties had not become disaster areas. The emperor instructed: 'Though flooding has not become a disaster, you must still give extra care to relief so that the common people do not lose their homes.'

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，請查丈建陽民田，上諭曰：「小民畏查丈如水火。
entries.en: In 1736 he asked to survey and remeasure civilian land in Jianyang. The emperor warned: 'Ordinary people fear land surveys as they fear fire and water.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he requested a survey and remeasurement of civilian fields in Jianyang. The emperor instructed: 'The common people dread surveys and remeasurements as they dread fire and flood.

entries.zh: 汝初為加賦起見，今又以豁除掩非，一存觀望之心，所謂無一而可也。」
entries.en: You began by trying to raise taxes, and now you propose exemptions to cover your mistakes, always hedging your bets—there is nothing in this that I can approve.'
entries.literal: At first you acted with an eye to increasing levies; now you use exemptions to cover your errors, always keeping a mind of hesitation—there is nothing here that can be approved.'

entries.zh: 尋奏減邵武永安所、霞浦福寧衛屯田徵米科則，豁閩、侯官諸縣額缺田地。
entries.en: Soon after he memorialized to lower grain tax rates on garrison farms at Yong'an in Shaowu and Funing in Xiapu, and to exempt registered shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized to reduce the grain levy rates on garrison fields at Yong'an sub-prefecture in Shaowu and Funing guard in Xiapu, and to exempt shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.

entries.zh: 又以平和、永安、清流諸縣田少丁多，請減免攤餘丁銀。
entries.en: He also asked to reduce or waive the apportioned surplus adult-male tax in Pinghe, Yong'an, Qingliu, and other counties where land was scarce but households were numerous.
entries.literal: He also, because Pinghe, Yong'an, Qingliu, and other counties had little land but many adult males, requested reduction or exemption of the apportioned surplus adult-male silver levy.

entries.zh: 又奏教民蠶績，疏濬省會城河。
entries.en: He further proposed teaching sericulture to the people and dredging the canal around the provincial capital.
entries.literal: He also memorialized to teach the people sericulture and to dredge the provincial capital's city moat.

entries.zh: 三年，調浙江巡撫，兼鹽政。
entries.en: In 1738 he was transferred to Zhejiang as governor, with concurrent charge of the salt monopoly.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Zhejiang, concurrently supervising the salt administration.

entries.zh: 奏請停仁和、海寧二縣草塘歲修銀，減嘉興屬七縣銀米十之二。
entries.en: He asked to suspend annual repair funds for earthen seawalls in Renhe and Haining and to cut grain and silver taxes in Jiaxing's seven subordinate counties by twenty percent.
entries.literal: He memorialized to halt the annual repair silver for sod seawalls in Renhe and Haining counties and to reduce grain and silver levies in the seven counties under Jiaxing by two-tenths.

entries.zh: 又奏陳鹽政諸事：請禁商人短秤；
entries.en: He also laid out salt-policy reforms: merchants must be forbidden to use short weights;
entries.literal: He also memorialized on various salt-administration matters: requesting a ban on merchants using short weights;

entries.zh: 飭州縣捕私鹽毋擾民；
entries.en: prefectural and county officials must seize smuggled salt without harassing the populace;
entries.literal: ordering prefectures and counties to seize illicit salt without harassing the people;

entries.zh: 毋捕肩挑小販；
entries.en: they must not arrest petty peddlers carrying salt on shoulder-poles;
entries.literal: not to arrest peddlers carrying salt on shoulder-poles;

entries.zh: 鹽場徵課不得刑比。
entries.en: and salt-field tax collection must not rely on corporal punishment.
entries.literal: and that salt-field tax collection must not employ corporal punishment by analogy.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「所奏各條皆是。
entries.en: The emperor replied: 'Every point in your memorial is sound.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Each item you have memorialized is correct.

entries.zh: 汝先過刻，茲乃事事以寬沽名。
entries.en: You used to be excessively harsh; now you court popularity by leniency on every issue.
entries.literal: You were formerly too severe; now on every matter you use leniency to buy a reputation.

entries.zh: 過猶不及，汝其識之！」
entries.en: Excess is no better than deficiency—remember that!'
entries.literal: To go too far is as bad as not going far enough—mark this well!'

entries.zh: 尋請裁鹽場協辦鹽大使，改海寧草塘為石塘。
entries.en: Soon after he asked to abolish assistant salt commissioners at the salt fields and to rebuild Haining's earthen seawall in stone.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he requested the abolition of assistant salt commissioners at the salt fields and the conversion of Haining's sod seawall into a stone seawall.

entries.zh: 既，又請濬備塘河運石。
entries.en: He then asked to dredge the backup seawall canal to transport building stone.
entries.literal: Later he again requested dredging the backup seawall canal to transport stone.

entries.zh: 五年，上諭曰：「盧焯至浙江，沽名邀譽，舉鄉賢名宦，絡繹不絕。
entries.en: In 1740 the emperor said: 'Since Lu Chao arrived in Zhejiang he has been currying favor, nominating local worthies and celebrated officials in an endless stream.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the emperor instructed: 'Since Lu Chao reached Zhejiang he has courted reputation and sought praise, recommending local worthies and famous officials without cease.

entries.zh: 海塘外已漲沙數十里，焯既請停草塘歲修，又請改建石塘。
entries.en: Sand had already built up for dozens of li beyond the seawall, yet Chao first asked to halt annual repairs to the earthen dike and then asked to rebuild it in stone.
entries.literal: Outside the seawall sand had already accreted for several tens of li; Chao had both requested stopping annual sod-wall repairs and requested rebuilding as a stone seawall.

entries.zh: 心無定見，惟事揣摩，已彰明較著矣。」
entries.en: He has no settled judgment and only tries to guess what I want—this is already perfectly obvious.'
entries.literal: His mind has no fixed view; he only guesses at what is wanted—this is already glaringly clear.'

entries.zh: 六年，左都御史劉吳龍劾焯營私受賄，上解焯任，命總督德沛、副都統旺扎爾按治，事皆實，請奪官刑訊。
entries.en: In 1741 Left Censor-in-chief Liu Wulong accused Chao of corruption and bribery. The emperor removed him from office and ordered Governor-general Depè and Vice Banner Commander Wangzhar to investigate; every charge was proved, and they recommended stripping his rank and putting him to the question.
entries.literal: In the sixth year Left Censor-in-chief Liu Wulong impeached Chao for private dealings and taking bribes. The emperor relieved Chao of his post and ordered Governor-general Depè and Vice Banner Commander Wangzhar to investigate; the charges were all substantiated, and they requested deprivation of office and interrogation under torture.

entries.zh: 事連嘉湖道呂守曾、嘉興知府楊景震。
entries.en: The case also involved Jiahu circuit intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing prefect Yang Jingzhen.
entries.literal: The case implicated Jiahu Circuit intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing prefect Yang Jingzhen.

entries.zh: 守曾已擢山西布政使，逮至浙江，自殺。
entries.en: Shouzeng had already been promoted to Shanxi treasurer; when he was arrested and brought to Zhejiang, he committed suicide.
entries.literal: Shouzeng had already been promoted to treasurer of Shanxi; when arrested and brought to Zhejiang, he killed himself.

entries.zh: 杭州民數百為焯訟冤，毀副都統廳前鼓亭。
entries.en: Several hundred Hangzhou residents marched to plead Chao's innocence and tore down the drum pavilion before the vice banner commander's office.
entries.literal: Several hundred Hangzhou residents petitioned on Chao's behalf, claiming injustice, and destroyed the drum pavilion in front of the vice banner commander's yamen.

entries.zh: 德沛等以聞，上諭責辦理不妥。
entries.en: Depè reported the incident, and the emperor rebuked them for mishandling the case.
entries.literal: Depè and the others reported this; the emperor instructed and rebuked them for improper handling.

entries.zh: 七年，讞上，焯、景震皆坐不枉法贓，擬絞。
entries.en: In 1742 the final judgment was handed up: Chao and Jingzhen were both found guilty of taking bribes without perverting justice and were sentenced to death by strangulation.
entries.literal: In the seventh year the verdict was submitted; Chao and Jingzhen were both convicted of taking bribes without perverting the law and were sentenced to strangulation.

entries.zh: 八年，焯以完贓減等，戍軍台。
entries.en: In 1743, because he had made full restitution, his sentence was reduced and he was exiled to garrison labor.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, because Chao made restitution of the illicit gains, his penalty was reduced by one degree and he was banished to military garrison service.

entries.zh: 十六年，上南巡，閱海塘，念焯勞，召還。
entries.en: In 1751, on a southern tour, the emperor inspected the seawall, remembered Chao's service, and recalled him.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, during the emperor's southern tour, he inspected the seawall and, recalling Chao's labors, summoned him back.

entries.zh: 二十年，擢巡撫。
entries.en: In 1755 he was promoted to governor.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was elevated to governor.

entries.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，江蘇布政使夏邑彭家屏以病告家居，覲徐州行在，入對，言鄉縣被水。
entries.en: In 1757, on the emperor's southern tour, Jiangsu treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, who had retired on grounds of illness, came to the traveling palace at Xuzhou, was granted an audience, and reported flooding in his home district.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, during the emperor's southern tour, Jiangsu treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, having reported illness and retired home, presented himself at the traveling palace in Xuzhou, was received in audience, and said his home county had suffered flooding.

entries.zh: 上諮圖爾炳阿，圖爾炳阿奏收成至九分，上責圖爾炳阿文過。
entries.en: The emperor asked Tu Erbing'a, who reported a harvest of ninety percent; the emperor rebuked him for whitewashing the situation.
entries.literal: The emperor consulted Tu Erbing'a; Tu Erbing'a memorialized that the harvest reached nine-tenths, and the emperor rebuked him for glossing over faults.

entries.zh: 圖爾炳阿又奏「去歲被水尚未成災」，上斥為怙惡不悛。
entries.en: Tu Erbing'a then reported that 'last year's floods have not yet amounted to a disaster,' and the emperor denounced him as incorrigible.
entries.literal: Tu Erbing'a again memorialized that 'last year's flooding has not yet become a disaster,' and the emperor denounced him as persisting in evil without repentance.

entries.zh: 遣員外郎觀音保密察災狀得實，上奪圖爾炳阿官，髮烏里雅蘇台效力。
entries.en: He sent Vice Director Guanyinbao to investigate in secret and confirmed the disaster. The emperor stripped Tu Erbing'a of his rank and sent him to serve at Uliastai.
entries.literal: He dispatched Vice Director Guanyinbao to investigate secretly; the disaster conditions were found true. The emperor stripped Tu Erbing'a of office and sent him to serve at Uliastai.

entries.zh: 上發徐州，夏邑民張欽、劉元德詣行在訴知縣孫默諱災及治賑不實，上親鞫，元德言諸生段昌緒指使。
entries.en: As the emperor left Xuzhou, Xiayi residents Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande came to the traveling palace to accuse Magistrate Sun Mo of concealing the disaster and bungling relief. The emperor questioned them personally, and Yuande said the student Duan Changxu had put them up to it.
entries.literal: As the emperor departed Xuzhou, Xiayi commoners Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande came to the traveling palace to accuse Magistrate Sun Mo of concealing the disaster and mishandling relief; the emperor personally examined them, and Yuande said the licentiate Duan Changxu had instigated them.

entries.zh: 上復遣侍衛成林會圖爾炳阿至夏邑按治，於昌緒家得傳鈔吳三桂檄。
entries.en: The emperor again sent Bodyguard Cheng Lin with Tu Erbing'a to investigate in Xiayi, where they found copied proclamations of Wu Sangui in Changxu's house.
entries.literal: The emperor again dispatched Bodyguard Cheng Lin to join Tu Erbing'a in going to Xiayi to investigate; at Changxu's home they found circulated copies of a proclamation of Wu Sangui.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「圖爾炳阿察出逆檄，緝邪之功大，諱災之罪小。
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Tu Erbing'a uncovered the seditious proclamation; his merit in rooting out sedition is great, and his offense in concealing the disaster is small.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Tu Erbing'a uncovered the treasonous proclamation—his merit in suppressing heterodoxy is great, his offense in concealing the disaster is small.

entries.zh: 且以如此梗不知化之民，而治其司牧者以罪，是不益長澆風乎？
entries.en: And for subjects this stubborn and unreformed, to punish their magistrates instead—would that not only encourage moral decay?
entries.literal: Moreover, for such stubborn and unregenerate commoners, to punish their local officials—would this not only encourage a degenerate trend?

entries.zh: 免圖爾炳阿罪，仍留巡撫任治賑。
entries.en: Tu Erbing'a was pardoned and kept in office as governor to oversee relief.
entries.literal: Tu Erbing'a's punishment was remitted and he was retained in the governorship to manage relief.

entries.zh: 圖爾炳阿若因有前此罪斥之旨，心存成見，或不釋然於災民，則是自取罪戾，亦不能逃朕洞鑑。」
entries.en: If Tu Erbing'a, remembering my earlier rebuke, holds a grudge or takes out his resentment on the flood victims, he will bring punishment on himself—and he cannot escape my scrutiny.'
entries.literal: If Tu Erbing'a, because of the earlier edict rebuking him, harbors prejudice or is not reconciled to the disaster victims, then he brings punishment on himself and cannot escape My penetrating scrutiny.'

entries.zh: 尋家屏亦以藏禁書罪至死，圖爾炳阿仍以匿災下吏議，奪官，命留任。
entries.en: Soon afterward Jiaping was also sentenced to death for hiding banned books; Tu Erbing'a was again referred to the courts for concealing the disaster, stripped of rank, but ordered to remain in office.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Jiaping was also sentenced to death for concealing banned books; Tu Erbing'a was still referred to the judicial authorities for concealing the disaster, stripped of office, but ordered to remain in his post.

entries.zh: 逾數月，召詣京師，命往烏里雅蘇台治餉。
entries.en: Several months later he was summoned to Beijing and sent to Uliastai to manage supplies.
entries.literal: After several months he was summoned to the capital and ordered to go to Uliastai to manage provisions.

entries.zh: 阿思哈，薩克達氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Asiha, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Asiha, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 自官學生考授內閣中書，累遷刑部郎中，充軍機處章京。
entries.en: Having passed the examination from the Imperial Academy, he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, rose through the Board of Punishments to director, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
entries.literal: From student of the Imperial Academy he passed examination for appointment as secretary in the Grand Secretariat, was promoted repeatedly to director in the Board of Punishments, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 乾隆十年，擢甘肅布政使。
entries.en: In 1745 he was promoted to provincial treasurer of Gansu.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he was elevated to treasurer of Gansu.

entries.zh: 十四年，擢江西巡撫。
entries.en: In 1749 he was made governor of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was elevated to governor of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 疏言：「各營操演槍砲，須實子彈。
entries.en: He memorialized: 'When garrisons drill with muskets and cannon, they must use live ammunition.
entries.literal: He memorialized: 'When each garrison drills with muskets and cannon, live ammunition is required.

entries.zh: 營馬應令騎兵自飼。
entries.en: Garrison horses should be fed by the cavalrymen themselves.
entries.literal: Garrison horses should be ordered to be fed by the cavalry themselves.

entries.zh: 技藝以純熟得用為要，步法、架勢不必朝更夕改。」
entries.en: Combat skill should be judged by practical mastery, not by constantly changing footwork and forms from day to day.'
entries.literal: In martial skill what matters is pure mastery that can be put to use; footwork and postures need not be changed morning and evening.'

entries.zh: 上嘉其言得要。
entries.en: The emperor praised his advice as sound.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his words as hitting the essential point.

entries.zh: 旋調山西。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.
entries.literal: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.

entries.zh: 十六年，平陽旱，未親往撫卹，詔責之。
entries.en: In 1751 Pingyang suffered drought, but he did not go in person to comfort the people, and an imperial edict rebuked him.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year Pingyang suffered drought; he did not go in person to comfort and relieve, and an edict rebuked him.

entries.zh: 十七年，蒲、解等處复災，請以平陽富民捐款解河東道加賑。
entries.en: In 1752 Pu, Xie, and other districts were hit again; he asked wealthy households in Pingyang to donate funds to the Hedong circuit for supplemental relief.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Pu, Xie, and other places again suffered disaster; he requested that wealthy households in Pingyang donate funds to be remitted to the Hedong Circuit for supplemental relief.

entries.zh: 上諭之曰：「賑濟蠲緩，重者數百萬，少亦數十萬，悉動正帑，從無顧惜。
entries.en: The emperor told him: 'Relief, tax remission, and deferments cost millions in the worst cases and hundreds of thousands in the least—all paid from the regular treasury without hesitation.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him: 'For relief, tax remission, and deferment, the heavy cases run to several millions and the light to several hundreds of thousands—all drawn from the regular treasury without stint.

entries.zh: 富戶所捐幾何，貯庫助賑，殊非體制。
entries.en: What can wealthy donors really contribute? Storing private donations in the treasury for relief is entirely improper.
entries.literal: How much can wealthy households donate? To store it in the treasury to aid relief is quite contrary to proper practice.

entries.zh: 此端一開，則偏災之地，貧民既苦艱食，富戶又令出貲。
entries.en: Once that door is opened, in every partial disaster the poor already go hungry while the rich are pressed for money too.
entries.literal: Once this precedent is opened, in locally stricken areas the poor already suffer from scarce food and the wealthy are again ordered to pay out funds.

entries.zh: 國家撫卹災黎，何忍出此？」
entries.en: When the state relieves disaster victims, how can we stoop to such a scheme?'
entries.literal: When the state comforts and relieves disaster victims, how can we bear to resort to this?'

entries.zh: 責阿思哈卑鄙錯謬，不勝巡撫任，召還，奪官。
entries.en: He condemned Asiha as mean and misguided, unfit to serve as governor, recalled him, and stripped his rank.
entries.literal: He rebuked Asiha as base and mistaken, unfit for the governorship, recalled him, and stripped his office.

entries.zh: 尋授吏部員外郎。
entries.en: He was soon appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

entries.zh: 二十年，命以布政使銜往準噶爾軍前經理糧運。
entries.en: In 1755 he was sent to the Zunghar front with treasurer's rank to manage grain supply.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered, with the rank of provincial treasurer, to go to the Zunghar front to manage grain transport.

entries.zh: 擢內閣學士。
entries.en: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: He was elevated to Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 三十五年，又調貴州。
entries.en: In 1770 he was transferred again, to Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was again transferred to Guizhou.

entries.zh: 桐梓縣民為亂，命速赴任，會湖廣總督吳達善捕治。
entries.en: When commoners in Tongzi County rebelled, he was ordered to take post quickly and join Huguang governor-general Wu Dashan in suppressing them.
entries.literal: Commoners of Tongzi County rose in disorder; he was ordered to hurry to his post and join Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan in suppressing them.

entries.zh: 亂定，古州黨堆寨苗香要等為亂，复偕吳達善督兵捕誅之。
entries.en: After that rebellion was crushed, the Miao leader Xiangyao and others at Dangdui Stockade in Guzhou rose again; Zhaolin again joined Wu Dashan in leading troops to capture and execute them.
entries.literal: When the disorder was settled, the Miao Xiangyao and others of Dangdui Stockade in Guzhou again rebelled; he again joined Wu Dashan in commanding troops to capture and execute them.

entries.zh: 兆麟奏黨堆寨苗老呴以阻香要亂被殺，令即寨立廟以祀良苗，並將死義被旌及香要叛逆伏誅狀，譯苗語榜廟門，俾令警戒；
entries.en: Zhaolin reported that Elder Xu of Dangdui Stockade had been killed for opposing Xiangyao's revolt. He had a temple built at the stockade to honor loyal Miao and posted notices in Miao at its gate describing those honored for dying in loyalty and Xiangyao's rebellion and execution, as a warning;
entries.literal: Zhaolin memorialized that the Miao elder Xu of Dangdui Stockade had been killed for blocking Xiangyao's rebellion; he ordered a temple built at the stockade to honor loyal Miao, and had the deeds of those who died loyally and were honored, and of Xiangyao's rebellion and execution, translated into Miao and posted at the temple gate for warning;

entries.zh: 並請移駐將吏，建下江營土城，駐兵鎮撫。
entries.en: He also asked to redeploy officers, build an earthen fort at Xiajiang Camp, and garrison troops to keep order.
entries.literal: He also requested relocating stationed officers, building an earthen fort at Xiajiang Camp, and stationing troops to pacify the region.

entries.zh: 是夏，兆麟奏請於鄰省湖南、四川、廣西買米運貴州糶濟。
entries.en: That summer Zhaolin asked permission to buy grain in Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi and ship it to Guizhou for relief sales.
entries.literal: That summer Zhaolin memorialized requesting to purchase grain in neighboring provinces Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi and transport it to Guizhou for sale as relief.

entries.zh: 至秋，豐收，復奏請停運。
entries.en: By autumn the harvest was good and he asked to halt the shipments.
entries.literal: By autumn the harvest was abundant, and he again memorialized requesting that transport be stopped.

entries.zh: 上斥其冒昧，勗令詳慎。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked his impulsiveness and urged greater care.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked his rashness and urged him to be thorough and cautious.

entries.zh: 兆麟復奏請簡發知府三員赴貴州，上以「此端一開，各省效尤，妨吏部選法；
entries.en: Zhaolin then asked that three prefects be specially sent to Guizhou. The emperor warned: 'Open that door and every province will follow, undermining the Board's appointment system;
entries.literal: Zhaolin again memorialized requesting that three prefects be specially dispatched to Guizhou; the emperor said: 'Once this precedent is opened, every province will follow suit and obstruct the Board's appointment methods;

entries.zh: 且開幸進之門」，下旨嚴飭。
entries.en: and it opens a path for favor-seekers.' A stern edict followed.'
entries.literal: moreover it opens a gate to lucky advancement,' and issued a stern edict of rebuke.'

entries.zh: 會貴州布政使觀音保入覲，訐兆麟粗率喜自誇，口給便捷，人號為「鐵嘴」。
entries.en: When Guizhou treasurer Guanyinbao came to court, he accused Zhaolin of being brash and boastful, quick-tongued and glib; people called him 'Iron Mouth.'
entries.literal: When Guizhou provincial treasurer Guanyinbao came to audience, he denounced Zhaolin as crude, reckless, and fond of boasting; quick with speech, he was called 'Iron Mouth.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「觀音保人已粗率，今尚以兆麟為粗率，則粗率更甚可知。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Guanyinbao is already a rough man; if even he finds Zhaolin crude, Zhaolin must be rougher still.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Guanyinbao is already crude and reckless; if he still finds Zhaolin crude and reckless, then Zhaolin must be cruder still, as one can infer.'

entries.zh: 諭兆麟猛省痛改。
entries.en: Zhaolin was told to take the warning to heart and mend his ways.
entries.literal: Zhaolin was instructed to reflect deeply and reform thoroughly.

entries.zh: 尋詔詣京師，降補甘肅按察使。
entries.en: He was soon summoned to the capital and demoted to provincial judge of Gansu.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward an edict summoned him to the capital and he was demoted to provincial judge of Gansu.

entries.zh: 三十六年，坐貴州任內失察廠員虧欠鉛斤，奪官。
entries.en: In 1771 he was stripped of rank for failing during his Guizhou tenure to detect lead shortages among factory clerks.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, for failure to detect during his Guizhou tenure that factory staff were deficient in lead owed, his office was stripped.

entries.zh: 四十一年，東巡，兆麟迎駕，詔與三品銜。
entries.en: During the emperor's 1776 eastern tour, Zhaolin met the procession and was granted third-rank insignia.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year, during the eastern tour, Zhaolin met the imperial procession and was granted third-rank insignia by edict.

entries.zh: 四十六年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1781.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year he died.

entries.zh: 四十五年，調江蘇。
entries.en: In 1780 he was transferred to Jiangsu.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 四十六年，甘肅布政使王亶望坐偽災冒賑得罪，事連鶚元弟同知鵷元。
entries.en: In 1781 Gansu treasurer Wang Tanwang was convicted of inventing a disaster to claim relief funds; the case also implicated Eyuan's younger brother, sub-prefect Yuanyuan.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year Gansu Provincial Treasurer Wang Tanwang was convicted for fabricating disaster and fraudulently claiming relief; the case implicated Eyuan's younger brother, sub-prefect Yuanyuan.

entries.zh: 上責鶚元隱忍瞻徇，知其事而不舉，降三品頂戴，停廉俸。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for covering up the affair and showing favoritism—he had known but not reported it. His rank insignia was reduced to third grade and his integrity stipend suspended.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for concealment and favoritism, knowing of the matter yet not reporting it; his insignia was reduced to third rank and his integrity stipend suspended.

entries.zh: 四十八年，還原品頂戴，支廉俸如故。
entries.en: In 1783 his original rank insignia and integrity stipend were restored.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year his original rank insignia was restored and his integrity stipend paid as before.

entries.zh: 五十年，江南旱。
entries.en: In 1785 Jiangnan suffered drought.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year Jiangnan suffered drought.

entries.zh: 五月，鶚元奏淮、徐、海三府如得雨二三寸，猶可種雜糧。
entries.en: In May Eyuan reported that in the Huai, Xu, and Hai prefectures, if two or three inches of rain fell, farmers might still plant secondary crops.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Eyuan memorialized that in the three prefectures of Huai, Xu, and Hai, if two or three inches of rain fell, miscellaneous grains could still be planted.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「得雨二三寸未為霑足，焉能種雜糧？
entries.en: The emperor replied: 'Two or three inches of rain is not enough to soak the fields—how can anyone plant secondary crops?
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Two or three inches of rain is not sufficient soaking—how can miscellaneous grains be planted?

entries.zh: 地方雨水，民瘼攸關。
entries.en: Local rainfall is a matter of the people's welfare.
entries.literal: Local rainfall is intimately tied to the people's suffering.

entries.zh: 鶚元何得含混入告？」
entries.en: How can Eyuan blur the truth in his reports?'
entries.literal: How can Eyuan mingle truth and falsehood in his reports?'

entries.zh: 尋奏請截漕十萬石，淮、徐、海三府州被災較重，碾米治賑，如所議行。
entries.en: Soon after he asked to divert 100,000 shi of tribute grain, mill it, and use it for relief in the harder-hit Huai, Xu, and Hai districts. The plan was approved.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized requesting diversion of one hundred thousand shi of tribute grain; the three prefectures and departments of Huai, Xu, and Hai had suffered more heavily, and rice was to be husked for relief—as deliberated, it was carried out.

entries.zh: 論曰：法者所以持天下之平。
entries.en: The historians comment: Law exists to uphold fairness in the realm.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Law is what upholds fairness under Heaven.

entries.zh: 人君馭群臣，既知其不肖，乃以一日之愛憎喜怒，屈法以從之，此非細故也。
entries.en: When a ruler already knows his ministers are unworthy yet bends the law to suit a passing mood of affection, anger, joy, or resentment, the consequences are grave.
entries.literal: When a ruler governs his ministers, having already known their unworthiness, yet bends the law to follow a day's love, hatred, joy, or anger—this is no small matter.

entries.zh: 焯、阿思哈、景素坐貪皆勘實，猶尚復起；
entries.en: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of corruption on solid evidence, yet were restored to office;
entries.literal: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of greed with substantiated investigations, yet were still restored;

entries.zh: 圖爾炳阿匿災至面謾，反誅告者；
entries.en: Tu Erbing'a concealed a disaster even to the emperor's face, yet those who reported it were punished;
entries.literal: Tu Erbing'a concealed disaster to the point of deceiving the emperor face to face, yet those who reported it were punished instead;

entries.zh: 兆麟口給，鶚元迎上指，至不勝疆政而始去之。
entries.en: Zhaolin was glib, Eyuan read the emperor's mind—only when they proved unfit for frontier rule were they finally removed.
entries.literal: Zhaolin was glib of tongue, Eyuan courted the emperor's intent—only when they could no longer bear frontier governance were they removed.

entries.zh: 高宗常謂：「朕非甚懦弱姑息之主，不能執法。」
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor often said: 'I am not so weak and indulgent that I cannot enforce the law.'
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor often said: 'I am not a very weak and indulgent ruler who cannot enforce the law.'

entries.zh: 執法固難，自克其愛憎喜怒，尤不易言也。
entries.en: Enforcing the law is hard enough; mastering one's own passions is harder still.
entries.literal: Enforcing the law is indeed difficult; to master one's own love, hatred, joy, and anger is even harder to speak of.

entries.zh: 二十年，授鴻臚寺少卿，署陝西西安巡撫。
entries.en: In 1755 he was made vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and served as acting governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acted as governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 二十一年，調署湖北，以陳宏謀代焯。
entries.en: In 1756 he was transferred to act as governor of Hubei, with Chen Hongmou slated to replace him.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to act in Hubei, with Chen Hongmou replacing Chao.

entries.zh: 宏謀未至，上命發歸化城米運金川饋軍，急驛諭宏謀。
entries.en: Before Hongmou arrived, the throne ordered grain from Guihua City shipped to supply the Jinchuan campaign and sent an urgent courier to inform Hongmou.
entries.literal: Before Hongmou arrived, the emperor ordered grain from Guihua City sent to provision the army in Jinchuan, urgently dispatching a courier to instruct Hongmou.

entries.zh: 焯發視，奏言：「歸化城雖產米，路遠費重；
entries.en: Chao investigated and reported: 'Guihua City does produce grain, but the route is long and the cost prohibitive;
entries.literal: Chao inspected and memorialized: 'Although Guihua City produces grain, the route is long and the cost heavy;

entries.zh: 西安有貯米，先發以饋軍。
entries.en: Xi'an has grain in store—let that be issued first to feed the troops.
entries.literal: Xi'an has stored grain—issue it first to provision the army.

entries.zh: 仍請擅行罪。」
entries.en: He still asked to be punished for acting without authorization.'
entries.literal: He still requested punishment for acting on his own authority.

entries.zh: 上嘉焯知大體，合機宜，實授湖北巡撫。
entries.en: The emperor praised Chao for understanding the larger situation and acting appropriately, and confirmed him as governor of Hubei.
entries.literal: The emperor praised Chao for grasping the larger situation and fitting the occasion, and formally appointed him governor of Hubei.

entries.zh: 二十二年，西安布政使劉藻入覲，言焯在西安入貢方物，但量給薄值；
entries.en: In 1757 Xi'an treasurer Liu Zao presented himself at court and reported that while in Xi'an Chao had accepted local tribute goods but paid only token prices;
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year Xi'an treasurer Liu Zao came to court and said that in Xi'an Chao had accepted tribute goods but only paid scant prices;

entries.zh: 及調任湖北，欲借庫帑，未應付。
entries.en: and that after moving to Hubei he had tried to borrow from the provincial treasury but had been refused.
entries.literal: and that after his transfer to Hubei he had wished to borrow from the treasury but had not been accommodated.

entries.zh: 上責焯負恩，奪官，戍巴里坤。
entries.en: The emperor accused Chao of betraying his favor, stripped his rank, and exiled him to Barkol.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Chao for ingratitude, stripped his office, and banished him to Barkol.

entries.zh: 二十六年，召還。
entries.en: In 1761 he was recalled.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was recalled.

entries.zh: 三十二年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1767.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he died.

entries.zh: 圖爾炳阿，佟佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Tu Erbing'a, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Tu Erbing'a, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 初授吏部筆帖式，累遷郎中。
entries.en: He began as a clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments and rose through successive promotions to director.
entries.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments and was promoted repeatedly to director.

entries.zh: 乾隆三年，授陝西甘肅道。
entries.en: In 1738 he was appointed intendant of the Shaanxi-Gansu circuit.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed to the Shaanxi-Gansu Circuit.

entries.zh: 累遷雲南布政使。
entries.en: He was eventually promoted to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.
entries.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to treasurer of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 十二年，擢巡撫。
entries.en: In 1747 he was made governor.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was elevated to governor.

entries.zh: 十五年，永嘉知縣楊茂虧銀米，圖爾炳阿令後政彌補結案。
entries.en: In 1750 Yongjia magistrate Yang Mao was found short in silver and grain; Tu Erbing'a ordered his successor to make good the deficit and closed the case.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Yongjia magistrate Yang Mao was short in silver and grain; Tu Erbing'a ordered his successor to make up the deficit and closed the case.

entries.zh: 總督碩色論劾，上責圖爾炳阿欺隱徇庇，奪官，逮京師，下刑部治罪，坐監守自盜，擬斬監候。
