entries.en: Governor-general Shuose memorialized against him; the emperor condemned Tu Erbing'a for covering up the case and showing favoritism, stripped his rank, had him brought to Beijing, and referred him to the Board of Punishments, which convicted him of custodial embezzlement and sentenced him to beheading, commuted after review.
entries.literal: Governor-general Shuose impeached him in a memorial; the emperor rebuked Tu Erbing'a for concealment and favoritism, stripped his office, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and handed him to the Board of Punishments, which convicted him of custodial theft and sentenced him to beheading after the autumn assizes.

entries.zh: 十七年，上以圖爾炳阿贓未入己，釋出獄。
entries.en: In 1752 the emperor ruled that Tu Erbing'a had not personally profited from the shortfall and released him from prison.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor, because Tu Erbing'a's illicit gains had not entered his own pocket, released him from prison.

entries.zh: 授吏部員外郎。
entries.en: He was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
entries.literal: He was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

entries.zh: 未幾，授河南布政使，調山東，又復還河南。
entries.en: Soon after he was made treasurer of Henan, transferred to Shandong, and then sent back to Henan.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed treasurer of Henan, transferred to Shandong, and then returned again to Henan.

entries.zh: 二十二年，命署江西巡撫，蒞任，清理屯田，尋真除。
entries.en: In 1757 he was appointed acting governor of Jiangxi; on taking office he sorted out garrison land tenure and was soon confirmed in the post.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to act as governor of Jiangxi; on assuming office he cleared up garrison fields, and shortly afterward received formal appointment.

entries.zh: 學政謝溶生劾阿思哈婪賄派累，命尚書劉統勳、侍郎常鈞等按鞫，得實，擬絞。
entries.en: Provincial education commissioner Xie Rongsheng impeached Asiha for extortion and corrupt levies. The emperor ordered Minister Liu Tongxun, Vice Minister Chang Jun, and others to investigate; the charges proved true and strangulation was recommended.
entries.literal: The provincial education commissioner Xie Rongsheng impeached Asiha for greedily accepting bribes and imposing burdensome levies; the emperor ordered Ministers Liu Tongxun and Vice Minister Chang Jun and others to investigate and try the case; the charges were found true, and strangulation was proposed.

entries.zh: 二十六年，詔免罪，以三品頂戴髮烏魯木齊效力。
entries.en: In 1761 he was pardoned by edict and sent to serve at Urumqi with third-rank insignia.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year an edict pardoned his crime; with third-rank hat insignia he was dispatched to Urumqi to serve.

entries.zh: 二十八年，命往伊犁協同辦事。
entries.en: In 1763 he was assigned to Ili to assist in local administration.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was ordered to go to Ili to assist in affairs.

entries.zh: 三十四年，擢雲貴總督。
entries.en: In 1769 he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 師徵緬甸，阿思哈出銅壁關至蠻暮軍中，奏軍中糧馬不敷。
entries.en: During the Burma campaign Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to the army at Manmu and reported shortages of grain and horses.
entries.literal: When the army marched against Burma, Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to the army at Manmu and memorialized that army grain and horses were insufficient.

entries.zh: 上責其畏難，解任，以副都統銜在領隊大臣上行走。
entries.en: The emperor accused him of shrinking from hardship, removed him from office, and assigned him to serve under the expedition commander with assistant commandant's rank.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him for fearing hardship; he was dismissed from office and, with the rank of assistant commandant, was ordered to serve under the expedition commander.

entries.zh: 旋召為吏部侍郎，入對失上指，奪官，戍伊犁。
entries.en: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, but in audience he displeased the emperor, was stripped of rank, and exiled to Ili.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments; in audience he missed the emperor's intent; his office was stripped and he was exiled to Ili.

entries.zh: 三十九年，釋回，仍充軍機章京。
entries.en: In 1774 he was released and restored as a grand council clerk.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was released and returned, again serving as a grand council clerk.

entries.zh: 擢左都御史。
entries.en: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 大學士舒赫德師討王倫，命阿思哈偕額駙拉旺多爾濟率健銳、火器兩營以往。
entries.en: When Grand Secretary Suhede marched against Wang Lun, Asiha was ordered to accompany Imperial Son-in-Law Lawang Duo'erji at the head of the Elite and Firearms brigades.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Suhede led troops to suppress Wang Lun; Asiha was ordered to accompany Imperial Son-in-Law Lawang Duo'erji leading the Elite and Firearms brigades.

entries.zh: 事定，拉旺多爾濟言城北搜剿王倫餘黨，阿思哈未同往，下吏議，奪官，命留任。
entries.en: After the rebellion was suppressed, Lawang Duo'erji reported that Asiha had not joined a search north of the city for Wang Lun's remaining followers. Officials were ordered to investigate; he was stripped of rank but allowed to keep his post.
entries.literal: When matters were settled, Lawang Duo'erji reported that in searching north of the city for Wang Lun's remaining followers Asiha had not gone along; the case was referred to officials for deliberation, his office was stripped, but he was ordered to remain in his post.

entries.zh: 四十一年，署吏部尚書，旋授漕運總督。
entries.en: In 1776 he served as acting minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then was appointed grain transport governor-general.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year he acted as minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then was appointed grain transport governor-general.

entries.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡莊恪。
entries.en: He died and was granted state funeral honors; his posthumous title was Zhuangke ('Steadfast and Reverent').
entries.literal: He died; imperial sacrifices and burial honors were granted, and he was posthumously titled Zhuangke.

entries.zh: 阿思哈初撫江西，上眷之獨厚。
entries.en: When Asiha first governed Jiangxi, the emperor favored him unusually.
entries.literal: When Asiha first served as governor of Jiangxi, the emperor favored him with special warmth.

entries.zh: 廣西巡撫衛哲治入覲，上問各省督撫孰為最劣，哲治引罪，上謂：「姑置汝！」
entries.en: When Guangxi governor Wei Zhezhi came to court, the emperor asked who among the provincial governors was the worst. Zhezhi took the blame himself. The emperor said: 'Never mind you for now—'
entries.literal: Guangxi governor Wei Zhezhi came to audience; the emperor asked which governor or governor-general in the provinces was worst; Zhezhi pleaded guilty; the emperor said: 'Leave you aside for now!'

entries.zh: 哲治舉阿思哈對，時以為難能。
entries.en: Zhezhi named Asiha instead. At the time many considered that a remarkable act of candor.
entries.literal: Zhezhi named Asiha in reply; at the time this was regarded as a difficult feat.

entries.zh: 宮兆麟，字伯厚，江南懷遠人。
entries.en: Gong Zhaolin, styled Bohou, was from Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Gong Zhaolin, courtesy name Bohou, was a native of Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 自貢生授湖北安陸通判，累遷至山東糧道。
entries.en: Starting as a presented scholar appointed Anlu subprefect in Hubei, he rose through successive posts to grain intendant of Shandong.
entries.literal: From presented scholar he was appointed Anlu subprefect in Hubei, and through successive promotions reached grain intendant of Shandong.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十一年，授湖南按察使。
entries.en: In 1766 he was appointed provincial judge of Hunan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he was appointed provincial judge of Hunan.

entries.zh: 桂陽州民侯七郎毆殺從兄岳添，賄其兄學添自承。
entries.en: Hou Qilang, a commoner of Guiyang Prefecture, beat his cousin Yue Tian to death and bribed his elder brother Xue Tian to confess on his behalf.
entries.literal: A commoner of Guiyang Prefecture, Hou Qilang, beat to death his cousin Yue Tian; he bribed his elder brother Xue Tian to confess in his stead.

entries.zh: 知州張宏燧讞上，巡撫李因培疑之，令兆麟詳鞫得實。
entries.en: Prefect Zhang Hongsui sent up the verdict, but Governor Li Yinpei was suspicious and had Zhaolin conduct a detailed trial; the facts came out.
entries.literal: Prefect Zhang Hongsui submitted the verdict upward; Governor Li Yinpei was suspicious and ordered Zhaolin to examine and try the case in detail; the truth was obtained.

entries.zh: 因培調福建去，巡撫常鈞庇宏燧，以七郎呼冤劾兆麟，兆麟亦入奏。
entries.en: After Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun shielded Hongsui and impeached Zhaolin, citing Qilang's cry of injustice. Zhaolin also memorialized the throne.
entries.literal: When Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun shielded Hongsui; Qilang cried injustice and impeached Zhaolin, and Zhaolin also memorialized the throne.

entries.zh: 上遣侍郎期成額會總督定長按治，如兆麟讞；
entries.en: The emperor sent Vice Minister Qicheng'e with Governor-General Ding Chang to investigate; the case followed Zhaolin's findings;
entries.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Qicheng'e to join Governor-General Ding Chang in investigating and handling the case according to Zhaolin's verdict;

entries.zh: 兆麟又發宏燧買金行賄狀，期成額等奏聞，逮訊，買金非行賄，乃迎合因培及湖北布政使赫升額意指，代武陵知縣馮其柘補虧空。
entries.en: Zhaolin also uncovered Hongsui's gold purchases. After Qicheng'e reported this and arrests were made, it emerged that the gold was not a bribe but had been bought to oblige Yinpei and Hubei treasurer Hesheng'e and to make up a deficit for Wuling magistrate Feng Qizhe.
entries.literal: Zhaolin further exposed Hongsui's act of purchasing gold to bribe; Qicheng'e and others memorialized; on arrest and interrogation, the gold purchase was not bribery but rather complied with Yinpei and Hubei provincial treasurer Hesheng'e's wishes to cover Wuling magistrate Feng Qizhe's deficit.

entries.zh: 因培、赫升額、常鈞、宏燧皆坐譴。
entries.en: Yinpei, Hesheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all punished.
entries.literal: Yinpei, Hesheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all punished for their involvement.

entries.zh: 三十二年，兆麟調雲南按察使。
entries.en: In 1767 Zhaolin was transferred to provincial judge of Yunnan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year Zhaolin was transferred to provincial judge of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 三十三年，遷布政使，擢廣西巡撫。
entries.en: In 1768 he became provincial treasurer and was promoted governor of Guangxi.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he was moved to provincial treasurer and promoted governor of Guangxi.

entries.zh: 雲南軍營需硝，敕兆麟籌畫，兆麟以廣西舊存硝七萬七千餘斤運剝隘，复撥通省營貯火藥二十萬斤繼運，得旨嘉許。
entries.en: When Yunnan's military camps needed saltpeter, the emperor ordered Zhaolin to arrange supply. He shipped over 77,000 jin of saltpeter stored in Guangxi to Bo'ai, then forwarded 200,000 jin of gunpowder from Guangxi arsenals. The emperor praised the effort.
entries.literal: Yunnan's military camps needed saltpeter; an edict ordered Zhaolin to plan supplies; Zhaolin shipped more than seventy-seven thousand jin of saltpeter previously stored in Guangxi to Bo'ai, then allocated two hundred thousand jin of gunpowder stored in camps province-wide for continued transport; an approving edict was received.

entries.zh: 調湖南。
entries.en: He was transferred to Hunan.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Hunan.

entries.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，大學士舒赫德督兵討之。
entries.en: In 1774 Wang Lun led a rebellion in Shouzhang; Grand Secretary Suhede took command against him.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year commoners of Shouzhang, Wang Lun, rebelled; Grand Secretary Suhede commanded troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 上命景素具車馬濟師，令分守河西。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Jingsu to supply transport for the army and hold the west bank of the river.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Jingsu to provide carts and horses to aid the army and commanded him to hold the west bank of the river separately.

entries.zh: 賊以糧艘結浮橋欲渡，景素與總兵萬朝興、副將瑪爾當阿等督兵御之，董勸回民助師。
entries.en: The rebels lashed grain boats into a pontoon to cross the river. Jingsu, Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others held them off and rallied local Muslims to support the army.
entries.literal: The rebels joined grain boats into a pontoon bridge to cross; Jingsu with Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others commanded troops to resist, and urged Hui people to assist the army.

entries.zh: 夜焚橋，賊不得渡。
entries.en: They burned the bridge by night and kept the rebels from crossing.
entries.literal: At night they burned the bridge, and the rebels could not cross.

entries.zh: 事旋定，擢山東巡撫。
entries.en: After the rebellion was crushed he was promoted governor of Shandong.
entries.literal: Matters were soon settled, and he was promoted governor of Shandong.

entries.zh: 疏請編查保甲。
entries.en: He memorialized asking to compile and inspect baojia registers.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting compilation and inspection of baojia household registers.

entries.zh: 四十年，疏請選京師健銳、火器營裨佐發山東，司營伍教演。
entries.en: In 1775 he asked that adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades be sent to Shandong to train local garrisons.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized requesting selection of adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades to be sent to Shandong to manage camp drill and instruction.

entries.zh: 四十一年，上東巡，臨視臨清毀橋斷道及亂民竄據所在，景素述當時戰狀，上嘉其勞，賜黃馬褂。
entries.en: During the 1776 eastern tour the emperor inspected Linqing, where bridges had been destroyed and rebels had held ground. Jingsu described the fighting; the emperor praised his service and granted him a yellow jacket.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year, during the emperor's eastern tour, he personally viewed the destroyed bridges and severed roads at Linqing and where rebels had lurked; Jingsu narrated the fighting at the time; the emperor praised his labors and granted a yellow jacket.

entries.zh: 汶上宋家窪舊渠淤墊，瀦水淹民田。
entries.en: The old canal at Songjiawa in Wenshang had silted up and standing water was flooding farmland.
entries.literal: At Songjiawa in Wenshang the old canal was silted and choked, and pooled water flooded commoners' fields.

entries.zh: 四十二年，景素奏請濬舊渠，並開支河二，令仍趨南陽、昭陽二湖，下部議行。
entries.en: In 1777 he asked to dredge the old canal and cut two branch channels to restore flow to Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes. The ministries approved.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year Jingsu memorialized requesting dredging of the old canal and opening two branch channels so water would again flow toward Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes; the memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

entries.zh: 擢兩廣總督，四十三年，調閩浙。
entries.en: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, then in 1778 transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was promoted governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; in the forty-third year he was transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 疏言：「浙西歉收，總督楊廷璋請撥台灣倉穀十萬接濟。
entries.en: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang had a poor harvest. Governor-General Yang Tingzhang asked to draw 100,000 shi of grain from Taiwan's granaries for relief.
entries.literal: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang suffered poor harvest; Governor-General Yang Tingzhang requested allocation of one hundred thousand shi of Taiwan granary grain for relief.

entries.zh: 北風盛發，未能即到。
entries.en: Strong north winds would delay shipment.
entries.literal: North winds were strong and the grain could not arrive immediately.

entries.zh: 請於福州、福寧、興化、泉州四府屬撥倉穀十萬，聽商運赴嘉、湖出糶；
entries.en: He proposed releasing 100,000 shi from granaries in Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou and letting merchants haul it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for relief sales;
entries.literal: He requested that one hundred thousand shi of granary grain be drawn from the four prefectures of Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou, allowing merchants to transport it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for sale as relief;

entries.zh: 仍飭台灣運歸四府補倉。」
entries.en: Taiwan's granaries would later be restocked to replace the four prefectures' reserves.'
entries.literal: Taiwan grain was still to be ordered transported back to replenish the four prefectures' granaries.'

entries.zh: 得旨嘉獎。
entries.en: The emperor approved and commended the plan.
entries.literal: An approving edict was received with commendation.

entries.zh: 四十四年，調直隸。
entries.en: In 1779 he was transferred to Zhili.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili.

entries.zh: 薦於易簡為布政使，上以易簡為大學士敏中弟，責景素。
entries.en: He recommended Yu Yijian as treasurer, but the emperor rebuked him because Yijian was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong.
entries.literal: He recommended Yu Yijian for provincial treasurer; the emperor, since Yijian was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong, rebuked Jingsu.

entries.zh: 十二月，卒，贈太子太保，賜卹如例。
entries.en: He died in the twelfth month and was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the usual mourning honors.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he died; he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bereavement grants were awarded according to precedent.

entries.zh: 閔鶚元，字少儀，浙江歸安人。
entries.en: Min Eyuan, styled Shaoyi, was from Gui'an in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Min Eyuan, courtesy name Shaoyi, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 乾隆十年進士，授刑部主事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in 1745 and was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.
entries.literal: A jinshi in the tenth year of Qianlong, he was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.

entries.zh: 再遷郎中，督山東學政。
entries.en: He was promoted to director and appointed Shandong provincial education commissioner.
entries.literal: After a further promotion to director, he supervised as Shandong provincial education commissioner.

entries.zh: 二十七年，自學政授山東按察使，調安徽。
entries.en: In 1762 he moved from education commissioner to provincial judge of Shandong, then transferred to Anhui.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, from education commissioner he was appointed provincial judge of Shandong, then transferred to Anhui.

entries.zh: 遷湖北布政使，調廣西、江寧。
entries.en: He became treasurer of Hubei and served successively in Guangxi and Jiangning.
entries.literal: He was promoted provincial treasurer of Hubei, transferred to Guangxi and Jiangning.

entries.zh: 四十一年，遷安徽巡撫。
entries.en: In 1776 he was transferred to governor of Anhui.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to governor of Anhui.

entries.zh: 四十四年，雲貴總督李侍堯以贓敗，罪至斬，下大學士、九卿議，請從重立決；
entries.en: In 1779 Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Li Shiyao was convicted of corruption, a capital offense. The case went to the grand secretaries and Nine Ministers, who recommended immediate execution;
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Li Shiyao was ruined by bribery; the offense warranted decapitation. The case was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for deliberation, who requested immediate execution with aggravated severity;

entries.zh: 復下各省督撫議，咸請如大學士九卿議。
entries.en: The case was then sent to every provincial governor for comment; all endorsed the capital recommendation.
entries.literal: It was again referred to the governors-general and governors of each province for deliberation; all requested conformity with the grand secretaries' and Nine Ministers' recommendation.

entries.zh: 鶚元窺上指欲寬侍堯，獨奏言：「侍堯歷任封疆，勤幹有為，中外推服。
entries.en: Eyuan sensed that the emperor wished to spare Shiyao and alone memorialized: 'Shiyao has served on the frontiers with diligence and ability, and is respected throughout the bureaucracy.
entries.literal: Eyuan divined that the emperor wished to be lenient toward Shiyao and alone memorialized: 'Shiyao has served on the frontiers, diligent and capable, admired within and without.

entries.zh: 請用議勤、議能例，稍寬一線。」
entries.en: He asked that the precedents for rewarding diligence and ability be applied to grant him a measure of clemency.'
entries.literal: He requested application of the precedents for deliberating on diligence and on ability, with a slight margin of leniency.'

entries.zh: 上從之，侍堯得復起。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, and Shiyao was restored to office.
entries.literal: The emperor assented, and Shiyao was able to rise again.

entries.zh: 五十五年，高郵巡檢陳倚道察知書吏偽印重徵，知州吳瑍置不問；
entries.en: In 1790 Gaoyou inspector Chen Yidao discovered that clerks had used forged seals to levy extra taxes; Prefect Wu Yin ignored it;
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year Gaoyou sub-prefectural inspector Chen Yidao detected that clerks had used forged seals to levy extra taxes; Prefect Wu Yin took no action;

entries.zh: 牒上，鶚元亦置不問，揭報戶部。
entries.en: when the report reached Eyuan, he too ignored it and merely forwarded it to the Board of Revenue.
entries.literal: when the report was forwarded upward, Eyuan also took no action and merely forwarded it to the Board of Revenue.

entries.zh: 上諮鶚元，鶚元猶庇瑍不以實陳，乃遣尚書慶桂、侍郎王昶按治；
entries.en: The emperor questioned Eyuan, who still shielded Yin and did not tell the truth. The emperor then sent Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang to investigate;
entries.literal: The emperor questioned Eyuan; Eyuan still shielded Yin and did not report truthfully, whereupon Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang were dispatched to investigate;

entries.zh: 責鶚元欺罔，奪官，逮鶚元等下刑部治罪。
entries.en: Eyuan was condemned for deceit, stripped of rank, and arrested with his associates for trial by the Board of Punishments.
entries.literal: Eyuan was rebuked for deception, stripped of office, and Eyuan and others were arrested and handed to the Board of Punishments for trial.

entries.zh: 巡撫福崧劾鶚元得句容知縣王光陛牒發糧書侵挪錢糧，但令江寧府察覈。
entries.en: Governor Fusong also accused Eyuan of receiving a report from Jurong magistrate Wang Guangbi exposing grain clerks' embezzlement, yet referring it only to Jiangning prefecture for review.
entries.literal: Governor Fusong impeached Eyuan for receiving a dispatch from Jurong Magistrate Wang Guangbi exposing grain clerks' embezzlement of funds and grain, yet only ordering Jiangning Prefecture to investigate.

entries.zh: 上責鶚元玩視民瘼，徇情骫法，命置重典。
entries.en: The emperor condemned Eyuan for neglecting the people's welfare and bending the law out of favoritism, and ordered severe punishment.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for treating the people's suffering lightly and bending the law out of personal favor, ordering severe punishment.

entries.zh: 獄具，擬斬立決，命改監候。
entries.en: The verdict recommended immediate execution; the emperor commuted the sentence to imprisonment pending review.
entries.literal: When the case was concluded, immediate decapitation was recommended; the emperor ordered commutation to imprisonment awaiting autumn review.

entries.zh: 五十六年，釋還裡。
entries.en: In 1791 he was released and sent home.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was released and returned home.

entries.zh: 嘉慶二年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1797.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he died.

entries.zh: 楊景素，字樸園，江南甘泉人，提督捷孫。
entries.en: Yang Jingsu, styled Puyuan, was from Ganquan in Jiangnan and grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.
entries.literal: Yang Jingsu, courtesy name Puyuan, was a native of Ganquan in Jiangnan, grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.

entries.zh: 父鑄，古北口總兵。
entries.en: His father Zhu was garrison commander at Gubeikou.
entries.literal: His father Zhu was commander at Gubeikou.

entries.zh: 景素孱弱，不好章句，貧不能自給。
entries.en: Jingsu was sickly, had no taste for classical scholarship, and was too poor to support himself.
entries.literal: Jingsu was frail and weak, disliked textual study, and in poverty could not support himself.

entries.zh: 入貲授縣丞，發直隸河工效力。
entries.en: He bought his way into office as a county assistant magistrate and was assigned to Zhili river works.
entries.literal: He entered office by purchase of rank as county assistant magistrate and was sent to serve on Zhili river works.

entries.zh: 乾隆三年，補蠡縣縣丞，累遷保定知府。
entries.en: In 1738 he became assistant magistrate of Li County and rose through successive posts to prefect of Baoding.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed county assistant magistrate of Li County, and through successive promotions reached prefect of Baoding.

entries.zh: 十八年，授福建汀漳龍道。
entries.en: In 1753 he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long circuit in Fujian.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian.

entries.zh: 漳浦民蔡榮祖欲為亂，景素率營卒擒斬之。
entries.en: When Zhangpu commoner Cai Rongzu plotted rebellion, Jingsu led garrison troops to capture and execute him.
entries.literal: A commoner of Zhangpu, Cai Rongzu, intended to rebel; Jingsu led camp soldiers to capture and execute him.

entries.zh: 調台灣道。
entries.en: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.

entries.zh: 釐定漢民墾種地，並生熟番界址。
entries.en: He fixed the boundaries of Han settlers' reclaimed land and the frontier between raw and acculturated aboriginal peoples.
entries.literal: He fixed boundaries of Han reclaimed land and of raw and acculturated aboriginal territories.

entries.zh: 革遊民為通譯而不法者，代以熟番。
entries.en: He removed lawless Han vagrants who worked as interpreters and replaced them with acculturated aborigines.
entries.literal: He eliminated indigent Han who served as interpreters but acted lawlessly, replacing them with acculturated aborigines.

entries.zh: 又禁入山採木，借修造戰船材料為名，累諸番。
entries.en: He also banned timber gathering in the hills under the pretext of supplying warship repairs, a burden long imposed on the aborigines.
entries.literal: He also forbade entering the mountains to cut timber under the pretext of gathering materials to repair and build war vessels, which had burdened the aborigines.

entries.zh: 三十三年，授河南按察使。
entries.en: In 1768 he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.

entries.zh: 三十五年，擢甘肅布政使，調直隸。
entries.en: In 1770 he became treasurer of Gansu and was transferred to Zhili.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted provincial treasurer of Gansu and transferred to Zhili.

entries.zh: 命從尚書裘曰修勘察堤埝各工。
entries.en: He was ordered to accompany Minister Qiu Yixiu on inspections of dikes and embankments.
entries.literal: He was ordered to follow Minister Qiu Yixiu in inspecting dikes and embankment works.

entries.zh: 坐失察雄縣知縣胡錫瑛侵蝕災賑，下吏議，奪官，命留任，俟八年無過，方准開復。
entries.en: He was stripped of rank for failing to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, but allowed to remain in office; restoration would come only after eight years without fault.
entries.literal: For failure to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, the case was referred to officials; his office was stripped but he was ordered to remain in post, and only after eight years without fault would restoration be permitted.

entries.zh: 列傳一百二十四
entries.en: Biography 124
entries.literal: Biographies, Number 124

entries.zh: 乾隆二十六年，成進士，殿試進呈卷列第三。
entries.en: In 1761 he passed the metropolitan examination and took his jinshi degree; his palace-examination paper was ranked third among those presented to the throne.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he became a jinshi; in the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third.

entries.zh: 高宗熟視字體如素識，以昔為尹繼善繕疏，曾邀宸賞，詢知人品，即拔置第一。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor studied his calligraphy as if it were already familiar—he had once written drafts for Yin Jishan and won the emperor's notice—and on learning who he was, promptly placed him first.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor scrutinized his handwriting as if he had known it before; because in the past he had drafted memorials for Yin Jishan and had once won imperial approval, upon inquiry learning his character, he immediately raised him to first place.

entries.zh: 及引見，風度凝然，上益喜。
entries.en: When he was brought before the throne, his deportment was grave and steady, which pleased the emperor still more.
entries.literal: When he was presented for audience, his bearing was composed and dignified; the emperor was all the more pleased.

entries.zh: 又以陝人入本朝百餘年無大魁者，時值西陲戡定，魁選適得西人，御製詩以紀其事。
entries.en: Moreover, no native of Shaanxi had won first place in the examinations in over a century of the dynasty; with the western campaigns just concluded, the top graduate happened to come from the west, and the emperor wrote a verse to mark the occasion.
entries.literal: Moreover, for more than a century since the dynasty's founding no Shaanxi native had taken the highest honors; at this time the western frontier had just been pacified, and the top choice happened to be a westerner—the emperor composed a poem to commemorate the event.

entries.zh: 尋直南書房，屢司文柄。
entries.en: He was soon posted to the Southern Imperial Study and repeatedly oversaw literary and examination affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was assigned to the Southern Imperial Study and repeatedly held charge of literary affairs at court.

entries.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。
entries.en: After five promotions he rose to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of Academician of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 三十九年，授刑部侍郎，調吏部，擢左都御史。
entries.en: In 1774 he was made vice minister of justice, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed vice minister of justice, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and promoted to censor-in-chief of the Left.

entries.zh: 四十八年，丁母憂，即家擢兵部尚書。
entries.en: In 1783, while mourning his mother at home, he was promoted to minister of war.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he entered mourning for his mother; while still at home he was promoted to minister of war.

entries.zh: 車駕南巡，傑赴行在謝，上曰：「汝來甚好。
entries.en: When the emperor toured the south, Jie went to the traveling palace to give thanks; the emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage made its southern tour, Jie went to the traveling palace to give thanks; the emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.

entries.zh: 君臣久別，應知朕念汝。
entries.en: After so long a separation between ruler and minister, you ought to know that I have been thinking of you.
entries.literal: Ruler and minister have been long parted; you ought to know that I have been thinking of you.

entries.zh: 然汝儒者，不欲奪汝情，歸終制可也。」
entries.en: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your filial duty—you may return and complete the full mourning period."
entries.literal: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your filial feeling—you may return and complete the full mourning period."

entries.zh: 服闋，還朝。
entries.en: When the mourning period ended, he returned to court.
entries.literal: When the mourning period ended, he returned to court.

entries.zh: 五十一年，命為軍機大臣、上書房總師傅。
entries.en: In 1786 he was appointed Grand Councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.

entries.zh: 次年，拜東閣大學士，管理禮部。
entries.en: The following year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Board of Rites.
entries.literal: The following year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Board of Rites.

entries.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後平，兩次圖形紫光閣，加太子太保。
entries.en: After Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession, his portrait was twice placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession; twice his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 誥既以喪歸，川、楚兵事方亟，高宗欲召之，每見大臣，數問；
entries.en: After Gao returned home in mourning, the Sichuan and Huguang campaigns were urgent; the Qianlong Emperor wished to recall him and asked repeatedly whenever he saw senior ministers;
entries.literal: After Gao returned home in mourning, military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang were urgent; the Gaozong Emperor wished to summon him and whenever he saw great ministers asked repeatedly;

entries.zh: 「董誥何時來？」
entries.en: "When will Dong Gao come?"
entries.literal: "When will Dong Gao come?"

entries.zh: 逾年，葬母畢，詣京師，和珅遏不上聞。
entries.en: After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital; Heshen blocked the report from reaching the emperor.
entries.literal: After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital; Heshen blocked the report from reaching the emperor.

entries.zh: 會駕出，誥於道旁謝恩，高宗見之，喜甚，命暫署刑部尚書，素服視事，不預典禮，專辦秋讞及軍營紀略，且曰：「誥守制已逾小祥，不得已用人之苦心，眾當共諒。」
entries.en: When the imperial carriage went out, Gao gave thanks by the roadside; the Qianlong Emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, ordering him temporarily to act as minister of justice in plain mourning dress, excluding him from ceremonies but putting him in charge of autumn assizes and military summaries, and saying: "Gao's mourning has already passed the lesser anniversary; the bitter necessity of using him—everyone should understand."
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage went out, Gao gave thanks by the roadside; the Gaozong Emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, ordering him temporarily to act as minister of justice, to handle affairs in plain mourning dress without taking part in ceremonies, and to specialize in autumn assizes and military camp summaries, saying: "Gao's mourning observance has already passed the lesser anniversary; the bitter necessity of using a man—everyone should understand together."

entries.zh: 尋以王三槐就擒，與軍機大臣同被議敘。
entries.en: Soon, when Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received commendation along with the Grand Councilors.
entries.literal: Soon, because Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received commendation along with the Grand Councilors.

entries.zh: 四年春，高宗崩，和珅伏誅，命誥复直軍機，晉太子太保。
entries.en: In the spring of 1799 the Qianlong Emperor died; Heshen was executed; Gao was ordered back to regular Grand Council duty and promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; Heshen was executed; Gao was ordered to resume regular Grand Council duty and was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 既，服闋，授文華殿大學士，兼刑部尚書如故。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while continuing as minister of justice.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and continued as before as minister of justice.

entries.zh: 高宗山陵禮成，命題神主，晉太子太傅。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed, he was ordered to compose the spirit-tablet inscription and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed, he was ordered to compose the spirit tablet inscription and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 七年，三省教匪平，予騎都尉世職。
entries.en: In 1802 the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified; he was given a hereditary post as commandant of cavalry.
entries.literal: In the seventh year the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified; he was given a hereditary post as commandant of cavalry.

entries.zh: 十二年，高宗實錄告成，詔以誥在館八年，始終其事，特加優獎，賜其父邦達入祀賢良祠。
entries.en: In 1807 the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed; an edict noted that Gao had spent eight years in the project office and seen it through from start to finish, gave him special commendation, and granted his father Bangda enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthies.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year the Veritable Records of the Gaozong Emperor were completed; an edict said that because Gao had been in the project office eight years and had seen it through from start to finish, he received special commendation and his father Bangda was granted enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthies.

entries.zh: 十四年，萬壽慶典，晉太子太師。
entries.en: In 1809, at the longevity celebration, he was promoted to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the longevity celebration, he was promoted to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 充上書房總師傅。
entries.en: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.
entries.literal: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.

entries.zh: 十七年，晉太保。
entries.en: In 1812 he was promoted to Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 洎仁宗親政，傑為首輔，遇事持大體，竭誠進諫，上優禮之。
entries.en: When the Jiaqing Emperor took personal rule, Jie became chief minister; he upheld the larger principles in policy, admonished with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with exceptional favor.
entries.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took personal rule, Jie became chief minister; in affairs he upheld the larger pattern, admonished with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with special favor.

entries.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，溫詔慰留，許扶杖入朝。
entries.en: In 1800, citing age and illness he asked to retire; a warm edict urged him to stay and allowed him to attend court with a walking staff.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, citing age and illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, permitting him to attend court leaning on a staff.

entries.zh: 七年，固請致仕，晉太子太傅，在籍食俸。
entries.en: In 1802 he firmly asked to retire; he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and drew salary in his native place.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he firmly requested to retire from office; he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and received salary while at home.

entries.zh: 八年春，瀕行上疏，略謂：「各省虧空之弊，起於乾隆四十年以後，州縣營求餽送，以國帑為夤緣，上司受其挾制，彌補無期。
entries.en: In the spring of 1803, on the eve of his departure he memorialized in summary: "Provincial deficits began after 1775: districts and counties solicited gifts, treated the treasury as a ladder for patronage, and superiors were held hostage—shortfalls could never be made good.
entries.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, on the eve of departure he submitted a memorial saying in summary: "The abuse of deficits in the provinces began after the fortieth year of Qianlong; districts and counties sought gifts and presents, used state funds as a ladder for connections, and superiors were constrained by them—making good the shortfall had no end in sight.

entries.zh: 至嘉慶四年以後，大吏知尚廉節，州縣仍形拮据，由於苦樂不均，賢否不分，宜求整飭之法。
entries.en: Since 1799 senior officials have valued integrity, yet districts and counties remain strapped, because hardship and ease are uneven and the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished—rectification is needed.
entries.literal: From the fourth year of Jiaqing onward, great officials knew to value integrity, yet districts and counties were still straitened, because hardship and ease were unevenly distributed and the worthy and unworthy were not distinguished—methods of rectification should be sought.

entries.zh: 又，舊制，驛丞專司驛站，無可誅求。
entries.en: Moreover, under the old system post-station assistants managed relay stations alone and had no scope for extortion.
entries.literal: Moreover, under the old system post-station assistants were solely in charge of relay stations and had no means of extortion.

entries.zh: 自裁歸州縣，濫支苛派，官民俱病。
entries.en: Since those posts were abolished and their duties folded into districts and counties, spending has been abused and levies harsh—officials and people alike suffer.
entries.literal: Since the posts were abolished and returned to districts and counties, expenditures were abused and levies were harsh—officials and people alike suffered.

entries.zh: 宜先清驛站，以杜虧空。
entries.en: Relay stations should be put in order first to stop deficits.
entries.literal: Relay stations should first be cleared up to stop deficits.

entries.zh: 今當軍務告竣，朝廷勤求治理，無大於此二者。
entries.en: Now that the war is ending and the court is striving for good governance, nothing matters more than these two reforms.
entries.literal: Now that military affairs are concluded, the court diligently seeks good governance—nothing is greater than these two matters.

entries.zh: 請睿裁獨斷，以挽積重之勢。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to decide decisively and reverse this long-accumulated trend."
entries.literal: I pray Your sagely judgment may decide alone and turn back this long-accumulated trend."

entries.zh: 所言切中時弊，上嘉納之。
entries.en: His words struck at the abuses of the day; the emperor commended and accepted them.
entries.literal: What he said struck at the abuses of the time; the emperor commended and accepted it.

entries.zh: 陛辭日，賜高宗御用玉鳩杖、御製詩二章，以寵其行，有云：「直道一身立廊廟，清風兩袖返韓城。」
entries.en: On the day of his farewell audience he received the Qianlong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two imperial poems to honor his departure; one line read: "With upright conduct he stood alone in the hall of state; with clear wind in both sleeves he returns to Hancheng."
entries.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he was given the Gaozong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two imperial poems to honor his departure; one line read: "With upright conduct he stood alone in the hall of state; with clear wind in both sleeves he returns to Hancheng."

entries.zh: 時論謂足盡其生平。
entries.en: Contemporary opinion held that this fully summed up his life.
entries.literal: Contemporary opinion said this fully summed up his life.

entries.zh: 既歸，歲時頒賞不絕，每有陳奏，上輒親批答，語如家人。
entries.en: After he returned home, seasonal gifts never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in the tone of family conversation.
entries.literal: After he returned home, seasonal gifts and rewards never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in a tone like family.

entries.zh: 董誥，字蔗林，浙江富陽人，尚書邦達子。
entries.en: Dong Gao, whose style was Zhelin, came from Fuyang in Zhejiang; he was the son of Minister Dong Bangda.
entries.literal: Dong Gao, style name Zhelin, was a native of Fuyang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Dong Bangda.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，殿試進呈卷列第三，高宗因大臣子，改二甲第一。
entries.en: He took his jinshi in 1763; his palace-examination paper ranked third, but because he was a senior minister's son the Qianlong Emperor placed him first in the second class instead.
entries.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong; in the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third, but because he was a great minister's son the Gaozong Emperor changed him to first in the second class.

entries.zh: 選庶吉士，即預修國史、三通、皇朝禮器圖。
entries.en: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he at once joined work on the national history, the Three Comprehensive Encyclopedias, and the Illustrated Rites of the Dynasty.
entries.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and at once took part in compiling the national history, the Three Comprehensive Encyclopedias, and the Illustrated Rites of the Dynasty.

entries.zh: 散館，授編修。
entries.en: When his Hanlin term ended he was appointed compiler.
entries.literal: When the Hanlin term ended he was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 三十二年，命入懋勤殿寫金字經為皇太后祝嘏。
entries.en: In 1767 he was ordered to the Hall of Diligent Study to copy a gold-letter sutra for the empress dowager's birthday blessings.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was ordered to enter the Hall of Diligent Study to write a gold-letter sutra to pray for the empress dowager's longevity.

entries.zh: 次年，大考翰詹，因寫經未與試，特加一級。
entries.en: The following year, in the triennial Hanlin examination, he was excused because of the sutra work and given a special promotion.
entries.literal: The following year, in the great examination of Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, because he had been copying the sutra and did not take the test, he was specially given one promotion.

entries.zh: 尋擢中允，丁父憂。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to middle attendant, then entered mourning for his father.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to middle attendant and entered mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 三十六年，服闋，入直南書房。
entries.en: In 1771, when mourning ended, he took up regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when mourning ended, he entered regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study.

entries.zh: 初，邦達善畫，受高宗知。
entries.en: Bangda had been skilled at painting and won the Qianlong Emperor's notice.
entries.literal: At first Bangda was skilled at painting and won the Gaozong Emperor's notice.

entries.zh: 誥承家學，繼為侍從，書畫亦被宸賞，尤以奉職恪勤為上所眷注。
entries.en: Gao inherited the family tradition and in turn became a court attendant; his calligraphy and painting also won imperial praise, but above all his dutiful service won the emperor's special regard.
entries.literal: Gao inherited the family learning and in turn became an attendant at court; his calligraphy and painting also won imperial approval, but above all his dutiful and diligent service won the emperor's special regard.

entries.zh: 累遷內閣學士。
entries.en: After repeated promotions he rose to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
entries.literal: After repeated promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.

entries.zh: 四十年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部，歷署吏、刑兩部侍郎，兼管樂部。
entries.en: In 1775 he was made vice minister of works, transferred to the Board of Revenue, served in turn as acting vice minister of the Boards of Personnel and Justice, and concurrently managed the music section of the Board of Rites.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to vice minister of works, transferred to the Board of Revenue, successively acted as vice minister of the Boards of Personnel and Justice, and concurrently managed the Board of Rites' music section.

entries.zh: 充四庫館副總裁，接辦全書薈要，命輯滿洲源流考。
entries.en: He served as deputy chief compiler of the Siku Library, took over the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile an Investigation of Manchu Origins.
entries.literal: He served as deputy chief compiler of the Siku Library project, took over compilation of the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile an Investigation of Manchu Origins.

entries.zh: 四十四年，命為軍機大臣。
entries.en: In 1779 he was appointed Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 五十二年，加太子少保，擢戶部尚書。
entries.en: In 1787 he was made Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to minister of revenue.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year he was given the title Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to minister of revenue.

entries.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後底定，並列功臣，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: After Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession, he was listed among the meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession; he was listed among the meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，授受禮成，詔硃珪來京，將畀以閣務，仁宗賀以詩。
entries.en: In 1796, when the succession rites were completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital for a Grand Secretariat post; the Jiaqing Emperor congratulated him with a poem.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the succession rites were completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital to be given Grand Secretariat duties; the Renzong Emperor congratulated him with a poem.

entries.zh: 屬稿未竟，和珅取白高宗曰：「嗣皇帝欲市恩於師傅。」
entries.en: Before the draft was finished, Heshen told the Qianlong Emperor, "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor."
entries.literal: The draft was not yet finished when Heshen reported to the Gaozong Emperor, saying, "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor."

entries.zh: 高宗色動，顧誥曰：「汝在軍機、刑部久，是於律意云何？」
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor's expression changed; he turned to Gao and said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Board of Justice—what is your view of this under the law?"
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor's expression changed; he turned to Gao and said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Board of Justice—what is your view of the intent of the law?"

entries.zh: 誥叩頭曰：「聖主無過言。」
entries.en: Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage sovereign speaks without fault."
entries.literal: Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage sovereign speaks without fault."

entries.zh: 高宗默然良久，曰：「汝大臣也，善為朕輔導之。」
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor was silent a long while, then said, "You are a great minister—guide him well for me."
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor was silent a long while, then said, "You are a great minister—guide him well for me."

entries.zh: 乃以他事罷珪之召。
entries.en: Then on another pretext Gui's summons was canceled.
entries.literal: Then on another pretext Gui's summons was canceled.

entries.zh: 時大學士懸缺久，難其人。
entries.en: At that time the Grand Secretary post had long been vacant; a suitable man was hard to find.
entries.literal: At that time the post of Grand Secretary had long been vacant; a suitable man was hard to find.

entries.zh: 高宗謂劉墉、紀昀、彭元瑞三人皆資深，墉遇事模棱，元瑞以不檢獲愆，昀讀書多而不明理，惟誥在直勤勉，超拜東閣大學士，明詔宣示，俾三人加愧勵焉。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor said Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior: Liu Yong was equivocal in affairs; Peng Yuanrui had been censured for misconduct; Ji Yun read widely but lacked sound judgment—only Gao, diligent in regular duty, was promoted over their heads to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict to shame and spur the three.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor said that Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior in service: Liu Yong was equivocal in affairs; Peng Yuanrui had been censured for lack of restraint; Ji Yun read much but did not understand principle—only Gao, diligent in regular duty, was promoted over their heads to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict proclaiming this to make the three feel still greater shame and spur.

entries.zh: 命總理禮部，仍兼管戶部事。
entries.en: He was ordered to take general charge of the Board of Rites while still managing the Board of Revenue.
entries.literal: He was ordered to take general charge of the Board of Rites while still concurrently managing affairs of the Board of Revenue.

entries.zh: 二年，丁生母憂，特賜陀羅經被，遣御前侍衛、額駙丰紳殷德奠醊。
entries.en: In 1797 he entered mourning for his birth mother; he was specially given a dharaṇī sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard and imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.
entries.literal: In the second year he entered mourning for his birth mother; he was specially given a dharaṇī sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard and imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.

entries.zh: 硃珪，字石君，順天大興人。
entries.en: Zhu Gui, whose style was Shijun, came from Daxing in Shuntian.
entries.literal: Zhu Gui, style name Shijun, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.

entries.zh: 先世居蕭山，自父文炳始遷籍。
entries.en: His ancestors lived in Xiaoshan; his father Wenbing was the first to transfer the family's registration.
entries.literal: His ancestors lived in Xiaoshan; from his father Wenbing the family transferred its registration.

entries.zh: 文炳官盩厔知縣，曾受經於大學士硃軾。
entries.en: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had studied the classics under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.
entries.literal: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had once studied the classics under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.

entries.zh: 珪少傳軾學，與兄筠同鄉舉，並負時譽。
entries.en: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; he and his elder brother Yun passed the provincial examination together and both enjoyed contemporary renown.
entries.literal: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; with his elder brother Yun he passed the provincial examination in the same year, and both enjoyed contemporary renown.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年成進士，年甫十八，選庶吉士，散館授編修。
entries.en: In 1748 he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and when his term ended was appointed compiler.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and when the term ended was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 數遇典禮，撰進文冊。
entries.en: He repeatedly took part in great ceremonies and drafted the submitted ceremonial documents.
entries.literal: He repeatedly encountered great ceremonies and drafted the submitted ceremonial documents.

entries.zh: 高宗重其學行，累遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor valued his learning and conduct; after repeated promotions he rose to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor valued his learning and conduct; after repeated promotions he reached reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 二十五年，出為福建糧驛道。
entries.en: In 1760 he was posted outside the capital as grain and courier intendant of Fujian.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as grain and courier intendant of Fujian.

entries.zh: 擢按察使，治獄平恕，以父憂去。
entries.en: He was promoted to provincial judge; in handling cases he was fair and lenient, and left office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge; in handling cases he was fair and lenient, and left office on his father's bereavement.

entries.zh: 三十二年，補湖北按察使。
entries.en: In 1767 he was appointed provincial judge of Hubei to fill a vacancy.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed provincial judge of Hubei to fill a vacancy.

entries.zh: 會緬甸用兵，以部署驛務詳慎，被褒獎。
entries.en: During the Burma campaign, his careful deployment of relay-station affairs won commendation.
entries.literal: When Burma was at war, because his deployment of relay-station affairs was detailed and careful, he received commendation.

entries.zh: 四十年，召入覲，改授侍講學士，直上書房，侍仁宗學。
entries.en: In 1775 he was summoned to audience, made expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, entered regular duty in the Upper Imperial Study, and tutored the Jiaqing Emperor.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he was summoned to audience, transferred to expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, entered regular duty in the Upper Imperial Study, and attended the Renzong Emperor's studies.

entries.zh: 四十四年，典福建鄉試。
entries.en: In 1779 he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.

entries.zh: 次年，督福建學政。
entries.en: The following year he supervised education in Fujian.
entries.literal: The following year he supervised education in Fujian.

entries.zh: 瀕行，上五箴於仁宗：曰養心，曰敬身，曰勤業，曰虛己，曰致誠。
entries.en: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Jiaqing Emperor: on nurturing the mind, revering the person, diligent endeavor, emptying the self, and attaining sincerity.
entries.literal: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Renzong Emperor: on nurturing the mind, on revering the person, on diligent endeavor, on emptying the self, and on attaining sincerity.

entries.zh: 仁宗力行之，後親政，嘗置左右。
entries.en: The Jiaqing Emperor practiced them vigorously; after taking personal rule he kept them at hand.
entries.literal: The Renzong Emperor practiced them vigorously; after taking personal rule he kept them at hand.

entries.zh: 五十一年，擢禮部侍郎，典江南鄉試，督浙江學政。
entries.en: In 1786 he was made vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised education in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year he was promoted to vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised education in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 還朝，調兵部。
entries.en: On returning to court he was transferred to the Board of War.
entries.literal: On returning to court he was transferred to the Board of War.

entries.zh: 五十五年，典會試。
entries.en: In 1790 he presided over the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 出為安徽巡撫。
entries.en: He was posted as governor of Anhui.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Anhui.

entries.zh: 皖北水災，馳驛往賑，攜僕數人，與村民同舟渡，賑宿州、泗州、碭山、靈壁、五河、盱眙餘災，輕者貸以糧種。
entries.en: When northern Anhui suffered floods, he rushed by post-horse to give relief with only a few servants, crossing in the same boats as villagers; he relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and lent grain seed to lighter cases.
entries.literal: When northern Anhui suffered flood disaster, he rushed by post-horse to give relief, taking only a few servants and crossing in the same boat with villagers; he relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and to lighter cases lent grain seed.

entries.zh: 築決堤，展春賑，並躬蒞其事，民無流亡。
entries.en: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work; the people did not flee.
entries.literal: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work; the people did not flee.

entries.zh: 五十九年，調廣東。
entries.en: In 1794 he was transferred to Guangdong.
entries.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 尋署兩廣總督，授左都御史、兵部尚書，仍留巡撫任。
entries.en: Soon he acted as governor-general of the Two Guangs, was made left censor-in-chief and minister of war, and still retained the governorship.
entries.literal: Soon he acted as governor-general of the Two Guangs, was given the posts of left censor-in-chief and minister of war, and still retained the governorship.

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，授總督，兼署巡撫。
entries.en: In 1796 he was appointed governor-general and concurrently acted as governor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor-general and concurrently acted as governor.

entries.zh: 珪初以文學受知，洎出任疆寄，負時望，將大用。
entries.en: Gui had first won notice through literary accomplishment; when he took up frontier office he bore high expectations and was on the verge of great promotion.
entries.literal: Gui had first won notice through literary accomplishment; when he went out to hold frontier responsibility he bore contemporary expectations and was about to be greatly employed.

entries.zh: 和珅忌之，授受禮成，珪進頌冊，因加指摘，高宗曰：「陳善納誨，師傅之職宜爾，非汝所知也。」
entries.en: Heshen envied him; when the succession rites were completed Gui presented a eulogy booklet and was criticized for it; the Qianlong Emperor said, "To present good counsel and accept admonition is a tutor's proper duty—this is not for you to understand."
entries.literal: Heshen envied him; when the succession rites were completed Gui presented a eulogy booklet and was therefore criticized; the Gaozong Emperor said, "To present good counsel and accept admonition is what a tutor's office properly does—this is not for you to understand."

entries.zh: 會大學士缺，詔召珪，卒為和珅所沮。
entries.en: When a Grand Secretary post fell vacant, an edict summoned Gui, but Heshen blocked it in the end.
entries.literal: When a Grand Secretary post fell vacant, an edict summoned Gui, but in the end Heshen blocked it.

entries.zh: 以廣東艇匪擾劫閩、浙，責珪不能緝捕，寢前命，左遷安徽巡撫。
entries.en: Because Guangdong boat bandits raided Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them; the earlier order was set aside and he was demoted to governor of Anhui.
entries.literal: Because Guangdong boat bandits harassed and plundered Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them; the earlier order was set aside and he was demoted to governor of Anhui.

entries.zh: 皖北复災，親治賑，官吏無侵蝕。
entries.en: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again; he personally managed relief, and officials did not embezzle.
entries.literal: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again; he personally managed relief, and officials did not embezzle.

entries.zh: 三省教匪起，安徽亦多伏莽。
entries.en: When sect rebels rose in the three provinces, Anhui also had many hidden desperadoes.
entries.literal: When sect rebels rose in the three provinces, Anhui also had many hidden desperadoes.

entries.zh: 珪曰：「疑而索之，是激之變。」
entries.en: Gui said, "To suspect people and hunt them down is to provoke rebellion."
entries.literal: Gui said, "To suspect and search for them is to provoke rebellion."

entries.zh: 親駐界上籌防禦，遍蒞潁、亳所屬，集鄉老教誡之，民感化，境內迄無事。
entries.en: He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went throughout the districts under Ying and Bo, gathered village elders to instruct them, won the people over, and kept the province peaceful.
entries.literal: He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went everywhere through the districts under Ying and Bo, gathered village elders to instruct them, the people were moved to reform, and within the jurisdiction there was no trouble to the end.

entries.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書，調吏部，仍留巡撫任。
entries.en: The following year he was made minister of war, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and still retained the governorship.
entries.literal: The following year he was appointed minister of war, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and still retained the governorship.

entries.zh: 四年正月，高宗崩，仁宗即馳驛召珪，聞命奔赴。
entries.en: In the first month of 1799 the Qianlong Emperor died; the Jiaqing Emperor at once sent post-horses to summon Gui; on hearing the order he rushed to obey.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; the Renzong Emperor at once sent post-horses to summon Gui; on hearing the order he rushed to obey.

entries.zh: 途中上疏，略曰：「天子之孝，以繼志述事為大。
entries.en: En route he memorialized in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his undertakings.
entries.literal: En route he submitted a memorial saying in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his undertakings.

entries.zh: 親政伊始，遠聽近瞻，默運乾綱，雱施渙號。
entries.en: At the outset of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield imperial authority, and pour forth edicts like rain.
entries.literal: At the outset of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield the heavenly net, and pour forth edicts like rain.

entries.zh: 陽剛之氣，如日重光，惻怛之仁，無幽不浹。
entries.en: Let your firm, yang spirit shine like the sun renewed; let compassionate benevolence reach even the darkest corners.
entries.literal: The yang and firm spirit, like the sun's renewed light; compassionate benevolence reaching even the darkest places.

entries.zh: 修身則嚴誠欺之界，觀人則辨義利之防。
entries.en: In self-cultivation, strictly mark the boundary between sincerity and deceit; in judging others, distinguish righteousness from profit.
entries.literal: In cultivating the person, strictly mark the boundary between sincerity and deceit; in observing others, distinguish the barrier between righteousness and profit.

entries.zh: 君心正而四維張，朝廷清而九牧肅。
entries.en: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds hold firm; when the court is pure the provinces are orderly.
entries.literal: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds are extended; when the court is pure the nine provinces are orderly.

entries.zh: 身先節儉，崇獎清廉，自然盜賊不足平，財用不足阜。
entries.en: Take the lead in frugality, honor and reward integrity—then bandits will be easy to pacify and revenues easy to enrich.
entries.literal: Take the lead in frugality, honor and reward integrity—then naturally bandits need not be hard to pacify nor revenues hard to enrich.

entries.zh: 惟原皇上無忘堯、舜自​​任之心，臣敢不勉行義事君之道。」
entries.en: I only pray Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon oneself; how dare your servant not strive to serve the ruler with righteousness."
entries.literal: I only pray Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon oneself; how dare your servant not strive to practice the way of righteous service to the ruler."

entries.zh: 至京哭臨，上執珪手哭失聲。
entries.en: On reaching the capital he attended the mourning audience; the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.
entries.literal: On reaching the capital he attended the mourning audience; the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.

entries.zh: 命直南書房，管戶部三庫，加太子少保，賜第西華門外。
entries.en: He was ordered to regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study, to manage the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, made Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted a residence outside the Xihua Gate.
entries.literal: He was ordered to regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study, to manage the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, given the title Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted a residence outside the Xihua Gate.

entries.zh: 時召獨對，用人行政悉以諮之。
entries.en: He was frequently summoned for private audience; appointments and administration were all consulted with him.
entries.literal: He was frequently summoned for private audience; in appointments and administration everything was consulted with him.

entries.zh: 珪造膝密陳，不關白軍機大臣，不沽恩市直，上傾心一聽，初政之美，多出贊助。
entries.en: Gui spoke confidentially knee to knee, did not inform the Grand Councilors, and did not curry favor openly; the emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.
entries.literal: Gui spoke confidentially knee to knee, did not inform the Grand Councilors, and did not curry favor by open display; the emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.

entries.zh: 先是彭元瑞於西華門內墜馬，珪呼其輿入舁之，為御史週栻所劾。
entries.en: Earlier Peng Yuanrui had fallen from his horse inside the Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan chair inside to carry him, and censor Zhou Shi impeached him for it.
entries.literal: Earlier Peng Yuanrui had fallen from his horse inside the Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan chair inside to carry him up, and was impeached by censor Zhou Shi.

entries.zh: 尋有珪輿人毆傷禁門兵，忌者嗾護軍統領訐之。
entries.en: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat a Forbidden Gate guard; his enemies incited the banner guard commander to denounce him.
entries.literal: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and wounded a Forbidden Gate guard; enviers incited the banner guard commander to denounce him.

entries.zh: 詔：「珪素恪謹，造次不檢，特申戒。」
entries.en: An edict said: "Gui has always been careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished."
entries.literal: An edict said: "Gui has always been careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished."

entries.zh: 坐褫宮銜，解三庫事，鐫級留任。
entries.en: He was stripped of palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade, and kept in office.
entries.literal: He was punished by stripping of palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade, and kept in office.

entries.zh: 七年，協辦大學士，复太子少保。
entries.en: In 1802 he served as associate Grand Secretary and was restored as Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he served as associate Grand Secretary and was restored as Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，晉太子少傅。
entries.en: Soon he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 九年，上幸翰林院，聯句賜宴，御書「天祿儲才」額刻懸院中，以墨書賜珪家。
entries.en: In 1804 the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, gave a linked-verse banquet, and had the imperial inscription "Heaven's Blessings Store Talent" carved and hung in the academy; an ink inscription was bestowed on Gui's family.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, gave a linked-verse banquet, and had the imperial inscription "Heaven's Blessings Store Talent" carved and hung in the academy; ink writing was bestowed on Gui's family.

entries.zh: 十年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理工部。
entries.en: In 1805 he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and put in charge of the Board of Works.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and put in charge of the Board of Works.

entries.zh: 上以是命遵高宗諭，遣詣裕陵謝。
entries.en: Because this appointment followed the Qianlong Emperor's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yuling mausoleum to give thanks.
entries.literal: Because this appointment followed the Gaozong Emperor's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yuling mausoleum to give thanks.

entries.zh: 逾歲，年七十六，以老乞休，溫詔慰留，賜玉鳩杖；
entries.en: After a year, at seventy-six, he asked to retire citing age; a warm edict urged him to stay and granted him a jade dove staff;
entries.literal: After a year, at seventy-six, citing age he begged to retire; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, granting a jade dove staff;

entries.zh: 命天寒，間二三日入直。
entries.en: and ordered that in cold weather he need enter regular duty only every two or three days.
entries.literal: he was ordered that in cold weather he need enter regular duty only every two or three days.

entries.zh: 未幾，召對乾清宮，眩暈，扶歸第，數日卒。
entries.en: Before long, summoned for audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, he grew dizzy, was helped home, and died within several days.
entries.literal: Before long, summoned for audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, he grew dizzy, was helped back to his residence, and died within several days.

entries.zh: 上親奠，哭之慟。
entries.en: The emperor personally offered libations and wept with deep grief.
entries.literal: The emperor personally offered libations and wept with deep grief.

entries.zh: 贈太傅，祀賢良祠，賜金治喪。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and granted gold for the funeral.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and granted gold for the funeral.

entries.zh: 詔：「珪自為師傅，凡所陳說，無非唐、虞、三代之言，稍涉時趨者不出諸口，啟沃至多。
entries.en: An edict said: "Since Gui became tutor, everything he said was the language of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; what touched current fashion never left his mouth—his counsel was abundant.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Since Gui became tutor, everything he stated was nothing but the words of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; what slightly touched current fashion never left his mouth—his counsel was abundant.

entries.zh: 揆諸諡法，足當'正'字而無愧，特諡文正。
entries.en: Measured against posthumous naming standards, he fully merits the character for 'correct' without shame; he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzheng.
entries.literal: Measured against posthumous naming standards, he fully merits the character 'correct' without shame; he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzheng.

entries.zh: 又見其門庭卑隘，清寒之況，不減儒素。」
entries.en: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his plain poverty was no less than that of a scholar of modest means."
entries.literal: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his condition of clean poverty was no less than that of a plain scholar."

entries.zh: 命內府備筵，遣皇子加奠。
entries.en: He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.
entries.literal: He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.

entries.zh: 啟殯日，遣慶郡王永璘祖奠目送。
entries.en: On the day the coffin was opened for burial, Prince Yonglin of Qing was sent to offer ancestral libations and see him off.
entries.literal: On the day the coffin was opened for burial, Prince Yonglin of Qing was sent to offer ancestral libations and see him off with his eyes.

entries.zh: 逾年，上謁西陵，珪墓近蹕路，遣官賜奠。
entries.en: After a year, when the emperor visited the Western Tombs, Gui's tomb lay near the imperial route; an official was sent to offer libations.
entries.literal: After a year, when the emperor visited the Western Tombs, Gui's tomb was near the imperial route; an official was sent to grant libations.

entries.zh: 高宗實錄成，特賜祭，擢長子錫經為四品京堂。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed, sacrificial rites were specially granted and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital office.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's Veritable Records were completed, sacrificial rites were specially granted and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital office.

entries.zh: 二十年，復因謁陵回鑾，親奠其墓，恩禮始終無與比。
entries.en: In 1815, again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish had no equal.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish had no equal.

entries.zh: 論曰：君子小人消長之機，國運系焉。
entries.en: The appraisal says: The rise and fall of gentlemen and petty men is where the nation's fortune lies.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: The mechanism by which gentlemen and petty men wax and wane is where the nation's fortune lies.

entries.zh: 王杰、董誥、硃珪皆高宗拔擢信任之臣，和珅一再間沮，卒不屈撓。
entries.en: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Qianlong Emperor selected and trusted; Heshen repeatedly obstructed them, yet in the end they did not yield.
entries.literal: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Gaozong Emperor selected and trusted; Heshen repeatedly obstructed them between, yet in the end they did not yield or bend.

entries.zh: 一旦共、驩伏法，眾正盈朝，攄其忠誠，啟沃新主，殄寇息民，苞桑永固。
entries.en: Once Heshen was executed, the upright filled the court; they poured forth their loyalty, nourished the new sovereign, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest, and secured the realm like deep-rooted mulberry.
entries.literal: Once Gong and Huan were executed by law—the names by which Heshen is here indicated—the upright filled the court; they poured forth their loyalty, nourished the new sovereign, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest, and the nation was firmly secured like mulberry roots in earth.

entries.zh: 天留數人，弼成仁宗初政之盛，可謂大臣矣。
entries.en: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Jiaqing Emperor's early reign—they may truly be called great ministers.
entries.literal: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Renzong Emperor's early reign—they may be called great ministers.

entries.zh: 傑體不逾中人，和靄近情，而持守剛正，歷事兩朝，以忠直結主知。
entries.en: Jie was of no more than average stature, kindly and approachable, yet steadfastly upright; serving two reigns, he won the sovereign's trust through loyalty and integrity.
entries.literal: Jie's physique did not exceed that of an average man; he was kindly and approachable, yet upheld firm integrity; serving two reigns, he won the sovereign's trust through loyalty and uprightness.

entries.zh: 當致仕未行，會有陳德於禁城驚犯乘輿，急趨朝請對曰：「德庖廚賤役，安敢妄蓄逆謀？
entries.en: Before he had retired, Chen De shocked the court by assaulting the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City; Jie hurried to court and said: "De is a lowly kitchen servant—how could he harbor treasonous designs on his own?
entries.literal: When he had not yet retired, there occurred Chen De's startling assault on the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City; Jie hurried to court and requested an audience, saying: "De is a lowly kitchen servant—how would he dare harbor rebellious designs?

entries.zh: 此必有元姦大憝主使行明張差之事，當除肘腋之患。」
entries.en: There must be a chief villain behind him, as in the Zhang Cha affair—this threat at the emperor's very side must be uprooted."
entries.literal: There must be a chief villain behind him directing this, as in the clear case of Zhang Cha—the trouble at the elbow and armpit must be removed."

entries.zh: 至十八年林清逆黨之變，上思其言，特賜祭焉。
entries.en: By 1813, when Lin Qing's rebels struck, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites in his honor.
entries.literal: By the eighteenth year, when Lin Qing's rebel faction rose, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites.

entries.zh: 十八年，扈從秋狝。
entries.en: In 1813 he accompanied the autumn hunt at Rehe.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the autumn hunt at Rehe.

entries.zh: 林清逆黨突入禁城，時回鑾，中途聞變，有議俟調大兵成列而後進者，誥曰：「是滋亂也，獻俘者行至矣！」
entries.en: Lin Qing's rebels suddenly entered the Forbidden City; the court was returning from Rehe and heard of the disturbance en route; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; the captors are already on their way!"
entries.literal: Lin Qing's rebel faction suddenly entered the Forbidden City; at that time the court was returning from Rehe; midway they heard of the disturbance; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled in formation before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; those who present captives are already on the road!"

entries.zh: 即日扈駕進次，人心乃定。
entries.en: That same day he accompanied the imperial carriage forward, and public morale steadied.
entries.literal: That same day he accompanied the imperial carriage to advance to the next stop, and popular sentiment was calmed.

entries.zh: 窮治邪教，誥謂：「燒香祈福，愚民無知，率所常有。
entries.en: In prosecuting heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to pray for blessings is what ignorant common people routinely do.
entries.literal: In the thorough prosecution of heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to pray for blessings is what ignorant common people do without knowledge—it is what they always do.

entries.zh: 惟從逆者不可貸。」
entries.en: Only those who joined rebellion cannot be pardoned."
entries.literal: Only those who followed rebellion cannot be pardoned."

entries.zh: 凡論上，皆以是定讞。
entries.en: In every case submitted for judgment, verdicts were fixed by this principle.
entries.literal: In every case submitted for judgment, verdicts were fixed by this principle.

entries.zh: 林清既誅，滑縣逆匪尋平，論功，迭被優敘，賜子淳為郎中。
entries.en: After Lin Qing was executed, the Hua County rebels were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given a directorship in a ministry.
entries.literal: After Lin Qing was executed, the rebels of Hua County were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given the post of director in a ministry.

entries.zh: 二十年，因病請致政，溫詔慰留，改管兵部。
entries.en: In 1815, citing illness he asked to retire; a warm edict urged him to stay and transferred his charge to the Board of War.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, citing illness he requested retirement from office; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, changing his charge to the Board of War.

entries.zh: 未幾，復命管刑部。
entries.en: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Board of Justice.
entries.literal: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Board of Justice.

entries.zh: 二十三年，再疏乞休，許致仕食全俸。
entries.en: In 1818 he again memorialized to retire; permission was granted to retire on full salary.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he again memorialized begging to retire; permission was granted to retire and draw full salary.

entries.zh: 是年十月，卒，贈太傅。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year he died; posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died; posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 上親奠，入祀賢良祠，賜金治喪，御製詩輓之，嘉其父子歷事三朝，未嘗增置一畝之田、一椽之屋，命刻詩於墓，以彰忠藎。
entries.en: The emperor personally offered libations; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies; gold was granted for the funeral; an imperial elegy praised father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding a single mu of land or a single beam of house; the emperor ordered the poem carved on the tomb to honor their loyalty and integrity.
