entries.literal: The emperor personally offered libations; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies; gold was granted for the funeral; an imperial poem mourned him, praising father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding a single mu of land or a single rafter of house; the emperor ordered the poem carved on the tomb to manifest their loyalty and integrity.

entries.zh: 諡文恭。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Wengong.
entries.literal: His posthumous name was Wengong.

entries.zh: 誥直軍機先後四十年，熟於朝章故事，有以諮者，無不悉。
entries.en: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years in all; he knew court regulations and precedents inside out—whoever consulted him found nothing he did not know.
entries.literal: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years in all; he was versed in court regulations and precedents—whoever consulted him found nothing he did not know thoroughly.

entries.zh: 凡所獻納皆面陳，未嘗用奏牘。
entries.en: Whatever he presented he always stated in person; he never used written memorials.
entries.literal: Whatever he presented was always stated in person; he never used written memorials.

entries.zh: 當和珅用事，與王杰支柱其間，獨居深念，行處幾失常度，卒贊仁宗殲除大憝。
entries.en: When Heshen held power, he and Wang Jie held the line between them; alone he brooded deeply, and in walking about he nearly lost his composure—yet in the end he helped the Jiaqing Emperor destroy the great villain.
entries.literal: When Heshen held power, he and Wang Jie propped up affairs between them; alone he thought deeply, and in walking about he nearly lost normal composure—yet in the end he assisted the Renzong Emperor in destroying the great villain.

entries.zh: 及林清之變，獨持鎮定，尤為時稱雲。
entries.en: At Lin Qing's disturbance he alone kept his composure, which contemporaries especially praised.
entries.literal: At the time of Lin Qing's disturbance he alone maintained composure, which contemporaries especially praised.

entries.zh: 王杰，字偉人，陝西韓城人。
entries.en: Wang Jie, whose style was Weiren, came from Hancheng in Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Wang Jie, style name Weiren, was a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 以拔貢考銓藍田教諭，未任，遭父喪，貧甚，為書記以養母。
entries.en: He qualified through the tribute-student channel for the post of director of studies at Lantian, but before he could assume it his father died. Penniless, he took work as a clerk to support his mother.
entries.literal: Having passed the examination as a selected tribute student, he was appointed through examination to be director of studies at Lantian, but before taking office he suffered his father's bereavement; being extremely poor, he worked as a secretary to support his mother.

entries.zh: 歷佐兩江總督尹繼善、江蘇巡撫陳宏謀幕，皆重之。
entries.en: He later served on the secretariats of Yin Jishan, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and Chen Hongmou, governor of Jiangsu, and both men valued him highly.
entries.literal: He successively served on the staffs of Yin Jishan, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and Chen Hongmou, governor of Jiangsu; both held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 初從武功孫景烈遊，講濂、洛、關、閩之學；
entries.en: Early on he studied under Sun Jinglie of Wugong in the Neo-Confucian traditions associated with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi;
entries.literal: At first he associated with Sun Jinglie of Wugong, studying the learning of the Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min schools;

entries.zh: 及見宏謀，學益進，自謂生平行己居官得力於此。
entries.en: After he came to know Hongmou his studies advanced further still, and he would say that everything he achieved in private conduct and in public office he owed to this education.
entries.literal: When he met Hongmou his learning advanced further; he said himself that in his conduct through life and in office he owed his strength to this.

entries.zh: 松筠，字湘浦，瑪拉特氏，蒙古正藍旗人。
entries.en: Song Yun, whose style was Xiangpu, belonged to the Marat clan and was a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Song Yun, style Xiangpu, of the Marat clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 繙譯生員，考授理籓院筆帖式，充軍機章京，能任事，為高宗所知。
entries.en: Having qualified as a translation licentiate, he passed the examination for a clerkship in the Court of Colonial Affairs, served on the Grand Council staff, showed himself capable in office, and won the notice of the Qianlong emperor.
entries.literal: A translation licentiate, he passed examination and was appointed a clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs, served as a Grand Council secretary, proved capable in office, and came to the notice of Emperor Gaozong.

entries.zh: 累遷銀庫員外郎。
entries.en: He rose in stages to vice-director of the silver treasury.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice-director of the silver treasury.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十八年，超擢內閣學士，兼副都統。
entries.en: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was singled out for rapid promotion to academician of the Grand Secretariat and made vice commander of a Banner as well.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was promoted by special selection to Academician of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently vice commander of the Banner.

entries.zh: 保寧，圖伯特氏，蒙古正白旗人，靖逆將軍納穆札勒子。
entries.en: Bao Ning belonged to the Tubote clan, a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, and was the son of Pacification General Namuzhale.
entries.literal: Bao Ning, of the Tubote clan, a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, was the son of Pacification General Namuzhale.

entries.zh: 乾隆中，納穆札勒殉節回疆，錫封三等公。
entries.en: In the Qianlong era, Namuzhale gave his life defending the frontier in the Western Regions and was posthumously granted the title of third-rank duke.
entries.literal: During the Qianlong reign, Namuzhale died defending his post in the Western Regions and was posthumously enfeoffed as a third-rank duke.

entries.zh: 書麟，字紱齋，高佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，大學士高晉子。
entries.en: Shu Lin, whose style was Fuzhai, belonged to the Gaojia clan and the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner; he was the son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.
entries.literal: Shu Lin, style name Fuzhai, of the Gaojia clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was the son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.

entries.zh: 初授鑾儀衛整儀尉，累遷冠軍使，擢西安副都統。
entries.en: He began as an orderly officer in the Imperial Procession Guard, rose through successive posts to champion commissioner, and was then appointed vice commander-in-chief at Xi'an.
entries.literal: At first he was appointed orderly officer of the Imperial Procession Guard, was promoted repeatedly to champion commissioner, and was raised to vice commander-in-chief at Xi'an.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十八年，大軍徵金川，命為領隊大臣，從參贊大臣豐升額，力戰輒先登，克堅碉數十，功最。
entries.en: In Qianlong 38, during the great campaign against Jinchuan, he was made lead commander under Participating Commander Feng Sheng'e. In hard fighting he repeatedly led the assault, took dozens of fortified blockhouses, and earned the highest distinction.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, when the great army campaigned against Jinchuan, he was ordered to serve as lead commander, following the participating commander Feng Sheng'e; in fierce fighting he was always first to scale the walls, captured several dozen strong blockhouses, and his merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 金川平，加等議敘，圖形紫光閣。
entries.en: After Jinchuan was pacified, he was granted an enhanced merit award and his likeness was enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
entries.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified, he received an extra-grade merit review and had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

entries.zh: 授廣西巡撫，以父憂去。
entries.en: He was appointed governor of Guangxi but resigned when his father died.
entries.literal: He was appointed governor of Guangxi, then left office on account of his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 起，署兵部侍郎。
entries.en: When recalled from mourning, he served as acting vice minister of War.
entries.literal: Recalled from mourning, he served as acting vice minister of War.

entries.zh: 四十九年，出為安徽巡撫，歲旱，請留漕糧五萬石、關稅銀三十五萬兩賑之。
entries.en: In the forty-ninth year he became governor of Anhui. During a drought he asked to retain fifty thousand piculs of transport grain and 350,000 taels of customs revenue for famine relief.
entries.literal: In the forty-ninth year he went out as governor of Anhui; the year was drought-stricken, and he requested that fifty thousand piculs of grain transport tax and three hundred fifty thousand taels of customs silver be retained for relief.

entries.zh: 阜陽有荒地六千餘頃，疏請寬限清釐，民間交易用官弓丈量，以杜欺隱，期於漸復舊額。
entries.en: More than six thousand qing of wasteland lay in Fuyang. He memorialized for a longer deadline to clear and register it, required private land sales to be measured with the official bow to curb fraud, and aimed to restore the original tax quota over time.
entries.literal: In Fuyang there were more than six thousand qing of wasteland; he memorialized asking for an extended deadline for clearance and survey, that private transactions use the official measuring bow to prevent fraud and concealment, and that the old quota be gradually restored.

entries.zh: 帝以書麟盡心民瘼，予優敘。
entries.en: The emperor rewarded him with a superior merit review for his devoted attention to the people's hardships.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Shu Lin devoted himself to the people's hardships, granted him a superior merit review.

entries.zh: 黃、運兩河漫溢，帝因兩江總督李世傑未諳河工，命書麟佐之。
entries.en: When the Yellow River and Grand Canal burst their banks, the emperor ordered Shu Lin to assist Governor-General Li Shijie of the Two Jiangs, who was inexperienced in hydraulic engineering.
entries.literal: The Yellow and Grand Canal rivers overflowed; because the governor-general of the Two Jiangs, Li Shijie, was not versed in river works, the emperor ordered Shu Lin to assist him.

entries.zh: 與世傑及河督李奉翰議，漫口有四，惟司家莊、湯家莊兩處分溜，急興工堵築；
entries.en: With Li Shijie and Canal Director Li Fenghan he decided that of the four breach points, only Sijiazhuang and Tangjiazhuang had a split current, and that blocking and repair work there must begin at once.
entries.literal: Together with Li Shijie and the canal director Li Fenghan he deliberated: there were four breach points, but only at Sijiazhuang and Tangjiazhuang had the current split, and work to block and build should be urgently undertaken;

entries.zh: 又奏：「桃源境內河流因順黃壩生有淤灘，水勢紆折不暢。
entries.en: He also reported: "Within Taoyuan, silt bars along the Yellow River alignment had choked the channel and slowed the current.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "Within Taoyuan the river, because of silt banks formed along the Yellow River alignment, had a winding course and sluggish flow.

entries.zh: 於玉皇閣下挑引河，俾黃流東注會清，以資宣洩。」
entries.en: A diversion should be cut below Jade Emperor Pavilion so the Yellow current can run east into the Huai and ease the flood."
entries.literal: Below Jade Emperor Pavilion a diversion channel should be cut so that the Yellow current may flow east into the Huai and aid discharge."

entries.zh: 五十二年，擢兩江總督。
entries.en: In the fifty-second year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

entries.zh: 書麟素行清謹，出巡屬邑，輕騎減從，民不擾累，特詔嘉之。
entries.en: Shu Lin was known for integrity and restraint. On tours of his districts he traveled light with a small escort, sparing the people trouble, and received a special imperial commendation.
entries.literal: Shu Lin had always conducted himself with integrity and caution; when touring subordinate districts he used light escort and reduced retinue, the people were not harassed or burdened, and he received a special imperial commendation.

entries.zh: 和珅柄政，書麟與之忤。
entries.en: When Heshen dominated the government, Shu Lin stood at odds with him.
entries.literal: When Heshen held power, Shu Lin was at odds with him.

entries.zh: 未幾，有高郵巡檢陳倚道揭報書吏假印重徵事，遣重臣鞫實，坐書麟瞻徇，下部嚴議；
entries.en: Soon afterward Gaoyou inspector Chen Yidao exposed clerks who had used forged seals to levy extra taxes. The emperor sent a senior official to investigate; Shu Lin was found guilty of shielding the culprits and the case was referred for severe punishment.
entries.literal: Before long, Gaoyou sub-prefectural inspector Chen Yidao exposed a case of clerks using forged seals to levy extra taxes; a high minister was sent to investigate, and Shu Lin was found guilty of shielding and favoritism, the case referred for severe deliberation;

entries.zh: 又失察句容書吏侵用錢糧，褫職，遣戍伊犁。
entries.en: He was also stripped of office for failing to detect Jurong clerks' embezzlement of tax funds and was exiled to Yili.
entries.literal: He had also failed to detect Jurong clerks' embezzlement of tax funds; he was stripped of office and sent into exile at Yili.

entries.zh: 尋起為山西巡撫。
entries.en: He was soon recalled and appointed governor of Shanxi.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled and made governor of Shanxi.

entries.zh: 內閣學士尹壯圖論州縣虧空由於派累，疆臣中惟李世傑、書麟獨善其身，和珅尤忌之，命壯圖赴各省清查倉庫，自山西始，壯圖因獲譴。
entries.en: Cabinet Academician Yin Zhuangtu argued that local deficits came from excessive levies. Among frontier governors only Li Shijie and Shu Lin had kept their hands clean, which Heshen especially resented. Heshen sent Zhuangtu to audit provincial granaries, starting in Shanxi, and Zhuangtu himself was punished in the affair.
entries.literal: Cabinet academician Yin Zhuangtu argued that prefectural and county deficits arose from levied exactions; among frontier officials only Li Shijie and Shu Lin kept themselves clean, and Heshen especially resented them; he ordered Zhuangtu to go to each province to audit granaries, beginning with Shanxi, and Zhuangtu was punished as a result.

entries.zh: 五十六年，仍授兩江總督。
entries.en: In the fifty-sixth year he was again appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was again appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

entries.zh: 兩淮鹽政巴寧阿交結商人，坐書麟徇庇，复奪職，予三等侍衛，赴新疆效力。
entries.en: Lianghuai salt controller Ba Ning'a had colluded with merchants. Shu Lin was again dismissed for shielding him, given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and sent to Xinjiang to redeem himself through service.
entries.literal: Lianghuai salt controller Ba Ning'a colluded with merchants; Shu Lin was found guilty of shielding him, again lost his post, was given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and sent to Xinjiang to redeem himself through service.

entries.zh: 金士松，字亭立，江蘇吳江人，寄籍宛平。
entries.en: Jin Shisong, courtesy name Tingli, was from Wujiang in Jiangsu but registered his domicile at Wanping.
entries.literal: Jin Shisong, style name Tingli, was a native of Wujiang, Jiangsu, with registered domicile at Wanping.

entries.zh: 舉順天鄉試，改歸原籍。
entries.en: After passing the metropolitan provincial exam he reverted his registration to his native prefecture.
entries.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination and then changed back to his original domicile.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In Qianlong 25 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
entries.literal: In the 25th year of Qianlong, he became a jinshi, was selected as Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 遷侍讀，直懋勤殿寫經。
entries.en: He was promoted to Reader and assigned to copy scriptures in the Hall of Assiduous Cultivation.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Reader, assigned to the Maojin Hall to copy scriptures.

entries.zh: 典福建鄉試，督廣東學政。
entries.en: He presided over the Fujian provincial exams and served as Guangdong educational commissioner.
entries.literal: He presided over the Fujian provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Guangdong.

entries.zh: 直南書房，累遷詹事，以生母憂歸。
entries.en: After serving in the Southern Library and rising to Grand Tutor, he went home to mourn his birth mother.
entries.literal: He was assigned to the Southern Library, was promoted in succession to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned home on mourning for his birth mother.

entries.zh: 服闋，會高宗南巡，迎鑾道左，回京督順天學政。
entries.en: After mourning he greeted the Qianlong Emperor during a southern tour and, on returning to Beijing, took charge of Shuntian education.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, it coincided with the Gaozong Emperor's southern tour; he welcomed the imperial procession on the roadside; returning to the capital he served as educational commissioner of Shuntian.

entries.zh: 以寄籍辭，詔免迴避，聯任凡七年。
entries.en: He tried to decline because of domicile rules, but the emperor waived the conflict-of-interest requirement and let him serve seven years straight.
entries.literal: He declined on grounds of domicile registration; an edict exempted him from the avoidance rule, and he held the post consecutively for seven years in all.

entries.zh: 累擢禮部侍郎，調兵部。
entries.en: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites and was then transferred to War.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 五十年，帝御乾清宮，賜千叟宴。
entries.en: In Qianlong 50 the emperor held the Thousand Elders Banquet in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
entries.literal: In the 50th year, the Emperor held court at the Palace of Heavenly Purity and granted a Banquet for a Thousand Elders.

entries.zh: 士松年五十七，未得與，特命試詩，賞賚同一品。
entries.en: At fifty-seven he was too young for the banquet, but the emperor had him compose a poem and rewarded him as if he ranked among the guests.
entries.literal: Shisong was fifty-seven and did not qualify to attend; he was specially ordered to submit a poem for examination, and rewards were granted equal to those of the first rank.

entries.zh: 調吏部，直講經筵，校勘石經，遷左都御史。
entries.en: He moved to Civil Appointments, lectured at the imperial classics sessions, collated the stone classics, and became Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments, lectured at the Classic Lectures, collated the Stone Classics, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，再與千叟宴，遷禮部尚書。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 1 he attended the Thousand Elders Banquet again and was promoted to Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, he again attended the Thousand Elders Banquet and was promoted to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 二年，調兵部，罷直書房。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 2 he was moved to War and released from library duty.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and dismissed from duty in the Library.

entries.zh: 五年，扈蹕謁裕陵，途次嬰疾，遣御醫診視。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 5, on the way to pay respects at the Yuling Mausoleum, he fell ill and the emperor sent a court physician.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, while accompanying the imperial procession to visit the Yuling Mausoleum, he fell ill en route and the emperor sent an imperial physician to examine him.

entries.zh: 還京，卒，諡文簡，祀賢良祠。
entries.en: He died after returning to Beijing, was posthumously titled Wenjian, and honored in the Temple of Worthies.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, he died; posthumous title Wenjian; enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

entries.zh: 鄒炳泰，字仲文，江蘇無錫人。
entries.en: Zou Bingtai, courtesy name Zhongwen, was from Wuxi in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Zou Bingtai, style name Zhongwen, was a native of Wuxi, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，纂修四庫全書，遷國子監司業。
entries.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 37, he entered the Hanlin, served as compiler on the Complete Library project, and rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: Jinshi in the 37th year of Qianlong, selected Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler, compiled the Siku Quanshu, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 國學因元、明舊，未立辟雍，炳泰援古制疏請。
entries.en: The academy still followed Yuan and Ming models and lacked a ceremonial hall; Bingtai memorialized citing ancient precedent.
entries.literal: The Imperial Academy followed Yuan and Ming precedent and had no Piyong Hall; Bingtai cited ancient rites in a memorial requesting one.

entries.zh: 四十八年，高宗釋奠禮成，因下詔增建辟雍。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48, after the emperor's ceremonial offerings at the academy, he ordered construction of the Hall of the Circular Moat.
entries.literal: In the 48th year, after the Gaozong Emperor completed the sacrifice and libation rites, he issued an edict ordering the addition of a Piyong Hall.

entries.zh: 逾兩年，始舉臨雍禮，稱盛典焉。
entries.en: Two years later the emperor presided at the academy for the first time—a ceremony hailed as grand indeed.
entries.literal: More than two years later, the Emperor's visit to the Academy rite was first performed, and it was hailed as a great ceremony.

entries.zh: 尋超擢炳泰為祭酒。
entries.en: Bingtai was soon promoted ahead of schedule to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Bingtai was exceptionally promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 累遷內閣學士，歷山東、江西學政。
entries.en: He rose to Grand Secretariat academician and served as educational commissioner in Shandong and Jiangxi.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician and served as educational commissioner of Shandong and Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年，授禮部侍郎，調倉場，剔除積弊。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 4 he became Vice Minister of Rites, took charge of the granaries, and cleared away long-standing corruption.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to granary administration, and eliminated longstanding abuses.

entries.zh: 坐糧廳顏培天不職，劾去之。
entries.en: He impeached Yan Peitian of the grain office for neglect of duty and had him removed.
entries.literal: Because Yan Peitian of the grain office was derelict in duty, he impeached and had him removed.

entries.zh: 六年，京察，特予議敘。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 6 the capital personnel review singled him out for commendation.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, at the capital evaluation, he was specially granted consideration for reward and promotion.

entries.zh: 軍船交糧掛欠，已許抵補，後至者復然。
entries.en: Transport boats that delivered short were allowed to make up the deficit—and later arrivals did the same.
entries.literal: When military transport boats delivered grain with deficits on account, offset was already permitted; those arriving later did the same again.

entries.zh: 炳泰慮年年積欠，與同官達慶意不合，自具疏奏，詔斥其偏執使氣，鐫級留任。
entries.en: Fearing endless accumulated shortfalls, he clashed with colleague Da Qing and memorialized on his own; the emperor rebuked his obstinacy, demoted him one rank, but kept him in office.
entries.literal: Bingtai feared annual accumulation of deficits; he did not agree with his colleague Da Qing; he submitted his own memorial; an edict rebuked him for obstinate temperament, stripped one rank, and kept him at his post.

entries.zh: 又奏監督輪值宿倉，倉役出入滋弊，宜令於倉外官房居住，從之。
entries.en: He also argued that supervisors sleeping inside the granaries invited graft and should live in the outside quarters—the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: He also memorialized that supervisors took turns lodging in the granary, that entry and exit by granary servants fostered abuse, and that they ought to be ordered to reside in the official quarters outside the granary; the proposal was adopted.

entries.zh: 十年，擢左都御史，遷兵部尚書，兼署工部，管理戶部三庫。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 10 he became Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of War, acted as Minister of Works, and supervised the three revenue treasuries.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Minister of War, concurrently acting Minister of Works, and managing the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十一年，兼管順天府尹事。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 11 he also oversaw the Shuntian prefect's office.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he concurrently oversaw the affairs of the Shuntian prefect.

entries.zh: 十二年，調吏部。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 12 he was transferred to Civil Appointments.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.

entries.zh: 十四年，加太子少保。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 14 he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was given the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 倉吏高添鳳盜米事覺，坐久任倉場無所覺察，褫宮銜，降二品頂戴，​​革職留任，久乃復之。
entries.en: When granary clerk Gao Tianfeng's theft came to light, Bingtai was blamed for failing to detect it during his long tenure; he lost his honorific rank and second-rank insignia, was dismissed but kept on, and eventually had them restored.
entries.literal: When the theft of grain by granary clerk Gao Tianfeng was discovered, he was held responsible for long service in granary administration without detection; his palace rank was stripped, he was demoted to second-rank insignia, dismissed from office but retained at his post, and only after a long time was it restored.

entries.zh: 十六年，署戶部尚書。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 16 he acted as Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, acting Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 尋以吏部尚書協辦大學士。
entries.en: He soon served as Associate Grand Secretary while holding the Civil Appointments portfolio.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, as Minister of Civil Appointments he served as Associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 論曰：國家優禮詞臣，迴翔禁近，坐致公卿。
entries.en: The commentators observe: The state honors literary officials; service near the throne readily leads to the highest offices.
entries.literal: The commentary says: The state treats literary officials with favor; they move within the forbidden precincts and attain the rank of high minister without effort.

entries.zh: 沈初、金士松，高宗舊臣，獲恩禮終。
entries.en: Shen Chu and Jin Shisong, veterans of the Qianlong reign, enjoyed imperial favor to the end of their lives.
entries.literal: Shen Chu and Jin Shisong were old ministers of the Gaozong Emperor and received imperial favor to the end.

entries.zh: 王懿修父子同朝，尤稱盛事。
entries.en: Wang Yixiu and his son serving together at court was especially celebrated.
entries.literal: Wang Yixiu and his son serving in the same court was especially hailed as a grand occasion.

entries.zh: 黃鉞以不附和珅，特邀殊遇，改授館職，馴參機務。
entries.en: Huang Yue, for refusing to follow Heshen, won special favor, was transferred to Hanlin service, and eventually joined the Grand Council.
entries.literal: Huang Yue, because he did not attach himself to Heshen, received special extraordinary favor, was transferred to Hanlin posts, and steadily participated in council affairs.

entries.zh: 鄒炳泰、戴聯奎皆有耿介之操，晚節枯菀乃殊，要不失為端人焉。
entries.en: Zou Bingtai and Dai Liankui were both men of upright character; their late careers ended differently, yet both remained men of integrity.
entries.literal: Zou Bingtai and Dai Liankui both had upright and unyielding character; their late years withered or flourished differently, but in the end neither failed to be a man of integrity.

entries.zh: 沈初，字景初，浙江平湖人。
entries.en: Shen Chu, courtesy name Jingchu, came from Pinghu in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Shen Chu, style name Jingchu, was a native of Pinghu, Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 少有異禀，讀書目數行下，同郡錢陳群稱為異才。
entries.en: As a boy he showed unusual talent and could read several lines at a glance; Qian Chenqun of his prefecture hailed him as a prodigy.
entries.literal: In youth he possessed unusual gifts; when reading, his eye took in several lines at once; Qian Chenqun of the same commandery called him a prodigy.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十七年，南巡，召試，賜舉人，授內閣中書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 27, during the emperor's southern tour, he was summoned for a special examination, granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the 27th year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he was summoned for examination, granted juren status, and appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 明年，成一甲第三名進士，授編修。
entries.en: The following year he finished third in the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: The next year, he placed third in the first class of jinshi, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 三十二年，直懋勤殿，合寫經為皇太后祝釐。
entries.en: In Qianlong 32 he served in the Hall of Assiduous Cultivation, copying scriptures with others to invoke blessings for the empress dowager.
entries.literal: In the 32nd year, he was assigned to the Maoqin Hall, where he joined others in copying sutras to pray for blessings for the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 逾年，大考翰詹，以直內廷未與試，詔褒初學問優美，特晉一秩，擢侍講。
entries.en: When the Hanlin triennial examinations came around, he was exempted because he was serving in the inner palace; the emperor commended his scholarship and promoted him one rank to Reader-in-Waiting.
entries.literal: The following year, in the triennial examination of Hanlin and Hanlin Bachelors, because he was on duty in the inner court he did not take part in the test; an edict praised Chu's excellent learning and specially promoted him one rank, appointing him Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 三十六年，直南書房，督河南學政，未赴任，丁祖母承重憂。
entries.en: In Qianlong 36 he served in the Southern Library and was named Henan educational commissioner, but before he could take up the post he went into mourning for his grandmother.
entries.literal: In the 36th year, he was assigned to the Southern Library; he was appointed educational commissioner of Henan but before taking up the post entered mourning for his paternal grandmother, bearing the heaviest obligations of filial mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，遷右庶子。
entries.en: After mourning he was made Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he was transferred to Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 累擢禮部侍郎，督福建學政。
entries.en: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites and served as Fujian's educational commissioner.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and served as educational commissioner of Fujian.

entries.zh: 遭本生父憂，服闋，起兵部侍郎。
entries.en: After mourning his biological father he returned to office as Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: He suffered mourning for his biological father; when mourning ended, he took up the post of Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 尋以母病乞歸終養。
entries.en: He soon petitioned to retire home to care for his ailing mother until her death.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, because of his mother's illness, he requested leave to return home for final care.

entries.zh: 後起故官，督順天學政，調江蘇。
entries.en: Later recalled, he served as Shuntian educational commissioner and then was transferred to Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Later he was recalled to his former office, served as educational commissioner of Shuntian, and was transferred to Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 任滿回京，調吏部，又督江西學政。
entries.en: After his term he returned to the capital, moved to the Board of Civil Appointments, and later served as Jiangxi educational commissioner.
entries.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital, was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments, and again served as educational commissioner of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 子宗誠，字廉甫。
entries.en: His son Zong Cheng, courtesy name Lianfu.
entries.literal: His son Zong Cheng, style name Lianfu.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十五年一甲三名進士，授編修。
entries.en: In Qianlong 55 he placed third in the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: In the 55th year of Qianlong, third in the first class of jinshi, appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 嘉慶中，歷典雲南、四川、陝西鄉試，督河南、山東、江西學政，洊擢禮部侍郎，歷工部、兵部，典會試。
entries.en: Under Jiaqing he presided over provincial exams in Yunnan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, served as educational commissioner in Henan, Shandong, and Jiangxi, rose to Vice Minister of Rites, held posts in Works and War, and presided over the metropolitan examinations.
entries.literal: During the Jiaqing reign, he presided in succession over the provincial examinations of Yunnan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, served as educational commissioner of Henan, Shandong, and Jiangxi, was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, served in the Ministries of Works and War, and presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 道光二年，擢兵部尚書，歷署禮部、工部尚書，兼管順天府尹。
entries.en: In Daoguang 2 he became Minister of War, acted as Minister of Rites and Minister of Works, and also oversaw the Shuntian prefect's office.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, promoted to Minister of War, served in succession as acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Works, and concurrently oversaw the Shuntian prefect.

entries.zh: 當懿修為侍郎時，宗誠已官學士，尋隨父扈蹕東巡，侍宴翰林院，父子同席。
entries.en: While Yixiu was a vice minister, Zong Cheng was already an academician; he later joined his father on an eastern tour and, at a Hanlin banquet, father and son sat at the same table.
entries.literal: When Yixiu was Vice Minister, Zong Cheng already held the rank of Academician; soon afterward he accompanied his father on the eastern tour in the imperial retinue, attended a banquet at the Hanlin Academy, and father and son shared the same seat.

entries.zh: 高宗實錄成，賜宴禮部，懿修以尚書主席。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed, the court held a banquet at the Ministry of Rites with Yixiu, as minister, presiding.
entries.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Gaozong Emperor were completed, a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites; Yixiu as Minister presided.

entries.zh: 懿修致仕後，宗誠繼直上書房，海內推為榮遇。
entries.en: After Yixiu retired, Zong Cheng continued in the Upper Library—a succession widely hailed as a great honor.
entries.literal: After Yixiu retired, Zong Cheng continued service in the Upper Library; throughout the realm this was acclaimed as a signal honor.

entries.zh: 上亦以其兩世官禁近，皆能清慎，特優睞焉。
entries.en: The emperor also favored them specially, noting that for two generations they had served close to the throne with integrity and discretion.
entries.literal: The Emperor also, because for two generations they had held posts near the throne and both were able to be pure and cautious, showed them special favor.

entries.zh: 道光十七年，卒。
entries.en: He died in Daoguang 17.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year of Daoguang, he died.

entries.zh: 炳泰在吏部久，尤慎銓政。
entries.en: Bingtai had long served at Civil Appointments and was famously meticulous about personnel decisions.
entries.literal: Bingtai served long in the Board of Civil Appointments and was especially careful in appointment matters.

entries.zh: 十八年，銓選兵部主事有誤，同官瑚圖禮徇司員議，回護堅執。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 18 a War Ministry appointment went wrong; colleague Hutuli sided with the staff and refused to back down.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, there was an error in the selection of a secretary in the Ministry of War; colleague Hutuli indulged the departmental staff's opinion and stubbornly shielded them.

entries.zh: 炳泰力爭曰：「吾年已衰，何戀戀祿位？
entries.en: Bingtai protested: "I am old—why should I cling to rank and salary?
entries.literal: Bingtai argued forcefully: "I am already old in years—why should I cling so to salary and rank?

entries.zh: 不可使朝廷法自我壞！」
entries.en: I cannot be the one to break the court's law!"
entries.literal: One must not let the laws of the court be broken starting with me!"

entries.zh: 自具疏白其故，上韙其言，卒罷瑚圖禮。
entries.en: He memorialized the emperor himself; the emperor approved, and Hutuli was dismissed.
entries.literal: He submitted his own memorial explaining the reason; the Emperor approved his words, and Hutuli was finally dismissed.

entries.zh: 既而有降革官捐复者二人，準駁不當，侍郎初彭齡論與不合，疏聞，上斥炳泰無定見，鐫級留任。
entries.en: Later he mishandled two demoted officials seeking reinstatement by purchase; Vice Minister Chu Pengling disagreed, and the emperor rebuked Bingtai's inconsistency, demoted him one rank, and kept him on.
entries.literal: Afterward there were two dismissed officials who purchased restoration; approval and rejection were improper; Vice Minister Chu Pengling's opinion differed; when the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor rebuked Bingtai for lack of fixed judgment, stripped one rank, and kept him at his post.

entries.zh: 又盜劫兵部主事姚堃於昌平八仙莊，詔以地近京畿，官吏闒茸，不能治盜，罷炳泰兼管府尹事。
entries.en: When bandits robbed War Ministry secretary Yao Kun near Changping, the emperor blamed local incompetence so close to the capital and stripped Bingtai of his concurrent prefectural duties.
entries.literal: Also, Secretary Yao Kun of the Ministry of War was robbed by bandits at Baxian Village in Changping; an edict held that the place was near the capital region, officials were negligent, and bandits could not be suppressed; Bingtai was removed from concurrent oversight of the prefect's affairs.

entries.zh: 及教匪林清變起，逆黨多居固安及黃村，追論炳泰在官不能覺察，以中允、贊善降補。
entries.en: When Lin Qing's sectarian rebellion broke out—many rebels lived in Gu'an and Huangcun—the court held that Bingtai should have known; he was demoted to middle academicianship and tutor.
entries.literal: When the heterodox sect rebel Lin Qing's uprising erupted, many rebels lived in Gu'an and Huangcun; retrospectively it was held that Bingtai in office had failed to detect them; he was demoted and reassigned as Academician Expositor and Mentor.

entries.zh: 尋休致，歸。
entries.en: He soon retired and went home.
entries.literal: Soon he retired and returned home.

entries.zh: 二十五年，卒。
entries.en: He died in Jiaqing 25.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he died.

entries.zh: 列傳一百三十八
entries.en: Biographies 138
entries.literal: Biographies 138

entries.zh: 晟自為曹郎，以治獄明慎受知高宗，敭歷中外，至是凡三入佐刑部。
entries.en: From his days as a bureau secretary, his careful and lucid handling of criminal cases had won Qianlong's trust. He had served widely in the capital and in the provinces, and by now had entered the Ministry of Punishments as its second-in-command three times.
entries.literal: From the time Cheng served as a bureau secretary, his clear and careful handling of criminal cases won the esteem of the Gaozong Emperor. He served in posts both within the capital and in the provinces, and by this point had entered the Ministry of Punishments as assistant minister three times.

entries.zh: 仁宗尤重刑事，晟讞鞫務得其平，多平反者。
entries.en: Jiaqing placed special weight on criminal justice. Cheng reviewed cases with an eye to fairness, and many wrongful convictions were overturned.
entries.literal: The Renzong Emperor especially valued criminal matters; in reviewing and trying cases Cheng strove to reach fair judgments, and many were reversed.

entries.zh: 江西巡撫張誠基剿義寧州匪，飾稱自率兵臨陣，為屬吏所訐。
entries.en: When Jiangxi Governor Zhang Chengji suppressed bandits in Yining, he falsely claimed to have led the troops in person, and a subordinate exposed him.
entries.literal: Jiangxi Governor Zhang Chengji suppressed bandits in Yining Prefecture but falsely claimed that he personally led troops into battle, and was impeached by a subordinate.

entries.zh: 命晟往按，得實，逮誠基，遂暫署巡撫。
entries.en: Cheng was sent to investigate, confirmed the charge, had Zhang arrested, and briefly acted as governor himself.
entries.literal: Cheng was ordered to go and investigate; the facts were established, Zhang Chengji was arrested, and Cheng then temporarily served as acting governor.

entries.zh: 尋回京。
entries.en: He soon returned to Beijing.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 九年，兼署戶部侍郎，命赴南河查勘清口運道，疏言河身淤墊，黃水增高，致清水不能暢注，宜啟祥符五瑞等閘以減黃，增運口蓋壩以蓄清，如議行。
entries.en: In 1804 he served additionally as acting vice minister of revenue and was sent to inspect the Qingkou transport channel on the Southern Canal. He reported that silting had raised the bed, the Yellow River had risen, and clear water could no longer run freely. He proposed opening the Xiangfu and Wurui gates to bleed off Yellow River water and raising the cover dam at the transport mouth to hold clear water. The court approved his plan.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he also served as acting vice minister of Revenue and was ordered to go to the Southern Canal to survey the Qingkou transport route. In a memorial he said the river channel was silted and raised, the Yellow River water had risen higher, and clear water could not flow freely; the Xiangfu and Wurui sluice gates should be opened to reduce the Yellow River flow, and the transport mouth cover dam should be increased to store clear water. His proposals were adopted.

entries.zh: 擢刑部尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of punishments.
entries.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 十一年，以老疾乞休，溫詔慰留。
entries.en: In 1806, pleading age and illness, he asked to retire, but a gracious edict urged him to stay on.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, citing age and illness, he requested retirement; a warm edict urged him to remain.

entries.zh: 以刑部事繁，特調工部。
entries.en: Because the Ministry of Punishments was overburdened, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: Because the Ministry of Punishments was overburdened with business, he was specially transferred to the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 章再上，乃命解職在京養疴。
entries.en: When he memorialized again, he was released from office to recover his health in Beijing.
entries.literal: When he memorialized again, he was ordered to leave office and convalesce in the capital.

entries.zh: 尋以前在直隸失察籓庫虛收事，降四品京堂。
entries.en: He was soon demoted to fourth-rank capital official for an earlier failure in Zhili to uncover false entries in a provincial treasury.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, because of his earlier failure in Zhili to detect false receipts in the princely storehouse, he was reduced to a fourth-rank capital official.

entries.zh: 歸，卒於家。
entries.en: He went home and died there.
entries.literal: He returned home and died there.

entries.zh: 姜晟，字光宇，江蘇元和人。
entries.en: Jiang Cheng, whose courtesy name was Guangyu, came from Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Jiang Cheng, courtesy name Guangyu, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，授刑部主事，累遷郎中。
entries.en: He took his jinshi degree in 1766, entered the Ministry of Punishments as a principal secretary, and rose step by step to director.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and was promoted successively to director.

entries.zh: 擢光祿寺少卿，轉太僕寺，仍兼刑部行走。
entries.en: Promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, he continued to hold concurrent duty in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, while still serving concurrently in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 四十四年，出為江西按察使。
entries.en: In 1779 he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he went out to serve as Jiangxi provincial judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 逾年，超擢刑部侍郎，屢命赴各省按事讞獄。
entries.en: The following year he was promoted ahead of schedule to vice minister of punishments and was often sent to the provinces to investigate affairs and review capital cases.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was promoted out of turn to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and was repeatedly ordered to go to the provinces to investigate cases and review criminal judgments.

entries.zh: 五十二年，授湖北巡撫。
entries.en: In 1787 he was made governor of Hubei.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year he was appointed governor of Hubei.

entries.zh: 時大軍徵台灣，晟運米十萬石濟餉需，上嘉之，予議敘。
entries.en: While the main forces were campaigning in Taiwan, he shipped a hundred thousand shi of rice to cover army rations. The throne commended him and recommended him for a merit citation.
entries.literal: At that time the great army was campaigning against Taiwan; Cheng transported one hundred thousand shi of grain to meet pay and provisions needs. The emperor praised this and granted him consideration for merit-based promotion.

entries.zh: 五十三年，荊州江堤潰，命大學士阿桂等往勘，以晟未能疏濬上游漲沙，並坐屬吏婪索淮鹽匣費，褫頂帶。
entries.en: In 1788 the Jingzhou river embankment collapsed. Grand Secretary Agui and others were sent to inspect the breach. Cheng was blamed for not clearing the silt that had built up upstream and also for subordinates who had extorted fees on Huai salt transport chests; he was stripped of his rank insignia.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year the Jingzhou river dike burst. The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui and others to go and survey the damage. Cheng was held responsible for failing to dredge the upstream silt buildup, and also implicated because subordinates had extorted Huai salt chest fees; his official insignia were stripped.

entries.zh: 尋召授刑部侍郎。
entries.en: He was soon recalled and reappointed vice minister of punishments.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 列傳一百三十九
entries.en: Biographies 139
entries.literal: Biographies number one hundred thirty-nine

entries.zh: 十二年，疏請八旗兵米酌給二成折色，詔斥妄改舊章，革職留任。
entries.en: In 1807 he proposed that twenty percent of Banner grain rations be paid in commuted cash. The throne rebuked him for rashly altering established rules and demoted him while keeping him in office.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized that twenty percent of Banner troops' grain rations be paid in commuted cash; an edict rebuked him for rashly altering established regulations, and he was stripped of office but retained in his post.

entries.zh: 先後疏論治河，請改建王營減壩，培築高堰、山盱堤后土坡及河岸大堤，修復雲梯關外海口，遣大臣勘議，並採其說施行。
entries.en: He submitted a series of memorials on river works, urging reconstruction of the Wangying spillway, reinforcement of the Gaoyan and Shanxu rear slopes and the main river dikes, and repair of the seagate beyond Yuntiguan. The court sent grand ministers to inspect his plans and put many of them into effect.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on river control, requesting reconstruction of the Wangying spillway, reinforcement of the Gaoyan and Shanxu rear slopes and the great river dikes, and repair of the seagate outside Yuntiguan; grand ministers were sent to survey and discuss, and his proposals were adopted and carried out.

entries.zh: 十四年，運河屢壞堤，荷花塘決口合而復潰，鐫級留任。
entries.en: In 1809 canal dikes failed repeatedly; the Hehuatang breach was sealed and then broke open again, and he was reduced in rank but kept in office.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year the Grand Canal dikes broke repeatedly; the breach at Hehuatang closed and then burst again, and he was demoted in rank but retained in his post.

entries.zh: 山陽知縣王伸漢冒賑，酖殺委員李毓昌，至是事覺，詔斥鐵保偏聽固執，河工日壞，吏治日弛，釀成重獄，褫職，遣戍烏魯木齊。
entries.en: Wang Shenhan, magistrate of Shanyang, had embezzled relief funds and poisoned Commissioner Li Yuchang; the crime now came to light. The throne rebuked Tie Bao for partiality and stubbornness, blamed him for worsening river works and slackening administration, stripped him of office, and sent him into exile at Urumqi.
entries.literal: Wang Shenhan, magistrate of Shanyang, had embezzled relief funds and poisoned Commissioner Li Yuchang; now the affair came to light. An edict rebuked Tie Bao for partiality and obstinacy, saying river works grew worse daily and official discipline slackened daily, producing a grave case; he was stripped of office and sent in exile to Urumqi.

entries.zh: 逾年，給三等侍衛，充葉爾羌辦事大臣。
entries.en: A year later he was made a third-class bodyguard and appointed commissioner at Yarkand.
entries.literal: After a year he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed commissioner at Yarkand.

entries.zh: 尋授翰林院侍講學士，調喀什噶爾參贊大臣。
entries.en: He was soon made Hanlin reader-in-waiting and transferred to assistant commissioner at Kashgar.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin reader-in-waiting and transferred to assistant commissioner at Kashgar.

entries.zh: 授浙江巡撫，未之任，改吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was named governor of Zhejiang but never took up the post and was instead made vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: He was appointed governor of Zhejiang but did not take up the post and was changed to vice minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 擢禮部尚書，調吏部。
entries.en: He rose to minister of rites and was transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was promoted to minister of rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 請芟吏、兵兩部苛例，條陳時政，多見施行。
entries.en: He asked that harsh precedents in the ministries of personnel and war be cut back, memorialized on current affairs, and saw many of his proposals adopted.
entries.literal: He requested pruning of harsh precedents in the ministries of personnel and war, set forth current policy in articles, and many of his proposals were implemented.

entries.zh: 林清之變，召對，極言內監通賊有據，因窮治逆黨，內監多銜恨，遍騰謗言。
entries.en: During the Lin Qing uprising he was summoned to audience and argued forcefully that eunuchs had aided the rebels. His thorough pursuit of the conspiracy earned the hatred of many eunuchs, who spread slander against him far and wide.
entries.literal: At the Lin Qing incident he was summoned for audience and strongly stated that there was evidence of eunuchs colluding with rebels; because he pursued the rebel party to the end, many eunuchs bore resentment and spread slander everywhere.

entries.zh: 會伊犁將軍松筠劾鐵保前在喀什噶爾治叛裔玉素普之獄，誤聽人言，枉殺回民毛拉素皮等四人，上怒，追念江南李毓昌之獄，斥其屢蹈重咎，褫職，發往吉林效力。
entries.en: When Ili General Songyun impeached Tie Bao for wrongly executing four Muslims, including Mullah Supi, in the case of the rebel Yusupu at Kashgar after heeding false reports, the emperor's anger revived memories of the Li Yuchang affair in the south. Rebuking him for repeated grave failures, the court stripped him of office and sent him to serve in Jilin.
entries.literal: When Ili General Songyun impeached Tie Bao for, while at Kashgar earlier, hearing false reports in the case of the rebel descendant Yusupu and wrongly executing four Muslims including Mullah Supi, the emperor was angry, recalled the Li Yuchang case in Jiangnan, rebuked him for repeatedly incurring grave blame, stripped him of office, and sent him to serve in Jilin.

entries.zh: 二十三年，召為司經局洗馬。
entries.en: In 1818 he was recalled as groom of the Directorate of Education.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he was recalled as groom of the Directorate of Education.

entries.zh: 道光初，以疾乞休，賜三品卿銜。
entries.en: Early in the Daoguang reign he retired on grounds of illness and was granted third-rank chamberlain rank.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang, on grounds of illness he requested retirement and was granted third-rank chamberlain rank.

entries.zh: 四年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1824.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died.

entries.zh: 十八年，教匪林清逆黨闌入禁城，桂芳方直內廷，偕諸王大臣率兵殲捕，敘勞，加二級。
entries.en: In 1813 Lin Qing's rebel sect broke into the Forbidden City while Guifang was on duty in the inner court. He joined princes and grand ministers in leading troops to crush the intruders and was rewarded with two steps of promotion.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the rebel party of the sectarian Lin Qing broke into the Forbidden City; Guifang was then on duty in the inner court and, together with princes and grand ministers, led troops to exterminate and capture them; for merit he was given two steps of promotion.

entries.zh: 上遇變修省，訓誡臣工，頒御製文七篇，示內廷諸臣，命各抒所見，書以進禦。
entries.en: After the crisis the emperor turned to self-examination, admonished the bureaucracy, issued seven imperial essays, showed them to inner-court officials, and ordered each to submit written views to the throne.
entries.literal: After the crisis the emperor cultivated self-examination, admonished his ministers, issued seven imperial compositions, showed them to inner-court officials, and ordered each to express his views in writing for presentation to the throne.

entries.zh: 桂芳書罪己詔后曰：「皇上臨御以來，承列聖深仁厚澤，日以愛民為政，四海之內，莫不聞睹。
entries.en: Guifang wrote after the emperor's self-reproach edict: 'Since Your Majesty came to the throne, inheriting the deep benevolence of successive sage rulers, you have governed daily with love for the people, and all within the four seas have witnessed it.
entries.literal: Guifang wrote after the self-reproach edict: 'Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, inheriting the deep benevolence and thick grace of successive sages, you have daily governed with love for the people; within the four seas none has failed to hear and see this.

entries.zh: 今茲事變，豈不怪異？
entries.en: That such an incident should occur—is it not strange?
entries.literal: Now this incident—is it not strange?

entries.zh: 而臣竊以為此未足為聖德之累。
entries.en: Yet I venture to think this is not enough to diminish Your Majesty's sagely virtue.
entries.literal: Yet your servant privately thinks this is not enough to burden sagely virtue.

entries.zh: 昔孔子論仁至於濟眾，論敬至於安百姓，皆曰：'堯、舜其猶病諸。
entries.en: Confucius, in speaking of benevolence as far as benefiting the multitude and of reverence as far as securing the people, said of each: 'Even Yao and Shun would still have found it difficult.'
entries.literal: Formerly Confucius, in discussing benevolence up to benefiting the multitude and respect up to securing the people, said of both: 'Even Yao and Shun would still have found it difficult.'

entries.zh: '豈真以堯、舜之聖為未至哉？
entries.en: Did he truly mean that Yao and Shun had not yet attained sagehood?
entries.literal: Did he truly regard the sagehood of Yao and Shun as not yet attained?

entries.zh: 夫天下之大，萬民之眾，而決其無一夫之梗者，蓋自古其難之。
entries.en: In a realm so vast and a populace so numerous, to ensure that not a single man is recalcitrant has been difficult since antiquity.
entries.literal: For all the vastness of the realm and the multitude of the people, to decide that not a single man is recalcitrant has from antiquity been difficult.

entries.zh: 然而揆之人事，則實有未盡者。
entries.en: Yet measured by human affairs, there were indeed things left undone.
entries.literal: Yet measured by human affairs, there truly were things not fully done.

entries.zh: 夫林清先以習教被系，既釋歸，轉益煽亂。
entries.en: Lin Qing was first arrested for sect activity, and after his release he only fomented rebellion the more.
entries.literal: Lin Qing was first arrested for practicing sect teachings; after release he returned home and only fomented rebellion the more.

entries.zh: 數年之間，往來糾結於曹、衛、齊、魯之間，其黨至數千人。
entries.en: Within a few years he traveled through Cao, Wei, Qi, and Lu organizing his following, which grew to several thousand.
entries.literal: Within a few years he traveled back and forth organizing conspiracies among Cao, Wei, Qi, and Lu; his party reached several thousand.

entries.zh: 閹寺職官，竟有與其謀者，而未事之先，曾無一人抉發，是吏無政也。
entries.en: Eunuchs and officials even joined his plot, yet before the attack not one person exposed it—this shows that official administration had failed.
entries.literal: Eunuchs and officials actually joined in his plot, yet before the affair not one person exposed it—this shows that officials had no government.

entries.zh: 藏利刃，懷白幟，度越門關，飲於都市，無诇而知者，是邏者、門者無禁也。
entries.en: They hid blades, carried white banners, passed gate after gate, and drank in the markets without anyone detecting them—this shows that patrolmen and gatekeepers enforced no ban.
entries.literal: They hid sharp blades, carried white banners, crossed gate after gate, drank in the marketplaces, and none who inquired knew—this shows that patrolmen and gatekeepers had no prohibition.

entries.zh: 禁兵千計，賊不及百，闔門而擊之，俄頃可盡，乃兩日一夜始悉擒戮，是軍無律也。
entries.en: Palace guards numbered in the thousands while the rebels were fewer than a hundred; with the gates closed they could have been destroyed in moments, yet it took two days and a night to capture and kill them all—this shows that the army had no discipline.
entries.literal: Palace guards numbered in the thousands, rebels not a hundred; closing the gates and striking them could have exterminated them in a moment, yet only after two days and one night were all captured and killed—this shows that the army had no discipline.

entries.zh: 夫吏惰卒驕，文武並弛，而法制禁令為虛器，則事之可憂，豈獨在賊？
entries.en: When officials grow slack, soldiers arrogant, civil and military discipline alike relax, and laws become empty forms, the danger lies not only in the rebels themselves?
entries.literal: When officials are slack and soldiers arrogant, civil and military alike are lax, and laws and prohibitions become empty vessels, then what is to be feared in the affair lies not only in the rebels?

entries.zh: 我皇上觀微知著，洞悉天下之故，詔曰'方今大弊在因循怠玩'，至哉言乎！
entries.en: Your Majesty observes the subtle and knows the manifest and has thoroughly grasped the state of the realm. The edict declaring that 'the great evil of the age lies in routine and slack indulgence' is words of the highest wisdom!
entries.literal: Our emperor observes the subtle and knows the manifest, thoroughly understands the reasons of all under heaven, and in an edict said: 'At present the great evil lies in routine and slack indulgence'—how excellent a saying!

entries.zh: 臣敬繹之，蓋因循怠玩，亦有所由。
entries.en: I respectfully interpret this: routine and slack indulgence also have their causes.
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully interprets this: routine and slack indulgence also have their causes.

entries.zh: 無才與識，則有因循而已；
entries.en: Without talent and judgment, there is only routine;
entries.literal: Without talent and knowledge, there is only routine;

entries.zh: 無志與氣，則有怠玩而已。
entries.en: without will and resolve, there is only slack indulgence.
entries.literal: without will and spirit, there is only slack indulgence.

entries.zh: 是故得人而任之，則因循怠玩之習不患不除。
entries.en: Therefore, if the right men are found and entrusted with office, the habits of routine and slack indulgence can surely be uprooted.
entries.literal: Therefore if the right men are obtained and entrusted, the habits of routine and slack indulgence need not be feared as impossible to remove.

entries.zh: 儻非其人，微獨不能除其習而已；
entries.en: If the wrong men are chosen, not only will those habits remain;
entries.literal: If they are not the right men, not only can the habits not be removed;

entries.zh: 就令除之，不因循而且為煩苛，不怠玩而且為躁競，其無裨於治則均耳。
entries.en: even if one tries to remove them, the result will be not routine but vexatious harshness, not slackness but rash contention—equally useless for good government.
entries.literal: even if one removes them, one will not be routine but will become vexatiously harsh, not slack but will become rash and contentious—the harm to good government is the same.

entries.zh: 是在皇上詢事考言，循名責實，器使之以奏其能，專任之以收其效，因小失而崇丕業，在陛下一旋轉間耳。」
entries.en: The remedy lies in Your Majesty inquiring into affairs and testing words, matching names to realities, employing each man according to his capacity, entrusting him fully to secure results, and turning a small setback into a great achievement—all within a single turn of Your Majesty's will.'
entries.literal: This lies in Your Majesty inquiring into affairs and examining words, matching names to realities, employing men according to their capacity so they may display their ability, entrusting them fully so as to gather their effect, and through a small loss exalting a great enterprise—all within a single turn of Your Majesty.'

entries.zh: 鐵保慷慨論事，高宗謂其有大臣風。
entries.en: Tie Bao debated state affairs with bold candor, and Emperor Qianlong said he had the bearing of a great minister.
entries.literal: Tie Bao spoke on affairs with generous forthrightness; Emperor Gaozong said he had the bearing of a great minister.

entries.zh: 及居外任，自欲有所表見，倨傲，意為愛憎，屢以措施失當被黜。
entries.en: In provincial office he was eager to make his mark, grew arrogant, let personal likes and dislikes guide him, and was repeatedly dismissed for misjudged policies.
entries.literal: When he held provincial posts he wished to make a mark, was arrogant, acted from favor and dislike, and was repeatedly dismissed for improper measures.

entries.zh: 然優於文學，詞翰並美。
entries.en: Yet he excelled in letters, and both his prose and poetry were admired.
entries.literal: Yet he excelled in letters, and both his prose and poetry were fine.

entries.zh: 兩典禮闈及山東、順天鄉試，皆得人。
entries.en: He twice presided over the metropolitan examination and over the Shandong and Shuntian provincial examinations, each time choosing able candidates.
entries.literal: Twice he presided over the metropolitan examination and the Shandong and Shuntian provincial examinations, and in each case selected able men.

entries.zh: 留心文獻，為八旗通志總裁。
entries.en: He devoted himself to historical sources and served as chief compiler of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners.
entries.literal: He attended to historical documents and served as chief compiler of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners.

entries.zh: 多得開國以來滿洲、蒙古、漢軍遺集，先成白山詩介五十卷，復增輯改編，得一百三十四卷，進禦，仁宗制序，賜名熙朝雅頌集。
entries.en: He gathered many surviving works by Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner writers since the founding of the dynasty, first compiled the Baishan Shijie in fifty juan, then expanded and revised it to one hundred thirty-four juan. He presented it to the throne; Emperor Renzong wrote a preface and bestowed the title Elegant Odes of a Flourishing Age.
entries.literal: He obtained many surviving collections of Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner writers since the founding of the dynasty, first compiled the Baishan Shijie in fifty juan, then expanded and revised it to one hundred thirty-four juan, presented it to the throne, and Emperor Renzong wrote a preface and granted the title Xichao Yasong Ji.

entries.zh: 自著曰懷清齋集。
entries.en: His own collected writings were entitled the Huaiqing Studio Collection.
entries.literal: His own collected writings are entitled Huaiqingzhai Ji.

entries.zh: 鐵保，字冶亭，棟鄂氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Tie Bao, whose courtesy name was Yeting, came from the Donggo clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Tie Bao, courtesy name Yeting, of the Donggo clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 先世姓覺羅，稱為趙宋之裔，後改今氏。
entries.en: His forebears had borne the surname Jueluo and were claimed as descendants of the Song house; the family later adopted its present clan name.
entries.literal: His ancestors bore the surname Jueluo and were said to be descendants of the Song of Zhao; later they changed to the present clan name.

entries.zh: 父誠泰，泰宁鎮總兵，世為將家。
entries.en: His father Cheng Tai was regional commander at Taining, and for generations the family had produced soldiers.
entries.literal: His father Cheng Tai was regional commander at Taining; for generations the family had been a military house.

entries.zh: 鐵保折節讀書，年二十一，成乾隆三十七年進士，授吏部主事，襲恩騎尉世職。
entries.en: Tie Bao applied himself to learning and, at twenty-one, passed the jinshi examination in 1772. He entered the Ministry of Personnel as a principal secretary and inherited a hereditary enjiwei rank.
entries.literal: Tie Bao bent himself to study; at twenty-one he became jinshi in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, and inherited the hereditary enjiwei rank.

entries.zh: 於曹司中介然孤立，意有不可，爭辯勿撓。
entries.en: In the ministry he held himself apart with integrity: whenever he thought a matter unjust, he argued his case without yielding.
entries.literal: In the ministry offices he stood apart with integrity; when he thought something wrong, he argued without yielding.

entries.zh: 大學士阿桂屢薦之，遷郎中，擢少詹事，因事罷。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Agui recommended him repeatedly. He rose to director and then junior grand tutor before being dismissed over a dispute.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Agui repeatedly recommended him; he was promoted to director, then to junior grand tutor, and was dismissed because of an affair.

entries.zh: 尋補戶部員外郎，調吏部。
entries.en: He was soon reappointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: Soon he was reappointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 擢翰林院侍講學士，仍兼吏部行走，歷侍讀學士、內閣學士。
entries.en: He was promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting while still serving in the Ministry of Personnel, then rose through reader and academician of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting while still serving concurrently in the Ministry of Personnel, and passed through reader and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 五十四年，遷禮部侍郎，兼副都統。
entries.en: In 1789 he became vice minister of rites with a concurrent post as deputy lieutenant-general.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of rites with concurrent duty as deputy lieutenant-general.

entries.zh: 校射中的，賜花翎。
entries.en: He scored a hit in the archery review and was awarded the peacock feather.
entries.literal: In the archery review he hit the target and was granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 調吏部。
entries.en: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 弟玉保，字閬峰。
entries.en: His younger brother Yu Bao, whose courtesy name was Langfeng.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yu Bao, courtesy name Langfeng.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十六年進士，入翰林，有才名。
entries.en: He took his jinshi degree in 1781, entered the Hanlin, and won a reputation for literary talent.
entries.literal: Jinshi in the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, he entered the Hanlin and had a reputation for talent.

entries.zh: 高宗親試八旗翰詹，與兄鐵保並被擢，時比以郊、祁，軾、轍。
entries.en: Emperor Qianlong personally examined the Banner Hanlin and Heir Apparent's household; he and his elder brother Tie Bao were both advanced, and contemporaries likened them to two earlier pairs of brothers: Song Jiao and Song Qi, and Su Shi and Su Zhe.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong personally examined the Banner Hanlin and Household of the Heir Apparent; he and his elder brother Tie Bao were both promoted, and at the time they were compared to Song Jiao and Song Qi, and to Su Shi and Su Zhe.

entries.zh: 官至兵部侍郎，究心兵家言。
entries.en: He rose to vice minister of war and devoted himself to the art of war.
entries.literal: He rose to vice minister of war and devoted himself to military writings.

entries.zh: 川、楚教匪起，嘗原自效行間。
entries.en: When sectarian rebels broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, he once volunteered for active service.
entries.literal: When sectarian rebels rose in Sichuan and Hubei, he once volunteered to serve in the field.

entries.zh: 會上欲用為巡撫，為和珅所阻，鬱鬱卒，年甫四十。
entries.en: The emperor was about to appoint him governor when Heshen blocked the move. He died in low spirits at barely forty.
entries.literal: Just then the emperor wished to appoint him governor, but Heshen obstructed it; he died in dejection at barely forty.

entries.zh: 列傳一百四十
entries.en: Biographies 140
entries.literal: Biographies 140

entries.zh: 魁倫，完顏氏，滿洲正黃旗人，副將軍查弼納孫也。
entries.en: Kui Lun, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and a grandson of the deputy general Zhabina.
entries.literal: Kui Lun, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and grandson of the deputy general Zhabina.

entries.zh: 襲世管佐領，兼輕車都尉，授四川漳臘營參將，累擢建昌鎮總兵。
entries.en: He inherited the hereditary assistant commandant post, held the concurrent title of Commandant of Light Chariots, served as deputy commander of the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan, and rose by stages to commander-in-chief of Jianchang Garrison.
entries.literal: He inherited the hereditary assistant commandant post, also held the title of Commandant of Light Chariots, was appointed a deputy commander in the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan, and was repeatedly promoted to commander-in-chief of Jianchang Garrison.

entries.zh: 嘗入覲，高宗詢家世，魁倫陳戰功甚悉。
entries.en: On one audience at court, the Gaozong Emperor asked about his lineage, and Kui Lun recounted his family’s battle honors at length.
entries.literal: Once when he came to court for an audience, the Gaozong Emperor inquired into his family background, and Kui Lun set forth his forebears’ military achievements in great detail.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十三年，擢福州將軍。
entries.en: In the fifty-third year of the Qianlong reign he was appointed military governor of Fuzhou.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year of Qianlong he was promoted to Fuzhou Military Governor.

entries.zh: 喜聲伎，制行不謹，總督伍拉納欲劾之。
entries.en: He was fond of music and performers and careless in his conduct, and Governor-General Wula Na sought to impeach him.
entries.literal: He delighted in music and entertainers and was lax in conduct; Governor-General Wula Na wished to impeach him.

entries.zh: 伍拉納故貪，逼勒屬吏財賄，复縱洋盜，盜艇集五虎門外不問。
entries.en: Wula Na was notoriously corrupt, squeezed his subordinates for bribes, and winked at foreign pirates, whose vessels clustered outside the Five Tiger Gate unchecked.
entries.literal: Wula Na was by nature greedy, extorted bribes from subordinate officials, and again indulged foreign pirates, whose boats gathered outside the Wuhu Gate without inquiry.

entries.zh: 魁倫遂疊疏劾閩省吏治廢弛，伍拉納及巡撫浦霖溺職，按察使錢受椿等迎合助虐。
entries.en: Kui Lun then filed repeated memorials denouncing Fujian’s collapsed governance, accusing Wula Na and Governor Pu Lin of neglecting duty and Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun and others of flattering their superiors and aiding abuse.
entries.literal: Kui Lun then sent repeated memorials impeaching the slack administration of Fujian, charging Wula Na and Governor Pu Lin with dereliction, and the surveillance commissioner Qian Shouchun and others with currying favor and abetting oppression.

entries.zh: 上怒，褫伍拉納等職逮問，命長麟署總督，偕魁倫鞫訊，得伍拉納等貪婪及庫藏虧絀狀，俱伏法。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, stripped Wula Na and his associates of rank and ordered them arrested; he appointed Chang Lin acting governor-general and had him investigate jointly with Kui Lun. Their corruption and the treasury shortfalls were proved, and all were put to death.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged, stripped Wula Na and the others of office and had them arrested for trial, ordered Chang Lin to act as governor-general, and together with Kui Lun conducted the inquiry; the greed of Wula Na and the others and the deficits in the treasury were established, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 伍拉納為和珅姻戚，當按治時，上切責長麟瞻徇，罷去，以事由魁倫舉發，特寬之，代署總督，嚴捕海盜，屢獲其魁。
entries.en: Wula Na was related by marriage to Heshen. During the prosecution the emperor sharply rebuked Chang Lin for partiality and dismissed him. Because Kui Lun had brought the matter to light, he was treated with special leniency, made acting governor-general, waged a vigorous campaign against pirates, and repeatedly took their ringleaders.
entries.literal: Wula Na was a relative by marriage of Heshen; when the case was being handled the emperor sharply rebuked Chang Lin for favoritism and removed him. Because the affair had been exposed by Kui Lun, he was specially lenient, made acting governor-general in Chang Lin’s place, strictly hunted pirates, and repeatedly captured their leaders.

entries.zh: 列傳一百四十二
entries.en: Biographies 142
entries.literal: Biographies, Number 142

entries.zh: 四年，高宗崩，仁宗始親政。
entries.en: In 1799 the Qianlong emperor died and the Jiaqing emperor took the reins himself.
entries.literal: In the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died and the Renzong Emperor began to rule in person.

entries.zh: 大學士硃珪書起之，供職，與修高宗實錄，第一次稿本成，意有不樂。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui recalled him by letter. He resumed office and worked on the Qianlong Veritable Records, but when the first draft was done he was deeply dissatisfied.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui summoned him back by letter; he took office and helped compile the Veritable Records of Gaozong. When the first draft was finished he was displeased in mind.

entries.zh: 將告歸，上書軍機王大臣言事，略曰：「今天子求治之心急矣，天下望治之心孔迫矣，而機局未轉者，推原其故，蓋有數端。
entries.en: On the eve of resigning he sent a long letter to the Grand Council prince-ministers. It began: "The emperor's hunger for reform is keen and the empire's longing for order still keener, yet the machinery of government has barely moved. The reasons, I believe, are several.
entries.literal: About to request leave and return home, he submitted a letter to the Grand Council prince-ministers stating his views, in summary as follows: "Today the Son of Heaven's desire for good government is urgent, and the empire's longing for good government is exceedingly pressing, yet the machinery of state has not turned—tracing the causes, there are several.

entries.zh: 亮吉以為勵精圖治，當一法祖宗初政之勤，而尚未盡法也。
entries.en: Liangji argued that reviving government should mean matching the diligence of the dynasty's early reigns—and that standard had not yet been met.
entries.literal: Liangji held that in striving for diligent rule one ought wholly to follow the diligence of the founding policies of the ancestors, yet this had not been fully followed.

entries.zh: 用人行政，當一改權臣當國之時，而尚未盡改也。
entries.en: Appointments and policy ought to break decisively with the era of domineering ministers—and that break was still incomplete.
entries.literal: In employing men and administering affairs one ought to change completely the conditions of the time when powerful ministers held the state, yet this had not been fully changed.

entries.zh: 風俗則日趨卑下，賞罰則仍不嚴明，言路則似通而未通，吏治則欲肅而未肅。
entries.en: Morals were sinking day by day; rewards and punishments remained lax; the path of candid counsel looked open but was not; and the bureaucracy was meant to be tightened but was not.
entries.literal: Customs daily sank lower; rewards and punishments were still not strict and clear; the avenue of remonstrance seemed open yet was not truly open; and official administration wished to be rectified yet was not truly rectified.

entries.zh: 何以言勵精圖治尚未盡法也？
entries.en: Why had revival of government not yet been achieved?
entries.literal: Why say that striving for diligent rule has not yet been fully followed?

entries.zh: 自三四月以來，視朝稍晏，竊恐退朝之後，俳優近習之人，熒惑聖聽者不少。
entries.en: Since spring, audiences had been held later and later. I feared that after court, actors and favored attendants were misleading the emperor in no small number.
entries.literal: Since the third and fourth months audiences have been held somewhat late; I fear that after leaving court, actors and intimate attendants who beguile the imperial ear are not few.

entries.zh: 此親臣大臣啟沃君心者之過也。
entries.en: That was the fault of the intimate ministers who were supposed to guide the ruler's mind.
entries.literal: This is the fault of intimate ministers and great officials who ought to nourish the ruler's mind.

entries.zh: 蓋犯顏極諫，雖非親臣大臣之事，然不可使國家無嚴憚之人。
entries.en: Blunt remonstrance at the risk of one's life was not their special duty, yet the state could not afford to lack men whom others deeply feared.
entries.literal: For although risking one's life in blunt remonstrance is not the special duty of intimate ministers, the state must not be without men whom others deeply fear.

entries.zh: 乾隆初年，純皇帝宵旰不遑，勤求至治，其時如鄂文端、硃文端、張文和、孫文定等，皆侃侃以老成師傅自居。
entries.en: In the early Qianlong years the emperor labored from dawn to midnight in pursuit of perfect government. Men such as E Wenduan, Zhu Wenduan, Zhang Wenhe, and Sun Wending spoke plainly and styled themselves seasoned mentors of the throne.
entries.literal: In the early Qianlong years the Chun Emperor toiled from dawn till midnight without rest, diligently seeking perfect rule; at that time men such as E Wen-duan, Zhu Wen-duan, Zhang Wen-he, and Sun Wen-ding all spoke forthrightly and took themselves to be seasoned tutors.

entries.zh: 亮吉恭修實錄，見一日中硃筆細書，折成方寸，或詢張、鄂，或詢孫、硃，曰某人賢否，某事當否，日或十馀次。
entries.en: While helping compile the Veritable Records, Liangji saw how in a single day the emperor's vermilion brush would jot tiny folded notes—now asking Zhang or E, now Sun or Zhu, whether so-and-so was fit for office or whether such-and-such ought to be done—sometimes a dozen times in one day.
entries.literal: Liangji, in reverently compiling the Veritable Records, saw that in a single day the vermilion brush would write fine characters folded to an inch square, now asking Zhang or E, now asking Sun or Zhu, whether a certain man was worthy or unworthy, whether a certain matter ought to be done or not—sometimes more than ten times a day.

entries.zh: 諸臣亦皆隨時隨事奏片，質語直陳，是上下無隱情。
entries.en: Ministers likewise filed timely memorial slips in plain, direct language, so that nothing was hidden between throne and officials.
entries.literal: The various ministers also submitted memorial slips on every occasion and matter, speaking plainly in direct language, so that above and below there were no hidden facts.

entries.zh: 純皇帝固聖不可及，而亦眾正盈朝，前後左右皆嚴憚之人故也。
entries.en: The emperor's sagacity was beyond compare, but it also helped that upright men filled the court and that everyone around him was someone to be feared.
entries.literal: The Chun Emperor was indeed sage beyond reach, but it was also because upright men filled the court and those before, behind, left, and right were all men deeply feared.

entries.zh: 今一則處事太緩，自乾隆五十五年以後，權私蒙蔽，事事不得其平者，不知凡幾矣。
entries.en: Today, first, business moved too slowly. Since 1790 private interests had clouded judgment, and wrongs left unsettled were beyond counting.
entries.literal: Now, first, affairs are handled too slowly; since the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, private power has veiled the truth, and cases in which things were not settled fairly—who knows how many?

entries.zh: 千百中無有一二能上達者，即能上達，未必即能見之施行也。
entries.en: Of hundreds of grievances scarcely one or two reached the throne, and even then they might never be acted on.
entries.literal: Of a thousand or hundred cases scarcely one or two could reach the throne; even if they did reach it, they might not necessarily be seen and carried out.

entries.zh: 如江南洋盜一案，參將楊天相有功駢戮，洋盜某漏網安居，皆由署總督蘇凌阿昏憒糊塗，貪贓玩法，舉世知其冤，而洋盜公然上岸無所顧忌，皆此一事釀成。
entries.en: Consider the Jiangnan pirate case: Battalion Commander Yang Tianxiang, a man with real merit, was executed in a mass killing while a pirate went free—all because Acting Governor Su Ling'a was muddled, greedy, and lawless. Everyone knew Yang had been wronged, yet pirates now landed openly without fear. One botched case had taught them they could.
entries.literal: Take the Jiangnan pirate case: Battalion Commander Yang Tianxiang, who had merit, was executed together with others, while a certain pirate escaped the net and lived at ease—all because Acting Governor Su Ling'a was muddled and stupid, greedy for bribes and contemptuous of law. The whole world knew his injustice, yet pirates openly came ashore without fear; all this was brewed by that one affair.

entries.zh: 況蘇凌阿權相私人，朝廷必無所顧惜，而至今尚擁巨貲，厚自頤養。
entries.en: Worse, Su Ling'a was a creature of the late power-holder; the court owed him no tenderness, yet he still sat on a fortune and lived in comfort.
entries.literal: Moreover Su Ling'a was a private man of the powerful minister; the court ought certainly not to spare him, yet to this day he still holds great wealth and nourishes himself lavishly.

entries.zh: 江南查辦此案，始則有心為承審官開釋，繼則並聞以不冤覆奏。
entries.en: The Jiangnan inquiry first seemed bent on excusing the presiding judge; later word came that the court had been told there was no injustice at all.
entries.literal: In Jiangnan's investigation of this case, at first there was intent to exonerate the presiding judge; later it was even heard that a memorial was submitted covering the matter as not unjust.

entries.zh: 夫以聖天子赫然獨斷，欲平反一事而尚如此，則此外沉冤何自而雪乎？
entries.en: If even when the sage emperor himself intervened to right one case the outcome was still such, how were all the other buried wrongs ever to be cleared?
entries.literal: If with the sage Son of Heaven's august independent decision, wishing to reverse one case, it is still thus, then how can other submerged wrongs ever be cleared?

entries.zh: 一則集思廣益之法未備。
entries.en: Second, the methods for pooling counsel had not been put in place.
entries.literal: Second, the method of gathering many thoughts to broaden benefit is not yet complete.

entries.zh: 堯、舜之主，亦必詢四岳，詢群牧。
entries.en: Even rulers as great as Yao and Shun questioned the Four Peaks and the regional lords.
