entries.literal: Even rulers like Yao and Shun must inquire of the Four Peaks and inquire of the various pastors.

entries.zh: 蓋恐一人之聰明有限，必博收眾採，庶無失事。
entries.en: One man's wit is limited; only by gathering many voices could mistakes be avoided.
entries.literal: For they feared that one man's intelligence is limited; one must broadly gather and widely collect, so that nothing is missed.

entries.zh: 請自今凡召見大小臣工，必詢問人材，詢問利弊。
entries.en: Henceforth, whenever officials of any rank were received in audience, let the emperor ask about talent and about what policies helped or harmed the realm.
entries.literal: I ask that from now on, whenever great and small officials are received in audience, the ruler must inquire about talent and inquire about advantages and disadvantages.

entries.zh: 所言可採，則存檔冊以記之。
entries.en: Sound advice should be entered in the archives.
entries.literal: If what is said can be adopted, then store it in registers for record.

entries.zh: 倘所舉非人，所言失實，則治其失言之罪。
entries.en: If a man recommended proved unfit or his report false, let him be punished for misleading the throne.
entries.literal: If those recommended are unworthy or what is said is untrue, then punish the offense of erroneous speech.

entries.zh: 然寄耳目於左右近習，不可也；
entries.en: Yet one must not rely on intimate attendants for one's eyes and ears;
entries.literal: Yet to entrust one's eyes and ears to intimate attendants at one's side—this cannot be done;

entries.zh: 詢人之功過於其黨類，亦不可也。
entries.en: nor ask a man's clique about his merits and faults.
entries.literal: nor to inquire about a man's merits and faults from his faction—this also cannot be done.

entries.zh: 蓋人材至今日，銷磨殆盡矣。
entries.en: Talent, by now, had been ground nearly away.
entries.literal: For talent by today has been worn down nearly to exhaustion.

entries.zh: 以模棱為曉事，以軟弱為良圖，以鑽營為取進之階，以苟且為服官之計。
entries.en: Men took equivocation for wisdom, timidity for prudence, intrigue for the path to promotion, and muddling through for the art of office.
entries.literal: They take equivocation for understanding affairs, weakness for a good plan, wire-pulling for the ladder of advancement, and temporizing for the strategy of holding office.

entries.zh: 由此道者，無不各得其所欲而去，衣缽相承，牢結而不可解。
entries.en: All who lived by that code left with what they wanted; the habit passed from hand to hand like a master's robe and bowl, knotted tight beyond undoing.
entries.literal: Those who follow this path all depart having gained what they desire; the robe and bowl are handed down in succession, bound fast and impossible to undo.

entries.zh: 夫此模棱、軟弱、鑽營、苟且之人，國家無事，以之備班列可也；
entries.en: In quiet times such equivocators, weaklings, schemers, and temporizers might suffice to fill the ranks;
entries.literal: Such equivocating, weak, wire-pulling, temporizing men, when the state has no troubles, may serve to fill the ranks;

entries.zh: 適有緩急，而慾望其奮身為國，不顧利害，不計夷險，不瞻徇情面，不顧惜身家，不可得也。
entries.en: but in crisis one could not expect them to throw themselves into the state's service heedless of gain or loss, ease or danger, favor or family.
entries.literal: but when urgency arises, to expect them to throw themselves forward for the state, heedless of advantage and harm, reckoning neither ease nor danger, neither looking to personal ties nor sparing their persons and families—this cannot be obtained.

entries.zh: 至於利弊之不講，又非一日。
entries.en: The refusal to weigh policy's costs and benefits was nothing new either.
entries.literal: As for the failure to discuss advantages and disadvantages, this too is not a matter of a single day.

entries.zh: 在內部院諸臣，事本不多，而常若猝猝不暇，汲​​汲顧影，皆云多一事不如少一事。
entries.en: Inside the capital boards, business was not heavy, yet ministers acted perpetually rushed and anxious, all chanting that one trouble spared was better than one taken on.
entries.literal: Among ministers within the boards and courts, their business is not much, yet they always seem hurried and without leisure, anxiously watching their shadows, all saying that one more matter is not as good as one less.

entries.zh: 在外督撫諸臣，其賢者斤斤自守，不肖者亟亟營私。
entries.en: Among provincial governors, the worthy clung narrowly to their own integrity while the unworthy scrambled for private profit.
entries.literal: Among governors and governors-general outside, the worthy guard every inch for themselves, while the unworthy hurry to pursue private gain.

entries.zh: 國計民生，非所計也，救目前而已；
entries.en: National finances and people's livelihoods were not their concern—only the crisis of the moment;
entries.literal: National revenue and the people's livelihood are not what they calculate—only rescuing the present moment;

entries.zh: 官方吏治，非所急也，保本任而已。
entries.en: official discipline was not urgent—only keeping their own posts.
entries.literal: official standards and administration of officials are not what they urgently pursue—only preserving their own tenure.

entries.zh: 慮久遠者，以為過憂；
entries.en: Anyone who looked ahead was called an alarmist;
entries.literal: Those who consider the long term are deemed to worry excessively;

entries.zh: 事興革者，以為生事。
entries.en: anyone who pushed reform was called a troublemaker.
entries.literal: those who undertake innovation and reform are deemed to stir up trouble.

entries.zh: 此又豈國家求治之本意乎？
entries.en: Was that what the state meant by seeking good government?
entries.literal: Is this again the original intent of the state's pursuit of good government?

entries.zh: 二則進賢退不肖似尚游移。
entries.en: Second, promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy still seemed hesitant and half-hearted.
entries.literal: Second, advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy still seems hesitant and wavering.

entries.zh: 夫邪教之起，由於激變。
entries.en: Sectarian rebellion arose from official cruelty and provocation.
entries.literal: The rise of heterodox sects stems from harsh provocation.

entries.zh: 原任達州知州戴如煌，罪不容逭矣。
entries.en: The former prefect of Dazhou, Dai Ruhuang, deserved no mercy.
entries.literal: The former Dazhou Prefect Dai Ruhuang's crimes admit no escape.

entries.zh: 幸有一眾口交譽之劉清，百姓服之，教匪亦服之。
entries.en: Fortunately there was Liu Qing, praised on every side—trusted by the people and even by the rebels.
entries.literal: Fortunately there is a Liu Qing whom all mouths praise together; the common people submit to him, and the sect rebels also submit to him.

entries.zh: 此時正當用明效大驗之人。
entries.en: This was the moment to use men whose merit had already been proved in plain sight.
entries.literal: At this time one ought precisely to employ men of clear effect and great proof.

entries.zh: 聞劉清尚為州牧，僅從司道之後辦事，似不足盡其長矣。
entries.en: Yet Liu Qing was still only a prefect, working behind his superiors—hardly enough to use his full capacity.
entries.literal: I hear Liu Qing is still a prefect, merely handling affairs behind the provincial and circuit officials—this seems insufficient to exhaust his strengths.

entries.zh: 亮吉以為川省多事，經略縱極嚴明，勦賊匪用之，撫難民用之，整飭官方辦理地方之事又用之，此不能分身者也。
entries.en: Sichuan was in turmoil. However able the commissioner-general, he needed himself to fight rebels, pacify the people, and straighten out local government—one man could not do everything.
entries.literal: Liangji holds that Sichuan has many troubles; however strict and clear the commissioner-general may be, he must use himself to suppress bandits, use himself to pacify suffering people, and use himself again to rectify officials and handle local affairs—this is what one man cannot divide.

entries.zh: 何如擇此方賢吏如劉清者，崇其官爵，假以事權，使之一意招徠撫綏，以分督撫之權，以蕆國家之事。
entries.en: Why not pick proven local men like Liu Qing, raise their rank, give them real authority, and let them win people back while sharing the governors' burden and finishing the state's work?
entries.literal: Why not select worthy local officials of this region such as Liu Qing, elevate their rank and titles, lend them administrative authority, and let them devote themselves to winning people over and pacifying them, thereby dividing the power of governors and completing the state's affairs?

entries.zh: 有明中葉以來，鄖陽多事，則別設鄖陽巡撫；
entries.en: In mid-Ming times, when Yunyang was troubled, a separate Yunyang governor was appointed;
entries.literal: Since the mid-Ming, when Yunyang had many troubles, a separate Yunyang governor-general was established;

entries.zh: 偏沅多事，則別設偏沅巡撫。
entries.en: when the Hunan frontier was troubled, a separate Pian-Yuan governor was appointed.
entries.literal: when Pian-Yuan had many troubles, a separate Pian-Yuan governor-general was established.

entries.zh: 事竣則撤之，此不可拘拘於成例者也。
entries.en: When the crisis ended the post was abolished. One must not be slaves to precedent.
entries.literal: When affairs were concluded they were withdrawn—this is what cannot be bound rigidly by precedent.

entries.zh: 夫設官以待賢能，人果賢能，似不必過循資格。
entries.en: Posts exist to employ talent; where talent is real, seniority need not rule.
entries.literal: Offices are established to await the worthy and able; if a man is truly worthy and able, it seems one need not overly follow seniority and qualification.

entries.zh: 如劉清者，進而尚未進也。
entries.en: Men like Liu Qing ought to rise—and had not.
entries.literal: As for one like Liu Qing, he ought to advance yet has not yet advanced.

entries.zh: 戴如煌雖以別案解任，然尚安處川中。
entries.en: Dai Ruhuang had been removed on another charge, yet still lived comfortably in Sichuan.
entries.literal: Although Dai Ruhuang was removed from office on another case, he still dwells at ease in Sichuan.

entries.zh: 聞教匪甘心欲食其肉，知其所在，即極力焚劫。
entries.en: Rebels were said to long to devour him alive; wherever he was found they burned and looted with all their might.
entries.literal: I hear the sect rebels are willing at heart to eat his flesh; knowing where he is, they immediately exert all force to burn and plunder.

entries.zh: 是以數月必移一處，教匪亦必隨而蹟之。
entries.en: So every few months he had to move, and the rebels tracked him wherever he went.
entries.literal: Therefore every few months he must move to another place, and the sect rebels also inevitably track his trail.

entries.zh: 近在川東與一道員聯姻，恃以無恐。
entries.en: Lately in eastern Sichuan he had married into a circuit intendant's family and felt secure.
entries.literal: Recently in eastern Sichuan he formed a marriage alliance with a circuit intendant and relies on this to feel no fear.

entries.zh: 是救一有罪之人，反殺千百無罪之人，其理尚可恕乎？
entries.en: To spare one guilty man while thousands of innocents died for it—could that be justified?
entries.literal: To save one guilty man while instead killing hundreds and thousands of innocent men—can this principle still be forgiven?

entries.zh: 純皇帝大事之時，即明發諭旨數和珅之罪，並一一指其私人，天下快心。
entries.en: At the Qianlong emperor's death the throne had openly listed Heshen's crimes and named his creatures one by one, to the nation's relief.
entries.literal: At the time of the Chun Emperor's great mourning, he immediately issued open edicts enumerating Heshen's crimes and pointing out one by one his private men—the whole realm rejoiced.

entries.zh: 乃未幾而又起吳省蘭矣，召見之時，又聞其為吳省欽辨冤矣。
entries.en: Yet soon Wu Shenglan was back in favor, and at his audience he was said to be pleading his brother Wu Shengqin's innocence.
entries.literal: Yet before long Wu Shenglan rose again; at the time of his audience it was again heard that he was pleading innocence for Wu Shengqin.

entries.zh: 夫二吳之為和珅私人，與之交通貨賄，人人所知。
entries.en: Everyone knew the two Wu were Heshen's men and had traded in bribes with him.
entries.literal: That the two Wu were Heshen's private men and trafficked in bribes with him is known to everyone.

entries.zh: 故曹錫寶之糾和珅家人劉全也，以同鄉素好，先以摺稿示二吳，二吳即袖其走權門，藉為進身之地。
entries.en: When Cao Xibao impeached Heshen's servant Liu Quan, he showed the draft first to the two Wu as fellow townsmen; they tucked it away and rushed to the power-holders, turning betrayal into advancement.
entries.literal: When Cao Xibao impeached Heshen's household servant Liu Quan, being fellow-townsmen on good terms he first showed the memorial draft to the two Wu; the two Wu immediately tucked it away and ran to the power-holders' gates, using it as a place to advance themselves.

entries.zh: 今二吳可雪，不幾與褒贈曹錫寶之明旨相戾乎？
entries.en: If the two Wu were now cleared, would that not flatly contradict the edict that had honored Cao Xibao?
entries.literal: If now the two Wu can be cleared, does this not nearly contradict the clear edict that honored and rewarded Cao Xibao?

entries.zh: 夫吳省欽之傾險，秉文衡，尹京兆，無不聲名狼藉，則革職不足蔽辜矣。
entries.en: Wu Shengqin's treachery had left his name in ruins whether as chief examiner or as Jingzhao intendant; dismissal alone could not answer for his crimes.
entries.literal: As for Wu Shengqin's treacherous cunning, whether holding the literary balance, governing Jingzhao, in every case his reputation was in ruins—then dismissal from office is insufficient to cover his guilt.

entries.zh: 吳省蘭先為和珅教習師，後反稱和珅為老師，大考則第一矣，視學典試不絕矣，非和珅之力而誰力乎？
entries.en: Wu Shenglan had once been Heshen's tutor, then called Heshen his teacher; he took first in the Hanlin examination and kept receiving education and examination posts—whose power was that if not Heshen's?
entries.literal: Wu Shenglan first was Heshen's tutoring master, then in turn called Heshen his teacher; in the great examination he took first place, and appointments as education commissioner and chief examiner never ceased—if not by Heshen's power, then by whose?

entries.zh: 則降官亦不足蔽辜矣。
entries.en: Demotion in rank was likewise too light a penalty.
entries.literal: Then demotion in rank is also insufficient to cover his guilt.

entries.zh: 是退而尚未退也。
entries.en: So the unworthy were meant to go—and had not truly gone.
entries.literal: Thus they ought to be removed yet have not yet been removed.

entries.zh: 何以言用人行政未盡改也？
entries.en: Why had appointments and policy not yet been fully reformed?
entries.literal: Why say that employing men and administering affairs has not yet been fully changed?

entries.zh: 蓋其人雖已致法，而十馀年來，其更變祖宗成例，汲引一己私人，猶未嘗平心討論。
entries.en: Though Heshen himself had been punished, more than ten years of his changes to ancestral precedent and packing of offices with his creatures had never been calmly reviewed.
entries.literal: For although that man has already been brought to law, over more than ten years his alterations of the ancestors' established precedents and drawing in of his own private men have still never been calmly discussed.

entries.zh: 內閣、六部各衙門，何為國家之成法，何為和珅所更張，誰為國家自用之人，誰為和珅所引進，以及隨同受賄舞弊之人，皇上縱極仁慈，縱慾寬脅從，又因人數甚廣，不能一切屏除。
entries.en: In the Grand Secretariat, the Six Ministries, and every yamen—which rules were the state's and which Heshen's, who had been the court's own men and who Heshen's creatures, who had shared in bribery and fraud—the emperor might be merciful and wish to spare the coerced, and the numbers were too vast to purge everyone at once.
entries.literal: In the Grand Secretariat, the Six Ministries, and each yamen—what was the state's established law, what was changed by Heshen, who were men the state employed for itself, who were introduced by Heshen, and those who together accepted bribes and committed malfeasance—the emperor, however extremely merciful, however wishing to pardon the coerced, and because the number of persons is very broad, cannot remove them all.

entries.zh: 然竊以為實有真知灼見者，自不究其從前，亦當籍其姓名，於升遷調補之時，微示以善惡勸懲之法，使人人知聖天子雖不為已甚，而是非邪正之辨，未嘗不洞悉，未嘗不區別。
entries.en: Yet for men of real insight, even without prosecuting the past, their names should be recorded; at every promotion or transfer let a quiet signal show reward and punishment, so all would know that though the emperor would not go to extremes, he still saw clearly who was upright and who was not.
entries.literal: Yet I venture to hold that for those who truly have penetrating insight, even if one does not investigate their past, one should still register their names; at the time of promotion, transfer, and supplementation, subtly show the method of encouraging good and punishing evil, so that everyone knows that although the sage Son of Heaven does not go to excess, the distinction between right and wrong, orthodox and deviant, has never failed to be thoroughly understood and never failed to be differentiated.

entries.zh: 如是而夙昔之為私人者，尚可革面革心而為國家之人。
entries.en: Then even former creatures of the faction might turn anew and serve the state in earnest.
entries.literal: Thus those who in former days were private men might still change face and change heart and become men of the state.

entries.zh: 否則，朝廷常若今日清明可也，萬一他日復有效權臣所為者，而諸臣又群起而集其門矣。
entries.en: Otherwise the court might stay clear for a day, but if another power-holder rose tomorrow the officials would flock to his gate again.
entries.literal: Otherwise, while the court may always be as clear as today, if someday there should again be one who imitates what the powerful minister did, the various officials will again rise as a group and gather at his gate.

entries.zh: 何以言風俗日趨卑下也？
entries.en: Why did he say morals were sinking day by day?
entries.literal: Why say that customs daily sink lower?

entries.zh: 士大夫漸不顧廉恥，百姓則不顧綱常。
entries.en: Scholar-officials no longer cared for integrity, and the people no longer cared for the moral order.
entries.literal: The scholar-officials gradually cease to regard integrity and shame; the common people then cease to regard the moral order.

entries.zh: 然此不當責之百姓，仍當責之士大夫也。
entries.en: But the blame lay not with the people—it lay with the scholar-official class.
entries.literal: Yet this ought not to be charged to the common people; it should still be charged to the scholar-officials.

entries.zh: 以亮吉所見，十馀年來，有尚書、侍郎甘為宰相屈膝者矣；
entries.en: In Liangji's own observation over more than ten years, ministers and vice-ministers had willingly knelt to the chief minister;
entries.literal: In what Liangji has seen over more than ten years, there have been ministers and vice-ministers willing to bend the knee to the chief minister;

entries.zh: 有大學士、七卿之長，且年長以倍，而求拜門生，求為私人者矣；
entries.en: grand secretaries and heads of the chief ministries, though twice the minister's age, who sought to enroll as his disciples and become his creatures;
entries.literal: there have been grand secretaries and heads of the Seven Chief Ministries, though twice his senior in years, who sought to become his disciples and sought to become his private men;

entries.zh: 有交宰相之僮隸，並樂與抗禮者矣。
entries.en: men who socialized with the minister's page boys and treated them as equals with pleasure.
entries.literal: there have been those who associated with the chief minister's boy servants and were even pleased to exchange courtesies on equal terms.

entries.zh: 太學三館，風氣之所由出也。
entries.en: The Imperial University and the Three Academies were where public tone was formed.
entries.literal: The Imperial University and the Three Academies are where the prevailing tone originates.

entries.zh: 今則有昏夜乞憐，以求署祭酒者矣；
entries.en: Now men begged by night for acting appointment as university chancellor;
entries.literal: Now there are those who beg piteously in the dark of night to obtain acting appointment as university chancellor;

entries.zh: 有人前長跪，以求講官者矣。
entries.en: and prostrated themselves in public to win lectureship posts.
entries.literal: there are those who prostrate themselves in long kneeling before others to obtain lectureship posts.

entries.zh: 翰林大考，國家所據以升黜詞臣者也。
entries.en: The Hanlin great examination was how the state promoted and demoted its literary officers.
entries.literal: The Hanlin great examination is what the state relies on to promote and demote literary officials.

entries.zh: 今則有先走軍機章京之門，求認師生，以探取御製詩韻者矣；
entries.en: Now candidates ran first to Grand Council clerks, claimed them as teachers, and tried to learn the rhyme schemes of the emperor's examination poems in advance;
entries.literal: Now there are those who first run to the doors of Grand Council clerks, seek to be recognized as teacher and student, in order to probe and obtain the rhyme schemes of the emperor's composed poems;

entries.zh: 行賄於門闌侍衛，以求傳遞代倩，藏捲而去，制就而入者矣。
entries.en: bribed gate guards to carry papers out and back, hid their booklets while answers were written for them, and re-entered with finished compositions.
entries.literal: bribe the gate guards and attendants in order to have papers passed and answers written for them, hide the examination booklet and leave, then enter with the composition already finished.

entries.zh: 及人人各得所欲，則居然自以為得計。
entries.en: Once everyone got what he wanted, he calmly assumed he had found a winning scheme.
entries.literal: When each person each obtains what he desires, then calmly he considers himself to have hit upon a successful plan.

entries.zh: 夫大考如此，何以責鄉會試之懷挾替代？
entries.en: If the Hanlin great examination was like this, how could one condemn the provincial and metropolitan exams for smuggling in crib sheets and stand-ins?
entries.literal: If the great examination is thus, how can one blame the provincial and metropolitan examinations for carrying forbidden materials and substitution?

entries.zh: 士大夫之行如此，何以責小民之誇詐夤緣？
entries.en: If the conduct of the literati was like this, how could one blame commoners for boastful fraud and backdoor dealings?
entries.literal: If the conduct of scholar-officials is thus, how can one blame common people for boastful fraud and crony climbing?

entries.zh: 輦轂之下如此，何以責四海九州之營私舞弊？
entries.en: If things were like this at the capital itself, how could one blame the provinces for private profiteering and fraud?
entries.literal: If under the imperial capital it is thus, how can one blame the four seas and nine provinces for pursuing private gain and fraudulent practice?

entries.zh: 純皇帝因內閣學士許玉猷為同姓石工護喪，諭廷臣曰：'諸臣縱不自愛，如國體何？
entries.en: The late emperor, learning that Grand Secretariat academician Xu Yuyou had a stonemason of the same surname attend his mourning, told the court: 'Even if you ministers care nothing for yourselves, what of the dignity of the state?'
entries.literal: The Pure Emperor, because Grand Secretariat academician Xu Yuyou had a stonemason of the same surname attend his mourning, instructed the court ministers, saying: 'Even if you ministers do not care for yourselves, what of the national dignity?'

entries.zh: '是知國體之尊，在諸臣各知廉恥。
entries.en: Thus one sees that the honor of the state rests on every minister knowing shame and integrity.
entries.literal: From this one knows that the honor of the national dignity lies in each minister knowing shame and integrity.

entries.zh: 夫下之化上，猶影響也。
entries.en: The lower orders take their cue from above as surely as a body casts a shadow.
entries.literal: The transformation of the lower by the upper is like shadow and echo.

entries.zh: 士氣必待在上者振作之，風節必待在上者獎成之。
entries.en: Scholarly morale must be revived from above; moral integrity must be fostered and rewarded from above.
entries.literal: Scholarly morale must wait for those above to rouse it; moral integrity must wait for those above to reward and complete it.

entries.zh: 舉一廉樸之吏，則貪欺者庶可自愧矣；
entries.en: Promote one honest, unassuming official, and the greedy and deceitful might feel ashamed;
entries.literal: To recommend one honest and plain official, then the greedy and deceitful might feel shame;

entries.zh: 進一恬退之流，則奔競者庶可稍改矣；
entries.en: advance one who is content to stand aside, and the office-seekers might mend their ways a little;
entries.literal: To advance one retiring and unambitious sort, then the scrambling competitors might slightly reform;

entries.zh: 拔一特立獨行、敦品勵節之士，則如脂如韋、依附朋比之風或可漸革矣。
entries.en: raise up a man of independent conduct who cultivates character and integrity, and the fashion for slick flattery and cliquish dependence might slowly change.
entries.literal: To elevate one who stands alone in conduct and cultivates character and integrity, then the tendency to be slick as grease or pliant as leather and cling to faction might gradually be reformed.

entries.zh: 而亮吉更有所慮者，前之所言，皆士大夫之不務名節者耳。
entries.en: Yet Liangji has a further worry: what I have described so far concerns only those literati who neglect reputation and integrity.
entries.literal: But Liangji has a further worry: what was said before concerns only scholar-officials who do not pursue reputation and integrity.

entries.zh: 幸有矯矯自好者，類皆惑於因果，遁入虛無，以蔬食為家規，以談禪為國政。
entries.en: There are also men of proud independence—but most of them are lost in doctrines of karma, retreat into empty speculation, make vegetarianism a household rule, and treat Chan meditation as statecraft.
entries.literal: Fortunately there are those who stand aloof and prize their own standards, but most are confused by karma and cause-effect, flee into emptiness, take vegetable diet as family rule, and take Chan talk as state policy.

entries.zh: 一二人倡於前，千百人和於後。
entries.en: One or two take the lead, and hundreds and thousands follow.
entries.literal: One or two lead in front, hundreds and thousands harmonize behind.

entries.zh: 甚有出則官服，入則僧衣。
entries.en: Some even wear official robes abroad and monastic robes at home.
entries.literal: Some even go out in official robes and enter in monk's robes.

entries.zh: 惑智驚愚，駭人觀聽。
entries.en: They bewilder the learned, alarm the simple, and shock all who see and hear them.
entries.literal: Bewildering the wise and startling the foolish, shocking people's eyes and ears.

entries.zh: 亮吉前在內廷，執事曾告之曰：『某等親王十人，施齋戒殺者已十居六七，羊豕鵝鴨皆不入門。』
entries.en: When I was in the inner court, a colleague told me: 'Of us ten princes, six or seven already keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing—sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks never enter our doors.'
entries.literal: Liangji formerly in the inner court, his colleagues once told him: 'Of us princes, ten men—those who keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing already number six or seven out of ten; sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks none enter our doors.'

entries.zh: 及此回入都，而士大夫持齋戒殺又十居六七矣。
entries.en: Now that I am back in the capital, six or seven out of ten literati keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing as well.
entries.literal: When returning to the capital this time, among scholar-officials those holding vegetarian fasts and abstaining from killing again number six or seven out of ten.

entries.zh: 深恐西晉祖尚玄虛之習复見於今，則所關世道人心非小也。
entries.en: I deeply fear that the Western Jin fashion for empty speculation may reappear today; what is at stake in the spirit of the age and the hearts of the people is no small matter.
entries.literal: Deeply fearing that the Western Jin custom of revering the abstruse and empty might reappear today—then what is involved in the spirit of the age and people's hearts is no small matter.

entries.zh: 何以言賞罰仍不嚴明也？
entries.en: Why do I say that rewards and punishments are still not strict and clear?
entries.literal: Why say that rewards and punishments are still not strict and clear?

entries.zh: 自徵苗匪、教匪以來，福康安、和琳、孫士毅則蒙蔽欺妄於前，宜綿、惠齡、福寧則喪師失律於後，又益以景安、秦承恩之因循畏葸，而川、陝、楚、豫之民，遭劫者不知幾百萬矣。
entries.en: Since the campaigns against the Miao and the sect rebels, Fu Kang'an, He Lin, and Sun Shiyi deceived and concealed at the outset; Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Fu Ning lost armies and violated discipline later on; to these were added Jing'an and Qin Cheng'en's procrastination and timidity—and the people of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, and Henan who suffered devastation must number several millions.
entries.literal: Since the campaigns against Miao bandits and sect rebels, Fu Kang'an, He Lin, and Sun Shiyi deceived and concealed in the beginning; Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Fu Ning lost armies and violated discipline afterward; further added Jing'an and Qin Cheng'en's procrastination and timidity—and the people of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, and Henan who suffered plunder number surely several millions.

entries.zh: 已死諸臣姑置勿論，其現在者未嘗不議罪也。
entries.en: The ministers who are already dead may be set aside; those still living have not escaped censure.
entries.literal: The ministers already dead may be set aside without discussion; those still living have not failed to be judged guilty.

entries.zh: 然重者不過新疆換班，輕者不過大營轉餉；
entries.en: Yet the heaviest penalty has been no more than rotation to Xinjiang; the lightest no more than supplying the main camp;
entries.literal: Yet the severe punishment is no more than transfer to Xinjiang on rotation; the light is no more than supplying provisions at the great camp;

entries.zh: 甚至拏解來京之秦承恩，則又給還家產，有意復用矣；
entries.en: even Qin Cheng'en, who was brought to the capital under arrest, had his family property restored and is evidently to be employed again;
entries.literal: Even Qin Cheng'en, who was escorted as prisoner to the capital, then had family property returned, with intent to employ again;

entries.zh: 屢奉嚴旨之惠齡，則又起補侍郎。
entries.en: Hui Ling, who had repeatedly received stern edicts, has been reappointed Vice Minister.
entries.literal: Hui Ling, who repeatedly received stern edicts, then was raised again to fill the post of Vice Minister.

entries.zh: 夫蒙蔽欺妄之殺人，與喪師失律以及因循畏葸之殺人無異也，而猶邀寬典異數，亦從前所未有也。
entries.en: Deception and concealment that cost lives are no different from losing armies, violating discipline, or dithering in fear that cost lives—yet these men still receive lenient and extraordinary treatment, something never seen before.
entries.literal: Deceiving and concealing that kills people is no different from losing armies and violating discipline and procrastinating in timidity that kills people—yet they still receive lenient statutes and special treatment, also unprecedented.

entries.zh: 故近日經略以下、領隊以上，類皆不以賊匪之多寡、地方之蹂躪掛懷。
entries.en: Hence commissioners and column leaders alike generally pay no heed to how many rebels remain or how badly the countryside is ravaged.
entries.literal: Therefore recently from commissioners downward and column leaders upward, all generally do not care about the number of bandit rebels or the trampling of regions.

entries.zh: 彼其心未始不自計曰：『即使萬不可解，而新疆換班，大營轉餉，亦尚有成例可援，退步可守。』
entries.en: In their hearts they tell themselves: 'Even if all else fails, rotation to Xinjiang and supply duty at the main camp still offer precedents to cite and a line of retreat to hold.'
entries.literal: In their hearts they never fail to calculate for themselves: 'Even if utterly irredeemable, Xinjiang rotation and great camp supply still have precedents to cite, retreats to hold.'

entries.zh: 國法之寬，及諸臣之不畏國法，未有如今日之甚者。
entries.en: Never has the law been so lax, or ministers so unafraid of the law, as today.
entries.literal: The leniency of national law and the ministers' fearlessness of national law have never been as severe as today.

entries.zh: 純皇帝之用兵金川、緬甸，訥親僨事，則殺訥親；
entries.en: When the late emperor campaigned in Jinchuan and Burma, Neqin failed and was executed;
entries.literal: When the Pure Emperor used troops in Jinchuan and Burma, when Neqin failed, he killed Neqin;

entries.zh: 額爾登額僨事，則殺額爾登額；
entries.en: E'erdeng'e failed and was executed;
entries.literal: when E'erdeng'e failed, he killed E'erdeng'e;

entries.zh: 將軍、提、鎮之類，伏失律之誅者，不知凡幾。
entries.en: generals, provincial commanders, and garrison commanders who suffered death for breach of discipline were beyond counting.
entries.literal: among generals, regional commanders, and garrison commanders, those who suffered execution for violating discipline—who knows how many.

entries.zh: 是以萬里之外，得一廷寄，皆震懼失色，則馭軍之道得也。
entries.en: Ten thousand li away, a single dispatch from court made every commander tremble and turn pale—such was the right way to command armies.
entries.literal: Therefore ten thousand li away, upon receiving one court dispatch, all trembled in fear and changed color—thus the way of controlling armies was attained.

entries.zh: 今自乙卯以迄己未，首尾五年，僨事者屢矣。
entries.en: From 1795 to 1799, a full five years, failures have been repeated.
entries.literal: Now from yimao to jiwei, first to last five years, failures have been frequent.

entries.zh: 提、鎮、副都統、偏裨之將，有一膺失律之誅者乎？
entries.en: Has a single provincial commander, garrison commander, deputy commandant, or field officer suffered death for breach of discipline?
entries.literal: Among regional commanders, garrison commanders, deputy commandants, and subordinate officers, has there been one who suffered execution for violating discipline?

entries.zh: 而欲諸臣之不玩寇、不殃民得乎？
entries.en: How then can one expect officials not to trifle with the enemy and not bring disaster on the people?
entries.literal: Yet can one expect the ministers not to trifle with bandits and not harm the people?

entries.zh: 夫以純皇帝之聖武，又豈見不及此？
entries.en: With the late emperor's sacred martial prowess, could his vision have failed to reach this far?
entries.literal: With the Pure Emperor's sacred martial prowess, how could his vision not reach this?

entries.zh: 蓋以歸政在即，欲留待皇上蒞政之初，神武獨斷，一新天下之耳目耳。
entries.en: Presumably because abdication was near, he wished to leave this for Your Majesty's first days in power—to decide with your own sacred resolve and renew the eyes and ears of the empire.
entries.literal: Presumably because abdication of power was imminent, he wished to reserve it for when Your Majesty first took the reins, to decide alone with divine martial spirit and renew the eyes and ears of all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 倘蕩平尚無期日，而國帑日見銷磨，萬一支絀偶形，司農告匱。
entries.en: If pacification still has no end in sight while the treasury is worn down day by day, a sudden shortfall may leave the Minister of Revenue reporting empty coffers.
entries.literal: If pacification still has no date in sight, while the national treasury daily is worn down, should shortage suddenly appear, the Minister of Revenue would report empty coffers.

entries.zh: 言念及此，可為寒心，此尤宜急加之意者也。
entries.en: To reflect on this is chilling; this above all deserves your urgent attention.
entries.literal: To speak and think of this can make one chill at heart—this especially deserves urgent attention.

entries.zh: 何以言言路似通而未通也？
entries.en: Why do I say the avenue of remonstrance seems open yet is not truly open?
entries.literal: Why say the avenue of speech seems open yet is not open?

entries.zh: 九卿臺諫之臣，類皆毛舉細故，不切政要。
entries.en: The Nine Chief Offices and the censorate mostly nitpick trifles and never touch what matters in government.
entries.literal: The ministers of the Nine Chief Offices and the censorate and remonstrance bureaus mostly pick at minute matters, not touching on essentials of government.

entries.zh: 否則發人之陰私，快己之恩怨。
entries.en: Otherwise they expose private scandals to settle personal scores.
entries.literal: Otherwise they expose others' private matters, gratify their own enmities and favors.

entries.zh: 十件之中，幸有一二可行者，發部議矣，而部臣與建言諸臣，又各存意見，無不議駁，並無不通駁，則又豈國家詢及芻蕘、詢及瞽史之初意乎？
entries.en: Of ten proposals, perhaps one or two are feasible and are sent to the ministries for deliberation—yet ministry officials and the memorialists again take opposing sides, debate everything, and rebut everything. How is this the state's original intent in seeking counsel from the humblest and the lowliest?
entries.literal: Of ten items, fortunately one or two may be feasible and are sent to the ministry for deliberation—but ministry officials and the memorializing officials again each hold opinions, none without debate and rebuttal, and none without thorough rebuttal—then how is this the original intent of the state inquiring of the grass cutter and inquiring of the blind historian?

entries.zh: 然或因其所言瑣碎，或輕重失倫，或虛實不審，而一概留中，則又不可。
entries.en: Yet to retain every memorial at court because it is trivial, disproportionate, or unverified would also be wrong.
entries.literal: Yet if because what they say is trivial, or weight and lightness are out of order, or truth and falsehood are unexamined, and all are retained at court, that again is not permissible.

entries.zh: 其法莫如隨閱隨發，面諭廷臣，或特頒諭旨，皆隨其事之可行不可行，明白曉示之。
entries.en: The better course is to read and respond as each memorial arrives—to instruct the court in person or issue a special edict, plainly stating whether the proposal is feasible or not.
entries.literal: The method is none better than to review and issue as one goes, instruct the court ministers in person, or specially promulgate an edict—all according to whether the matter is feasible or not, clearly informing them.

entries.zh: 即或彈劾不避權貴，在諸臣一心為國，本不必避嫌怨。
entries.en: Even when impeachment does not spare the powerful, ministers who serve the state with one heart need not fear personal resentment.
entries.literal: Even if impeachment does not avoid the powerful, among the ministers with one heart for the state, there is originally no need to avoid suspicion and resentment.

entries.zh: 以近事論，錢灃、初彭齡皆常彈及大僚矣，未聞大僚敢與之為仇也。
entries.en: In recent years Qian Feng and Chu Pengling often impeached high officials, yet no senior minister dared treat them as enemies.
entries.literal: Taking recent events, Qian Feng and Chu Pengling both often impeached great officials, yet one has not heard that great officials dared make enemies of them.

entries.zh: 若其不知國體，不識政要，冒昧立言，或攻發人之陰私，則亦不妨使眾共知之，以著其非而懲其後。
entries.en: If a memorialist does not understand the dignity of the state or the essentials of policy, speaks rashly, or attacks private scandals, let the court know openly—expose the fault and warn those who follow.
entries.literal: If they do not know the national dignity, do not understand essentials of government, rashly speak, or attack and expose others' private matters, then it is also not improper to let the multitude know together, to show their error and warn those who follow.

entries.zh: 蓋諸臣既敢挾私而不為國，更可無煩君上之回護矣。
entries.en: When ministers dare to serve private ends rather than the state, Your Majesty need not shield them at all.
entries.literal: Since the ministers already dare to harbor private motives and not serve the state, all the more there is no need for the sovereign to shield them.

entries.zh: 何以言吏治欲肅而未肅也？
entries.en: Why do I say that official administration is meant to be rectified yet has not been rectified?
entries.literal: Why say that official administration wishes to be rectified yet is not rectified?

entries.zh: 未欲吏治之肅，則督、撫、籓、臬其標準矣。
entries.en: If official administration is to be rectified, governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners are the standard.
entries.literal: If one wishes official administration to be rectified, then governors-general, governors, provincial administration commissioners, and provincial judicial commissioners are the standard.

entries.zh: 十馀年來，督、撫、籓、臬之貪欺害政，比比皆是。
entries.en: For more than ten years, greedy and corrupt governors and provincial commissioners have been everywhere.
entries.literal: For more than ten years, governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners' greed, deceit, and harm to government have been everywhere.

entries.zh: 幸而皇上親政以來，李奉翰已自斃，鄭元鸘已被糾，富綱已遭憂，江蘭已內改。
entries.en: Fortunately since Your Majesty took personal rule, Li Fenghan has died, Zheng Yuanshuang has been impeached, Fu Gang has left office in mourning, and Jiang Lan has been transferred inland.
entries.literal: Fortunately since Your Majesty's personal rule, Li Fenghan has already died by himself, Zheng Yuanshuang has already been impeached, Fu Gang has already suffered bereavement, Jiang Lan has already been transferred within.

entries.zh: 此外，官大省、據方面者如故也，出巡則有站規、有門包，常時則有節禮、生日禮，按年則又有幫費。
entries.en: Beyond them, the great provincial officers remain as before: on tour they collect station fees and gate packets; in ordinary times festival gifts and birthday gifts; each year support fees as well.
entries.literal: Besides these, great-province officials holding regional power remain as before: on inspection tours there are station fees and gate packets; in ordinary times there are festival gifts and birthday gifts; by the year there are also support fees.

entries.zh: 升遷調補之私相餽謝者，尚未在此數也。
entries.en: The private gifts exchanged at promotions and transfers are not even included in this tally.
entries.literal: Private mutual gifts at promotion, transfer, and filling of posts are not yet counted in this number.

entries.zh: 以上諸項，無不取之於州縣，州縣則無不取之於民。
entries.en: Every item above is drawn from the prefectures and counties, and they in turn draw it all from the people.
entries.literal: All the above items are without exception taken from prefectures and counties; prefectures and counties without exception take from the people.

entries.zh: 錢糧漕米，前數年尚不過加倍，近則加倍不止。
entries.en: Land tax and transport grain, which a few years ago were merely doubled, are now more than doubled.
entries.literal: Land tax and transport grain, in earlier years still no more than doubled; recently they are more than doubled without stop.

entries.zh: 督、撫、籓、臬以及所屬之道、府，無不明知故縱，否則門包、站規、節禮、生日禮、幫費無所出也。
entries.en: Governors, provincial commissioners, and their circuit and prefectural subordinates all knowingly condone this—otherwise their gate packets, station fees, festival gifts, birthday gifts, and support fees would have no source.
entries.literal: Governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners and their subordinate circuit and prefectural intendants—all without exception clearly know and deliberately indulge, otherwise gate packets, station fees, festival gifts, birthday gifts, and support fees would have nowhere to come from.

entries.zh: 州縣明言於人曰：『我之所以加倍加數倍者，實層層衙門用度，日甚一日，年甚一年。』
entries.en: Prefectural and county magistrates tell the people plainly: 'The reason I double and redouble levies is that expenses at every level of government grow worse day by day and year by year.'
entries.literal: Prefectures and counties plainly tell people: 'The reason I double and multiply several times is truly that yamen expenses layer upon layer grow day by day and year by year.'

entries.zh: 究之州縣，亦恃督、撫、籓、臬、道、府之威勢以取於民，上司得其半，州縣之入己者亦半。
entries.en: In the end the magistrates too rely on the power of governors and commissioners to squeeze the people: half goes to their superiors, half they keep.
entries.literal: Investigating prefectures and counties, they also rely on the power and prestige of governors-general, governors, provincial commissioners, circuits, and prefectures to take from the people; superiors get half, what prefectures and counties keep for themselves is also half.

entries.zh: 初行尚有畏忌，至一年二年，則成為舊例，牢不可破矣。
entries.en: At first they still had some scruples; within a year or two it became fixed custom, impossible to break.
entries.literal: At first there was still fear and restraint; by one or two years it became an old precedent, firmly unbreakable.

entries.zh: 訴之督、撫、籓、臬、道、府，皆不問也。
entries.en: Appeals to governors, commissioners, circuits, and prefectures go unanswered.
entries.literal: Appeals to governors-general, governors, provincial commissioners, circuits, and prefectures—all go unanswered.

entries.zh: 千萬人中，或有不甘冤抑，赴京控告者，不過發督撫審究而已，派欽差就訊而已。
entries.en: Of millions of people, a few who cannot bear injustice may go to the capital to complain—but the outcome is only an order for the provincial authorities to investigate, or an imperial commissioner sent to inquire.
entries.literal: Among tens of millions, perhaps some who will not endure wrongful oppression go to the capital to lodge complaints—nothing more than sending the governor-general and governor to investigate, or dispatching an imperial commissioner to inquire on the spot.

entries.zh: 試思百姓告官之案，千百中有一二得直者乎？
entries.en: Consider: of a thousand cases in which commoners sue officials, do one or two obtain justice?
entries.literal: Consider: in cases of common people suing officials, of a thousand or hundred is there one or two who obtain justice?

entries.zh: 即欽差上司稍有良心者，不過設為調停之法，使兩無所大損而已。
entries.en: Even an imperial commissioner or superior with some conscience merely arranges a compromise so that neither side suffers too greatly.
entries.literal: Even imperial commissioners and superiors with slight conscience do no more than set up methods of mediation, so that both sides suffer no great loss.

entries.zh: 若欽差一出，則又必派及通省，派及百姓，必使之滿載而歸而心始安，而可以無後患。
entries.en: Once an imperial commissioner is dispatched, he assesses the whole province and the common people alike, and will not rest until he returns with his pockets full and no fear of later trouble.
entries.literal: If an imperial commissioner goes out, then again he must assess the whole province and assess the common people, must make them return fully loaded before his heart is at ease and he can be without later trouble.

entries.zh: 是以州縣亦熟知百姓之技倆不過如此，百姓亦習知上控必不能自直，是以往往至於激變。
entries.en: Magistrates know the people's remedies go no further than this; the people know appeals to the capital never bring justice—so matters often end in violent upheaval.
entries.literal: Therefore prefectures and counties also well know that the common people's tricks go no further than this; the common people also habitually know that appealing upward certainly cannot obtain justice for themselves—therefore they often come to violent upheaval.

entries.zh: 湖北之當陽，四川之達州，其明效大驗也。
entries.en: Dangyang in Hubei and Dazhou in Sichuan are glaring proof.
entries.literal: Dangyang in Hubei and Dazhou in Sichuan are clear proof on a grand scale.

entries.zh: 亮吉以為今日皇上當法憲皇帝之嚴明，使吏治肅而民樂生；
entries.en: Liangji believes that today Your Majesty should follow the strict clarity of the Manifest Emperor, rectify official administration, and let the people live in peace;
entries.literal: Liangji considers that today Your Majesty should follow the Manifest Emperor's strict clarity, cause official administration to be rectified and the people to rejoice in life;

entries.zh: 然後法仁皇帝之寬仁，以轉移風俗，則文武一張一弛之道也。」
entries.en: then follow the generous benevolence of the Benevolent Emperor to transform customs—such is the civil and martial way of tension and release."
entries.literal: then follow the Benevolent Emperor's generous benevolence, to transform customs—then this is the civil and martial way of one tension and one relaxation."

entries.en: Thus ended the memorial.
entries.literal: Thus closed the memorial.

entries.zh: 洪亮吉，字稚存，江蘇陽湖人。
entries.en: Hong Liangji, whose style was Zhicun, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Hong Liangji, style name Zhicun, was a native of Yanghu in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 少孤貧，力學，孝事寡母。
entries.en: Orphaned early and raised in poverty, he threw himself into study and cared devotedly for his widowed mother.
entries.literal: He lost his father young and was poor, but studied diligently and served his widowed mother with filial devotion.

entries.zh: 初佐安徽學政硃筠校文，繼入​​陝西巡撫畢沅幕，為校刊古書。
entries.en: He first helped Zhu Yun, the Anhui education commissioner, review examination essays, then joined Bi Yuan's staff in Shaanxi to edit and publish classical texts.
entries.literal: At first he assisted Anhui Education Commissioner Zhu Yun in examining literary compositions; later he entered the staff of Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan to collate and publish ancient books.

entries.zh: 詞章考據，著於一時，尤精揅輿地。
entries.en: His literary work and philological scholarship made him famous in his time, above all his expertise in historical geography.
entries.literal: His belles-lettres and evidential scholarship were renowned in his day, and he was especially skilled in researching geography and cosmography.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十五年，成一甲第二名進士，授翰林院編修，年已四十有五。
entries.en: In 1790 he took second place in the top tier of the palace examination and was made a Hanlin compiler at the age of forty-five.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of the Qianlong reign he placed second in the first class of the jinshi examination and was appointed Hanlin Academician Compiler, by which time he was already forty-five.

entries.zh: 長身火色，性豪邁，喜論當世事。
entries.en: Tall and ruddy-faced, he had a bold temperament and loved to debate current affairs.
entries.literal: Tall in stature and ruddy in complexion, he was bold in temperament and fond of discussing affairs of the day.

entries.zh: 未散館，分校順天鄉試。
entries.en: Before finishing his Hanlin probation, he was put on the board that graded the Shuntian provincial examination.
entries.literal: Before completing his probation at the Hanlin Academy, he was assigned to grade the Shuntian provincial examination.

entries.zh: 督貴州學政，以古學教士，地僻無書籍，購經、史、通典、文選置各府書院，黔士始治經史。
entries.en: As Guizhou education commissioner he taught the classics. The province was remote and bookless, so he bought standard works—the Classics, histories, the Tongdian, and the Wenxuan—for every prefectural academy, and Guizhou scholars at last began serious study of the canon.
entries.literal: As Guizhou Education Commissioner he taught scholars the classical learning; the region was remote and lacked books, so he purchased the Classics, histories, the Tongdian, and the Wenxuan for the academies in each prefecture, and only then did Guizhou scholars begin to study the Classics and histories.

entries.zh: 為詩古文有法。
entries.en: His poetry and prose were composed with real craft.
entries.literal: His poetry and ancient-style prose followed proper methods.

entries.zh: 任滿還京，入直上書房，授皇曾孫奕純讀。
entries.en: When his term ended he returned to Beijing, entered the Imperial Study, and tutored the emperor's great-grandson Yi Chun.
entries.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital, entered the Imperial Study on direct appointment, and instructed the emperor's great-grandson Yi Chun in reading.

entries.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考翰詹，試徵邪教疏，亮吉力陳內外弊政數千言，為時所忌。
entries.en: In 1798, at the triennial Hanlin examination, candidates were asked to draft a memorial on sectarian rebellion. Liangji poured thousands of words into a blunt catalogue of abuses at court and in the provinces, and made powerful enemies.
entries.literal: In the third year of the Jiaqing reign, at the great examination of Hanlin and Imperial Academy members, the topic was a memorial on suppressing heterodox sects; Liangji forcefully set forth several thousand characters on abuses at court and in the provinces, and was resented by his contemporaries.

entries.zh: 以弟喪陳情歸。
entries.en: He pleaded a brother's death and went home.
entries.literal: He submitted a petition on account of his younger brother's death and returned home.

entries.zh: 嘉慶三年，遷御史。
entries.en: In 1798 he was transferred to the censorate.
entries.literal: Jiaqing year 3, transferred to censor.

entries.zh: 時教匪擾數省，師久無功，際岐遍訪人士來京者，具得其狀。
entries.en: Sectarian rebels were ravaging several provinces and the campaigns dragged on without victory. Jiqi questioned every traveler who came to Beijing until he had the full picture.
entries.literal: At the time sectarian rebels disturbed several provinces; armies long without success; Jiqi everywhere visited people coming to the capital and fully learned the situation.

entries.zh: 四年春，上疏，略曰：「竊見三年以來，先帝頒師征討邪教，川、陝責之總督宜綿，巡撫惠齡、秦承恩；
entries.en: In the spring of 1799 he submitted a memorial that began: "For three years now the late emperor has sent armies against the sectarians. Sichuan and Shaanxi fall to Governor-General Yi Mian and Grand Coordinators Hui Ling and Qin Cheng'en;
entries.literal: Year 4 spring, submitted memorial, summary saying: "I have seen that for three years the late emperor has dispatched armies to campaign against heterodox teachings; Sichuan and Shaanxi charged to Governor-General Yi Mian, Grand Coordinators Hui Ling and Qin Cheng'en;

entries.zh: 楚北責之總督畢沅、巡撫汪新。
entries.en: Northern Chu to Governor-General Bi Yuan and Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.
entries.literal: North Chu charged to Governor-General Bi Yuan, Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.

entries.zh: 諸臣釀釁於先，藏身於後，止以重兵自衛，裨弁奮勇者，無調度接應，由是​​兵無鬥志。
entries.en: These ministers provoked the trouble up front and hid in the rear, guarding only themselves with heavy forces. Brave subordinate officers received no coordination or relief—and so the men lost heart for battle.
entries.literal: These officials brewed trouble in front and hid in the rear, only using heavy troops to defend themselves; assistant commanders who fought bravely had no coordination or relief, and thereby the troops lost fighting spirit.

entries.zh: 川、楚傳言云：'賊來不見官兵面，賊去官兵才出現。
entries.en: Sichuan and Hubei had a saying: "When the rebels come you never see a government soldier's face; when the rebels leave, the troops finally show up."
entries.literal: Sichuan and Chu rumor says: 'When bandits come one does not see government troops' faces; when bandits go, government troops only then appear.

entries.zh: '又云：'賊去兵無影，兵來賊沒踪。
entries.en: Another line ran: "The rebels are gone and the troops vanish; the troops arrive and the rebels disappear."
entries.literal: 'Again it says: 'When bandits go the troops have no shadow; when troops come the bandits leave no trace.

entries.zh: 可憐兵與賊，何日得相逢？
entries.en: Poor soldiers and poor rebels—when will they ever meet?
entries.literal: Pity the troops and the bandits—on what day can they meet?

entries.zh: '前年總督勒保至川，大張告示，痛責前任之失，是其明證。
entries.en: The year before, when Governor-General Le Bao reached Sichuan, he put up broad proclamations bitterly condemning his predecessors' failures—that itself was proof enough.
entries.literal: The year before, Governor-General Le Bao arrived in Sichuan, posted broad notices, and bitterly blamed his predecessors' failures—that is clear proof.

entries.zh: 畢沅、汪新相繼殂逝，景安繼為總督。
entries.en: Bi Yuan and Wang Xin died in succession, and Jing An succeeded as governor-general.
entries.literal: Bi Yuan and Wang Xin died in succession; Jing An succeeded as governor-general.

entries.zh: 今宜綿、惠齡、秦承恩縱慢於左，景安怯玩於右，勒保縱能實力剿捕，陝、楚賊多，起滅無時，則勒保終將掣肘。
entries.en: Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Qin Cheng'en are slack and negligent on one flank; Jing An is timid and indifferent on the other. Even if Le Bao fights in earnest, rebels in Shaanxi and Hubei rise and fall without end, and Le Bao will in the end be hamstrung.
entries.literal: Now Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Qin Cheng'en are indulgent and slow on the left; Jing An is timid and indifferent on the right. Even if Le Bao can with real strength suppress and capture, Shaanxi and Chu have many bandits rising and perishing without cease, and Le Bao will in the end be checked and restrained.

entries.zh: 欽惟先帝昔徵緬甸，見楊應琚挑撥掩覆之罪，立予拿問。
entries.en: Consider how the late emperor, campaigning in Burma, found Yang Yingju guilty of provocation and concealment and had him seized at once for trial.
entries.literal: Respectfully consider: the late emperor formerly campaigned in Burma, saw Yang Yingju's crime of provocation and concealment, and immediately had him seized for inquiry.

entries.zh: 今宜綿等曠玩三年之久，幸荷寬典，而轉益懷安，任賊越入河南盧氏、魯山等縣。
entries.en: Yi Mian and the rest have been negligent for three full years, spared by imperial leniency only to grow more complacent, and allowed rebels to push into Lushi, Lushan, and other counties in Henan.
entries.literal: Now Yi Mian and the rest have been negligent for three years, fortunately received lenient treatment, yet instead grew more complacent and let bandits cross into Lushi, Lushan, and other counties in Henan.

entries.zh: 景安雖無吞餉聲名，而罔昧自甘，近亦有賊焚掠襄、光各境，均為法所不容。
entries.en: Jing An may not have a reputation for swallowing army funds, but he is willfully obtuse; of late rebels have burned and pillaged through Xiangyang and Guanghua—and all of this the law cannot abide.
entries.literal: Jing An, though without a reputation for embezzling rations, is willfully ignorant and self-content; recently bandits have also burned and looted through Xiangyang and Guanghua—all of which the law cannot permit.

entries.zh: 況今軍營副封私札，商同軍機大臣改壓軍報。
entries.en: Moreover, sealed private letters are now coming from military camps, and officials are conspiring with Grand Council ministers to tamper with and suppress battle reports.
entries.literal: Moreover, sealed private letters now come from military camps, and officials consult with Grand Council ministers to alter and suppress battle reports.

entries.zh: 供據已破，雖由內臣聲勢，而彼等掩覆僨事，情更顯然。
entries.en: The evidence is already exposed. Even if inner court ministers lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are plainer still.
entries.literal: The evidence is already exposed; although inner eunuchs lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are even plainer.

entries.zh: 請旨懲究，另選能臣，與勒保會同各清本境，則軍令風行，賊必授首。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to punish and investigate, choose other able men, and send them with Le Bao to pacify each province in its own territory. Then army orders will run like the wind, and the rebels will surely lose their heads.
entries.literal: I beg an imperial decree to punish and investigate, separately select capable ministers, and send them with Le Bao to pacify each province in its own territory; then military orders will run like the wind and the bandits will surely present their heads.

entries.zh: 比年發餉至數千萬，軍中子女玉帛奇寶錯陳，而兵食反致有虧。
entries.en: In recent years pay has run to tens of millions, while camps teem with women, jade, silk, and curios—yet the soldiers' rations themselves fall short.
entries.literal: In recent years pay issued has reached tens of millions; in the camps women, children, jade, silk, and rare treasures are piled in profusion, yet the soldiers' rations themselves fall short.

entries.zh: 載贓而歸，風盈道路，嘲之者有'與其請餉，不如書會票'之語。
entries.en: Men return laden with plunder and the roads buzz with gossip. Mockers say it is easier to draw up a draft at the money-shop than to beg the army for pay.
entries.literal: They return laden with loot and the roads buzz with gossip; mockers say, 'Rather than beg for pay, better to write a draft at the money-shop.'

entries.zh: 先帝嚴究軍需局，察出四川漢州知州與德楞泰互爭報銷，及湖北道員胡齊崙侵餉數十萬，一則追賠，一則拿究。
entries.en: The late emperor cracked down on the military supplies bureau, found the Hanzhou prefect in Sichuan disputing accounts with Degengtai, and Hubei circuit intendant Hu Qilun embezzling hundreds of thousands in pay—one ordered to repay, the other seized for trial.
entries.literal: The late emperor strictly investigated the military supplies bureau, found the Hanzhou prefect in Sichuan disputing expense reports with Degengtai, and the Hubei circuit intendant Hu Qilun embezzling hundreds of thousands in pay—one ordered to repay, the other seized for trial.

entries.zh: 他屬類此者必多，尤宜急易新手清釐。
entries.en: Many other districts surely have like cases, and new men ought to be put in charge at once to audit the books.
entries.literal: Other jurisdictions surely have many similar cases; it is especially urgent to put new hands in charge and audit the books.

entries.zh: 則侵盜之跡，必能破露，不但兵餉與善後事宜均得充裕，銷算亦不敢牽混矣。」
entries.en: Embezzlement will then come to light; army funds and postwar relief will both be ample, and no one will dare doctor the accounts."
entries.literal: Then traces of embezzlement can surely be exposed; not only will army pay and postwar relief be ample, but no one will dare doctor the accounts."

entries.en: Thus he closed the memorial.
entries.literal: End of the memorial quotation.

entries.zh: 管世銘，字緘若，與亮吉同里。
entries.en: Guan Shiming, style name Jianruo, was a fellow townsman of Hong Liangji.
entries.literal: Guan Shiming, style name Jianruo, was of the same native place as Liangji.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十三年進士，授戶部主事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in 1778 and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 累遷郎中，充軍機章京。
entries.en: He rose through the ranks to director and served as a Grand Council clerk.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, and served as Grand Council clerk.

entries.zh: 深通律令，凡讞牘多世銘主奏。
entries.en: He was deeply versed in law; most judicial memorials were drafted under his direction.
entries.literal: He was deeply versed in statutes and ordinances; of judicial documents most were drafted under Shiming's lead.

entries.zh: 屢從大臣赴浙江、湖北、吉林、山東按事，大學士阿桂尤善之，倚如左右手。
entries.en: He repeatedly accompanied senior ministers on investigations in Zhejiang, Hubei, Jilin, and Shandong. Grand Secretary A Gui favored him especially and relied on him as on his own hands.
entries.literal: He repeatedly followed great ministers to Zhejiang, Hubei, Jilin, and Shandong to investigate affairs; Grand Secretary A Gui especially favored him and relied on him as on right and left hands.

entries.zh: 時和珅用事，世銘憂憤，與同官論前代輔臣賢否，語譏切無所避。
entries.en: At the time Heshen held power. Guan was troubled and angry; with colleagues he discussed whether chief ministers of past dynasties had been worthy, speaking with biting sarcasm and holding nothing back.
entries.literal: At the time Heshen held power; Shiming was anxious and indignant, and with fellow officials discussed whether former-age chief ministers were worthy or not, his words sarcastic and cutting without avoidance.

entries.zh: 會遷御史，則大喜，夜起傍徨，草疏將劾之，詔仍留軍機處。
entries.en: When he was due for promotion to censor he was overjoyed, rose at night in agitation, and drafted a memorial to impeach Heshen—but an edict kept him at the Grand Council instead.
entries.literal: When he was about to be transferred to censor, he was greatly delighted, rose at night pacing in circles, drafted a memorial about to impeach him—but an edict still retained him at the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 故事，御史留直者，儀注仍視郎官，不得專達封事。
entries.en: By precedent, a censor who remained on Grand Council duty was still treated ceremonially as a director and could not submit sealed memorials on his own.
entries.literal: By precedent, a censor retained on duty still followed ceremonial rules as a director, and could not exclusively present sealed memorials.

entries.zh: 世銘自言愧負此官，阿桂慰之曰：「報稱有日，何必急以言自見。」
entries.en: Guan said he had failed the office. A Gui comforted him: 'Your day to repay the appointment will come—why must you hurry to make yourself known through words.'
entries.literal: Shiming himself said he was ashamed to fail this office; A Gui comforted him, saying: 'A day to repay the appointment will come—why must you hurry to make yourself seen through words.'

entries.zh: 蓋留直阿桂所請，隱全之，使有待。
entries.en: A Gui had requested that he remain on duty, secretly protecting him and bidding him wait.
entries.literal: This was because retention on duty was requested by A Gui, who secretly protected him completely, letting him wait.

entries.zh: 嘉慶三年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1798.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, he died.

entries.zh: 谷際岐，字西阿，雲南趙州人。
entries.en: Gu Jiqi, style name Xi'a, was a native of Zhaozhou, Yunnan.
entries.literal: Gu Jiqi, style name Xi'a, was a native of Zhaozhou in Yunnan.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，與校四庫全書。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in 1775, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and helped collate the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and participated in collating the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries.

entries.zh: 充會試同考官，所拔多知名士。
entries.en: He served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination and selected many men who later won renown.
entries.literal: Served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination; those he selected were mostly famous scholars.

entries.zh: 乞養歸，主講五華書院，教士有法。
entries.en: He asked leave to care for his parents and went home to head the Wuhua Academy, where he taught with real discipline.
entries.literal: Begged leave to nurse parents and returned; lectured at Wuhua Academy; teaching scholars had method.

entries.zh: 連丁父母憂，服闋，起原官。
entries.en: He mourned both parents in succession; when the mourning period ended, he was restored to his former post.
entries.literal: In succession observed parents' mourning; when mourning ended, resumed original office.

entries.zh: 列傳一百四十三
entries.en: Biographies 143
entries.literal: Biographies, Number 143

entries.zh: 清性坦率，厭苛禮，不合於上官，又不耐簿書錢穀，遂乞病，上亦知之，改授山東登州鎮總兵，調曹州鎮。
entries.en: Frank by nature, weary of stiff ritual, ill-suited to superiors, and unable to bear ledgers and grain accounts, he pleaded illness; the emperor understood, made him brigadier of Dengzhou in Shandong, then moved him to Caozhou.
entries.literal: Qing was frank by nature, disliked stiff ceremony, did not suit his superiors, and could not endure paperwork and revenue accounts; he asked to retire on grounds of illness, the emperor knew him well, changed his appointment to brigadier-general of Dengzhou Garrison in Shandong, then transferred him to Caozhou Garrison.

entries.zh: 道光二年，以老休致，命在籍食全俸。
entries.en: In Daoguang 2 he retired on age and was allowed full salary at home.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he retired for age; he was ordered to draw full salary while living at home.

entries.zh: 八年，卒，賜祭葬，祀山東名宦，官其孫熾昌為兵部主事；
entries.en: In the eighth year he died; state rites were granted, he was honored in Shandong's temple of worthy officials, and his grandson Chichang was given a secretaryship in the Ministry of War;
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted, he was entered in the temple of eminent officials of Shandong, and his grandson Chichang was given a post as a secretary in the Ministry of War;

entries.zh: 瑩，舉人。
entries.en: his grandson Ying became a provincial graduate.
entries.literal: Ying became a provincial graduate.

entries.zh: 列傳一百四十八
entries.en: Biography 148
entries.literal: Biographies 148

entries.zh: 嘉慶十四年，海盜蔡牽平，以功賜花翎。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 14 the pirate Cai Qian was pacified, and Chonghua received the peacock feather for his service.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing the sea pirate Cai Qian was pacified; for merit he was granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 硃渥欲歸誠，未決，崇華隻身至海舶，諭以禍福，遂受降。
entries.en: Zhu Wo wanted to surrender but hesitated. Chonghua went alone to his vessel, explained the consequences of his choice, and won his submission.
entries.literal: Zhu Wo wished to surrender but had not decided; Chonghua went alone to his ship, instructed him on fortune and disaster, and he then accepted surrender.

entries.zh: 十七年，署台灣淡水同知。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he served as acting subprefect of Tamsui in Taiwan.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he acted as subprefect of Tamsui, Taiwan.

entries.zh: 高媽達妖言惑眾，捕獲，訊得劉林、祝現謀以次年閏八月望在京師舉事，四方起應之。
entries.en: Gao Mada was arrested for spreading sedition. Under interrogation he revealed that Liu Lin and Zhu Xian planned an uprising in the capital on the full moon of the intercalary eighth month the following year, with supporters to rise across the empire.
entries.literal: Gao Mada used demonic talk to mislead the masses; captured and interrogated, it was learned that Liu Lin and Zhu Xian plotted to rise in the capital on the full moon of the intercalary eighth month of the following year, with responses rising in all directions.

entries.zh: 崇華牒請奏聞，大吏以其語不經，置之，僅以傳教罪誅高媽達。
entries.en: Chonghua urgently memorialized the court, but senior officials dismissed his report as incredible and executed Gao Mada only for illegal preaching.
entries.literal: Chonghua memorialized requesting that it be reported to the throne; high officials, deeming his words absurd, set it aside and executed Gao Mada only on the charge of preaching heterodox doctrine.

entries.zh: 至十八年九月十五日，果有林清、祝現之變，劉林者即林清別名也。
entries.en: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, the uprising of Lin Qing and Zhu Xian broke out exactly as foretold—Liu Lin being Lin Qing's alias.
entries.literal: By the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, the disturbances of Lin Qing and Zhu Xian indeed occurred; Liu Lin was Lin Qing's alias.

entries.zh: 自高媽達伏法，福建匪黨巳解散，得無事。
entries.en: After Gao Mada's execution the rebel cells in Fujian had already broken up, and the province escaped further trouble.
entries.literal: Since Gao Mada was executed, Fujian bandit factions had already dispersed, and the province remained untroubled.

entries.zh: 尋以道員謁選，授河南南汝光道。
entries.en: Soon selected as an expectant intendant, he was appointed to the Nan-Ru-Guang circuit in Henan.
entries.literal: Soon, as an expectant intendant awaiting selection, he was appointed to the Nan-Ru-Guang circuit of Henan.

entries.zh: 教匪鉅魁劉松久在逃，懸緝十餘載，偵知潛匿安徽宿州傳教，捕獲之。
entries.en: Liu Song, a leading sect rebel who had been at large for more than a decade, was discovered preaching secretly in Suzhou, Anhui, and captured.
entries.literal: The great teaching-sect rebel chief Liu Song had long been at large; wanted for more than ten years, Chonghua learned he was secretly preaching in Suzhou, Anhui, and captured him.

entries.zh: 母憂去官。
entries.en: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: He left office on his mother's death.

entries.zh: 論曰：剿平教匪，不獨賴將帥戮力，一時守土之吏，與有勞焉。
entries.en: The historian comments: Pacifying the White Lotus rebels depended not only on the generals' exertions—the local officials of the day also bore their share of the burden.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Suppressing and pacifying the teaching rebels did not rely on generals and commanders alone; the local officials of the time also shared in the labor.

entries.zh: 最顯者為四川劉清，而方積亦倡行堅壁清野，保障一方，後復屢定番亂，蜀人與清並稱。
entries.en: The most celebrated was Liu Qing of Sichuan, but Fang Ji also pioneered the strategy of sealing towns and stripping the countryside, securing his district, and later quelled tribal revolts again and again—the people of Sichuan ranked him alongside Liu Qing.
entries.literal: The most prominent was Liu Qing of Sichuan; Fang Ji also pioneered fortified villages and cleared countryside, securing one region, and later repeatedly pacified tribal rebellions—the people of Shu ranked him with Qing.

entries.zh: 他如硃爾漢之保鞏昌，楊頀之清叛產、撫難民，廖寅之擒劉之協，皆卓有建樹。
entries.en: Others too made distinguished contributions: Zhu Erhan's defense of Gongchang, Yang Hu's sorting of rebel property and relief of refugees, and Liao Yin's capture of Liu Zhixie.
entries.literal: Others such as Zhu Erhan's defense of Gongchang, Yang Hu's clearing of rebel property and relief of refugees, and Liao Yin's capture of Liu Zhixie all achieved outstanding accomplishments.

entries.zh: 陳昌齊、硃爾賡額於治海寇並具謀略，而硃爾賡額功尤顯矣。
entries.en: Chen Changqi and Zhu Ergenge both showed strategic talent against maritime pirates, though Zhu Ergenge's achievements stood out above all.
entries.literal: Chen Changqi and Zhu Ergenge both possessed strategy in dealing with sea bandits, and Zhu Ergenge's merit was especially conspicuous.

entries.zh: 查崇華預發林清逆謀，為疆臣所格；
entries.en: Cha Chonghua had forewarned of Lin Qing's conspiracy but was overruled by provincial governors;
entries.literal: Cha Chonghua forewarned of Lin Qing's treasonous plot but was blocked by frontier officials;

entries.zh: 及筦西征軍需，以撙節稱，故同著於篇。
entries.en: and when he managed supplies for the western campaign he won renown for thrift. For these reasons he is included in this chapter as well.
entries.literal: when he managed western campaign supplies he was famed for economy, and therefore is recorded together in this chapter.

entries.zh: 列傳一百四十九
entries.en: Biography 149
entries.literal: Biographies 149

entries.zh: 元，乾隆五十四年進士，選庶吉士，散館第一，授編修。
entries.en: In Qianlong 54 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, placed first when leaving the academy, and received appointment as compiler.
entries.literal: Yuan passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, ranked first upon leaving the academy, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 逾年大考，高宗親擢第一，超擢少詹事。
entries.en: The following year, in the palace examination, the Gaozong Emperor personally placed him first and exceptionally promoted him to junior vice-president of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The next year in the great examination the Gaozong Emperor personally ranked him first and promoted him in exceptional fashion to junior vice-president of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 召對，上喜曰：「不意朕八旬外復得一人！」
entries.en: When summoned for audience, the emperor said with delight, "I never thought that after my eightieth year I should gain another man like this!"
entries.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor said with pleasure: "I did not expect that beyond my eightieth year I should gain another such man!"

entries.zh: 直南書房、懋勤殿，遷詹事。
entries.en: He was assigned to the Southern Study and Maqin Hall, and was promoted to supervisor of the Heir Apparent’s Household.
entries.literal: He served in the Southern Study and the Maqin Hall, and was transferred to supervisor of the Heir Apparent’s Household.

entries.zh: 五十八年，督山東學政，任滿，調浙江。
entries.en: In year 58 he served as educational commissioner of Shandong; when his term ended he was moved to Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he supervised education in Shandong; when his term ended he was transferred to Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 歷兵部、禮部、戶部侍郎。
entries.en: He served in succession as vice-minister of War, Rites, and Revenue.
entries.literal: He successively held the posts of vice-minister of War, of Rites, and of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十九年，命按事安徽、江蘇、浙江。
entries.en: In year 19 he was ordered to investigate affairs in Anhui, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to conduct investigations in Anhui, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 自禁煙議起，海疆久不靖。
entries.en: Since the opium prohibition debate, the maritime frontier had long been unsettled.
entries.literal: From the time the opium prohibition was debated, the maritime frontier had long been unsettled.

entries.zh: 林則徐既罷，琦善主撫，復不得要領。
entries.en: Lin Zexu had been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu had already been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.

entries.zh: 金釗素不附和議，與穆彰阿等意齟《齒吾》。
entries.en: Jinzhao had never favored appeasement and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.
entries.literal: Jinzhao had never favored the appeasement faction and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.

entries.zh: 一日召對，上從容問廣東事可付諸何人，金釗以林則徐對，上不悅。
entries.en: One day at audience the emperor casually asked whom Guangdong affairs could be entrusted to; Jinzhao named Lin Zexu; the emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: One day at audience the emperor casually asked to whom Guangdong affairs could be entrusted; Jinzhao answered Lin Zexu; the emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 至二十一年，事且益棘，詔予則徐四品卿銜赴浙江軍營，亦未果用之。
entries.en: By year 21 affairs grew urgent; an edict gave Lin Zexu fourth-rank vice-minister rank and sent him to the Zhejiang army, yet he was still not effectively used.
entries.literal: By the twenty-first year affairs grew more urgent; an edict gave Lin Zexu fourth-rank vice-minister rank and sent him to the Zhejiang army camp, yet he was still not effectively used.

entries.zh: 未幾，有吏部司員陳起詩規避倉差，金釗還其呈牘禁勿遞，為所訐，坐降四級調用。
entries.en: Soon a Personnel clerk, Chen Qishi, tried to evade granary duty; Jinzhao returned his petition and forbade submission; Chen impeached him and he was demoted four ranks and transferred.
entries.literal: Before long a Personnel bureau clerk, Chen Qishi, tried to evade granary duty; Jinzhao returned his petition and forbade its submission; Chen impeached him, and he was punished by demotion four ranks and transfer.

entries.zh: 逾年，授光祿寺卿。
entries.en: After more than a year he was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 以衰老乞罷，住京養疴，許以二品頂戴致仕。
entries.en: He asked to retire for age and illness, stayed in the capital to nurse his health, and was permitted to retire with second-rank button.
entries.literal: He asked to retire on account of age and infirmity, remained in the capital to nurse his illness, and was permitted to retire with second-rank button.

entries.zh: 久之，上仍眷念，二十九年，皇太后之喪，具疏上慰，賜頭品頂戴。
entries.en: Long afterward the emperor still cherished him; in year 29, at the empress dowager's mourning, he submitted a memorial of condolence and was granted the first-rank button.
entries.literal: After a long time the emperor still cherished him; in the twenty-ninth year, at the empress dowager's mourning, he submitted a memorial of condolence and was granted the first-rank button.

entries.zh: 咸豐四年，重宴鹿鳴，加太子太保。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 4 he again attended the deer-ming banquet and was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he again attended the deer-ming banquet and was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 六年，卒，詔以尚書例賜卹，諡文端。
entries.en: In year 6 he died; an edict granted ministerial posthumous rites, with posthumous title Wenduan.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he died; an edict granted posthumous rites according to the ministerial standard, with posthumous title Wenduan.

entries.zh: 金釗自為翰林，布衣脫粟，後常不改。
entries.en: From his Hanlin days Jinzhao wore plain cloth and ate simple grain, and seldom changed afterward.
entries.literal: From his days as a Hanlin scholar Jinzhao wore plain cloth and ate simple grain, and afterward he seldom changed.

entries.zh: 當官廉察，負一時清望，雖被排擠，卒以恩禮終。
entries.en: In office he was incorrupt and bore the age's reputation for integrity; though pushed aside, he ended with imperial favor.
entries.literal: In office he was incorrupt and observant and bore the pure reputation of the age; though squeezed out, he ended with imperial favor and ritual.

entries.zh: 子修，通政司副使。
entries.en: His son Xiu was vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
entries.literal: His son Xiu was vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

entries.zh: 列傳一百五十一
entries.en: Biography 151
entries.literal: Biographies 151

entries.zh: 覺羅寶興，字獻山，隸鑲黃旗。
entries.en: Jueluo Baoxing (style name Xianshan) belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Jueluo Baoxing, style name Xianshan, was registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He took his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 15 (1810), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In Jiaqing 15 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 累遷少詹事，入直上書房。
entries.en: He rose step by step to vice chamberlain of the Hanlin Academy and was assigned to the Upper Study on standing duty.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice chamberlain and entered permanent service in the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 十八年，仁宗幸熱河，林清逆黨突入禁城，寶興散直，至東華門與賊遇，急入告警。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 18 (1813), while the Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe, Lin Qing's rebels broke into the Forbidden City. Baoxing was between shifts; at the East Flowery Gate he ran into the assailants and dashed inside to sound the alarm.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe; Lin Qing's rebel faction burst into the Forbidden City. Baoxing was off duty; reaching the East Flowery Gate he met the rebels and rushed in to raise the alarm.

entries.zh: 宣宗方在上書房，聞警戒備，賊不得逞。
entries.en: The future Daoguang Emperor was in the Upper Study; once the warning spread, the palace was put on guard and the rebels were thwarted.
entries.literal: The Daoguang Emperor was then in the Upper Study; hearing the alarm, preparations were made and the rebels could not succeed.

entries.zh: 上還京，擢寶興內閣學士。
entries.en: After the emperor returned to Beijing, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 十九年，授禮部侍郎。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he was made vice minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed vice minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 以事忤旨，詔斥寶興不學，降大理寺卿，罷直書房。
entries.en: He later offended the throne on another matter; an edict called him unlearned, demoted him to president of the Court of Judicial Review, and stripped him of Upper Study duty.
entries.literal: For an affair that offended the imperial will, an edict rebuked Baoxing as unlearned, demoted him to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and dismissed him from Upper Study duty.

entries.zh: 复坐部刊科場條例誤「高宗」為「高祖」，降二級調用。
