entries.en: He was penalized again when regulations his ministry published for the civil service examinations named 'Gaozu' instead of 'Gaozong'; he dropped two ranks and was reassigned.
entries.literal: He was punished again because his ministry's printed examination regulations mistakenly gave 'Gaozu' for 'Gaozong'; he was demoted two ranks and transferred.

entries.zh: 尋予三等侍衛，充吐魯番領隊大臣。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he received the rank of third-class imperial bodyguard and was sent as the Turpan expedition commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon he was given third-class imperial bodyguard and appointed leading officer for Turpan.

entries.zh: 先是寶興以馬邊諸廳縣增設防兵，籌議邊防經費，請按糧津貼，計可徵銀百萬兩，以三十萬為初設防兵之需。
entries.en: To pay for new garrisons along the Ma Bian line, Baoxing had proposed a grain surcharge expected to yield one million taels—three hundred thousand for startup costs.
entries.literal: Earlier Baoxing, because Ma Bian and other subprefectures and counties were adding frontier troops, planned border defense funds and requested a grain surcharge, calculating that one million taels of silver could be levied, with three hundred thousand for initial troop establishment.

entries.zh: 每歲經費，即以餘銀七十萬兩生息，置田供支。
entries.en: The remaining seven hundred thousand taels would be invested and used to buy land whose rents would cover yearly upkeep.
entries.literal: Annual expenses were to be met by investing the remaining seven hundred thousand taels at interest and purchasing land for support.

entries.zh: 上以津貼病民，撥部帑銀百萬。
entries.en: The emperor rejected the surcharge as burdensome and allotted one million taels from central funds instead.
entries.literal: The emperor held that the surcharge harmed the people and allocated one million taels from the ministry treasury.

entries.zh: 翰林院侍讀學士王炳瀛奏：「四川前買義田，遍​​及百餘州縣，若更以數十萬帑銀於各州縣買田收租，膏腴將盡歸公產。
entries.en: Hanlin reader Wang Bingying warned: "Sichuan already held charitable estates in over a hundred jurisdictions; spending hundreds of thousands more taels to buy land province-wide would turn most fertile soil into government holdings.
entries.literal: Hanlin Academy attendant reader Wang Bingying memorialized: 'Sichuan has previously bought charitable fields spread across more than a hundred prefectures and counties; if hundreds of thousands more in treasury silver were used to buy land and collect rent in every prefecture and county, fertile land would nearly all become public property.

entries.zh: 請限於四廳近邊地收買，安置屯防。」
entries.en: He asked that purchases be confined to land near the four frontier subprefectures for garrison settlement."
entries.literal: He requested limiting purchases to land near the four subprefectures on the frontier and settling garrison colonists there.'

entries.zh: 下寶興妥議，疏言：「邊防完竣，用銀二十二萬兩有奇，以三十七萬發鹽茶各商，歲得息三萬七千餘兩，足敷增設練勇餉械之需。
entries.en: Baoxing was told to work out the details. He reported: "Finishing the frontier works would take just over 220,000 taels; lending 370,000 to salt and tea merchants would yield 37,000 taels a year—enough for the new militia's pay and equipment.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to Baoxing for proper deliberation. He memorialized: 'Border defense completed will cost a little over 220,000 taels; lend 370,000 to salt and tea merchants, yielding over 37,000 taels interest yearly, sufficient for the pay and arms of added militia.

entries.zh: 餘銀四十萬，聽部撥別用。」
entries.en: The remaining 400,000 taels would revert to the ministry for other uses."
entries.literal: The remaining 400,000 taels were left to the ministry to allocate elsewhere.'

entries.zh: 遂罷買田議，二十一年，拜文淵閣大學士，留四川總督任。
entries.en: The land-purchase scheme was dropped. In Daoguang 21 (1841) he became a Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while remaining governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: The land-purchase plan was then abandoned. In the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while retaining the Sichuan governor-generalship.

entries.zh: 時大學士琦善、協辦大學士伊里布相繼罷，在朝滿洲大臣鮮當上意，故有是授。
entries.en: Qishan and Yilibu had just been removed from office, and few Manchu ministers in Beijing still enjoyed the emperor's trust—hence Baoxing's elevation.
entries.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu had been dismissed in succession; few Manchu ministers at court pleased the emperor, hence this appointment.

entries.zh: 二十六年，入覲，命留京管理刑部，充上書房總師傅，兼翰林院掌院學士。
entries.en: In Daoguang 26 (1846) he was summoned to court, kept in Beijing to head the Ministry of Justice, made chief tutor of the Upper Study, and named chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he came to audience, was ordered to remain in the capital to administer the Ministry of Justice, appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, and concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 二十八年元旦，加恩年老諸臣，加太保。
entries.en: At the New Year audience of Daoguang 28 (1848) he received the honorary rank of Grand Tutor among favors granted to senior ministers.
entries.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-eighth year, in extending grace to aged officials, he was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 十月，卒，年七十二，諡文莊。
entries.en: He died in the tenth month at seventy-two and was posthumously titled Wenzhuang.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he died, aged seventy-two; his posthumous title was Wenzhuang.

entries.zh: 列傳一百五十二
entries.en: Biography 152
entries.literal: Biographies 152

entries.zh: 李鴻賓，字鹿蘋，江西德化人。
entries.en: Li Hongbin, courtesy name Luping, came from Dehua in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Li Hongbin, styled Luping, was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。
entries.en: He took his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
entries.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Jiaqing, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.

entries.zh: 遷御史、給事中。
entries.en: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 十八年，巡視東漕。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he inspected the eastern grain transport route.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he inspected the eastern grain transport.

entries.zh: 會林清之變，數疏陳時政利弊；
entries.en: At the time of Lin Qing's rebellion he repeatedly memorialized on the strengths and failings of current policy;
entries.literal: At the time of Lin Qing's rebellion he repeatedly memorialized on the advantages and harms of current policy;

entries.zh: 又以山東、河南、直隸毗連之地，頻年遭兵，條上善後事，始受仁宗知。
entries.en: and because Shandong, Henan, and Zhili were adjoining regions that had suffered warfare for years, he set forth measures for recovery. Only then did he win the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.
entries.literal: and because Shandong, Henan, and Zhili were adjoining regions that had suffered warfare for years, he set forth items on post-disaster measures and first won the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.

entries.zh: 命偕河督吳璥、巡撫同興按河督李亨特貪劣不職狀，得實以聞。
entries.en: He was ordered, together with River Director Wu Jing and Governor Tongxing, to investigate River Director Li Hengte's greed and incompetence. The charges were substantiated and reported.
entries.literal: He was ordered together with River Director Wu Jing and Governor Tongxing to investigate River Director Li Hengte's greedy and incompetent conduct; the facts were established and reported.

entries.zh: 列傳一百五十三
entries.en: Biography 153
entries.literal: Biography 153

entries.zh: 十八年，河南天理會教匪李文成等倡亂，陷滑縣，直隸、山東皆響應，林清糾黨犯禁門。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year Li Wencheng and other Heavenly Principle (Tianli) sect rebels in Henan rose in revolt, seized Huaxian, and drew responses from Zhili and Shandong; Lin Qing mustered followers and attacked the Forbidden Gate.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year Henan Tianli sect rebels led by Li Wencheng and others rose, seized Huaxian, and Zhili and Shandong all responded; Lin Qing gathered a party and attacked the Forbidden Gate.

entries.zh: 初，命總督溫承惠往剿，清既誅，乃發京兵，授那彥成欽差大臣，加都統銜，督師率楊遇春、楊芳等討之，迭詔責戰甚急。
entries.en: At first Governor-General Wen Chenghui was ordered to suppress them; after Lin Qing was killed, capital troops were sent out, Na Yancheng was made Imperial Commissioner with commandant rank to direct Yang Yuchun, Yang Fang, and others, and repeated edicts urgently pressed for action.
entries.literal: At first Governor-General Wen Chenghui was ordered to suppress them; after Lin was executed, capital troops were dispatched, Na Yancheng was made Imperial Commissioner with commandant rank, directed the armies with Yang Yuchun, Yang Fang, and others to attack, and repeated edicts urgently pressed for battle.

entries.zh: 那彥成以小丑不足平，惟慮遁入太行，勢且蔓延，十月，至衛輝，合師而後進。
entries.en: Na Yancheng regarded the rebels as trifling foes but feared they might slip into the Taihang Mountains and spread; in the tenth month he reached Weihui, united the armies, and then advanced.
entries.literal: Na Yancheng held these petty foes not worth pacifying but feared they would escape into the Taihang Mountains and the trouble would spread; in the tenth month he reached Weihui, united the armies, and then advanced.

entries.zh: 賊踞桃源集、道口，與滑縣為犄角，連敗之於新鎮、丁欒集。
entries.en: The rebels held Taoyuanji and Daokou in mutual support with Huaxian; they were repeatedly defeated at Xinzhen and Dingluanji.
entries.literal: The rebels held Taoyuanji and Daokou in mutual support with Huaxian; they were repeatedly defeated at Xinzhen and Dingluanji.

entries.zh: 遇春擊破道口，殲賊萬餘，焚其巢；
entries.en: Yang Yuchun broke Daokou, destroyed more than ten thousand rebels, and burned their lair;
entries.literal: Yuchun broke Daokou, destroyed more than ten thousand rebels, and burned their lair;

entries.zh: 尋破桃源集，追道口餘賊，抵滑縣。
entries.en: He soon took Taoyuanji, pursued the Daokou remnant rebels, and reached Huaxian.
entries.literal: Soon after he took Taoyuanji, pursued the Daokou remnant rebels, and reached Huaxian.

entries.zh: 文成遁輝縣司寨，楊芳、德英阿追破之，文成自焚死。
entries.en: Li Wencheng fled to Sizhai in Huixian; Yang Fang and De'ying'a pursued and defeated him, and Wencheng burned himself to death.
entries.literal: Wencheng fled to Huixian Sizhai; Yang Fang and De'ying'a pursued and broke him; Wencheng burned himself to death.

entries.zh: 親督遇春等圍滑城數旬，以地雷攻拔之，獲首虜二萬餘。
entries.en: He personally directed Yang Yuchun and others in besieging Huacheng for several weeks, stormed it with land mines, and captured more than twenty thousand leaders and captives.
entries.literal: He personally directed Yuchun and others in besieging Huacheng for several tens of days, stormed it with land mines, and captured more than twenty thousand leaders and captives.

entries.zh: 山東賊亦平。
entries.en: The Shandong rebels were also pacified.
entries.literal: The Shandong rebels were also pacified.

entries.zh: 捷聞，加太子少保，封三等子爵，賜雙眼花翎，授直隸總督，賜祭其祖阿桂墓。
entries.en: On news of victory he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as third-rank viscount, granted the double-eyed peacock feather, appointed governor-general of Zhili, and granted sacrifice at his grandfather Agui's tomb.
entries.literal: On news of victory he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed third-rank viscount, granted the double-eyed peacock feather, appointed Zhili Governor-General, and granted sacrifice at his grandfather Agui's tomb.

entries.zh: 玉麟，字子振，哈達納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Yu Lin, whose style was Zizhen, was of the Hadanara clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Yu Lin, style name Zizhen, of the Hadanara clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 乾隆六十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: A jinshi of the sixtieth year of the Qianlong reign, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
entries.literal: Jinshi in the sixtieth year of Qianlong, selected Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 嘉慶初，三遷為祭酒。
entries.en: Early in the Jiaqing reign he was promoted three times until he became Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: Early in Jiaqing, thrice promoted to become Libationer.

entries.zh: 歷詹事、內閣學士。
entries.en: He served as Chancellor of the Supervisorate of Instruction and Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: Served as Chancellor of the Supervisorate of Instruction and Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 纂修實錄久，特詔充總纂，奏事列名總裁後。
entries.en: After long service compiling the veritable records, he was specially ordered to serve as chief compiler; when reporting to the throne his name was listed after the chief directors.
entries.literal: Long compiling veritable records, specially ordered to serve as chief compiler; when reporting affairs his name was listed after the chief directors.

entries.zh: 入直上書房。
entries.en: He entered duty in the Shangshufang (the palace school).
entries.literal: Entered duty in the Shangshufang.

entries.zh: 歷禮部、吏部侍郎，典會試。
entries.en: He served as vice minister in the Ministries of Rites and Personnel and presided over metropolitan examinations.
entries.literal: Served as vice ministers in the Ministries of Rites and Personnel and presided over metropolitan examinations.

entries.zh: 奉使鞫安徽壽州獄，及湖北官銀匠侵虧錢糧事，大吏並被嚴譴。
entries.en: Commissioned to try the Shouzhou case in Anhui and the Hubei silversmiths' embezzlement of grain taxes, he secured severe rebukes for the senior officials involved.
entries.literal: Commissioned to try the Anhui Shouzhou case and Hubei silversmiths' embezzlement of grain taxes; high officials were all severely rebuked.

entries.zh: 後歷赴湖南、江西、直隸、河南按事，時稱公正。
entries.en: He was later sent repeatedly to Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhili, and Henan to investigate cases, and at the time was praised for his fairness.
entries.literal: Later he was repeatedly sent to Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhili, and Henan to investigate cases, and was called fair at the time.

entries.zh: 十二年，督安徽學政，調江蘇。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he supervised education in Anhui and was transferred to Jiangsu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he supervised Anhui education and was transferred to Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 十六年，兼右翼總兵。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he also served as Right Wing commander.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, concurrently Right Wing commander.

entries.zh: 坐吏部銓序有誤，奪職。
entries.en: He lost office after being censured for errors in the Ministry of Personnel's ranking order.
entries.literal: Censured for errors in Ministry of Personnel ranking order, office taken.

entries.zh: 未幾，授內閣學士，兼護軍統領、左翼總兵，遷戶部侍郎。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently commander of the Guard Corps and Left Wing commander, and promoted to vice minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: Before long appointed Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently commander of the Guard Corps and Left Wing commander, promoted to vice minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十八年八月，車駕自熱河回蹕，迎至白澗，先還京。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year he welcomed the imperial carriage returning from Rehe as far as Baijian, then went back to Beijing ahead of it.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year the imperial carriage returned from Rehe; he welcomed it to Baijian and returned first to the capital.

entries.zh: 會林清逆黨犯禁門，率所部擊捕；
entries.en: When Lin Qing's rebels stormed the Forbidden Gate, he led his troops to attack and capture them;
entries.literal: When Lin Qing's rebel faction stormed the Forbidden Gate, he led his troops to attack and capture them;

entries.zh: 坐門禁懈弛，褫職。
entries.en: yet he was censured for lax gate security and stripped of office.
entries.literal: censured for lax gate security, stripped of office.

entries.zh: 十九年，予三等侍衛，赴葉爾羌辦事。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year he was given third-rank guardsman and sent to Yarkand as resident commissioner.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, given third-rank guardsman, sent to Yarkand as resident commissioner.

entries.zh: 二十二年，加副都統銜，充駐藏大臣。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he was given vice commandant rank and served as resident commissioner in Tibet.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, granted vice commandant rank, served as Resident Commissioner in Tibet.

entries.zh: 歷左翼總兵、鑲白旗漢軍副都統，遷左都御史，禮部、吏部、兵部尚書。
entries.en: He served as Left Wing commander and vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner Chinese forces, then rose to Left Censor-in-Chief and minister of Rites, Personnel, and War in succession.
entries.literal: Served as Left Wing commander, vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner Chinese Banner forces, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, ministers of Rites, Personnel, and War.

entries.zh: 列傳一百五十四
entries.en: Biography 154
entries.literal: Biographies 154

entries.zh: 林則徐 ，字少穆，福建侯官人。
entries.en: Lin Zexu, styled Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu, style name Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

entries.zh: 少警敏，有異才。
entries.en: From boyhood he was quick-witted and perceptive, and showed uncommon ability.
entries.literal: In youth he was alert and keen; he possessed extraordinary talent.

entries.zh: 年二十，舉鄉試。
entries.en: At twenty he passed the provincial civil service examination.
entries.literal: At age twenty, he passed the provincial examination.

entries.zh: 巡撫張師誠闢佐幕。
entries.en: Governor Zhang Shicheng brought him onto his staff as a secretarial aide.
entries.literal: Governor Zhang Shicheng invited him to serve as a staff assistant in his office.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1811 he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.

entries.zh: 歷典江西、雲南鄉試，分校會試。
entries.en: He went on to supervise the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and served as an examiner for the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Jiangxi and Yunnan and served on the board for the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 遷御史，疏論福建閩安副將張寶以海盜投誠，宜示裁抑，以防驕蹇，被嘉納。
entries.en: Promoted to censor, he memorialized that Vice-Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, a former pirate who had submitted to the government, ought to be kept firmly in hand lest he grow arrogant and unruly. The throne approved his advice.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Censor and submitted a memorial arguing that Vice-Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, who had surrendered after being a pirate, should be shown restraint and kept in check to guard against arrogance and insubordination; the memorial was well received.

entries.zh: 未幾，出為杭嘉湖道，修海塘，興水利。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was posted as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, where he repaired sea walls and developed irrigation works.
entries.literal: Before long he went out to serve as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, repaired sea dikes, and promoted water conservancy.

entries.zh: 道光元年，聞父病，引疾歸。
entries.en: In 1821, on learning that his father was ill, he asked leave on grounds of sickness and went home.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, hearing that his father was ill, he cited illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 二年，起授淮海道，未之任，署浙江鹽運使。
entries.en: The following year he was recalled and appointed intendant of the Huaihai Circuit, though before assuming that office he served as acting commissioner of salt transport for Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed to the Huaihai Circuit, but before taking up the post he served as acting Zhejiang Salt Transport Commissioner.

entries.zh: 遷江蘇按察使，治獄嚴明。
entries.en: He was then made judicial commissioner of Jiangsu, where he tried cases with firm and impartial rigor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Judicial Commissioner of Jiangsu and handled legal cases with strict clarity.

entries.zh: 四年，大水，署布政使，治賑。
entries.en: In 1824, when severe flooding struck, he acted as financial commissioner and directed famine relief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year there was a great flood; he served as acting Financial Commissioner and managed relief.

entries.zh: 尋丁母憂，命赴南河修高家堰堤工，事竣回籍。
entries.en: He soon entered mourning for his mother, but was ordered to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojiayan embankment. When the project was complete he returned home.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; he was ordered to go to the Southern Rivers to repair the dike works at Gaojiayan, and when the work was finished he returned to his native place.

entries.zh: 六年，命署兩淮鹽政，以未終制辭，服闋，補陝西按察使。
entries.en: In 1826 he was ordered to act as salt controller for the Two Huai districts, but declined because he was still in mourning. After the mourning period he was appointed judicial commissioner of Shaanxi.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to serve as acting Salt Controller of the Two Huai regions, but he declined because mourning was not yet complete; when mourning ended he was appointed Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 遷江寧布政使，父憂歸。
entries.en: He was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning, then went home to mourn his father.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Financial Commissioner of Jiangning, then returned home upon his father's death.

entries.zh: 十年，補湖北布政使，調河南，又調江寧。
entries.en: In 1830 he was appointed financial commissioner of Hubei, then transferred to Henan and afterward to Jiangning.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Hubei, transferred to Henan, and then transferred again to Jiangning.

entries.zh: 十一年，擢河東河道總督。
entries.en: In 1831 he was promoted to governor-general of the Eastern River conservancy.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern River Conservancy.

entries.zh: 疏陳稭料為河工第一弊藪，親赴各廳察驗；
entries.en: He memorialized that straw supplies were the greatest source of abuse in river engineering and personally inspected every office involved;
entries.literal: In a memorial he stated that straw materials were the foremost source of corruption in river works, and he personally went to each office to inspect and verify;

entries.zh: 又言碎石實足為埽工之輔，應隨宜施用。
entries.en: he also argued that crushed stone could usefully supplement revetment work and ought to be deployed wherever appropriate.
entries.literal: he also said that crushed stone could truly serve as an auxiliary to revetment works and should be applied as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 十二年，調江蘇巡撫。
entries.en: In 1832 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to be Governor of Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 吳中洊飢，奏免逋賦，籌撫卹。
entries.en: When famine struck the Wu region again and again, he memorialized for remission of back taxes and organized relief and compensation.
entries.literal: Wu suffered repeated famine; he memorialized to remit overdue taxes and organized relief and consolation.

entries.zh: 前在籓司任，議定賑務章程，行之有效，至是仍其法，宿弊一清。
entries.en: During an earlier term as provincial treasurer he had drafted relief regulations that worked well, and he now applied the same methods again, clearing away entrenched abuses at a stroke.
entries.literal: While previously serving as provincial treasurer he had drawn up regulations for relief work that proved effective; now he continued that method, and long-standing abuses were entirely cleared away.

entries.zh: 賑竣，乃籌積穀備荒。
entries.en: Once relief was complete, he set about building up grain reserves against future dearth.
entries.literal: When relief was finished, he then planned grain reserves against famine.

entries.zh: 清釐交代，盡結京控諸獄。
entries.en: He straightened out administrative transitions and cleared the backlog of cases appealed to the capital.
entries.literal: He cleared up handovers of office and settled all cases of appeals lodged in the capital.

entries.zh: 考覈屬吏，疏言：「察吏莫先於自察，必將各屬大小政務，逐一求盡於心，然後能以驗群吏之盡心與否。
entries.en: When reviewing subordinate officials he memorialized: 'The best way to judge officials is to begin by judging oneself. One must master every major and minor affair under one's jurisdiction before one can tell whether one's subordinates are truly doing their duty.
entries.literal: In evaluating subordinate officials he submitted a memorial saying: 'There is no inspecting officials better than first inspecting oneself; one must thoroughly understand in one's heart each major and minor administrative matter under one's jurisdiction, and only then can one test whether the officials under one are doing their utmost.

entries.zh: 如大吏之心先未貫徹，何從察其情偽？
entries.en: If a senior official has not first mastered the work himself, how can he discern sincerity from pretense?
entries.literal: If the mind of the superior official is not first fully penetrated, how can one investigate their truth and falsity?

entries.zh: 臣惟持此不敢不盡之心，事事與僚屬求實際。」
entries.en: I hold myself to this standard of undivided effort and pursue practical results in every matter together with my colleagues.'
entries.literal: Your servant holds this mind that dares not fail to do his utmost and in every matter seeks practical results together with his colleagues.'

entries.zh: 詔嘉之，勉以力行。
entries.en: The throne commended him and urged him to carry the principle through in action.
entries.literal: The edict praised this and exhorted him to put it forcefully into practice.

entries.zh: 先是總督陶澍奏濬三江，則徐方為臬司，綜理其事，旋以憂去。
entries.en: Earlier, Governor-General Tao Shu had proposed dredging the Three Rivers. Lin, then serving as judicial commissioner, had overseen the project, but soon left office to mourn.
entries.literal: Previously Governor-General Tao Shu had memorialized to dredge the Three Rivers; Lin was then judicial commissioner and managed the affair in general, but soon left on account of mourning.

entries.zh: 至是黃浦、吳淞工已竣，則徐力任未竟者，劉河工最要，撥帑十六萬五千有奇，白茆次要，官紳集捐十一萬兩，同時開濬，以工代賑。
entries.en: By then work on the Huangpu and Wusong channels was complete, and Lin took charge of what remained. The Liu River was the priority, funded with more than 165,000 taels from the treasury; the Baimao River was secondary, with officials and local gentry contributing 110,000 taels. Both projects were dredged at once, with labor substituted for direct relief.
entries.literal: By this time the Huangpu and Wusong works were finished; Lin vigorously took on what remained unfinished. The Liu River project was most important: 165,000-odd taels were allocated from the treasury; the Baimao project was secondary, with officials and gentry raising 110,000 taels in donations; both were dredged at the same time, using labor in place of relief.

entries.zh: 兩河舊皆通海，易淤，且鑿河工鉅，改為清水長河，與黃埔、吳淞交匯通流。
entries.en: Both rivers had originally reached the sea, which made them prone to silting and entailed enormous dredging costs. They were therefore converted into long freshwater channels that fed into the Huangpu and Wusong.
entries.literal: Both rivers had formerly connected to the sea, silted easily, and required enormous dredging costs; they were changed into long freshwater channels that joined and flowed together with the Huangpu and Wusong.

entries.zh: 各於近海修閘建壩，潮汐泥沙不能壅入，內河漲，則由壩洩出歸海。
entries.en: Sluices and dams were built near the coast so that tidal mud and sand could not choke the channels; when the inland rivers swelled, the excess water was discharged through the dams back to the sea.
entries.literal: At each place near the sea sluices and dams were built so that tidal mud and sand could not be blocked in; when the inner rivers rose, water was released through the dams back to the sea.

entries.zh: 复就原河逢灣取直​​，節省工費三萬餘兩，用濬附近劉河之七浦河，及附近白茆之徐六涇、東西護塘諸河。
entries.en: Straightening the old river bends saved more than 30,000 taels, which was applied to dredging the Qipu River near the Liu River and the Xu Liujing and East and West Hutang channels near Baimao.
entries.literal: Further, where the original rivers bent, straight cuts were made, saving more than 30,000 taels in construction costs, which were used to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River, and the Xu Liujing, East and West Hutang, and other rivers near Baimao.

entries.zh: 又濬丹徒、丹陽運河，寶帶橋泖淀諸工，以次興舉，為吳中數十年之利。
entries.en: He also dredged the canals at Dantu and Danyang and the works at Baodai Bridge and Maodian, launching these projects in turn and securing benefits for the Wu region that would last for decades.
entries.literal: He also dredged the Dantu and Danyang canals, the Baodai Bridge and Maodian works, and other projects undertaken in sequence, bringing decades of benefit to the Wu region.

entries.zh: 兩署兩江總督。
entries.en: He twice served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
entries.literal: He twice served as acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.

entries.zh: 十七年，擢湖廣總督。
entries.en: In 1837 he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of Huguang.

entries.zh: 荊、襄歲罹水災，大修堤工，其患遂弭。
entries.en: The Jing and Xiang regions had suffered flooding year after year; he launched major dike repairs, and the disaster was finally brought under control.
entries.literal: Jing and Xiang suffered flood disasters year after year; he undertook major dike works, and the calamity was then abated.

entries.zh: 整頓鹽課，以減價敵私無成效，專嚴緝私之禁，銷數大增。
entries.en: He reformed the salt tax. Cutting official prices to undercut smugglers had failed, so he concentrated on enforcing the ban on illicit trade, and legal sales rose sharply.
entries.literal: He reorganized the salt tax: lowering prices to compete with smuggling had no effect, so he focused on strictly enforcing the ban on smuggling, and sales increased greatly.

entries.zh: 湖南鎮筸兵悍，數肇釁，巡閱撫馭，密薦總兵楊芳，擢為提督，移駐辰州，慎固苗疆屯防。
entries.en: The garrison at Zhenqian in Hunan was unruly and had repeatedly stirred up trouble. Lin toured the region, restored discipline, and privately recommended Brigade Commander Yang Fang for promotion to provincial commander with headquarters at Chenzhou, tightening the defenses of the Miao frontier.
entries.literal: The troops of Zhenqian in Hunan were fierce and repeatedly provoked disturbances; he toured and inspected, pacified and controlled them, secretly recommended Brigade Commander Yang Fang, promoted him to Provincial Commander, moved his headquarters to Chenzhou, and carefully strengthened the garrison defenses of the Miao frontier.

entries.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請禁鴉片煙，下中外大臣議。
entries.en: In 1838 Huang Juezi, grand secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial, memorialized for a ban on opium, and the throne ordered ministers throughout the empire to discuss the proposal.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year Grand Secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial Huang Juezi requested a ban on opium, and the matter was referred for discussion to ministers at home and abroad.

entries.zh: 則徐請用重典，言：「此禍不除，十年之後，不惟無可籌之餉，且無可用之兵。」
entries.en: Lin called for harsh penalties, writing: 'Unless this scourge is uprooted, within ten years the state will lack not only funds to levy, but soldiers fit to fight.'
entries.literal: Lin requested the use of severe penalties, saying: 'If this calamity is not removed, within ten years there will be not only no revenue that can be raised, but also no troops that can be used.'

entries.zh: 宣宗深韙之，命入覲，召對十九次。
entries.en: The Daoguang Emperor strongly agreed, summoned him to court, and conferred with him privately nineteen times.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved this, ordered him to come to audience, and summoned him for nineteen private interviews.

entries.zh: 授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦，十九年春，至。
entries.en: He was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to conduct the investigation. He arrived there in the spring of 1839.
entries.literal: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter; in the spring of the nineteenth year he arrived.

entries.zh: 總督鄧廷楨已嚴申禁令，捕拏煙犯，洋商查頓先避回國。
entries.en: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already tightened enforcement of the ban and arrested opium offenders; the merchant Jardine had already fled home.
entries.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already strictly proclaimed the prohibition, arrested opium offenders, and the foreign merchant Dent had already fled back to his country.

entries.zh: 則徐知水師提督關天培忠勇可用，令整兵嚴備。
entries.en: Lin judged Naval Commander Guan Tianpei loyal and capable, and ordered him to ready the fleet and tighten defenses.
entries.literal: Lin knew that Naval Commander Guan Tianpei was loyal and brave and could be relied upon; he ordered him to ready the troops and make strict preparations.

entries.zh: 檄諭英國領事義律查繳煙土，驅逐躉船，呈出煙土二萬餘箱，親蒞虎門驗收，焚於海濱，四十餘日始盡。
entries.en: He ordered British consul Charles Elliot to surrender all opium and expel the receiving ships. More than 20,000 chests were turned over; Lin personally supervised their receipt at Humen and had them burned on the shore, a process that took more than forty days to complete.
entries.literal: He issued a proclamation instructing British Consul Elliot to investigate and surrender opium, expel the receiving ships, and present more than 20,000 chests of opium; he personally went to Humen to inspect the receipt, and it was burned on the seashore, taking more than forty days to finish.

entries.zh: 請定洋商夾帶鴉片罪名，依化外有犯之例，人即正法，貨物入官，責具甘結。
entries.en: He proposed fixed penalties for foreign merchants caught smuggling opium: under the law governing foreigners who commit crimes, the offender would be executed, the goods confiscated, and a written pledge of compliance required.
entries.literal: He requested that the crime of foreign merchants smuggling opium be fixed according to the precedent for offenses by foreigners: the person would be executed immediately, goods confiscated by the state, and a written bond of compliance required.

entries.zh: 他國皆聽命，獨義律枝梧未從。
entries.en: Merchants of other nations complied, but Elliot alone stalled and refused.
entries.literal: Other countries all obeyed; only Elliot prevaricated and did not comply.

entries.zh: 於是閱視沿海砲台，以虎門為第一門戶，橫檔山、武山為第二門戶，大小虎山為第三門戶。
entries.en: He then inspected the coastal fortifications, treating Humen as the outer gate, Hengdang and Wushan as the second line, and Great and Little Tiger Mountains as the third.
entries.literal: Thereupon he inspected the coastal fortifications, taking Humen as the first gateway, Hengdang Mountain and Wushan as the second gateway, and Great and Little Tiger Mountains as the third gateway.

entries.zh: 海道至橫檔分為二支，右多暗沙，左經武山前，水深，洋船由之出入。
entries.en: At Hengdang the channel split in two: the right branch was riddled with hidden shoals, while the left, passing Wushan, was deep enough for foreign ships to use.
entries.literal: The sea route divided into two branches at Hengdang: the right had many hidden sandbars, while the left passed before Wushan, where the water was deep, and foreign ships entered and exited by it.

entries.zh: 關天培創議於此設木排鐵練二重，又增築虎門之河角砲台，英國商船後至者不敢入。
entries.en: Guan Tianpei proposed installing two layers of chained timber booms there and building the Hejiao battery at Humen. British merchant ships that arrived afterward did not dare enter.
entries.literal: Guan Tianpei originated the proposal to set up double layers of chained floating barriers here, and also added the Hejiao fort at Humen; later-arriving British merchant ships did not dare enter.

entries.zh: 義律請令赴澳門載貨，冀囤煙私販，嚴斥拒之，潛泊尖沙嘴外洋。
entries.en: Elliot asked to be allowed to load cargo at Macao, evidently intending to stockpile opium for illicit sale. Lin refused him sharply, and Elliot lay at anchor secretly off Chunshui Tsui.
entries.literal: Elliot requested permission to go to Macao to load cargo, hoping to hoard opium for private sale; Lin sternly rejected this, and Elliot secretly anchored in the outer waters off Chunshui Tsui.

entries.zh: 會有英人毆斃華民，抗不交犯，遂斷其食物，撤買辦、工人以困之。
entries.en: When a British subject beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the culprit, Lin cut off their supplies and withdrew purchasing agents and workers to isolate them.
entries.literal: It happened that a Briton beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the offender; Lin therefore cut off their food supplies and withdrew purchasing agents and laborers to press them.

entries.zh: 七月，義律藉索食為名，以貨船載兵犯九龍山砲台，參將賴恩爵擊走之。
entries.en: In the seventh month Elliot, claiming he needed provisions, sent merchant ships carrying troops against the Kowloon Hill battery. Assistant Commander Lai Enjue repulsed them.
entries.literal: In the seventh month Elliot, under the pretext of seeking food, used merchant ships to carry troops and attacked the Kowloon Hill battery; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue drove them off.

entries.zh: 疏聞，帝喜悅，報曰：「既有此舉，不可再示柔弱。
entries.en: When Lin's report reached the throne, the emperor was pleased and replied: 'Now that this stand has been taken, you must not show weakness again.
entries.literal: When the memorial was received, the Emperor was pleased and replied: 'Since this action has been taken, weakness must not be shown again.

entries.zh: 不患卿等孟浪，但戒卿等畏葸。」
entries.en: I am not afraid you will be too bold; I warn you only against being timid.'
entries.literal: I do not worry that you are rash, but only warn you against timidity.'

entries.zh: 御史步際桐言出結徒虛文，則徐以彼國重然諾，不肯出結，愈不能不向索取，持之益堅。
entries.en: Censor Bu Jitong argued that demanding written pledges was mere empty form. Lin replied that since the British prized their word, their refusal to sign made the demand all the more necessary, and he held his ground more firmly.
entries.literal: Censor Bu Jitong said that requiring written bonds was empty formality; Lin argued that since that country valued keeping promises, their refusal to give bonds made it all the more necessary to demand them, and he held his position more firmly.

entries.zh: 尋義律浼澳門洋酋轉圜，原令載煙之船回國，貨船聽官查驗。
entries.en: Elliot soon asked the foreign chief at Macao to mediate, agreeing that opium ships would return home while cargo vessels would submit to official inspection.
entries.literal: Soon Elliot asked the foreign chief at Macao to mediate; he originally ordered the opium-carrying ships to return home, while cargo ships were to submit to official inspection.

entries.zh: 九月，商船已具結進口，義律遣兵船阻之，開砲來攻，關天培率游擊麥廷章奮擊敗之。
entries.en: In the ninth month merchant ships that had signed bonds were entering port when Elliot sent warships to block them and opened fire. Guan Tianpei, with Battalion Commander Mai Tingzhang, fought back vigorously and routed them.
entries.literal: In the ninth month merchant ships had already signed bonds and entered port; Elliot sent warships to block them, opened fire and attacked, and Guan Tianpei led Battalion Commander Mai Tingzhang in a fierce counterattack and defeated them.

entries.zh: 十月，又犯虎門官湧，官軍分五路進攻，六戰皆捷。
entries.en: In the tenth month the British attacked Guanyong at Humen again. Government forces advanced in five columns and won six successive engagements.
entries.literal: In the tenth month they again attacked Guanyong at Humen; the government forces advanced in five columns and won victory in six engagements.

entries.zh: 詔停止貿易，宣示罪狀，飭福建、浙江、江蘇嚴防海口。
entries.en: An edict halted trade with Britain, published a list of its offenses, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to tighten coastal defenses.
entries.literal: An edict halted trade, proclaimed their offenses, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to strictly guard their sea ports.

entries.zh: 先已授則徐兩江總督，至是調補兩廣。
entries.en: Lin had already been appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs; he was now transferred to the Two Guang.
entries.literal: Lin had already been appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiangs; now he was transferred to fill the Two Guang posts.

entries.zh: 府尹曾望顏請罷各國通商，禁漁船出洋。
entries.en: Prefect Zeng Wangyan proposed cutting off trade with all nations and banning fishing boats from going to sea.
entries.literal: Prefect Zeng Wangyan requested that trade with all countries be stopped and fishing boats forbidden to go to sea.

entries.zh: 則徐疏言：「自斷英國貿易，他國喜，此盈彼絀，正可以夷制夷。
entries.en: Lin memorialized: 'Since we have cut off trade with Britain, the other nations are pleased. One side gains what the other loses—this is precisely the moment to play foreign powers against one another.
entries.literal: Lin submitted a memorial saying: 'Since trade with Britain has been cut off, other countries are pleased; where one gains, the other loses—this is exactly how barbarians may be used to control barbarians.

entries.zh: 如概與之絕，轉恐聯爲一氣。
entries.en: If we break with them all indiscriminately, we may drive them to unite against us.
entries.literal: If we cut off relations with all of them indiscriminately, I fear they may instead unite as one force.

entries.zh: 粵民以海為生，概禁出洋，其勢不可終日。」
entries.en: The people of Guangdong live from the sea; a total ban on going to sea could not be sustained for long.'
entries.literal: The people of Guangdong live by the sea; to forbid going to sea altogether is a policy that cannot last a single day.'

entries.zh: 時英船寄椗外洋，以利誘奸民接濟銷菸。
entries.en: Meanwhile British ships lay at anchor off Lintin, using profit to lure local collaborators into supplying them and selling opium.
entries.literal: At this time British ships lay at anchor in the outer waters off Lintin, using profit to entice traitorous locals to supply them and sell opium.

entries.zh: 二十年春，令關天培密裝砲械，僱漁船疍戶出洋設伏，候夜順風縱火，焚毀附夷匪船，接濟始斷。
entries.en: In the spring of 1840 he ordered Guan Tianpei to secretly arm boats, hire fishing vessels and Tanka boatmen for an ambush at sea, and on a favorable night set fire to the collaborators' supply ships. Only then was the illicit traffic cut off.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he ordered Guan Tianpei secretly to equip cannon and arms, hire fishing boats and Tanka boat people to go to sea and set an ambush, wait for a favorable night wind to set fire, burn and destroy the traitorous boats attached to the foreigners, and only then was supply cut off.

entries.zh: 五月，再焚夷船於磨刀洋。
entries.en: In the fifth month he burned more foreign ships at Modaoyang.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he again burned foreign ships at Modaoyang.

entries.zh: 諜知新來敵船揚帆北鄉，疏請沿海各省戒嚴。
entries.en: Intelligence reported that newly arrived enemy ships had sailed north, and he memorialized for coastal provinces to go on alert.
entries.literal: Spies learned that newly arrived enemy ships had set sail northward; he memorialized requesting that coastal provinces be placed on alert.

entries.zh: 又言夷情詭譎，若迳赴天津求通貿易，請優示懷柔，依嘉慶年間成例，將遞詞人由內地送粵。
entries.en: He also warned that the foreigners were cunning and unpredictable: if they sailed straight to Tianjin to demand trade, he asked that they be treated with deliberate courtesy and, following the Jiaqing precedent, that their envoys be escorted overland to Guangdong.
entries.literal: He also said that foreign temperament was deceitful and treacherous; if they went directly to Tianjin seeking trade, he requested that gentle conciliation be shown and that, following the precedent of the Jiaqing period, the petitioners be escorted overland from the interior to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 六月，英船至廈門，為閩浙總督鄧廷楨所拒。
entries.en: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were turned back by Governor-General Deng Tingzhen of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were repelled by Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Deng Tingzhen.

entries.zh: 其犯浙者陷定海，掠寧波。
entries.en: Those that struck Zhejiang captured Dinghai and raided Ningbo.
entries.literal: Those that invaded Zhejiang captured Dinghai and plundered Ningbo.

entries.zh: 則徐上疏自請治罪，密陳兵事不可中止，略曰：「英夷所憾在粵而滋擾於浙，雖變動出於意外，其窮蹙實在意中。
entries.en: Lin memorialized asking to be punished and privately argued that the war must not be stopped. In summary he wrote: 'The British grievance began in Guangdong, yet they are now spreading trouble into Zhejiang. The turn of events may be unexpected, but their desperation is not.
entries.literal: Lin submitted a memorial requesting punishment for himself and secretly stated that military operations must not be halted, saying in summary: 'The grievance of the English barbarians lies in Guangdong, yet they are spreading disturbance in Zhejiang; although the change was unexpected, their desperation was actually within expectation.

entries.zh: 惟其虛憍性成，愈窮蹙時，愈欲顯其桀驁，試其恫喝，甚且別生秘計，冀售其奸；
entries.en: Arrogance is bred in them; the more cornered they become, the more they wish to show defiance, test our resolve with threats, and even hatch secret schemes to advance their designs;
entries.literal: Only because their arrogant and empty nature is ingrained, the more desperate they become the more they wish to display their defiance, test their intimidation, and even devise secret schemes hoping to carry out their treachery;

entries.zh: 一切不得行，仍必帖耳俯伏。
entries.en: but when none of this succeeds, they will still have to submit in the end.
entries.literal: when none of this succeeds, they will still inevitably submit with bowed ears.

entries.zh: 第恐議者以為內地船砲非外夷之敵，與其曠日持久，不如設法羈縻。
entries.en: My fear is that some advisers will say our ships and guns cannot match the foreigners, and that rather than fight a protracted war we should seek to appease them.
entries.literal: I only fear that those in council may think that the ships and cannon of the interior are no match for the foreign barbarians, and that rather than prolong matters day after day, it would be better to devise means of restraint and conciliation.

entries.zh: 抑知夷情無厭，得步進步，威不能克，患無已時。
entries.en: Yet the foreigners are insatiable: yield an inch and they take a mile. If force fails to check them, the trouble will never end.
entries.literal: Yet know that barbarian temperament knows no satiety; give them an inch and they take a mile—if authority cannot overcome them, calamity will have no end.

entries.zh: 他國紛紛效尤，不可不慮。」
entries.en: Other nations will follow their example one after another, and that danger cannot be ignored.'
entries.literal: Other countries will one after another follow suit; this cannot be left unconsidered.'

entries.zh: 因請戴罪赴浙，隨營自效。
entries.en: He therefore asked to go to Zhejiang at his own disgrace and serve with the army there.
entries.literal: He therefore requested to go to Zhejiang bearing guilt and serve in the camps to redeem himself.

entries.zh: 七月，義律至天津，投書總督琦善，言廣東燒煙之釁，起自則徐及鄧廷楨二人，索價不與，又遭詬逐，故越境呈訴。
entries.en: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and wrote to Governor Qishan, blaming Lin and Deng Tingzhen for the Guangdong opium burning, claiming they had refused compensation and driven him out, and had therefore come north to petition.
entries.literal: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and sent a letter to Governor Qishan, saying that the provocation of burning opium in Guangdong originated with Lin and Deng Tingzhen; they would not agree to compensation and moreover subjected him to abuse and expulsion, so he crossed the border to lodge his complaint.

entries.zh: 琦善據以上聞，上意始動。
entries.en: Qishan reported this to the throne, and the emperor's resolve began to falter.
entries.literal: Qishan reported this upward, and the Emperor's mind began to waver.

entries.zh: 時英船在粵窺伺，复連敗之蓮花峰下及龍穴洲。
entries.en: Meanwhile British ships were lurking off Guangdong, and Lin defeated them again below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.
entries.literal: At this time British ships were watching and waiting in Guangdong; he again defeated them in succession below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.

entries.zh: 捷書未上，九月，詔曰：「鴉片流毒內地，特遣林則徐會同鄧廷楨查辦，原期肅清內地，斷絕來源，隨地隨時，妥為辦理。
entries.en: Before the victory report reached court, an edict issued in the ninth month declared: 'Opium poisons the empire. Lin Zexu was specially dispatched with Deng Tingzhen to eradicate it at home and cut off its source, handling the matter properly as circumstances required.
entries.literal: Before the victory report was submitted, in the ninth month an edict said: 'Opium poisons the interior; Lin Zexu was specially dispatched together with Deng Tingzhen to investigate and handle the matter, originally expecting to purge the interior and cut off the source, handling it properly according to place and time.

entries.zh: 乃自查辦以來，內而奸民犯法不能淨盡，外而興販來源並未斷絕，沿海各省紛紛徵調，糜餉勞師，皆林則徐等辦理不善之所致。」
entries.en: Yet since the campaign began, smugglers at home have not been fully suppressed, the source abroad has not been severed, and coastal provinces have been mobilized at great cost in funds and manpower—all because Lin Zexu and his colleagues handled the affair badly.'
entries.literal: Yet since the investigation began, within, law-breaking traitors have not been entirely eliminated; without, the source of trafficking has not been cut off; coastal provinces have been repeatedly mobilized, wasting funds and exhausting the army—all caused by the poor handling of Lin Zexu and others.'

entries.zh: 下則徐等嚴議，飭即來京，以琦善代之。
entries.en: Lin and the others were referred for severe punishment, ordered to come at once to the capital, and Qishan was appointed in Lin's place.
entries.literal: Lin and the others were referred for severe deliberation, ordered to come immediately to the capital, and Qishan was appointed to replace them.

entries.zh: 尋議革職，命仍回廣東備查問差委。
entries.en: He was soon stripped of office and ordered back to Guangdong to await inquiry and further assignment.
entries.literal: Soon it was decided to dismiss him from office, and he was ordered to return to Guangdong to await investigation and assignment of duties.

entries.zh: 琦善至，義律要求賠償煙價，廈門、福州開埠通商，上怒，復命備戰。
entries.en: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the destroyed opium and the opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade. The emperor was enraged and ordered war preparations resumed.
entries.literal: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the opium, and the opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade; the Emperor was angered and again ordered preparations for war.

entries.zh: 二十一年春，予則徐四品卿銜，赴浙江鎮海協防。
entries.en: In the spring of 1841 Lin was given fourth-rank court officer status and sent to Zhejiang to help defend Zhenhai.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year Lin was granted the rank of fourth-grade Court Officer and sent to Zhejiang to assist in the defense of Zhenhai.

entries.zh: 時琦善雖以擅與香港逮治，和戰仍無定局。
entries.en: By then Qishan had been arrested for ceding Hong Kong on his own authority, but whether to make peace or continue the war remained unsettled.
entries.literal: At this time, although Qishan had been arrested and punished for independently ceding Hong Kong, peace and war still had no fixed outcome.

entries.zh: 五月，詔斥則徐在粵不能德威並用，褫卿銜，遣戍伊犁。
entries.en: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Lin for failing to combine persuasion and force in Guangdong, stripped him of his court rank, and banished him to Yili.
entries.literal: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Lin for failing to combine virtue and authority in Guangdong, stripped him of his Court Officer rank, and sent him into exile at Yili.

entries.zh: 會河決開封，中途奉命襄辦塞決，二十二年，工竣，仍赴戍，而浙江、江南師屢敗。
entries.en: The Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng, and en route he was ordered to help seal the breach. When the work was finished in 1842 he resumed his journey into exile, even as imperial forces in Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered defeat after defeat.
entries.literal: It happened that the Yellow River broke its banks at Kaifeng; en route he was ordered to assist in blocking the breach; in the twenty-second year the work was finished and he still went to exile, while the armies of Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered repeated defeats.

entries.zh: 是年秋，和議遂成。
entries.en: That autumn peace was concluded.
entries.literal: That autumn peace negotiations were concluded.

entries.zh: 二十四年，新疆興治屯田，將軍布彥泰請以則徐綜其事。
entries.en: In 1844 colonization projects were launched in Xinjiang, and General Buyantai asked that Lin oversee them.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year military colonization was undertaken in Xinjiang; General Buyantai requested that Lin oversee the affair in general.

entries.zh: 週曆南八城，濬水源，闢溝渠，墾田三萬七千餘頃，請給回民耕種，改屯兵為操防，如議行。
entries.en: He toured the eight southern cities, opened water sources, dug canals, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of land. He proposed assigning the fields to Hui farmers for cultivation and converting garrison troops to drill-and-defense duty, and the plan was adopted.
entries.literal: He toured the eight southern cities, dredged water sources, opened canals and ditches, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of fields; he requested that these be given to Hui people to cultivate, and that garrison troops be changed to drill-and-defense duty; this was carried out as proposed.

entries.zh: 二十五年，召還，以四五品京堂候補。
entries.en: In 1845 he was recalled to serve as a fourth- or fifth-rank capital official awaiting appointment.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled and appointed as a fourth- or fifth-grade capital official awaiting assignment.

entries.zh: 尋署陝甘總督。
entries.en: He soon served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.

entries.zh: 二十六年，授陝西巡撫，留甘肅，偕布彥泰治叛番，擒其酋。
entries.en: In 1846 he was appointed governor of Shaanxi but remained in Gansu, where he and Buyantai suppressed rebellious tribes and captured their leader.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Governor of Shaanxi, remained in Gansu, and together with Buyantai pacified rebellious tribes, capturing their chieftain.

entries.zh: 二十七年，授雲貴總督。
entries.en: In 1847 he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 雲南漢、回互鬥焚殺，歷十數年。
entries.en: In Yunnan, Han and Hui communities had been fighting, burning, and killing one another for more than a decade.
entries.literal: In Yunnan Han and Hui had mutually fought, burned, and killed for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 會保山回民控於京，漢民奪犯，毀官署，拆瀾滄江橋以拒，鎮道不能制。
entries.en: When Hui petitioners from Baoshan appealed in the capital, local Han seized the prisoners, wrecked the yamen, and tore down the Lancang River bridge to block pursuit. The regional officials could not restore order.
entries.literal: It happened that Hui people of Baoshan petitioned in the capital; Han people seized the prisoners, destroyed the government offices, and dismantled the Lancang River bridge to resist, and the military and civil officials could not control them.

entries.zh: 則徐主止分良莠，不分漢、回。
entries.en: Lin held that officials should distinguish the good from the bad, not Han from Hui.
entries.literal: Lin maintained that one should distinguish only good from bad, not Han from Hui.

entries.zh: 二十八年，親督師往剿，途中聞彌渡客回滋亂，移兵破其巢，殲匪數百。
entries.en: In 1848 he personally led an expedition against the rebels. En route he learned that guest Hui in Midu had risen in revolt, diverted his forces to destroy their stronghold, and killed several hundred insurgents.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he personally led troops to suppress the rebels; en route he heard that guest Hui in Midu were stirring up disorder, shifted his forces to destroy their lair, and killed several hundred bandits.

entries.zh: 保山民聞風股栗，縛犯迎師，誅其首要，散其脅從，召漢、回父老諭以恩信。
entries.en: The people of Baoshan were terrified into submission: they bound up the culprits and welcomed his army, executed the ringleaders, released those who had been coerced, and gathered Han and Hui elders to hear his assurances of clemency.
entries.literal: The people of Baoshan trembled at the news, bound up the offenders and welcomed the army, executed the ringleaders, dispersed their coerced followers, and summoned Han and Hui elders to instruct them in grace and trust.

entries.zh: 遂搜捕永昌、順寧、雲州、姚州歷年戕官諸重犯，威德震洽，邊境乃安。
entries.en: He then hunted down major offenders in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who had murdered officials over the years. His authority and magnanimity restored calm to the frontier.
entries.literal: Thereupon he searched out and arrested major offenders in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who over the years had killed officials; his authority and virtue spread in harmony, and the frontier was then pacified.

entries.zh: 加太子太保，賜花翎。
entries.en: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the peacock feather.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 二十九年，騰越邊外野夷滋擾，遣兵平之。
entries.en: In 1849 tribes beyond the Tengyue frontier stirred up trouble, and he sent troops to suppress them.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year wild tribes beyond the Tengyue frontier caused repeated disturbances; he dispatched troops and pacified them.

entries.zh: 以病乞歸。
entries.en: He asked to retire on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: On grounds of illness he requested to return home.

entries.zh: 逾年，文宗嗣位，疊詔宣召，未至，以廣西逆首洪秀全稔亂，授欽差大臣，督師進剿，並署廣西巡撫。
entries.en: The next year, after Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the throne, repeated summons reached him, but before he could arrive Hong Xiuquan had long been in rebellion in Guangxi. Lin was appointed imperial commissioner to lead a punitive expedition and also served as acting governor of Guangxi.
entries.literal: The following year Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the throne and repeatedly issued edicts summoning him; before he arrived, because the rebel leader Hong Xiuquan in Guangxi had long been in rebellion, he was appointed Imperial Commissioner to lead troops in suppression and also served as acting Governor of Guangxi.

entries.zh: 行次潮州，病卒。
entries.en: He fell ill and died at Chaozhou on the march.
entries.literal: En route, at Chaozhou, he died of illness.

entries.zh: 則徐威惠久著南服，賊聞其出，皆震悚，中道遽歿，天下惜之。
entries.en: Lin's authority and benevolence had long been famed in the south, and the rebels were terrified when they heard he was coming. His sudden death on the road was mourned throughout the empire.
entries.literal: Lin's authority and kindness had long been renowned in the south; when the rebels heard he was coming out, all were shaken with fear, but he died suddenly en route, and the whole realm mourned him.

entries.zh: 遺疏上，優詔賜卹，贈太子太傅，諡文忠。
entries.en: When his final memorial reached the throne, the emperor granted generous posthumous honors, made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong.
entries.literal: His final memorial was submitted; a gracious edict granted posthumous honors, conferred the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and gave the posthumous name Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 雲南、江蘇並祀名宦，陝西請建專祠。
entries.en: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among eminent local officials, and Shaanxi petitioned for a temple in his honor.
entries.literal: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among distinguished officials, and Shaanxi requested a dedicated temple be built.

entries.zh: 則徐才識過人，而待下虛衷，人樂為用，所蒞治績皆卓越。
entries.en: Lin's talent and judgment were exceptional, yet he treated subordinates with genuine openness, and men were eager to serve him. Every post he held yielded outstanding results.
entries.literal: Lin's talent and insight surpassed others, yet he treated subordinates with open sincerity; people were glad to serve him, and every office he held produced outstanding results.

entries.zh: 道光之季，東南困於漕運，宣宗密詢利弊，疏陳補救本原諸策，上畿輔水利議，文宗欲命籌辦而未果。
entries.en: In the late Daoguang era the southeast was crippled by the grain-transport system. When the emperor privately asked about remedies, Lin memorialized on fundamental reforms and submitted a plan for waterworks in the capital region. Emperor Wenzong intended to put him in charge, but the plan never came to fruition.
entries.literal: In the late Daoguang period the southeast was distressed by grain transport; Emperor Xuanzong privately inquired about advantages and disadvantages, and Lin submitted memorials setting forth fundamental remedial policies and presented a plan for water conservancy in the capital region; Emperor Wenzong wished to appoint him to organize it but the plan was not realized.

entries.zh: 海疆事起，時以英吉利最強為憂，則徐獨曰：「為中國患者，其俄羅斯乎！」
entries.en: When trouble on the coast began, most feared Britain above all. Lin alone said: 'The power that will truly threaten China—is it not Russia?'
entries.literal: When the maritime crisis arose, the age worried that England was strongest; Lin alone said: 'The one that will afflict China—is it not Russia?'

entries.zh: 後其言果驗。
entries.en: Time would prove him right.
entries.literal: Later his words indeed proved true.

entries.zh: 鄧廷楨，字嶰筠，江蘇江寧人。
entries.en: Deng Tingzhen, styled Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Deng Tingzhen, style name Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1801 he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.

entries.zh: 屢分校鄉、會試，稱得士。
entries.en: He served repeatedly as an examiner for provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for recognizing talent.
entries.literal: He repeatedly served on boards for provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for selecting worthy scholars.

entries.zh: 十五年，授台灣遺缺知府，浙江巡撫蔣攸銛請留浙，補寧波。
entries.en: In 1810 he was appointed prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan, but Governor Jiang Youqian of Zhejiang asked that he remain in the province, and he was posted to Ningbo.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan; Governor of Zhejiang Jiang Youqian requested that he remain in Zhejiang and he was appointed to Ningbo.

entries.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補陝西延安府，歷榆林、西安，以善折獄稱。
entries.en: After mourning his mother he was assigned to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, later served in Yulin and Xi'an, and won renown for his skill in adjudicating cases.
entries.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, served in Yulin and Xi'an, and was known for skill in resolving legal cases.

entries.zh: 平反韓城、南鄭冤獄，又全同州嫠婦母子，陝民歌頌，傳播京師。
entries.en: He overturned wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng and saved a widow and her son in Tongzhou from injustice. The people of Shaanxi praised him, and word of his deeds reached the capital.
entries.literal: He reversed wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng, and also preserved the lives of a widow and her son in Tongzhou; the people of Shaanxi sang his praises, and the story spread to the capital.

entries.zh: 二十五年，超擢湖北按察使，權布政使。
entries.en: In 1820 he was promoted ahead of schedule to judicial commissioner of Hubei and acted as financial commissioner.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted by special selection to Judicial Commissioner of Hubei and served as acting Financial Commissioner.

entries.zh: 沿江民田歷年沈沒，而賦額仍在，為民累，悉請免之。
entries.en: Farmland along the river had been flooded for years while tax quotas remained unchanged, burdening the people. He memorialized for full remission.
entries.literal: Farmland along the river had been submerged year after year, yet the tax quota remained, burdening the people; he requested that all such taxes be remitted.

entries.zh: 道光元年，遷江西布政使。
entries.en: In 1821 he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 以前在西安失察渭南令故出縣民柳全璧殺人罪，罣誤，奪職。
entries.en: He was stripped of office for having failed, while serving in Xi'an, to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released a county man named Liu Quanbi from a murder charge.
entries.literal: Because while in Xi'an he had failed to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released the county man Liu Quanbi from a murder charge, he was implicated in error and dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 議戍軍台，宣宗知其無私，特免遣戍，予七品銜，發直隸委用。
entries.en: Although exile to a garrison post was proposed, Emperor Xuanzong knew he had acted without private motive and specially exempted him from banishment, gave him seventh-rank status, and assigned him to service in Zhili.
entries.literal: It was proposed that he be sent to garrison duty; Emperor Xuanzong knew he had no private guilt and specially exempted him from exile, granted him seventh-rank status, and assigned him for service in Zhili.

entries.zh: 尋授通永道。
entries.en: He was soon appointed intendant of the Tongyong Circuit.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Tongyong Circuit.

entries.zh: 四年，擢陝西按察使，遷布政使。
entries.en: In 1824 he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Shaanxi and then to financial commissioner.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi and transferred to Financial Commissioner.

entries.zh: 六年，擢安徽巡撫。
entries.en: In 1826 he was promoted to governor of Anhui.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Governor of Anhui.

entries.zh: 自嘉慶時，安徽多大獄，鳳、潁兩郡俗尤悍，常以兵定，責繳兵械，私藏尚多。
entries.en: Since the Jiaqing era Anhui had been plagued by major cases. Feng and Ying prefectures were especially unruly, and troops had often been needed to restore order. Although weapons were ordered surrendered, many remained hidden.
entries.literal: Since the Jiaqing period Anhui had seen many major cases; the customs of Feng and Ying prefectures were especially fierce, and order was often restored by force; they were ordered to surrender weapons, yet many were still hidden in private hands.

entries.zh: 廷楨乃立限，責成保長，逾限及私造者置之法。
entries.en: Deng set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible for compliance, and punished anyone who missed it or manufactured weapons in secret.
entries.literal: Deng then set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible, and punished those who exceeded the deadline or manufactured weapons privately.

entries.zh: 任吏皆得人，刁悍之風稍戢。
entries.en: He appointed capable officials at every level, and the region's lawless temper gradually eased.
entries.literal: The officials he appointed were all capable men, and the fierce and unruly atmosphere gradually subsided.

entries.zh: 舊例，潁州屬三人以上凶器傷人者，極邊煙瘴充軍，僉妻發配。
entries.en: Under old regulations, when three or more persons in Yingzhou wounded someone with a lethal weapon, the offenders were exiled to the farthest malarial frontier and their wives were banished with them.
entries.literal: By old regulation, in cases under Yingzhou where three or more persons wounded others with lethal weapons, the offenders were sent to military exile in the farthest malarial frontier, and their wives were collectively sent into banishment.

entries.zh: 廷楨疏言：「悍俗誠宜重懲，婦女顧名節，多自殘求免，或自盡傷生，情在可矜，請停其例。」
entries.en: Deng memorialized: 'These violent customs deserve harsh punishment, but women mindful of their reputation often mutilate themselves to avoid banishment, or take their own lives. Their plight deserves compassion, and I ask that this regulation be suspended.'
entries.literal: Deng submitted a memorial saying: 'The fierce custom truly deserves severe punishment, but women, mindful of chastity, often mutilate themselves to seek exemption, or kill themselves and harm their lives; the circumstances deserve compassion—please suspend this regulation.'

entries.zh: 遇水災，親乘舟勘賑。
entries.en: When floods struck, he personally went out by boat to inspect the damage and direct relief.
entries.literal: When flood disasters occurred, he personally boarded a boat to inspect and provide relief.

entries.zh: 修復安豐塘、芍陂水門，濬鳳陽沫河，加築堤閘。
entries.en: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the Quepi sluice gates, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and strengthened dikes and floodgates.
entries.literal: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the sluice gates of Quepi, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and added dikes and sluices.

entries.zh: 嚴緝捕，屢獲劇盜。
entries.en: He tightened pursuit of criminals and repeatedly captured major bandits.
entries.literal: He strictly pursued arrests and repeatedly captured major bandits.

entries.zh: 以獲南河掘堤首犯陳端，詔嘉獎。
entries.en: He won imperial commendation for capturing Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach conspiracy.
entries.literal: Because he captured Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach case, an edict commended and rewarded him.

entries.zh: 治皖十載，政尚安靜，境內大和。
entries.en: He governed Anhui for ten years with a policy of quiet administration, and the province enjoyed broad peace.
entries.literal: He governed Anhui for ten years; his policy favored quiet governance, and within the province there was great harmony.

entries.zh: 十五年，擢兩廣總督。
entries.en: In 1835 he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guang.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guang.

entries.zh: 鴉片煙方盛行，漏銀出洋為大患。
entries.en: Opium was then rampant, and the drain of silver abroad had become a grave national problem.
entries.literal: Opium was then flourishing, and the outflow of silver overseas was a great calamity.

entries.zh: 十六年，英吉利商人以躉船載煙，廷楨禁止不許進口，猶泊外洋，嚴旨驅逐。
entries.en: In 1836 British merchants used receiving ships to store opium offshore. Deng barred import, but the ships remained at anchor in outer waters until stern edicts ordered them driven away.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year British merchants used receiving ships to carry opium; Deng forbade import, yet they still anchored in outer waters, and stern edicts ordered their expulsion.

entries.zh: 沿海奸民勾結，禁令猝難斷絕。
entries.en: Coastal collaborators kept the trade alive, and the ban could not be cut off overnight.
entries.literal: Traitorous locals along the coast colluded with them, and the prohibition could not be abruptly severed.

entries.zh: 廷楨與提督關天培整備海防，迭於大嶼山口、急水洋獲蟹艇，載銀鉅萬，盡數充賞，破獲囤煙私販。
entries.en: Deng and Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei strengthened coastal defenses, repeatedly seizing smuggling boats at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang laden with tens of thousands of taels of silver. The confiscated funds were distributed as rewards, and they broke up opium stockpiles and illicit trafficking rings.
entries.literal: Deng together with Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei prepared coastal defenses, repeatedly at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang captured smuggling boats carrying tens of thousands of taels of silver, confiscated all as reward funds, and broke up stockpiled opium and private trafficking.

entries.zh: 十八年，英船載屬番男婦五百餘人赴澳門居住，驅令回國。
entries.en: In 1838 British ships brought more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to settle at Macao. Deng ordered them sent home.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year British ships carried more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to live at Macao; he drove them to return to their country.

entries.zh: 詔下禁煙議，疏言：「法行於豪貴，則小民易從；
entries.en: When the throne ordered debate on banning opium, he memorialized: 'If the law is enforced first upon the powerful and well connected, ordinary people will follow more easily;
entries.literal: When the edict on the opium prohibition debate was issued, he submitted a memorial saying: 'If the law is enforced upon the powerful and noble, then common people will easily follow;

entries.zh: 令嚴於中土，則外貨自絀。」
entries.en: if the prohibition is strict within China itself, foreign opium will lose its market.'
entries.literal: if the prohibition is strict within the empire, then foreign goods will naturally diminish.'

entries.zh: 十九年，林則徐奉命至廣東，廷楨與之同心協力，盡獲躉船積煙，焚之，嚴私販之罪；
entries.en: In 1839 Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong on imperial orders. Deng worked with him in full concert, seized all opium stored on receiving ships and burned it, and imposed severe penalties on smugglers;
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangdong; Deng worked with him in full accord, seized all opium stockpiled on receiving ships, burned it, and strictly punished private trafficking;

entries.zh: 臨以兵威，屢戰皆捷，事詳則徐傳。
entries.en: backed the policy with military force and won repeated victories. The details are given in Lin's biography.
entries.literal: faced them with military force, and won victory in repeated battles—the details are given in Lin's biography.

entries.zh: 奸民因失業，遍騰蜚語。
entries.en: Smugglers who had lost their livelihood spread malicious rumors everywhere.
entries.literal: Traitorous locals, having lost their livelihoods, spread slander everywhere.

entries.zh: 廷楨疏陳，略曰：「臣緝懲鴉片，三載於茲。
entries.en: Deng memorialized in summary: 'I have pursued and punished the opium trade for three years now.
entries.literal: Deng submitted a memorial stating in summary: 'Your servant has pursued and punished opium for three years now.

entries.zh: 豪猾之徒，刑僇逋逃，身家既失，怨讟遂興。
entries.en: Powerful ruffians, punished and driven into flight, have lost their fortunes and now vent their resentment in slander.
entries.literal: Crafty and powerful men, punished and fleeing, having lost their families and property, then gave rise to resentment and slander.

entries.zh: 查檢為希旨，掩捕為貪功，偵伺為詭謀，推​​鞫為酷罰。
entries.en: Inspections are called currying favor; secret arrests, greed for credit; surveillance, conspiracy; and forced confessions, cruel punishment.
entries.literal: Inspections are called currying favor, secret arrests are called greed for merit, surveillance is called scheming, and interrogation under torture is called cruel punishment.

entries.zh: 誣以納賄，目以營私。
entries.en: They accuse us of taking bribes and pursuing private profit.
entries.literal: They falsely accuse us of taking bribes and label us as seeking private gain.

entries.zh: 譏建議為急於理財，訾新例為輕於改律，狂悖紛熒，無非為煙匪洩憤。」
entries.en: They mock the policy as a rush to raise revenue and denounce the new regulations as reckless changes to the law—all of it nothing but the opium traffickers venting their rage.'
entries.literal: They mock the proposal as haste to raise revenue, denounce the new regulations as lightly changing the law, and their wild and rebellious clamor is nothing but venting by opium criminals.'

entries.zh: 詔慰勉之。
entries.en: The throne replied with words of comfort and encouragement.
entries.literal: An edict comforted and encouraged him.

entries.zh: 調兩江、雲貴，皆未赴，閩防方急，遂調閩浙總督。
entries.en: He was transferred first to the Two Jiangs and then to Yunnan-Guizhou, but took neither post. With Fujian's defenses under pressure, he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Two Jiangs and to Yunnan-Guizhou, but went to neither; as Fujian's defenses were urgent, he was then transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 購洋砲十四運閩，以閩洋無內港，砲台建於海灘，沙浮不固，奏改為砲墩，囊沙堆築，外護以船。
entries.en: He purchased fourteen foreign cannon for Fujian. Because the Fujian coast lacked inner harbors and beach batteries rested on shifting sand, he proposed gun platforms built of sand-filled bags and shielded by boats.
entries.literal: He purchased fourteen foreign cannon and shipped them to Fujian; because Fujian's coast had no inner harbors and batteries built on the beach rested on shifting sand, he memorialized to change them into gun platforms, piled up with bagged sand and protected on the outside by boats.

entries.zh: 募水勇飾商船出洋巡緝。
entries.en: He recruited naval militia, fitted out merchant vessels, and sent them to sea on patrol.
entries.literal: He recruited naval fighters, fitted out merchant ships, and sent them to sea to patrol and suppress smuggling.

entries.zh: 二十年三月，英船窺廈門，遣提督程恩高等迎敵於梅林澳，擊走之。
entries.en: In the third month of 1840 British ships probed Xiamen. He sent Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet them at Meilin Bay and drive them off.
entries.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year British ships spied on Xiamen; he dispatched Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet the enemy at Meilin Bay and drive them off.

entries.zh: 奸民勾通出洋運煙，分責水陸師嚴緝，遇即攻擊，迭有殲擒。
entries.en: Local collaborators continued to carry opium out to sea. He assigned naval and land forces to pursue them relentlessly, attacking on sight and repeatedly killing or capturing offenders.
entries.literal: Traitorous locals colluded to transport opium to sea; he divided responsibility between naval and land forces for strict pursuit, attacked on sight, and repeatedly killed and captured offenders.

entries.zh: 六月，敵船駛入廈門，求通貿易，阻之，遂開砲，來撲砲台，參將陳勝元、守備陳光福奮擊，斃其前隊數人，發砲傷敵甚眾，乃遁。
entries.en: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen demanding trade. When refused, they opened fire and assaulted the batteries. Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought back fiercely, killing several in the enemy vanguard and wounding many more with cannon fire until the enemy withdrew.
entries.literal: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen seeking trade; blocked, they opened fire and came to assault the batteries; Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought fiercely, killed several in the enemy vanguard, fired cannon and wounded many of the enemy, and they then fled.

entries.zh: 其分犯浙洋者，陷定海，廷楨率師赴剿，行次清風嶺，詔以閩防緊要，止其赴浙，遂駐兵泉州，招募練勇。
entries.en: Other enemy ships that struck the Zhejiang coast captured Dinghai. Deng marched to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict halted his advance, citing the urgency of Fujian's defenses. He then stationed troops at Quanzhou and recruited militia.
entries.literal: Those that separately invaded the Zhejiang coast captured Dinghai; Deng led troops to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict, citing the urgency of Fujian's defenses, stopped his advance to Zhejiang; he then stationed troops at Quanzhou and recruited militia.

entries.zh: 疏言：「英船二十餘艘聚泊定海，內地師船恐難驟近，必改造堅大之船，多配砲火，間道而進，方能制勝。」
entries.en: He memorialized: 'More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai. Our coastal junks probably cannot close with them quickly. We must build stouter, larger vessels, arm them heavily, and advance by indirect routes if we are to prevail.'
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: 'More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai; inland war junks probably cannot quickly approach—they must be rebuilt into stout, large vessels, fitted with many guns and firepower, and advance by indirect routes before victory can be achieved.'

entries.zh: 九月，詔以廷楨等在粵辦理不善，轉滋事端，與林則徐同奪職。
entries.en: In the ninth month an edict blamed Deng and his colleagues for mishandling affairs in Guangdong and provoking further trouble. He was dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.
entries.literal: In the ninth month an edict stated that Deng and others had handled affairs poorly in Guangdong and instead stirred up trouble, and they were dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.

entries.zh: 二十一年，琦善撤沿海兵備，虎門失守，复追論廷楨久任兩廣，廢弛營務，與則徐同戍伊犁。
entries.en: In 1841 Qishan withdrew coastal defenses and Humen fell. Deng was again blamed for lax military administration during his long tenure in the Two Guang and was banished to Yili together with Lin.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year Qishan withdrew coastal defenses, Humen fell, and Deng was again held accountable for long service in the Two Guang and neglect of military affairs, and was exiled to Yili together with Lin.

entries.zh: 二十三年，釋還。
entries.en: In 1843 he was released and allowed to return.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.

entries.zh: 尋予三品頂戴，授甘肅布政使。
entries.en: He was soon given third-rank insignia and appointed financial commissioner of Gansu.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was granted third-rank insignia and appointed Financial Commissioner of Gansu.

entries.zh: 議清查荒地，親往歷勘，由銀州東盡洮、隴，西極酒泉，得田一萬九千四百餘頃，又番貢地一千五百餘頃，寧夏馬廠地歸公一百餘頃，熟地昇科，荒者招墾，詔嘉其勤，复二品頂戴。
