entries.en: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he inspected the territory in person from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan. He identified more than 19,400 qing of fields, 1,500 qing of tribal tribute land, and more than 100 qing of Ningxia horse-pasture returned to the state. Cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland opened to settlers. The throne praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.
entries.literal: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he personally went to inspect it; from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan, he found 19,400-odd qing of fields, plus 1,500-odd qing of tribute lands of tribes, and more than 100 qing of horse-pasture land in Ningxia returned to the state; cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland was opened for reclamation; an edict praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.

entries.zh: 二十五年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。
entries.en: In 1845 he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Governor of Shaanxi and served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.

entries.zh: 番匪擾蒙部，遣兵邀擊於硫磺溝，平之。
entries.en: When tribal bandits raided the Mongol territories, he sent troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and restored order.
entries.literal: Tribal bandits disturbed the Mongol territories; he dispatched troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and pacified them.

entries.zh: 尋回任。
entries.en: He soon returned to his regular post.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he returned to his regular post.

entries.zh: 二十六年，卒於官。
entries.en: In 1846 he died in office.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.

entries.zh: 廷楨治行早為時稱，屢躓屢起，宣宗知之深，故卒用之。
entries.en: Deng's record in office had long been admired. Though he fell and rose again more than once, Emperor Xuanzong knew him well and in the end continued to use him.
entries.literal: Deng's administrative conduct had long been praised in his time; though he stumbled and rose repeatedly, Emperor Xuanzong understood him deeply and therefore ultimately employed him again.

entries.zh: 績學好士，幕府多名流，論學不輟。
entries.en: A scholar himself, he loved to gather men of learning; his staff included many distinguished figures, and he never stopped discussing scholarship.
entries.literal: He was deeply learned and loved scholars; his staff included many eminent men, and he never ceased discussing learning.

entries.zh: 尤精於音韻之學，所著筆記、詩、詞並行世。
entries.en: He was especially expert in phonology, and his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated widely.
entries.literal: He was especially skilled in phonology; his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 子爾恆，亦官至陝西巡撫，自有傳。
entries.en: His son Erheng also rose to governor of Shaanxi and has a biography of his own.
entries.literal: His son Erheng also rose to Governor of Shaanxi and has his own biography.

entries.zh: 當廷楨之去福建也，逾年，英兵復至，陷廈門，遂窺台灣。
entries.en: After Deng left Fujian, British forces returned the following year, captured Xiamen, and then turned toward Taiwan.
entries.literal: When Deng left Fujian, a year later British troops again arrived, captured Xiamen, and then cast their eyes on Taiwan.

entries.zh: 總兵達洪阿偕台灣道姚瑩屢卻之。
entries.en: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a and Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly drove them back.
entries.literal: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a together with Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly repelled them.

entries.zh: 及和議成，同獲譴。
entries.en: When peace was concluded, both were punished.
entries.literal: When peace was concluded, both were punished.

entries.zh: 達洪阿，字厚庵，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Da Hong'a, styled Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Da Hong'a, style name Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 由護軍洊擢總兵。
entries.en: Starting as a guardsman, he rose step by step to brigade commander.
entries.literal: From a guardsman he was repeatedly promoted to Brigade Commander.

entries.zh: 道光十五年，調台灣鎮。
entries.en: In 1835 he was transferred to command the Taiwan garrison.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Taiwan garrison command.

entries.zh: 十八年，剿嘉義縣匪沈和等，賜花翎，加提督銜。
entries.en: In 1838 he suppressed the bandits Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was awarded the peacock feather, and given provincial commander rank.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the bandits Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was granted the peacock feather, and given the rank of Provincial Commander.

entries.zh: 二十一年八月，英兵船至雞籠海口，達洪阿與姚瑩督兵御之。
entries.en: In the eighth month of 1841 British warships reached Jilong Harbor. Da Hong'a and Yao Ying directed the defense.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year British warships reached Jilong Harbor; Da Hong'a and Yao Ying directed troops to resist them.

entries.zh: 副將邱鎮功燃巨砲折其桅，敵船衝礁破碎，擒斬甚眾，賜雙眼花翎。
entries.en: Vice-Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a heavy cannon and snapped the enemy mast. The enemy ship struck a reef and broke apart, and many of the crew were captured or killed. Da Hong'a was awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.
entries.literal: Vice-Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a great cannon and broke their mast; the enemy ship struck a reef and was shattered, and many were captured and killed; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

entries.zh: 九月，敵船再至雞籠三沙灣，复卻之。
entries.en: In the ninth month enemy ships returned to Sansha Bay at Jilong, and he drove them off again.
entries.literal: In the ninth month enemy ships again reached Sansha Bay at Jilong, and he again repelled them.

entries.zh: 剿平嘉義、鳳山土匪，予騎都尉世職。
entries.en: He suppressed bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.
entries.literal: He suppressed bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

entries.zh: 二十二年，敵船犯淡水、彰化間之大安港，欲入口。
entries.en: In 1842 enemy ships attacked Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua, intending to force their way in.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year enemy ships attacked Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua, intending to enter the port.

entries.zh: 達洪阿謀於姚瑩，瑩曰：「此未可與海上爭鋒，必以計殲之。」
entries.en: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying, who said: 'We cannot meet them head-on at sea. They must be destroyed by stratagem.'
entries.literal: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying; Yao said: 'This is not a case where we can contend at sea; they must be destroyed by stratagem.'

entries.zh: 乃募漁舟投敵任鄉導，誘令從土地公港入，擱淺中流，伏發，大破之，落水死者無算，其竄入漁舟者，擊斬殆盡。
entries.en: They recruited fishing boats and sent men to pose as guides for the enemy, luring the ships into Tudi Gong Harbor where they ran aground midstream. An ambush was sprung, the enemy was routed, countless men drowned, and those who fled into fishing boats were nearly all killed.
entries.literal: Thereupon they recruited fishing boats, sent men to the enemy to serve as guides, lured them to enter by Tudi Gong Harbor, stranded them midstream, sprang an ambush, and routed them greatly; those who drowned were beyond counting, and those who fled into fishing boats were nearly all killed.

entries.zh: 詔嘉台灣三次破敵，達洪阿等智勇兼施，大揚國威，賜號阿克達春巴圖魯，加太子太保銜。
entries.en: An edict commended Taiwan's three victories over the enemy, praising Da Hong'a and his colleagues for combining strategy and courage and greatly enhancing national prestige. He was granted the title Akedachun Baturu and the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: An edict praised Taiwan's three defeats of the enemy, stating that Da Hong'a and others combined wisdom and courage and greatly displayed national prestige; he was granted the title Akedachun Baturu and the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 敵船遊奕外洋，乘間掩擊，迭有俘獲，遂不復至。
entries.en: When enemy ships cruised offshore, Da Hong'a struck at every opening, repeatedly taking prisoners, and the enemy did not return.
entries.literal: Enemy ships cruised in outer waters; taking opportunities they launched surprise attacks and repeatedly captured prisoners, and the enemy then did not come again.

entries.zh: 既而英師再陷定海，浙江、江蘇軍屢挫，乃議和。
entries.en: Soon afterward British forces captured Dinghai again, imperial armies in Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace negotiations began.
entries.literal: Soon afterward British forces again captured Dinghai, the armies of Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace negotiations were then undertaken.

entries.zh: 英將濮鼎查訴稱台灣所戮皆遭風難民，達洪阿等冒功捏奏，命總督怡良赴台灣查辦。
entries.en: British general Pottinger claimed that those killed in Taiwan were shipwrecked civilians and that Da Hong'a and his colleagues had fabricated their reports to claim false credit. Governor Yiliang was ordered to Taiwan to investigate.
entries.literal: British General Pottinger complained that those killed in Taiwan were all shipwrecked victims, that Da Hong'a and others had falsely claimed merit and fabricated memorials, and the order was given for Governor Yiliang to go to Taiwan to investigate.

entries.zh: 至即傳旨革職逮問，兵民不服，勢洶洶，達洪阿等撫慰乃散。
entries.en: On his arrival an edict immediately dismissed Da Hong'a from office and ordered his arrest. Soldiers and civilians were outraged and the situation grew volatile until Da Hong'a and his colleagues calmed the crowd.
entries.literal: Upon arrival an edict was immediately transmitted dismissing them from office and ordering arrest for inquiry; soldiers and civilians were discontented and the situation grew turbulent; Da Hong'a and the others pacified them and the crowd then dispersed.

entries.zh: 至京，下刑部獄，尋釋之，予三等侍衛，充哈密辦事大臣。
entries.en: When he reached the capital he was imprisoned by the Ministry of Justice, but was soon released, given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and appointed commissioner at Hami.
entries.literal: When he reached the capital he was placed in the Ministry of Justice prison; soon he was released, granted the rank of Third-Class Bodyguard, and appointed Commissioner at Hami.

entries.zh: 歷伊犁參贊大臣，西寧辦事大臣。
entries.en: He later served as assistant commissioner at Yili and commissioner at Xining.
entries.literal: He successively served as Assistant Commissioner at Yili and Commissioner at Xining.

entries.zh: 二十六年，偕陝甘總督布彥泰剿平黑錯寺番匪。
entries.en: In 1846 he joined Governor-General Buyantai of Shaanxi and Gansu in suppressing the tribal insurgents at Heicuosi.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Governor-General Buyantai of Shaanxi and Gansu, he suppressed and pacified the tribal bandits of Heicuosi.

entries.zh: 三十年，授副都統。
entries.en: In 1850 he was appointed vice commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Vice Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 咸豐元年，從大學士賽尚阿勦賊廣西，破紫金山西南砲台。
entries.en: In 1851 he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.

entries.zh: 以病回京。
entries.en: He returned to the capital on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: On grounds of illness he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 三年，粵匪犯畿輔，率八旗兵赴臨洺關進剿。
entries.en: In 1853, when Guangdong rebels threatened the capital region, he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to attack them.
entries.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels invaded the capital region; he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to advance in suppression.

entries.zh: 從欽差大臣勝保擊賊靜海，四戰皆捷，追至下西河，副都統佟鑑、天津知縣謝子澄陣亡。
entries.en: Serving under Imperial Commissioner Shengbao, he fought rebels at Jinghai, won four successive engagements, and pursued them to Xiaxihe. Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian and Tianjin Magistrate Xie Zicheng were killed in action.
entries.literal: Following Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin he attacked rebels at Jinghai, won victory in four battles, pursued them to Xiaxihe, and Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian and Tianjin Magistrate Xie Zicheng died in battle.

entries.zh: 詔斥達洪阿先退，革職，留營效力。
entries.en: An edict rebuked Da Hong'a for having retreated first, stripped him of office, and ordered him to remain with the army to redeem himself through service.
entries.literal: An edict rebuked Da Hong'a for retreating first, dismissed him from office, and ordered him to remain with the army to redeem himself through service.

entries.zh: 四年，敗賊獻縣，復原官。
entries.en: In 1854 he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to his former rank.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he defeated rebels at Xian County and was restored to his original office.

entries.zh: 尋追賊阜城，受傷，卒於軍。
entries.en: He soon pursued the rebels to Fucheng, was wounded, and died in camp.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he pursued rebels to Fucheng, was wounded, and died in the army.

entries.zh: 贈都統銜，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡壯武。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted commander-in-chief rank, awarded the hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of Commander-in-Chief, given the hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and one Cloud Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

entries.zh: 姚瑩自有傳。
entries.en: Yao Ying has a biography of his own.
entries.literal: Yao Ying has his own biography.

entries.zh: 論曰：林則徐才略冠時，禁煙一役，承宣宗嚴切之旨，操之過急；
entries.en: The commentators say: Lin Zexu's talent and strategic vision were unmatched in his day. In the opium suppression campaign he carried out Emperor Xuanzong's stern orders, but pressed the policy too hard;
entries.literal: The commentary says: Lin Zexu's talent and strategy surpassed his age; in the opium prohibition campaign he carried out Emperor Xuanzong's stern and urgent orders, but handled matters too hastily;

entries.zh: 及敵氛蹈瑕他犯，遂遭讒屏斥。
entries.en: when the enemy exploited the opening and struck elsewhere, he fell victim to slander and was driven from office.
entries.literal: when the enemy seized on a flaw and invaded elsewhere, he then suffered slander and was removed from office.

entries.zh: 論者謂粵事始終倚之，加之操縱，潰裂當不致此。
entries.en: Some argue that if Guangdong affairs had been entrusted to him throughout and he had been given full control, the collapse would never have gone so far.
entries.literal: Commentators say that if the Guangdong affair had relied on him throughout and given him control, the collapse would not have reached this point.

entries.zh: 則徐瀕謫，疏陳：「自道光元年以來，粵關徵銀三千餘萬兩，收其利必防其害。
entries.en: On the verge of dismissal, Lin memorialized: 'Since 1821 the Guangdong customs have collected more than thirty million taels of silver. Whoever reaps such profit must also guard against its harm.
entries.literal: As Lin faced dismissal, he submitted a memorial stating: 'Since the first year of Daoguang, the Guangdong customs have collected more than thirty million taels of silver; in reaping its benefits one must guard against its harm.

entries.zh: 使以關稅十分之一制砲造船，制夷已可裕如。」
entries.en: If even one-tenth of customs revenue were devoted to casting cannon and building ships, we would already have ample means to check the foreigners.'
entries.literal: If one-tenth of the customs revenue were used to cast cannon and build ships, controlling the barbarians would already be ample.'

entries.zh: 誠為讜論。
entries.en: That was sound counsel indeed.
entries.literal: This was truly sound counsel.

entries.zh: 惟當時內治廢弛，外情隔膜，言和言戰，皆昧機宜，其禍豈能倖免哉？
entries.en: Yet at the time internal governance was slack, foreign realities were poorly understood, and whether advisers spoke for peace or war none grasped the moment. How could disaster have been avoided?
entries.literal: Only at that time internal governance was lax, foreign conditions were poorly understood, and whether speaking of peace or war all failed to grasp the proper moment—how could such calamity have been escaped?

entries.zh: 鄧廷楨與則徐同心禦侮，克保岩疆。
entries.en: Deng Tingzhen worked in full concert with Lin to resist foreign aggression and successfully defended the coastal frontier.
entries.literal: Deng Tingzhen and Lin Zexu joined in heart to resist insult and were able to preserve the rocky frontier.

entries.zh: 若達洪阿、姚瑩卻敵台灣，固由守禦有方，亦因敵非專注，朝廷皆不得已而罪之，諸人卒皆復起，而名節播宇內、煥史冊矣。
entries.en: As for Da Hong'a and Yao Ying driving back the enemy in Taiwan, their success owed something to sound defense but also to the fact that the enemy was not fully committed. The court punished them under political necessity, yet all eventually rose again, and their reputations spread throughout the empire and endure brightly in the historical record.
entries.literal: As for Da Hong'a and Yao Ying repelling the enemy in Taiwan, it was indeed because their defense was well ordered, but also because the enemy was not fully focused; the court punished them all under unavoidable circumstances, yet these men all eventually rose again, and their reputations spread throughout the realm and shine upon the historical record.

entries.zh: 琦善 琦善，字靜庵，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Qi Shan. Qi Shan, whose style was Jing'an, belonged to the Borjigit clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Qi Shan — Qi Shan, style name Jing'an, of the Borjigit clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 父成德，熱河都統，以先世格得理爾率屬歸附，世襲一等侯爵。
entries.en: His father Chengde served as military governor of Rehe. An earlier ancestor, Gedeli'er, had led his followers in submission to the dynasty, and the family thereafter held a hereditary first-class marquisate.
entries.literal: His father Chengde was military governor of Rehe; because an ancestor Gedeli'er had led his dependents to submit, the family hereditarily held the rank of first-class marquis.

entries.zh: 琦善由廕生授刑部員外郎，累遷通政司副使。
entries.en: Qi Shan entered official life by hereditary privilege as a vice director in the Ministry of Justice and rose in due course to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
entries.literal: Qi Shan entered office through hereditary privilege as a department vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and was promoted in succession to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十九年，出為河南按察使，歷江寧、河南布政使。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of the Jiaqing reign (1814), he was appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and later served as provincial treasurer in Jiangning and Henan.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, he went out as Henan provincial judicial commissioner, and served in succession as Jiangning and Henan provincial treasurer.

entries.zh: 二十四年，擢河南巡撫。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing (1819), he was promoted to governor of Henan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was promoted to Henan governor.

entries.zh: 河決馬營壩，偕尚書吳璥督工，甫塞而儀封南岸又決，奪職，予主事銜留工。
entries.en: When the Yellow River burst at Maying Dam, he joined Minister Wu Jing in supervising repairs. The breach had scarcely been closed when the south bank at Yifeng gave way again. He was dismissed from office but kept on the works with the nominal rank of department director.
entries.literal: When the Yellow River broke through at Maying Dam, together with Minister Wu Jing he supervised the works; they had just closed the breach when the south bank at Yifeng broke again. He was stripped of office and given the nominal rank of department director while retained on the project.

entries.zh: 尋授河南按察使，調山東。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and then transferred to Shandong.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and transferred to Shandong.

entries.zh: 道光元年，就擢巡撫。
entries.en: In the first year of the Daoguang reign (1821), he was promoted to provincial governor on the spot.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, he was thereupon promoted to governor.

entries.zh: 父憂，奪情任事，襲侯爵。
entries.en: On his father's death he was excused from mourning leave to remain in office and succeeded to the family marquisate.
entries.literal: When his father died, he was released from mourning obligations to continue in office and inherited the marquisate.

entries.zh: 捕治臨清教匪馬進忠，又籌濟高家堰工費八十萬。
entries.en: He captured and punished the Linqing sect rebel Ma Jinzhong and raised eight hundred thousand taels for repairs at the Gaojiayan embankment.
entries.literal: He captured and punished the Linqing sect rebel Ma Jinzhong, and also raised eight hundred thousand taels for works at the Gaojiayan embankment.

entries.zh: 五年，京察，詔嘉其明幹有為，能任勞怨，加總督銜。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Daoguang (1825), the capital evaluation brought an edict praising his clarity, drive, and willingness to bear hardship and blame, and he was granted the nominal rank of governor-general.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, at the capital evaluation, an edict praised his clarity, efficiency, and capacity for action, and his willingness to bear hardship and blame; he was given the nominal rank of governor-general.

entries.zh: 尋擢兩江總督，兼署漕運總督。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs and concurrently served as acting grain transport commissioner.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs and concurrently acted as grain transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 時高堰屢決，淤運阻漕。
entries.en: The Gaoyan embankment had repeatedly failed, silt had choked the canal, and grain transport was blocked.
entries.literal: At the time the Gaoyan embankment had repeatedly broken, silt had choked the transport route, and grain tribute was obstructed.

entries.zh: 琦善請用盤運法，並暫行海運，如議行。
entries.en: Qi Shan proposed relay transport along the route and a temporary switch to sea shipment; both plans were carried out.
entries.literal: Qi Shan requested the use of the relay transport method and a temporary shift to sea transport; both measures were adopted as proposed.

entries.zh: 七年，議啟王家營舊減壩，大濬正河，尋以減壩堵合，黃水倒漾，复閉禦黃壩，漕船倒塘灌放，詔斥失機，議革職，寬之，降授內閣學士。
entries.en: In the seventh year (1827), he proposed reopening the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredging the main channel. When the sluice was closed again, Yellow River water backed up, the control dam had to be shut, and tribute barges had to be worked through the lock in reverse. The court rebuked him for missing his chance; though dismissal was proposed, he was spared and demoted to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, it was proposed to reopen the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredge the main channel on a large scale; soon afterward, when the relief sluice was sealed again, Yellow River water backed up, the Yellow River control dam was closed once more, and tribute barges had to be emptied and filled in reverse in the lock. An edict rebuked him for missing the moment; dismissal was proposed, but he was spared and demoted to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 尋复授山東巡撫。
entries.en: He was soon reappointed governor of Shandong.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed governor of Shandong.

entries.zh: 九年，擢四川總督。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Daoguang (1829), he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 十一年，調直隸。
entries.en: In the eleventh year (1831), he was transferred to Zhili.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he was transferred to Zhili.

entries.zh: 十六年，協辦大學士。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year (1836), he was appointed associate grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was made associate grand secretary.

entries.zh: 十八年，拜文淵閣大學士，仍留總督任。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year (1838), he was made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion but kept his governorship.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was appointed grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while retaining his post as governor-general.

entries.zh: 琦善久膺疆寄，為宣宗所倚任。
entries.en: Qi Shan had long held important provincial posts and enjoyed the Daoguang Emperor's trust.
entries.literal: Qi Shan had long held frontier commissions and was relied upon by the Daoguang Emperor.

entries.zh: 二十年，海疆事急，駐天津籌辦防務。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of Daoguang (1840), with the coastal crisis mounting, he was posted to Tianjin to organize defenses.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, as the coastal crisis grew urgent, he was stationed at Tianjin to organize coastal defense.

entries.zh: 八月，英兵船至海口，投書乞通商，訴林則徐、鄧廷楨等燒煙啟釁。
entries.en: In the eighth month, British warships reached the river mouth with a letter asking to resume trade and blaming Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others for burning opium and starting the conflict.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, British warships reached the mouth of the river and sent a letter requesting trade, complaining that Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others had burned opium and provoked hostilities.

entries.zh: 琦善招宴英領事義律及兵官，許以代奏。
entries.en: Qi Shan entertained the British consul Charles Elliot and his officers and promised to present their petition to the throne.
entries.literal: Qi Shan invited the British consul Charles Elliot and his officers to a banquet and promised to memorialize the throne on their behalf.

entries.zh: 遂入覲面陳，授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦。
entries.en: He then had an audience with the emperor, was appointed imperial commissioner, and sent to Guangdong to investigate.
entries.literal: He then entered audience and stated the matter in person; he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate.

entries.zh: 諭沿海疆吏但防要隘，遇英船毋開砲，義律乃率船回粵。
entries.en: Coastal officials were told to hold only the vital passes and not to fire on British ships; Elliot then took his fleet back to Guangdong.
entries.literal: Coastal officials were instructed to defend only the key passes and not to open fire when they met British ships; Elliot then led his fleet back to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 尋罷則徐、廷楨，命琦善署兩廣總督兼粵海關監督。
entries.en: Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were soon removed, and Qi Shan was made acting governor-general of the Two Guangs and superintendent of the Guangdong customs.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were dismissed, and Qi Shan was ordered to act as governor-general of the Two Guangs and concurrently as superintendent of the Guangdong customs.

entries.zh: 密疏臚陳粵事，略曰：「林則徐示令繳煙，許以賞犒，洋人頗存奢望。
entries.en: In a secret memorial he laid out the Guangdong situation at length, writing in part: "When Lin Zexu ordered the surrender of opium and promised rewards, the foreigners entertained high hopes.
entries.literal: In a secret memorial he set forth the Guangdong situation in detail, saying in summary: 'Lin Zexu issued orders to surrender opium and promised rewards; the foreigners cherished high hopes.

entries.zh: 迨後每煙一箱，僅給茶葉五斤，所得不及本銀百分之一；
entries.en: Later they received only five catties of tea per chest of opium—less than one percent of the silver they had paid;
entries.literal: Later, for each chest of opium only five catties of tea were given; what they received did not amount to one percent of the original silver;

entries.zh: 又勒具'再販船貨入官、人即正法'甘結，迄未遵依，此釁所由起也。
entries.en: and they were forced to sign a bond stating that anyone who sold opium again would forfeit ship and cargo and face execution—a pledge they never accepted. That is how the quarrel began.
entries.literal: they were also forced to submit a written bond that 'if opium is sold again, the cargo shall be confiscated and the person executed at once,' which they never obeyed—this is how the quarrel arose.'

entries.zh: 當義律具禀繳煙，距撤退買辦五日，非出情原。
entries.en: When Elliot petitioned to surrender the opium, it was only five days after the compradors had been withdrawn—not from genuine goodwill.
entries.literal: When Elliot submitted his petition to surrender the opium, it was only five days after the compradors had been withdrawn—not from willing good faith.

entries.zh: 時義律僅止孤身，設有黨援，未必降心俯首。
entries.en: At the time Elliot stood alone; with allies at hand he might never have submitted so readily.
entries.literal: At the time Elliot was alone; had he had party support, he might not have bowed his head in submission.

entries.zh: 英吉利國王無給林則徐文書之事，惟呂宋國王曾有來文，或因此誤傳。
entries.en: The king of England had never written to Lin Zexu; only the king of Luzon had once sent a letter, and the story may have grown from that mistake.
entries.literal: The king of England had never sent Lin Zexu a letter; only the king of Luzon had once written, and the report may have arisen from that confusion.

entries.zh: 林則徐稱定海陰濕，洋人病死甚多。
entries.en: Lin Zexu claimed that Dinghai was damp and unhealthy and that many foreigners had died there.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that Dinghai was damp and gloomy and that many foreigners had died of illness.

entries.zh: 諮查洋人米穀牲畜尚充，疫癘病斃者多水手舵工，頭目死者不過數人。
entries.en: Inquiry showed that the foreigners still had ample grain and livestock; most deaths were among sailors and helmsmen, and only a few officers had died.
entries.literal: On inquiry, the foreigners' grain, livestock, and provisions were still ample; most who died of pestilence were sailors and helmsmen, and only a few officers had died.

entries.zh: 從前外洋來信，祗言貿易。
entries.en: Letters from abroad had formerly spoken only of trade.
entries.literal: Former letters from overseas spoke only of trade.

entries.zh: 自林則徐欲悉外情，多方購求漁利之人，造作播傳，真偽互見，此時紛紛查探，適墮術中。
entries.en: Once Lin Zexu sought to learn everything about the foreigners, he paid widely for information from profiteers who invented and spread tales, mixing truth with falsehood; the frantic inquiries of the moment fell straight into their trap.
entries.literal: Since Lin Zexu wished to know all foreign conditions, he bought information widely from profiteers who fabricated and spread reports, true and false mingled; at this time investigations were launched in every direction and fell straight into their trap.

entries.zh: 林則徐奏各國憤英人阻其貿易，美利堅、法蘭西將遣船來與理論。
entries.en: Lin Zexu reported that other nations resented Britain for blocking their trade and that the United States and France would send warships to remonstrate with the English.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu memorialized that every nation resented the English for blocking their trade, and that the United States and France would send ships to reason with them.

entries.zh: 訪聞各國曾有此說，然迄未見兵船來粵。
entries.en: Inquiry showed that such talk had circulated among the other powers, but no warships had yet appeared at Guangdong.
entries.literal: On inquiry, the various nations had indeed spoken in this way, but no warships had yet come to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 前有美國二船，乘英人不備，進口，至今未敢駛出。
entries.en: Two American ships had earlier entered port while the British were unprepared and still had not dared to leave.
entries.literal: Earlier two American ships had entered port while the English were off guard and still dared not sail out.

entries.zh: 畏葸如斯，縱力足頡頏，恐未肯傷其同類。
entries.en: They were so timid that even if strong enough to stand up to Britain, they would hardly strike their own kind.
entries.literal: So timid were they that even if their strength matched Britain's, they would probably not harm their own kind.

entries.zh: 虎門燒煙時，洋人觀者撰文數千言紀事，事誠有之，語多含譏刺，非心服。
entries.en: When opium was burned at Humen, foreign witnesses wrote a long account of the event. The deed was real enough, but the tone was largely sarcastic—not submission from the heart.
entries.literal: When opium was burned at Humen, foreign onlookers wrote an account of several thousand words; the event indeed occurred, but the language was largely sarcastic and showed no heartfelt submission.

entries.zh: 林則徐稱具結之後，查驗他國來船，絕無鴉片。
entries.en: Lin Zexu claimed that after the bond was signed, inspection of other nations' ships found no opium whatsoever.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that after the bond was signed, inspection of ships from other countries found no opium at all.

entries.zh: 如指上年而言，事屬以往，船貨無憑；
entries.en: If he meant the previous year, the matter was already past and there was no way to verify ship or cargo;
entries.literal: If he meant the previous year, the matter lay in the past and ship and cargo could not be verified;

entries.zh: 若指本年而言，來船尚未進口，不能知其有，亦安能信其無？」
entries.en: if he meant this year, the incoming ships had not yet entered port—how could one know they carried opium, still less believe they carried none?"
entries.literal: if he meant this year, the incoming ships had not yet entered port—how could one know they had it, and how could one believe they did not?'

entries.zh: 並言將軍阿精阿請團練水勇，及林則徐請鼓勵員弁，俟事定再議。
entries.en: He also noted that General Ajing'a had asked to organize militia and naval levies and that Lin Zexu had sought rewards for officers and men—both to be reconsidered once affairs were settled.
entries.literal: He also stated that General Ajing'a had requested militia and naval levies, and that Lin Zexu had asked to reward officers and men—both matters to be discussed again when affairs were settled.

entries.zh: 疏入，報聞，則徐以是獲罪。
entries.en: The memorial was received and noted; on its account Lin Zexu was punished.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned; Lin Zexu was punished on this account.

entries.zh: 時廣東撤水師歸營，猝被敵轟擊，掠去米艇兵丁，巡撫怡良以聞。
entries.en: Guangdong had just withdrawn its naval forces to barracks when the enemy suddenly opened fire, seized grain boats and troops, and Governor Yiliang reported the attack.
entries.literal: At the time Guangdong had withdrawn the naval forces to camp; they were suddenly bombarded by the enemy, who seized grain boats and soldiers; Governor Yiliang reported the matter.

entries.zh: 琦善又陳：「英人回粵，詞氣傲慢，義律託疾將回國，且兵船日增。」
entries.en: Qi Shan reported further: "The English have returned to Guangdong in an arrogant tone; Elliot claims illness and will go home, and their warships grow in number every day."
entries.literal: Qi Shan further reported: 'The English have returned to Guangdong with arrogant language; Elliot pleads illness and will return home, and warships increase daily.'

entries.zh: 得旨，仍暫停貿易，一面與議，一面籌防。
entries.en: The court ordered trade to remain suspended for the present while negotiating on one side and preparing defenses on the other.
entries.literal: An edict was received: trade was still to be suspended for the time being, while negotiating on one hand and preparing defenses on the other.

entries.zh: 義律堅持索還煙價，並增廈門、福州通商，嚴旨拒不許。
entries.en: Elliot insisted on compensation for the destroyed opium and on opening trade at Xiamen and Fuzhou as well; stern edicts refused both demands.
entries.literal: Elliot insisted on repayment for the destroyed opium and on adding Xiamen and Fuzhou as trading ports; stern edicts refused permission.

entries.zh: 十二月，義律見防禦漸撤，數遣挑戰，琦善諭止之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Elliot saw defenses thinning and sent repeated challenges; Qi Shan ordered him to desist.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Elliot saw defenses being gradually withdrawn and repeatedly sent challenges; Qi Shan ordered him to stop.

entries.zh: 義律曰：「戰後再議，未為遲也。」
entries.en: Elliot replied: "We can talk after we fight—it will not be too late."
entries.literal: Elliot said: 'To negotiate after fighting would not be too late.'

entries.zh: 乃犯虎門外沙角、大角兩砲台，副將陳連升力戰死之，遂陷。
entries.en: He then attacked the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries outside Humen. Vice Commander Chen Liansheng fought to the death, and both forts fell.
entries.literal: He then attacked the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries outside Humen; Vice Commander Chen Liansheng fought fiercely and died, and the forts fell.

entries.zh: 提督關天培守靖遠砲台，總兵李廷鈺守威遠砲台，並請援，琦善不敢明發兵，夜遣二百人往。
entries.en: Regional Commander Guan Tianpei held Jingyuan Battery and Brigadier Li Tingyu held Weiyuan; both begged for help. Qi Shan dared not send troops openly and sent only two hundred men by night.
entries.literal: Regional Commander Guan Tianpei held Jingyuan Battery and Brigadier Li Tingyu held Weiyuan Battery; both asked for reinforcements. Qi Shan dared not openly dispatch troops and sent two hundred men by night.

entries.zh: 二十一年正月，事聞，上震怒，下琦善嚴議，命御前大臣貝子奕山為靖逆將軍，戶部尚書隆文、湖南提督楊芳副之，率師赴粵協剿。
entries.en: When news reached the court in the first month of 1841, the emperor was furious. Qi Shan was placed under severe investigation. Beizi Yishan, a grand minister in attendance, was named General for the Pacification of Rebels, with Minister of Revenue Long Wen and Hunan Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong for joint suppression.
entries.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, when the matter was reported, the emperor was greatly angered, placed Qi Shan under severe investigation, and appointed the imperial clansman Prince Yishan, a grand councilor in attendance, as pacification commissioner, with Minister of Revenue Long Wen and Hunan regional commander Yang Fang as his deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong for joint suppression.

entries.zh: 義律數索香港，志在必得，琦善當事急，佯許之而不敢上聞。
entries.en: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong and meant to have it. Under pressure, Qi Shan pretended to agree but dared not tell the court.
entries.literal: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong, determined to obtain it; Qi Shan, pressed by the crisis, pretended to agree but dared not report it to the throne.

entries.zh: 至是，義律獻出所踞砲台，並原繳還定海以易香港全島，別議通商章程。
entries.en: Elliot then offered to return the batteries he held and to restore Dinghai in exchange for all of Hong Kong, with trade terms to be settled separately.
entries.literal: At this point Elliot offered to return the batteries he held and proposed to restore Dinghai in exchange for the whole island of Hong Kong, with trade regulations to be discussed separately.

entries.zh: 琦善親與相見蓮花城定議，往返傳語，由差遣之鮑鵬將事，同城將軍、巡撫皆不預知。
entries.en: Qi Shan met him at Lianhuacheng to settle terms, messages passing through the envoy Bao Peng. The local general and governor knew nothing in advance.
entries.literal: Qi Shan met him in person at Lianhuacheng to settle terms, exchanging messages back and forth through the envoy Bao Peng, who managed the affair; the general and governor in the same city were not informed beforehand.

entries.zh: 及英人佔踞香港，出示安民，巡撫怡良奏聞，琦善方疏陳：「地勢無可扼，軍械無可恃，兵力不固，民情不堅，如與交鋒，實無把握，不如暫事羈縻。」
entries.en: When the British occupied Hong Kong and issued a reassuring proclamation, Governor Yiliang reported it. Only then did Qi Shan write: "The ground offers no strong point, our arms cannot be trusted, the troops are unreliable, and the people are not steadfast. We have no real chance in a fight; it is better to temporize."
entries.literal: When the English occupied Hong Kong and issued a proclamation to reassure the people, Governor Yiliang memorialized the throne; only then did Qi Shan report: 'The terrain offers no choke point, arms cannot be relied on, troops are not solid, and popular sentiment is not firm; if we engage, we truly have no assurance—better to temporize for the moment.'

entries.zh: 上益怒，詔斥琦善擅予香港，擅許通商之罪，褫職逮治，籍沒家產。
entries.en: The emperor's anger deepened. An edict condemned Qi Shan for ceding Hong Kong and allowing trade on his own authority. He was dismissed, arrested, and his property was confiscated.
entries.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and issued an edict rebuking Qi Shan for the crimes of ceding Hong Kong on his own authority and permitting trade on his own authority; he was stripped of office, arrested for trial, and his property was confiscated.

entries.zh: 英兵遂奪虎門靖遠砲台，提督關天培死之。
entries.en: British forces then took Jingyuan Battery at Humen, and Regional Commander Guan Tianpei was killed.
entries.literal: The English troops then seized Jingyuan Battery at Humen, and Regional Commander Guan Tianpei died.

entries.zh: 奕山等至，戰復不利，廣州危急，許以煙價六百萬兩，圍始解，而福建、浙江復被擾。
entries.en: Yishan's forces fared no better in battle. Guangzhou was in peril until six million taels were promised as opium indemnity and the siege lifted, while Fujian and Zhejiang were raided again.
entries.literal: When Yishan and the others arrived, fighting again went badly; Guangzhou was in peril; six million taels were promised as opium indemnity before the siege was lifted, while Fujian and Zhejiang were again harassed.

entries.zh: 琦善逮京，讞論大辟，尋釋之，命赴浙江軍營效力，未至，改發軍台。
entries.en: Qi Shan was brought to the capital for trial and sentenced to death, but was soon released and ordered to serve with the Zhejiang army. Before he arrived, he was sent instead to a military penal station.
entries.literal: Qi Shan was brought to the capital under arrest; judgment called for execution, but he was soon released and ordered to serve at the Zhejiang army camp; before he arrived, he was instead sent to a military penal station.

entries.zh: 二十二年，浙師复敗，吳淞不守，英兵遂入江，江寧戒嚴，於是耆英、伊里布等定和議，海內莫不以罷戰言和歸咎於琦善為作俑之始矣。
entries.en: In 1842 the Zhejiang army was beaten again, Wusong fell, and British forces entered the Yangtze. Jiangning was put under martial law. Qiying, Yi Libu, and others then concluded peace. Across the empire, the decision to stop fighting and sue for peace was blamed on Qi Shan as the man who had set it all in motion.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Zhejiang army was defeated again; Wusong could not be held; British troops entered the Yangtze; Jiangning was placed under martial alert; then Qiying, Yi Libu, and others settled the peace. Throughout the empire, ending the war and speaking of peace were blamed on Qi Shan as having been the one who started it.

entries.zh: 是年秋，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。
entries.en: That autumn he was made a fourth-class imperial bodyguard and assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
entries.literal: That autumn he was given the rank of fourth-class imperial bodyguard and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

entries.zh: 二十三年，以三品頂戴授熱河都統。
entries.en: In 1843 he was appointed military governor of Rehe with the third-rank cap button.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, with the third-rank cap button he was appointed military governor of Rehe.

entries.zh: 御史陳慶鏞疏論僨事諸臣罪狀，上重違清議，再褫琦善職，意仍鄉用，未幾，予三等侍衛，充駐藏大臣。
entries.en: Censor Chen Qingyong listed the crimes of the officials who had mishandled the crisis. Bowing to public opinion, the emperor stripped Qi Shan of office again, though he still meant to use him. Soon he was made a third-class bodyguard and resident commissioner in Tibet.
entries.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crimes of the officials involved in the affair; the emperor, giving weight to pure opinion, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though he still intended to employ him; before long he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.

entries.zh: 二十六年，授四川總督。
entries.en: In 1846 he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 二十八年，詔嘉其治蜀於吏治營伍實心整頓，复頭品頂戴。
entries.en: In 1848 an edict praised his earnest reform of civil administration and the army in Sichuan, and his first-rank cap button was restored.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, an edict praised his governance of Shu for earnestly reforming civil administration and the army camps, and his first-rank cap button was restored.

entries.zh: 尋協辦大學士，留總督任。
entries.en: He was soon made associate grand secretary while keeping the governorship.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was made associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.

entries.zh: 以平瞻對野番功被議敘。
entries.en: For pacifying the wild tribes at Zhandui he was recommended for honors.
entries.literal: For pacifying the wild tribes at Zhandui he was recommended for reward.

entries.zh: 二十九年，調陝甘總督，兼署青海辦事大臣，剿雍沙番及黑城撒拉回匪。
entries.en: In 1849 he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu and acting Qinghai commissioner, where he campaigned against the Yongsha tribes and the Salar rebels of Heicheng.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and concurrently acted as Qinghai commissioner, suppressing the Yongsha tribes and the Salar rebels of Heicheng.

entries.zh: 既而言官劾其妄殺，命都統薩迎阿往按，革職逮問。
entries.en: Censors soon accused him of reckless killing. Banner General Saying'a was sent to investigate. Qi Shan was dismissed and arrested.
entries.literal: Before long censors impeached him for reckless killing; Banner General Saying'a was ordered to investigate; he was stripped of office and arrested for questioning.

entries.zh: 咸豐二年，定讞發吉林效力贖罪，尋釋回。
entries.en: In 1852 he was sentenced to serve in Jilin to expiate his crime and was soon released.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, judgment was fixed: he was sent to Jilin to serve in expiation of his crime, and was soon released and returned.

entries.zh: 時粵匪已犯湖南，勢日熾，屢易帥皆不能制。
entries.en: The Taiping rebels had already entered Hunan from Guangdong, their strength growing daily, and repeated changes of commander failed to check them.
entries.literal: At the time the Guangdong rebels had already invaded Hunan; their power grew daily; commanders were repeatedly changed yet none could control them.

entries.zh: 起琦善署河南巡撫，駐防楚、豫界上。
entries.en: Qi Shan was recalled to act as governor of Henan and posted on the Huguang-Henan frontier.
entries.literal: Qi Shan was recalled to act as governor of Henan and stationed on the border between Huguang and Henan.

entries.zh: 以捐餉加都統銜，授欽差大臣，專辦防務。
entries.en: For contributing funds he received the nominal rank of banner general and was named imperial commissioner in charge of defense.
entries.literal: For contributing funds he was given the nominal rank of banner general and appointed imperial commissioner with sole charge of defense.

entries.zh: 湖北省城失守，觀望不能救。
entries.en: When the Hubei provincial capital fell, he held back and could not relieve it.
entries.literal: When the provincial capital of Hubei fell, he looked on and could not save it.

entries.zh: 三年春，賊遂連陷安徽、江寧省城，分擾鎮江、揚州，命琦善偕直隸提督陳金​​綬防江北。
entries.en: In the spring of 1853 the rebels seized the capitals of Anhui and Jiangning and raided Zhenjiang and Yangzhou. Qi Shan was ordered, with Zhili commander Chen Jinshou, to defend the north bank of the Yangtze.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third year, the rebels then took in succession the provincial capitals of Anhui and Jiangning and raided Zhenjiang and Yangzhou; Qi Shan was ordered, together with Zhili regional commander Chen Jinshou, to defend the north bank of the Yangtze.

entries.zh: 三月，連敗賊於浦口雷塘，進剿揚州，分屯寶塔山、司徒廟，五戰皆捷。
entries.en: In the third month he beat the rebels repeatedly at Pukou and Leitang, advanced on Yangzhou, and encamped at Baota Hill and Situ Temple; he won five engagements in a row.
entries.literal: In the third month he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Pukou and Leitang, advanced to suppress Yangzhou, and encamped separately at Baota Hill and Situ Temple; five battles were all victorious.

entries.zh: 秋，破浦口援賊，合圍揚州。
entries.en: In autumn he routed rebel reinforcements at Pukou and joined in the siege of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In autumn he broke the rebel reinforcements at Pukou and jointly besieged Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 十二月，賊突圍出竄瓜洲，以收復揚州入告，詔斥勇潰縱賊，責令進剿瓜洲、儀徵，儀徵克復。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out toward Guazhou. He reported the recovery of Yangzhou, but an edict rebuked his troops for cowardice and letting the enemy escape and ordered him to pursue at Guazhou and Yizheng. Yizheng was retaken.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out of the encirclement and fled to Guazhou; he reported the recovery of Yangzhou; an edict rebuked the troops for cowardice and letting the rebels escape and ordered him to advance against Guazhou and Yizheng; Yizheng was recovered.

entries.zh: 四年夏，連戰金川、瓜洲、三汊河，屢奏斬獲。
entries.en: In the summer of 1854 he fought at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Cha River and repeatedly reported enemy killed and captured.
entries.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he fought in succession at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Cha River and repeatedly reported kills and captures.

entries.zh: 自琦善與向榮分主大江南北軍事，攻戰年餘，鎮江、瓜洲迄未克復，無得力水師，不能扼賊，琦善雖議增水師，亦未果。
entries.en: From the time Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command north and south of the Yangtze, they fought for more than a year without retaking Zhenjiang or Guazhou. Without a capable navy they could not block the rebels, and Qi Shan's proposal to expand the fleet also came to nothing.
entries.literal: From the time Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command of military affairs north and south of the Yangtze, they fought for more than a year, yet Zhenjiang and Guazhou were still not recovered; without an effective navy they could not choke the rebels; although Qi Shan proposed to increase the naval forces, this too did not succeed.

entries.zh: 是年秋，卒於軍，贈太子太保、協辦大學士，依總督例賜卹，諡文勤。
entries.en: That autumn he died in camp. He was posthumously made Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, granted mourning honors as a governor-general, and given the posthumous name Wenqin.
entries.literal: That autumn he died in camp; he was posthumously given the title Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, mourning grants according to the governor-general precedent, and the posthumous name Wenqin.

entries.zh: 恭鏜 子恭鏜，黑龍江將軍。
entries.en: Gongtang. His son Gongtang served as general of Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: Gongtang — His son Gongtang was general of Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 孫瑞洵，烏里雅蘇台參贊大臣；
entries.en: His grandson Ruixun was commissioner at Uliastai;
entries.literal: His grandson Ruixun was commissioner at Uliastai;

entries.zh: 瑞澂，兩湖總督。
entries.en: Ruichen was governor-general of the Two Huguang.
entries.literal: Ruichen was governor-general of the Two Huguang.

entries.zh: 瑞澂自有傳。
entries.en: Ruichen has his own biography.
entries.literal: Ruichen has his own biography.

entries.zh: 伊里布，字莘農，鑲黃旗紅帶子。
entries.en: Yi Libu, whose style was Xinnong, was a girdled clansman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Yi Libu, style name Xinnong, a girdled clansman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，授國子監學正，改補典簿。
entries.en: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of Jiaqing (1801) and was appointed director of studies in the Imperial Academy, later transferred to archivist.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed director of studies in the Imperial Academy, later transferred to archivist.

entries.zh: 出為雲南府南關通判，署澂江知府，遷騰越知州。
entries.en: He served as subprefect of Nanguan in Yunnan, acted as prefect of Chengjiang, and was promoted to magistrate of Tengyue.
entries.literal: He went out as subprefect of Nanguan in Yunnan prefecture, acted as prefect of Chengjiang, and was transferred to magistrate of Tengyue.

entries.zh: 二十四年，總督伯麟薦其熟練邊務，能馭土司，治緬匪有功，以應升用。
entries.en: In 1819 Governor-General Bolin recommended him as skilled in frontier affairs, able to manage native chiefs, and successful against Burmese raiders, and urged his promotion.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Governor-General Bolin recommended that he was skilled in frontier affairs, able to control native chiefs, and had merit in suppressing Burmese bandits, and that he should be promoted accordingly.

entries.zh: 道光元年，從總督慶保剿平永北大姚夷匪，賜花翎，署永昌知府。
entries.en: In 1821, serving under Governor-General Qingbao, he helped suppress the Yi rebels of Yongbei and Dayao, received the peacock feather, and acted as prefect of Yongchang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, following Governor-General Qingbao he suppressed the Yi rebels of Yongbei and Dayao, was granted the peacock feather, and acted as prefect of Yongchang.

entries.zh: 擢安徽太平知府。
entries.en: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.
entries.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.

entries.zh: 歷山西冀寧道，浙江按察使，湖北、浙江布政使。
entries.en: He served as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer in Hubei and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He served in succession as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer in Hubei and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 五年，擢陝西巡撫，調山東。
entries.en: In 1825 he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and transferred to Shandong.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and transferred to Shandong.

entries.zh: 丁父憂，署雲南巡撫。
entries.en: On his father's death he acted as governor of Yunnan.
entries.literal: When his father died, he acted as governor of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 服闋，乃實授。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he received the post in full.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he received formal appointment.

entries.zh: 時阮元為總督，伊里布和而廉，有政聲。
entries.en: While Ruan Yuan was governor-general, Yi Libu was known for mildness and integrity and earned a reputation for sound governance.
entries.literal: At the time Ruan Yuan was governor-general; Yi Libu was mild and incorrupt, and had a reputation for good administration.

entries.zh: 回疆兵事起，自請從軍，詔斥不諳回情，妄行陳奏，奪職留任，尋復之。
entries.en: When fighting broke out on the Muslim frontier he volunteered for the campaign. An edict rebuked him for misunderstanding frontier conditions and memorializing rashly. He was stripped of rank but kept his post and was soon restored.
entries.literal: When military affairs arose in the Muslim frontier, he volunteered to join the campaign; an edict rebuked him for not understanding frontier conditions and for rash memorializing; he was stripped of office but kept in his post, and was soon restored.

entries.zh: 十三年，擢雲貴總督。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 京察，以久任邊疆，鎮撫得宜，被議敘。
entries.en: At the capital evaluation he was recommended for honors for long frontier service and effective pacification.
entries.literal: At the capital evaluation, for long service on the frontier and proper pacification and control, he was recommended for reward.

entries.zh: 十八年，協辦大學士，留總督任。
entries.en: In 1838 he was made associate grand secretary while keeping the governorship.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was made associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.

entries.zh: 四川綦江奸民穆繼賢仇殺貴州仁懷武生趙應彩，遂糾眾踞方家溝為亂，伊里布率提督余步雲、布政使慶祿等破其巢，斬獲千餘，誅賊首穆繼賢、謝法真等，餘匪悉平，賜雙眼花翎。
entries.en: At Qijiang in Sichuan the outlaw Mu Jixian murdered Zhao Yingcai, a military licentiate of Renhuai in Guizhou, then raised a gang and seized Fangjiagou. Yi Libu led Provincial Military Commander Yu Buyun and Provincial Administration Commissioner Qinglu against their stronghold, killing or capturing more than a thousand men and executing the leaders Mu Jixian and Xie Fazhen. The rest were pacified, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather.
entries.literal: In Qijiang, Sichuan, the villain Mu Jixian killed in a feud the military licentiate Zhao Yingcai of Renhuai in Guizhou, then gathered a crowd and seized Fangjiagou in rebellion. Yi Libu led Regional Commander Yu Buyun, Provincial Treasurer Qinglu, and others to destroy their lair; more than a thousand were killed or captured; the bandit chiefs Mu Jixian, Xie Fazhen, and others were executed; the remaining bandits were all pacified; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

entries.zh: 十九年，調兩江總督。
entries.en: In 1839 he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

entries.zh: 二十年秋，英兵陷定海，命為欽差大臣，赴浙江查辦。
entries.en: In the autumn of 1840, after British forces took Dinghai, he was named imperial commissioner and sent to investigate in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the twentieth year, when British troops took Dinghai, he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Zhejiang to investigate.

entries.zh: 時已有論致寇由斷絕貿易燒煙起釁者，密諭察訪確情毋回護。
entries.en: Some already blamed the conflict on cutting off trade and burning opium. He was secretly told to investigate the facts and not shield anyone.
entries.literal: At the time there were already arguments that the enemy had been provoked by cutting off trade and burning opium; he was secretly instructed to investigate the true facts and not shield anyone.

entries.zh: 尋以琦善代林則徐，命沿海遇敵勿擊。
entries.en: Qi Shan soon replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to fire on the enemy.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward Qi Shan replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to attack when they met the enemy.

entries.zh: 伊里布初至浙，駐鎮海籌防，疏報擊沉敵船，有所擒獲，命慰諭英人攻擊出於誤會，促令退兵交地，俘虜俟敵退釋還。
entries.en: On reaching Zhejiang Yi Libu was posted at Zhenhai to organize defenses. He reported sinking enemy ships and taking prisoners, and was told to assure the British the clash was a misunderstanding, urge withdrawal and the return of territory, and release prisoners once they left.
entries.literal: When Yi Libu first reached Zhejiang, he was stationed at Zhenhai to organize defense; he memorialized that enemy ships had been sunk and captives taken; he was ordered to reassure the English that the attack had been a misunderstanding, urge them to withdraw and return the territory, and release prisoners after the enemy withdrew.

entries.zh: 伊里布遣家丁張喜偕員弁赴定海犒師，英人亦答餽，奏聞，諭卻勿受。
entries.en: Yi Libu sent his servant Zhang Xi with officers to Dinghai with gifts for the troops. The British sent gifts in return. When this was reported, the court ordered that such exchanges be refused.
entries.literal: Yi Libu sent his household servant Zhang Xi with officers to Dinghai to present gifts to the troops; the English also returned gifts; when this was reported, an edict ordered that such gifts be refused.

entries.zh: 請增調安徽、兩湖兵，允之。
entries.en: He asked for reinforcements from Anhui and the Two Huguang, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: He requested additional troops from Anhui and the Two Huguang; permission was granted.

entries.zh: 裕謙方代署兩江總督，疏言：「各省皆可議守，獨浙江必應速戰。」
entries.en: Yu Qian, then acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs, wrote: "Every province may talk of defense, but Zhejiang must fight at once."
entries.literal: Yu Qian was then acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs and memorialized: 'Every province may discuss defense, but Zhejiang alone must fight at once.'

entries.zh: 且言：「定海西境岑港為第一險要，應以精兵先據之。」
entries.en: He also added: "Cengang on Dinghai's western border is the foremost strategic point and should be seized first by elite troops."
entries.literal: He also said: 'Cengang on the western border of Dinghai is the foremost strategic point and should be seized first by picked troops.'

entries.zh: 下伊里布體察辦理。
entries.en: Yi Libu was ordered to investigate and act accordingly.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to Yi Libu for investigation and action.

entries.zh: 既而琦善在粵議款不得要領，兵端又開，二十一年正月，詔促伊里布進兵規复定海。
entries.en: When Qi Shan's talks in Guangdong broke down and fighting resumed, an edict in the first month of 1841 ordered Yi Libu to advance and retake Dinghai.
entries.literal: Before long Qi Shan's negotiations in Guangdong failed to reach essentials and fighting reopened; in the first month of the twenty-first year, an edict urged Yi Libu to advance and recover Dinghai.

entries.zh: 二月，義律既踞香港，盡調英船赴粵，以交還定海告。
entries.en: In the second month Elliot, having taken Hong Kong, moved his fleet to Guangdong and offered to return Dinghai.
entries.literal: In the second month, Elliot having occupied Hong Kong, he moved all British ships to Guangdong and announced that Dinghai would be returned.

entries.zh: 詔斥附和琦善，以兵砲未集，藉詞緩攻，致敵船遁去，褫協辦大學士、雙眼花翎，暫留兩江總督任，以裕謙代為欽差大臣督浙師。
entries.en: An edict condemned him for echoing Qi Shan and delaying the attack until the enemy escaped. He lost his associate grand secretary rank and peacock feather but kept the Two Jiangs governorship for the time being. Yu Qian replaced him as imperial commissioner over the Zhejiang forces.
entries.literal: An edict rebuked him for siding with Qi Shan, using the excuse that troops and guns were not yet assembled to delay the attack and let the enemy ships escape; he was stripped of associate grand secretary and the double-eyed peacock feather, temporarily retained as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and Yu Qian was appointed imperial commissioner in his place to command the Zhejiang army.

entries.zh: 裕謙論劾伊里布遣家丁赴敵船事，命解任，帶張喜來京，下刑部訊鞫，褫職，遣戍軍台。
entries.en: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his servant to the enemy ships. He was removed from office, Zhang Xi was brought to the capital for trial at the Ministry of Justice, and Yi Libu was stripped of rank and sent to a military penal station.
entries.literal: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his servant to the enemy ships; he was ordered relieved of duty, Zhang Xi was brought to the capital, the case was sent to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation, his office was stripped, and he was banished to a military penal station.

entries.zh: 未幾，定海、鎮海、寧波相繼陷，裕謙殉之。
entries.en: Soon Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in turn, and Yu Qian died defending the province.
entries.literal: Before long Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in succession, and Yu Qian died for the cause.

entries.zh: 二十二年春，揚威將軍奕經援浙，復挫敗。
entries.en: In the spring of 1842 the General Who Displays Might (Yangwei), Yijing, came to relieve Zhejiang and was beaten again.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year, the expeditionary general Yijing came to aid Zhejiang and was again defeated.

entries.zh: 巡撫劉韻珂疏陳浙事危急，薦伊里布無急功近名之心，為一時僅見，請發軍營效力贖罪。
entries.en: Governor Liu Yunke reported that Zhejiang was in peril and praised Yi Libu as free of ambition for quick glory—a rare quality—and asked that he be sent to the army to redeem himself.
entries.literal: Governor Liu Yunke memorialized that Zhejiang affairs were critical, recommended that Yi Libu had no mind for quick success or fame and was rare in his time, and asked that he be sent to serve in the army to expiate his crime.

entries.zh: 於是予七品頂戴，隨杭州將軍耆英赴浙，密諭相機辦理。
entries.en: He was given the seventh-rank cap button and sent to Zhejiang with Hangzhou General Qiying, with secret orders to act as circumstances required.
entries.literal: He was therefore given the seventh-rank cap button and went to Zhejiang with Hangzhou General Qiying, with secret instructions to act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 及英兵犯乍浦，耆英遣往設計退兵。
entries.en: When British forces attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to arrange their withdrawal.
entries.literal: When British troops attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to devise means to make them withdraw.

entries.zh: 五月，署乍浦副都統，復令張喜傳語，英兵遂去乍浦，犯吳淞，由海入江，鎮江失守。
entries.en: In the fifth month he acted as vice commander at Zhapu and again sent Zhang Xi with messages. The British left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangtze from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he acted as vice commander at Zhapu; Zhang Xi was again sent with messages; the British then left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangtze from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.

entries.zh: 伊里布奉命偕耆英赴江寧議和，事詳耆英傳。
entries.en: Yi Libu was ordered to join Qiying at Jiangning to negotiate peace; the details appear in Qiying's biography.
entries.literal: Yi Libu was ordered to go with Qiying to Jiangning to negotiate peace; the matter is detailed in Qiying's biography.

entries.zh: 和議既成，英兵退，約於廣東議稅則，命偕耆英詳慎酌商，授廣州將軍、欽差大臣，辦理善後事宜。
entries.en: After peace was made and the British withdrew, tariff talks were set for Guangdong. He was ordered to consult carefully with Qiying, appointed general of Guangzhou and imperial commissioner, and put in charge of postwar arrangements.
entries.literal: After peace was concluded and the British withdrew, it was agreed that tariff rules would be discussed in Guangdong; he was ordered to consult carefully with Qiying, was appointed general of Guangzhou and imperial commissioner, and charged with postwar arrangements.

entries.zh: 二十三年，至粵，見民心不服，夷情狡橫，憂悴。
entries.en: In 1843 he reached Guangdong, found the people unreconciled and the foreigners crafty and domineering, and was worn down with anxiety.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he reached Guangdong, saw that popular sentiment was not reconciled and that the foreigners were crafty and overbearing, and was worn with worry.

entries.zh: 踰月病卒，贈太子太保，諡文敏。
entries.en: A little over a month later he died of illness. He was posthumously made Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenmin.
entries.literal: After more than a month he died of illness; he was posthumously given the title Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenmin.

entries.zh: 宗室耆英，字介春，隸正藍旗。
entries.en: Zongshi Qiying, whose style was Jiechun, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Zongshi Qiying, style name Jiechun, enrolled in the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 父祿康，嘉慶間官東閣大學士。
entries.en: His father Lukang served as grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion under Jiaqing.
entries.literal: His father Lukang served as grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion during the Jiaqing reign.

entries.zh: 耆英以廕生授宗人府主事，遷理事官。
entries.en: Qiying entered office by hereditary privilege in the Court of the Imperial Clan and rose to supervising clerk.
entries.literal: Qiying entered office through hereditary privilege as a director in the Court of the Imperial Clan and was transferred to supervising clerk.

entries.zh: 累擢內閣學士，兼副都統、護軍統​​領。
entries.en: He rose to academician of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.

entries.zh: 道光二年，遷理籓院侍郎，調兵部。
entries.en: In 1822 he was moved to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, he was transferred to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 四年，送宗室閒散移駐雙城堡。
entries.en: In 1824 he escorted idle clansmen to their resettlement at Shuangcheng Fort.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he escorted idle clansmen to be resettled at Shuangcheng Fort.

entries.zh: 五年，授內務府大臣，歷工部、戶部。
entries.en: In 1825 he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household and later served in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household Department and served in succession in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.

entries.zh: 七年，授步軍統領。
entries.en: In 1827 he was appointed commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he was appointed commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.

entries.zh: 九年，擢禮部尚書，管理太常寺、鴻​​臚寺、太醫院，兼都統。
entries.en: In 1829 he was promoted to minister of Rites, placed over the sacrificial and ceremonial courts and the Imperial Medical Institute, and made a banner commander as well.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he was promoted to minister of Rites, placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of Ceremonial, and the Imperial Medical Institute, and concurrently served as banner commander.

entries.zh: 十二年，畿輔旱，疏請察吏省刑，嘉納之，授內大臣。
entries.en: In 1832, during drought in the capital region, he urged closer scrutiny of officials and lighter punishments. The court approved and made him an inner court minister.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, when the capital region suffered drought, he memorialized requesting scrutiny of officials and reduction of punishments; this was favorably received and he was appointed inner court minister.

entries.zh: 十四年，以管理步軍統領勤事，被議敘。
entries.en: In 1834 he was recommended for honors for diligent service as commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, for diligent service as commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie, he was recommended for reward.

entries.zh: 歷工部、戶部尚書。
entries.en: He served in succession as minister of Works and minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: He served in succession as minister of Works and minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十五年，以相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子少保。
entries.en: In 1835, for surveying the imperial tomb site at Longquanyu, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, for surveying the auspicious site for the eternal tomb at Longquanyu, he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 命赴廣東、江西按事。
entries.en: He was sent to investigate affairs in Guangdong and Jiangxi.
entries.literal: He was ordered to go to Guangdong and Jiangxi to investigate affairs.

entries.zh: 十七年，內監張道忠犯賭博，耆英瞻徇釋放，事覺，降兵部侍郎。
entries.en: In 1837 the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was caught gambling. Qiying favored him and ordered his release. When this came out, Qiying was demoted to vice president of the Ministry of War.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was guilty of gambling; Qiying showed favoritism and released him; when the matter came to light, Qiying was demoted to vice president of the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 尋出為熱河都統。
entries.en: He was soon sent out as military governor of Rehe.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he went out as military governor of Rehe.

entries.zh: 十八年，授盛京將軍。
entries.en: In 1838 he was appointed general of Mukden.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was appointed general of Mukden.

entries.zh: 詔嚴禁鴉片，無論宗室、覺羅，按律懲治。
entries.en: An edict strictly forbade opium and ordered that clansmen and girdled clansmen alike be punished by law.
entries.literal: An edict strictly forbade opium; whether clansmen or girdled clansmen, all were to be punished according to law.

entries.zh: 疏請旗民十家聯保，以憑稽察。
entries.en: He asked that Banner households be grouped in mutual-guarantee units of ten families for easier inspection.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting that Banner households be grouped in mutual guarantee units of ten families for inspection purposes.

entries.zh: 二十年，海疆戒嚴，疏請旅順口為水路衝衢，當扼要籌備。
entries.en: In 1840, when the coast was put on alert, he urged that Lüshunkou, a vital sea route, be fortified at the decisive points.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, when the coast was placed under martial alert, he memorialized that Lüshunkou was a vital water route and should be fortified at key points.

entries.zh: 英船入奉天洋面，先後游弋山海關、秦皇島等處，錦州、山海關皆設防。
entries.en: British ships entered Fengtian waters and cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other points. Defenses were raised at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.
entries.literal: British ships entered the waters off Fengtian and successively cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other places; defenses were set at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.

entries.zh: 二十二年正月，粵事急，琦善既黜，調耆英廣州將軍，授欽差大臣，督辦浙江洋務。
entries.en: In the first month of 1842, with Guangdong in crisis and Qi Shan dismissed, Qiying was made general of Guangzhou, imperial commissioner, and supervisor of foreign affairs in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year, when Guangdong affairs grew urgent and Qi Shan had been dismissed, Qiying was transferred to general of Guangzhou, appointed imperial commissioner, and put in charge of foreign affairs in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 因御史蘇廷魁奏英吉利為鄰國所破，詔促耆英赴廣州本任，乘機進剿，尋知其訛傳，仍留浙江。
entries.en: When Censor Su Tingkui reported that Britain had been defeated by its neighbors, the court ordered Qiying to Guangzhou to exploit the chance to attack. The story proved false, and he stayed in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Because Censor Su Tingkui memorialized that England had been broken by neighboring states, an edict urged Qiying to proceed to his proper post at Guangzhou and seize the chance to attack; it was soon learned to be false report, and he remained in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 五月，吳淞失守，命偕伊里布赴江蘇相機籌辦。
entries.en: In the fifth month, after Wusong fell, he was ordered to Jiangsu with Yi Libu to act as circumstances required.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, when Wusong fell, he was ordered to go with Yi Libu to Jiangsu to handle matters as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 英兵已入江，越圌山關，陷鎮江，踞瓜洲，耆英與揚威將軍奕經先後奏請羈縻招撫。
entries.en: British forces had entered the Yangtze, crossed Guishan Pass, taken Zhenjiang, and seized Guazhou. Qiying and Expeditionary General Yijing both asked to temporize and negotiate.
entries.literal: British troops had already entered the Yangtze, crossed Guishan Pass, took Zhenjiang, and held Guazhou; Qiying and Expeditionary General Yijing successively memorialized requesting temporizing pacification.

entries.zh: 七月，英兵薄江寧下關，伊里布先至，英人索煙價、商欠、戰費共二千一百萬兩，廣州、福州、廈門、寧波、上海五港通商，英官與中國官員用平行禮，及劃抵關稅、釋放漢奸等款。
entries.en: In the seventh month, as British forces closed on Xiaguan below Jiangning, Yi Libu arrived first. The British demanded twenty-one million taels for opium indemnity, commercial debts, and war costs; trade at Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai; equal ceremonial status for British and Chinese officials; customs offsets; release of Chinese collaborators; and other terms.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, when British troops pressed on Xiaguan at Jiangning, Yi Libu arrived first; the English demanded twenty-one million taels in total for opium indemnity, commercial debts, and war costs; trade at five ports—Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai; parallel ceremonial status between English and Chinese officials; and provisions on offsetting customs duties and releasing Chinese collaborators, among other clauses.

entries.zh: 越三日，耆英至，稍稍駁詰之。
entries.en: Three days later Qiying arrived and raised mild objections.
entries.literal: Three days later Qiying arrived and mildly disputed some points.

entries.zh: 英兵突張紅旗，置砲鍾山上臨城，急止之，遣侍衛咸齡、江寧布政使恩彤、寧紹台道鹿澤良，偕伊里布家丁張喜，詣英舟，許據情奏聞。
entries.en: The British suddenly raised a red flag and mounted guns on Zhong Hill overlooking the city. The move was hastily stopped. Imperial Bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning Treasurer Entong, Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang, and Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi were sent to the British ships with authority to report back to the throne.
entries.literal: The British suddenly raised a red flag and placed guns on Zhong Hill overlooking the city; this was urgently stopped; Imperial Bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning Provincial Treasurer Entong, and Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang, together with Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi, were sent to the British ships with permission to memorialize the throne according to the facts.

entries.zh: 宣宗憤甚，大學士穆彰阿以糜餉勞師無效、剿與撫費亦相等為言，乃允之。
entries.en: The Daoguang Emperor was furious, but Grand Secretary Muzhanga argued that the costly campaign had failed and that fighting and negotiating would cost about the same. The court then agreed.
entries.literal: The Daoguang Emperor was greatly angered; Grand Secretary Muzhanga argued that wasting funds and exhausting the army had been ineffective and that suppression and pacification would cost about the same, and permission was then granted.

entries.zh: 耆英等與英將濮鼎查、馬利遜會盟於儀鳳門外靜海寺，同籤條約，先予六百萬，餘分三年給，和議遂成。
entries.en: Qiying and his party met the British commanders Henry Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, signed the treaty, paid six million taels at once with the rest over three years, and peace was concluded.
entries.literal: Qiying and the others met in alliance with the British generals Henry Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, jointly signed the treaty, paid six million first with the remainder over three years, and peace was concluded.

entries.zh: 九月，英兵盡數駛出吳淞，授兩江總督，命籌辦通商及浙江、福建因地制宜之策。
entries.en: In the ninth month, after all British forces had left Wusong, he was made governor-general of the Two Jiangs and ordered to organize trade and local policies for Zhejiang and Fujian.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, when all British troops had sailed out of Wusong, he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs and ordered to arrange trade and policies suited to local conditions in Zhejiang and Fujian.

entries.zh: 二十三年，授欽差大臣，赴廣東議通商章程，就粵海關稅則分別增減，各口按新例一體開關，臚列整頓稅務條款，下廷議施行。
entries.en: In 1843 he was named imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade rules, adjust Guangdong customs tariffs, open every port under the new regulations, and lay out tax reforms for court approval.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade regulations; at the Guangdong customs he adjusted tariffs up or down as appropriate; every port opened under the new rules alike; he set forth clauses for reorganizing tax administration, which were referred to court deliberation for implementation.

entries.zh: 又奏美利堅、法蘭西等國一體通商，允之。
entries.en: He also asked that the United States, France, and other powers trade on the same terms, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: He also memorialized that the United States, France, and other countries should trade on the same terms; this was approved.

entries.zh: 美國請入京瞻覲，卻不許。
entries.en: The United States asked for an audience in the capital, but the request was refused.
entries.literal: The United States requested an audience in the capital; this was refused.

entries.zh: 二十四年，調授兩廣總督，兼辦通商事宜。
entries.en: In 1844 he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs with charge of trade affairs.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was transferred and appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs, with concurrent charge of trade affairs.

entries.zh: 二十五年，協辦大學士，留總督任。
entries.en: In 1845 he was made associate grand secretary while keeping the governorship.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was made associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.

entries.zh: 比利時、丹麥等國請通商，命體察約束。
entries.en: Belgium, Denmark, and other states asked to trade, and he was told to investigate and keep them within bounds.
entries.literal: Belgium, Denmark, and other countries requested trade; he was ordered to investigate and impose restrictions.

entries.zh: 二十六年，京察，以殫心竭慮坐鎮海疆，被議敘。
entries.en: At the 1846 capital evaluation he was recommended for honors for devoting himself to the coastal frontier.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, at the capital evaluation, for devoting heart and strength to holding the maritime frontier, he was recommended for reward.

entries.zh: 疏上練兵事宜，繕呈唐臣陸贄守備事宜狀，請下各將軍督撫置諸座右。
entries.en: He memorialized on military training and submitted a copy of the Tang official Lu Zhi's memorial on defense, asking that every general and governor keep it at hand.
entries.literal: He memorialized on troop training, transcribed and presented the Tang official Lu Zhi's memorial on defense arrangements, and asked that it be sent down to every general and governor to keep at hand.

entries.zh: 英國請於西藏定界通商，諭耆英堅守成約，毋為搖惑。
entries.en: Britain asked to demarcate borders and trade in Tibet. Qiying was told to hold to existing treaties and not be swayed.
entries.literal: Britain requested demarcation and trade in Tibet; Qiying was instructed to hold firmly to existing treaties and not be shaken.

entries.zh: 故事，廣東洋商居住澳門，貿易有定界，赴洋行發貨，不得擅入省城。
entries.en: By long-standing practice, foreign merchants in Guangdong lived in Macao, traded within fixed limits, dealt through the factories, and might not enter the provincial capital without permission.
entries.literal: By precedent, foreign merchants in Guangdong lived in Macao, trade had fixed boundaries, they went to the foreign factories to ship goods, and might not enter the provincial capital without permission.

entries.zh: 自江寧和議有省城設立棧房及領事入城之約，粵民猶持舊例，愬於大吏，不省，乃舉團練，眾議洶洶，不受官吏約束。
