entries.en: The Jiangning treaty allowed warehouses in the provincial capital and consuls to enter the city, but Guangdong people clung to the old rules, appealed to the authorities in vain, and raised militia. Public feeling ran high and would not obey officials.
entries.literal: Since the Jiangning peace treaty provided for warehouses in the provincial capital and consuls entering the city, the people of Guangdong still held to the old practice, appealed to the high officials who paid no heed, then raised militia; public opinion was turbulent and would not submit to official control.

entries.zh: 二十三年，濮鼎查將入城，粵民不可，逡巡去。
entries.en: In 1843, when Pottinger was about to enter the city, the Guangdong people refused and he withdrew after hesitation.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, when Pottinger was about to enter the city, the people of Guangdong would not allow it and he withdrew after hesitation.

entries.zh: 二十五年，英船復至，耆英遣廣州知府餘保純詣商，粵民鼓譟，安撫乃罷。
entries.en: In 1845 British ships returned. Qiying sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun to negotiate, but the crowd clamored and the affair ended only after pacification.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when British ships came again, Qiying sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun to negotiate with the merchants; the people of Guangdong clamored, and the matter was dropped only after pacification.

entries.zh: 英人以登岸每遭窘辱，貽書大吏誚讓，群情憤激，不可曉諭。
entries.en: The British complained in letters to the high officials that their men were humiliated whenever they came ashore. Public anger was fierce and beyond persuasion.
entries.literal: Because the English were humiliated whenever they came ashore, they sent letters to the high officials reproaching them; popular feeling was furious and could not be reasoned with.

entries.zh: 至二十七年，英船突入省河，要求益堅，耆英謾許兩年後踐約，始退，自請議處。
entries.en: In 1847 British ships suddenly entered the provincial river with firmer demands. Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years; they then withdrew, and he asked to be punished.
entries.literal: By the twenty-seventh year, British ships suddenly entered the provincial river; their demands grew firmer; Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years before they withdrew, and he asked to be punished.

entries.zh: 諭嚴為防備，務出萬全。
entries.en: He was ordered to strengthen defenses and leave nothing to chance.
entries.literal: He was instructed to prepare defenses strictly and to leave nothing to chance.

entries.zh: 耆英知終必有釁。
entries.en: Qiying knew trouble would come in the end.
entries.literal: Qiying knew that trouble would come in the end.

entries.zh: 二十八年，請入覲，留京供職，賜雙眼花翎，管理禮部、兵部，兼都統。
entries.en: In 1848 he asked for an audience, remained at court, received the double-eyed peacock feather, and was put in charge of the Ministries of Rites and War while serving as a banner commander.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he requested an audience, remained in the capital on duty, was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, and was placed in charge of the Ministries of Rites and War while concurrently serving as banner commander.

entries.zh: 尋拜文淵閣大學士，命赴山東查辦鹽務，校閱浙江營伍。
entries.en: He was soon made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and sent to investigate salt administration in Shandong and inspect Zhejiang army camps.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and ordered to go to Shandong to investigate salt administration and to inspect the army camps of Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「求治莫先於用人、理財、行政諸大端。
entries.en: In 1850, when the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he responded to the call for advice, writing in part: "Good government begins with the great tasks of choosing men, managing finances, and administering affairs.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he responded to the edict calling for memorials, saying in summary: 'In seeking good government, nothing comes before the great matters of employing men, managing finances, and administering affairs.

entries.zh: 用人之道，明試以功。
entries.en: Men should be chosen by testing their achievements.
entries.literal: The way to employ men is to test them clearly by achievement.

entries.zh: 人有剛柔，才有長短。
entries.en: Men differ in temperament, and talent has its strengths and limits.
entries.literal: Men differ in firmness and softness, and talent has its strengths and weaknesses.

entries.zh: 用違其才，君子亦恐誤事；
entries.en: Use a man against his talent, and even an upright man may fail;
entries.literal: Use a man against his talent, and even a gentleman may fail in his task;

entries.zh: 用得其當，小人亦能濟事。
entries.en: use him fittingly, and even a base man can get the work done.
entries.literal: use him fittingly, and even a petty man can accomplish the work.

entries.zh: 設官分職，非為眾人藏身之地。
entries.en: Offices exist to serve the state, not to give everyone a hiding place.
entries.literal: Offices and duties are established, not to give everyone a place to hide.

entries.zh: 實心任事者，雖小人當保全；
entries.en: Whoever serves faithfully, though base, should be kept;
entries.literal: Whoever serves in earnest, though a petty man, should be preserved;

entries.zh: 不肯任怨者，雖君子當委置。
entries.en: whoever will not bear hard tasks, though upright, should be set aside.
entries.literal: whoever will not bear responsibility, though a gentleman, should be set aside.

entries.zh: 行政在於得人，迂腐之說，無裨時務，泥古之論，難合機宜，財非人不理。
entries.en: Administration depends on the right men. Pedantry does not help the times, antiquarianism does not fit the moment, and finances cannot be managed without capable men.
entries.literal: Administration lies in getting the right men; pedantic doctrines do not help present affairs; antiquarian arguments hardly suit the moment; finances cannot be managed without the right men.

entries.zh: 今賦額四千餘萬，支用有餘，不能如額，以致短絀。
entries.en: The tax quota now exceeds forty million taels and should leave a surplus, yet collections fall short and deficits follow.
entries.literal: Today the tax quota is more than forty million, expenditures should leave a surplus, yet the quota cannot be met, causing shortfalls.

entries.zh: 致絀之由，非探本窮源，不能通盤清釐。
entries.en: The causes of deficit cannot be cleared up without tracing them to the root.
entries.literal: The causes of shortfall cannot be cleared comprehensively without tracing matters to their roots.

entries.zh: 與其正賦外別費經營，不如於正賦中覈實籌畫。」
entries.en: Rather than raising extra levies outside the regular tax, it is better to plan realistically within the regular tax itself."
entries.literal: Rather than raising separate funds outside the regular land tax, it is better to plan realistically within the regular tax itself.'

entries.zh: 疏入，特諭曰：「身為端揆，一言一動，舉朝所矜式。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, a special edict declared: "As chief minister, your every word and act is a model for the whole court.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, a special edict said: 'As chief minister, every word and act is a model for the whole court.

entries.zh: 耆英率意敷陳，持論過偏，顯違古訓，流弊曷可勝言。」
entries.en: Qiying has spoken rashly, his views are too one-sided, he plainly violates ancient teaching, and the harm that may follow is beyond telling."
entries.literal: Qiying has spoken at will, his arguments are too one-sided, he plainly violates ancient teaching, and the evils that may flow from this are beyond telling.'

entries.zh: 傳旨申飭。
entries.en: An imperial rebuke was transmitted.
entries.literal: An imperial message was transmitted rebuking him.

entries.zh: 耆英不自安，屢稱病。
entries.en: Qiying grew uneasy and repeatedly pleaded illness.
entries.literal: Qiying was ill at ease and repeatedly pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 是年十月，上手詔揭示穆彰阿及耆英罪狀，斥「耆英在廣東抑民奉夷，謾許入城，幾致不測之變。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year the emperor issued a hand edict listing the crimes of Muzhanga and Qiying, condemning Qiying for "in Guangdong suppressing the people while favoring foreigners, rashly promising them entry into the city, and nearly causing disaster.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of that year, the emperor issued a hand edict revealing the crimes of Muzhanga and Qiying, rebuking Qiying for 'in Guangdong suppressing the people and favoring the barbarians, rashly promising entry into the city, and nearly bringing on unforeseen disaster.

entries.zh: 數面陳夷情可畏，應事周旋，但圖常保祿位。
entries.en: He repeatedly told the throne that the foreigners were fearsome, temporized in every crisis, and cared only to keep his rank and salary.
entries.literal: He repeatedly stated in audience that the barbarians were to be feared, dealt with affairs by temporizing, and sought only to keep his salary and rank.

entries.zh: 穆彰阿暗而難明，耆英顯而易見，貽害國家，其罪則一」。
entries.en: Muzhanga works in the dark and is hard to expose; Qiying's faults are plain to see. Yet in harming the state their crime is the same."
entries.literal: Muzhanga is hidden and hard to expose, Qiying is obvious and easy to see, but in harming the state their crime is one.'

entries.zh: 猶念其迫於時勢，從寬降為部屬。
entries.en: Mindful that he had been pressed by the times, the court leniently demoted him to a subordinate post.
entries.literal: Still mindful that he had been pressed by the times, he was leniently demoted to a subordinate post.

entries.zh: 尋補工部員外郎。
entries.en: He was soon reappointed vice director in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was reappointed as a department vice director in the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，耆英子馬蘭鎮總兵慶錫奏請父子兄弟同赴軍前，命耆英隨巡防王大臣效力，以捐餉予四品頂戴。
entries.en: In 1853, as the Guangdong rebels advanced north, Qiying's son Qingxi, brigadier at Malan Town, asked that father, sons, and brothers serve at the front together. Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrolling defense commissioners and received the fourth-rank cap button for contributing funds.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when the Guangdong rebels invaded northward, Qiying's son Qingxi, brigadier at Malan Town, memorialized asking that father, sons, and brothers go together to the front; Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrolling defense princes and ministers, and for contributing funds was given the fourth-rank cap button.

entries.zh: 五年，慶錫向屬員借貸被劾，耆英坐私告，革職圈禁。
entries.en: In 1855 Qingxi was impeached for borrowing from subordinates. Qiying was punished for making a private report, dismissed, and placed under house arrest.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Qingxi was impeached for borrowing money from subordinates; Qiying was punished for making a private report, stripped of office, and placed under house arrest.

entries.zh: 八年，英人糾合法、美、俄諸國兵船犯天津，爭改條約，命大學士桂良、尚書花沙納扆往查辦。
entries.en: In 1858 Britain joined France, the United States, and Russia in sending warships against Tianjin to demand treaty revisions. Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were sent to investigate.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, the English gathered French, American, and Russian warships to attack Tianjin and pressed to revise the treaty; Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were ordered to proceed and investigate.

entries.zh: 巡防王大臣薦耆英熟悉情形，召對，自陳原力任其難，予侍郎銜，赴天津協議。
entries.en: The patrolling defense commissioners recommended Qiying as knowing the situation. Summoned to audience, he said he was willing as before to bear the burden, was given vice presidential rank, and sent to negotiate at Tianjin.
entries.literal: The patrolling defense princes and ministers recommended Qiying as familiar with the situation; he was summoned to audience, stated that he was willing as before to bear the difficulty, was given the nominal rank of vice president, and sent to Tianjin to negotiate.

entries.zh: 初耆英之在廣東也，五口通商事多由裁決，一意遷就。
entries.en: While Qiying was in Guangdong, trade at the five treaty ports largely rested in his hands, and he yielded on every point.
entries.literal: When Qiying had been in Guangdong, affairs of trade at the five ports were largely decided by him, and he yielded in every matter.

entries.zh: 七年冬，廣州陷，檔案為英人所得，譯出耆英章奏，多掩飾不實，深惡之。
entries.en: In the winter of 1857 Guangzhou fell and the British seized the archives. Qiying's memorials, once translated, proved largely false and evasive, and the foreigners came to hate him bitterly.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, when Guangzhou fell, archives were taken by the English; Qiying's memorials were translated and found largely to conceal and distort the truth; they hated him deeply.

entries.zh: 及至天津，英人拒不見，惶恐求去，不候旨，回通州，於是欺謾之跡益彰，為王大臣論劾，嚴詔逮治，賜自盡。
entries.en: At Tianjin the British refused to see him. In fear he begged to leave and returned to Tongzhou without waiting for orders, exposing his deceit all the more clearly. The commissioners impeached him, a stern edict ordered his arrest, and he was granted suicide.
entries.literal: When he reached Tianjin, the English refused to see him; in fear he begged to leave, returned to Tongzhou without awaiting orders, and thus his deceit became still plainer; the princes and ministers impeached him, a stern edict ordered his arrest, and he was granted suicide.

entries.zh: 論曰：罷戰言和，始發於琦善，去備媚敵，致敗之由。
entries.en: The historian comments: The move to stop fighting and sue for peace began with Qi Shan. Abandoning preparedness and courting the enemy was what led to defeat.
entries.literal: The historian comments: To cease fighting and speak of peace began with Qi Shan; abandoning preparedness and courting the enemy was the cause of defeat.

entries.zh: 伊里布有忍辱負重之心，無安危定傾之略，且廟謨未定，廷議紛紜，至江寧城下之盟，乃與耆英結束和議，損威喪權，貽害莫挽。
entries.en: Yi Libu was willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, but lacked a strategy to save the state in crisis. Court policy was unsettled and debate divided. When the treaty was signed below the walls of Jiangning, he and Qiying concluded peace at the cost of prestige and sovereignty, with consequences that could not be undone.
entries.literal: Yi Libu had a heart willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, but no strategy to secure safety and turn crisis aside; moreover court policy was unsettled and court debate was divided; when the treaty was made below the walls of Jiangning, he and Qiying concluded the peace, diminishing prestige and forfeiting authority, with harm that could not be retrieved.

entries.zh: 耆英獨任善後，留廣州入城之隙，兵釁再開，浸致庚申之禍。
entries.en: Qiying alone handled the aftermath and left the question of entry into Guangzhou unresolved. Fighting broke out again and eventually led to the disaster of 1860.
entries.literal: Qiying alone bore postwar arrangements, left the opening of entry into Guangzhou, fighting broke out again, and gradually led to the disaster of Gengshen.

entries.zh: 三人者同受惡名，而耆英不保其身命，宜哉。
entries.en: All three earned a foul reputation, yet only Qiying failed to keep his life—and rightly so.
entries.literal: The three alike bore an evil name, yet Qiying alone did not preserve his life—as was fitting.

entries.zh: 二十一年，命為靖逆將軍，督師廣東，尚書​​隆文、提督楊芳為參贊副之。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he was named Pacification General to command the Guangdong front, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as his deputies.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to serve as Pacification General, commanding troops in Guangdong, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as deputy advisers.

entries.zh: 時英兵已陷虎門，楊芳先至，聽美利堅人居間，乞許通商，被嚴斥，促奕山速赴軍。
entries.en: By then the British had already captured Humen. Yang Fang reached Guangdong first and, taking advice from American go-betweens, asked permission to resume trade; he was sharply rebuked, and Yishan was ordered to reach the army without delay.
entries.literal: At that time the English army had already taken Humen. Yang Fang arrived first and, heeding American intermediaries, petitioned to allow trade; he was sternly rebuked and Yishan was urged to hurry to the front.

entries.zh: 三月，抵廣州。
entries.en: In the third month he arrived at Guangzhou.
entries.literal: In the third month he reached Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 英艦橫亙省河，奕山問計於林則徐，則徐議先遣洋商設法羈縻，俾英艦暫退；
entries.en: British warships blocked the provincial river. Yishan sought Lin Zexu's counsel; Lin urged that foreign merchants first be used to stall the enemy so the British fleet might pull back for a time;
entries.literal: English warships lay across the provincial river. Yishan asked Lin Zexu for a plan; Lin proposed first sending foreign merchants to negotiate restraint so the English ships might temporarily withdraw;

entries.zh: 塞河道，積沙囊於岸以御砲，然後以守為攻。
entries.en: then block the channel, heap sandbags along the banks against artillery, and only afterward turn defense into attack.
entries.literal: block the river channel, pile sandbags on the banks to ward off cannon fire, and then take defense as offense.

entries.zh: 奕山不能用，且自琦善撤防，舊儲木椿鉅石皆為敵移去，時以杉板小船游弋以誘我師。
entries.en: Yishan would not follow this advice. After Qi Shan had stripped the defenses, the enemy had carried off the old stockpiles of piles and boulders, and now sent out light fir boats to bait our forces.
entries.literal: Yishan could not adopt this. Moreover, since Qi Shan had withdrawn the defenses, the old stores of wooden piles and massive stones had all been removed by the enemy, who now cruised in fir-plank skiffs to lure our army.

entries.zh: 楊芳主持重，以募勇未集，不欲浪戰。
entries.en: Yang Fang urged restraint: the hired militia were not yet gathered, and he did not want a rash battle.
entries.literal: Yang Fang favored caution; the recruited braves were not yet assembled, and he did not wish to fight recklessly.

entries.zh: 奕山初亦然之，既而惑於左右言，欲僥倖一試，芳止之不可。
entries.en: Yishan at first agreed, but then his entourage persuaded him to gamble on one stroke of luck; Fang could not hold him back.
entries.literal: Yishan at first agreed, but then, misled by advisers around him, he wished to try his luck once; Fang could not dissuade him.

entries.zh: 夜進兵，乘風毀七艘，報捷，詰旦乃知誤焚民舟，而英兵大至，連舟抵城下；
entries.en: They attacked by night and, with the wind behind them, burned seven craft and reported a victory; at daybreak they found they had set fire to civilian boats, while the main British force came up and moored in a line beneath the walls;
entries.literal: At night they advanced; riding the wind they destroyed seven vessels and reported victory—but at dawn they learned they had mistakenly burned civilian boats, while the English army arrived in force and linked their ships under the city walls;

entries.zh: 禦於河南，互有殺傷，遂閉城。
entries.en: They fought south of the river with losses on both sides, then closed the city gates.
entries.literal: They fought them off south of the river with casualties on both sides, then shut the gates.

entries.zh: 圈禁逾年，與琦善同起用，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。
entries.en: After more than a year under house arrest he was restored with Qi Shan, made a Fourth Class Bodyguard, and sent as assistant commissioner to Yarkand.
entries.literal: After more than a year in confinement he was reemployed together with Qi Shan, granted Fourth Class Bodyguard, and appointed Assistant Commissioner at Yarkand.

entries.zh: 為御史陳慶鏞論劾，仍褫職。
entries.en: Censor Chen Qingyong impeached him and he lost his post again.
entries.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized against him and he was again stripped of office.

entries.zh: 未幾，复予二等侍衛，充葉爾羌參贊大臣，調伊犁領隊大臣。
entries.en: Soon he was made Second Class Bodyguard again, adviser commissioner at Yarkand, then brigade general of Ili.
entries.literal: Before long he was again granted Second Class Bodyguard, appointed Adviser Commissioner at Yarkand, and transferred to Brigade General of Ili.

entries.zh: 坐審鞫英吉沙爾領隊大臣齋清額誣捕良回獄不當，褫職發黑龍江。
entries.en: He was dismissed and exiled to Heilongjiang for mishandling the trial of Zhai Qing'e, brigade general of Yengisar, who had been accused of falsely imprisoning innocent Muslims.
entries.literal: For improperly trying Brigade General of Yengisar Zhai Qing'e on a charge of falsely arresting innocent Hui, he was stripped of office and sent to Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 三十年，釋回。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year he was freed and allowed to return.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was released and returned.

entries.zh: 咸豐初，歷伊犁、英吉沙爾領隊大臣。
entries.en: Early in Xianfeng he served in turn as brigade general of Ili and Yengisar.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he served successively as Brigade General of Ili and Yengisar.

entries.zh: 二年，召授工部侍郎，調刑部，兼副都統。
entries.en: In the second year he was recalled as vice minister of Works, moved to Punishments, and made vice commander-in-chief as well.
entries.literal: In the second year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently made Vice Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 三年，命率密雲駐防赴山東防粵匪，卒於徐州軍次，依侍郎例賜卹。
entries.en: In the third year he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Taiping rebels and died at Xuzhou on campaign; he received the standard vice-minister burial honors.
entries.literal: In the third year he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Cantonese rebels and died at the army camp in Xuzhou; condolence payments were granted according to the vice-minister precedent.

entries.zh: 英兵犯浙江，定海、鎮海及寧波府城相繼陷，裕謙死事，命為揚威將軍，督師往剿，都統哈哴阿、提督胡超為參贊，尋易侍郎文蔚、都統特依順副之。
entries.en: When the British invaded Zhejiang and Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell one after another, Yu Qian died in the fighting. Yijing was named Campaign General to lead the punitive force, with Ha'er'a and Hu Chao as deputies; before long Wen Wei and Te Yishun replaced them.
entries.literal: When the English army attacked Zhejiang, Dinghai, Zhenhai, and the prefectural city of Ningbo fell in succession and Yu Qian died in service, he was ordered to serve as Campaign General, commanding troops to suppress the enemy, with Banner Commander Ha'er'a and Provincial Military Commander Hu Chao as deputies; soon Minister Wen Wei and Banner Commander Te Yishun replaced them as deputies.

entries.zh: 陛辭日，宣宗禦勤政殿，訓示方略，特詔：「申明軍紀，凡失守各城逃將逃兵，軍法從事。」
entries.en: On the day he took leave of the throne, the Daoguang Emperor received him in the Hall of Diligent Government, laid out the strategy, and issued a special order: "Enforce discipline strictly: any commander or soldier who abandons a fallen city shall face the full penalty of military law."
entries.literal: On the day of his audience of leave, the Daoguang Emperor went to the Hall of Diligent Government and instructed him on strategy, with a special edict: "Make military discipline clear: all generals and soldiers who abandon their posts and flee from cities that fall shall be dealt with by military law."

entries.zh: 發交內庫花翎等件，有功者立予懋賞，勉以恩威並用，整飭戎行。
entries.en: The emperor gave him peacock feathers and other rewards from the palace stores, promising prompt honors for merit, and urged him to combine mercy and punishment and restore discipline in the ranks.
entries.literal: Peacock feathers and other items from the imperial treasury were issued; those with merit were to be rewarded at once with lavish honors, and he was exhorted to use both kindness and severity to put the army in order.

entries.zh: 大學士穆彰阿奏請釋琦善出獄，隨赴軍前效力，奕經卻之。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Muzhanga asked that Qi Shan be freed from prison to serve at the front; Yijing declined.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Muzhanga memorialized to release Qi Shan from prison so he might serve at the front; Yijing refused.

entries.zh: 宗室奕山，恂郡王允禵四世孫，隸鑲藍旗。
entries.en: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, an imperial clansman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 授乾清門侍衛。
entries.en: He was appointed an attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
entries.literal: He was appointed an attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

entries.zh: 道光七年，從征喀什噶爾，擢頭等侍衛、御前行走。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the Daoguang reign, he took part in the expedition against Kashgar and was promoted to First Class Bodyguard with the right to attend the emperor on duty.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang, he joined the campaign against Kashgar and was promoted to First Class Bodyguard with the privilege of imperial escort duty.

entries.zh: 歷伊犁領隊大臣、參贊大臣。
entries.en: He served in turn as Brigade General of Ili and as Adviser Commissioner.
entries.literal: He served successively as Brigade General of Ili and as Adviser Commissioner.

entries.zh: 十八年，授伊犁將軍。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he was appointed military governor of Ili.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed General of Ili.

entries.zh: 二十年，偕副都統關福赴塔什圖畢治墾務，闢田十六萬四千馀畝，奏請置回千戶及五品伯克以下官。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he went with Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Fu to Tashitubi to direct reclamation work, opened more than 164,000 mu of farmland, and memorialized the throne to set up Hui thousand-household units and officials from fifth-rank bakhshi down.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Fu he went to Tashitubi to oversee land reclamation, opening more than 164,000 mu of fields, and memorialized to establish Hui thousand-household posts and officials from fifth-rank bakhshi downward.

entries.zh: 召授正白旗領侍衛內大臣、御前大臣。
entries.en: He was recalled to court and appointed Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard of the Plain White Banner and Imperial Minister.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard of the Plain White Banner and Imperial Minister.

entries.zh: 十八年，入直南書房。
entries.en: In 1813 he was assigned to duty in the Southern Study.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered service in the Southern Study.

entries.zh: 會因林清之變，下詔求言，文田疏陳，略謂：「堯、舜、三代之治，不越教養兩端：為民正趨向之路，知有長上，自不干左道之誅；
entries.en: After the Lin Qing rebellion, the throne called for memorials of counsel; Wentian submitted a memorial arguing, in essence: "The rule of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties rested on only two pillars—moral instruction and material support: by guiding the people onto the proper path so they recognized authority above them, they would not stray into heterodox cults and invite punishment;
entries.literal: When the Lin Qing incident occurred, an edict was issued soliciting advice; Wentian submitted a memorial stating, in summary: "The governance of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties did not go beyond two principles—education and nurture: to set the people on the right path, so that knowing they had superiors, they would not run afoul of heterodox doctrines and face punishment;

entries.zh: 為民廣衣食之源，各保身家，自不致有為惡之意。
entries.en: by expanding the people's means of livelihood so that each household could secure its own welfare, they would not be driven to evil intent in the first place.
entries.literal: to broaden the sources of food and clothing for the people, so that each might preserve household and person, and would not come to harbor intent to do evil.

entries.zh: 近日南方患賦重，北方患徭多，民困官貧，急宜省事。
entries.en: Lately the south has groaned under heavy taxes and the north under excessive corvée; with the people in distress and officials strapped, government business urgently needs to be streamlined.
entries.literal: Recently the south has suffered from heavy taxation and the north from excessive corvée labor; the people are distressed and officials impoverished—affairs of state should urgently be simplified.

entries.zh: 久督撫任期，則州縣供億少，寬​​州縣例議，則人才保全多。」
entries.en: If governors-general and governors served longer terms, counties and districts would have to supply their establishments less; if the routine charges against county and district magistrates were relaxed, more talented men could be preserved in office."
entries.literal: If governors-general and governors serve long terms, then the burden of supplying their establishments falls less on counties and districts; if regulations burdening counties and districts are relaxed, then more talented men can be preserved in office."

entries.zh: 次年復上疏，言：「上之於下，不患其不畏，而患其不愛。
entries.en: The next year he memorialized again: "A ruler need not worry that his subjects lack fear; he should worry that they lack affection.
entries.literal: The following year he submitted another memorial, saying: "Between superior and subordinate, the concern is not that they do not fear, but that they do not love.

entries.zh: 漢文吏治蒸蒸，不至於姦，愛故也。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wen of Han the civil service thrived without sinking into corruption—because the people were governed with affection.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wen of Han the administration flourished and did not descend into wickedness—because of love.

entries.zh: 秦顓法律，衡石程書，一夫夜呼，亂者四起，畏故也。
entries.en: The Qin ruled through draconian law, weighing documents by the stone and assigning them by quota; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.
entries.literal: The Qin relied on harsh laws, weighing documents by the stone and scheduling them by the bushel; one man cried out in the night and rebels rose on every side—because of fear.

entries.zh: 自數年來，開上控之端，刁民得逞其奸；
entries.en: In recent years the practice of appealing cases to the capital has opened the way for scheming litigants to have their way;
entries.literal: In recent years the door to appeals to the capital has been opened, and crafty commoners have been able to carry out their schemes;

entries.zh: 大吏畏其京控，遇案親提，訐訴不過一人，牽涉常至數十，農商廢業，中道奔波，受胥吏折辱，甚至瘐死道斃。
entries.en: senior officials, dreading capital appeals, personally take charge of cases; though the plaintiff is a single individual, dozens are often dragged in; farmers and merchants abandon their livelihoods, travel halfway across the country, endure abuse from clerks and runners, and some even die of exhaustion along the road.
entries.literal: high officials, fearing appeals to the capital, personally take up cases when they arise; though the accuser is but one person, those implicated often number dozens; farmers and merchants abandon their trades, rush about on the road midway, suffer humiliation at the hands of clerks and runners, and some even die of exhaustion on the road.

entries.zh: 國家慎刑之意，亦曰有冤抑耳。
entries.en: The state's purpose in exercising caution with punishments is precisely to redress wrongful oppression.
entries.literal: The state's intent in being cautious with punishments is likewise said to be that there may be wrongful oppression.

entries.zh: 從前馬譚氏一案，至今未有正兇，無辜致斃者累累。
entries.en: In the old Ma–Tan clan case, the real culprit has still not been identified, while innocent people were put to death in great numbers.
entries.literal: In the former case of the Ma and Tan clans, to this day the true culprit has not been found, and the innocents who were put to death are numerous.

entries.zh: 是一冤未雪，而含冤者且數十人。
entries.en: One wrong goes unavenged while dozens more bear injustice.
entries.literal: Thus one injustice goes unredressed while those who suffer injustice number dozens.

entries.zh: 承審官刑撻橫加，以期得實，其中冤抑，正復不少。
entries.en: Trial officers beat and flog defendants freely in hopes of extracting confessions, and wrongful convictions are far from uncommon.
entries.literal: The examining officials apply beating and flogging indiscriminately in hopes of obtaining the truth; among them wrongful oppression is by no means rare.

entries.zh: 欲召天和，其可得乎？
entries.en: How can one hope to summon heavenly harmony under such conditions?
entries.literal: If one wishes to summon heavenly harmony, how can it be attained?

entries.zh: 頃者林清構逆，搜捕四出，至今未已。
entries.en: When Lin Qing recently rebelled, searches and arrests were launched everywhere and have not yet ended.
entries.literal: Recently Lin Qing raised rebellion; searches and arrests have been sent out on all sides and have not ceased to this day.

entries.zh: 小人意圖見長，不能無殃及無辜，奉旨嚴禁，仰見皇上如天之仁。
entries.en: Petty schemers, emboldened by success, inevitably drag in the innocent as well; the recent strict prohibition shows the Emperor's heaven-like mercy.
entries.literal: Petty men, seeing their schemes succeed, cannot but involve the innocent as well; an edict has strictly forbidden this, and one looks up to perceive the Emperor's heaven-like benevolence.

entries.zh: 臣以為事愈多則擾愈眾，莠民易逞機謀，良善惟增苦累。
entries.en: I believe that the more cases multiply, the wider the disruption spreads; scoundrels find it easy to plot, while the law-abiding gain only added misery.
entries.literal: Your subject believes that the more affairs there are, the more numerous the disturbances; wicked commoners easily carry out their schemes, while the good suffer only added hardship.

entries.zh: 應令大小官吏，可結速結，無多株引，庶上下相愛，暴亂不作矣。
entries.en: Officials at every level should be required to close cases promptly when they can, without dragging in unrelated parties, so that rulers and ruled may live in mutual regard and violent disorder may be prevented.
entries.literal: Officials great and small should be ordered to conclude cases that can be concluded quickly, without implicating many others, so that superiors and subordinates may love one another and violent disorder not arise.

entries.zh: 至所謂養民之政，不外於農桑本務。
entries.en: As for policies that truly nurture the people, they come down to nothing more than the fundamental work of farming and sericulture.
entries.literal: As for what is called the policy of nurturing the people, it does not go beyond the fundamental tasks of farming and sericulture.

entries.zh: 大江以南，地不如中原之廣，每歲漕儲正供，為京畿所仰給者，無他，人力盡也。
entries.en: South of the Yangzi the land is narrower than the Central Plain, yet each year the canal grain that feeds the capital comes from there alone—the people have given all their strength.
entries.literal: South of the Great River the land is not as broad as the Central Plain; each year the regular grain tribute transported by canal, on which the capital region relies for supply, has no other source—the people's labor is exhausted.

entries.zh: 兗州以北，古稱沃衍；
entries.en: North of Yanzhou was once renowned as rich and fertile;
entries.literal: North of Yanzhou was anciently called fertile and expansive;

entries.zh: 河南一省，皆殷、週畿內；
entries.en: the whole of Henan lay within the heartlands of the Yin and Zhou;
entries.literal: the whole province of Henan lay within the inner domains of Yin and Zhou;

entries.zh: 燕、趙之間，亦夙稱富國。
entries.en: and the lands between Yan and Zhao were long famed as prosperous states.
entries.literal: the region between Yan and Zhao was also long called a wealthy country.

entries.zh: 今則地成曠土，人盡惰民，安得不窮困而為盜賊？
entries.en: Today those fields lie fallow and the people have grown idle—how can they escape poverty and turn to banditry?
entries.literal: Now the land has become wasteland and the people are all indolent commoners—how can they not fall into destitution and become bandits?

entries.zh: 歲一歉收，先請緩徵，稍甚則加蠲貸，又其甚則截漕發粟以賑之，所以耗國帑者何可算也。
entries.en: After a poor harvest, tax collection is first deferred; if conditions worsen, remissions and loans follow; in the worst cases canal grain is diverted for relief—the drain on the treasury is incalculable.
entries.literal: In a year of poor harvest, deferment of collection is first requested; if somewhat worse, remission and loans are added; if still worse, canal grain is diverted and grain issued for relief—the drain on the national treasury is beyond calculation.

entries.zh: 運河屢淤，東南漕未可恃，設有意外，何以處此？
entries.en: The Grand Canal silts up again and again, and southeastern grain transport cannot be relied on—if disaster strikes, how will the capital be fed?
entries.literal: The Grand Canal is repeatedly silted up; southeastern canal transport cannot be relied upon—if some unforeseen event occurs, how is this to be dealt with?

entries.zh: 臣見歷來保薦州縣，必首列勸課農桑，其實盡屬虛談，從無過問。
entries.en: In every recommendation of local magistrates, promoting farming and sericulture heads the list, yet in practice this is mere rhetoric and no one ever checks.
entries.literal: Your subject has seen that in recommendations of county and district magistrates, exhortation to promote farming and sericulture is always listed first, yet in reality it is all empty talk and never followed up.

entries.zh: 大吏奏報糧價，有市價至四五千錢，僅報二兩內外，其於收成，又虛加分數，相習成風。
entries.en: Senior officials reporting grain prices will cite market rates of four or five thousand cash per unit while reporting only about two taels, and routinely inflate harvest figures—a practice now habitual throughout the bureaucracy.
entries.literal: When great officials report grain prices, though market prices reach four or five thousand cash, they report only about two taels; as for harvest yields, they also inflate the figures—a practice that has become habitual.

entries.zh: 但使董勸有方，行之一方而收利，自然爭起相效，田野皆闢，水旱有資，豈必盡資官帑，善政乃行哉？
entries.en: With sound supervision and encouragement, once one region prospered others would naturally follow; wasteland would be reclaimed and reserves built against flood and drought—good government need not depend entirely on the treasury.
entries.literal: If only supervision and encouragement were well directed, and implemented in one region with profit gained, naturally all would vie to follow; fields would all be opened, and there would be resources against flood and drought—must one rely entirely on the official treasury for good government to be carried out?

entries.zh: 民之犯刑，由於不率教；
entries.en: People break the law because they have not been properly instructed;
entries.literal: The people's violation of the penal code stems from not following instruction;

entries.zh: 其不率教，由於衣食缺乏而廉恥不興。
entries.en: and they fail to follow instruction because they lack food and clothing and therefore lack the sense of honor and shame that instruction requires.
entries.literal: their failure to follow instruction stems from lack of food and clothing and the failure of probity and shame to arise.

entries.zh: 其次第如此，故養民為首務也。」
entries.en: This is the chain of causation; nurturing the people must therefore come first."
entries.literal: The sequence of causes is thus; therefore nurturing the people is the foremost task."

entries.zh: 奏入，仁宗嘉納之，特詔飭各省以勸課農桑為亟，速清訟獄，嚴懲誣枉。
entries.en: The memorial was well received by Emperor Renzong, who issued a special edict ordering every province to prioritize agricultural promotion, clear court backlogs swiftly, and punish false accusations severely.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Renzong praised and accepted it, issuing a special edict ordering each province to make exhortation to farming and sericulture urgent, to clear lawsuits and prisons quickly, and to punish severely false accusations.

entries.zh: 文田持己方嚴，數督學政，革除陋例，斥偽體，拔真才，典試號得士。
entries.en: Wentian was known for strict personal integrity; as education commissioner he abolished corrupt practices, rejected spurious examination styles, and selected genuine talent—his examinations were famed for producing worthy scholars.
entries.literal: Wentian held himself with strict integrity; he several times supervised education, abolished improper practices, rejected spurious literary styles, selected true talent, and when presiding over examinations was famed for obtaining worthy men.

entries.zh: 論學尊宋儒，所著書則宗漢學。
entries.en: In his teaching he honored Song Neo-Confucianism, yet his scholarly writings followed the Han Learning tradition.
entries.literal: In discussing learning he honored Song Neo-Confucians, yet in his writings he followed Han Learning.

entries.zh: 博綜群籍，兼諳天文佔驗。
entries.en: He mastered a wide range of texts and was also versed in astronomy and astrological divination.
entries.literal: He broadly mastered many texts and was also versed in astronomy and divination.

entries.zh: 林清之變未起，彗入紫微垣；
entries.en: Before the Lin Qing rebellion, a comet entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure;
entries.literal: Before the Lin Qing incident arose, a comet entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure;

entries.zh: 道光初，彗見南斗下，主外夷兵事：文田皆先事言之。
entries.en: at the start of the Daoguang reign a comet appeared below the Southern Dipper, portending war with foreigners—Wentian had predicted each of these events in advance.
entries.literal: at the beginning of Daoguang a comet appeared below the Southern Dipper, presaging military affairs with foreign barbarians—Wentian had spoken of all these beforehand.

entries.zh: 姚文田，字秋農，浙江歸安人。
entries.en: Yao Wentian, whose courtesy name was Qiunong, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Yao Wentian, courtesy name Qiunong, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 乾隆五十九年，高宗幸天津，召試第一，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。
entries.en: In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, serving as a Grand Council clerk.
entries.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong, the Gaozong Emperor visited Tianjin; he ranked first in the summoned examination and was appointed Inner Cabinet Secretary, serving as a clerk of the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年一甲一名進士，授修撰。
entries.en: In 1799 he took the jinshi degree as the top scholar in the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi of the first rank in the first class and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

entries.zh: 迭典廣東、福建鄉試，督廣東、河南學政，累遷祭酒。
entries.en: He successively served as chief examiner for the Guangdong and Fujian provincial examinations, held the post of education commissioner in Guangdong and Henan, and rose step by step to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: In succession he presided over the provincial examinations of Guangdong and Fujian, supervised education as provincial education commissioner in Guangdong and Henan, and was promoted repeatedly until he became Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 鮑桂星，字雙五，安徽歙縣人。
entries.en: Bao Guixing, whose courtesy name was Shuangwu, came from She County in Anhui.
entries.literal: Bao Guixing, style name Shuangwu, was a man of She County, Anhui.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷中允。
entries.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose to vice-director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was promoted to vice-director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 九年，典試河南，留學政。
entries.en: In the ninth year he presided over the Henan provincial examination and stayed on as educational commissioner.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he served as chief examiner for Henan and remained behind as educational commissioner.

entries.zh: 十三年，典試江西。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he served as chief examiner for Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 十五年，督湖北學政。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he supervised education in Hubei.

entries.zh: 累遷至內閣學士。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 十八年，任滿，既受代，聞林清之變，疏陳十事，急馳至京，仁宗嘉之，曰：「汝所奏已次第施行矣。」
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, as soon as his term ended and he had handed over his post, he learned of Lin Qing's uprising. He submitted a memorial outlining ten measures and rushed to the capital. Emperor Renzong praised him, saying, "The items you raised are already being implemented, one after another."
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, when his term ended and he had already handed over office, he heard of the Lin Qing incident, memorialized ten matters in a memorial, and hurried to the capital; the Renzong Emperor praised him, saying, "What you memorialized has already been carried out in order."

entries.zh: 擢工部侍郎，充武英殿總裁。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice minister of Works and appointed chief director of the Wuying Hall.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Works and made chief director of the Wuying Hall.

entries.zh: 桂星性質直，勇於任事。
entries.en: Guixing was blunt and upright by nature, and bold in shouldering responsibility.
entries.literal: Guixing's nature was upright and blunt, and he was bold in taking on affairs.

entries.zh: 十九年，疏陳刊書及校勘事宜。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year he submitted a memorial on book publishing and textual collation.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized on the publication of books and matters of collation and proofreading.

entries.zh: 又劾提調劉榮​​黼等不職，命王大臣按之。
entries.en: He also impeached supervising officials including Liu Rongdian for neglect of duty, and the throne ordered a senior prince-minister to conduct an inquiry.
entries.literal: He also impeached the supervising officials Liu Rongdian and others for dereliction of duty, and the emperor ordered a princely minister to investigate.

entries.zh: 榮黼面訐桂星曾言滿總裁熙昌所校，不過偏旁點畫，修改徒延時日；
entries.en: Rongdian confronted Guixing in person, alleging that Guixing had once said the Manchu chief director Xi Chang's collation work amounted to nothing more than tweaking radicals and stroke dots, needlessly dragging out the schedule;
entries.literal: Rongdian confronted Guixing face to face, charging that Guixing had once said that what the Manchu chief director Xi Chang had collated amounted only to radicals and dots and strokes, and that the revisions merely prolonged the days;

entries.zh: 且言近日有旨，旗人不足恃，故督撫多用漢人。
entries.en: and further claimed that a recent edict had declared Bannermen unreliable, so that governors-general and governors were increasingly appointing Han Chinese.
entries.literal: and he also said that recently there had been an edict that Bannermen could not be relied upon, so governors-general and governors increasingly employed Han Chinese.

entries.zh: 上聞之，怒，命傳詢。
entries.en: The emperor heard of it, grew furious, and ordered the matter referred for investigation.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard this he grew angry and ordered the matter transmitted for inquiry.

entries.zh: 桂星對聞自侍郎周兆基，且言在部與滿員共事，多有徇私背公，而兆基不承；
entries.en: Guixing answered that he had heard it from Vice Minister Zhou Zhaoji, adding that in the ministry he had often seen Manchu colleagues indulge private favor at public expense, which Zhaoji denied;
entries.literal: Guixing replied that he had heard it from vice minister Zhou Zhaoji, and also said that in the ministry, when working with Manchu colleagues, there was much favoritism contrary to the public good, yet Zhaoji would not admit it;

entries.zh: 又指同官熙昌及慶溥囑託部事，兩人亦不承。
entries.en: he also accused colleagues Xi Chang and Qing Pu of soliciting favors in ministry business, and both denied it.
entries.literal: he also named colleagues Xi Chang and Qing Pu as having solicited favors in ministry affairs, and neither of the two would admit it.

entries.zh: 以任性妄言，下部嚴議，詔斥桂星指訐慶溥、熙昌囑託無據，其咎小；
entries.en: For reckless and willful speech the case was sent to the ministry for severe deliberation. An edict rebuked Guixing: his charge that Qing Pu and Xi Chang had solicited favors lacked proof and was a lesser offense;
entries.literal: Because of willful reckless speech, the case was sent down to the ministry for severe deliberation; an edict rebuked Guixing: accusing Qing Pu and Xi Chang of solicitation was without evidence—the fault was small;

entries.zh: 妄言朝廷輕滿洲重漢人，亂政之大者：革職，不准回籍，令在京閉門思過，責五城御史嚴察；
entries.en: but claiming the court slighted Manchus while favoring Han Chinese was a grave offense against good government. He was stripped of office, forbidden to return home, ordered to remain in Beijing under house arrest to reflect on his conduct, with the Five-City censors instructed to keep strict watch;
entries.literal: recklessly saying that the court slighted Manchus and favored Han Chinese was a great matter of disordering government: he was dismissed from office, not permitted to return to his native place, ordered to remain in the capital behind closed doors to reflect on his faults, and the Five-City censors were charged to watch him strictly;

entries.zh: 如私著詩文有怨望誹謗之詞，從重治罪。
entries.en: and if any private poetry or prose he composed contained resentment or slander, he was to be punished severely.
entries.literal: if in private writings of poetry or prose there were words of resentment, discontent, or slander, he was to be punished severely.

entries.zh: 越五年，上意解，复官編修。
entries.en: Five years later, when the emperor's anger had cooled, Guixing was restored to his former post as compiler.
entries.literal: Five years later the emperor's anger eased, and his office as compiler was restored.

entries.zh: 宣宗即位，召對，諭曰：「汝昔所劾，今已罷斥。」
entries.en: When Emperor Daoguang ascended the throne, Guixing was summoned for an audience. The emperor told him, "The men you impeached back then have now been removed from office."
entries.literal: When the Daoguang Emperor took the throne, Guixing was summoned for audience; the emperor instructed him, saying, "Those you impeached in the past have now been dismissed."

entries.zh: 擢侍講，又擢通政司副使，意頗鄉用。
entries.en: He was promoted to expositor-in-waiting and then to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and the court appeared ready to make greater use of him.
entries.literal: He was promoted to expositor-in-waiting, then again to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and the court seemed inclined to employ him.

entries.zh: 道光四年，擢詹事。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒。
entries.en: Not long afterward he died.
entries.literal: Before long he died.

entries.zh: 吳孝銘，字伯新，江蘇陽湖人。
entries.en: Wu Xiaoming, whose courtesy name was Boxin, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Wu Xiaoming, style name Boxin, was a man of Yanghu, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十四年進士，選庶吉士，散館授工部主事，充軍機章京。
entries.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and on leaving the academy was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and then clerk in the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and served as a Grand Council clerk.

entries.zh: 十八年，林清之亂甫定，大軍會攻滑縣，孝銘從大臣行，參軍事。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, just after Lin Qing's rebellion was suppressed, imperial forces converged on Huaxian. Xiaoming accompanied the commanding ministers and assisted in military planning.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Lin Qing uprising had just been pacified, the great army converged to attack Huaxian; Xiaoming accompanied the great ministers on the campaign and took part in military affairs.

entries.zh: 累遷郎中。
entries.en: He rose in succession to the rank of director.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to director.

entries.zh: 道光中，回疆用兵，首逆張格爾潛逋未獲，議者欲以克復四城，分封回部酋長。
entries.en: During the Daoguang reign, as campaigns continued in the Western Regions, the rebel leader Zhang Ge'er was still at large. Some officials proposed enfeoffing Muslim chieftains by parceling out the four recovered cities among them.
entries.literal: In the Daoguang period, when troops were used in the Muslim borderlands, the chief rebel Zhang Ge'er remained at large uncaptured; some advisers wished to enfeoff Muslim tribal chiefs by dividing the four recovered cities among them.

entries.zh: 孝銘密言於樞臣曰：「是可行於乾隆時，不可行於今日，行之邊患且益甚。」
entries.en: Xiaoming told the Grand Council privately, "That might have worked in the Qianlong era, but not today. Carry it out and the frontier crisis will only deepen."
entries.literal: Xiaoming said privately to the Grand Council: "This could be done in the Qianlong period; it cannot be done today. If done, border troubles will grow worse still."

entries.zh: 議中止。
entries.en: The plan was dropped.
entries.literal: The proposal was halted.

entries.zh: 張格爾旋就俘，賜花翎。
entries.en: Zhang Ge'er was captured soon afterward, and Xiaoming was awarded the peacock feather insignia.
entries.literal: Zhang Ge'er was soon captured, and Xiaoming was granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 左都御史松筠出為熱河都統，蓴上疏，謂松筠正人，宜留置左右，失上意，降編修，九歲不調。
entries.en: When Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun was posted out as commander of Rehe, Chun memorialized that Songyun was a man of integrity who should be kept close to the throne. The memorial displeased the emperor; Chun was demoted to compiler and went nine years without a new appointment.
entries.literal: When Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun was sent out as commander of Rehe, Chun memorialized, saying Songyun was an upright man and ought to be kept at the emperor's side; he lost imperial favor, was demoted to compiler, and for nine years received no transfer.

entries.zh: 先是嘉慶中蓴在史館，撰和珅傳，及進禦，經他人竄改，和珅曾數因事被高宗詰責，並未載入傳。
entries.en: Earlier, during the Jiaqing reign, Chun had been in the Historiography Office and drafted Heshen's biography. By the time it reached the throne others had altered it, omitting the many occasions on which Emperor Gaozong had censured Heshen for misconduct.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the Jiaqing period, while Chun was in the Historiography Office he drafted the biography of Heshen; when it was presented to the throne it had been tampered with by others. Heshen had several times been rebuked by the Gaozong Emperor for various matters, yet none of this was entered in the biography.

entries.zh: 仁宗怒其失實，嚴詔詰問。
entries.en: Emperor Renzong, angered by the distortion, issued a stern edict demanding an account.
entries.literal: The Renzong Emperor was angry at its lack of truth and issued a stern edict demanding explanation.

entries.zh: 大臣以蓴原稿進，仁宗深是之，而奪竄改者官。
entries.en: Senior ministers submitted Chun's original draft. Emperor Renzong strongly endorsed it and dismissed the officials who had altered the text.
entries.literal: The great ministers submitted Chun's original draft; the Renzong Emperor deeply approved it, and stripped the tamperers of office.

entries.zh: 宣宗一日閱實錄至此事，嘉蓴直筆，因言前保留松筠，必非阿私，特擢蓴右中允。
entries.en: One day Emperor Daoguang, reading the Veritable Records, came upon the episode and praised Chun's honest historiography. Saying that Chun's earlier defense of Songyun could not have been sycophancy, he specially promoted Chun to right vice-director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: One day the Daoguang Emperor, reading the Veritable Records, came upon this affair and praised Chun's honest brush; he said that Chun's earlier effort to retain Songyun could not have been private flattery, and specially promoted Chun to right vice-director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 未一歲，复侍講學士原職。
entries.en: Within a year he was restored to his former rank as expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: In less than a year he was restored to his former post as expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 瀕年大水，江、浙、兩湖被災尤數，承回疆兵事後，度支大絀。
entries.en: Year after year there were great floods; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the lake provinces suffered especially often. Coming on the heels of the Western Region campaigns, the treasury was severely depleted.
entries.literal: Near the end of his life great floods occurred; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the two lake provinces suffered disaster especially often. This came after the border campaigns in the Muslim regions, and state revenue was severely strained.

entries.zh: 戶部擬議，宗室日以蕃衍，衣食悉仰之官，耗財之大者，請自係出世祖以上子孫皆改為覺羅，為覺羅者以次遞革。
entries.en: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a plan noting that the imperial clan was expanding daily while its members depended entirely on state stipends—a major fiscal drain. It proposed reclassifying all descendants of the Shizu Emperor and earlier as jueluo, with each new jueluo generation subject to successive reductions in rank and allowance.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a proposal: imperial clansmen daily multiplied, and food and clothing all depended on official provision—a great drain on finances. It requested that from descendants of the Shizu on upward all be changed to jueluo status, and that those made jueluo be reduced in rank in succession.

entries.zh: 孝銘曰：「茲事當密陳，不宜顯言。
entries.en: Xiaoming said, "This should be raised in confidence, not proclaimed openly.
entries.literal: Xiaoming said: "This matter ought to be reported confidentially; it should not be stated openly.

entries.zh: 法當緩更，不宜驟易。
entries.en: Reform should proceed gradually, not all at once.
entries.literal: The method ought to be changed slowly; it should not be altered abruptly.

entries.zh: 宗室久受恩養，一旦降爵減糧令下即大困，因而呼籥，朝廷不得已，將必復之，是良法美意終於不行也。」
entries.en: The clan has grown accustomed to imperial favor. The moment you cut ranks and rations they will be plunged into hardship and flood the court with petitions. Beijing will have no choice but to roll the policy back—so even a sound measure will never take hold."
entries.literal: The imperial clan has long received imperial nurture; once an order lowering rank and reducing grain allotments is issued they will at once be greatly distressed, and thus will cry out in appeal; the court will have no choice but to restore them—so a good law and fine intention will in the end not be carried out."

entries.zh: 部臣是其言，即使草奏上之。
entries.en: The ministry officials accepted his advice and had him draft the memorial for submission.
entries.literal: The ministry officials approved his words and had him draft the memorial to present it.

entries.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、光祿寺少卿、通政司參議、順天府丞，仍留直軍機處。
entries.en: He rose through vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, councillor of the Office of Transmission, and vice prefect of Shuntian, all while retaining his Grand Council post.
entries.literal: He served in succession as vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, councillor of the Office of Transmission, and vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, while remaining on duty in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 十四年，擢太僕寺卿，再遷宗人府丞。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister of the Imperial Stud and soon afterward to vice minister of the Imperial Clan Court.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and again transferred to vice minister of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 列傳一百六十四
entries.en: Biography 164
entries.literal: Biographies, Number 164

entries.zh: 林則徐至粵，盡焚躉船存煙，議外國人販煙罪。
entries.en: Lin Zexu reached Guangdong, burned all the opium stored on the receiving ships, and pressed charges against foreign traffickers.
entries.literal: Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong, completely burned the stored opium on the receiving ships, and deliberated the crime of foreigners trafficking opium.

entries.zh: 英領事義律不就約束，兵釁遂開。
entries.en: The British consul Charles Elliot refused to comply, and war broke out.
entries.literal: The English consul Elliot did not submit to restraint, and military hostilities thereupon opened.

entries.zh: 二十年，命爵滋偕左都御史祁俊藻赴福建查辦禁煙，與總督鄧廷楨籌備海防。
entries.en: In Daoguang 20 (1840), Juezi was sent with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to Fujian to oversee the opium ban and, with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, to prepare coastal defences.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, Juezi was ordered together with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to go to Fujian to investigate and handle prohibition of opium, and with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen to plan coastal defense.

entries.zh: 洎英兵來犯，廷楨屢挫敵於廈門，上疑之。
entries.en: When British forces attacked, Deng Tingzhen reported repeated victories at Xiamen, which the Emperor found hard to believe.
entries.literal: When English troops came to attack, Tingzhen repeatedly defeated the enemy at Xiamen; the Emperor was suspicious.

entries.zh: 爵滋與俊藻方至浙江按事，復命赴福建察奏。
entries.en: Juezi and Qi Junzao were inspecting affairs in Zhejiang when they were ordered back to Fujian to investigate and report.
entries.literal: Juezi and Junzao had just reached Zhejiang on an inspection mission when they were again ordered to go to Fujian to investigate and memorialize.

entries.zh: 疏陳：「廷楨所奏不誣；
entries.en: They reported: "Deng Tingzhen's accounts were not false;
entries.literal: They memorialized, stating: 'What Tingzhen reported is not false;

entries.zh: 定海不可不速復；
entries.en: Dinghai must be recovered without delay;
entries.literal: Dinghai cannot but be swiftly recovered;

entries.zh: 水師有專門之技，宜破格用人。」
entries.en: and the navy's specialized skills require appointing men outside the usual seniority rules."
entries.literal: the navy has specialized skills—it is fitting to employ men outside normal rules.'

entries.zh: 具言戰守方略。
entries.en: They laid out detailed plans for offense and defense.
entries.literal: They fully set forth strategies for fighting and defense.

entries.zh: 又言浙江為閩、粵之心腹，與江蘇為脣齒，請飭伊里布不可偏聽琦善，信敵必退。
entries.en: They also warned that Zhejiang was the strategic heart linking Fujian and Guangdong to Jiangsu, and urged the court to tell Yilibu not to heed Qishan alone or assume the enemy would simply withdraw.
entries.literal: They also said Zhejiang was the heart and belly of Fujian and Guangdong, and with Jiangsu was lip and teeth; they requested ordering Yilibu not to listen one-sidedly to Qishan and believe the enemy would certainly withdraw.

entries.zh: 及回京，復極言英人勞師襲遠不足慮，宜竟與絕市，募兵節餉，為持久計，以海防圖進。
entries.en: Back in Beijing, Juezi argued forcefully that Britain's expeditionary forces were overextended, urged a complete trade embargo, recruitment and fiscal retrenchment for a war of attrition, and submitted a coastal defence map.
entries.literal: When they returned to the capital, they again spoke at length that the English, laboring their armies to strike from afar, were not worth worrying about; it was fitting to cut off trade entirely, raise troops and economize supplies, make long-term plans, and present a coastal defense map.

entries.zh: 既而琦善在粵議撫不得要領，連歲命將出師，廣東、浙江皆不利。
entries.en: Qishan's peace negotiations in Guangdong then failed, and repeated campaigns in Guangdong and Zhejiang went badly.
entries.literal: Soon after, Qishan in Guangdong negotiated appeasement without grasping essentials; year after year generals were ordered to take the field; in Guangdong and Zhejiang all were unfavorable.

entries.zh: 二十二年，英兵由海入江，乃定和議於江寧，煙禁自此弛矣。
entries.en: In Daoguang 22 (1842), British forces advanced up the Yangzi from the sea, and peace was concluded at Nanjing—the opium prohibition was effectively abandoned.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, English troops entered the Yangzi from the sea; the peace treaty was then fixed at Jiangning, and from this the opium ban was relaxed.

entries.zh: 尋丁父憂去官。
entries.en: He soon resigned to observe mourning for his father.
entries.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his father and left office.

entries.zh: 金應麟，字亞伯，浙江錢塘人。
entries.en: Jin Yinglin (style name Yabo) came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Jin Yinglin, courtesy name Yabo, was a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 以舉人入貲為中書。
entries.en: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a secretariat drafter.
entries.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased office and became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 道光六年，成進士，授刑部主事，總辦秋審，先後從大臣讞獄四川、湖北、山西。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in Daoguang 6 (1826), was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn judicial review, and accompanied senior officials on case reviews in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn assizes, and successively followed senior ministers in reviewing cases in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.

entries.zh: 累擢郎中，改御史，遷給事中。
entries.en: He rose through the ranks to director, then censor, then supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, transferred to censor, and moved to supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 疏請修改刑例，於鬥毆、報盜、劫囚、誣告、私鑄、服舍違式、斷罪引律、奴婢毆主、故禁故勘平人、應捕人追捕罪人、犯罪存留養親、官司出入人罪、徒流遷徙地方、外省駐防逃人，逐條論列，多被採取改定；
entries.en: He memorialized for revisions to the penal code, addressing affray, reporting bandits, prison breaks, false accusation, private coining, mourning and residence violations, sentencing citations, slaves assaulting masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture, authorized pursuit of criminals, retention for filial support, official misconduct in criminal cases, places of exile, and fugitives from provincial garrisons—article by article; many of his proposals were adopted;
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting revision of the penal code, on affray, reporting bandits, rescuing prisoners, false accusation, private coining, violation of mourning and residence regulations, citing statutes in sentencing, slaves and maids beating masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture of commoners, authorized pursuers chasing criminals, crimes with retention for supporting parents, officials improperly entering or releasing persons in crimes, places of penal servitude and exile, and escaped bondsmen in provincial garrisons—discussing each article in turn; many were adopted and revised;

entries.zh: 又論銅船恣橫不法及驛站擾累諸弊，並下各省督撫禁革。
entries.en: he also exposed abuses by copper-transport boats and the burdens imposed by the courier stations, and the court ordered provincial governors to suppress them.
entries.literal: he also discussed the abuses of copper-transport ships acting lawlessly and post stations causing harassment and burdens—all were sent down to each province's governors for prohibition and reform.

entries.zh: 先後封事數十上，劾疆臣琦善、河臣吳邦慶尤為時稱。
entries.en: He submitted dozens of confidential memorials in all; his impeachments of Governor-General Qishan and river conservancy official Wu Bangqing won particular acclaim.
entries.literal: In succession he submitted several tens of confidential memorials; his impeachments of frontier official Qishan and river official Wu Bangqing were especially praised by the times.

entries.zh: 宣宗嘉其敢言，擢太常寺少卿。
entries.en: The Daoguang Emperor praised his outspokenness and promoted him to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor commended his daring speech and promoted him to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 遭憂歸，服闋，授鴻臚寺卿。
entries.en: After a period of mourning he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
entries.literal: He entered mourning and returned home; when mourning ended he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 疏論水師廢弛，漕政頹紊。
entries.en: He memorialized on the decay of the navy and the disorder of the grain transport system.
entries.literal: He memorialized on the navy's lax discipline and the grain transport administration's decline and disorder.

entries.zh: 十九年，出為直隸按察使，鞫護理長蘆鹽運使楊成業等得贓獄，論遣戍，前運使陳崇禮等並罣議。
entries.en: In Daoguang 19 he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried Acting Changlu Salt Transport Commissioner Yang Chengye and others for bribery, sentenced them to exile, and implicated former transport commissioners including Chen Chongli.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried Acting Changlu Salt Transport Commissioner Yang Chengye and others in a bribery case, sentenced them to banishment, and former transport commissioners Chen Chongli and others were also implicated in deliberation.

entries.zh: 尋召為大理寺少卿。
entries.en: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: Soon after he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 慶鏞上疏論刑賞失措，曰：「行政之要，莫大於刑賞。
entries.en: Chen Qingyong memorialized that rewards and punishments had been mishandled: "Nothing matters more in government than how punishments and rewards are applied.
entries.literal: Qingyong memorialized on the misplacement of punishments and rewards, saying: 'The essential of administering government is nothing greater than punishments and rewards.

entries.zh: 刑賞之權，操之於君，喻之於民，所以示天下之大公也。
entries.en: That authority rests with the sovereign and must be made clear to the people, for it embodies the empire's fundamental fairness.
entries.literal: The authority of punishments and rewards is wielded by the ruler and explained to the people—thereby showing the great impartiality of all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 大學論平天下之道，在於絜矩。
entries.en: The Great Learning teaches that bringing peace to the realm depends on holding the measuring square—applying the same standard to oneself that one applies to others.
entries.literal: The Great Learning discusses the Way of pacifying all under Heaven—it lies in measuring the square.

entries.zh: 矩者何，民之好惡是已。
entries.en: What is the measuring square? The people's likes and dislikes.
entries.literal: What is the square? It is the people's likes and dislikes—that is all.

entries.zh: 海疆多事以來，自總督、將軍以至州縣丞倅，禽駭獸奔。
entries.en: Since the coastal troubles began, governors-general, generals, and officials down to county deputies have fled in panic like startled birds and beasts.
entries.literal: Since coastal affairs became numerous, from governors-general and generals down to prefectural and county assistants, they were like birds startled and beasts fleeing.

entries.zh: 皇上赫然震怒，失律之罪，法有莫逭。
entries.en: The Emperor was furious, and the law allowed no escape for those who had broken discipline.
entries.literal: The Emperor manifestly shook with anger; the crime of violating discipline—under the law none could escape.

entries.zh: 於是辱國之將軍奕山、奕經，參贊文蔚，總督牛鑑，提督餘步雲，先後就逮，步雲伏法。
entries.en: The disgraced generals Yishan and Yijing, staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun were arrested in turn; Buyun was executed.
entries.literal: Thereupon the generals who disgraced the state—Yishan, Yijing, the staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun—were successively arrested; Buyun was executed according to law.

entries.zh: 血氣之倫，罔不拊手稱快，謂國法前雖未伸於琦善，今猶伸於餘步雲。
entries.en: Men of spirit applauded, saying that although the law had not reached Qishan before, it had at least been applied to Yu Buyun.
entries.literal: Men of hot blood, none did not clap hands and call it satisfying, saying that although state law before had not been applied to Qishan, now it was still applied to Yu Buyun.

entries.zh: 乃未幾起琦善為葉爾羌幫辦大臣。
entries.en: Before long, however, Qishan was reappointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
entries.literal: Yet before long Qishan was raised as assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

entries.zh: 邸報既傳，人情震駭，猶解之曰：'古聖王之待罪人，有投四裔以御魑魅者。
entries.en: When the court gazette announced this, the public was appalled, though some explained it by saying that ancient sage kings had banished criminals to the four corners of the realm to ward off evil spirits.
entries.literal: Once the court gazette spread, popular feeling was shaken with horror; yet people still explained it, saying: 'The ancient sage kings' treatment of criminals included casting them to the four borderlands to ward off demons.'

entries.zh: '皇上之於琦善，殆其類是，而今且以三品頂戴用為熱河都統矣，且用奕經為葉爾羌幫辦大臣，文蔚為古城領隊大臣矣。
entries.en: Perhaps the Emperor's treatment of Qishan was of that kind—yet now he was appointed Rehe lieutenant-general with third-rank insignia, Yijing was made Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei leading commissioner at Gucheng.
entries.literal: The Emperor's treatment of Qishan was perhaps of that kind—yet now he was employed as Rehe lieutenant-general with third-rank hat button, and Yijing was employed as Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei as leading commissioner at Gucheng.

entries.zh: 琦善於戰事方始，首先示弱，以惰軍心，海內糜爛，至於此極。
entries.en: Qishan had been the first to show weakness when war began, sapping army morale and bringing the empire to ruin.
entries.literal: Qishan, when hostilities had just begun, was first to show weakness and thereby enervate army morale; within the seas all was rotten, reaching this extreme.

entries.zh: 既罷斥終身不齒，猶恐不足饜民心而作士氣。
entries.en: Dismissal and lifelong disgrace would scarcely satisfy public outrage or restore military morale.
entries.literal: Having been dismissed and for life not ranked among gentlemen, one still fears this is insufficient to satisfy popular hearts and raise military spirit.

entries.zh: 奕經之罪，雖較琦善稍減，文蔚之罪，較奕經又減。
entries.en: Yijing's guilt was somewhat less than Qishan's, and Wenwei's somewhat less than Yijing's.
entries.literal: Yijing's crime, though somewhat less than Qishan's; Wenwei's crime, again somewhat less than Yijing's.

entries.zh: 然皇上命將出師，若何慎重。
entries.en: Yet how grave a matter it is when the Emperor sends generals to war.
entries.literal: Yet when the Emperor orders generals to take the field, how grave the matter.

entries.zh: 奕經頓兵半載，曾未身歷行間，騁其虛憍之氣，自詭一鼓而復三城；
entries.en: Yijing kept his army idle for half a year without ever seeing battle, boasted emptily that one assault would recover three cities,
entries.literal: Yijing halted his army for half a year, never personally experienced the battle line, gave rein to his empty arrogance, and falsely claimed that with one drumbeat he would recover three cities;

entries.zh: 卒之機事不密，貽笑敵人，覆軍殺將，一敗不支。
entries.en: then let his plans leak, made himself a laughingstock to the enemy, lost his army and his generals, and collapsed in a single defeat.
entries.literal: in the end his plans were not secret, he gave the enemy cause for laughter, the army was overthrown and generals killed, and one defeat could not be sustained.

entries.zh: 此不待別科騷擾供億、招權納賄之罪，而已不可勝誅。
entries.en: Without even counting his harassment of the people, waste of supplies, abuse of power, and acceptance of bribes, his crimes were already beyond measure.
entries.literal: Without waiting for separate counts of harassing the populace, provisioning expenses, grasping power, and accepting bribes, already his crimes were beyond execution.

entries.zh: 臣亦知奕經為高宗純皇帝之裔，皇上親親睦族，不忍遽加顯戮。
entries.en: I know that Yijing is a descendant of the Qianlong Emperor, and that Your Majesty, cherishing imperial kin, is reluctant to execute him outright.
entries.literal: Your servant also knows that Yijing is a descendant of the Gaozong Chun Emperor, and the Emperor, cherishing kin and harmonizing the clan, is unwilling hastily to add manifest execution.

entries.zh: 然即幸邀寬典，亦當禁錮終身，無為天潢宗室羞，豈圖收禁未及三月，輒复棄瑕錄用？
entries.en: Even if he were spared, he should be imprisoned for life rather than bring shame on the imperial house—who imagined he would be released and reappointed in less than three months?
entries.literal: Yet even if he fortunately receives lenient treatment, he should still be imprisoned for life, not bringing shame on the imperial clan—who would have thought that confinement had not reached three months before he was again employed despite his flaws?

entries.zh: 且此數人者，皇上特未知其見惡於民之深耳。
entries.en: Moreover, Your Majesty may not yet realize how deeply the people hate these men.
entries.literal: Moreover, regarding these several men, the Emperor simply does not yet know how deeply they are hated by the people.

entries.zh: 倘俯採輿論，孰不切齒琦善為罪魁，誰不疾首於奕山、奕經、牛鑑、文蔚，而以為投畀之不容緩？
entries.en: If Your Majesty heeded public opinion, who would not denounce Qishan as the chief culprit, or demand that Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei be cast out without delay?
entries.literal: If Your Majesty would condescend to adopt popular opinion, who would not gnash teeth at Qishan as chief culprit? Who would not wring hands at Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei, and regard casting them out as not to be delayed?

entries.zh: 此非臣一人之私言也。
entries.en: This is not my opinion alone.
entries.literal: This is not your servant's private words alone.

entries.zh: 側聞琦善意侈體汰，跋扈如常，葉爾羌之行，本屬怏怏；
entries.en: I hear that Qishan remains as extravagant and overbearing as ever and went to Yarkand reluctantly;
entries.literal: Your servant has heard on the side that Qishan's intentions were extravagant and his person dissolute, overbearing as before; the journey to Yarkand was originally undertaken resentfully;

entries.zh: 今果未及出關，即蒙召還。
entries.en: and before he had even left the frontier pass, he was recalled.
entries.literal: now in truth before he had even passed beyond the pass he received summons to return.

entries.zh: 熱河密邇神京，有識無識，莫不撫膺太息，以為皇上鄉用琦善之意，尚不止此。
entries.en: Rehe lies close to the capital; learned and common people alike sigh in dismay, fearing the Emperor intends to employ Qishan even closer to court.
entries.literal: Rehe is close to the divine capital; the informed and uninformed alike beat their breasts and sigh deeply, thinking the Emperor's intention to employ Qishan near home does not stop here.

entries.zh: 萬一有事，則熒惑聖聰者，必仍系斯人。
entries.en: If trouble should arise again, this same man would surely be the one to mislead Your Majesty.
entries.literal: If by chance something occurs, then he who would bewilder the sage hearing must still be this man.

entries.zh: 履霜堅冰，深可懍懼。
entries.en: As the proverb says, frost underfoot foretells solid ice—a prospect that should fill us with dread.
entries.literal: Treading frost leads to solid ice—deeply to be feared with dread.

entries.zh: 頃者禦試翰詹，以'烹阿封即墨'命題，而今茲刑賞顧如此，臣未知皇上所謂阿者何人？
entries.en: At the recent Hanlin examination the topic was "boiling A and enfeoffing Jimo," yet rewards and punishments now run the opposite way—I do not know whom Your Majesty considers "A."
entries.literal: Recently at the imperial examination for Hanlin bachelors the topic was 'boiling A and enfeoffing Jimo'; yet now punishments and rewards turn out thus—your servant does not know whom the Emperor calls 'A'?

entries.zh: 即墨者何人？
entries.en: And who is "Jimo"?
entries.literal: And who is 'Jimo'?

entries.zh: 假如聖意高深，偶或差忒，而以即墨為阿，阿為即墨，將毋譽之毀之者有以淆亂是非耶？
entries.en: If the imperial mind has erred and Jimo is treated as A and A as Jimo, will not flatterers and detractors alike confuse right and wrong?
entries.literal: Suppose the sage intention is profound and occasionally errs, and Jimo is taken for A and A for Jimo—will not those who praise and those who destroy have means to confuse right and wrong?

entries.zh: 所望皇上立奮天威，收回成命，體大學絜矩之旨，鑑盈廷毀譽之真，國法稍伸，民心可慰。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to rouse imperial authority, withdraw these appointments, heed the Great Learning's teaching on the measuring square, discern true praise and blame in the court, give the law some force, and console the people's hearts."
entries.literal: What is hoped is that the Emperor will immediately rouse heavenly authority, withdraw the settled order, embody the Great Learning's intent of the measuring square, discern the truth of praise and blame filling the court, let state law be somewhat applied, and popular hearts be consoled.'

entries.zh: 疏上，宣宗嘉之，諭曰：「朕無知人之明，以致琦善、奕經、文蔚諸人喪師失律，惟有反躬自責，不欲諉罪臣工。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the Daoguang Emperor praised it and said: "I lacked the wisdom to judge men, and so Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and broke discipline. I can only blame myself and will not shift guilt onto my officials.
entries.literal: When the memorial went up, the Xuanzong Emperor commended it and instructed, saying: 'We lack the clarity to know men, so that Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and the rest lost armies and violated discipline—we can only turn and blame ourselves, and do not wish to shift guilt onto officials.

entries.zh: 今該御史請收回成命，朕非文過飾非之君，豈肯回護？」
