entries.en: This censor asks me to withdraw my orders. I am not a ruler who covers his faults—how could I shield them?"
entries.literal: Now this censor requests withdrawing the settled order. We are not a ruler who covers faults and whitewashes errors—how could We be willing to shield them?'

entries.zh: 复革琦善等職，令閉門思過。
entries.en: He then stripped Qishan and the others of their posts and ordered them to remain at home in reflection.
entries.literal: He again stripped Qishan and the others of office and ordered them to close their doors and reflect on their faults.

entries.zh: 於是直聲震海內。
entries.en: His reputation for integrity then resounded throughout the empire.
entries.literal: Thereupon his upright reputation shook all within the seas.

entries.zh: 黃爵滋金應麟陳慶鏞蘇廷魁朱琦
entries.en: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi
entries.literal: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, Zhu Qi

entries.zh: 陳慶鏞，字頌南，福建晉江人。
entries.en: Chen Qingyong (style name Songnan) came from Jinjiang in Fujian.
entries.literal: Chen Qingyong, courtesy name Songnan, was a man of Jinjiang in Fujian.

entries.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授戶部主事，遷員外郎，授御史。
entries.en: He earned his jinshi in Daoguang 12 (1832), entered the Hanlin Academy, was posted to the Ministry of Revenue as a principal clerk, rose to vice director, and was made a censor.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, on leaving the academy was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to outside-section vice director, and was appointed censor.

entries.zh: 二十三年，海疆僨事，獲罪諸臣浸復起用。
entries.en: In Daoguang 23, after the coastal disasters, officials who had been punished were gradually brought back into service.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, when coastal affairs went awry, the various officials who had been punished were gradually reemployed.

entries.zh: 列傳一百六十五
entries.en: Biography 165
entries.literal: Biographies 165

entries.zh: 二十七年，安集延布魯特糾合回子圍喀什噶爾、英吉沙爾，詔布彥泰率兵赴肅州，授為定西將軍，奕山為參贊大臣，將大舉出師。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year Kokand and Burut allies with local Muslims besieged Kashgar and Yengisar; Bu Yantai was ordered to Jiuquan as Pacification General of the West, with Yishan as adviser, for a major campaign.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year [1847], Kokand and the Buruts joined with Muslims to besiege Kashgar and Yengisar; Bu Yantai was ordered to lead troops to Jiuquan, appointed Pacification General of the West, with Yishan as adviser, for a major expedition.

entries.zh: 會奕山率邊兵戰捷，賊退，二城解圍，軍事告竣，布彥泰回任。
entries.en: Yishan's frontier force won, the enemy withdrew, both cities were saved, and Bu Yantai returned to his governorship.
entries.literal: Yishan led frontier troops to victory, the rebels retreated, the two cities were relieved, military affairs concluded, and Bu Yantai returned to his post.

entries.zh: 二十九年，因病請罷，許之。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year he sought release for illness and was allowed to retire.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year [1849], he asked to resign on account of illness and was permitted.

entries.zh: 時為固原知州徐采饒等所訐，命協辦大學士祁俊藻往會總督琦善按之，坐關防不密、清查歧誤，及失察家人，議降調革任。
entries.en: He was then denounced by Guyuan prefect Xu Cairao and others; Associate Grand Secretary Qi Junzao joined Governor-General Qishan in an inquiry; lax seals, audit mistakes, and unchecked servants earned a sentence of demotion and dismissal.
entries.literal: At that time he was impeached by Guyuan prefect Xu Cairao and others; Associate Grand Secretary Qi Junzao was sent to join Governor-General Qishan in investigation; he was found guilty of lax seal control, errors in audit, and failure to supervise his household, and was sentenced to demotion, dismissal, and forfeiture.

entries.zh: 尋予二等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣，調伊犁參贊大臣，偕將軍奕山會議俄羅斯通商事宜，語詳奕山傳。
entries.en: Soon he was restored as second-class bodyguard, made assistant minister at Yarkand, then Ili resident commissioner, and with General Yishan handled Russian trade—the details appear in Yishan's biography.
entries.literal: Soon after he was given second-class bodyguard and served as assistant minister at Yarkand, was transferred to Ili resident commissioner, and with General Yishan negotiated Russian trade matters, detailed in Yishan's biography.

entries.zh: 咸豐二年，授正白旗漢軍副都統，仍留邊任。
entries.en: In the second year of Xianfeng he was made vice commander of the Plain White Chinese Banner but kept on the frontier.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng [1852], he was appointed vice commander of the Plain White Chinese Banner while remaining on frontier duty.

entries.zh: 四年，回京，命赴王慶坨軍營，以疾未行，請開缺。
entries.en: In the fourth year he returned to Beijing, was ordered to the Wangqingtuo camp, could not go for illness, and asked to be relieved.
entries.literal: In the fourth year [1854], he returned to the capital and was ordered to the Wangqingtuo army camp; illness prevented his going, and he asked to be relieved.

entries.zh: 光緒六年，卒，年九十。
entries.en: He died in the sixth year of Guangxu, aged ninety.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu [1880], he died at the age of ninety.

entries.zh: 詔念前勞，依都統例賜卹。
entries.en: The throne remembered his earlier service and granted commander-level funeral honors.
entries.literal: An edict recalled his earlier service and granted funeral honors according to the commander standard.

entries.zh: 二十七年，安集延布魯特回眾入卡，圍喀什噶爾、英吉沙爾二城，薩迎阿檄調諸城兵往剿，葉爾羌參贊大臣奕山率諸軍由巴爾楚克進，三戰皆捷。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year Kokand and Burut Muslims crossed the pass and besieged Kashgar and Yengisar; Sa Ying'a mobilized the garrison cities while Yishan advanced from Barkul and won three straight victories.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year [1847], Kokand and Burut Muslims entered the border pass and besieged Kashgar and Yengisar; Sa Ying'a ordered troops from the garrison cities to suppress them; Yarkand resident commissioner Yishan led the armies forward from Barkul and won three battles in succession.

entries.zh: 薩迎阿別遣兵扼樹窩子，二城圍尋解。
entries.en: Sa Ying'a also blocked Shuwozi with a detached force, and both sieges soon lifted.
entries.literal: Sa Ying'a separately sent troops to hold Shuwozi, and the sieges of the two cities were soon lifted.

entries.zh: 時方命陝甘總督布彥泰督師，未出關而事平。
entries.en: Bu Yantai had just been ordered to take command, but the crisis ended before he crossed the frontier.
entries.literal: At that time Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Bu Yantai had just been ordered to command the army, but before he left the pass the affair was settled.

entries.zh: 咸豐元年，召授正白旗滿洲都統，會陝甘總督琦善剿青海番匪，言官劾其妄殺，命薩迎阿赴西寧按之。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianfeng he was made Plain White Manchu Banner commander; when censors accused Qishan of slaughter in the Qinghai fan campaign, Sa Ying'a was sent to Xining to investigate.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng [1851], he was summoned and appointed Manchu commander of the Plain White Banner; when Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Qishan was suppressing Qinghai fan bandits, censors impeached Qishan for indiscriminate killing, and Sa Ying'a was ordered to Xining to investigate.

entries.zh: 奏調刑部司員梁照、奎椿、武汝清隨同鞫訊，得番子十四名無辜誣服狀，疏陳琦善剿辦黑城撒拉回子及黃喀窪番賊，尚非無故興師，惟將雍沙番族殺斃多名，實係妄加誅戮，並及文武妄拿、刑求逼供，詔褫琦善職，逮京訊治，命薩迎阿暫署陝甘總督。
entries.en: With Ministry of Justice clerks Liang Zhao, Kuichun, and Wu Ruqing he found fourteen fan had confessed under duress; Qishan's strikes at Heicheng Salars and Huangkawa bandits were not wholly groundless, but the Yongsha killings and torture were real; Qishan was stripped and sent to Beijing for trial while Sa Ying'a acted as governor-general.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting Ministry of Justice clerks Liang Zhao, Kuichun, and Wu Ruqing to join the inquiry; fourteen fan were found to have confessed under false charges; he reported that Qishan's campaigns against Heicheng Salar Muslims and Huangkawa fan bandits were not wholly without cause, but that killing many of the Yongsha fan clan was truly indiscriminate slaughter, together with civil and military officials' wrongful arrests and torture to force confession; an edict stripped Qishan of office and summoned him to the capital for trial, and ordered Sa Ying'a to act temporarily as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

entries.zh: 甘肅營務廢弛，雖議整頓，而番匪時復出擾。
entries.en: Gansu defenses remained slack; fan raids continued despite talk of reform.
entries.literal: Gansu military affairs were lax; although reorganization was discussed, fan bandits again raided from time to time.

entries.zh: 新授福建巡撫王懿德途經金縣，士民呈控，奏下薩迎阿察治，屢被詰責。
entries.en: When incoming Fujian governor Wang Yide passed Jinxian, locals petitioned; the case went to Sa Ying'a, who drew repeated reprimands.
entries.literal: The newly appointed Fujian governor Wang Yide, passing through Jinxian, was petitioned by local scholars and commoners; the memorial was sent down to Sa Ying'a for investigation and he was repeatedly rebuked.

entries.zh: 二年，解任回京。
entries.en: In the second year he was relieved and returned to Beijing.
entries.literal: In the second year [1852], he was relieved and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 自琦善之逮治也，刑部尚書恆春以薩迎阿論劾過當，欲令原訊司員對簿，獨侍郎曾國籓持不可。
entries.en: After Qishan's arrest, Justice Minister Hengchun thought Sa Ying'a had overreached and wanted the original clerks to confront him; only Vice Minister Zeng Guofan dissented.
entries.literal: From the time of Qishan's arrest, Minister of Justice Hengchun held that Sa Ying'a's impeachment had been excessive and wished the original examining clerks to confront him in court; only Vice Minister Zeng Guofan objected.

entries.zh: 及廷臣會訊讞上，琦善遣戍吉林，司道以下文武論罪有差，被誣番子免罪，略如原讞。
entries.en: At the joint court review Qishan went to exile in Jilin, officials were punished by rank, the framed fan were freed, and the outcome largely matched Sa Ying'a's report.
entries.literal: When the court ministers jointly reported the verdict, Qishan was exiled to Jilin, civil and military officials from intendant down were punished in varying degrees, the falsely charged fan were acquitted, and the outcome largely followed the original finding.

entries.zh: 薩迎阿坐未取應議各員供詞，遽行擬罪，又因子書紳與司員同坐問供，下部議，書紳降三級調用，薩迎阿降四級留任。
entries.en: Sa Ying'a was faulted for sentencing before collecting required testimony and for letting his son Shuzhen sit with the clerks; Shuzhen was demoted three ranks, Sa Ying'a four but kept in post.
entries.literal: Sa Ying'a was found guilty of sentencing without first obtaining the statements of officials who should have been consulted, and also because his son Shuzhen sat with the clerks during interrogation; the ministry deliberated: Shuzhen was demoted three ranks and transferred, Sa Ying'a demoted four ranks but retained in office.

entries.zh: 歷署鑲藍旗、正紅旗蒙古都統。
entries.en: He later acted as Mongol commander of the Bordered Blue and Plain Red Banners.
entries.literal: He successively acted as Mongol commander of the Bordered Blue and Plain Red Banners.

entries.zh: 六年，出署西安將軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he went out to act as Xi'an general.
entries.literal: In the sixth year [1856], he went out to act as Xi'an general.

entries.zh: 逾歲卒，詔念回疆軍務曾著勞績，賜卹，諡恪僖。
entries.en: He died a little over a year later; the throne recalled his frontier service, granted funeral honors, and gave the posthumous title Kexi.
entries.literal: A little more than a year later he died; an edict recalled his meritorious service on the Muslim borderlands, granted funeral honors, and gave the posthumous title Kexi.

entries.zh: 瑚松額，巴岳忒氏，滿洲正黃旗人，西安駐防。
entries.en: Hu Song'e, of the Bayuete clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner on garrison duty at Xi'an.
entries.literal: Hu Song'e, of the Bayuete clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, stationed at the Xi'an garrison.

entries.zh: 嘉慶初，以前鋒從將軍恆瑞剿湖北教匪，後隸那彥成、德楞泰部下，積功擢協領。
entries.en: Early in the Jiaqing reign he served as a vanguard under General Hengrui in the campaign against the Hubei sect rebels, then came under Nayancheng and Delengtai; his accumulated merit won him promotion to assistant commander.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign, as a vanguard he followed General Hengrui to suppress the sect rebels in Hubei; later he served under Nayancheng and Delengtai, and through accumulated merit was promoted to assistant commander.

entries.zh: 十八年，滑縣教匪起，瑚松額率馬隊從副都統富僧德戰道口及滑縣城下，屢有功，賜花翎。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, when sect rebels broke out in Huaxian, Hu Song'e led mounted troops with Vice Commander Fu Sengde at Daokou and beneath the walls of Huaxian, winning repeated credit and receiving a peacock feather.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year [1813], when sect rebels rose in Huaxian, Hu Song'e led cavalry following Vice Commander Fu Sengde to fight at Daokou and below Huaxian city wall, repeatedly distinguishing himself, and was awarded a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 二十三年，擢福州副都統，署福州將軍。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Fuzhou vice commander and served as acting Fuzhou general.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year [1818], he was promoted to vice commander at Fuzhou and acted as Fuzhou general.

entries.zh: 二十六年，偕尚書文慶按長蘆鹽運使陳鑑挪撥鹽課，彌補加價，褫其職，歷任鹽政運司議譴有差。
entries.en: In 1846, with Wen Qing, he investigated Changlu transport commissioner Chen Jian for diverting salt revenue to cover surcharges; Chen was dismissed and past salt officials punished in varying degrees.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Minister Wen Qing he investigated Changlu salt transport commissioner Chen Jian's diversion of salt revenue to cover price increases; Chen was dismissed and successive salt officials were censured to varying degrees.

entries.zh: 二十九年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士，命赴甘肅偕琦善按前任總督布彥泰清查舛誤、縱容家丁，下嚴議。
entries.en: In 1849, as revenue minister and associate grand secretary, he went to Gansu with Qi Shan to investigate ex-governor-general Buyantai for accounting errors and tolerating servants; Buyantai was severely punished.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary, he was ordered to Gansu with Qi Shan to investigate former governor-general Buyantai for errors in accounts and indulgence of household servants; severe punishment was imposed.

entries.zh: 回京，請便道省墓，途次聞宣宗崩，過里門不入。
entries.en: On the way back he asked to visit his ancestors' graves; hearing of Daoguang's death on the road, he passed his own gate without entering.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital he asked to visit his family's graves en route; on the road he heard of Xuanzong's death and did not enter his home though he passed the gate.

entries.zh: 文宗即位，拜體仁閣大學士，仍管戶部。
entries.en: When Xianfeng succeeded, Junzao became grand secretary of the Tiren Hall and still headed revenue.
entries.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Junzao was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall and still headed the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 俊藻自道光中論洋務與穆彰阿不合，至是文宗銳意圖治，罷穆彰阿，俊藻遂領樞務，開言路，起用舊臣，俊藻左右之。
entries.en: Since Daoguang he had clashed with Mujangga over foreign policy; now Xianfeng meant to govern vigorously, removed Mujangga, and Junzao led the council, reopened memorial channels, and brought back veteran ministers—Junzao at his side throughout.
entries.literal: Junzao had disagreed with Mujangga on foreign affairs since the Daoguang era; now Wenzong was eager to reform, dismissed Mujangga, and Junzao took the lead in council affairs, opened channels for memorials, and reemployed old ministers—with Junzao guiding him.

entries.zh: 粵匪北犯，心存疏言賊氛逼近，請扼河而守，畿南直駐重兵，河南、山西、陝西各要隘並力堵截，速調駐熱河、綏遠之蒙古馬隊進口內衛京畿；
entries.en: As Taiping forces marched north he urged holding the river line, massing troops south of Beijing, blocking Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi passes, and bringing Mongol cavalry from Rehe and Suiyuan to guard the capital;
entries.literal: When Guangdong rebels invaded north, Xincun memorialized that rebel flames were drawing near, asking to hold the river line, station heavy forces directly south of the capital, block all key passes in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi together, and quickly move Mongol cavalry stationed at Rehe and Suiyuan into the interior to guard the capital region;

entries.zh: 京師九門嚴緝姦宄，運通倉存糧入城；
entries.en: hunt traitors at the nine gates and move Tongcang grain into the city;
entries.literal: strictly hunt traitors at the capital's nine gates and move grain from the Tongcang into the city;

entries.zh: 並敕琦善、鄧紹良規复揚州、鎮江，為會剿江寧之計。
entries.en: and order Qi Shan and Deng Shaoliang to recover Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as prelude to retaking Nanjing.
entries.literal: and order Qi Shan and Deng Shaoliang to plan recovery of Yangzhou and Zhenjiang as a plan for joint suppression of Jiangning.

entries.zh: 又疏陳順天防務，畫分汛地，舉行團練；
entries.en: He also divided Shuntian defense zones and organized militia;
entries.literal: He also memorialized on Shuntian defenses, dividing garrison zones and organizing militia;

entries.zh: 府屬各營舊隸總督管轄，請旨暫歸調遣。
entries.en: and asked that camps formerly under the governor-general answer to him for the moment.
entries.literal: the various camps under the prefecture had formerly been under the governor-general's jurisdiction; he asked that for the present they be placed under his dispatch.

entries.zh: 未幾，賊犯天津，僧格林沁率師進剿，命順天府設糧台。
entries.en: Soon rebels threatened Tianjin; Sengge Rinchen marched out and Shuntian set up a grain bureau.
entries.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Tianjin; Sengge Rinchen led troops to suppress them, and Shuntian was ordered to set up a grain bureau.

entries.zh: 心存請發內帑三十二萬兩、京倉米二千六百石以給軍食，添制軍需火藥。
entries.en: Xincun secured 320,000 taels from the inner treasury and 2,600 shi of capital grain for the army, plus more gunpowder.
entries.literal: Xincun asked to issue three hundred twenty thousand taels from the inner treasury and two thousand six hundred shi of capital-granary rice for army provisions, and to add manufacture of military gunpowder.

entries.zh: 又偕團防大臣會議京城防守事宜，舉光祿寺卿宋晉、太僕寺卿王茂廕綜理其事，並詔允行。
entries.en: He met defense commissioners, put Song Jin and Wang Maoyin in charge of capital defense, and won approval.
entries.literal: He also met with the capital defense commissioners to discuss capital defense, recommending Court of Imperial Entertainments minister Song Jin and Court of the Imperial Stud minister Wang Maoyin to oversee the matter—all approved by edict.

entries.zh: 時議行鈔幣，心存疏言：「軍營搭放票鈔，諸多窒礙。
entries.en: When paper money was debated, he wrote: 'Paying troops in paper notes faces many obstacles.
entries.literal: At the time paper money was under discussion; Xincun memorialized: 'Issuing paper notes in army camps has many obstacles.

entries.zh: 鈔幣之法，施行當有次第，此時甫經頒發，並未試用，勢難驟用之軍營。」
entries.en: Currency reform needs stages; notes have just been issued and untested—they cannot be forced on the army yet.'
entries.literal: The method of paper currency should be applied in due order; it has only just been issued and not yet tried—it will be hard to use it suddenly in army camps.'

entries.zh: 詔斥為阻撓，即責籌次等施行之法，俾無阻滯。
entries.en: An edict called this obstruction and ordered him to devise workable steps at once.
entries.literal: An edict rebuked this as obstruction and immediately charged him to devise graded methods of implementation so there would be no hindrance.

entries.zh: 會言官論通州捕役勾結土匪行劫，命刑部侍郎文瑞鞫得實，心存以徇庇革職。
entries.en: When censors exposed Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits, Wen Rui proved it and Xincun was dismissed for shielding them.
entries.literal: When censors discussed Tongzhou constables colluding with bandits to rob, Vice Minister of Justice Wen Rui investigated and found it true; Xincun was dismissed for favoritism.

entries.zh: 杜受田，字芝農，山東濱州人。
entries.en: Du Shoutian, whose courtesy name was Zhinong, came from Binzhou in Shandong.
entries.literal: Du Shoutian, courtesy name Zhinong, was a man of Binzhou in Shandong.

entries.zh: 父堮，嘉慶六年進士，由翰林院編修累官禮部侍郎，重宴鹿鳴，加太子少保，卒贈太傅，諡文端。
entries.en: His father E had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
entries.literal: His father E was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.

entries.zh: 是年冬，穆宗崩，德宗繼統即位，晉武英殿大學士。
entries.en: That winter Emperor Tongzhi died and Emperor Guangxu ascended the throne; Wen Xiang was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.
entries.literal: That winter Emperor Muzong died; Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne and took office, and Wen Xiang was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.

entries.zh: 以久病請罷，溫詔慰留，解諸兼職，專任軍機大臣及總理各國事務。
entries.en: He asked to retire on account of chronic illness; a gracious edict kept him in service, stripped him of other concurrent posts, and left him solely as grand councilor and head of foreign affairs at the Zongli Yamen.
entries.literal: Because of long illness he asked to resign; a warm edict comforted and retained him, relieved him of various concurrent posts, and charged him solely as Grand Councilor and director of the General Management of Affairs of All Foreign Countries.

entries.zh: 時國家漸多故，文祥深憂之，密陳大計疏曰：「洋人為患中國，愈久愈深，而其窺伺中國之間，亦愈熟愈密。
entries.en: As troubles multiplied, Wen Xiang grew deeply alarmed and submitted a secret memorial on grand strategy: "The foreign menace to China grows deeper with time, and their search for openings in China grows ever more practiced and relentless.
entries.literal: At that time the state gradually had many troubles; Wen Xiang deeply worried over them and in a secret memorial on the great plan said: "Foreigners as a calamity to China grow the longer the deeper, and their watching for openings in China also grows the more practiced and the more close.

entries.zh: 從前屢戰屢和，迄無定局，因在事諸臣操縱未宜。
entries.en: For years we fought and made peace by turns without ever reaching a stable settlement, because those in charge mishandled affairs.
entries.literal: From former times there were repeated wars and repeated peace, yet to the end no settled pattern, because the officials in charge did not handle matters properly.

entries.zh: 及庚申定約，設立衙門專司其事，以至於今，未見決裂。
entries.en: After the treaties of the 1860 crisis and the founding of a dedicated office for foreign affairs, relations have held—so far without open rupture.
entries.literal: When the Gengshen treaty was fixed and a yamen was established to specialize in these matters, down to today no rupture has been seen.

entries.zh: 就事論事，固當相機盡心辦理，而揣洋人之用心，求馭外之大本，則不繫於此，所繫者在人心而已矣。
entries.en: Day-to-day business must still be handled conscientiously as circumstances allow; but if we read foreign intentions and seek the true foundation for managing them, that foundation lies not in procedure but in the hearts of the people.
entries.literal: Judging matters as matters, one should indeed seize the moment and handle them with full heart; but considering foreigners' intent and seeking the great root of governing outsiders, it does not depend on this—the dependence is on popular sentiment alone.

entries.zh: 溯自嘉慶年間，洋人漸形強悍，始而海島，繼而口岸，再及內地，蓄力厲精習機器，以待中國之間，一逞其欲。
entries.en: Since the Jiaqing reign foreigners have grown steadily bolder—first on offshore islands, then at treaty ports, then inland—training troops, mastering machinery, and waiting for a crack in China through which to press their ambitions.
entries.literal: Tracing back from the Jiaqing years, foreigners gradually showed fierceness: first on sea islands, then at treaty ports, then reaching the interior; they stored strength, sharpened skill, studied machines, and waited for an opening in China to give full vent to their desires.

entries.zh: 道光年間，肆掠江、浙，自江寧換約以後，覬覦觀望。
entries.en: Under Daoguang they ravaged the lower Yangzi; after the Nanjing treaty they watched and waited for their chance.
entries.literal: In the Daoguang years they rampaged through Jiangsu and Zhejiang; after the treaty exchange at Jiangning they watched and coveted.

entries.zh: 直至粵匪滋事，以為中國有此犯上作亂之事，人心不一，得其間矣。
entries.en: When the Taiping rebellion broke out they judged that China was torn by rebellion and divided in loyalty—and that their opening had come.
entries.literal: Until the Guangdong bandits stirred trouble, they thought China had this matter of rebellion against superiors and disorder, popular hearts not united—they had gained their opening.

entries.zh: 於是其謀遂洩，闖入津門，雖經小挫，而其意愈堅，致有庚申之警。
entries.en: Their designs then came into the open: they forced the Tianjin approaches, and though checked briefly, pressed on until the crisis of 1860.
entries.literal: Thereupon their plot was revealed; they burst into the Tianjin gates; though they met small setbacks, their intent grew firmer, leading to the alarm of Gengshen.

entries.zh: 然其時勢局固危，民心未二，勤王之師雖非勁旅，而聞警偕來；
entries.en: The situation was dire, yet the people had not turned against the throne; relief armies were not elite troops, but they rallied when the alarm sounded;
entries.literal: Yet at that time the situation was indeed perilous, popular hearts were not divided, and though the armies that came to aid the throne were not crack troops, on hearing the alarm they came together;

entries.zh: 奸細之徒雖被誘脅，而公憤同具，以是得受羈縻，成此和局。
entries.en: and though spies were suborned, public outrage was united. On that basis the foreigners could be held in restraint and the present peace settlement was formed.
entries.literal: traitorous elements though enticed and coerced, yet shared public outrage was alike present; by this they were able to be held in restraint and this peace settlement was formed.

entries.zh: 十餘年來，仰賴皇太后、皇上勵精圖治，宵旰勤勞，無間隙之可尋；
entries.en: For more than a decade the realm has relied on the empress dowager and Your Majesty ruling with tireless diligence, leaving no opening for exploit;
entries.literal: For more than ten years, relying on the Empress Dowager and Your Majesty exerting spirit to govern well, toiling from dawn to dusk, no gap could be found;

entries.zh: 在事諸臣始得遇事維持，未至啟釁，偶有乾求，尚能往返爭持，不至太甚，非洋務之順手，及在事者折沖之力，皆我皇太后、皇上朝乾夕惕，事事期符民隱，人心固結，有以折外族之心，而杜未形之患也。
entries.en: so that officials handling foreign affairs could hold the line, avoid provocation, and even push back on unreasonable demands. That is not because foreign policy has gone smoothly or because negotiators have been unusually skillful, but because Your Majesty and the empress dowager have ruled with constant vigilance, aligned policy with the people's wishes, and kept popular loyalty firm—thereby restraining foreign ambition and heading off dangers before they appear.
entries.literal: officials in charge could then meet affairs and maintain them, not reach the point of provoking conflict; when occasionally there were demands, they could still go back and forth in contention and not reach excess—not because foreign affairs went smoothly or because those in charge had the power to parry, but all because our Empress Dowager and Your Majesty are vigilant morning and evening, in every matter expecting to accord with the people's hidden wishes, popular hearts firmly bound, having means to bend the hearts of foreign tribes and stop troubles not yet formed.

entries.zh: 然而各國火器技藝之講求益進，彼此相結之勢益固。
entries.en: Yet every power advances further in arms and technology, and their alliances grow tighter.
entries.literal: Yet each country's pursuit of firearms and craft advances daily, and the tendency of mutual alliance grows firmer.

entries.zh: 使臣久駐京師，聞我一政之當則憂，一或不當則喜，其探測愈精。
entries.en: Envoys long resident in Beijing rejoice when we misstep and worry when we govern well; their scrutiny grows ever sharper.
entries.literal: Envoys long stationed in the capital hear one policy of ours that is right and worry, one that is not right and rejoice; their probing grows more precise.

entries.zh: 俄人逼於西疆，法人計佔越南，緊接滇、粵，英人謀由印度入藏及蜀，蠢蠢欲動之勢，益不可遏。
entries.en: Russia presses the western frontier; France schemes at Vietnam on Yunnan and Guangdong's border; Britain eyes Tibet and Sichuan from India. Restless aggression grows harder to contain by the day.
entries.literal: Russians press on the western frontier, French plan to seize Vietnam adjoining Yunnan and Guangdong, English plot from India into Tibet and Shu—the restless stirring tendency grows ever harder to check.

entries.zh: 所伺者中國之間耳，所惎者中國大本之未搖，而人心之難違耳。
entries.en: They wait only for an opening in China; what restrains them is that the dynasty's foundation has not yet shaken and that the people's will cannot easily be defied.
entries.literal: What they watch for is only an opening in China; what they fear is only that China's great foundation has not shaken and that popular hearts are hard to defy.

entries.zh: 說者謂各國性近犬羊，未知政治，然其國中偶有動作，必由其國主付上議院議之，所謂謀及卿士也；
entries.en: Some dismiss the powers as barbarous and ignorant of government; yet when their rulers act, they refer matters to the upper house—what the classics call consulting the high ministers;
entries.literal: Some say the various countries are by nature like dogs and sheep and do not understand government; yet when occasionally there is action in their states, it must be referred by their sovereign to the upper house for deliberation—what is called consulting the high ministers;

entries.zh: 付下議院議之，所謂謀及庶人也。
entries.en: and to the lower house—consulting the common people.
entries.literal: referred to the lower house for deliberation—what is called consulting the common people.

entries.zh: 議之可行則行，否則止，事事必合乎民情而後決然行之。
entries.en: What passes deliberation they enact; what fails they drop. Nothing is done until it aligns with popular sentiment.
entries.literal: If deliberation finds it feasible they act; if not they stop; in every matter they must accord with popular sentiment before resolutely carrying it out.

entries.zh: 自治其國以此，其觀他國之廢興成敗亦以此。
entries.en: They govern themselves by this standard, and they judge other nations' rise and fall by it as well.
entries.literal: They govern their own countries by this, and they view other countries' decline, rise, success, and failure also by this.

entries.zh: 儻其國一切政治皆與民情相背，則各國始逞所欲為，取之恐後矣。
entries.en: When a state's policies run against its people, the powers rush to exploit it, each fearing to arrive too late.
entries.literal: If a country's every policy runs against popular sentiment, then the various countries begin to give full play to what they wish and seize it, fearing to be late.

entries.zh: 如土耳其、希臘等國，勢極弱小，而得以久存各大國之間者，其人心固也。
entries.en: Turkey and Greece are very weak yet endure among the great powers because their peoples remain united.
entries.literal: Such as Turkey, Greece, and other countries—extremely weak in power—yet able long to survive among the great powers: their popular hearts are firm.

entries.zh: 強大如法國，而德國得以勝之者，以法王窮侈任性，負國債之多不可復計，雖日益額餉以要結兵心，而民心已去，始有以乘其間也。
entries.en: France was mighty, yet Germany defeated it because the French king lived in ruinous luxury, piled up unpayable debt, and tried to buy the army with ever higher pay while losing the people—giving Germany its opening.
entries.literal: Mighty as France, yet Germany was able to overcome it—because the French king was extravagant to exhaustion and willful, national debt beyond reckoning; though daily increasing pay to bind soldiers' hearts, popular hearts had already departed, and only then was there means to seize the opening.

entries.zh: 夫人必自侮而後人侮之，物必先自腐而後蟲生焉。
entries.en: Only those who despise themselves are despised by others; only what rots from within breeds worms.
entries.literal: A man must first insult himself and afterward others insult him; a thing must first rot itself and afterward worms are born.

entries.zh: 理之所在，勢所必至。
entries.en: Such is the logic of events; such is what must follow.
entries.literal: Where principle lies, tendency necessarily arrives.

entries.zh: 中國之有外國，猶人身之有疾病，病者必相證用藥，而培元氣為尤要。
entries.en: Foreign powers afflicting China are like disease afflicting the body: symptoms must be treated, but strengthening the body's vital force matters most.
entries.literal: China having foreigners is like the human body having illness; the ill must be treated with medicine suited to symptoms, yet nourishing the vital energy is especially important.

entries.zh: 外國無日不察我民心之向背，中國必求無事不愜於民心之是非。
entries.en: Foreigners watch daily whether the people stand with or against the throne; China must ensure that nothing we do offends popular judgment of right and wrong.
entries.literal: Foreign countries have no day on which they do not examine whether our popular hearts turn toward or away; China must seek that in no matter it fail to satisfy the people's right and wrong.

entries.zh: 中國天澤分嚴，外國上議院、下議院之設，勢有難行，而義可採取。
entries.en: China's hierarchy of imperial grace is strict; we cannot simply copy foreign parliaments, but we can adopt their underlying principle.
entries.literal: In China heaven's favor and rank are sharply divided; establishing foreign upper and lower houses would be hard in tendency, yet the principle may be adopted.

entries.zh: 凡我用人行政，一舉一動，揆之至理，度之民情，非人心所共愜，則急止勿為；
entries.en: In appointing officials and governing, every act should be weighed against principle and popular sentiment; what the people cannot accept should be stopped at once;
entries.literal: In all our employment of men and administration of affairs, every move and act—measure to utmost principle, estimate against popular sentiment; what popular hearts do not together find pleasing, then urgently stop and do not do;

entries.zh: 事係人心所共快，則務期於成。
entries.en: and what the people wholeheartedly support should be carried through to success.
entries.literal: matters that concern what popular hearts together rejoice in, then strive to bring to completion.

entries.zh: 崇節儉以裕帑需，遇事始能有備，納諫諍以開言路，下情藉以上通。
entries.en: Practice frugality to fill the treasury and prepare for emergencies; welcome remonstrance to open channels so grievances from below reach the throne.
entries.literal: Uphold frugality to enrich treasury needs, so that when affairs come there may be preparation; accept remonstrance to open the path of speech, so lower sentiments may thereby reach above.

entries.zh: 總期人心永結，大本永固，當各外國環伺之時，而使之無一間可乘，庶彼謀不能即遂，而在我亦堪自立。
entries.en: Keep popular loyalty firm and the dynasty's foundation secure, so that while foreign powers circle they find no opening—their designs may fail, and China may still stand on its own.
entries.literal: In sum expect popular hearts forever bound and the great foundation forever firm; when the various foreign countries encircle and watch, cause them to have not one opening to exploit—then perhaps their plots cannot immediately succeed, and on our side we may also stand firm.

entries.zh: 此為目前猶可及之計，亦為此時不能稍緩之圖。
entries.en: This is a course still within reach—and one that brooks no delay.
entries.literal: This is a plan still attainable at present, and also a design that at this time cannot be slightly delayed.

entries.zh: 若待其間之既開，而欲為斡旋補苴之法，則和與戰俱不可恃。
entries.en: Once the opening appears, neither negotiation nor war can be relied on.
entries.literal: If one waits until the opening is already made and then wishes to apply mediating, patching methods, then both peace and war are alike unreliable.

entries.zh: 即使仍可苟安，而大局已不堪復問，則何如預防其間之為計也。
entries.en: Even temporary safety would leave the larger situation beyond repair. How much better to prevent the opening before it comes.
entries.literal: Even if one could still scrape by in security, the great situation would already be beyond asking again—how much better to plan by preventing the opening beforehand.

entries.zh: 咸豐六年王茂廕奏陳夷務，謂：'海外諸國日起爭雄，自人視之，雖有中外之分，自天視之，殆無彼此之意。'
entries.en: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'Overseas powers contend daily for dominance; men see a line between China and abroad, but Heaven may see no such distinction.'
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on barbarian affairs, saying: 'Overseas countries daily rise to contend for supremacy; viewed by men, though there is division of China and abroad, viewed by Heaven, probably there is no intent of this and that.'

entries.zh: 引書言'皇天無親，惟德是輔'，及大學平天下章三言得失，首人心、次天命、而終以君心為證。
entries.en: He quoted the Classic—'High Heaven has no favorites; it aids only the virtuous'—and the Great Learning on ordering the realm, which three times names the sources of success and failure: first the people's hearts, then Heaven's mandate, and finally the ruler's own heart as proof.
entries.literal: He cited the Classic: 'High Heaven has no partiality; it assists only virtue,' and the Great Learning chapter on bringing peace to the world, which thrice speaks of gain and loss—first popular hearts, next Heaven's mandate, and finally taking the ruler's heart as proof.

entries.zh: 何其言之危且切歟！
entries.en: How grave and urgent his warning was!
entries.literal: How perilous and urgent his words!

entries.zh: 欲戢夷心，莫要於順民心，能順民心，斯足以承天心，固不待蓍蔡而昭然若睹耳。
entries.en: To quiet foreign ambition, nothing matters more than winning the people's hearts; win the people and you win Heaven's favor—no divination needed to see that truth.
entries.literal: To restrain barbarian hearts, nothing is more essential than following popular hearts; able to follow popular hearts, that suffices to receive Heaven's heart—indeed without need of divination by yarrow or milfoil it is clear as if seen.

entries.zh: 臣受恩最重，辦理洋務最久，實有見於洋人居心積慮之處，而現時尤為迫切緊要之關。
entries.en: I have received the deepest favor and handled foreign affairs longer than any other minister; I have seen where foreigners scheme, and I know this moment is the critical hinge.
entries.literal: Your servant has received grace most heavily and handled foreign affairs longest; I truly have insight into where foreigners harbor intent and long plotting, and at present this is especially the urgent, critical hinge.

entries.zh: 外國之求間在此，中國之彌間亦在此。
entries.en: Foreigners seek their opening here; China must close it here.
entries.literal: Foreign countries' seeking of openings lies here; China's closing of openings also lies here.

entries.zh: 在事諸臣，僅謀其末，我皇上實操其本。
entries.en: Officials in charge can manage only details; Your Majesty holds the root in his own hands.
entries.literal: Officials in charge only plot the branches; Your Majesty truly holds the root.

entries.zh: 用敢直陳，伏乞俯鑑芻言，將此摺時置左右，力求端本之治，以回隱患之萌。
entries.en: I therefore speak plainly and beg Your Majesty to heed these humble words, keep this memorial close at hand, and pursue government that heals the root—before hidden dangers take hold.
entries.literal: Therefore I dare speak plainly, prostrate and beg Your Majesty to look down and discern these humble words, place this memorial often at your side, strive for government that rectifies the root, and turn back the sprouting of hidden calamity.

entries.zh: 天下幸甚！」
entries.en: The realm would be blessed indeed!"
entries.literal: Great fortune for the realm!"

entries.zh: 文慶，字孔修，費莫氏，滿州鑲紅旗人，兩廣總督永保之孫也。
entries.en: Wen Qing, whose style was Kongxiu, belonged to the Feimo clan and came from the Manchu Bordered Red Banner; he was a grandson of Yongbao, who had served as governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
entries.literal: Wen Qing, style name Kongxiu, of the Feimo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner, was the grandson of Yongbao, Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.

entries.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Daoguang reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a Compiler.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.

entries.zh: 五遷至詹事。
entries.en: After five promotions he rose to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 歷通政使、左副都御史、內閣學士。
entries.en: He went on to serve as commissioner of the Transmission Office, left vice censor-in-chief, and a grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He successively served as Commissioner of the Transmission Office, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十二年，授禮部侍郎，兼副都統。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of the reign he was made vice minister of rites and concurrently vice banner commander.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently serving as Vice Banner Commander.

entries.zh: 十三年，總理孝慎皇后喪儀，會奏軍民薙發及停止宴會期限疏中，誤引「百姓如喪考妣，四海遏密八音」語，下諸臣嚴議。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he directed the mourning ceremonies for Empress Xiaoshen. In a joint memorial setting out the periods for military and civilian tonsure and for suspending banquets, he wrongly cited the lines “The people mourned as for a father and mother, and music was stilled throughout the realm”—language appropriate to an emperor's death, not an empress's. The case was sent to the ministers for severe review.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he oversaw the mourning rites for Empress Xiaoshen. In a joint memorial on the periods for tonsure by military and civilians and for suspension of banquets, he mistakenly quoted the phrase "the common people mourned as for father and mother; throughout the four seas music was hushed for eight tones." The matter was referred to the ministers for strict deliberation.

entries.zh: 宣宗以文慶翰林出身，隨聲附和，獨重譴，褫副都統，降三品頂戴。
entries.en: Emperor Daoguang held that Wen Qing, as a Hanlin graduate, had merely echoed others; Wen Qing alone received a heavy penalty—loss of his vice banner command and demotion to third-rank insignia.
entries.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor, considering that Wen Qing was of Hanlin origin and had echoed others' views, imposed a punishment on him alone that was especially severe: he was stripped of his post as Vice Banner Commander and demoted to a third-rank peacock feather.

entries.zh: 尋復之，歷吏部、戶部侍郎。
entries.en: He was soon restored and served in turn as vice minister of personnel and of revenue.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored; he successively served as Vice Minister of the Board of Personnel and Board of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十六年，偕尚書湯金釗赴陝西、四川按劾巡撫楊名颺、布政使李羲文，並下嚴議，尋复按名颺被訐事，褫其職。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he joined Minister Tang Jinzhao on an investigative tour of Shaanxi and Sichuan to impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and provincial administration commissioner Li Yiwen; both cases went to strict review. When the inquiry into denunciations against Yang was reopened, Yang was stripped of office.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tang Jinzhao he went to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate and impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Yiwen; both were referred to strict deliberation. Soon after, upon reinvestigating the matter of Yang Mingyang being denounced, Yang was stripped of his post.

entries.zh: 金釗留署陝西巡撫。
entries.en: Tang Jinzhao stayed on to administer the Shaanxi governorship.
entries.literal: Tang Jinzhao remained in charge of the Shaanxi governorship.

entries.zh: 文慶又按河南武陟知縣趙銘彝貪婪狀，劾褫職。
entries.en: Wen Qing also looked into corruption charges against Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and secured his removal from office.
entries.literal: Wen Qing also investigated the greedy conduct of Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and impeached him, resulting in dismissal.

entries.zh: 調戶部侍郎。
entries.en: He was transferred to the vice ministry of revenue.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十七年，命在軍機大臣上學習行走，兼右翼總兵。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he was assigned to train under the Grand Council and walk in attendance there, while also commanding the Right Wing.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to study and walk in attendance at the Grand Council, concurrently serving as Commander of the Right Wing.

entries.zh: 命赴熱河，偕都統耆英按歷任總管虧短庫款，褫職追繳。
entries.en: He was sent to Rehe with Commander-in-chief Qi Ying to audit successive superintendents who had shorted the treasury; the guilty were dismissed and made to repay.
entries.literal: He was ordered to go to Rehe, and together with Commander-in-chief Qi Ying investigated successive superintendents who had misappropriated treasury funds; they were dismissed and required to make restitution.

entries.zh: 十九年，以查辦熱河虧空案內擬罪未晰，召問，奏對失實，下部議，罷直軍機。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year the penalties proposed in the Rehe deficit case were found unclear; summoned to audience, he answered untruthfully, the matter went to ministerial review, and he was removed from the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, because the assigned penalties in the case of deficits at Rehe were unclear, he was summoned for questioning; his memorial responses were untrue, the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation, and he was removed from service at the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 二十年，典江南鄉試，以上下江中額有誤，又私攜湖南舉人熊少牧入闈閱卷，議褫職。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he served as chief examiner for the Jiangnan provincial tests; errors in the Upper and Lower Jiang quota, together with his smuggling the Hunan graduate Xiong Shaomu into the hall to mark papers, led to a recommendation for dismissal.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination; because the quota allocation between Upper and Lower Jiang was erroneous, and because he privately brought the Hunan provincial graduate Xiong Shaomu into the examination hall to grade papers, it was decided he should be dismissed.

entries.zh: 桂良，字燕山，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，閩浙總督玉德子。
entries.en: Gui Liang, styled Yanshan, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and the Manchu Plain Red Banner; he was the son of Yude, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Gui Liang, courtesy name Yanshan, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, was the son of Yude, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 入貲為禮部主事，晉員外郎。
entries.en: He gained office by purchase as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites and was later promoted to vice director.
entries.literal: He purchased entry and became a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then was promoted to vice director.

entries.zh: 出為四川順慶知府，調成都。
entries.en: He was posted as prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan, then transferred to the Chengdu prefecture.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan, then was transferred to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 歷建昌道，河南按察使，四川、廣東、江西布政使。
entries.en: He served in turn as Jianchang circuit intendant, Henan judicial commissioner, and treasurer of Sichuan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi.
entries.literal: He successively held the posts of Jianchang circuit intendant, Henan provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer of Sichuan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 道光十四年，擢河南巡撫。
entries.en: In Daoguang 14 (1834), he was appointed governor of Henan.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign, he was promoted to governor of Henan.

entries.zh: 嘉慶中，林清、李文成等以八卦教倡亂，既誅，而汲縣潞州屯墳塔猶祀其神曰「無生老母」，習教者猶眾。
entries.en: During the Jiaqing reign, Lin Qing and Li Wencheng had stirred rebellion in the name of the Eight Trigrams sect. After their execution, the grave pagoda at Luanzhou tun in Jixian still honored their god as the "Eternal Mother," and many locals continued to follow the cult.
entries.literal: In the Jiaqing era, Lin Qing, Li Wencheng, and others had raised rebellion through the Eight Trigrams teaching; though they had been executed, at the grave pagoda at Luanzhou tun in Jixian County their deity was still worshipped under the name "Eternal Mother without Birth," and adherents of the teaching remained numerous.

entries.zh: 御史黃爵滋以為言，命桂良察治，毀其墳廟，廉得河南境內無生廟三十九所，並毀之；
entries.en: When censor Huang Juezi brought the matter to court, Gui Liang was ordered to investigate. He tore down the cult shrines and, on inquiry, found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" temples across Henan and had them all demolished as well;
entries.literal: Censor Huang Juezi reported on this; Gui Liang was ordered to investigate and rectify the matter, demolish the grave temples, and through investigation found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" shrines within Henan, all of which were likewise destroyed;

entries.zh: 地方官失察，譴黜有差。
entries.en: local officials who had failed to detect the cult were censured and demoted according to their degree of fault.
entries.literal: local officials who had failed in oversight were reprimanded and demoted to varying degrees.

entries.zh: 十九年，擢湖廣總督，調閩浙，又調雲貴。
entries.en: In Daoguang 19 he became governor-general of Huguang, then was moved to Fujian-Zhejiang and afterward to Yunnan-Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang, transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang, and again transferred to Yunnan and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 二十年，兼署雲南巡撫。
entries.en: In Daoguang 20 he also served as acting governor of Yunnan.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, he additionally served as acting governor of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 滇省多盜，奏定緝捕章程；
entries.en: Because banditry was rife in Yunnan, he submitted regulations for pursuit and arrest;
entries.literal: Yunnan had many bandits; he memorialized to fix regulations for pursuit and capture;

entries.zh: 又請迤南、迤西、迤東各標營官兵責成巡道就近稽察。
entries.en: and asked that troops of the southern, western, and eastern banner camps be placed under nearby circuit intendants for local inspection.
entries.literal: and further requested that the troops of the southern, western, and eastern garrison banners be charged to the circuit intendants for inspection nearby.

entries.zh: 時貴州諸苗蠢動，鎮遠、黎平、都勻、古州苗尤悍，州縣不能制，疏請遴勁兵專主剿捕。
entries.en: Meanwhile Miao uprisings spread across Guizhou; those in Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were especially fierce and beyond county control, so he asked that elite troops be chosen for a dedicated suppression campaign.
entries.literal: At the time the Miao of Guizhou were stirring everywhere; those of Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were especially fierce, and prefectures and counties could not control them, so he memorialized to select crack troops devoted solely to suppression.

entries.zh: 二十五年，入覲，留京，署兵部尚書，兼正白旗漢軍都統。
entries.en: In Daoguang 25 he came to audience, stayed in the capital as acting minister of War, and concurrently commanded the Han Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he came to court audience, remained in the capital, served as acting minister of War, and concurrently held the post of commander of the Han Army of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 尋出為熱河都統。
entries.en: He was soon appointed commander of the Rehe garrison.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he went out as commander of Rehe.

entries.zh: 二十八年，召來京，以其女妻皇六子奕訢，授鑲紅旗漢軍都統。
entries.en: In Daoguang 28 he was recalled to Beijing, his daughter was married to the sixth imperial son Yixin, and he was made commander of the Han Bordered Red Banner.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was summoned to the capital; his daughter was given in marriage to the emperor's sixth son Yixin, and he was appointed commander of the Han Army of the Bordered Red Banner.

entries.zh: 文煜，字星岩，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
entries.en: Wen Yu, styled Xingyan, was a Feimo Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Wen Yu, courtesy name Xingyan, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 由官學生授太常寺庫使，累遷刑部郎中。
entries.en: An Imperial Academy student, he became storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was repeatedly transferred to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 出為直隸霸昌道、四川按察使。
entries.en: He served as Baxing circuit intendant in Zhili and judicial commissioner of Sichuan.
entries.literal: He went out as Baxing circuit intendant of Zhili and provincial judicial commissioner of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 咸豐三年，遷江寧布政使。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 3 he was made treasurer of Jiangning.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangning.

entries.zh: 時江寧已陷賊，文煜從琦善江北大營。
entries.en: Nanjing had already fallen, so Wen Yu joined Qishan at the northern Yangzi camp.
entries.literal: At the time Jiangning had already fallen to rebels; Wen Yu followed Qishan at the Great Camp north of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 四年，琦善歿於揚州，所部練勇及江北糧台事宜，命文煜接辦。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 4 Qishan died at Yangzhou, and Wen Yu took over his militia and the northern Yangzi grain depot.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Qishan died at Yangzhou; the trained braves under his command and affairs of the grain depot north of the Yangzi were ordered to be taken over by Wen Yu.

entries.zh: 五年春，粵匪由瓜洲東竄沙頭港，文煜遣勇擊之，賊由對岸扎簰爭渡，偕水師以大砲合擊，賊退瓜洲。
entries.en: In the spring of Xianfeng 5 rebels fled east from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor. Wen Yu sent militia to attack; when they lashed rafts to cross the river, he joined the navy in a cannon barrage and drove them back to Guazhou.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Cantonese rebels fled east from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor; Wen Yu sent braves to attack them; the rebels on the opposite bank lashed rafts to compete in crossing; together with the navy he used great cannon in a joint attack, and the rebels withdrew to Guazhou.

entries.zh: 文煜以沙頭港為裡下河門戶，賊所必爭，築土城砲台，疏請添募練勇守禦，從之。
entries.en: Wen Yu saw Shatou Harbor as the gateway to the Lixia River region and a point the rebels would contest. He built earthen walls and batteries and asked to recruit more militia for defense; the court agreed.
entries.literal: Wen Yu held that Shatou Harbor was the gateway to the Lixia River region and a place the rebels would certainly contest; he built earthen walls and batteries and memorialized to add recruitment of trained braves for defense; this was approved.

entries.zh: 既而賊踞揚州，窺裡下河，文煜擊之於萬安橋，大有斬獲，賊勢乃挫。
entries.en: When rebels held Yangzhou and threatened the Lixia River region, Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with heavy casualties on their side, checking their advance.
entries.literal: Before long the rebels held Yangzhou and watched for a chance against the Lixia River region; Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with many kills and captures, and the rebel momentum was checked.

entries.zh: 七年，調江蘇布政使，治江南大營糧台。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 7 he became treasurer of Jiangsu and directed the southern Yangzi army's grain depot.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangsu and directed the grain depot of the Great Camp south of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 以支給撙節，為軍中所不便，提督和春劾其拘泥，命來京候另簡用。
entries.en: His frugal disbursements displeased the army. Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to Beijing to await reassignment.
entries.literal: Because his disbursements were frugal, this was inconvenient for the army; Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.

entries.zh: 尋授直隸布政使。
entries.en: He was soon appointed treasurer of Zhili.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhili.

entries.zh: 瑞常歷事三朝，端謹無過，累司文柄，時稱耆碩。
entries.en: Rui Chang served three reigns with upright diligence, repeatedly held charge of literary affairs, and was regarded as a venerable elder statesman.
entries.literal: Rui Chang served three reigns, was upright and without fault, repeatedly held literary authority, and was called a venerable elder of his time.

entries.zh: 十一年，卒，贈太保，祀賢良祠，諡文端。
entries.en: In 1872 he died and was posthumously made grand tutor, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, with the posthumous title Wenduan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he died; posthumously made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.

entries.zh: 子文暉，官至盛京禮部侍郎。
entries.en: His son Wenhui eventually became vice minister of rites at Mukden.
entries.literal: His son Wenhui rose to Vice Minister of Rites at Mukden.

entries.zh: 柏葰，原名松葰，字靜濤，巴魯特氏，蒙古正藍旗人。
entries.en: Bai Jun, originally named Songjun, with the style Jingtao, was of the Balute clan and a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner.
entries.literal: Baizhan, original name Songzhan, style name Jingtao, of the Balute clan, a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 道光六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1826 he passed the jinshi examination, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 累遷內閣學士，兼正紅旗漢軍副都統。
entries.en: He rose in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, while also serving as vice commander of the Chinese Plain Red Banner.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently serving as Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese Plain Red Banner.

entries.zh: 十八年，出為盛京工部侍郎，調刑部，兼管奉天府尹。
entries.en: In 1838 he was posted as vice minister of works at Mukden, transferred to punishments, and concurrently served as Fengtian prefect.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was sent out as Vice Minister of Works at Mukden, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently administered the Fengtian prefect.

entries.zh: 二十年，召授刑部侍郎，調吏部，又調戶部。
entries.en: In 1840 he was recalled and made vice minister of punishments, then moved to personnel and later to revenue.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, transferred to Personnel, then again to Revenue.

entries.zh: 二十三年，充諭祭朝鮮正使，例有餽贐，奏卻之。
entries.en: In 1843 he served as chief envoy to Korea to announce sacrifices; customary gifts were offered, but he memorialized the court to refuse them.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he served as chief envoy to announce sacrifices to Korea; per custom there were gifts, which he memorialized to decline.

entries.zh: 二十五年，充總管內務府大臣。
entries.en: In 1845 he was appointed grand minister superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he served as Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 二十六年，典江南鄉試。
entries.en: In 1846 he presided over the Jiangnan provincial civil examination.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination.

entries.zh: 疏言：「徵漕大戶短欠，取償小戶，劣紳挾制官吏，大戶包攬小戶，畸輕畸重，旗丁需索，加增津貼諸弊，請嚴禁。」
entries.en: He submitted a memorial stating: "When grain-transport levies were collected, wealthy households' shortfalls were shifted onto poorer ones; disreputable gentry coerced officials; wealthy contractors bundled small taxpayers into uneven burdens; and banner troops extorted extra transit fees—all of which should be strictly prohibited."
entries.literal: He memorialized: "In collecting grain transport dues, large households fall short and recover it from small ones; inferior gentry coerce officials; large households take contracts for small ones, making burdens uneven; banner soldiers extort and surcharges on transit allowances multiply—such abuses should be strictly forbidden."

entries.zh: 如議行。
entries.en: The court approved his proposal and put it into effect.
entries.literal: The proposal was approved and carried out.

entries.zh: 尋偕倉場侍郎陳孚恩盤查山東籓庫，劾布政使王篤濫用幕友及地方官縱盜，巡撫崇恩以下議譴有差。
entries.en: He soon joined Granary Vice Minister Chen Fu'en in auditing Shandong's provincial treasury, impeaching Administration Commissioner Wang Du for misusing private secretaries and local officials for tolerating bandits; Governor Chong'en and others were censured in varying degrees.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, together with Granary Vice Minister Chen Fu'en he audited the Shandong provincial treasury, impeaching Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Du for employing private secretaries improperly and local officials for condoning banditry; the governor Chong'en and others below were censured to varying degrees.

entries.zh: 二十八年，擢左都御史。
entries.en: In 1848 he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

entries.zh: 三十年，遷兵部尚書，授內大臣。
entries.en: In 1850 he became minister of war and was appointed an inner minister.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to Minister of War and appointed an Inner Minister.

entries.zh: 尋調吏部，管理三庫，兼翰林院掌院學士。
entries.en: He was soon moved to personnel, put in charge of the three treasuries, and also made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Personnel, placed in charge of the Three Treasuries, and concurrently served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 咸豐三年，命偕侍郎善燾赴盛京按協領塔芬布輕聽謠言，調兵護宅，幾至激變，得實，論遣戍。
entries.en: In 1853 he and Vice Minister Shan Xi were sent to Mukden to investigate Assistant Commander Tafenbu, who had credulously acted on rumors, called out troops to guard his home, and nearly sparked a mutiny; the case proved true and he was sentenced to exile.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was ordered with Vice Minister Shan Xi to go to Mukden to investigate Assistant Commander Tafenbu, who had lightly believed rumors, mobilized troops to guard his residence, and nearly provoked a riot; the facts were established and exile was ordered.

entries.zh: 將軍奕興坐袒護，革任。
entries.en: General Yixing was stripped of his post for covering up the affair.
entries.literal: General Yixing was punished for shielding him and dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋以前在鑲白旗蒙古都統任揀選承襲有誤，罷內務府大臣，降授左副都御史。
entries.en: Shortly afterward, an earlier mistake in approving succession claims while he was Mongol commander of the Bordered White Banner cost him the Imperial Household post; he was demoted to vice censor-in-chief of the left.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, because while Mongol Commander-in-Chief of the Bordered White Banner he had erred in selecting heirs for succession, he was removed as Grand Minister of the Imperial Household and demoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

entries.zh: 未幾，出為馬蘭鎮總兵。
entries.en: Before long he was posted as regional commander at Malan.
entries.literal: Before long he was sent out as Regional Commander at Malan.

entries.zh: 五年，擢熱河都統，搜捕山匪。
entries.en: In 1855 he was made commander-in-chief at Rehe and led operations against mountain bandits.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief at Rehe and hunted mountain bandits.

entries.zh: 疏言：「熱河將惰兵疲，州縣不諳吏治。
entries.en: He memorialized: "At Rehe the generals had grown slack and the troops exhausted, while local officials were unskilled in governance.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "At Rehe the generals are lax and the troops weary; prefectures and counties do not understand administration.

entries.zh: 行使大錢，民皆罷市。
entries.en: The circulation of large-denomination coins had driven the people to close their markets in protest.
entries.literal: Large-value coins are circulated and the people have all shut their markets.

entries.zh: 礦匪佔踞山場，委員侵蝕商款。」
entries.en: Mining bandits held the hills, and government commissioners were embezzling merchants' funds."
entries.literal: Mining bandits occupy the hills, and commissioners embezzle merchants' funds."

entries.zh: 詔嚴切查辦。
entries.en: The throne ordered a rigorous investigation.
entries.literal: An edict ordered strict investigation and punishment.

entries.zh: 召授戶部尚書，兼正黃旗漢軍都統。
entries.en: He was recalled to serve as minister of revenue and concurrently as commander of the Chinese Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue, concurrently serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 六年，命在軍機大臣上行走，兼翰林院掌院學士。
entries.en: In 1856 he was appointed to the Grand Council while retaining the Hanlin chancellorship.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council and concurrently as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 尋以戶部尚書協辦大學士。
entries.en: He was soon made associate grand secretary while serving as minister of revenue.
entries.literal: Soon, as Minister of Revenue, he was made Associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 八年，典順天鄉試，拜文淵閣大學士。
entries.en: In 1858 he oversaw the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.

entries.zh: 三年，粵匪陷江寧，复陷揚州，漕督楊殿邦​​退保淮安，廷議調山西、陝西兵七千赴援。
entries.en: In the third year the Cantonese rebels captured Jiangning and then Yangzhou; Grain Transport Commissioner Yang Dianbang withdrew to defend Huai'an, and the court debated dispatching seven thousand troops from Shanxi and Shaanxi as reinforcements.
entries.literal: In the third year the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning and then Yangzhou; the grain transport commissioner Yang Dianbang withdrew to defend Huai'an, and the court deliberated sending seven thousand troops from Shanxi and Shaanxi to aid.

entries.zh: 鳳標與尚書文慶，侍郎全慶、王慶雲合疏，言：「淮安賊所必爭，萬一賊眾渡河，則河南、山東民情震動，撲滅愈難。
entries.en: Fengbiao joined Minister Wenqing and Vice Ministers Quanqing and Wang Qingyun in a joint memorial: "Huai'an is ground the rebels are certain to contest; if their forces cross the river, the people of Henan and Shandong will be thrown into alarm and suppression will become far more difficult.
entries.literal: Fengbiao, together with Minister Weng Qing and Vice Ministers Quan Qing and Wang Qingyun, jointly memorialized, saying: "Huai'an is ground the rebels are sure to contest; if by chance the rebel host crosses the river, the people of Henan and Shandong will be shaken, and suppression will become harder still.

entries.zh: 請命山東巡撫李僡親往淮安扼賊北竄，並請敕直隸總督迅派布政使張集馨率兵扼要駐守，以為京師屏蔽。」
entries.en: We ask that Governor Li Shen of Shandong be sent in person to Huai'an to block the rebels' northward advance, and that the Zhili governor-general be ordered to dispatch Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Jixin at once with troops to hold the strategic points that shield the capital."
entries.literal: We ask that the Shandong governor Li Shen be ordered to go in person to Huai'an to block the rebels' northward flight, and that the Zhili governor-general be commanded to dispatch Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Jixin at once with troops to hold key points as a shield for the capital."

entries.zh: 疏入，如所請行。
entries.en: The memorial was adopted and carried out as proposed.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the court acted as requested.

entries.zh: 五月，賊陷河南歸德，鳳標與大學士賈楨、尚書翁心存等條擬防剿六事，多被採擇。
entries.en: In the fifth month the rebels captured Guide in Henan; Fengbiao joined Grand Secretary Jia Zhen, Minister Weng Xincong, and others in drafting six proposals for defense and suppression, many of which the court adopted.
entries.literal: In the fifth month the rebels took Guide in Henan; Fengbiao, together with Grand Secretary Jia Zhen, Minister Weng Xincong, and others, drafted six items on defense and suppression, many of which were adopted.

entries.zh: 未幾，悍賊林鳳祥等竄畿輔，复偕楨、心存等奏陳預籌守城事宜。
entries.en: Before long the fierce rebel Lin Fengxiang and others broke into the capital region; Fengbiao again joined Zhen, Xincong, and others in memorializing on preparations for the capital's defense.
entries.literal: Before long the fierce rebel Lin Fengxiang and others raided the capital region; Fengbiao again joined Zhen, Xincong, and others in memorializing on advance preparations for defending the city.

entries.zh: 疏入，報聞。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the court noted receipt.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.

entries.zh: 四年，授刑部尚書。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 六年，宣宗實錄、聖訓告成，加太子少保。
entries.en: In the sixth year, when the Xuanzong Emperor's Veritable Record and Sacred Instructions were completed, he was granted the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, when the Xuanzong Emperor's Veritable Record and Sacred Instructions were reported completed, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 尋調兵部，復調戶部。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Board of War and then back to the Board of Revenue.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to War and then again to Revenue.

entries.zh: 賈楨，字筠堂，山東黃縣人。
entries.en: Jia Zhen, whose style was Yuntang, came from Huang County in Shandong.
entries.literal: Jia Zhen, style name Yuntang, was a native of Huang County in Shandong.

entries.zh: 父允升，乾隆六十年進士，由檢討歷官兵部侍郎。
entries.en: His father Yunsheng had taken his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of the Qianlong reign and advanced from Hanlin compiler to Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: His father Yun Sheng passed the jinshi examination in the sixtieth year of Qianlong and rose from compiler to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 六年，同文館議考選正途五品以下京外官入館肄習天文算學，聘西人為教習。
entries.en: In 1867 the Tongwenguan proposed recruiting regular-track officials of fifth rank and below from court and provinces to study astronomy and mathematics there, with Westerners engaged as teachers.
entries.literal: In the sixth year the Tongwenguan proposed selecting regular-track officials of fifth rank and below from the capital and provinces to study astronomy and mathematics in the hall, hiring Westerners as instructors.

entries.zh: 倭仁謂根本之圖，在人心不在技藝，尤以西人教習為不可；
entries.en: Wo Ren argued that the root lay in men's hearts, not in technical skill, and above all that Western teachers were intolerable;
entries.literal: Wo Ren said the fundamental plan lies in men's hearts, not in techniques, and especially that Western instructors were unacceptable;

entries.zh: 且謂必習天文算學，應求中國能精其法者，上疏請罷議。
entries.en: and that if such studies were needed, Chinese masters of the methods should be found. He memorialized the throne to abandon the plan.
entries.literal: and said that if astronomy and mathematics must be studied, Chinese who mastered the methods should be sought; he memorialized asking that the proposal be dropped.

entries.zh: 於是詔倭仁保薦，別設一館，即由倭仁督率講求。
entries.en: The throne then ordered Wo Ren to nominate teachers, open a separate hall, and direct the instruction himself.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Wo Ren to recommend men, set up a separate hall, and have Wo Ren supervise the study.

entries.zh: 復奏意中並無其人，不敢妄保。
entries.en: He replied again that he knew no one fit for the task and dared not nominate anyone lightly.
entries.literal: He memorialized again that he had no one in mind and dared not recommend rashly.

entries.zh: 尋命在總理各國事務衙門行走。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve in the Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs.

entries.zh: 倭仁屢疏懇辭，不允；
entries.en: Wo Ren repeatedly begged off in memorials, without success;
entries.literal: Wo Ren repeatedly memorialized earnestly to decline; it was not granted;

entries.zh: 因稱疾篤，乞休，命解兼職，仍在弘德殿行走。
entries.en: he then pleaded grave illness and asked to retire; the court released him from his extra duties but kept him at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
entries.literal: he then claimed grave illness and begged retirement; he was ordered relieved of concurrent posts but to remain at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

entries.zh: 八年，疏言大婚典禮宜崇節儉，及武英殿災，复偕徐桐、翁同龢疏請勤修聖德，停罷一切工程，以弭災變，並嘉納之。
entries.en: In 1869 he urged frugality for the imperial wedding rites; after fire struck the Hall of Martial Glory, he joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in asking the emperor to deepen his virtue and halt all building projects to appease Heaven's warning—and the court welcomed their counsel.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized that the grand wedding rites should honor frugality; when the Hall of Martial Glory burned, he again joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in memorializing to cultivate sage virtue diligently, halt all construction, and quell calamities—and all was praised and accepted.

entries.zh: 十年，晉文華殿大學士，以疾再乞休。
entries.en: In 1871 he was promoted to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall and again asked leave on account of illness.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and again begged retirement on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 尋卒，贈太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文端。
entries.en: He died soon after. The court granted him the posthumous rank of Grand Tutor, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave him the posthumous name Wenduan.
entries.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor, entered the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and honored with the posthumous name Wenduan.

entries.zh: 光緒八年，河南巡撫李鶴年奏建專祠於開封，允之。
entries.en: In 1882 Henan governor Li Henian asked to erect a private shrine to Wo Ren at Kaifeng, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu the Henan governor Li Henian memorialized to build a private shrine at Kaifeng; it was approved.

entries.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，河北土寇蜂起，用尚書周祖培薦，命治河北團練。
entries.en: In 1853, as Taiping forces pushed north and local bandits swarmed over Hebei, he was ordered—on Minister Zhou Zupei's recommendation—to organize militia defense in the province.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Taiping rebels invaded north and local bandits rose throughout Hebei; on Minister Zhou Zupei's recommendation he was ordered to organize militia training in Hebei.

entries.zh: 棠階聯絡村鎮，名曰「友助社」。
entries.en: Tangjie linked villages and market towns into units he called "Mutual Aid Society."
entries.literal: Tangjie linked villages and market towns under the name "Mutual Aid Society."

entries.zh: 賊踞溫縣東河灘柳林，四出焚掠，棠階督團練擊之，村民未習戰，且無火器，殺賊數十人，卒不敵。
entries.en: Bandits held the willow groves on Wen County's east river flats and raided far and wide. Tangjie led the militia against them, but the peasants were untrained and had no guns; though they killed several dozen bandits, they could not hold the field.
entries.literal: Bandits held the willow groves on the east river beach of Wen County and raided in all directions; Tangjie led the militia against them, but the villagers were untrained in warfare and had no firearms; they killed several dozen bandits but could not prevail in the end.

entries.zh: 會山東巡撫李僡率兵至，賊引去。
entries.en: When Shandong governor Li Huang arrived with troops, the bandits drew off.
entries.literal: When Shandong Governor Li Huang arrived with troops, the bandits withdrew.

entries.zh: 賊自渡黃河，始知民間有備，稍稍牽綴。
entries.en: Once the bandits crossed the Yellow River, they found the countryside armed and were somewhat slowed in their advance.
entries.literal: From the time the bandits crossed the Yellow River they learned that the populace was prepared and were somewhat held back.

entries.zh: 洎河北肅清，敘勞，加四品卿銜，賜花翎。
entries.en: When Hebei was cleared, his service was rewarded with a fourth-grade chamberlain's rank and the peacock feather.
entries.literal: When Hebei was pacified, his merit was recorded; he was given the rank of fourth-grade chamberlain and awarded the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 倭仁，字艮峰，烏齊格里氏，蒙古正紅旗人，河南駐防。
entries.en: Wo Ren, whose style was Genfeng, belonged to the Ujikri clan. A Mongol bannerman of the Plain Red Banner, he was stationed on garrison duty in Henan.
entries.literal: Wo Ren, style name Genfeng, of the Ujikri clan, a Mongol of the Plain Red Banner, garrisoned at Henan.

entries.zh: 道光九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1829 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 歷中允、侍講、侍讀、庶子、侍講學士、侍讀學士。
entries.en: He rose through the posts of middle attendant, lecturer, reader, tutor of the heir apparent, and finally lecturer-at-large and reader-at-large.
entries.literal: He served in succession as middle attendant, lecturer, reader, tutor of the heir apparent, lecturer-at-large, and reader-at-large.

entries.zh: 二十二年，擢詹事。
entries.en: In 1842 he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 二十四年，遷大理寺卿。
entries.en: In 1844 he was transferred to the presidency of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to be president of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「行政莫先於用人，用人莫先於君子小人之辨。
entries.en: When the Xianfeng Emperor acceded, Wo Ren answered an imperial call for counsel with a memorial that began: 'In governing, nothing precedes the choice of men; in choosing men, nothing precedes telling the gentleman from the petty man.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, in response to an edict he submitted a memorial, stating in part: 'In administration nothing comes before employing men; in employing men nothing comes before distinguishing gentlemen from petty men.

entries.zh: 夫君子小人藏於心術者難知，發於事蹟者易見。
entries.en: What a gentleman or a petty man keeps in the heart is hard to discern; what shows in his conduct is easy to see.
entries.literal: As for gentlemen and petty men, what is hidden in the mind is hard to know; what appears in deeds is easy to see.

entries.zh: 大抵君子訥拙，小人佞巧；
entries.en: As a rule, the gentleman is plain-spoken and unadorned, the petty man glib and artful;
entries.literal: Generally, gentlemen are slow-spoken and awkward; petty men are flattering and clever;

entries.zh: 君子澹定，小人躁競；
entries.en: the gentleman is calm and self-possessed, the petty man restless and grasping;
entries.literal: gentlemen are calm and settled; petty men are restless and contentious;

entries.zh: 君子愛惜人才，小人排擠異類；
entries.en: the gentleman cherishes able men, the petty man drives out anyone unlike himself;
entries.literal: gentlemen cherish talent; petty men drive out those unlike themselves;

entries.zh: 君子圖遠大，以國家元氣為先，小人計目前，以聚斂刻薄為務。
entries.en: The gentleman looks to the long view and puts the nation's underlying strength first; the petty man counts only the moment and makes squeezing revenue and harshness his business.
entries.literal: Gentlemen plan for the long term and put the nation's vital energy first; petty men reckon only the present and make extortion and meanness their task.

entries.zh: 剛正不撓、無所阿鄉者，君子也；
entries.en: He who is upright, unbending, and curries favor with none is a gentleman;
entries.literal: Those who are upright and unyielding and curry favor with no one are gentlemen;

entries.zh: 依違兩可、工於趨避者，小人也。
entries.en: he who trims between two sides and is skilled at slipping away is a petty man.
entries.literal: those who waver between two sides and are skilled at evasion are petty men.

entries.zh: 諫諍匡弼、進憂危之議，動人主之警心者，君子也；
entries.en: He who admonishes and steadies the throne, who offers words of peril to rouse the sovereign's vigilance, is a gentleman;
entries.literal: Those who remonstrate and assist, who advance warnings of peril to stir the ruler's vigilance, are gentlemen;

entries.zh: 喜言氣數、不畏天變，長人君之逸志者，小人也。
entries.en: he who delights in omens and fate, who does not fear Heaven's warnings and instead feeds the ruler's wish for ease, is a petty man.
