entries.literal: those who delight in speaking of fate and portents and do not fear Heaven's changes, who foster the sovereign's mind of ease, are petty men.

entries.zh: 公私邪正，相反如此。
entries.en: Between public duty and private interest, between the straight and the crooked, the contrast is as stark as this.
entries.literal: Public and private, straight and crooked—so opposed are they.

entries.zh: 皇上天亶聰明，孰賢孰否，必能洞知。
entries.en: Your Majesty's Heaven-given discernment can surely see through who is worthy and who is not.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-bestowed intelligence—who is worthy and who is not, you must surely discern to the bottom.

entries.zh: 第恐一人之心思耳目，揣摩者眾，混淆者多，幾微莫辨，情偽滋紛，愛憎稍涉偏私，取捨必至失當。
entries.en: Yet I fear that a single mind and pair of ears, however keen, must face many who read your wishes and many who cloud them; the finest shades grow hard to tell apart, truth and pretense tangle, and the slightest tilt of favor or dislike will skew whom you keep and whom you cast aside.
entries.literal: Only I fear that with one man's thoughts and senses, those who study his wishes are many and those who confuse him many; the subtle becomes impossible to distinguish, sincerity and falsehood multiply, and if love and hate involve the slightest bias, choice and rejection must go wrong.

entries.zh: 知人則哲，豈有他術，在皇上好學勤求，使聖志益明，聖德日固而已。
entries.en: To know men is wisdom: there is no other secret. Your Majesty must study earnestly and seek counsel without cease, so your sage purpose grows ever clearer and your sage virtue firmer day by day.
entries.literal: To know men is to be wise—what other art is there? It lies only in Your Majesty's diligent study and seeking, so that the sage purpose grows clearer and sage virtue daily firmer.

entries.zh: 宋程顥雲，'古者人君必有誦訓箴諫之臣'。
entries.en: Cheng Hao of the Song said, 'In ancient times every ruler had ministers who recited lessons and offered frank remonstrance.'
entries.literal: Song Cheng Hao said, 'In antiquity the ruler must have ministers who recite admonitions and offer remonstrance.'

entries.zh: 請命老成之儒，講論道義，又擇天下賢俊，陪侍法從。
entries.en: I ask that seasoned Confucians be charged to expound the Way and its duties, and that worthy men from across the realm be chosen to attend you in study and counsel.
entries.literal: I beg that aged Confucians be ordered to discourse on moral principle, and that worthy men from throughout the realm be chosen to attend in the ruler's entourage.

entries.zh: 我朝康熙間，熊賜履上疏，亦以'延訪真儒'為說。
entries.en: In the Kangxi reign of our dynasty, Xiong Cili likewise memorialized the throne, urging that true scholars be sought out and consulted.
entries.literal: In our dynasty's Kangxi reign, Xiong Cili memorialized likewise urging 'extending visits to true Confucians.'

entries.zh: 二臣所言，皆修養身心之要，用人行政之源也。
entries.en: What these two ministers urged goes to the heart of self-cultivation—and to the root of how men are chosen and how the realm is governed.
entries.literal: What these two ministers said is all essential to cultivating body and mind, the source of employing men and governing.

entries.zh: 天下治亂系宰相，君德成就責講筵。
entries.en: Whether the realm is well or ill governed hangs on the chief minister; whether the ruler's virtue matures rests on those who teach him.
entries.literal: Order and disorder in the realm hinge on the chief minister; achievement of the ruler's virtue rests with the lecture hall.

entries.zh: 惟君德成就而後輔弼得人，輔弼得人而後天下可治。」
entries.en: Only when the ruler's virtue is formed can the right helpers be found; only when the right helpers are found can the realm be brought to order.'
entries.literal: Only when the ruler's virtue is achieved may the assistants be well chosen; only when assistants are well chosen may the realm be governed.'

entries.zh: 疏入，上稱其切直，因諭大小臣工進言以倭仁為法。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor praised its blunt honesty and told officials at every rank to speak their minds, taking Wo Ren as their example.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor praised its forthrightness and instructed officials great and small to speak frankly with Wo Ren as their model.

entries.zh: 未幾，禮部侍郎曾國籓奏用人三策，上复憶倭仁言，手詔同褒勉焉。
entries.en: Soon afterward Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan submitted three proposals on appointing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's memorial and with his own hand issued an edict commending them both.
entries.literal: Before long, Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan memorialized with three policies for employing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's words and personally issued an edict praising them together.

entries.zh: 咸豐三年正月，粵匪既陷武昌，兩江總督陸建瀛赴上游督師，祥厚偕江蘇巡撫楊文定留守江寧。
entries.en: In the first month of 1853, after the Taiping forces had captured Wuchang, Governor-General Lu Jianying of the Two Jiangs went upriver to take command of the campaign, while Xianghou and Jiangsu governor Yang Wending stayed behind to defend Nanjing.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year of Xianfeng, after the Cantonese rebels had taken Wuchang, the Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Lu Jianying went upstream to direct the army; Xianghou, together with Jiangsu Governor Yang Wending, remained to hold Jiangning.

entries.zh: 賊已蔽江而下，壽春鎮總兵恩長戰歿，建瀛遽退，文定亦不候旨迳赴鎮江。
entries.en: The rebels were already sweeping down the Yangtze. Shouchun commander En Chang was killed in action. Jianying pulled back in haste, and Wending likewise rushed off to Zhenjiang without waiting for orders from the throne.
entries.literal: The rebels had already covered the river and come downstream; Shouchun garrison commander En Chang died in battle; Jianying abruptly withdrew, and Wending likewise went straight to Zhenjiang without awaiting imperial orders.

entries.zh: 祥厚偕副都統霍隆武、提督福珠洪阿、布政使祁宿藻疏言：「督臣藉口江寧吃緊，趕回佈置，沿途險要，並不屯紮，上駛師船，一概撤回，專守水路之東西梁山。
entries.en: Xianghou, Deputy Commander Huo Longwu, Regional Commander Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Provincial Commissioner Qi Suzao submitted a joint memorial: "The governor-general, pleading the crisis at Nanjing, hurried back to make dispositions; yet he left no garrisons at any of the strategic points along the way, recalled every war-junk that had been sent upriver, and concentrated his efforts only on holding the Eastern and Western Liang hills on the water route.
entries.literal: Xianghou, together with Deputy Commander Huo Longwu, Regional Commander Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Qi Suzao memorialized, saying: "The Governor-General, citing the urgency at Jiangning, hurried back to make arrangements, yet at strategic points along the route he stationed no troops, recalled all war-junks going upstream, and devoted himself solely to guarding the Eastern and Western Liang hills on the water route.

entries.zh: 蕪湖為江蘇門戶，亦不設防。
entries.en: Wuhu, the gateway to Jiangsu, was left undefended as well.
entries.literal: Wuhu is the gateway to Jiangsu, yet no defense was set up there either.

entries.zh: 十八日隻身抵省，遂致闔城驚擾。
entries.en: On the eighteenth he reached the capital by himself, throwing the entire city into panic.
entries.literal: On the eighteenth he arrived at the provincial capital alone, and the whole city was thrown into alarm.

entries.zh: 臣等函勸速統舟師迎擊，乃督臣晏坐衙齋，三日不覆。
entries.en: We wrote urging him to assemble the fleet and strike the rebels at once, but the governor-general remained idle in his yamen and did not answer for three days.
entries.literal: We wrote urging him to gather the fleet at once and meet the enemy; yet the Governor-General sat idle in his yamen and for three days gave no reply.

entries.zh: 撫臣執意移駐鎮江，挽留不顧，民情加倍驚惶。
entries.en: The governor insisted on shifting his headquarters to Zhenjiang and ignored our pleas to remain; public fear only grew worse.
entries.literal: The Governor was determined to move his headquarters to Zhenjiang and paid no heed to our pleas to stay; popular alarm was doubled.

entries.zh: 自今固結民心，尚恐緩急難恃；
entries.en: Even if we rally the people now, we fear they will not stand by us when the crisis comes;
entries.literal: From this point, even if we now bind the people's hearts, we still fear they cannot be relied on in an emergency;

entries.zh: 若任其紛紛遷徙，土匪因而竊發，奸細尤易勾結。
entries.en: and if the populace is allowed to flee in disorder, local bandits will rise in the confusion and enemy agents will find it all the easier to collude with them.
entries.literal: if they are allowed to scatter in flight, local bandits will seize the chance to rise, and enemy agents will find it all the easier to collude.

entries.zh: 是未禦外侮，將成內變。
entries.en: We shall face internal disorder before we have even repelled the invader.
entries.literal: Thus before we have repelled the foreign foe, an internal upheaval will take shape.

entries.zh: 現在督撫臣首鼠兩端，進退無據，以致省城震動。
entries.en: At present the governor-general and governor waver and cannot decide whether to advance or withdraw, and the provincial capital is in turmoil.
entries.literal: At present the Governor-General and Governor are irresolute, with no firm ground for advance or retreat, so that the provincial capital is shaken.

entries.zh: 雖有旗兵志切同仇，無如兵力太單。
entries.en: Though the banner garrison is eager to fight, our numbers are far too few.
entries.literal: Although the banner troops are eager for revenge, there is no help for it that our forces are too few.

entries.zh: 賊船順流下竄，朝發夕至，守禦萬分緊迫，督同道府等官及八旗協領，激勵官兵，安慰居民，竭盡血誠，認真辦理。
entries.en: The rebel fleet is racing downstream and may reach us overnight. The defense is desperately urgent. We, together with the circuit intendants, prefects, and Eight Banners assistant commanders, are doing all we can to hearten the troops, reassure the people, and carry out the defense in earnest.
entries.literal: The rebel ships are fleeing downstream; they may set out in the morning and arrive by evening—the defense is desperately urgent. We, together with the circuit intendants, prefects, and other officials and the Eight Banners assistant commanders, are rousing the officers and troops, reassuring the inhabitants, and doing our utmost in all sincerity.

entries.zh: 請飭琦善、陳金綬迅速繞出賊前，協力堵剿，以固省城根本，維持南北大局。」
entries.en: We beg that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to get ahead of the rebels at once and join in blocking and destroying them, to secure Nanjing and uphold the balance of power between north and south."
entries.literal: We beg that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to move swiftly ahead of the rebels and join in blocking and suppressing them, to secure the foundation of the provincial capital and uphold the great balance of North and South."

entries.zh: 疏入，詔逮建瀛治罪，命祥厚兼署總督，與霍隆武、福珠洪阿、祁宿藻悉心防禦，以在籍前廣西巡撫鄒鳴鶴熟悉賊情，命同籌辦。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered Jianying arrested and punished. Xianghou was appointed acting governor-general and, with Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao, charged to organize the defense. Zou Minghe, the former Guangxi governor now at home and familiar with the rebels, was ordered to assist in planning.
entries.literal: When the memorial was received, an edict ordered Jianying arrested and punished; Xianghou was ordered to act concurrently as Governor-General and, with Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao, to devote themselves to defense; and Zou Minghe, former Governor of Guangxi now at home and familiar with the rebels, was ordered to assist in planning.

entries.zh: 列傳一百八十五
entries.en: Biography 185
entries.literal: Biographies 185

entries.zh: 宗稷辰，字滌甫，浙江會稽人。
entries.en: Zong Jichen, style name Difu, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Zong Jichen, whose style name was Difu, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 道光元年舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。
entries.en: He earned his juren degree in the first year of Daoguang (1821), received appointment as a Grand Secretariat secretary, and served on the Grand Council staff.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 遷起居注主事，再遷戶部員外郎。
entries.en: He was then moved to the Office of the Diarist as a director, and later promoted again to assistant department director in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be a director in the Office of the Diarist, and was promoted again to be an assistant department director in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 咸豐元年，遷御史。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he was promoted to censor.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to be a censor.

entries.zh: 疏請飭各省實行保甲，略言：「州縣宜久任，時日宜寬假，填寫門牌當詳細核對，董事胥役毋派費累民，酌用丞簿以為襄助，先編巨族以為聯屬，並可申明讀法之典，兼收團練、社倉之益。」
entries.en: He submitted a memorial calling on the provinces to enforce the baojia system in earnest, stating: "Magistrates should hold office long enough to see results, that deadlines should be realistic, that door-plate registers must be checked carefully, that clerks must not pad fees at the people's expense, that deputy magistrates and registrars could assist, that large lineages should be enrolled first to bind neighborhoods together, and that public reading of the law could be combined with militia drill and community granaries for mutual benefit."
entries.literal: He memorialized urging that every province rigorously implement the baojia system, stating in summary: "Prefects and magistrates ought to serve long terms; deadlines ought to be relaxed; household placards ought to be filled out with careful verification; supervising clerks and runners must not levy fees to burden the people; assistant magistrates and registrars may be employed to help; great clans should first be registered to form mutual ties; one may also proclaim the statutes on collective reading, and at the same time gain the benefits of militia training and community granaries."

entries.zh: 詔下直省督撫，各就地體察參酌行之。
entries.en: The throne ordered the governors of the metropolitan provinces to investigate local conditions and implement the plan as they saw fit.
entries.literal: An edict was sent down to the governors-general and governors of the metropolitan provinces, each to investigate on the spot and carry it out as appropriate.

entries.zh: 又疏言通籌出入，宜崇實去偽，舉清查、報效、生息三端；
entries.en: In another memorial on balancing income and expenditure he urged honesty over window-dressing and singled out three measures—audits, voluntary contributions, and interest-bearing reserves;
entries.literal: He also memorialized on coordinating revenue and expenditure overall, saying that truth should be honored and falsity rejected, and citing three measures: thorough investigation, voluntary contributions, and interest-bearing reserves;

entries.zh: 又疏請酌改經徵處，分令州縣戴罪嚴催：並下戶部覈議。
entries.en: and he asked that tax-collection districts be redrawn where needed and that prefects and magistrates be ordered, under threat of disciplinary liability, to press collection vigorously. The Board of Revenue was instructed to review the proposal.
entries.literal: he also memorialized requesting that collection districts be adjusted as appropriate, and that prefectures and counties be ordered severally to press collection under penalty of guilt: and the matter was referred to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.

entries.zh: 五年，聞上將謁陵，未有旨戒行，稷辰疏言：「畿南州縣被水，連歲用兵，民氣甫行休息，籥請展緩一年。」
entries.en: In the fifth year (1855), when word spread that the emperor would soon visit the tombs though no formal notice had been issued, Jichen memorialized: "The counties south of the capital had been flooded, years of war had only just eased, and the people needed rest—I beg a one-year postponement."
entries.literal: In the fifth year, hearing that the emperor was about to visit the imperial tombs though no edict had yet been issued warning of the journey, Jichen memorialized, saying: "The prefectures and counties south of the capital have suffered flooding; war has continued year after year; the people's strength has only just begun to recover— I respectfully ask that the visit be postponed for one year."

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「每歲謁陵，事同典禮，如果畿輔民力未逮，亦必權衡時勢，暫緩舉行。
entries.en: The emperor replied: "The annual tomb visit was a ritual obligation, but if the capital region could not bear the burden, the court would weigh the times and defer the ceremony.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: "The annual visit to the tombs is a matter of ritual propriety; if the strength of the people in the capital region is not equal to it, the times must also be weighed and the ceremony temporarily deferred.

entries.zh: 今茲並未降旨何日謁陵，宗稷辰揣度陳奏，徒博敢諫之名而無其實。
entries.en: This time no edict had even fixed a date for the visit; Zong Jichen had merely guessed and spoken up, winning a reputation for bold remonstrance without any real grounds.
entries.literal: On this occasion no edict has even been issued fixing the day of the visit; Zong Jichen guessed and submitted his views, merely seeking the name of bold remonstrance without the reality.

entries.zh: 此風不可長！」
entries.en: Such posturing must not be encouraged!"
entries.literal: This practice must not be allowed to spread!"

entries.zh: 下部議處。
entries.en: The case was sent to the appropriate ministry for disciplinary action.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the relevant ministry for disciplinary deliberation.

entries.zh: 尋又奏言：「自粵匪竄據長江，數年以來，文臣武將，能戰者稀。
entries.en: He soon memorialized again: "Since the Taiping rebels seized the Yangtze, able commanders—civil or military—have been scarce for years.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he again memorialized, saying: "Since the Cantonese rebels seized positions along the Yangtze, over several years civil and military officials alike who can actually fight have been few.

entries.zh: 如烏蘭泰、塔齊布、江忠源皆難得之將，而多不盡其用，且以死殉。
entries.en: Generals like Ulanga, Taqibu, and Jiang Zhongyuan were irreplaceable, yet the court often failed to use them fully, and they died in the field.
entries.literal: Men such as Ulanga, Taqibu, and Jiang Zhongyuan were all generals hard to come by, yet many were not fully employed, and moreover died in service.

entries.zh: 如勝保、張亮基、袁甲三皆勇於任事，而亦未盡其用，以罪罷去。
entries.en: Sheng Bao, Zhang Liangji, and Yuan Jiasan were all willing to take responsibility, yet they too were underused and removed on criminal charges.
entries.literal: Men such as Sheng Bao, Zhang Liangji, and Yuan Jiasan were all bold in undertaking affairs, yet they too were not fully employed, and were dismissed on charges of guilt.

entries.zh: 近日支持兩湖，賴有一二書生，如胡林翼、羅澤南，能以練膽為士卒先。
entries.en: Lately the two Hu provinces have been held up chiefly by a few scholar-officials—Hu Linyi and Luo Zenan—who drilled their men in courage and led from the front.
entries.literal: Recently in holding up the two Hu provinces we have relied on one or two scholars, such as Hu Linyi and Luo Zinan, who could train courage and take the lead before the troops.

entries.zh: 此二人者，實曾國籓有以開之。
entries.en: Both owed their start to Zeng Guofan's example.
entries.literal: These two men in fact had Zeng Guofan to open the way for them.

entries.zh: 此時若開文武兼資一科，誠足濟當時之急，而臣工多不敢薦舉者，一恐其才疏而得過，一恐其遇蹇而罔功。
entries.en: Opening a civil-military examination track now would truly meet the emergency, yet officials hesitate to recommend talent—fearing blame if the nominee proves mediocre, and futility if fortune turns against him.
entries.literal: At this time if an examination category for men skilled in both civil and military affairs were opened, it would truly suffice to meet the urgent needs of the day; yet many officials dare not recommend anyone—fearing on the one hand that if talent is slight they will be blamed, and on the other that if fortune is adverse they will accomplish nothing.

entries.zh: 處愁眉焚頂之時，守蹈常習故之轍，見有敗衄，動以餉匱為辭。
entries.en: In a crisis that should wring every brow, they cling to routine; at every defeat they blame empty coffers.
entries.literal: In a time when brows are knit and heads burn with worry, they cling to the beaten track of routine; whenever defeat occurs, they invariably plead shortage of pay.

entries.zh: 餉固不可不籌，試思用兵乏人，雖斂金百萬，棄如土苴，終歸無用。
entries.en: Funds must be found, but without capable commanders a million in silver is worthless as dust.
entries.literal: Pay must indeed be provided for, but consider: if in waging war men are lacking, even if a million in gold is levied and cast aside like dirt, in the end it is useless.

entries.zh: 臣聞見隘陋，非能盡識天下之才，所知湖南有左宗棠，通權達變，為疆吏所倚重，若使獨當一面，必不下於林翼、澤南。
entries.en: My own horizon is limited and I cannot know every worthy man in the empire, but in Hunan there is Zuo Zongtang—flexible, decisive, and already indispensable to provincial governors. Given an independent command he would rank with Hu Linyi and Luo Zinan.
entries.literal: Your servant's knowledge is narrow and shallow; I cannot know all the talent in the realm. Of those I know, in Hunan there is Zuo Zongtang, versatile and resourceful, relied upon by frontier officials; if he were given independent command of a front, he would certainly be no inferior to Linyi and Zenan.

entries.zh: 其屢經論薦，難進易退，肝膽經術，實可取材者，有若湖州之姚承輿。
entries.en: Repeatedly recommended yet reluctant to push forward, Yao Chengyu of Huzhou combines moral courage with classical learning and is genuinely employable.
entries.literal: One who has repeatedly been recommended in discussion, is hard to advance and easy to retire, and in boldness and classical learning is truly fit for employment, is Yao Chengyu of Huzhou.

entries.zh: 其策議深沉，才識過人者，有若常州之週騰虎、管晏，桂林之唐啟華，皆關心時務，今尚鬱鬱伏處田間。
entries.en: Men of deep strategic insight include Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan of Changzhou and Tang Qihua of Guilin—all engaged with public affairs, yet still living in obscurity on their farms.
entries.literal: Those whose policy deliberations are profound and whose talent and insight surpass others include Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan of Changzhou, and Tang Qihua of Guilin—all concerned with current affairs, yet still brooding in obscurity in the countryside.

entries.zh: 誠能破格招賢，連茹並進，則得一人可以平數州，得數人可以清一路。
entries.en: If the court would break precedent and recruit such men in clusters, one worthy could pacify several prefectures and a handful could secure an entire war zone.
entries.literal: If talent were truly recruited by breaking precedent and advanced in linked succession, then gaining one man could pacify several prefectures, and gaining several men could clear an entire route.

entries.zh: 長江雖阻，當不難分道建功，剋日平定。
entries.en: Even with the Yangtze in rebel hands, divided campaigns could still win the day and bring the rebellion to a swift end.
entries.literal: Though the Yangtze blocks the way, it should not be hard to achieve merit on separate fronts and bring pacification within a set day.

entries.zh: 伏乞皇上命內外臣工各舉所知，無論已仕未仕，果能文武兼資，皆許徵起，必可網羅而盡得之。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to order every official, inside and outside the capital, to nominate men he knows—serving or not—who truly combine civil and military gifts, and to summon them to office. In that way the court could gather every capable man in the land."
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully begs Your Majesty to order civil and military officials within and without to recommend those they know; whether already in office or not, if they truly combine civil and military ability, all may be summoned to service, and they can surely be gathered in and obtained to the full."

entries.zh: 疏入，下各督撫，命以宗棠等加考送部引見。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, the throne ordered the governors to examine Zuo Zongtang and the others and send them to the capital for audience.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, it was sent down to the governors-general and governors, with orders that Zongtang and the others be further examined and sent to the ministry for audience.

entries.zh: 宗棠自此膺簡拔，論者謂其知人。
entries.en: Zuo Zongtang was thus brought to the court's attention, and contemporaries praised Jichen for recognizing talent.
entries.literal: From this Zongtang received selection and promotion; commentators said that Jichen knew men.

entries.zh: 遷給事中。
entries.en: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be a supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 時京師行大錢，商民苦之。
entries.en: Large-denomination cash was then in circulation in the capital, to the merchants' and people's distress.
entries.literal: At the time the capital circulated large-denomination coins, and merchants and commoners suffered from them.

entries.zh: 稷辰上疏請復用制錢，號曰「祖錢」，而大錢改純用鐵鑄，兼行並用。
entries.en: Jichen memorialized to restore standard copper coinage under the name "ancestral cash," while large coins would be cast in iron only, with both kinds circulating side by side.
entries.literal: Jichen memorialized requesting restoration of standard copper cash, to be called "ancestral cash," while large coins were to be recast purely in iron, with both to circulate together.

entries.zh: 下部議，格不行。
entries.en: The relevant ministry deliberated, but the proposal was rejected.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation, but was blocked and not implemented.

entries.zh: 又以畿輔水患，疏請急賑，從之。
entries.en: He also memorialized for emergency relief when the capital region flooded, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: He also, because of flooding in the capital region, memorialized requesting urgent relief, and this was approved.

entries.zh: 尋授山東運河道，捻匪入境，於濟寧牛頭河濱築戰牆，北岸六千三百丈，南岸八千六百丈，賴以守禦。
entries.en: He was soon appointed intendant of the Shandong grain-transport circuit. When Nian rebels crossed the border he built fortified walls along the Niutou River at Jining—6,300 zhang on the north bank and 8,600 on the south—which held the line.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed intendant of the Shandong grain-transport circuit. When Nian bandits entered the province, at Niutou River bank in Jining he built battle walls—six thousand three hundred zhang on the north bank and eight thousand six hundred zhang on the south—and relied on them for defense.

entries.zh: 以功加鹽運使銜。
entries.en: For this service he received the brevet rank of salt-transport commissioner.
entries.literal: For his merit he was given the brevet rank of salt-transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 同治六年，引疾歸，尋卒。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tongzhi (1867) he retired on grounds of illness and died soon after.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he cited illness and retired, and soon afterward died.

entries.zh: 稷辰父霈正，官湖南零陵知縣，廉無餘貲。
entries.en: Jichen's father Peizheng had been magistrate of Lingling in Hunan and died leaving nothing beyond an honest name.
entries.literal: Jichen's father Peizheng served as magistrate of Lingling in Hunan, was incorruptible, and left no surplus wealth.

entries.zh: 稷辰事母孝。
entries.en: Jichen was devoted to his mother.
entries.literal: Jichen was filial in serving his mother.

entries.zh: 為學宗王守仁、劉宗周。
entries.en: In scholarship he followed Wang Yangming and Liu Zongzhou.
entries.literal: In learning he took Wang Shouren and Liu Zongzhou as his masters.

entries.zh: 罷官後，主餘姚龍山書院、山陰蕺山書院。
entries.en: After leaving office he directed the Longshan Academy in Yuyao and the Jishan Academy in Shanyin.
entries.literal: After leaving office he headed the Longshan Academy in Yuyao and the Jishan Academy in Shanyin.

entries.zh: 官京朝，請祀總兵葛雲飛本籍；
entries.en: While at court he petitioned for a shrine to Brigadier Ge Yunfei in Ge's home district;
entries.literal: While serving at court he requested that Brigadier General Ge Yunfei be enshrined in his native place;

entries.zh: 官山東，請修方孝孺祠，並刻正學集：其振勵風教多類此。
entries.en: and in Shandong he had Fang Xiaoru's shrine restored and the Correct Learning collection carved for printing—typical of his efforts to uphold moral culture.
entries.literal: while serving in Shandong he requested repair of the shrine to Fang Xiaoru and the carving of the Correct Learning collection: his efforts to revive custom and instruction were mostly of this kind.

entries.zh: 尹耕雲，字杏農，江蘇桃源人。
entries.en: Yin Gengyun, style name Xingnong, came from Taoyuan in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Yin Gengyun, whose style name was Xingnong, was a native of Taoyuan in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 道光三十年進士，授禮部主事，再遷郎中。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirtieth year of Daoguang (1850), entered the Ministry of Rites as a director, and was later promoted to bureau director.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Rites, and was later promoted to be a bureau director.

entries.zh: 咸豐五年，粵匪犯畿輔，惠親王綿愉為大將軍，僧格林沁參贊軍務，闢耕雲佐幕府，上書論防務，為文宗所知。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Xianfeng (1855), when Taiping forces threatened the capital region, Prince Hui Mianyu was named commander-in-chief with Sengge Rinchen as his deputy. Gengyun joined the staff, wrote on defense, and won the attention of the Xianfeng Emperor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels threatened the capital region, Prince Hui Mianyu served as commander-in-chief and Sengge Rinchen assisted in military affairs; Gengyun was recruited to the staff, submitted writings on defense, and came to the notice of the Wenzong Emperor.

entries.zh: 八年，授湖廣道監察御史，署戶科給事中。
entries.en: In the eighth year (1858) he was appointed Huguang circuit censor and acted as supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed censor on the Huguang circuit and acted as supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.

entries.zh: 時方多事，封章月數上。
entries.en: Troubled times kept him submitting several memorials a month.
entries.literal: The times were troubled, and sealed memorials went up several times each month.

entries.zh: 直隸總督訥爾經額坐貽誤封疆罷，復起。
entries.en: Zhili governor-general Ne'erjing'e had been dismissed for losing the frontier, then was brought back to office.
entries.literal: The Zhili governor-general Ne'erjing'e had been dismissed for dereliction on the frontier, then was reappointed.

entries.zh: 耕雲疏言：「訥爾經額之罪，天下共聞共見，未喻其復行起用之故。
entries.en: Gengyun memorialized: "Ne'erjing'e's failures are notorious, and no one understands why he has been reappointed.
entries.literal: Gengyun memorialized, saying: "Ne'erjing'e's guilt is known to all under Heaven, seen by all; the reason for his reappointment is not understood.

entries.zh: 方今江、淮、楚、豫軍務未靖，秉鉞之臣，星羅棋布，所以奮不顧身，必欲滅此朝食者，固由篤於忠義，亦以國家信賞必罰，有以畏服其心。
entries.en: With war still raging along the Yangtze, Huai, Chu, and Yu fronts, field commanders are everywhere. They risk their lives because they are loyal—but also because the dynasty's record of reward and punishment commands their respect.
entries.literal: At present military affairs in Jiang, Huai, Chu, and Yu are not yet settled; commanders with axes of authority are spread like stars in the sky or pieces on a board. That they throw themselves forward without regard for life and are determined to destroy the foe at breakfast is indeed due to deep loyalty and righteousness, but also because the state rewards faithfulness and punishes without fail, so that their hearts are held in awe and submission.

entries.zh: 萬一效尤解體，患何可言？
entries.en: If others follow his example and the armies lose heart, the consequences are unthinkable.
entries.literal: If others follow his example and the armies dissolve, what disaster can be spoken of?

entries.zh: 昔宣宗起用琦善，以陳慶鏞之言而罷。
entries.en: Under the Daoguang Emperor, Qishan had been reappointed but was dismissed after Chen Qingyong remonstrated.
entries.literal: Formerly the Daoguang Emperor reappointed Qishan, but because of Chen Qingyong's words he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 伏原紹述心傳，收回成命。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to follow that precedent and revoke the appointment."
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully begs that Your Majesty continue the transmitted intent of the heart and withdraw the present appointment."

entries.zh: 時粵匪复窺武漢，耕雲疏言：「武漢地踞上游，北窺關陝，南脅湖湘，東撼吳越，西製巴蜀，自古南北用兵，皆出死力爭之。
entries.en: When the Taiping forces again threatened Wuhan, Gengyun wrote: "Wuhan commanded the upper Yangtze—overlooking Shaanxi to the north, menacing Hunan and Hubei to the south, threatening Jiangsu and Zhejiang to the east, and holding Sichuan to the west—and every north-south war in history had been fought to the death for this position.
entries.literal: At the time Cantonese rebels again eyed Wuhan. Gengyun memorialized, saying: "Wuhan lies in the upper reaches; to the north it overlooks Guan and Shaan, to the south it threatens Hunan and Hubei, to the east it shakes Wu and Yue, to the west it controls Ba and Shu. From antiquity, whenever north and south waged war, both sides fought for it with their utmost strength.

entries.zh: 今賊窺伺楚北，分擾廣濟、黃岡，逼近省城，撫臣胡林翼兵勇數千，眾寡懸絕，江路綿遠，首尾不能兼顧。
entries.en: The rebels now probed northern Hubei, raided Guangji and Huanggang, and closed on the provincial capital. Governor Hu Linyi had only a few thousand men—far too few—and could not cover the long river line at once.
entries.literal: Now the rebels watch the north of Chu, raid separately in Guangji and Huanggang, and press close to the provincial capital. The governor Hu Linyi has only a few thousand troops; the disparity in numbers is extreme; the river route is long and far, and he cannot attend to both head and tail.

entries.zh: 侍郎曾國籓忠勇樸誠，應請授為欽差大臣，率其所部援湖北，較諸他臣事半功倍。」
entries.en: Vice President Zeng Guofan is loyal, brave, and steadfast; he should be named imperial commissioner to lead his own troops to relieve Hubei—no other choice would achieve so much so quickly."
entries.literal: The vice president of a ministry, Zeng Guofan, is loyal, brave, plain, and sincere; he should be appointed imperial commissioner and lead his own forces to relieve Hubei—compared with other officials, he would achieve twice the result with half the effort."

entries.zh: 粵匪陷定遠，耕雲疏言：「定遠失守，粵、捻新合，必謀北竄，恃山東為之屏蔽。
entries.en: When the rebels took Dingyuan, Gengyun warned: "The Taiping and Nian armies had joined forces and would surely drive north, using Shandong as their shield.
entries.literal: When Cantonese rebels took Dingyuan, Gengyun memorialized, saying: "With the loss of Dingyuan, Cantonese and Nian forces have newly joined; they are sure to plan a northern thrust and rely on Shandong as their screen.

entries.zh: 撫臣崇恩幸其不戕官據城，於賊退後虛報勝仗，內則巧為彌縫，掩一人耳目；
entries.en: Governor Chong'en was lucky the rebels had not slaughtered officials or held the city; when they withdrew he filed false victory reports and papered over the truth to deceive his superiors;
entries.literal: The governor Chong'en was fortunate that they did not kill officials and seize the city; after the rebels withdrew he falsely reported victories, inwardly covering matters with clever evasions to deceive one man's eyes and ears;

entries.zh: 外則恣其朘削，竭萬姓脂膏。
entries.en: outwardly he squeezed the people dry.
entries.literal: outwardly he indulged in squeezing the people and drained the fat and marrow of the myriad commoners.

entries.zh: 惟懇俯念籓籬重地，立予罷斥，簡大員往代。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to remember how vital this frontier province is, dismiss Chong'en at once, and send a senior replacement.
entries.literal: I only beg that Your Majesty look down and consider this vital borderland, immediately dismiss and cast him out, and select a high official to replace him.

entries.zh: 於洪湖​​多募水師，兼飭傅振邦全軍移駐固鎮、靈壁，冀收皖北，以固山東。」
entries.en: Recruit more river forces at Hong Lake, and order Fu Zhenbang's entire army to garrison Guzhen and Lingbi in hopes of recovering northern Anhui and securing Shandong."
entries.literal: At Hong Lake recruit many river troops in addition, and also order Fu Zhenbang's entire army to move and garrison at Guzhen and Lingbi, hoping to recover northern Anhui and thereby secure Shandong."

entries.zh: 及廬州失守，又​​疏言：「昔人建省安慶，與九江、江寧為犄角，控扼長江。
entries.en: When Luzhou fell as well, he memorialized again: "The province had once been seated at Anqing, forming a triangle with Jiujiang and Nanjing to control the Yangtze.
entries.literal: When Luzhou also fell, he again memorialized, saying: "Former men established the provincial seat at Anqing, forming a pincer with Jiujiang and Jiangning to control and choke the Yangtze.

entries.zh: 上年徙治廬州，已失形勝，茲並廬州亦不能守。
entries.en: Moving the seat to Luzhou last year had already sacrificed the strategic advantage; now even Luzhou was lost.
entries.literal: Last year the seat was moved to Luzhou, already losing the strategic advantage; now even Luzhou cannot be held.

entries.zh: 胡林翼等自武漢進逼九江，而安徽之賊，或自英、霍走湖北，牽我上游，或自徽、歙擾浙西，窺我腹地。
entries.en: While Hu Linyi pressed Jiujiang from Wuhan, Anhui rebels might strike into Hubei from Yingshan and Huoshan to tie down the upper river, or raid western Zhejiang from Huizhou and Shexian to threaten the interior.
entries.literal: Hu Linyi and others advanced from Wuhan to press Jiujiang, while the rebels in Anhui either came from Ying and Huo into Hubei, pulling at our upper reaches, or from Hui and She to harass western Zhejiang, spying on our interior.

entries.zh: 我軍分道救援，罷於奔命。
entries.en: Our armies were scattered on rescue missions and exhausted from constant marching.
entries.literal: Our armies were sent on separate rescue missions and were worn out running to and fro.

entries.zh: 賊有四達之路，我無三面之圍，雖日克一城，何益？
entries.en: The rebels could move in every direction while we could not close three sides of them; capturing a city a day would do little good.
entries.literal: The rebels have roads leading in four directions; we have no encirclement on three sides; even if we take a city each day, what is the use?

entries.zh: 撫臣福濟屢挫損威，候補京堂袁甲三素得民心，如以為巡撫，必奮身圖報。」
entries.en: Governor Fuji's repeated defeats had ruined his authority; Yuan Jiasan, an expectant capital official, enjoyed the people's trust and would throw himself into service if appointed governor."
entries.literal: The governor Fuji's repeated defeats have damaged his authority; the expectant capital official Yuan Jiasan has long won the people's hearts—if made governor, he would surely throw himself forward to repay the favor."

entries.zh: 及國籓進師，疏言：「軍興以來，徵調半天下，糜餉數千萬，卒未能掃穴擒渠，則以屢後時而數失機也。
entries.en: When Zeng Guofan marched, Gengyun wrote: "Since the war began half the empire had been mobilized and tens of millions spent, yet the rebel leadership remained at large—chiefly because the court had repeatedly been late and lost its chances.
entries.literal: When Guofan advanced his army, Gengyun memorialized, saying: "Since the armies were raised, half the realm has been mobilized and tens of millions in pay have been consumed, yet in the end the nest has not been swept and the ringleader captured—because opportunities have repeatedly been missed by arriving late.

entries.zh: 今曾國籓蓄養精銳，所向克捷。
entries.en: Now Zeng Guofan had trained elite troops and was winning wherever he fought.
entries.literal: Now Zeng Guofan has nurtured elite troops and wherever he turns he wins.

entries.zh: 陳玉成、張洛行率悍賊數十萬，齊向潛山、太湖抗拒，眾寡之數，十倍於我，一有疏虞，關係甚重。
entries.en: Chen Yucheng and Zhang Luoxing had massed hundreds of thousands of hardened rebels at Qianshan and Taihu—ten times Zeng's numbers. The slightest mistake would be catastrophic.
entries.literal: Chen Yucheng and Zhang Luoxing led several hundred thousand fierce rebels together to resist at Qianshan and Taihu; in numbers they were ten times our strength; the slightest lapse would have grave consequences.

entries.zh: 此時廬、鳳、六合賊勢必單，請飭袁甲三、張國樑刻期搗其巢穴，逼令反顧，或令間道為楚師聲援，亦足褫其狂魄。」
entries.en: Rebel forces at Luzhou, Fengyang, and Liuhe must now be thin. Order Yuan Jiasan and Zhang Guoliang to strike their bases on a fixed schedule, forcing them to turn back, or send them by side routes to support Zeng's army—either move would break the rebels' nerve."
entries.literal: At this time rebel strength at Lu, Feng, and Liuhe must surely be thin; I beg that Yuan Jiasan and Zhang Guoliang be ordered on a fixed date to strike their nests, forcing them to look back, or that they be sent by side routes to support the Chu army in sound—this too would suffice to shake their mad spirit."

entries.zh: 別疏劾河道總督庚長，請以甲三兼攝；
entries.en: In another memorial he impeached Grand Canal director-general Gengchang and asked that Yuan Jiasan hold the post concurrently;
entries.literal: In a separate memorial he impeached the Grand Canal director-general Gengchang and requested that Jiasan hold the post concurrently;

entries.zh: 又論雲南迴匪不宜專意主撫；
entries.en: he argued that pacification alone would not suffice against the Yunnan Hui rebels;
entries.literal: he also argued that in Yunnan the Hui rebels should not be handled with sole emphasis on pacification;

entries.zh: 又陳京師本計，平糶、採買、周恤、蓄積諸事宜並舉；
entries.en: he laid out a comprehensive capital relief program covering fair-price grain sales, procurement, relief, and reserves;
entries.literal: he also set forth the capital's fundamental plan, presenting together the matters of fair grain sales, procurement, relief, and storage;

entries.zh: 又言錢法積弊：諸疏多見採納。
entries.en: and he exposed long-standing abuses in the currency system. Most of these proposals were adopted.
entries.literal: and he also spoke of accumulated abuses in the currency system: many of these memorials were adopted.

entries.zh: 英、法合軍犯天津，耕雲專疏者七，會疏者二，力主決戰，上命王大臣集議。
entries.en: When British and French forces attacked Tianjin together, Gengyun filed seven solo memorials and joined two joint ones, all urging war to the finish. The emperor convened the princes and senior ministers to deliberate.
entries.literal: When British and French forces jointly attacked Tianjin, Gengyun submitted seven memorials on his own and joined two collective memorials, strongly urging decisive battle; the emperor ordered the princes and high ministers to assemble for deliberation.

entries.zh: 與鄭親王端華等議不合，耕云抗辯痛哭而罷。
entries.en: He clashed with Prince Zheng Duanhua and the peace party, argued fiercely, wept, and the council adjourned without agreement.
entries.literal: He disagreed with Prince Zheng Duanhua and others; Gengyun argued in opposition, wept, and the meeting broke up.

entries.zh: 耕云初在禮部，肅順頗重之，乃是為所憎。
entries.en: Gengyun had once been valued by Sushun in the Ministry of Rites; for that very reason Sushun now turned against him.
entries.literal: Gengyun had earlier been in the Ministry of Rites, where Sushun had valued him highly; for this he came to be hated by him.

entries.zh: 九年，科場獄起，以科道失糾下吏議，而耕雲以充內監試譴獨重，鐫二級調用。
entries.en: In the ninth year (1859) the examination scandal broke. Censors faced disciplinary review for failing to investigate, but Gengyun alone was heavily punished for having served as palace examiner—demoted two ranks and transferred.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the examination-hall case arose; censors and supervising secretaries were referred for disciplinary deliberation for failure to investigate, but Gengyun alone received the heavier punishment for serving as examiner for the palace examination and was demoted two ranks and transferred.

entries.zh: 十年，京師戒嚴，上將幸熱河，耕雲代團防大臣草疏諫阻，復自以書抵肅順，卒不聽。
entries.en: In the tenth year (1860), with the capital under martial law and the emperor preparing to flee to Rehe, Gengyun drafted a remonstrance for the defense commissioner and wrote personally to Sushun, but neither appeal was heard.
entries.literal: In the tenth year the capital was placed under martial law; the emperor was about to go to Rehe. Gengyun drafted a remonstrance for the defense commissioner and also sent a letter himself to Sushun, but in the end his advice was not heeded.

entries.zh: 侍郎文祥提督九門，遇耕雲東城，相持哭，因為規畫留守諸事。
entries.en: Vice President Wenxiang, commanding the Nine Gates, met Gengyun in the eastern city. They embraced and wept, and Gengyun outlined plans for holding Beijing during the emperor's absence.
entries.literal: Vice President Wenxiang was in charge of the Nine Gates; he met Gengyun in the eastern city, and they held each other weeping, whereupon Gengyun laid out plans for remaining behind to hold the capital.

entries.zh: 胡林翼疏薦耕雲胸有權略，請起用。
entries.en: Hu Linyi memorialized that Gengyun had real strategic talent and asked that he be recalled to service.
entries.literal: Hu Linyi memorialized recommending Gengyun as having strategy in his breast and requested his reappointment.

entries.zh: 會副都御史毛昶熙治河南團練，疏調從軍。
entries.en: Vice Censor-in-chief Mao Changxi, organizing Henan militia, then requested Gengyun's transfer to his staff.
entries.literal: At the time Vice Censor-in-chief Mao Changxi was organizing militia in Henan and memorialized to have Gengyun transferred to join the army.

entries.zh: 同治元年，率部卒五千，從僧格林沁平金樓寨教匪，又偕提督張曜克張岡捻巢，以道員記名，賜花翎。
entries.en: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862) he led five thousand men with Sengge Rinchen against the sect rebels at Jinlou Stockade, then with Brigadier Zhang Yao captured the Nian base at Zhanggang. He was noted for promotion to intendant and awarded the peacock feather.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he led five thousand troops, followed Sengge Rinchen in pacifying the sect rebels at Jinlou Stockade, and together with Brigadier Zhang Yao took the Nian nest at Zhanggang; he was recorded by name as an intendant and granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 三年，署河陝汝道。
entries.en: In the third year (1864) he served as acting intendant of the Henan-Shaanxi-Ru circuit.
entries.literal: In the third year he acted as intendant of the Henan-Shaanxi-Ru circuit.

entries.zh: 西征軍購糧陝州，市斛小，責屬縣償其不足，凡數百萬斤，耕雲悉請罷之。
entries.en: The western expedition bought grain at Shanzhou, but when local measures fell short the counties were forced to make up millions of jin in grain. Gengyun had every such levy cancelled.
entries.literal: The western expedition army purchased grain at Shanzhou; the market bushel was small, and subordinate counties were charged to make up the shortfall—altogether several million jin—Gengyun requested that all of this be abolished.

entries.zh: 客軍有不法者，斬以徇。
entries.en: He executed guest troops who broke the law as a public warning.
entries.literal: When guest troops committed unlawful acts, he beheaded them as a warning.

entries.zh: 境多刀匪，請得節制河、陝兵，饋餉以時，兵咸用命。
entries.en: Banditry was rife in his jurisdiction. Granted command over Henan and Shaanxi troops and paying rations on time, he brought the soldiers firmly under control.
entries.literal: The region had many armed bandits; he requested authority to command Henan and Shaanxi troops, paid rations on time, and the soldiers all obeyed orders.

entries.zh: 四年，張總愚犯畿輔，耕雲從巡撫李鶴年進軍磁州，建策築長圍斷賊歸路。
entries.en: In the fourth year (1865), when Zhang Zongyu raided the capital region, Gengyun marched with Governor Li Henian to Cizhou and proposed a long encirclement to cut off the rebels' retreat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Zhang Zongyu invaded the capital region; Gengyun followed Governor Li Henian in advancing on Cizhou and proposed building a long encirclement to cut off the rebels' line of retreat.

entries.zh: 兩署糧儲鹽法道，佐治善後事，濬惠濟河，塞河決，敘勞加布政使銜。
entries.en: Twice acting as grain-and-salt intendant, he helped manage postwar recovery, dredged the Huiji River, and sealed river breaches. For this he received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
entries.literal: He twice acted as intendant of grain storage and salt administration, assisted in postwar governance, dredged the Huiji River, blocked river breaches, and for his service was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

entries.zh: 十三年，補河陝汝道。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year (1874) he received regular appointment to the Henan-Shaanxi-Ru intendant post.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he received regular appointment as intendant of the Henan-Shaanxi-Ru circuit.

entries.zh: 河、陝徭役重，亞於常賦，耕雲立定制，嚴稽覈，民困稍甦。
entries.en: Corvée in Henan and Shaanxi weighed almost as heavily as regular taxes. Gengyun fixed the regulations, enforced audits strictly, and the people found some relief.
entries.literal: Corvée labor in Henan and Shaanxi was heavy, second only to regular taxes; Gengyun established fixed regulations and enforced strict audit, and the people's hardship was somewhat relieved.

entries.zh: 光緒三年，大旱，條上救荒七事，未及行，卒於官。
entries.en: In the third year of Guangxu (1877), during a severe drought, he submitted seven famine-relief measures, but died in office before they could be implemented.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangxu there was great drought; he submitted in items seven measures for famine relief, but before they could be carried out he died in office.

entries.zh: 耕雲在言路著直聲，出任監司，巡撫張之萬、李鶴年皆倚重之，軍事多所贊畫。
entries.en: Gengyun was famed for blunt memorials as a censor. As a provincial official, Governors Zhang Zhiwan and Li Henian relied on him heavily for military planning.
entries.literal: Gengyun won a reputation for bluntness on the remonstrance track; when he went out as a surveillance commissioner, Governors Zhang Zhiwan and Li Henian both relied on him, and he contributed much to military planning.

entries.zh: 卒後，巡撫李慶翱以災荒被劾，牽及冒領兵餉事，辭連耕雲，後終得白云。
entries.en: After his death, Governor Li Qing'ao was impeached over famine relief and implicated in false military-pay claims that touched Gengyun's name, but Gengyun was eventually cleared.
entries.literal: After his death, Governor Li Qing'ao was impeached over famine relief and was implicated in the matter of falsely claiming military pay, with testimony linking Gengyun; in the end Gengyun's name was cleared.

entries.zh: 王拯，初名錫振，字定甫，廣西馬平人。
entries.en: Wang Zheng, originally named Xizhen, style name Dingfu, came from Maping in Guangxi.
entries.literal: Wang Zheng, whose original name was Xizhen and whose style name was Dingfu, was a native of Maping in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 道光二十一年進士，授戶部主事，充軍機章京。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Daoguang (1841), entered the Ministry of Revenue as a director, and served on the Grand Council staff.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue, serving also as a clerk on the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 大學士賽尚阿視師廣西，以拯從，拯感時多難，慷慨思有所建白。
entries.en: When Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took command in Guangxi, Zheng accompanied him and, stirred by the crisis, resolved to speak out.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took command in Guangxi and took Zheng with him; Zheng, moved by the troubles of the times, thought boldly of making some proposal.

entries.zh: 咸豐間，自郎中累遷大理寺少卿。
entries.en: During the Xianfeng reign he rose from bureau director to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: During the Xianfeng reign he rose in cumulative promotion from bureau director to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 同治二年，降捻宋景詩由陝西還擾直隸、山東，拯奏言：「景詩岡屯磚圩，儼然嵎固，自陝逸回，其黨不過數百。
entries.en: In the second year of Tongzhi (1863), the surrendered Nian leader Song Jingshi came back from Shaanxi to raid Zhili and Shandong. Zheng wrote: "Jingshi's fortified stockade at Gangtun was a rebel stronghold in all but name, that his following since returning from Shaanxi numbered only a few hundred,
entries.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the surrendered Nian leader Song Jingshi returned from Shaanxi to harass Zhili and Shandong. Zheng memorialized, saying: "Jingshi's Gangtun brick stockade stands like a cornered beast's lair; since he fled back from Shaanxi, his band numbers no more than several hundred.

entries.zh: 崇厚等一再養癰，裹脅逾萬。
entries.en: yet Chonghou and others had repeatedly indulged him until his coerced following swelled past ten thousand.
entries.literal: Chonghou and others repeatedly nursed the abscess, and through coercion the force exceeded ten thousand.

entries.zh: 近复於昌邑、莘、聊城、臨清四州縣，令村莊將所獲麥與佃戶平分，運送岡屯，是其名為降伏，心跡轉益兇悖。
entries.en: Lately in Changyi, Shen, Liaocheng, and Linqing he had villages split their wheat harvests with tenants and send the grain to Gangtun. Though nominally surrendered, his actions grew ever more defiant.
entries.literal: Recently again in the four prefectures and counties of Changyi, Shen, Liaocheng, and Linqing, villages were ordered to divide the wheat harvested with tenant farmers and transport it to Gangtun—thus though he is called surrendered, in heart and deed he grows ever more fierce and rebellious.

entries.zh: 請密敕直隸督臣劉長佑計調來營，暴其罪而誅之。
entries.en: I beg a secret order to Zhili governor Liu Changyou to lure him to camp, expose his crimes, and put him to death.
entries.literal: I beg that a secret edict be sent to the Zhili governor Liu Changyou to plan summoning him to camp, expose his crimes, and execute him.

entries.zh: 若抗違不至，直隸官軍猶能越境進剿。
entries.en: If he refuses, Zhili troops can still cross the border to attack him.
entries.literal: If he resists and refuses to come, the Zhili government troops can still cross the border to advance and suppress him.

entries.zh: 景詩既除，如楊蓬嶺、程順書等首惡，皆可駢誅，以除巨憝，以安畿輔。」
entries.en: Once Jingshi is gone, ringleaders such as Yang Pengling and Cheng Shunshu can be executed together, removing the chief menace and securing the capital region."
entries.literal: Once Jingshi is removed, ringleaders such as Yang Pengling and Cheng Shunshu can all be executed together, to eliminate the great scourge and secure the capital region."

entries.zh: 疏入，未行。
entries.en: The memorial was received but not acted on.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, it was not carried out.

entries.zh: 其後景詩卒以叛誅。
entries.en: Jingshi was eventually executed for rebellion.
entries.literal: Afterward Jingshi was in the end executed for rebellion.

entries.zh: 軍事未定，曾國籓議於廣東籌餉，勞崇光創辦釐金，諸弊叢起。
entries.en: While the war continued, Zeng Guofan proposed raising funds in Guangdong; Lao Chongguang introduced the lijin transit tax, and abuses multiplied.
entries.literal: While military affairs were unsettled, Zeng Guofan proposed raising funds in Guangdong; Lao Chongguang inaugurated the lijin tax, and abuses clustered thickly.

entries.zh: 拯疏言：「兩粵為肇亂之區，岑溪、容縣，數載皆為賊踞。
entries.en: Zheng memorialized: "The two Guang provinces, where the rebellion had begun, still saw Cenxi and Rongxian held by rebels for years on end.
entries.literal: Zheng memorialized, saying: "The two Guang provinces are the region where the rebellion began; Cenxi and Rongxian have for several years all been occupied by rebels.

entries.zh: 信宜陳金缸尤為巨憝，群賊相為一氣，滋蔓難圖。
entries.en: Chen Jingang of Xinyi was the worst of them; the rebel bands acted as one and spread in ways hard to suppress.
entries.literal: Chen Jingang of Xinyi is especially the great scourge; the band of rebels breathe as one, spreading and hard to plot against.

entries.zh: 勞崇光舉辦釐金，率令紳商包充墊繳，燃眉剜肉，事何可常？
entries.en: Lao Chongguang's lijin scheme typically forced gentry and merchants to contract and advance payments—a desperate expedient that could not last.
entries.literal: Lao Chongguang inaugurated lijin, generally ordering gentry and merchants to contract for collection and advance payment—cutting flesh to put out the eyebrows' fire; how can such a thing be sustained?

entries.zh: 及崇光去任，徵收減少。
entries.en: After Chongguang left office, collections fell sharply.
entries.literal: When Chongguang left his post, collection diminished.

entries.zh: 近乃有釐務委員，或為眾所毆傷，或為民間枷號，雖民情頑獷，而官吏惡劣亦可概見。
entries.en: Lately lijin commissioners had been beaten by mobs or put in the cangue by villagers. The people were unruly, but the officials' conduct spoke for itself.
entries.literal: Recently lijin commissioners have been beaten by crowds or pilloried by the populace; though the people's temper is stubborn and violent, the wickedness of officials can also be seen in the round.

entries.zh: 以積年久亂之地，有負嵎圜視之賊，當一切利孔、百方搜剔之時，臣竊恐利未十而害已百。
entries.en: In a province long torn by war, with rebels still entrenched, squeezing every source of revenue by a hundred means may yield ten parts of profit and a hundred parts of harm.
entries.literal: In a place long chaotic through accumulated years, with rebels crouching like cornered beasts and glaring round, at a time when every source of profit is searched and squeezed by a hundred methods, your servant secretly fears that before profit reaches ten, harm has already reached a hundred.

entries.zh: 萬一兩粵复糜爛，更不知何所措手足，豈惟釐金不能辦而已？」
entries.en: If the two Guang provinces collapsed again, the court would not know where to turn—let alone collect lijin."
entries.literal: If by any chance the two Guang provinces again dissolve in chaos, one would not know where to set hand or foot—how much less could lijin alone be managed?"

entries.zh: 因薦廣東道員唐啟廕、兩淮運使郭嵩燾、浙江運使成孫詒。
entries.en: He recommended Guangdong circuit intendant Tang Qiyin, Lianghuai grain commissioner Guo Songtao, and Zhejiang grain commissioner Cheng Sunyi.
entries.literal: He therefore recommended the Guangdong circuit intendant Tang Qiyin, the Lianghuai grain-transport commissioner Guo Songtao, and the Zhejiang grain-transport commissioner Cheng Sunyi.

entries.zh: 旋用嵩燾督廣東釐金，自拯疏發之也。
entries.en: Guo Songtao was soon appointed to supervise Guangdong lijin on the strength of Zheng's memorial.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Songtao was used to supervise Guangdong lijin—this began from Zheng's memorial.

entries.zh: 三年，遷太常寺卿，署左副都御史。
entries.en: In the third year (1864) he was promoted to president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as left vice censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to be president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as left vice censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 疏論：「總理各國事務大臣侍郎崇綸、恆祺、董恂、薛煥委瑣齷齪，通國皆知，竊恐外邦輕侮，以為中朝卿貳之班，大都不過如若曹等，未免為中朝恥辱。
entries.en: He wrote: "The ministers in charge of foreign affairs—Chonglun, Hengqi, Dong Xun, and Xue Huan—were petty and contemptible, as everyone knew. Foreign powers might conclude that China's senior officials were no better, to the dynasty's shame.
entries.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The vice presidents of ministries who are ministers in charge of affairs with all nations—Chonglun, Hengqi, Dong Xun, and Xue Huan—are truly petty and base; the whole country knows it. Your servant fears foreign states will despise us, thinking that among the court's senior ranks most are no better than men of their sort, which cannot but be a disgrace to the dynasty.

entries.zh: 就令人材難得，或於總理衙門位置為宜，上應量為裁抑，或處以散職，或畀以虛銜，庶外邦服我旌別之嚴。
entries.en: Even if talent were scarce and the Zongli Yamen needed staff, the emperor should curb such men—assign sinecures or empty titles—so foreign powers would respect China's standards of rank.
entries.literal: Even if talented men are hard to obtain and placement in the Zongli Yamen is suitable, Your Majesty ought to restrain them in measure, or assign them sinecure posts, or give them empty titles, so that foreign states may respect our strict distinctions of rank.

entries.zh: 四方聞之，亦釋然於朝廷宥納群倫、羈縻彼族之意。」
entries.en: The empire would then understand that the court meant to embrace all parties while keeping foreigners on a leash."
entries.literal: When the four quarters hear of it, they will also be reassured of the court's intent to embrace all classes and keep those peoples on leading strings."

entries.zh: 尋遷通政使，仍署左副都御史。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to commissioner of the Transmission Office while continuing to act as left vice censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to be commissioner of the Transmission Office, still acting as left vice censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 疏言：「近日蘇、杭迭克，直、東肅清。
entries.en: He memorialized: "Suzhou and Hangzhou had fallen in turn and Zhili and the east were pacified.
entries.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Recently Suzhou and Hangzhou have been taken in succession, and Zhili and the east have been pacified.

entries.zh: 臣觀從來將興之業，垂成之功，未有不矢以小心，而始能底定者。
entries.en: Enterprises nearing success, I observe, are never settled without utmost caution.
entries.literal: Your servant observes that enterprises about to rise and achievements on the verge of completion have never failed to pledge utmost caution before they could be brought to settlement.

entries.zh: 金陵賊窟雖計於三四月間可拔，而丹陽與常州犄角，百戰悍賊如李秀成等，麇集死守。
entries.en: Jinling might fall within three or four months, but Danyang and Changzhou supported each other, and veterans like Li Xiucheng massed there for a last stand.
entries.literal: Though the rebel nest at Jinling is calculated to be taken within three or four months, Danyang and Changzhou form a pincer; battle-hardened fierce rebels such as Li Xiucheng gather and defend to the death.

entries.zh: 杭、嘉既克，餘黨歸併湖州。
entries.en: With Hangzhou and Jiaxing taken, the remnants concentrated at Huzhou.
entries.literal: Hang and Jia having been taken, the remnant bands merged at Huzhou.

entries.zh: 其自皖南竄越江西之賊，蔓延玉山、鉛山、金谿、建昌二三百里，眾號八九萬，並有闌入福建境者。
entries.en: Rebels fleeing southern Anhui into Jiangxi spread across two or three hundred li around Yushan, Qianshan, Jinxi, and Jianchang—eighty or ninety thousand by report—with some crossing into Fujian.
entries.literal: Those who fled from southern Anhui across into Jiangxi spread over two or three hundred li around Yushan, Qianshan, Jinxi, and Jianchang, numbering by report eighty or ninety thousand, and some also intruded into Fujian territory.

entries.zh: 又聞李世賢自率巨股由淳安、遂安接踵而至，曾國籓、左宗棠等用兵日久，前此屢陳不亟求功旦夕，同一老謀深計，獨於皖、浙毗境豫作防維之策，則國籓意在徽、寧各飭所部分防，宗棠以為不若並力取廣德扼賊竄路。
entries.en: Li Shixian was said to be leading a large force through Chun'an and Suian. Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang had long urged patience, yet on the Anhui-Zhejiang border they disagreed: Zeng wanted separate garrisons at Huizhou and Ningguo, while Zuo preferred a combined strike on Guangde to block the rebels' escape.
entries.literal: It is also heard that Li Shixian personally led a great band from Chun'an and Suian in close succession. Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, and others have waged war for a long time; before this they repeatedly stated that one should not urgently seek merit overnight—alike in aged counsel and deep planning—yet on the Anhui-Zhejiang border alone they prepared defensive measures in advance: Guofan's intent was that Huizhou and Ningguo each order their parts to defend separately, while Zongtang thought it better to combine forces to take Guangde and choke the rebels' escape route.

entries.zh: 兩議未及定，賊已由皖竄贛。
entries.en: Before the two plans could be settled, the rebels had already broken from Anhui into Jiangxi.
entries.literal: The two plans had not yet been settled when the rebels had already fled from Anhui into Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 賊又草竊已久，人數太眾，勢多不能聚殲而弗使一賊他遁。
entries.en: Long accustomed to guerrilla war and too numerous to encircle, the rebels often could not be destroyed wholesale without letting some escape.
entries.literal: The rebels have long been bandits in the grass; their numbers are too great, and the tendency is often that they cannot be gathered and annihilated without letting a single rebel escape elsewhere.

entries.zh: 臣則以此賊人多勢劇，一意奔突，前股未痛剿，後股又踵接。
entries.en: Because they were numerous and aggressive, they drove forward relentlessly—before one column could be crushed, another followed.
entries.literal: Your servant holds that because these rebels are numerous and their momentum fierce, they rush forward with single intent: before the forward band is painfully suppressed, the rear band follows close on its heels.

entries.zh: 萬一深入江西腹地，燼餘复熾，又至燎原。
entries.en: If they penetrated deep into Jiangxi, dying embers could flare again into a prairie fire.
entries.literal: If by any chance they penetrate deep into the interior of Jiangxi, embers will again blaze up and once more reach the stage of setting the prairie ablaze.

entries.zh: 且由贛逾閩，可以直走汀、潮，為數年來竄匪熟路。
entries.en: From Jiangxi through Fujian they could reach Tingzhou and Chaozhou by a route rebels had used for years.
entries.literal: Moreover, from Jiangxi across Fujian they can go straight to Ting and Chao—for years the familiar route of fleeing bandits.

entries.zh: 黃文金由此而來，石達開由此而去，前事可為深警。
entries.en: Huang Wenjin had come this way; Shi Dakai had gone this way—a lesson the court should heed.
entries.literal: Huang Wenjin came by this route; Shi Dakai went by this route—the past may serve as a deep warning.

entries.zh: 疊蒙諭旨，曾國籓、左宗棠、李鴻章、沈葆楨及閩、粵各督撫諄諄戒備。
entries.en: Imperial orders had repeatedly warned Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Shen Baozhen, and the Fujian and Guangdong governors to stand ready.
entries.literal: Repeatedly receiving imperial instructions, Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Shen Baozhen, and the governors-general and governors of Fujian and Guangdong have been earnestly warned to prepare.

entries.zh: 當此大功將竟，惟當效力一心，互籌戰守，務將分竄諸賊，前截後追，必使所至創夷，日就衰殘零落，不得喙息，以成巨患。
entries.en: With final victory near, all commanders must act as one—blocking ahead and pursuing behind—so that fleeing bands are battered wherever they go, grow weaker daily, and cannot regroup into a new catastrophe.
entries.literal: At this time when great merit is about to be completed, all should serve with one heart, consult together on war and defense, and strive to take the scattered fleeing rebels with interception ahead and pursuit behind, so that wherever they go they are wounded and destroyed, daily growing feeble, broken, and scattered, unable to catch breath and breathe easy, lest they become a great calamity.

entries.zh: 臣尤有請者，皖、浙諸軍與賊相持不為不久，所需餉項，國籓、宗棠等各於江、楚等省自為籌畫。
entries.en: I would add that the Anhui and Zhejiang armies have fought a long war; Zeng and Zuo have each raised funds in the Yangtze and Chu provinces.
entries.literal: Your servant has a further request: the armies of Anhui and Zhejiang have contended with the rebels not a short time; the pay they require Guofan, Zongtang, and others each plan for themselves in provinces such as Jiang and Chu.

entries.zh: 國籓奏於江省設立總台，以一省捐釐之數，為皖軍十萬養命之源。
entries.en: Zeng had established a central lijin office in Jiangsu, dedicating that province's levies to feeding his hundred thousand Anhui troops.
entries.literal: Guofan memorialized establishing a general office in Jiang province, using that province's lijin and contribution levies as the source of sustenance for one hundred thousand Anhui troops.

entries.zh: 浙軍固不能分撥，即國籓所部月餉，傳聞亦祗放數成，不得已而籌及廣東釐捐，乃又不能遽辦。
entries.en: Zhejiang's army could spare nothing; even Zeng's monthly pay was said to be issued only in part. Guangdong lijin was sought in desperation but could not be collected quickly.
entries.literal: The Zhejiang army certainly cannot share in allocation; even the monthly pay of Guofan's own forces, it is reported, is issued only several tenths in full; compelled by necessity they turned to Guangdong lijin contributions, yet these too cannot be raised promptly.

entries.zh: 夫民之不能見遠而各為其私者，情也。
entries.en: It is human nature that people think locally and act for themselves.
entries.literal: That the people cannot see far and each acts for private interest is human feeling.

entries.zh: 廣東有之，江西豈獨不然？
entries.en: Guangdong feels this way; would Jiangxi be any different?
entries.literal: Guangdong has this; how could Jiangxi alone be otherwise?

entries.zh: 日前沈葆楨奏請將江西茶稅、牙釐等款歸本省任收，旋用部議允留其半，在國籓等斷不至觖望。
entries.en: Shen Baozhen had recently asked that Jiangxi keep its tea tax and broker lijin; the ministry allowed half to remain in the province—a concession Zeng would surely accept.
entries.literal: Recently Shen Baozhen memorialized requesting that Jiangxi tea tax, broker lijin, and other items be collected by the province itself; soon the ministry deliberation approved retaining half; Guofan and others would certainly not be discontent.

entries.zh: 惟軍前將卒，當枕戈喋血切望成功之時，忽聞軍餉來源將減，眾心或生疑懼，何以得飽騰而資鼓舞？
entries.en: But troops at the front, fighting in hope of victory, might lose heart if pay were cut—how could they fight on full stomachs and high spirits?
entries.literal: Only the officers and soldiers at the front, at a time when they rest on their weapons and shed blood in keen hope of success, if they suddenly hear that the source of military pay will be reduced, the hearts of the masses may breed doubt and fear—how can they be fed full and roused to enthusiasm?

entries.zh: 擬請飭贛、皖、楚、粵各疆臣，值此事機至緊，無論如何變通為難，總當殫竭血誠，同心共濟。
entries.en: I propose ordering the governors of Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan-Hubei, and Guangdong that, urgent as the moment is, they must strain every resource and cooperate wholeheartedly.
entries.literal: It is proposed to order the frontier officials of Jiangxi, Anhui, Chu, and Guangdong that, as this juncture is most urgent, however difficult adjustment may be, they should altogether exhaust their loyal sincerity and aid one another with one heart.

entries.zh: 甘肅回氛未戢，中州餘捻尚存，汝南陳大喜等竄逸湖北，自隨、棗逼襄、樊；
entries.en: Hui unrest in Gansu was not yet settled; Nian remnants lingered in the central provinces; Chen Daxi of Runan had fled into Hubei and threatened Xiangyang and Fancheng from Suizhou and Zaoyang;
entries.literal: The Hui unrest in Gansu is not yet quelled; remnant Nian still remain in the central provinces; Chen Daxi and others of Runan fled into Hubei, pressing Xiang and Fan from Suizhou and Zaoyang;

entries.zh: 張總愚自南台山中出竄內、淅，時虞合併；
entries.en: Zhang Zongyu had broken from the Nantai mountains into Henan and Zhejiang, with fear they might join forces;
entries.literal: Zhang Zongyu came out from the Nantai mountains to flee into Henan and Zhejiang, and at times there was fear they would merge;

entries.zh: 漢中之賊，全竄寧、陝、商州一路，聞將會齊襄、樊回援金陵，誠亦未可輕忽。
entries.en: while Hanzhong rebels had poured into Ningxia, Shaanxi, and Shangzhou and were said to be massing at Xiangyang and Fancheng to relieve Jinling—a threat not to be ignored.
entries.literal: the rebels from Hanzhong have all fled along the Ning, Shaan, and Shangzhou route; it is heard they will assemble at Xiang and Fan to return and relieve Jinling—this too truly must not be lightly neglected.

entries.zh: 目前陝省軍務，政出多門，李雲麟追賊商於，忽卷旆而西，其在興安，未能遏賊竄逸，其在漢陰，遇賊避匿，縱勇淫掠，宜量加裁抑。
entries.en: Shaanxi's war effort was fragmented. Li Yunlin had pursued rebels in Shangyu, then marched west; at Xing'an he failed to stop their escape; at Hanyin he avoided battle while his men looted. He should be reined in.
entries.literal: At present military affairs in Shaanxi have policy issuing from many gates; Li Yunlin pursued rebels in Shangyu, then suddenly furled his banners and went west; at Xing'an he failed to stop rebels from fleeing; at Hanyin he met rebels and hid away, letting his braves plunder at will—he should be restrained in measure.

entries.zh: 劉蓉素嘗學問，懷負非常，漢中之賊，本所專辦，而竄擾四出，尤當誓志盪除，方為不負。
entries.en: Liu Rong was a scholar of real ambition charged with Hanzhong, yet rebels ranged everywhere. He must vow to destroy them or fail his charge.
entries.literal: Liu Rong has long pursued learning and harbors extraordinary ambition; the Hanzhong rebels were originally his special charge, yet they flee and harass in all directions—he especially ought to vow in his heart to sweep them away, and only then will he not fail his trust.

entries.zh: 多隆阿聲望最優，眾口爭傳為第一名將，乃近日聲望漸損，宜申聖諭訓飭。
entries.en: Duo Long'a had enjoyed the highest reputation as China's foremost general, yet lately his standing had slipped; the court should issue a stern reminder.
entries.literal: Duo Long'a enjoys the finest reputation; all mouths contend in calling him the foremost general—yet recently his reputation has gradually declined; imperial instructions of admonition should be conveyed.

entries.zh: 雷正綰所向克捷，諒足當一面之寄，顧全甘官吏，未有一二正人支持其間。
entries.en: Lei Zhengwan won wherever he fought and could hold an independent command, but he lacked upright officials in Gansu to support him.
entries.literal: Lei Zhengwan wins wherever he turns and is surely fit to be entrusted with an independent front; yet among Gansu officials as a whole there are not one or two upright men to support him in the midst.

entries.zh: 現聞蘭州與慶陽隔絕，恩麟權督印，不過使令便闢之材，識見陋劣；
entries.en: Lanzhou and Qingyang were now cut off. Enlin held the governor's seal in proxy—a man fit only for errands, with poor judgment;
entries.literal: It is now heard that Lanzhou and Qingyang are cut off from each other; Enlin holds the governor's seal in proxy—no more than talent for dispatching orders and clever evasion, with shallow and inferior insight;

entries.zh: 熙麟坐守慶陽、寧夏一區，又為慶昀種種紕繆所誤。
entries.en: while Xilin held Qingyang and Ningxia but was misled by Qingyun's repeated blunders.
entries.literal: Xilin sits guarding the Qingyang and Ningxia region, and is again misled by Qingyun's various blunders.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為亟宜遴簡公正有為之大臣，鎮撫整飭。
entries.en: I urge the prompt appointment of a capable, upright minister to restore order.
entries.literal: Your servant in his folly holds that a just and capable high minister should urgently be selected to pacify and put in order.

entries.zh: 今之天下，何易遽言率土奠安，而南北軍務漸定，西事再能就緒，亦即為大致之澄清。
entries.en: Peace across the empire is not yet at hand, but as north and south quiet down, settling the west would bring a broad measure of order.
entries.literal: The realm today—how easily can one hastily say that all within the four seas is settled in peace? Yet as military affairs north and south gradually settle, if western affairs can again be brought to order, that will also be a broad clarification.

entries.zh: 朝廷者天下之本，宮府清明嚴肅，與疆場奮迅振拔之氣，相感而自通。
entries.en: The court is the root of the realm: clarity and discipline at the center resonate with vigor in the field.
entries.literal: The court is the root of the realm; when the palace administration is clear and stern, it resonates of itself with the vigorous, uplifting spirit of the battlefront.

entries.zh: 天下大勢日轉，而亦正多難鉅之事，或遽以為時局清明，事機暢遂，若已治已安者然。
entries.en: The tide is turning, yet grave difficulties remain. Some may prematurely declare the times settled and secure.
entries.literal: The great tendency of the realm turns daily, yet there are also many difficult and weighty matters; some may hastily think the times clear, affairs smooth, as if already governed and already at peace.

entries.zh: 人情大抵喜新狃常，畏難而務獲，獨有當幾至誠君子，為能深察而切戒之。
entries.en: People love novelty yet cling to habit, fear hardship yet chase gain—only the sincere statesman who grasps the moment can see this clearly and warn against it.
entries.literal: Human feeling mostly delights in the new and clings to the old, fears difficulty and strives for gain; only the sincere gentleman who meets the moment can deeply observe and earnestly warn against this.

entries.zh: 昔諸葛亮為三代下一人，史獨稱之以謹慎。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang was the greatest man since antiquity, yet history praised him above all for caution.
entries.literal: Formerly Zhuge Liang was the one man since the Three Dynasties; history alone praises him for caution.

entries.zh: 硃子進戒宋孝宗曰：​​'使宴安酖毒之害，日滋而日長；
entries.en: Zhu Xi warned Emperor Xiaozong of Song: 'If the poison of ease and comfort grows day by day,
entries.literal: Master Zhu admonished Emperor Xiaozong of Song, saying: 'If the harm of ease and poisoned comfort grows daily longer;

entries.zh: 將臥薪嘗膽之志，日遠而日忘。
entries.en: the resolve to sleep on brushwood and taste gall will fade and be forgotten.'
entries.literal: the resolve to sleep on brushwood and taste gall will daily recede and daily be forgotten.

entries.zh: '臣不勝私憂過計，冒昧瀝陳。」
entries.en: I cannot restrain my private anxiety and venture these views too freely."
entries.literal: Your servant cannot bear his private worry and excessive calculation, and ventures to pour forth his views."

entries.zh: 疏入，報聞。
entries.en: The memorial was received and acknowledged.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was reported.

entries.zh: 尋告歸，卒。
entries.en: He soon retired and died.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he requested leave to return home and died.

entries.zh: 穆緝香阿，字居南，滿洲鑲紅旗人。
entries.en: Mu Jixianga, style name Junan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
entries.literal: Mu Jixianga, whose style name was Junan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

entries.zh: 由工部主事再遷郎中。
entries.en: He rose from director in the Ministry of Works to bureau director.
entries.literal: From director in the Ministry of Works he was promoted again to bureau director.

entries.zh: 同治四年，授山東道監察御史。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tongzhi (1865) he was appointed Shandong circuit censor.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he was appointed censor on the Shandong circuit.

entries.zh: 疏請慎擇宦寺，略言：「皇上沖齡御極，聖學日新，知識日開，左右侍從之輩，宜豫加慎選，勿使將來蠱惑聖聰。
entries.en: He memorialized for careful selection of eunuchs, noting: "The emperor had come to the throne young, that his learning advanced daily, and that attendants at his side should be chosen with care lest they later mislead him.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting careful selection of eunuchs, stating in summary: "The emperor ascended the throne at a tender age; his sacred learning renews daily and his knowledge opens daily; those who attend at his left and right ought to be chosen with forethought, lest in the future they bewitch and delude the sacred hearing.

entries.zh: 溯自漢末及前明，朝政之失，半由宦寺。
entries.en: From the late Han through the Ming, half the court's failures had come from eunuchs.
entries.literal: Tracing back from the end of Han and the former Ming, half the failures of court governance arose from eunuchs.

entries.zh: 蓋宦寺出身之始，每以小忠小信，便捷逢迎，無非售其固寵邀恩之計。
entries.en: Eunuchs begin with petty loyalty and quick flattery, all to secure favor and advancement.
entries.literal: For at the beginning of a eunuch's career, with small loyalty and small trustworthiness, quick compliance and flattery, it is nothing but the scheme of selling his plan to secure favor and seek grace.

entries.zh: 及黨與已成，則驕肆專橫，而箝制其上，雖英明之主，竟有百計不能除之者。
entries.en: Once their factions formed, they grew arrogant and controlled their superiors; even enlightened rulers sometimes could not remove them.
entries.literal: Once their faction is formed, they are arrogant, unrestrained, and domineering, and clamp down on those above them; even an enlightened ruler may have a hundred plans yet cannot remove them.

entries.zh: 當時臣民，切齒痛恨，終歸無可如何。
entries.en: Officials and people gnashed their teeth in hatred yet could do nothing.
entries.literal: Officials and people of the time gnashed their teeth in hatred, yet in the end could do nothing.

entries.zh: 我朝列聖相承，遠邁前代，不但不准此輩干預政事，雖應對進退間亦不假以辭色，使無由讒諂面諛，浸潤膚受。
entries.en: Our dynasty's emperors, surpassing all predecessors, forbade eunuchs not only from politics but even from familiar speech in daily attendance, blocking slander and flattery at the source.
entries.literal: Our dynasty's successive sage emperors, far surpassing former ages, not only did not permit this sort to intervene in government affairs—even in answering and advancing or retreating they were not lent words or countenance, so that they had no means for slander, flattery to the face, or gradual soaking into the skin.

entries.zh: 是以二百餘年，從不為患。
entries.en: For more than two hundred years they had never been a scourge.
entries.literal: Therefore for more than two hundred years they have never been a calamity.

entries.zh: 雖然如此嚴防，尚有防不勝防之慮。
entries.en: Yet even such strict guard could not banish every fear.
entries.literal: Though guarded so strictly, there is still the worry that defense cannot overcome what must be defended against.

entries.zh: 嘉慶癸酉之變，猶有通賊者，是此輩反覆已有明徵也。
entries.en: Even in the Jiaqing palace attack of 1813 some eunuchs had aided rebels—proof of their treachery.
entries.literal: In the Jiaqing guiyou incident there were still those who communicated with bandits—clear proof that this sort is fickle and treacherous.

entries.zh: 今皇太后垂簾聽政，洞悉其弊，杜漸防微，有鑑於前，不使宵小蒙蔽。
entries.en: The empress dowager now ruled from behind the curtain, understood these abuses, and guarded against petty men who might mislead the court.
entries.literal: Now the empress dowager holds the curtain and hears government, penetrating their abuses, stopping gradual encroachment and guarding against the slight, taking warning from the past, not permitting petty men to blind and cover.

entries.zh: 所以知人善任，朝政肅清。
entries.en: She knew men and used them well; the court was orderly and clean.
