entries.literal: Therefore she knows men and employs them well, and court governance is pure and clear.

entries.zh: 即數年後皇上親政，亦斷不致寵任此輩，貽誤事機，何待臣下鰓鰓過慮？
entries.en: When the emperor takes power in a few years he will surely not favor them to the ruin of state affairs—why must officials fret so anxiously?
entries.literal: Even when in a few years the emperor personally governs, he will certainly not favor and employ this sort to the harm of affairs—why must officials below worry with anxious lips?

entries.zh: 然獻曝之忱，有不能已者。
entries.en: Yet my earnest concern could not be suppressed.
entries.literal: Yet the feeling of offering sun-drying cannot be stilled.

entries.zh: 當此之時，正聖學擴充之際，雖臣工皆能盡心輔佐，而宦寺尤宜加意斟酌。
entries.en: This is a time when the emperor's learning is expanding; though officials serve him well, eunuchs especially require careful choice.
entries.literal: At this time, when sacred learning is expanding, though civil officials can all devote their hearts to assistance, eunuchs especially ought to receive deliberate consideration.

entries.zh: 臣以為宦寺之設，無非效奔走、供指使而已，萬不可使年輕敏捷之人，常侍左右。
entries.en: Eunuchs exist only to run errands and take orders; young, quick-witted men must never attend the emperor constantly.
entries.literal: Your servant holds that eunuchs are established for nothing but running errands and obeying orders; young and quick men must never constantly attend at left and right.

entries.zh: 請皇太后選忠正老成者為我皇上朝夕侍從，庶將來親政，必不致受其欺矇蠱惑，而無疆之聖德，基於此矣！」
entries.en: I beg the empress dowager to choose loyal, upright, mature men to attend the emperor day and night, so that when he rules in person he will not be misled—and his boundless virtue will rest on this foundation!"
entries.literal: I beg the empress dowager to select men loyal, upright, and mature in years to attend our emperor morning and evening, so that when he later governs in person he will certainly not suffer their deception, blindness, and bewitchment, and his boundless sacred virtue will have its foundation in this!"

entries.zh: 五年，疏論大學士曾國籓督師討捻，日久無功，請量加譴責。
entries.en: In the fifth year (1866) he memorialized that Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan's Nian campaign had dragged on without success and asked that Zeng be censured.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized on Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan's command in suppressing the Nian, long without success, requesting measured increase of censure.

entries.zh: 上以國籓迭疏引咎，特命回任專辦餉糈，雖未蕆全功，非貽誤軍情者可比，斥所奏過當，置不議。
entries.en: The emperor noted that Zeng had repeatedly accepted blame and was ordered back to supply duty; though he had not finished the campaign, he had not ruined the war effort. The memorial was dismissed as excessive.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Guofan repeatedly memorialized accepting blame, specially ordered him back to his post to devote himself to rations and forage; though he had not completed the full merit, he was not comparable to one who ruins military affairs—the memorial was rejected as excessive and set aside without deliberation.

entries.zh: 出為山西蒲州知府，尋卒。
entries.en: He was sent out as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi and died soon after.
entries.literal: He went out to be prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi, and soon died.

entries.zh: 穆緝香阿通知國故，家藏邸報，自國初以來幾備。
entries.en: Mu Jixianga was deeply versed in state affairs; his family held court gazettes from the dynasty's founding in near-complete runs.
entries.literal: Mu Jixianga was well informed in national lore; his family collection of court gazettes from the founding of the dynasty onward was nearly complete.

entries.zh: 遊百川，字彙東，山東濱州人。
entries.en: You Baichuan, style name Huidong, came from Binzhou in Shandong.
entries.literal: You Baichuan, whose style name was Huidong, was a native of Binzhou in Shandong.

entries.zh: 同治元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Tongzhi (1862), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 六年，遷御史，巡西城。
entries.en: In the sixth year (1867) he was promoted to censor and patrolled the western city.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to censor and inspected the western city.

entries.zh: 宗室寬和等所行多不法，奏劾懲治，一時貴近斂跡。
entries.en: Imperial clansmen such as Kuanhe had acted lawlessly; he impeached them, and for a time the privileged elite held their tongues.
entries.literal: The imperial clansmen Kuanhe and others acted largely unlawfully; he memorialized impeaching and punishing them, and for a time the noble and near restrained their steps.

entries.zh: 七年，捻匪自山東竄直隸，百川奏請飭統兵大臣迅速剿辦，又請嚴禁各省栽種罌粟，上皆採納。
entries.en: In the seventh year (1868), when Nian rebels fled from Shandong into Zhili, Baichuan urged swift suppression and a ban on opium cultivation in every province. The emperor adopted both proposals.
entries.literal: In the seventh year Nian bandits fled from Shandong into Zhili; Baichuan memorialized requesting that the commander-in-chief be ordered to suppress them swiftly, and also requested strict prohibition of opium cultivation in every province—the emperor adopted all.

entries.zh: 疏論內外官署胥吏積弊，詔通飭嚴禁。
entries.en: He exposed long-standing abuses by clerks in government offices, and the throne ordered a strict ban empire-wide.
entries.literal: He memorialized on accumulated abuses of clerks in government offices within and without; an edict was issued ordering strict prohibition throughout.

entries.zh: 復言：「除吏弊在肅官方，尤在揚士氣。
entries.en: He added: "Eliminating clerk abuses required purifying official conduct and, above all, reviving the morale of the scholar-official class.
entries.literal: He again stated: "Eliminating clerk abuses lies in purifying official conduct, and especially in raising the spirit of the scholar-official class.

entries.zh: 請飭部院堂官於每司中擇賢俊數員，付以事權，專其責任。
entries.en: He asked ministry chiefs to select several able men in each bureau, give them real authority, and hold them accountable.
entries.literal: I beg that ministry and yamen chiefs in each bureau select several worthy and talented men, entrust them with authority over affairs, and fix their responsibility.

entries.zh: 察有胥吏舞弊，據實上陳，仍以勤惰定功過。
entries.en: If clerks were found corrupt, they should report the facts; merit should still be judged by diligence or sloth.
entries.literal: If clerks are found practicing fraud, report according to fact; still judge merit and fault by diligence or sloth.

entries.zh: 賞罰既明，人才自奮。
entries.en: With clear rewards and punishments, capable men would rise of themselves.
entries.literal: Once rewards and punishments are clear, talent will of itself be roused.

entries.zh: 至外省地方官，本有懲治胥吏之權，嚴飭各督撫為地擇人，毋以人試地。
entries.en: Provincial officials already had power to punish clerks; governors must be ordered to match men to posts, not trial men in unsuitable places.
entries.literal: As for local officials in the provinces, they originally have the power to punish clerks; strictly order each governor-general and governor to choose men for the place, and not test the place with the man.

entries.zh: 舉賢劾不肖，再簡廉正大員，以時巡察，遇有貪官蠹吏，列狀奏聞。」
entries.en: Recommend the worthy and impeach the unworthy; appoint upright inspectors to tour on schedule and memorialize on every corrupt official or predatory clerk they find."
entries.literal: Recommend the worthy and impeach the unworthy; again select upright and incorruptible officials to inspect on schedule; when corrupt officials and predatory clerks are encountered, list the facts in memorials to the throne."

entries.zh: 黃河北徙，山東郡邑屢被水。
entries.en: The Yellow River had shifted north, and Shandong prefectures and counties suffered repeated flooding.
entries.literal: The Yellow River shifted northward, and prefectures and counties in Shandong were repeatedly afflicted by flood.

entries.zh: 百川疏請賑恤，河督文彬、巡撫丁寶楨請仍挽复淮、徐故道，命廷臣集議。
entries.en: Baichuan memorialized for relief. River director Wenbin and Governor Ding Baozhen asked to restore the old Huai–Xu channel, and the court ordered a ministerial debate.
entries.literal: Baichuan memorialized requesting relief; the river director Wenbin and Governor Ding Baozhen requested that the old course at Huai and Xu still be dredged and restored, and the court ordered ministers to assemble for deliberation.

entries.zh: 百川疏言：「黃水宜南宜北，必將折衷一是。
entries.en: Baichuan wrote: "The Yellow River might flow south or north, but the court must settle on one coherent policy.
entries.literal: Baichuan memorialized, saying: "Yellow River water may suit going south or north; a single balanced decision must be reached.

entries.zh: 如議挽復故道，論工程，論經費，引黃濟運，有未可遽定者三端：如即以大清河為黃水經流，舊道斷不能容，河面必須加寬，民間田廬如何移徙，如何安置，則度地宜審也；
entries.en: If the old course were to be restored, then on the questions of engineering, expense, and drawing the Yellow River into the canal to aid transport, there were three matters that could not be settled hastily. If the Daqing River were immediately made the Yellow River's main channel, the old course could not hold it and the riverbed would have to be widened; how would people's fields and homes be moved and resettled? Land surveys would have to be exact;
entries.literal: If it is proposed to dredge and restore the old course, considering the works, considering the expenses, and drawing the Yellow River to aid the grain transport—there are three points that cannot hastily be settled: if the Daqing River is taken at once as the Yellow River's main channel, the old course certainly cannot contain it, the river surface must be widened—how are common people's fields and dwellings to be moved, how are they to be resettled? Then surveying the land ought to be examined carefully;

entries.zh: 且即河面加寬，仍恐萬難容納，別開支河，勢不容已，徒駭、馬頰、鉤盤、鬲津猶可指名，可否開行，有無貽害，則分水宜權也；
entries.en: even widened, the channel might not suffice, and branch streams such as Tuhai, Mabang, Goupan, and Gejin would likely be needed—each opening must be weighed for benefit and harm;
entries.literal: moreover, even if the river surface is widened, there is still fear it can hardly contain the flow; opening branch channels is a trend that cannot be stopped—Tuhai, Mabang, Goupan, and Gejin can still be named; whether they may be opened, whether there will be harm—then dividing the water ought to be weighed;

entries.zh: 黃水北行，其事為創，萬一不善料理，人情騷動，物議沸騰，則相機宜慎也。
entries.en: the Yellow River's northward diversion would be unprecedented; mishandling it could stir public unrest and fierce debate—timing must be handled with care.
entries.literal: the Yellow River flowing north is an unprecedented matter; if by any chance it is not well managed, popular feeling will be agitated and public discussion will boil—then seizing the moment ought to be cautious.

entries.zh: 請特派大臣履行上下游詳勘，然後定策。」
entries.en: He asked that a senior minister survey the entire river course before any final decision."
entries.literal: I beg that a specially dispatched high minister conduct detailed survey of the upper and lower reaches, and then fix the policy."

entries.zh: 十二年，上親政，命葺治圓明園，奉皇太后駐蹕。
entries.en: In the twelfth year (1873) the emperor assumed personal rule and ordered repairs to the Old Summer Palace for the empress dowager's residence.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor took personal rule and ordered repair of the Old Summer Palace for the empress dowager's residence.

entries.zh: 御史沈淮疏請暫緩修理，上特諭宣示孝養兩宮之意，專修安佑宮供奉列聖御容，暨皇太后駐蹕之所，治事之地，量從節儉，不事華靡，此外均不必興修。
entries.en: Censor Shen Huai asked to defer repairs. The emperor proclaimed his filial duty to both palaces: only the Palace of Imperial Peace would be restored for ancestral portraits and the empress dowager's residence and offices, with strict economy and no extravagance elsewhere.
entries.literal: Censor Shen Huai memorialized requesting temporary deferral of repairs; the emperor specially instructed, proclaiming the intent of filial nurture of the two palaces, to repair only the Palace of Imperial Peace to enshrine the portraits of successive sages, together with the places where the empress dowager resides and conducts affairs, keeping to economy in measure, not pursuing splendor—beyond this nothing need be built.

entries.zh: 百川繼疏申諫，上召入詰責，百川侃侃正言無所撓，上為動容，一時敢諫之名動朝野。
entries.en: Baichuan remonstrated again. Summoned and rebuked by the emperor, he spoke frankly without yielding. The emperor was moved, and his reputation for bold remonstrance spread through the court.
entries.literal: Baichuan followed with a memorial remonstrating again; the emperor summoned him in and rebuked him; Baichuan spoke frankly and correctly without yielding; the emperor was moved, and for a time the name of bold remonstrance shook court and realm.

entries.zh: 尋以憂歸，服除補官，遷給事中。
entries.en: He soon went home for mourning; after the mourning period he returned to office and was promoted to supervising secretary.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he returned home on mourning leave; when mourning ended he resumed office and was transferred to supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 光緒五年，出為湖南衡永郴桂道，遷四川按察使，擢順天府尹，遷倉場侍郎。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Guangxu (1879) he became Hunan's Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui intendant, then Sichuan provincial judge, then metropolitan prefect of Shuntian, then vice president of the Granary and Storage Board.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he went out to be intendant of the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit in Hunan, was transferred to be Sichuan provincial judge, was promoted to be metropolitan prefect of Shuntian, and was transferred to be vice president of the Granary and Storage Board.

entries.zh: 九年，山東河決，被災者數十州縣，命百川往會巡撫陳士傑治工賑。
entries.en: In the ninth year (1883) a Shandong river breach flooded dozens of counties. Baichuan was sent to join Governor Chen Shijie in relief and repair work.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Shandong river breached; several tens of prefectures and counties suffered disaster; Baichuan was ordered to go and join Governor Chen Shijie in managing works and relief.

entries.zh: 百川輕騎週曆河南北岸、上下游，先散急賑。
entries.en: Baichuan rode through Henan's north and south banks and the river's upper and lower reaches, distributing emergency relief first.
entries.literal: Baichuan on light horse toured the north and south banks of Henan and the upper and lower reaches, first distributing urgent relief.

entries.zh: 會奏請築兩岸遙堤，复於其內築縷堤，使黃水不致氾濫；
entries.en: They jointly proposed outer dikes on both banks and inner thread dikes within them to contain the Yellow River;
entries.literal: Jointly they memorialized requesting construction of distant dikes on both banks, and again building thread dikes within them, so that Yellow River water would not overflow;

entries.zh: 又奏請濬小清河，分黃水入海：如議行。
entries.en: and dredging the Xiaoqing River to divert Yellow River water to the sea. The court approved.
entries.literal: they also memorialized requesting dredging of the Xiaoqing River to divide Yellow River water into the sea: as proposed, it was carried out.

entries.zh: 還京，以倉廒被火，罷歸。
entries.en: Back in the capital, he was dismissed after the granaries burned.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, because the granaries caught fire he was dismissed and sent home.

entries.zh: 居數年，卒。
entries.en: He lived in retirement several years and died.
entries.literal: After residing several years, he died.

entries.zh: （附） 沈淮 淮，字東川，浙江鄞縣人。
entries.en: (Supplement) Shen Huai. Shen Huai, style name Dongchuan, came from Yin county in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: (Supplement) Shen Huai. Huai, whose style name was Dongchuan, was a native of Yin county in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 道光二十九年舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。
entries.en: He earned his juren degree in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang (1849), entered the Grand Secretariat as a secretary, and served on the Grand Council staff.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, serving also as a clerk on the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 咸豐十年，文宗狩熱河，淮不及從，慟哭欲投井，家人守之不得死。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), when the Xianfeng Emperor fled to Rehe, Huai could not accompany him and wept so bitterly he tried to throw himself into a well; his family stopped him.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng the Wenzong Emperor went on hunt to Rehe; Huai could not follow in time, wept bitterly and wished to throw himself into a well, but his family guarded him and he could not die.

entries.zh: 遷刑部主事，進員外郎，授陝西道監察御史。
entries.en: He rose through the Ministry of Justice to assistant department director and was appointed Shaanxi circuit censor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be a director in the Ministry of Justice, advanced to assistant department director, and appointed censor on the Shaanxi circuit.

entries.zh: 疏劾戶部主事楊鴻典攬權納賄，下刑部逮治，僅以小過議鐫級，及閻敬銘為尚書，始奏劾譴黜。
entries.en: He impeached Revenue director Yang Hongdian for grasping power and taking bribes. The case went to the Ministry of Justice, but Yang was only lightly demoted until Yan Jingming became minister and secured his dismissal.
entries.literal: He memorialized impeaching Yang Hongdian, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, for monopolizing power and taking bribes; the case was sent to the Ministry of Justice for arrest and trial, but only a minor fault was debated for demotion by inscription; when Yan Jingming became minister, he at last memorialized impeachment and dismissal.

entries.zh: 園工興，淮疏首上，當時與百川齊名。
entries.en: When palace repairs began, Huai filed the first remonstrance and was famed alongside Baichuan.
entries.literal: When work on the gardens began, Huai's memorial was the first submitted; at the time he was famed equally with Baichuan.

entries.zh: 光緒元年，充順天鄉試監試，力疾從事，出闈，旋卒。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangxu (1875) he supervised the Shuntian provincial examination despite illness and died soon after leaving the examination compound.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as supervisor of the Shuntian provincial examination, working despite illness; upon leaving the examination compound he soon died.

entries.zh: 家固中人產，官京師，斥賣殆盡，人尤服其清節。
entries.en: His family had been comfortably off, but he sold nearly everything he owned during his years in the capital. People admired his integrity all the more.
entries.literal: His family was originally of middling means; while serving in the capital he sold off nearly everything, and people especially admired his integrity.

entries.zh: =【論】論曰：用兵之際，事機千變，京朝官以傳聞有所論列，往往不能切中。
entries.en: Commentary: In wartime opportunities shift constantly; capital officials who argue from rumor often miss the mark.
entries.literal: =【Commentary】= The commentary says: In times of military employment, opportunities shift by the thousand; capital officials who discuss matters based on hearsay often cannot strike the mark.

entries.zh: 宗稷辰歸重得人，尹耕雲論諸將帥罪，王拯請調和疆吏，一意辦賊，為能見其大。
entries.en: Zong Jichen stressed finding the right men; Yin Gengyun judged generals' failures; Wang Zheng urged frontier officials to cooperate and focus on defeating rebels—they saw the larger picture.
entries.literal: Zong Jichen valued obtaining men; Yin Gengyun discussed the guilt of various generals; Wang Zheng requested harmonizing frontier officials and devoting single intent to handling bandits—they were able to see the larger picture.

entries.zh: 拯所言尤詳盡，蓋直樞廷，見軍報，較得諸傳聞者異矣。
entries.en: Zheng was the most thorough, for he sat on the Grand Council and read military reports rather than rumor.
entries.literal: What Zheng stated was especially thorough and complete, for he was directly in the Grand Council and saw military reports—quite different from those who rely on hearsay.

entries.zh: 穆緝香阿請慎選宦寺，遊百川等阻修圓明園，謇謇負直諫名，良不虛也。
entries.en: Mu Jixianga urged careful choice of eunuchs; You Baichuan and others blocked Old Summer Palace repairs. Their reputations for blunt remonstrance were well earned.
entries.literal: Mu Jixianga requested careful selection of eunuchs; You Baichuan and others blocked repair of the Old Summer Palace—steadfast in bearing the name of blunt remonstrance, truly not in vain.

entries.zh: 鴻藻性至孝，為學守程硃，務實踐，持躬儉約。
entries.en: Hongzao was deeply filial by nature; in scholarship he followed the Cheng-Zhu school and stressed practical conduct, living frugally himself.
entries.literal: Hongzao was by nature deeply filial; in learning he adhered to the Cheng-Zhu school and stressed practical conduct, living frugally in personal conduct.

entries.zh: 傅穆宗十餘年，盡心啟沃。
entries.en: He tutored Emperor Tongzhi for more than a decade and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the young emperor's education.
entries.literal: He tutored Emperor Muzong for more than ten years and devoted his whole heart to nurturing him.

entries.zh: 一日，穆宗學書，故為戲筆。
entries.en: One day, while the emperor was practicing calligraphy, he deliberately made playful strokes.
entries.literal: One day, while Emperor Muzong was practicing calligraphy, he deliberately made playful strokes.

entries.zh: 鴻藻立前捧上手曰：「皇上心不靜，請少息。」
entries.en: Hongzao stood before him, took the emperor's hands in his own, and said: "Your Majesty's mind is unsettled; please pause a moment."
entries.literal: Hongzao stood before him, took the emperor's hand in both of his, and said: "Your Majesty's mind is not calm; please rest a moment."

entries.zh: 穆宗改容謝之。
entries.en: The emperor changed his manner and apologized.
entries.literal: Emperor Muzong changed his expression and apologized.

entries.zh: 其在樞府，獨守正持大體。
entries.en: On the Grand Council he alone upheld principle and kept sight of the larger stakes.
entries.literal: In the Grand Council he alone upheld rectitude and held to the larger principles.

entries.zh: 御史王鵬運諫止修頤和園，幾獲重譴，鴻藻力解之，得免。
entries.en: Censor Wang Pengyun protested repairs to the Summer Palace and nearly incurred severe punishment; Hongzao interceded vigorously and saved him.
entries.literal: Censor Wang Pengyun remonstrated against repairing the Summer Palace and nearly incurred severe punishment; Hongzao vigorously interceded for him and he was spared.

entries.zh: 德宗間日一往頤和園侍起居，時留駐蹕。
entries.en: Emperor Guangxu went every other day to the Summer Palace to attend the Empress Dowager, and sometimes remained there for extended stays.
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong went every other day to the Summer Palace to attend to the Empress Dowager's daily needs, and sometimes stayed there in residence.

entries.zh: 言官有言其不便者，太后大怒，欲黜之，鴻藻謂如此必失天下臣民之望，乃止。
entries.en: When censors protested the arrangement, the Empress Dowager was furious and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao warned that this would lose the trust of officials and subjects alike, and she relented.
entries.literal: When remonstrating officials spoke of the inconvenience of this, the Empress Dowager was greatly angered and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao said that to do so would surely lose the hopes of all officials and people under Heaven, and she desisted.

entries.zh: 所薦引多端士。
entries.en: Those he recommended were mostly men of talent.
entries.literal: Those he recommended and advanced were mostly men of talent.

entries.zh: 朝列有清望者，率倚以為重，然亦不免被劫持雲。
entries.en: Officials at court with reputations for integrity generally looked to him for support, yet he could not escape being manipulated, it is said.
entries.literal: Officials at court with pure reputations generally relied on him as a weighty support, yet he could not avoid being manipulated, it is said.

entries.zh: 光緒元年，署刑部右侍郎。
entries.en: In 1875 he served as acting Right Vice Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as acting Right Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 明年四月，上典學毓慶宮，命授讀，再辭，不允。
entries.en: The following April the emperor began his studies at the Palace of Accumulated Joy; Tonghe was ordered to tutor him, declined twice, and was not allowed to refuse.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the next year the emperor began his studies at the Palace of Accumulated Joy; Tonghe was ordered to tutor him, declined twice, and was not permitted to refuse.

entries.zh: 旋遷戶部，充經筵講官，晉都察院左都御史。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, appointed lecturer at the imperial lectures, and advanced to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.

entries.zh: 遷刑部尚書，調工部。
entries.en: He was transferred to Minister of Justice, then to the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and then to the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 六年，廷臣爭俄約久不決，懿旨派惇親王、醇親王及同龢與潘祖廕每日在南書房看摺件電報，擬片進呈取進止，至俄約改定始止。
entries.en: In 1880 the court disputed the Russian treaty for months; an imperial decree assigned Princes Dun and Chun, together with Tonghe and Pan Zuyin, to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Library and draft recommendations for the throne, continuing until the treaty was revised.
entries.literal: In the sixth year court officials disputed the Russian treaty for a long time without resolution; an imperial decree assigned Princes Dun and Chun, together with Tonghe and Pan Zuyin, to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Library, draft briefs for presentation and await decisions, continuing until the Russian treaty was revised.

entries.zh: 八年，命充軍機大臣。
entries.en: In 1882 he was appointed to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed a Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 十年，法越事起，同龢主一面進兵，一面與議，庶有所備。
entries.en: In 1884 war broke out between France and Vietnam; Tonghe argued for advancing troops while negotiating, so the court would not be caught unprepared.
entries.literal: In the tenth year hostilities arose between France and Vietnam; Tonghe held that troops should advance on one hand while negotiations proceeded on the other, so that some preparedness might be maintained.

entries.zh: 又言劉永福不足恃，非增重兵出關不可。
entries.en: He also argued that Liu Yongfu could not be relied upon and that substantial reinforcements must be sent beyond the frontier passes.
entries.literal: He also said that Liu Yongfu could not be relied upon and that substantial reinforcements must be sent beyond the passes.

entries.zh: 旋與軍機王大臣同罷，仍直毓慶宮。
entries.en: He was soon dismissed along with the princely Grand Councilors but continued to serve at the Palace of Accumulated Joy.
entries.literal: Soon he was dismissed along with the princely Grand Councilors but continued to attend at the Palace of Accumulated Joy.

entries.zh: 前後充會試總裁、順天鄉試考官，兩蒙賜「壽」，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。
entries.en: He served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination, twice received the character "Longevity" as an imperial gift, was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
entries.literal: Before and after he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination, twice received the character "Longevity" as a gift, was given Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

entries.zh: 嘗請假修墓，傳旨海上風險，命馳驛回京，恩眷甚篤。
entries.en: Once he asked leave to repair his family's tombs; an edict cited the dangers at sea and ordered him back to the capital by courier post—a mark of exceptional favor.
entries.literal: Once he asked leave to repair his family's tombs; an edict noted the dangers at sea and ordered him to return to the capital by courier post; imperial favor was very deep.

entries.zh: 二十年，再授軍機大臣。
entries.en: In 1894 he was again appointed to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was again appointed a Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 懿旨命撤講，上請如故。
entries.en: An imperial decree ordered his tutoring duties withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue unchanged.
entries.literal: An imperial decree ordered his tutoring duties withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue as before.

entries.zh: 同龢善伺上意，得遇事進言。
entries.en: Tonghe was skilled at reading the emperor's mind and seized occasions to offer counsel.
entries.literal: Tonghe was skilled at discerning the emperor's intent and was able to offer counsel when occasions arose.

entries.zh: 上親政久，英爽非復常度，剖決精當。
entries.en: The emperor had long ruled in person; his keen intelligence and precise judgments were no longer those of an ordinary monarch.
entries.literal: The emperor had long ruled in person; his keen intelligence was no longer ordinary, and his judgments were precise and apt.

entries.zh: 每事必問同龢，眷倚尤重。
entries.en: On every matter he consulted Tonghe; his reliance on him was especially heavy.
entries.literal: On every matter he would consult Tonghe; reliance upon him was especially heavy.

entries.zh: 時日韓起釁，同龢與李鴻藻主戰，孫毓汶、徐用儀主和。
entries.en: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored fighting while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.
entries.literal: At that time hostilities arose between Japan and Korea; Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored war, while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.

entries.zh: 會海陸軍皆敗，懿旨命赴天津傳諭李鴻章詰責之，同龢並言太后意決不即和。
entries.en: When both navy and army were defeated, an imperial decree sent him to Tianjin to rebuke Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also reported that the Empress Dowager was firmly set against immediate peace.
entries.literal: When both the navy and army were defeated, an imperial decree ordered him to go to Tianjin and convey instructions rebuking Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also stated that the Empress Dowager's mind was firmly set against immediate peace.

entries.zh: 歸薦唐仁廉忠赤可用，請設巡防處籌辦團防。
entries.en: On his return he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and capable and asked that a patrol defense office be established to organize local militia.
entries.literal: On his return he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and usable and asked that a patrol defense office be established to organize local militia defense.

entries.zh: 於是命恭親王督辦軍務，同龢、鴻藻等會商辦理。
entries.en: Prince Gong was then ordered to supervise military affairs, with Tonghe, Hongzao, and others to consult and handle matters jointly.
entries.literal: Thereupon Prince Gong was ordered to supervise military affairs, with Tonghe, Hongzao, and others to consult and handle matters jointly.

entries.zh: 上嘗問諸臣：「時事至此，和戰皆無可恃！」
entries.en: The emperor once asked his ministers: "Affairs have come to this pass—neither peace nor war offers any hope!"
entries.literal: The emperor once asked his ministers: "Affairs have come to this pass—neither peace nor war can be relied upon!"

entries.zh: 言及宗社，聲淚並發。
entries.en: Speaking of the fate of the dynasty, his voice broke and tears flowed together.
entries.literal: Speaking of the altars of state, his voice and tears burst forth together.

entries.zh: 及和議起，同龢與鴻藻力爭改約稿，並陳：「寧增賠款，必不可割地。」
entries.en: When peace talks began, Tonghe and Hongzao fought vigorously to revise the draft treaty, arguing together: "Better to increase indemnities than to cede territory."
entries.literal: When peace negotiations began, Tonghe and Hongzao fought vigorously to revise the draft treaty, stating together: "Better to increase indemnities than to cede territory."

entries.zh: 上曰：「台灣去，則人心皆去。
entries.en: The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, the hearts of the people will go with it.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, the hearts of the people will all be lost.

entries.zh: 朕何以為天下主？」
entries.en: How can I remain sovereign over the realm?"
entries.literal: How can I remain sovereign over the realm?"

entries.zh: 毓汶以前敵屢敗對，上責以賞罰不嚴，故至於此。
entries.en: Yuwen cited repeated defeats in reply; the emperor blamed lax discipline in rewards and punishments for having brought matters to this pass.
entries.literal: Yuwen replied citing repeated defeats at the front; the emperor blamed lax rewards and punishments for having brought matters to this pass.

entries.zh: 諸臣皆引咎。
entries.en: All the ministers accepted blame.
entries.literal: All the ministers accepted blame.

entries.zh: 上以和約事徘徊不能決，天顏憔悴。
entries.en: The emperor wavered over the peace treaty, unable to decide; his face showed the strain.
entries.literal: The emperor wavered over the peace treaty and could not decide; his countenance was haggard.

entries.zh: 同龢以俄、英、德三國謀阻割地，請展期換約，以待轉圜。
entries.en: Tonghe argued that Russia, Britain, and Germany were working to block territorial cession and asked to postpone ratification in hope of a better outcome.
entries.literal: Tonghe held that Russia, Britain, and Germany were working to block the cession of territory and asked that exchange of the treaty be postponed to await a turn for the better.

entries.zh: 與毓汶等執爭，終不可挽，和約遂定。
entries.en: He argued fiercely with Yuwen and others, but could not turn the tide, and the peace treaty was settled.
entries.literal: He argued fiercely with Yuwen and others, but in the end could not turn the tide, and the peace treaty was settled.

entries.zh: 明年，兼總理各國事務大臣。
entries.en: The following year he was concurrently appointed minister for foreign affairs.
entries.literal: The next year he was concurrently appointed minister for foreign affairs with all nations.

entries.zh: 二十三年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。
entries.en: In 1897, as Minister of Revenue, he was made associate grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, as Minister of Revenue he served as associate grand secretary.

entries.zh: 二十四年，上初召用主事康有為，議行新政。
entries.en: In 1898 the emperor first summoned the chief clerk Kang Youwei and discussed implementing the new policies.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the emperor first summoned and employed the chief clerk Kang Youwei and discussed implementing the new policies.

entries.zh: 四月，硃諭：「協辦大學士翁同龢近來辦事多不允協，以致眾論不服，屢經有人參奏。
entries.en: In April an edict in vermilion ink stated: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe has of late handled affairs in ways that accord poorly with others, provoking widespread dissatisfaction and repeated impeachments.
entries.literal: In the fourth month an edict in vermilion ink stated: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe of late has handled affairs in ways that accord poorly with others, so that public opinion is dissatisfied and he has repeatedly been impeached.

entries.zh: 且每於召對時諮詢事件，任意可否，喜怒見於詞色，漸露攬權狂悖情狀，斷難勝樞機之任。
entries.en: At imperial audiences he arbitrarily assents or denies, his joy and anger plain in word and face, gradually revealing a disposition to usurp power in reckless defiance—clearly unfit for the Grand Council.
entries.literal: Moreover, at each imperial audience when events are consulted, he arbitrarily assents or denies, joy and anger showing in his words and expression, gradually revealing a disposition to usurp power in reckless defiance—he clearly cannot bear the duties of the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 本應查明究辦，予以重懲；
entries.en: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;
entries.literal: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;

entries.zh: 姑念其在毓慶宮行走有年，不忍遽加嚴譴。
entries.en: yet considering his many years of service at the Palace of Accumulated Joy, severe punishment is withheld for now.
entries.literal: yet considering that he has attended at the Palace of Accumulated Joy for many years, severe punishment is not immediately imposed.

entries.zh: 翁同龢著即開缺回籍，以示保全。」
entries.en: Weng Tonghe is forthwith to leave office and return home, as an act of leniency."
entries.literal: Weng Tonghe is forthwith to vacate his post and return to his native place, as a sign of preservation."

entries.zh: 八月，政變作，太后復訓政。
entries.en: In August a coup occurred and the Empress Dowager resumed regency.
entries.literal: In the eighth month a political coup occurred and the Empress Dowager resumed regency.

entries.zh: 十月，又奉硃諭：「翁同龢授讀以來，輔導無方，往往巧藉事端，刺探朕意。
entries.en: In October another vermilion edict read: "Since Weng Tonghe began tutoring, his guidance has been inept; he often craftily seized pretexts to probe my intentions.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he again received an edict in vermilion ink: "Since Weng Tonghe began tutoring, his guidance has been without method; he often craftily seized upon pretexts to probe my intentions.

entries.zh: 至甲午年中東之役，信口侈陳，任意慫恿。
entries.en: In the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 he spoke recklessly and urged me on at will.
entries.literal: As for the Sino-Japanese war in the jiawu year, he spoke recklessly and extravagantly and urged me on at will.

entries.zh: 辦理諸務，種種乖謬，以致不可收拾。
entries.en: In handling affairs he erred in every way until matters became beyond repair.
entries.literal: In handling various affairs he was wrong in every way, until matters became beyond repair.

entries.zh: 今春力陳變法，濫保非人，罪無可逭。
entries.en: This spring he strongly urged reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men—crimes that admit no excuse.
entries.literal: This spring he strongly urged reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men—his crimes admit no escape.

entries.zh: 事後追維，深堪痛恨！
entries.en: Looking back, this is deeply to be regretted!
entries.literal: Looking back afterward, this is deeply to be hated!

entries.zh: 前令其開缺回籍，實不足以蔽辜，翁同龢著革職，永不敘用，交地方官嚴加管束。」
entries.en: The earlier order to send him home in truth does not cover his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed from office, never to be employed again, and handed over to local officials for strict supervision."
entries.literal: The earlier order for him to vacate his post and return home in truth does not cover his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed from office, never to be employed again, and handed over to local officials for strict supervision."

entries.zh: 三十年，卒於家，年七十有五。
entries.en: In 1904 he died at home at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he died at home at the age of seventy-five.

entries.zh: 宣統元年，詔復原官。
entries.en: In 1909 an edict restored his former rank.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuantong an edict restored his former rank.

entries.zh: 後追諡文恭。
entries.en: He was later given the posthumous title Wengong.
entries.literal: Later he was posthumously given the title Wengong.

entries.zh: 沈桂芬，字經笙，順天宛平人，本籍江蘇吳江。
entries.en: Shen Guifen, courtesy name Jingsheng, was registered in Wanping, Shuntian, though his family hailed from Wujiang in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Shen Guifen, styled Jingsheng, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian; his ancestral home was Wujiang in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He earned his jinshi degree in 1847, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 咸豐二年，大考一等，擢庶子。
entries.en: In 1852 he placed in the top class in the palace examination and was promoted to junior tutor in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, in the triennial examination he ranked in the first class and was promoted to junior tutor.

entries.zh: 累遷內閣學士。
entries.en: He rose step by step to become an academician of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 先後典浙江、廣東鄉試，督陝甘學政，充會試副總裁。
entries.en: He later served as chief examiner for the provincial examinations in Zhejiang and Guangdong, as educational commissioner for Shaanxi and Gansu, and as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Zhejiang and Guangdong, supervised education in Shaanxi and Gansu, and served as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 八年，丁父憂。
entries.en: In 1858 he withdrew to observe mourning for his father.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 服闋，補原官。
entries.en: When his mourning ended, he returned to his former office.
entries.literal: When the mourning period ended, he resumed his former post.

entries.zh: 晉禮部左侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 同治二年，出署山西巡撫，明年，實授。
entries.en: In 1863 he was sent out as acting governor of Shanxi, and the following year received the substantive appointment.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he went out to serve as acting governor of Shanxi; the next year he received the substantive appointment.

entries.zh: 連上移屯、練兵諸疏，並稱旨。
entries.en: He submitted a series of memorials on frontier settlement and military training, each of which met with the emperor's approval.
entries.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on colonization and troop training, and all won imperial approval.

entries.zh: 桂芬以山西民食不敷，自洋藥弛禁，栽種罌粟，糧價踴增。
entries.en: Guifen argued that Shanxi could not feed its people: once the ban on imported opium was eased, farmers turned to poppy cultivation and grain prices shot up.
entries.literal: Guifen held that the people's food supply in Shanxi was insufficient; since the ban on foreign opium had been relaxed, poppies were cultivated and grain prices soared.

entries.zh: 於是刊發條約，飭屬嚴禁。
entries.en: He therefore published the treaty provisions and ordered his subordinates to enforce a strict ban.
entries.literal: Thereupon he published the treaty provisions and ordered his subordinates to enforce a strict prohibition.

entries.zh: 疏陳現辦情形，上韙之，頒行各省，著為令。
entries.en: In a memorial he described the measures he had taken; the court endorsed his approach, ordered it circulated to every province, and made it standing policy.
entries.literal: In a memorial he set forth how the matter was being handled; the throne approved and ordered it promulgated in every province as a standing regulation.

entries.zh: 旋丁母憂。
entries.en: He soon withdrew again to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 六年，起禮部右侍郎，充經筵講官，命為軍機大臣。
entries.en: In 1867 he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Rites, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Rites, appointed lecturer at the imperial lectures, and ordered to serve on the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 歷戶部、吏部，擢都察院左都御史，兼總理各國事務大臣。
entries.en: He served in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel, was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently became a minister for foreign affairs.
entries.literal: He passed through the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel, was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and concurrently served as minister in charge of foreign affairs with all nations.

entries.zh: 遷兵部尚書，加太子少保。
entries.en: He was transferred to Minister of War and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 光緒元年，以本官協辦大學士。
entries.en: In 1875, while retaining his ministerial rank, he was appointed associate grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, with his existing rank he was made associate grand secretary.

entries.zh: 京畿旱，編修何金壽援漢代天災策免三公為言，請責斥樞臣，諭交部議。
entries.en: When drought struck the capital region, compiler He Jinshou cited the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies after natural disasters and demanded that the Grand Councilors be held responsible; the throne ordered the ministries to deliberate.
entries.literal: When drought struck the capital region, compiler He Jinshou cited the Han practice of dismissing the Three Excellencies in response to heavenly calamities and asked that the Grand Councilors be held accountable; an edict ordered the matter referred to the ministries for deliberation.

entries.zh: 桂芬坐革職，特旨改為革職留任。
entries.en: Guifen was found liable for dismissal, but a special edict allowed him to remain in office despite the demotion.
entries.literal: Guifen was sentenced to dismissal from office, but a special edict changed this to dismissal while retaining his post.

entries.zh: 旋復原官，充翰林院掌院學士，晉太子太保。
entries.en: He was soon restored to his former rank, appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and promoted to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Soon he was restored to his former rank, appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and advanced to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 榮祿以廕生賞主事，隸工部，晉員外郎。
entries.en: Through hereditary privilege as a yinsheng, Rong Lu received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Works and was later promoted to vice director.
entries.literal: Rong Lu, through yinsheng privilege, was granted the post of secretary and attached to the Ministry of Works, then promoted to vice director.

entries.zh: 出為直隸候補道。
entries.en: He was then posted as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.

entries.zh: 同治初，設神機營，賞五品京堂，充翼長，兼專操大臣。
entries.en: Early in the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji Camp was founded, he was given fifth-rank capital status, appointed wing commander, and made concurrent drill commissioner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji Camp was established, he was granted the rank of fifth-rank capital official, served as wing commander, and concurrently held the post of drill commissioner.

entries.zh: 再遷左翼總兵。
entries.en: He was soon promoted again to commander of the Left Wing.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to be commander of the Left Wing.

entries.zh: 用大學士文祥薦，改工部侍郎，調戶部，兼總管內務府大臣。
entries.en: On Grand Secretary Wen Xiang's recommendation, he became vice minister of Works, was transferred to Revenue, and was also appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
entries.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Wen Xiang, he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Works, then moved to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently made superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 穆宗崩，德宗嗣統。
entries.en: After Emperor Muzong's death, Emperor Dezong ascended the throne.
entries.literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne.

entries.zh: 榮祿言於恭親王，乃請頒詔，俟嗣皇帝有子，承繼穆宗。
entries.en: Rong Lu urged Prince Gong to seek an edict providing that when the new emperor should have a son, that son would carry on Emperor Muzong's succession.
entries.literal: Rong Lu spoke to Prince Gong, and they then requested that an edict be issued stating that when the succeeding emperor had a son, that son would inherit Muzong's line.

entries.zh: 其後始定以紹統者為嗣，
entries.en: Only later was it finally decided that the heir by succession would be adopted into Muzong's line.
entries.literal: Only afterwards was it finally settled that the one who succeeded to the line would be adopted as heir.

entries.zh: 光緒元年，兼步軍統領。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangxu, he was also made concurrent Metropolitan Infantry Commander.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, he was also concurrently appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.

entries.zh: 遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。
entries.en: He was moved to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 慈禧皇太后嘗欲自選宮監，榮祿奏非祖制，忤旨。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Cixi once wanted to select palace eunuchs herself; Rong Lu submitted that this violated ancestral practice and thereby drew her displeasure.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Cixi once wished to choose palace eunuchs herself; Rong Lu memorialized that this was not ancestral institution and offended her will.

entries.zh: 會學士寶廷奏言滿大臣兼差多，乃解尚書及內務府差。
entries.en: When Academician Bao Ting reported that Manchu ministers were holding too many concurrent appointments, Rong Lu was stripped of his ministry posts and his Imperial Household superintendency.
entries.literal: When Academician Bao Ting memorialized that Manchu grandees held too many concurrent posts, Rong Lu was relieved of his ministries and his post in the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 又以被劾納賄，降二級，旋開復，出為西安將軍。
entries.en: After he was impeached for bribery, he was demoted two ranks, soon reinstated, and appointed general at Xi'an.
entries.literal: He was again impeached for taking bribes, demoted two ranks, soon restored, and sent out as general at Xi'an.

entries.zh: 二十年，祝嘏留京，再授步軍統領。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, he stayed in the capital for the birthday celebrations and was again appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, while remaining in the capital for birthday felicitations, he was again appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.

entries.zh: 日本構釁，恭親王、慶親王督辦軍務，榮祿參其事。
entries.en: When Japan provoked war, Princes Gong and Qing were put in charge of military affairs, and Rong Lu assisted them.
entries.literal: When Japan provoked hostilities, Princes Gong and Qing supervised military affairs, and Rong Lu took part in them.

entries.zh: 和議成，疏薦溫處道袁世凱練新軍，是曰「新建陸軍」。
entries.en: Once peace was made, he recommended in a memorial that Yuan Shikai, intendant of the Wenzhou circuit, train a new army—the force known as the "Newly Created Army."
entries.literal: After peace was concluded, he memorialized recommending Yuan Shikai, intendant of Wenzhou circuit, to train a new army, called the "Newly Created Army."

entries.zh: 授兵部尚書、協辦大學士。
entries.en: He was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary.
entries.literal: He was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary.

entries.zh: 疏請益練新軍，而調甘肅提督董福祥軍入衛京師。
entries.en: In a memorial he asked to expand the new army's training and to bring Gansu provincial commander Dong Fuxiang's troops to guard the capital.
entries.literal: He memorialized asking to expand training of the new army and to transfer the army of Gansu provincial commander Dong Fuxiang to guard the capital.

entries.zh: 德宗暨慈禧皇太后相繼崩，醇親王載灃監國攝政。
entries.en: Emperor Guangxu and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession, and Prince Chun Zai Feng became regent.
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zai Feng acted as regent for the realm.

entries.zh: 之洞以顧命重臣晉太子太保。
entries.en: As a deathbed entrusted minister, Zhidong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Zhidong, as a heavy minister entrusted at the deathbed, was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 逾年，親貴浸用事，通私謁。
entries.en: Within a year imperial princes increasingly wielded power and accepted private audiences.
entries.literal: After a year, imperial kinsmen gradually wielded power and received private audiences.

entries.zh: 議立海軍，之洞言海軍費絀可緩立，爭之不得。
entries.en: When a new navy was proposed, Zhidong argued that funds were insufficient and the project could wait, but he could not prevail.
entries.literal: When a navy was discussed, Zhidong said naval funds were insufficient and establishment could be delayed; he contended but could not prevail.

entries.zh: 移疾，遂卒，年七十三，朝野震悼。
entries.en: He reported illness and died at seventy-three; court and country mourned deeply.
entries.literal: He reported illness, then died, aged seventy-three; court and populace were shaken with grief.

entries.zh: 贈太保，諡文襄。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian and honored with the posthumous title Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 論曰：德宗親政，憤於外侮，思變法自強。
entries.en: The historians comment: When Emperor Guangxu took personal rule, angry at foreign encroachment, he sought reform and self-strengthening.
entries.literal: The commentary says: When Emperor Dezong personally took power, indignant at foreign insult, he thought to reform the laws and strengthen himself.

entries.zh: 乃以輔導無人，戊戌黨禍，庚子匪亂，遂相繼而作。
entries.en: But lacking able counselors, the disaster of 1898 and the Boxer uprising of 1900 followed in turn.
entries.literal: Yet because there was no one to guide him, the party disaster of the wuxu year and the bandit disorder of the gengzi year followed in succession.

entries.zh: 太后再出垂簾，初堅復舊，繼勉圖新。
entries.en: When the empress dowager resumed regency, she first insisted on restoring the old order, then pressed on toward reform.
entries.literal: The empress dowager again came forth behind the curtain; at first she firmly sought restoration of the old, then strove to pursue the new.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，議行憲政。
entries.en: Under the Xuantong reign, constitutional government was debated and undertaken.
entries.literal: When the Xuantong reign began, constitutional government was debated and enacted.

entries.zh: 政體既變，國本遂搖，而大勢不可問矣。
entries.en: Once the political system changed, the foundations of the state shook, and the larger course of events was beyond remedy.
entries.literal: Once the political system changed, the foundation of the state was shaken, and the great trend could no longer be questioned.

entries.zh: 榮祿屢參大變，文韶久達世務。
entries.en: Rong Lu took part repeatedly in great crises; Wenshao had long mastered affairs of state.
entries.literal: Rong Lu repeatedly took part in great upheavals; Wenshao long understood affairs of the age.

entries.zh: 鴻禨後起，參議立憲，終以失寵太后，不免放斥。
entries.en: Hongji rose later and helped debate constitutional government, but ultimately lost the empress dowager's favor and was cast out.
entries.literal: Hongji rose later, took part in deliberating constitutional government, but in the end lost favor with the empress dowager and could not escape dismissal.

entries.zh: 唯之洞一時稱賢，而監國攝政，親貴用事，欲挽救而未能，遂以憂死。
entries.en: Only Zhang Zhidong was for a time hailed as a worthy minister; yet under the regency, imperial princes held power, and though he tried to save the situation he could not, and died in distress.
entries.literal: Only Zhidong was for a time called worthy; yet under regency rule, imperial kinsmen wielded power; he wished to rescue affairs but could not, and thus died of grief.

entries.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，尚何言哉？
entries.en: When worthy men pass like clouds, the state is laid waste—what more is there to say?
entries.literal: When men depart like clouds, the state is wasted and afflicted—what more can be said?

entries.zh: 二十四年，晉大學士，命為直隸總督。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu he was promoted to Grand Secretary and appointed governor-general of Zhili.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary and ordered to be governor-general of Zhili.

entries.zh: 是時上擢用主事康有為及知府譚嗣同等參預新政，議變法，斥舊臣，召直隸按察使袁世凱入覲，超授侍郎，統練兵。
entries.en: The emperor was then promoting Kang Youwei, a secretary, and Tan Sitong, a prefect, among others to take part in the new policies; reform was debated, veteran ministers were pushed aside, and Yuan Shikai, Zhili surveillance commissioner, was summoned to court, given a leap promotion to vice minister, and placed in command of military training.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor promoted and employed the secretary Kang Youwei and the prefect Tan Sitong and others to participate in the new policies, discussed reform, dismissed old ministers, summoned Zhili provincial surveillance commissioner Yuan Shikai for audience, granted him extraordinary promotion to vice minister, and put him in charge of troop training.

entries.zh: 榮祿不自安，御史楊崇伊奏請太后再垂簾，於是太后复臨朝訓政，召榮祿為軍機大臣，以世凱代之，命查拿康有為，斬譚嗣同等六人於市，以上有疾，詔徵醫；
entries.en: Uneasy at these developments, Rong Lu watched as Censor Yang Chongyi asked the empress dowager to resume regency behind the curtain; the empress dowager then took up government again, recalled Rong Lu as a Grand Councilor, put Yuan Shikai in his former post, ordered Kang Youwei arrested, and had Tan Sitong and five others executed in public; because the emperor was said to be ill, physicians were summoned by edict;
entries.literal: Rong Lu felt ill at ease; censor Yang Chongyi memorialized asking the empress dowager to resume the curtain again; thereupon the empress dowager again held court behind the curtain to instruct in government, summoned Rong Lu as Grand Councilor, replaced him with Yuan Shikai, ordered Kang Youwei seized, executed Tan Sitong and five others in the market, and because the emperor was ill, an edict summoned physicians;

entries.zh: 復命榮祿管兵部，仍節制北洋海陸各軍。
entries.en: Rong Lu was again put in charge of the Ministry of War and retained overall command of Beiyang land and naval forces.
entries.literal: Rong Lu was again ordered to administer the Ministry of War and still to control all Beiyang land and sea forces.

entries.zh: 榮祿乃奏設武衛軍，以聶士成駐蘆臺為前軍，董福祥駐薊州為後軍，宋慶駐山海關為左軍，世凱駐小站為右軍，而自募萬人為中軍，駐南苑。
entries.en: Rong Lu then proposed the Wuwei Army: Nie Shicheng at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right Army, while he personally raised ten thousand men for the Central Army at the Southern Park.
entries.literal: Rong Lu then memorialized to establish the Wuwei Army: Nie Shicheng stationed at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right Army, while he himself recruited ten thousand men as the Central Army, stationed at the Southern Park.

entries.zh: 時太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥俊為穆宗嗣，患外人為梗，用榮祿言，改稱「大阿哥」。
entries.en: The empress dowager then considered deposing the emperor and naming Prince Duan's son Pujun as heir to Muzong's line; fearing foreign interference, she followed Rong Lu's counsel and styled the boy "Great Elder Brother" instead.
entries.literal: At that time the empress dowager discussed deposing the emperor and establishing Prince Duan's son Pujun as Muzong's heir; fearing foreign obstruction, on Rong Lu's advice the title was changed to "Great Elder Brother."

entries.zh: 榮祿，字仲華，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Rong Lu, whose courtesy name was Zhonghua, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Rong Lu, courtesy name Zhonghua, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 祖喀什噶爾幫辦大臣塔斯哈，父總兵長壽，均見忠義傳。
entries.en: His grandfather Tasgha, who had served as assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, both have entries in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
entries.literal: His grandfather Tasgha, assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, regional commander, are both recorded in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

entries.zh: 光緒改元，授大理寺卿，補禮部右侍郎。
entries.en: When Guangxu ascended the throne he was appointed President of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice President of the Ministry of Rites on the right.
entries.literal: When Guangxu began his reign he was appointed President of the Court of Judicial Review and made Vice President of the Ministry of Rites on the right.

entries.zh: 數遷工部尚書，加太子少保。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works and granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works and granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 五年，主事吳可讀以死請為穆宗立嗣，祖廕被命集議，與徐桐等請申不建儲，彝訓疏存毓慶宮。
entries.en: In the fifth year the clerk Wu Kedu offered his life in a petition to name an heir for Emperor Muzong; Zuyin was ordered to convene deliberation and, with Xu Tong and others, urged adherence to the rule against establishing an heir and preservation of the precedents of the Yuyu Palace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the clerk Wu Kedu petitioned with his death to establish an heir for Emperor Muzong; Zuyin was ordered to convene deliberation and with Xu Tong and others asked to uphold the rule against naming an heir, retaining the precedents of the Yuyu Palace.

entries.zh: 明年，偕惇親王奕脤等辦中俄交涉。
entries.en: The following year he joined Prince Dun Yizun and others in managing Sino-Russian negotiations.
entries.literal: The next year he joined Prince Dun Yizun and others in handling Sino-Russian affairs.

entries.zh: 約既成，籌善後，條列練兵、簡器、開礦、備餉四事進。
entries.en: After the treaty was concluded he planned for the aftermath and submitted a program of four items: training troops, selecting arms, opening mines, and stockpiling provisions.
entries.literal: After the treaty was concluded he planned for the aftermath, listing four items—training troops, selecting weapons, opening mines, and preparing provisions—and submitted them.

entries.zh: 命入直軍機，父憂歸。
entries.en: He was ordered into the Grand Council, then retired on his father's death.
entries.literal: He was ordered into the Grand Council; he returned home on his father's death.

entries.zh: 服闋，起權兵部尚書，調補工部，兼管順天府尹事。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was recalled to serve as acting Minister of War, transferred to the Ministry of Works, and concurrently managed affairs as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to act as Minister of War, transferred to fill the Ministry of Works, and concurrently managed affairs as Shuntian Metropolitan Magistrate.

entries.zh: 大婚禮成，晉太子太保。
entries.en: After the grand wedding ceremonies were completed he was promoted to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the grand wedding ceremonies were completed he was promoted to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 十六年，卒，贈太子太傅，諡文勤。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he died; he was posthumously made Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenqin (Diligent in Culture).
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he died; posthumously made Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Wenqin.

entries.zh: 寶坻士紳感其救災勤勞，籥建專祠，報可。
entries.en: The gentry of Baodi, grateful for his tireless work in disaster relief, petitioned to erect a private shrine in his honor; the request was approved.
entries.literal: Gentry of Baodi, grateful for his diligent labor in disaster relief, petitioned to build a private shrine; approval was granted.

entries.zh: 李文田，字芍農，廣東順德人。
entries.en: Li Wentian, courtesy name Shaonong, was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
entries.literal: Li Wentian, style name Shaonong, was a man of Shunde in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 咸豐九年一甲三名進士，授編修。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 9 he placed third among the top-tier jinshi graduates and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was third among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed Compiler.

entries.zh: 入直南書房，充日講起居注官。
entries.en: He joined the Southern Study and served as Lecturer and Diarist of Imperial Activity.
entries.literal: He entered the Southern Study and served as Lecturer and Diarist of Imperial Activity.

entries.zh: 同治五年，大考，晉中允。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 5, in the triennial palace examination, he was promoted to Middle Sub-expositor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, in the great examination, he was promoted to Middle Sub-expositor.

entries.zh: 九年，督江西學政。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was made Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: He was successively promoted to Reader-in-Waiting with academic rank.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting with academic rank.

entries.zh: 秩滿，其母年已七十有七矣，將乞終養，會聞朝廷議修園籞，遂入都覆命。
entries.en: When his term expired his mother was already seventy-seven; he was about to request leave to care for her in her final years, but on hearing that the court was debating repairs to the imperial park, he went to the capital to report his return.
entries.literal: When his term expired his mother was already seventy-seven; he was about to request leave to nurse her to the end, but hearing that the court was discussing repair of the imperial park, he entered the capital to report his return.

entries.zh: 既至，謁軍機大臣寶鋆，告以東南事可危，李光昭姦猥無行，責其不能匡救。
entries.en: On arrival he called on Grand Councillor Baojun and warned that affairs in the southeast were gravely imperiled and that Li Guangzhao was licentious and unprincipled, reproaching him for failing to set matters right.
entries.literal: On arrival he visited Grand Councillor Baojun and told him that southeastern affairs were gravely imperiled and that Li Guangzhao was lecherous and baseless in conduct, reproaching him for failing to correct this.

entries.zh: 寶鋆曰：「居南齋亦可言，奚必責樞府？」
entries.en: Baojun said, "One may speak from the Southern Study—why must you hold the Grand Council responsible?"
entries.literal: Baojun said: One may speak from the Southern Study—why must you blame the Grand Council?

entries.zh: 文田日：「正為是來耳！」
entries.en: Wentian replied, "That is precisely why I have come!"
entries.literal: Wentian said: That is precisely why I have come!

entries.zh: 疏上，不報。
entries.en: His memorial was submitted; there was no reply.
entries.literal: His memorial went up; no response.

entries.zh: 逾歲，上停止園工封事，略言：「巴夏禮等焚毀圓明園，其人尚存。
entries.en: A year later, in a memorial halting park construction, he wrote in brief: "Parkes and his fellows burned the Old Summer Palace, and they are still alive.
entries.literal: A year later, in a memorial stopping park construction, he wrote in brief: Parkes and others burned the Old Summer Palace, and they are still alive.

entries.zh: 昔既焚之而不懼，安能禁其後之不復為？
entries.en: Since they burned it once without fear, how can you prevent them from doing it again?
entries.literal: Since they once burned it without fear, how can you forbid their doing it again?

entries.zh: 常人之家偶被盜劫，猶必固其門牆，慎其管鑰，未聞有揮金誇富於盜前者。
entries.en: When an ordinary household is robbed, it still strengthens its doors and walls and guards its keys; one has never heard of flaunting gold and wealth before the robbers.
entries.literal: When an ordinary household is robbed, it still must strengthen doors and walls and guard keys carefully; one has not heard of flaunting wealth with gold before the robbers.

entries.zh: 今彗星見，天象譴告，而猶忍而出此，此必內府諸臣及左右憸人導皇上以朘削窮民之舉。
entries.en: Now a comet has appeared—a heavenly warning—and yet you still propose this; this must be inner-palace ministers and sycophants at the emperor's side leading His Majesty to policies that drain and impoverish the people.
entries.literal: Now a comet has appeared—a heavenly reproof—and yet you still bear to propose this; this must be inner-palace ministers and sycophants at the emperor's side leading His Majesty to policies that drain and impoverish the people.

entries.zh: 使朘削而果無他患，則唐至元、明將至今存，大清何以有天下乎？
entries.en: If draining the people truly brought no other calamity, then from Tang through Yuan and Ming the dynasties would still stand—how then did the Great Qing win the realm?
entries.literal: If draining the people truly brought no other calamity, then from Tang through Yuan and Ming down to the present they would still stand—how then did the Great Qing obtain the realm?

entries.zh: 皇上亦思圓明園之所以興乎？
entries.en: Does Your Majesty also consider why the Old Summer Palace was built in the first place?
entries.literal: Does Your Majesty also consider why the Old Summer Palace rose in the first place?

entries.zh: 其時高宗西北拓地數千里，東西諸國讋憚天威，府庫充盈，物力豐盛，園工取之內帑而民不知，故皆樂園之成。
entries.en: At that time the Qianlong Emperor extended the northwest frontier by thousands of li; states east and west feared Heaven's majesty; the treasuries were full and resources abundant; park works were paid from the inner purse without the people knowing, so all rejoiced in the park's completion.
entries.literal: At that time the High Emperor extended territory northwest by thousands of li; eastern and western states feared Heaven's majesty; the treasuries were full and resources abundant; park works were taken from the inner purse without the people knowing, so all rejoiced in the park's completion.

entries.zh: 今皆反是，聖明在上，此不待思而決者矣。」
entries.en: Today all is the reverse; with sagely clarity above, this needs no deliberation to decide."
entries.literal: Today all is the opposite; with sagely clarity above, this needs no thought to decide.

entries.zh: 疏入，上為動容。
entries.en: When the memorial was received, the emperor was deeply moved.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was moved.

entries.zh: 俄乞假歸。
entries.en: Soon afterward he requested leave to return home.
entries.literal: Soon he requested leave to return home.

entries.zh: 光緒八年，遭母憂。
entries.en: In Guangxu 8 he mourned his mother's death.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he suffered his mother's death.

entries.zh: 服竟，起故官，入直如故。
entries.en: When mourning ended he resumed his former post and returned to palace service as before.
entries.literal: When mourning was over he resumed his former post and entered service as before.

entries.zh: 數遷至禮部侍郎，充經筵講官，領閣事。
entries.en: He was successively promoted to Vice President of the Ministry of Rites, appointed a lecturer at the classics colloquium, and placed in charge of Secretariat affairs.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice President of the Ministry of Rites, appointed Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and headed Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 二十年，疏請起用恭親王奕訢及前布政使遊智開，依行。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he memorialized to recall Prince Gong Yixin and the former provincial administer You Zhikai; both requests were granted.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he memorialized to recall Prince Gong Yixin and the former Provincial Administrator You Zhikai; the requests were carried out.

entries.zh: 明年，卒，卹如製，諡文誠。
entries.en: The following year he died; condolence gifts followed regulations, and he was given the posthumous name Wencheng (Sincere in Culture).
entries.literal: The next year he died; condolence gifts followed regulations; posthumous name Wencheng.

entries.zh: 孫詒經，字子授，浙江錢塘人。
entries.en: Sun Yijing, courtesy name Zishou, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Sun Yijing, style name Zishou, was a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 咸豐十年進士，選庶吉士。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 10 he passed the jinshi examination and was selected a Hanlin Bachelor.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he became a jinshi and was selected a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 聞杭州城陷，乞假歸，奉親闢居定海。
entries.en: On hearing that Hangzhou had fallen he requested leave to return home, took his parents, and moved to Dinghai.
entries.literal: On hearing that Hangzhou had fallen he begged leave to return, took his parents, and relocated to Dinghai.

entries.zh: 參寧紹台道張景渠軍，平浙東有功，還授檢討。
entries.en: He joined the forces of Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingqu, helped pacify eastern Zhejiang, and on his return was appointed Reviser.
entries.literal: He joined the army of Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingqu, contributed to pacifying eastern Zhejiang, and on return was appointed Reviser.

entries.zh: 以倭仁薦，入直南書房。
entries.en: On Woren's recommendation he joined the Southern Study.
entries.literal: On Woren's recommendation he entered the Southern Study.

entries.zh: 同治四年，擢司業。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 4 he was promoted to Vice Director of Education.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Vice Director of Education.

entries.zh: 上言：「弭災在卹刑，治獄先平法。
entries.en: He submitted: "To quell disasters one must temper punishment; to govern prisons one must first make the law even.
entries.literal: He submitted: To quell disasters lies in lenient punishment; to govern prisons one must first even the law.

entries.zh: 本律盜案不分首從，聖祖、世宗加以區別。
entries.en: The basic code for robbery cases did not distinguish principals from accessories; the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors added such distinctions.
entries.literal: The basic code for robbery did not distinguish principal from accessory; the Sacred Ancestor and Shizong added distinctions.

entries.zh: 自頃盜風充斥，概用重典，行十餘年，案不減少。
entries.en: Recently banditry has spread everywhere; severe punishments have been applied across the board for more than ten years, yet cases have not decreased.
entries.literal: Recently robbery has filled the land; severe punishments have been applied universally for more than ten years, yet cases have not diminished.

entries.zh: 則知弭盜之術，不在用法之嚴。
entries.en: This shows that the way to quell banditry does not lie in harsh application of the law.
entries.literal: Thus one knows that the art of quelling robbery does not lie in severity of law.

entries.zh: 請敕刑部改成例，复祖制。」
entries.en: He asked the Ministry of Punishments to revise the precedents and restore the ancestral system."
entries.literal: He asked the Ministry of Punishments to revise precedents and restore the ancestral system.

entries.zh: 議行。
entries.en: The proposal was adopted after deliberation.
entries.literal: Deliberation carried it out.

entries.zh: 會上將侍太后幸惇親王府，既，與夏同善諫罷。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to accompany the Empress Dowager on a visit to Prince Dun's mansion, he and Xia Tongshan admonished him and the visit was canceled.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to accompany the Empress Dowager to Prince Dun's mansion, afterward he and Xia Tongshan admonished and stopped it.

entries.zh: 未幾，復將詣恭親王府祀神，詒經再上疏，言：「聖學方新，宸修宜懋。
entries.en: Before long the emperor was again to go to Prince Gong's mansion to offer sacrifices; Yijing memorialized again, saying: "Sacred learning has just been renewed; imperial self-cultivation should be redoubled.
entries.literal: Before long the emperor was again to go to Prince Gong's mansion to sacrifice to the gods; Yijing again memorialized, saying: Sacred learning is just renewed; imperial self-cultivation should be vigorous.

entries.zh: 經帷屢曠，則神誌難專；
entries.en: If the classics lectern is repeatedly left idle, concentration of mind becomes difficult;
entries.literal: If the classics lectern is repeatedly idle, then concentration of spirit is hard;

entries.zh: 法駕時勤，則見聞易惑。
entries.en: if the imperial carriage is frequently abroad, what is seen and heard easily misleads.
entries.literal: if the imperial carriage is frequently abroad, then what is seen and heard easily misleads.

entries.zh: 一日行幸，一日已荒念典之功；
entries.en: One day's excursion is one day's neglect of the work of recalling the canon;
entries.literal: One day's excursion is one day's neglect of the work of recalling the canon;

entries.zh: 今日行禮，異日或啟遊觀之漸。」
entries.en: today's ceremony may tomorrow open the gradual slide toward sightseeing and pleasure."
entries.literal: today's ceremony may tomorrow open the gradual slide toward sightseeing.

entries.zh: 士論歸之。
entries.en: Scholar-official opinion rallied to him.
entries.literal: Scholarly opinion applauded him.

entries.zh: 遭父憂去，服除，仍原官，入直如故。
entries.en: He left office on his father's death; when mourning ended he resumed his former post and returned to palace service as before.
entries.literal: He left on his father's death; when mourning ended he held the same post and entered service as before.

entries.zh: 十年，遷侍講。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was promoted to Lecturer.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Lecturer.

entries.zh: 五月朔，日食。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 詒經以天道感應，本諸人事，於是有遇災修省之請。
entries.en: Yijing held that heavenly signs respond to human affairs; therefore he submitted a request that the court meet calamity with self-examination.
entries.literal: Yijing held that heavenly responses correspond to human affairs; therefore he submitted a request to meet calamity with self-examination.

entries.zh: 十三年夏，彗星見，越數日，太白經天，人心惶駭。
entries.en: In the summer of the thirteenth year a comet appeared; days later Venus crossed the sky at midday, and the people were panic-stricken.
entries.literal: In the summer of the thirteenth year a comet appeared; days later Venus crossed the heavens at midday; hearts were panic-stricken.

entries.zh: 詒經復有廣開言路及罷圓明園工程之請。
entries.en: Yijing again memorialized to broaden channels for frank counsel and to halt work on the Old Summer Palace.
entries.literal: Yijing again requested broadly opening channels for memorializing and halting work on the Old Summer Palace.

entries.zh: 遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: He was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting with academic rank.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting with academic rank.

entries.zh: 德宗纘業，大考一等，擢詹事。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, in the triennial examination he ranked first class and was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, in the great examination he ranked first class and was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 召對，命直抒所見，連上澄吏治、慎海防機宜甚悉。
entries.en: Summoned for audience, he was ordered to speak his mind plainly; he successively submitted detailed memorials on clarifying official discipline and prudent maritime defense.
entries.literal: Summoned for audience, he was ordered to speak his mind plainly; he successively submitted detailed memorials on clarifying official discipline and careful maritime defense.

entries.zh: 光緒元年，命直毓慶宮授讀，固辭不獲，益屏家事勿問，退唯默坐觀書，思所以為獻納地。
entries.en: In Guangxu 1 he was ordered to serve in the Yuyu Palace as tutor; though he firmly declined he could not refuse; he increasingly set household affairs aside, and in private hours would only sit in silence reading books, thinking how he might find occasion to offer counsel.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve in the Yuyu Palace as tutor; though he firmly declined he could not refuse; he increasingly set household affairs aside, and in retirement would only sit in silence reading books, thinking how he might find a place to offer counsel.

entries.zh: 先後累言盜案刑例宜復舊制，分首從；
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized that robbery cases should restore the old statutes distinguishing principals from accessories;
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that robbery cases should restore the old statutes distinguishing principals from accessories;

entries.zh: 畿輔旱，請鑿井灌田甦之；
entries.en: when the capital region suffered drought, he asked to dig wells to irrigate fields and revive agriculture;
entries.literal: when the capital region suffered drought, he asked to dig wells to irrigate fields and revive them;

entries.zh: 晉、豫飢，請移海防關稅經費卹之。
entries.en: when Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he asked to shift coastal-defense customs funds for relief.
entries.literal: when Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he asked to shift coastal-defense customs funds for relief.

entries.zh: 四年，復命視學江蘇，陛辭日，力陳捐納有礙民生，無裨國用，稱旨。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was again ordered to inspect education in Jiangsu; on the day of his audience to take leave he forcefully argued that the sale of offices harmed the people's livelihood and did not benefit state revenue; the emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was again ordered to inspect education in Jiangsu; on the day of his audience to take leave he forcefully stated that purchase of office harmed the people's livelihood and did not benefit state revenue; this pleased the throne.

entries.zh: 明年，被命巡視山東黃河，條上治下游三事：曰濬海口，曰直河灣，曰通支河，請移機器局經費治之。
entries.en: The following year he was ordered to inspect the Yellow River in Shandong and listed three measures for the lower reaches: dredging the sea mouth, straightening the river bend, and opening branch channels; he asked to shift machine-bureau funds to carry them out.
entries.literal: The next year he was ordered to inspect the Yellow River in Shandong and listed three measures for governing the lower reaches: dredging the sea mouth, straightening the river bend, and opening branch channels; he asked to shift machine-bureau funds to carry this out.

entries.zh: 其秋，閱緣江砲台，又歷陳三不可恃，請合數省力助守江口，已築者毋廢，未築者毋增，上然其言。
