entries.en: That autumn, inspecting the Yangzi coastal batteries, he again argued that they could not be relied on and asked several provinces to combine efforts to help guard the river mouth; what was already built should not be abandoned, what was not yet built should not be added—the emperor approved his reasoning.
entries.literal: That autumn, inspecting the Yangzi coastal batteries, he again set forth three reasons they could not be relied on and asked several provinces to combine efforts to help guard the river mouth; what was already built should not be abandoned, what was not yet built should not be added—the emperor approved his words.

entries.zh: 嘗割俸濬江陰城河，植松五萬餘於君山，民德之。
entries.en: He once contributed from his salary to dredge the Jiangyin city moat and planted more than fifty thousand pines on Jun Hill; the people were grateful.
entries.literal: He once cut his salary to dredge the Jiangyin city moat and planted more than fifty thousand pines on Jun Hill; the people were grateful.

entries.zh: 六年，卒，德宗聞之遽泣，其忠誠荷主知如此。
entries.en: In the sixth year he died; when Emperor Dezong heard of it he wept at once—such was the regard his loyalty had won from his sovereign.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he died; when Emperor Dezong heard of it he wept at once—such was how his loyalty had won the sovereign's regard.

entries.zh: 遺疏入，賜卹如例，諡文敬。
entries.en: His final memorial was received; condolence gifts were granted as regulations provided, and he was given the posthumous name Wenjing (Reverent in Culture).
entries.literal: His final memorial entered; condolence gifts were granted as regulations provided; posthumous name Wenjing.

entries.zh: 子庚复，主事；
entries.en: His son Gengfu became a Clerk;
entries.literal: His son Gengfu became a Clerk;

entries.zh: 敦复，御史。
entries.en: Dunfu became a Censor.
entries.literal: Dunfu, a Censor.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，攝政監國，复舉輪講之典。
entries.en: When Xuantong began his reign the regent supervised the state and again instituted the rotating lecture rite.
entries.literal: When Xuantong began his reign the regent supervised the state and again instituted the rotating lecture rite.

entries.zh: 英麟撰資治通鑑講章以進，皆發明精義，比附近情，冀以誠意相感動，章上，但循故事留覽而已。
entries.en: Yinglin composed lecture chapters on the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government and submitted them, all elucidating refined meanings and drawing parallels close to human affairs, hoping to move others through sincerity; when the chapters were received, they were only retained for review according to routine.
entries.literal: Yinglin composed lecture chapters on the Zizhi Tongjian and submitted them, all elucidating refined meanings and drawing parallels close to human feeling, hoping to move others through sincerity; when the chapters went up, they were only retained for review according to routine.

entries.zh: 三年，武昌變起，內閣改制，飭都察院及凡有言責者皆停奏事，英麟嘆息以為奇變。
entries.en: In the third year the Wuchang uprising erupted; the Grand Secretariat was reorganized and the Censorate and all who bore duty to speak were ordered to cease submitting memorials; Yinglin sighed, taking this as an extraordinary transformation.
entries.literal: In the third year the Wuchang uprising erupted; the Grand Secretariat was reorganized and the Censorate and all who bore duty to speak were ordered to cease submitting memorials; Yinglin sighed, taking this as a strange transformation.

entries.zh: 遜位詔下，遂乞罷歸。
entries.en: When the abdication edict was issued he requested to resign and return home.
entries.literal: When the abdication edict was issued he begged to resign and return home.

entries.zh: 德宗永遠奉安，猶奔赴崇陵謁送。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong was permanently laid to rest, he still hurried to the Chong Mausoleum to pay his respects at the farewell.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong was permanently laid to rest, he still hurried to the Chong Mausoleum to pay respects at the farewell.

entries.zh: 重宴瓊林，加太子太保。
entries.en: At the repeat Qionglin banquet he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: At the repeat Qionglin banquet he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 乙丑冬，卒，年八十有八。
entries.en: In the winter of the yichou year he died, aged eighty-eight.
entries.literal: In the winter of the yichou year he died, aged eighty-eight.

entries.zh: 二十六年，拳亂作，奉命在籍治團練。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising erupted; he was ordered to organize militia training in his home district.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising erupted; he was ordered to organize militia training while remaining at his native place.

entries.zh: 服闋，赴行在。
entries.en: When mourning ended he went to the temporary court.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he went to the temporary court.

entries.zh: 時財匱，議加丁口稅。
entries.en: At the time the treasury was depleted and the court debated adding a poll tax.
entries.literal: At the time the treasury was depleted and there was discussion of adding a poll tax.

entries.zh: 仁黼謂：「今日國勢極危，而人心未去者，良由世祖除明季三餉；
entries.en: Renfu said, "Today the state's situation is extremely perilous, yet the people's hearts have not departed—this is truly because the Shunzhi Emperor abolished the Ming dynasty's three levies;
entries.literal: Renfu said: Today the state's situation is extremely perilous, yet the people's hearts have not departed—this is truly because the Founding Emperor abolished the Ming dynasty's three levies;

entries.zh: 聖祖詔丁口以五十年為率，嗣後滋生永不加賦：深仁厚澤，民不能忘。
entries.en: the Kangxi Emperor decreed that poll registers be fixed at the fiftieth year and that thereafter new births would never be taxed—such deep benevolence the people cannot forget.
entries.literal: the Sacred Ancestor decreed that poll registers be fixed at the fiftieth year, and that thereafter new births would never be taxed—such deep benevolence and thick grace the people cannot forget.

entries.zh: 今議加丁稅，違祖制，拂民情，必不可。」
entries.en: To add a poll tax now would violate ancestral institutions and go against popular feeling—it absolutely cannot be done."
entries.literal: Now to discuss adding poll tax violates ancestral institutions and goes against popular feeling—it absolutely cannot be done.

entries.zh: 事遂寢。
entries.en: The proposal was shelved.
entries.literal: The matter was ultimately shelved.

entries.zh: 還京，擢順天府府尹。
entries.en: On returning to the capital he was promoted to Metropolitan Magistrate of Shuntian.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, he was promoted to Metropolitan Magistrate of Shuntian.

entries.zh: 再遷兵部侍郎，典試江西，歷學部、法部。
entries.en: He was again transferred to Vice President of the Ministry of War, presided over the Jiangxi examination, and served in the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Vice President of the Ministry of War, presided over the Jiangxi examination, and served in the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 列傳二百二十八
entries.en: Biographies, No. 228
entries.literal: Biographies, Number Two Hundred Twenty-Eight

entries.zh: 初，德宗繼統嗣文宗，懿旨謂將來生有皇子，即繼穆宗為嗣。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangxu had first succeeded as heir to Emperor Xianfeng, an empress dowager's decree held that any son born to him in future would succeed Emperor Tongzhi as heir.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne as heir to Emperor Wenzong, an empress dowager's decree stated that when a son should be born in future, he would succeed Emperor Muzong as heir.

entries.zh: 內閣侍讀學士廣安請頒鐵券，被訶責。
entries.en: Guang'an, Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Grand Secretariat, had asked for an iron bond of assurance and was reprimanded.
entries.literal: Guang'an, Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Grand Secretariat, requested issuance of an iron certificate and was rebuked.

entries.zh: 至是，穆宗奉安惠陵，主事吳可讀堅請為其立後，以屍諫，下廷臣議。
entries.en: Now, when Emperor Tongzhi was interred at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedu insisted that an heir be named for him and remonstrated by suicide; the court ordered a ministerial debate.
entries.literal: At this point, when Muzong was laid to rest at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup firmly requested that an heir be established for him and remonstrated with his corpse; the court ordered the ministers to deliberate.

entries.zh: 寶廷謂：「恭繹懿旨之意，蓋言穆宗未有儲貳，即以皇上所生之子為嗣，非言生皇子即時承繼也，言嗣而統賅焉矣。
entries.en: Baoting wrote: "Reverently construed, the empress dowager's decree means that because Tongzhi left no heir, the son the present emperor bears shall be his successor—not that any newborn son must succeed at once, but that 'heir' here embraces the whole line of succession.
entries.literal: Baoting said: "Reverently interpreting the empress dowager's decree, it means that since Muzong had no heir apparent, the son born to the present emperor would be his heir—not that a son born would immediately succeed, but that in speaking of heir the succession line is included.

entries.zh: 引伸之，蓋言將來即以皇上傳統之皇子繼穆宗為嗣也。
entries.en: Taken further, it means that in future the son who inherits the present emperor's own line will succeed Tongzhi as heir.
entries.literal: Extended further, it means that in future the son who inherits the present emperor's line will succeed Muzong as heir.

entries.zh: 因皇上甫承大統，故渾涵其詞，留待親政日自下明詔，此皇太后不忍歧視之慈心，欲以孝弟仁讓之休歸之皇上也。
entries.en: Because the emperor had only just ascended the throne, the wording was deliberately broad, leaving a clear edict for the day he took personal rule—this was the empress dowager's compassion, unwilling to divide loyalties, wishing to leave the emperor the credit of filial devotion, brotherly duty, benevolence, and forbearance.
entries.literal: Because the emperor had only just assumed the great succession, the wording was deliberately broad, to await the day of personal rule when a clear edict would be issued—this is the empress dowager's compassionate heart unwilling to discriminate, wishing to bestow the honor of filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and yielding upon the emperor.

entries.zh: 廣安不能喻，故生爭於前；
entries.en: Guang'an failed to grasp this and argued in life;
entries.literal: Guang'an could not understand, and therefore contended while alive;

entries.zh: 吳可讀不能喻，故死爭於後。
entries.en: Wu Kedup failed to grasp it and contended in death.
entries.literal: Wu Kedup could not understand, and therefore contended in death afterward.

entries.zh: 竊痛可讀殉死之忠，而又惜其遺摺之言不盡意也。
entries.en: I deeply grieve Wu Kedu's loyal death, yet regret that his final memorial did not fully express his intent.
entries.literal: I deeply grieve Kedup's loyal death, yet regret that the words of his final memorial did not fully express his meaning.

entries.zh: 可讀未喻懿旨言外之意，而其遺摺未達之意，皇太后早鑑及之，故曰'前降旨時即是此意'也。
entries.en: Wu Kedup did not grasp what lay beyond the empress dowager's words, yet she had long seen what his memorial left unsaid—hence her declaration that the earlier edict had meant exactly this.
entries.literal: Kedup did not grasp the meaning beyond the empress dowager's decree, yet the meaning his final memorial failed to reach the empress dowager had long discerned, and therefore she said, 'When the earlier edict was issued, it was exactly this meaning.'

entries.zh: 而可讀猶以忠佞不齊為慮，誠過慮也。
entries.en: Yet Wu Kedup still feared that loyal and treacherous ministers would not act as one—a needless anxiety.
entries.literal: Yet Kedup still worried that loyal and treacherous ministers would not stand together—truly excessive worry.

entries.zh: 宋太宗背杜太后，明景帝廢太子見深，雖因佞臣妄進邪說，究由二君有自私之心。
entries.en: Song Taizong betrayed Empress Dowager Du's charge; Ming Jingdi deposed the heir Zhu Jianshen—though flatterers fed them false counsel, both rulers acted from selfish motives.
entries.literal: Song Taizong betrayed Empress Dowager Du; Ming Jingdi deposed the heir apparent Zhu Jianshen—though wicked ministers advanced perverse counsel, in the end both rulers harbored selfish hearts.

entries.zh: 乃者兩宮懿旨懸於上，孤臣遺疏存於下，傳之九州，載之國史，皇上天生聖人，必能以皇太后之心為心。
entries.en: Now the two palaces' decrees stand above and a lone minister's dying memorial below, to be proclaimed throughout the realm and written into the dynastic record; the emperor, a sage by nature, will surely make the empress dowager's intent his own.
entries.literal: Now the two palaces' decrees hang above and the lone subject's final memorial remains below, to be transmitted through the nine regions and recorded in the national history; the emperor, a sage by nature, will surely take the empress dowager's heart as his own heart.

entries.zh: 請將前後懿旨恭呈御覽，明降諭旨，宣示中外，俾天下後世咸知我皇太后至慈，皇上至孝至弟至仁至讓，且以見穆宗至聖至明，付託得人也。
entries.en: I beg that the earlier and later decrees be presented for the emperor's review, that a clear edict be issued and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all the world and posterity may know the empress dowager's boundless compassion, the emperor's supreme filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and forbearance—and may see that Tongzhi, most sage and discerning, entrusted his line to the right man.
entries.literal: I request that the earlier and later empress dowager decrees be respectfully presented for imperial review, that a clear edict be issued and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all under heaven and posterity may know our empress dowager's utmost compassion, the emperor's utmost filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and yielding, and may also see Muzong's utmost sagacity and clarity in entrusting the right man.

entries.zh: 如是，則綱紀正，名分定，天理順，人情安矣。
entries.en: Then moral order will be restored, titles fixed, heaven's way satisfied, and human hearts at ease.
entries.literal: If so, then moral order is correct, titles are fixed, heavenly principle is followed, and human sentiment is at peace.

entries.zh: 因赴內閣集議，意微不合，謹以上聞。」
entries.en: Finding my view at slight variance with the Grand Secretariat deliberation, I respectfully submit this for the throne's attention."
entries.literal: Because at the Grand Secretariat assembly my view differed slightly, I respectfully report the above."

entries.zh: 宗室寶廷，字竹坡，隸滿洲鑲藍旗，鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗八世孫。
entries.en: The imperial clansman Baoting, whose courtesy name was Zhupo, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was an eighth-generation descendant of Prince Xian of Zheng, Jirhalang.
entries.literal: Imperial clansman Baoting, courtesy name Zhupo, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was eighth-generation descendant of Prince Xian of Zheng, Jirhalang.

entries.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 7, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed editor.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed an editor.

entries.zh: 累遷侍讀。
entries.en: He rose in due course to Lecturer of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Lecturer.

entries.zh: 光緒改元，疏請選師保以崇聖德，嚴宦寺以杜干預，覈實內務府以節糜費，訓練神機營以備緩急，懿旨嘉納。
entries.en: At the beginning of Guangxu he memorialized for the appointment of tutors to cultivate the emperor's virtue, tighter control of eunuchs to prevent interference, audit of the Imperial Household Department to cut waste, and drill of the Shenji Camp for emergencies—all measures praised and accepted by the empress dowager.
entries.literal: At the change to Guangxu he memorialized requesting selection of tutors to exalt sagely virtue, strict control of eunuchs to block interference, verification of the Imperial Household Department to curtail waste, and training of the Shenji Camp for emergencies; the empress dowager's decree commended and accepted this.

entries.zh: 大考三等，降中允，尋授司業。
entries.en: Rated third class in the triennial examination, he was demoted to Junior Mentor and soon appointed Vice Director of Studies.
entries.literal: In the grand examination he received third grade, was demoted to Junior Mentor, and soon after was appointed Vice Director of Studies.

entries.zh: 是時朝廷方銳意求治，詔詢吏治民生用人行政，寶廷力抉其弊，諤諤數百言，至切直。
entries.en: The court was then intent on reform and solicited views on administration, livelihood, appointments, and policy; Baoting exposed abuses in a memorial of several hundred blunt, penetrating words.
entries.literal: At this time the court was keen to seek good governance and issued an edict inquiring into official conduct, people's livelihood, appointment of men, and administration; Baoting forcefully exposed its ills in several hundred forthright words, most incisive and direct.

entries.zh: 晉、豫飢，應詔陳言，請罪己，並責臣工。
entries.en: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he answered the imperial call for advice, urging the emperor to reproach himself and hold his ministers accountable.
entries.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he responded to the edict with memorials requesting self-reproach by the throne and rebuke of officials as well.

entries.zh: 條上救荒四事，曰：察釐稅，開糧捐，購洋米，增糶局。
entries.en: He proposed four relief measures: audit tax collection, open grain-donation drives, purchase foreign rice, and expand government grain-sale offices.
entries.literal: He itemized four measures for famine relief: investigate tax levies, open grain contributions, purchase foreign rice, and increase government grain-sale stations.

entries.zh: 復以災廣賑劇，請行分貸法。
entries.en: Because the disaster was widespread and relief burdens heavy, he also urged a system of graded loans to the afflicted.
entries.literal: Again, because the disaster was widespread and relief severe, he requested implementation of a graded-loan method.

entries.zh: 畿輔旱，日色赤，市言訛駴，建議內嚴防範，外示鎮定，以安人心。
entries.en: During drought around the capital, when the sun appeared red and rumors panicked the markets, he urged tight internal security and outward calm to steady public sentiment.
entries.literal: When the capital region suffered drought and the sun appeared red, rumors and panic spread in the markets; he proposed strict precautions within and a show of calm without to settle people's minds.

entries.zh: 歷遷侍講學士，以六事進，曰：明黜陟，專責任，詳考詢，嚴程限，去欺矇，慎赦宥，稱旨。
entries.en: Promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting, he submitted six reforms: clarify promotions and demotions, fix responsibility, conduct thorough inquiries, enforce deadlines, root out fraud, and use amnesties sparingly—proposals the throne approved.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and advanced six proposals: clarify promotion and demotion, fix responsibility, conduct detailed inquiry, enforce strict deadlines, remove deception, and be cautious with amnesties—winning imperial approval.

entries.zh: 五年，轉侍讀學士。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was made Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 七年，授內閣學士，出典福建鄉試。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was appointed Academician of the Grand Secretariat and sent to preside over Fujian's provincial examination.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Academician of the Grand Secretariat and went out to preside over the Fujian provincial examination.

entries.zh: 既蕆事，還朝，以在途納妾自劾罷，築室西山，往居之。
entries.en: After completing his duties he returned to the capital, resigned in self-accusation for taking a concubine en route, built a residence on the Western Hills, and retired there.
entries.literal: When the assignment was completed, he returned to court, impeached himself and was dismissed for taking a concubine on the journey, built a house on the Western Hills, and went to live there.

entries.zh: 是冬，皇太后萬壽祝嘏，賞三品秩。
entries.en: That winter, on the empress dowager's birthday celebrations, he was honored with third-rank standing.
entries.literal: That winter, for the empress dowager's longevity birthday felicitations, he was granted third-rank standing.

entries.zh: 十六年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the sixteenth year.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 又奏：「廷臣謂穆宗繼統之議，已賅於皇太后前降懿旨之中，將來神器所歸，皇上自能斟酌盡善，固也。
entries.en: He also wrote: "Ministers say the question of Tongzhi's succession is already covered by the empress dowager's earlier decree, and that when the throne passes in future the emperor can weigh every matter to perfection—so far, so good.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "The court ministers say the question of Muzong's succession is already included in the empress dowager's earlier decree, and that when the sacred vessel finds its place in future the emperor himself can weigh all matters to perfection—this is so.

entries.zh: 然懿旨意深詞簡，不及此引伸明晰，異日皇上生有皇子，將繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不即繼乎？
entries.en: Yet the decree's intent is deep and its wording brief; without this fuller explanation, when the emperor has a son, will that son succeed Tongzhi at once or not?
entries.literal: Yet the empress dowager's intent is deep and her words brief; without this extended clarification, when the emperor bears a son in future, will he succeed Muzong as heir, or not succeed immediately?

entries.zh: 不即繼似違懿旨，即繼又嫌跡近建儲。
entries.en: Not succeeding at once would seem to violate the decree; succeeding at once would look too much like naming a crown prince.
entries.literal: Not succeeding immediately seems to violate the decree; succeeding immediately seems close to designating an heir apparent.

entries.zh: 就令僅言繼嗣，不標繼統之名，而臣民亦隱以儲貳視之，是不建之建也。
entries.en: Even if one spoke only of heirship without naming succession to the line, officials and people would still treat the child as crown prince in all but name—establishing an heir without formally doing so.
entries.literal: Even if one spoke only of succeeding as heir without labeling succession to the line, officials and people would still tacitly regard him as heir apparent—this is establishing an heir without establishing one.

entries.zh: 而此皇子賢也，固宗社福；
entries.en: If that prince proves worthy, the realm is blessed;
entries.literal: If this prince is worthy, it is indeed the fortune of the altars of state;

entries.zh: 如其不賢，將來仍傳繼統乎，抑舍而別傳乎？
entries.en: if he proves unworthy, will the line still pass to him, or be set aside for another?
entries.literal: if he is not worthy, in future will the succession line still be transmitted to him, or set aside for another transmission?

entries.zh: 別傳之皇子，仍繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不繼乎？
entries.en: Would a prince from another line still succeed Tongzhi as heir, or not?
entries.literal: Would the prince of the other transmission still succeed Muzong as heir, or not?

entries.zh: 即使仍繼穆宗，是亦不廢立之廢立也，豈太平盛事乎？
entries.en: Even if he did succeed Tongzhi, that would amount to deposing and enthroning without calling it so—hardly an age of great peace, would it?
entries.literal: Even if he still succeeded Muzong, this would be deposition and installation without deposition and installation—how could it be an occasion of great peace?

entries.zh: 至此時即欲皇上斟酌盡善，不亦難乎？
entries.en: By then, could the emperor still weigh every matter to perfection?
entries.literal: By that time, even if the emperor wished to weigh all to perfection, would it not be difficult?

entries.zh: 廷議之意，或以皇上親政，皇子應尚未生，不難豫酌一盡善之規。
entries.en: Ministers may think that when the emperor takes personal rule no prince will yet have been born, making it easy to frame a perfect plan in advance.
entries.literal: The intent of the court debate may be that when the emperor takes personal rule the prince will not yet have been born, and it will not be hard to pre-weigh a perfect plan.

entries.zh: 然國君十五而生子，皇子誕育如在徹簾之前，又何以處之乎？
entries.en: Yet rulers commonly father sons at fifteen; if a prince is born before the regency ends, what then?
entries.literal: Yet rulers at fifteen bear sons; if a prince is born before the curtain of regency is drawn, how is one to handle it?

entries.zh: 與其留此兩難之局以待皇上，何如及今斟酌盡善乎？
entries.en: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, would it not be better to settle it now?
entries.literal: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, would it not be better to weigh all to perfection now?

entries.zh: 且懿旨非皇上可改，此時不引伸明晰，將來皇上雖斟酌盡善，何敢自為變通乎？
entries.en: Moreover, the empress dowager's decree is not the emperor's to alter; if it is not clarified now, how could he later dare change it even if he wished to?
entries.literal: Moreover, the empress dowager's decree is not something the emperor may alter; if it is not extended and clarified now, in future even if the emperor wished to weigh all to perfection, how would he dare change it on his own?

entries.zh: 此未妥者一也。
entries.en: This is the first flaw in the ministers' plan.
entries.literal: This is one point not yet settled.

entries.zh: 廷議又謂繼統與建儲，文義似殊，而事體則一，似也。
entries.en: Ministers also say that succession to the line and naming a crown prince differ in wording but not in substance—so it seems.
entries.literal: The court debate also says that succeeding to the line and establishing an heir apparent differ in wording yet are one in substance—this seems so.

entries.zh: 然列聖垂訓，原言嗣統之常，今則事屬創局，可讀意在存穆宗之統，與無故擅請建儲者有間，文義之殊，不待言矣。
entries.en: Yet the teaching of our sage forebears concerned the normal rule of heir and succession; today's case is unprecedented. Wu Kedup sought to preserve Tongzhi's line—quite unlike those who presumptuously demand a crown prince without cause. The difference in wording scarcely needs stating.
entries.literal: Yet the instructions left by successive sage emperors spoke of the regular rule of heir and succession; today's matter is an unprecedented situation. Kedup's intent was to preserve Muzong's line, distinct from those who without cause presumptuously request establishment of an heir—the difference in wording needs no elaboration.

entries.zh: 今廷議不分別詞意，漫謂我朝家法未能深知，則日前懿旨'即是此意'之謂何，臣民不更滋疑乎？
entries.en: If ministers refuse to distinguish the terms and casually claim ignorance of dynastic law, what becomes of the empress dowager's words 'exactly this meaning'? Will not officials and people only grow more suspicious?
entries.literal: Now the court debate does not distinguish the terms and casually says our dynasty's household law is not deeply understood—then what of the empress dowager's earlier words 'exactly this meaning'? Will not officials and people only grow more doubtful?

entries.zh: 此未妥者又一也。」
entries.en: This is the second flaw."
entries.literal: This is another point not yet settled."

entries.zh: 疏入，詔藏毓慶宮。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered it filed in the Yuqing Palace.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered it stored in the Yuqing Palace.

entries.zh: 其他，俄使來議約，朝鮮請通商，均有所獻納。
entries.en: On other matters too—Russian treaty negotiations, Korea's request for trade—he submitted thoughtful proposals.
entries.literal: On other matters, when the Russian envoy came to negotiate a treaty and Korea requested trade, he offered proposals on each.

entries.zh: 黃體芳，字漱蘭，浙江瑞安人。
entries.en: Huang Tifang, whose courtesy name was Shulan, came from Rui'an in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Huang Tifang, courtesy name Shulan, was a man of Rui'an in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tongzhi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as an editor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an editor.

entries.zh: 日探討掌故，慨然有經世志。
entries.en: He spent his days studying state institutions and came to harbor a strong desire to put his learning to practical service.
entries.literal: Each day he investigated institutional precedents and was stirred with the ambition to order the age.

entries.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，頻上書言時政得失。
entries.en: Rising eventually to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, he repeatedly memorialized the throne on the strengths and failings of contemporary governance.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and frequently submitted memorials on the gains and losses of current policy.

entries.zh: 晉、豫飢，請籌急賑，整吏治，清庶獄，稱旨。
entries.en: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he urged emergency relief, reform of local administration, and review of routine legal cases—measures that met with the emperor's approval.
entries.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he requested urgent relief funds, rectification of official conduct, and clearing of ordinary legal cases, and won imperial approval.

entries.zh: 時議禁燒鍋裕民食，戶部覈駁，體芳謂燒鍋領帖，部獲歲銀三萬，因上董恂奸邪狀，坐鐫級。
entries.en: When officials debated banning distilleries to free grain for the populace, the Board of Revenue blocked the move. Tifang pointed out that licensed distillers paid the ministry thirty thousand taels a year; he then denounced Dong Xun's corruption and was demoted as punishment.
entries.literal: At the time there was debate over banning distilleries to spare grain for the people; the Board of Revenue rejected the proposal. Tifang said distillers held licensed permits and the ministry received thirty thousand taels of silver yearly, and he therefore memorialized the wickedness of Dong Xun and was punished by demotion in rank.

entries.zh: 吳可讀，字柳堂，甘肅皋蘭人。
entries.en: Wu Kedu, styled Liutang, was from Gaolan in Gansu.
entries.literal: Wu Kedu, styled Liutang, was a native of Gaolan in Gansu.

entries.zh: 初以舉人官伏羌訓導。
entries.en: He first took office as educational instructor at Fuxiang on the strength of his provincial graduate degree.
entries.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate he served as educational instructor at Fuxiang.

entries.zh: 道光三十年，成進士，授刑部主事。
entries.en: In 1850 he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 晉員外郎，遭憂去，主講蘭山書院。
entries.en: Promoted to vice director, he left office to mourn a parent and took charge of lecturing at Lanshan Academy.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice director, then left office on bereavement and became head lecturer at Lanshan Academy.

entries.zh: 會撒拉番蠢動，被命佐團練。
entries.en: When the Salar tribes rose in unrest, he was ordered to help organize local militia training.
entries.literal: When the Salar tribes stirred in unrest, he was ordered to assist in organizing local militia.

entries.zh: 服闋，起故官。
entries.en: When his mourning period ended, he returned to his former post.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he resumed his former post.

entries.zh: 遷吏部郎中，轉御史。
entries.en: He was transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Personnel and then appointed censor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then made a censor.

entries.zh: 各國使臣請覲，議禮久未決，可讀請免拜跪，時論韙之。
entries.en: When foreign envoys sought an audience and court ritual remained unsettled for a long time, Kedu urged that they be excused from kneeling and prostration, and opinion at the time sided with him.
entries.literal: When foreign envoys requested an audience, court ritual was long undecided; Kedu memorialized to exempt them from kneeling and prostration, and public opinion approved.

entries.zh: 烏魯木齊提督成祿誣民為逆，擊殺多人，虛飾胜狀，為左宗棠所劾。
entries.en: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, falsely branded the people rebels, killed many of them, and fabricated accounts of victory until Zuo Zongtang impeached him.
entries.literal: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, falsely accused the people of rebellion, killed many, and fabricated reports of victory; he was impeached by Zuo Zongtang.

entries.zh: 可讀繼陳其罪有可斬者十，不可緩者五，尋逮問，讞上論斬，廷臣請改監候。
entries.en: Kedu went on to list ten offenses warranting execution and five that could not be delayed. Cheng was soon arrested and tried; when the verdict recommended death, court officials asked that the sentence be commuted to imprisonment awaiting execution.
entries.literal: Kedu followed with ten capital offenses and five that brooked no delay; Cheng was soon arrested and tried, the verdict called for execution, and court officials asked that it be changed to imprisonment awaiting execution.

entries.zh: 可讀憤甚，复疏爭：「請斬成祿以謝甘民，再斬臣以謝成祿。」
entries.en: Furious, Kedu memorialized again: "I beg that Cheng Lu be executed to appease the people of Gansu, and that I be executed afterward to appease Cheng Lu."
entries.literal: Kedu was deeply angered and memorialized again in protest: "I beg that Cheng Lu be executed to appease the people of Gansu, and that I be executed next to appease Cheng Lu."

entries.zh: 語過戇直，被訶責，鐫三級。
entries.en: His language was recklessly blunt; he was rebuked and demoted three ranks.
entries.literal: His words were excessively blunt; he was rebuked and demoted three ranks.

entries.zh: 歸，复掌教蘭山。
entries.en: He went home and again headed teaching at Lanshan.
entries.literal: He returned home and again took charge of teaching at Lanshan.

entries.zh: 逾年，穆宗崩，德宗纘業，起吏部主事。
entries.en: A year later, after Emperor Muzong died and Emperor Dezong took the throne, Kedu was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: After a year the Muzong Emperor died and the Dezong Emperor succeeded; Kedu was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 光緒五年，穆宗奉安惠陵，自請隨赴襄禮。
entries.en: In 1879, when Emperor Muzong was laid to rest at Huiling, he volunteered to accompany the procession and assist in the burial rites.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, when Muzong was interred at Huiling, he volunteered to go and assist in the rites.

entries.zh: 還次薊州，宿廢寺，自縊，未絕，仰藥死，於懷中得遺疏，則請為穆宗立嗣也。
entries.en: On the way back he halted at Jizhou and lodged in a ruined temple. He hanged himself; before life left him he took poison as well. A final memorial found on his person asked that an heir be appointed for Emperor Muzong.
entries.literal: On the return he stopped at Jizhou, lodged in an abandoned temple, hanged himself; before he died he took poison, and from his breast was found a final memorial asking that an heir be established for Muzong.

entries.zh: 其言曰：「罪臣聞治不諱亂，安不忘危。
entries.en: It read: "Your guilty servant has heard that good government does not shrink from speaking of disorder, and security must not forget danger.
entries.literal: It read: "This guilty official has heard that in governing one does not shrink from disorder, and in security one does not forget danger.

entries.zh: 危亂而可諱忘，則進苦口於堯舜，為無疾呻吟，陳隱患於聖明，為不祥舉動。
entries.en: If danger may be hushed up and forgotten, then offering bitter counsel even to Yao and Shun would be called feigned groaning without illness, and warning of hidden perils before a sage ruler would be deemed an ill-omened act.
entries.literal: If danger and disorder may be concealed and forgotten, then offering bitter counsel to Yao and Shun would be feigned groaning without illness, and setting forth hidden perils before the sage would be an ill-omened act.

entries.zh: 罪臣前因言事獲譴，蒙我先皇帝曲賜矜全，免臣以斬而死，以囚而死，以傳訊觸忌而死。
entries.en: I was once punished for speaking out, yet my late emperor graciously spared me—spared me execution, imprisonment unto death, and death for giving offense under interrogation.
entries.literal: This guilty official was once punished for remonstrance, yet my late emperor graciously spared me, sparing me death by execution, death in prison, and death for giving offense in interrogation.

entries.zh: 犯三死而未死，不求生而再生，則今日罪臣未盡之餘年，皆我先皇帝數年前所賜也。
entries.en: Having faced three deaths yet lived, and not seeking life merely to live on, whatever years remain to me now are years my late emperor granted me years ago.
entries.literal: Having incurred three deaths yet not dying, and not seeking life only to live again, the remaining years of this guilty official today are all years my late emperor granted years ago.

entries.zh: 欽奉兩宮皇太后懿旨，以醇親王之子承繼文宗顯皇帝為子，入承大統為嗣皇帝，俟嗣皇帝生有皇子，即承繼大行皇帝為嗣。
entries.en: By decree of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as heir to Emperor Wenzong, ascended the throne as successor emperor, and when he should have a son of his own, that son would succeed the late emperor in turn.
entries.literal: By the august command of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as son to the Xian Emperor Wenzong, entered the succession as heir emperor, and when the heir emperor should have a son, that son would succeed the late emperor as heir.

entries.zh: 我皇上仁孝性成，承我兩宮皇太后授以寶位，將來千秋萬歲時，必能以我兩宮皇太后今日之心為心。
entries.en: Our emperor is filial and benevolent by nature. Having received the throne from the two empress dowagers, in time to come he will surely hold the same intentions they hold today.
entries.literal: Our emperor is filial and benevolent by nature; receiving the throne from the two empress dowagers, in ages to come he will surely keep their hearts of today as his own.

entries.zh: 而在廷之忠佞不齊，即眾論之異同不一。
entries.en: Yet at court the loyal and the treacherous are not alike, and public opinion is divided.
entries.literal: Yet at court loyal and treacherous are not alike, and public opinion is not of one mind.

entries.zh: 以宋初宰相趙普之賢，而猶首背杜太后；
entries.en: For all the worth of Zhao Pu, chief minister in the early Song, he was still foremost in defying Empress Dowager Du;
entries.literal: For all the worth of the early Song minister Zhao Pu, he was still foremost in going against Empress Dowager Du;

entries.zh: 以明大學士王直之為舊臣，而猶以黃𤥠請立景帝太子一疏不出我輩為愧。
entries.en: For all that Wang Zhi of the Ming was a grand secretary and a veteran minister, he still felt ashamed that Huang Hong's memorial to establish the Jing Emperor's crown prince had not come from men like us.
entries.literal: For all that Wang Zhi of the Ming was a grand secretary and an old minister, he still took shame that Huang Hong's memorial to establish the Jing Emperor's crown prince did not come from our party.

entries.zh: 賢者如此，遑問不肖？
entries.en: If even the worthy behave thus, what may be expected of the unworthy?
entries.literal: If the worthy are thus, how much more the unworthy?

entries.zh: 舊人如此，奚責新進？
entries.en: If veterans act thus, how can newcomers be blamed?
entries.literal: If old hands are thus, how can new men be blamed?

entries.zh: 名位已定者如此，況在未定。
entries.en: If even those whose rank is already settled behave thus, how much more when it is not yet settled.
entries.literal: If those whose titles and positions are fixed are thus, how much more when they are not yet fixed.

entries.zh: 惟有仰求我兩宮皇太后再降諭旨，將來大統，仍歸大行皇帝嗣子，嗣皇帝雖百斯男，中外臣工均不得以異言進。
entries.en: I can only humbly beg the two empress dowagers to issue another decree: that hereafter the succession remain with a son of the late emperor, and that even if the reigning emperor should have a hundred sons, no official at court or in the provinces may advance a contrary opinion.
entries.literal: I can only humbly beg the two empress dowagers to issue another decree: that hereafter the succession return to a son of the late emperor, and that though the heir emperor have a hundred sons, officials within and without may not advance dissenting views.

entries.zh: 如此，則猶是本朝子以傳子之家法，而我大行皇帝未有子而有子，即我兩宮皇太后未有孫而有孫，異日繩繩揖揖相引於萬代者，皆我兩宮皇太后所自出而不可移易者也。
entries.en: Thus the dynasty's house law of father passing the throne to son would be preserved. The late emperor would have no son and yet have a son; the two empress dowagers would have no grandson and yet have a grandson. The line that would stretch in orderly succession through ten thousand generations would all spring from the two empress dowagers and could not be altered.
entries.literal: Thus it would still be this dynasty's house law of father passing the throne to son; the late emperor would have no son yet have a son, and the two empress dowagers would have no grandson yet have a grandson; the line stretching through ten thousand generations would all spring from the two empress dowagers and could not be altered.

entries.zh: 彼時罪臣即欲有言，繼思降調不得越職言事。
entries.en: At that time I wished to speak out, but then reflected that after demotion one might not remonstrate outside one's proper office.
entries.literal: At that time this guilty official wished to speak, but then reflected that after demotion one might not remonstrate outside one's office.

entries.zh: 今逢我大行皇帝奉安山陵，恐積久漸忘，則罪臣昔日所留以有待者，今則迫不及待矣。
entries.en: Now, as the late emperor is laid to rest in the hills, I fear that with time this matter will be forgotten. What I once held back and waited to say can wait no longer.
entries.literal: Now, as the late emperor is laid to rest in the hills, I fear that with time this will be forgotten; what this guilty official once reserved and waited for can no longer wait.

entries.zh: 謹以我先皇帝所賜餘年，為我先皇帝上乞數行懿旨，惟望我兩宮皇太后、我皇上憐其哀鳴，勿以為無疾呻吟、不祥舉動，則罪臣雖死無憾。
entries.en: I respectfully use the remaining years my late emperor granted me to beg on his behalf for a few lines of decree, praying only that the two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this cry of grief and not dismiss it as feigned groaning or an ill-omened act. Then I may die without regret.
entries.literal: I respectfully use the remaining years my late emperor granted to beg on his behalf for a few lines of august decree, only hoping the two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this lament and not deem it feigned groaning or an ill-omened act; then this guilty official may die without regret.

entries.zh: 尤原我兩宮皇太后、我皇上體聖祖、世宗之心，調劑寬猛，養忠厚和平之福，任用老成；
entries.en: I further pray that the two empress dowagers and our emperor take to heart the spirit of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessings of loyalty and peace, and employ seasoned men;
entries.literal: I further pray the two empress dowagers and our emperor take to heart the minds of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessing of loyalty and peace, and employ seasoned men;

entries.zh: 毋爭外國之所獨爭，為中華留不盡；
entries.en: do not contend for what foreign powers alone contend over, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;
entries.literal: do not contend for what foreign states alone contend for, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;

entries.zh: 毋創祖宗之所未創，為子孫留有餘。
entries.en: do not innovate what the ancestors never innovated, and leave a surplus for posterity.
entries.literal: do not create what the ancestors never created, and leave surplus for posterity.

entries.zh: 罪臣言畢於斯，命畢於斯，謹以大統所繫上聞。」
entries.en: My words end here and my life ends here. I respectfully report what concerns the succession to the throne."
entries.literal: This guilty official's words end here and his life ends here; I respectfully report what concerns the succession."

entries.zh: 吏部奏諸朝，詔憫其忠，予優恤。
entries.en: The Ministry of Personnel reported the matter to court. An edict commiserated his loyalty and granted generous posthumous honors.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Personnel reported to the court; an edict commiserated his loyalty and granted generous condolence.

entries.zh: 下群臣議，遂定以繼德宗之統為穆宗之子，無異論。
entries.en: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and without dissent it was settled that the succession to Emperor Dezong would be as son to Emperor Muzong.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and it was settled without dissent that the succession to Dezong would be as son to Muzong.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，醇親王載灃既攝政，其弟載洵、載濤分長軍諮、海軍，頗用事。
entries.en: When Xuantong began its reign, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable power.
entries.literal: When Xuantong began its reign, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable power.

entries.zh: 春霖謂：「古者鄭寵共叔，失教旋譏，漢驕厲王，不容終病，載在史冊，為萬世戒。
entries.en: Chunlin said: "In antiquity, when Zheng favored Gongshu, loss of instruction brought swift reproach; when Han favored the arrogant Prince Li, he was not allowed to end his illness—these are recorded in the histories as warnings for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: Chunlin said: "In antiquity, when Zheng favored Gongshu, loss of instruction brought swift reproach; when Han favored the arrogant Prince Li, he was not allowed to end his illness—these are recorded in the histories as warnings for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 二王性成英敏，休戚相關，料不至蹈覆轍，而慎終於始，要宜杜漸防微。」
entries.en: The two princes are by nature clever and keen; their weal and woe are bound together, and they are not expected to repeat past failures; yet to be careful at the end as at the beginning, one should check evil in its first stages and guard against minute beginnings."
entries.literal: The two princes are by nature clever and keen; their weal and woe are bound together, and they are not expected to repeat past failures; yet to be careful at the end as at the beginning, one should check the gradual and guard the minute."

entries.zh: 又謂：「景皇帝以神器付之皇上，衝齡踐阼，軍國重事，監國攝政王主之。
entries.en: He also said: "The Jing Emperor entrusted the sacred vessel to our emperor; the emperor ascended the throne in tender years, and weighty military and state affairs are presided over by the regent.
entries.literal: He also said: "The Jing Emperor entrusted the sacred vessel to our emperor; the emperor ascended the throne in tender years, and weighty military and state affairs are presided over by the regent.

entries.zh: 治同其樂，亂同其憂，國之不保，家於何寄？」
entries.en: In order they share its joy; in disorder they share its sorrow—if the state is not preserved, upon what may the family rely?"
entries.literal: In order they share its joy; in disorder they share its sorrow—if the state is not preserved, upon what may the family rely?"

entries.zh: 篇末又言：「監國歲未及週，物議沸騰，至於此極。
entries.en: At the end of the piece he again said: "The regency has not yet reached a year, yet public criticism boils to this extreme.
entries.literal: At the end of the piece he again said: "The regency has not yet reached a year, yet public criticism boils to this extreme.

entries.zh: 臣不禁為祖宗三百年國祚效賈生痛哭流涕長太息矣！」
entries.en: Your servant cannot help, for the three hundred years of our ancestors' fortune perform Jia Yi's weeping and long sighing!"
entries.literal: Your servant cannot but for the three hundred years of our ancestors' fortune perform Jia Yi's weeping and long sighing!"

entries.zh: 明年，又劾江西巡撫馮汝騤謾欺狀，效宋臣包拯七上彈章，末復言：「是非不明，請將前後章奏明詔宣示，敕部平議。」
entries.en: The next year he again impeached Feng Rukui, governor of Jiangxi, for deceit, following the Song official Bao Zheng in seven successive impeachments; at the end he again said: "Right and wrong are unclear; I beg that the earlier and later memorials be proclaimed by clear edict and the ministry ordered to judge fairly."
entries.literal: The next year he again impeached Feng Rukui, governor of Jiangxi, for deceit, following the Song official Bao Zheng in seven successive impeachments; at the end he again said: "Right and wrong are unclear; I beg that the earlier and later memorials be proclaimed by clear edict and the ministry ordered to judge fairly."

entries.zh: 語至戇直，被訶責。
entries.en: His words were excessively blunt and he was rebuked.
entries.literal: His words were excessively blunt and he was rebuked.

entries.zh: 复劾奕劻老奸竊位，多引匪人；
entries.en: He again impeached Yikuang as an old traitor usurping office who drew in many wicked men;
entries.literal: He again impeached Yikuang as an old traitor usurping office who drew in many wicked men;

entries.zh: 非特簡忠良，不足以贊大猷、挽危局。
entries.en: not only by selecting the loyal and worthy could the great design be aided and the perilous situation turned.
entries.literal: not only by selecting the loyal and worthy could the great design be aided and the perilous situation turned.

entries.zh: 詞連尚書徐世昌，侍郎楊士琦、沈雲沛，總督陳夔龍、張人駿，巡撫寶棻、恩壽等十數人。
entries.en: His words implicated Ministers Xu Shichang and Vice Ministers Yang Shiqi and Shen Yunpei, Governors Chen Kuilong and Zhang Renjun, and Governors Bao Fen and En Shou and more than ten others.
entries.literal: His words implicated Ministers Xu Shichang and Vice Ministers Yang Shiqi and Shen Yunpei, Governors Chen Kuilong and Zhang Renjun, and Governors Bao Fen and En Shou and more than ten others.

entries.zh: 朝旨再責之，令回原衙門行走。
entries.en: The court again rebuked him and ordered him to return to serve in his original yamen.
entries.literal: The court again rebuked him and ordered him to return to serve in his original yamen.

entries.zh: 春霖遂稱疾歸。
entries.en: Chunlin then pleaded illness and returned home.
entries.literal: Chunlin then pleaded illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 越八年，卒。
entries.en: After eight years he died.
entries.literal: After eight years he died.

entries.zh: 江春霖，字杏村，福建莆田人。
entries.en: Jiang Chunlin, styled Xingcun, was from Putian in Fujian.
entries.literal: Jiang Chunlin, styled Xingcun, was a native of Putian in Fujian.

entries.zh: 光緒二十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。
entries.en: In 1894 he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.

entries.zh: 二十九年，轉御史，首論都御史陸寶忠幹煙禁，不宜為台長，劾親貴及樞臣疆臣，章凡數十上。
entries.en: In 1903 he was made censor; he first argued that Censor-in-Chief Lu Baozhong, who handled the opium ban, was unfit to head the censorate, impeached imperial kin and grand councilors and frontier officials, and submitted several tens of memorials.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was made censor; he first argued that Censor-in-Chief Lu Baozhong, who handled the opium ban, was unfit to head the censorate, impeached imperial kin and grand councilors and frontier officials, and submitted several tens of memorials.

entries.zh: 德宗季葉，袁世凱出督畿輔，入贊樞廷，權勢傾一時。
entries.en: In the late years of Emperor Dezong, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region and entered the grand council; his power tilted the age.
entries.literal: In the late years of Dezong, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region and entered the grand council; his power tilted the age.

entries.zh: 春霖獨論列十二事，謂：「洪範有言：'臣之有作威作福，其害於爾家，兇於爾國。
entries.en: Chunlin alone set forth twelve matters, saying: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers make might and blessings, it harms your house and is baleful to your state.'
entries.literal: Chunlin alone set forth twelve matters, saying: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers make might and blessings, it harms your house and is baleful to your state.'

entries.zh: '左氏傳云：'受君之祿，是以聚黨，有黨而爭命，罪孰大焉？
entries.en: The Zuo Commentary says: 'Receiving the ruler's salary is thereby to gather a faction; having a faction and contending for command—what crime is greater?'
entries.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: 'Receiving the ruler's salary is thereby to gather a faction; having a faction and contending for command—what crime is greater?'

entries.zh: '今世凱所為，其心即使無他，其跡要難共諒。
entries.en: What Shikai does today, even if his heart has no other intent, his tracks are hard to share in trust.
entries.literal: What Shikai does today, even if his heart has no other intent, his tracks are hard to share in trust.

entries.zh: 歷考史冊所載權臣，大者貽憂君國，小者禍及身家。
entries.en: Examining the powerful ministers recorded in history, the great bring worry to ruler and state, the small bring disaster on themselves and their families.
entries.literal: Examining the powerful ministers recorded in history, the great bring worry to ruler and state, the small bring disaster on themselves and their families.

entries.zh: 窺竊神器之徒，姑置勿論，即功在社稷，如霍光、李德裕、張居正，亦以權寵太盛，傾覆相尋。
entries.en: Those who stole the sacred vessel may be set aside; even those who served the altars of state, such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng, because favor and power grew too great, downfall followed in turn.
entries.literal: Those who stole the sacred vessel may be set aside; even those who served the altars of state, such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng, because favor and power grew too great, downfall followed in turn.

entries.zh: 今不獨為國家計，宜加裁抑，即欲使世凱子孫長守富貴，亦不可無善處之法。」
entries.en: Now, not only for the sake of the state should restraint be added; even if one wishes Shikai's descendants to long keep wealth and honor, there must be a good way to handle it."
entries.literal: Now, not only for the sake of the state should restraint be added; even if one wishes Shikai's descendants to long keep wealth and honor, there must be a good way to handle it."

entries.zh: 嗣是糾彈世凱及慶親王奕劻父子，連上八疏，皆不報，然朝貴頗嚴憚之。
entries.en: Thereafter he impeached Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang father and son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all unanswered; yet the court nobles greatly feared him.
entries.literal: Thereafter he impeached Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang father and son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all unanswered; yet the court nobles greatly feared him.

entries.zh: 內侍李蓮英漸著聲勢。
entries.en: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually grew prominent in influence.
entries.literal: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually grew prominent in power.

entries.zh: 逾歲，醇親王奕枻閱海軍，蓮英從，一新憂之。
entries.en: A year later Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy with Lianying in attendance, and Yixin was deeply troubled.
entries.literal: After a year Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy and Lianying accompanied him; Yixin was troubled.

entries.zh: 而適值山東患河，燕、晉、蜀、閩患水，遂以遇災修省為言，略曰：「我朝家法，嚴馭宦寺。
entries.en: It happened that Shandong was afflicted by the Yellow River and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min by floods. He therefore spoke under the rubric of meeting disaster with self-examination, saying in part: "Our dynasty's house law strictly controls eunuchs.
entries.literal: It happened that Shandong suffered from the Yellow River, and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min from floods; he therefore spoke under the rubric of meeting disaster with self-examination, saying in part: "Our dynasty's house law strictly controls eunuchs.

entries.zh: 世祖宮中立鐵牌，更億萬年，昭為法守。
entries.en: The Shizu Emperor set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a declared law to be kept.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a declared law to be kept.

entries.zh: 聖母垂簾，安得海假採辦出京，立寘重典。
entries.en: When the Holy Mother held court from behind the curtain, how could An Dehai leave the capital on the pretext of procurement? He was at once punished under the severest statute.
entries.literal: When the Holy Mother held the curtain, how could An Dehai on the pretext of procurement leave the capital? He was at once punished by heavy statute.

entries.zh: 皇上登極，張得喜等情罪尤重，謫配為奴。
entries.en: When our emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, whose offenses were still graver, were banished and enslaved.
entries.literal: When our emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, their offenses still graver, were banished and enslaved.

entries.zh: 是以綱紀肅然，罔敢恣肆。
entries.en: Thus discipline was stern and none dared act wantonly.
entries.literal: Thus discipline was stern and none dared act wantonly.

entries.zh: 乃今夏巡閱海軍之役，太監李蓮英隨至天津，道路譁傳，士庶駴愕，意深宮或別有不得已苦衷，匪外廷所能喻。
entries.en: Yet this summer, during the naval inspection, the eunuch Li Lianying followed to Tianjin. Rumor spread along the roads and gentry and commoners were startled, thinking the inner palace might have some unavoidable hardship that the outer court could not comprehend.
entries.literal: Yet this summer, in the naval inspection, the eunuch Li Lianying followed to Tianjin; the roads buzzed with rumor and gentry and commoners were startled, thinking the inner palace might have some unavoidable hardship that the outer court could not comprehend.

entries.zh: 然宗籓至戚，閱軍大典，而令刑餘之輩《廣則》乎其間，其將何以詰戎兵崇體制？
entries.en: Yet for a prince of the imperial clan, a kinsman of the first rank, at a great ceremony of inspecting the army, to let eunuchs take part in it—how may troops be disciplined and institutional dignity upheld?
entries.literal: Yet for a prince of the imperial clan, a kinsman of the first rank, at a great ceremony of inspecting the army, to let mutilated men take part in it—how may troops be disciplined and the system honored?

entries.zh: 況作法於涼，其弊猶貪。
entries.en: Moreover, as the proverb says, if one sets the pattern in a cool season, the resulting abuse will still be greed.
entries.literal: Moreover, if one sets the pattern in a cool season, the resulting abuse will still be greed.

entries.zh: 唐之監軍，豈其本意，積漸者然也。
entries.en: The Tang practice of eunuch army supervisors—was that its original intent? It came about through gradual accretion.
entries.literal: The Tang practice of supervising armies—was that its original intent? It came about through gradual accretion.

entries.zh: 聖朝法制修明，萬無慮此。
entries.en: Our sage dynasty's laws are well ordered; there is no need at all to fear this.
entries.literal: Our sage dynasty's laws are well ordered; there is no need at all to fear this.

entries.zh: 而涓涓弗塞，流弊難言，杜漸防微，亦宜垂意。
entries.en: Yet if the trickle is not stopped, the abuse that follows is hard to describe. To check evil in its first stages and guard against minute beginnings is also fit to receive attention.
entries.literal: Yet if the trickle is not stopped, the flowing abuse is hard to describe; to check the gradual and guard the minute is also fit to receive attention.

entries.zh: 從古閹宦，巧於逢迎而昧於大義，引援黨類，播弄語言，使宮闈之內，疑貳漸生，而彼得售其小忠小信之為，以陰竊夫作福作威之柄。
entries.en: From antiquity eunuchs have been skilled at flattery and blind to great principle. They draw in factions and manipulate words until doubts gradually arise within the palace, and they may sell their petty loyalty and petty trust to steal in secret the power to bestow favors and wield authority.
entries.literal: From antiquity eunuchs have been skilled at flattery and blind to great principle; they draw in factions, manipulate words, so that within the palace doubts gradually arise, and they may sell their petty loyalty and petty trust to steal in secret the power to bestow blessings and wield authority.

entries.zh: 我皇太后、皇上明目達聰，豈有跬步之地而或敢售其欺？
entries.en: Our empress dowager and emperor are clear-sighted and keen of hearing—would there be even a step's breadth where one dared practice deception?
entries.literal: Our empress dowager and emperor are clear-sighted and keen of hearing—would there be even a step's breadth where one dared sell deception?

entries.zh: 顧事每忽於細微，情易溺於近習，侍御僕從，罔非正人，辨之宜早辨也。」
entries.en: Yet affairs are often neglected in small matters, and feeling easily drowns in familiar attendants. Those who serve at one's side should all be upright men—the distinction ought to be made early."
entries.literal: Yet affairs are often neglected in minute matters, and feeling easily drowns in familiar attendants; none who serve and attend are not upright men—one should distinguish early."

entries.zh: 疏上，太后怒，詰責疏言「苦衷」何指？
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the empress dowager was angry and demanded what the memorial meant by "unavoidable hardship."
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the empress dowager was angry and demanded what the memorial meant by "unavoidable hardship."

entries.zh: 一新曰：「臣所謂'不得已苦衷'者，意以親籓遠涉，內侍隨行，藉以示體恤、昭慎重也。
entries.en: Yixin said: "What I meant by 'unavoidable hardship' was the thought that a princely kinsman traveled far and a palace attendant went along, thereby showing consideration and proclaiming caution.
entries.literal: Yixin said: "What this official meant by 'unavoidable hardship' was the thought that a princely kinsman traveled far and a palace attendant went along, thereby showing consideration and proclaiming caution.

entries.zh: 顧在朝廷為曲體，在臣庶則為創見。
entries.en: At court this might be read as accommodating consideration; among officials and commoners it was a startling novelty.
entries.literal: Yet at court this was accommodating the person; among officials and commoners it was a startling novelty.

entries.zh: 風聞北洋大臣以座船迎醇親王，王弗受，而太監隨乘之，至駴人觀聽。
entries.en: It was rumored that the Beiyang minister welcomed Prince Chun with a seat-boat. The prince refused it, but the eunuch rode in it anyway, to the shock of all who saw and heard.
entries.literal: It was rumored that the Beiyang minister welcomed Prince Chun with a seat-boat; the prince refused, but the eunuch rode in it, to the shock of all who saw and heard.

entries.zh: 一不謹慎，流弊遂已至斯，臣所為不能已於言也。」
entries.en: One moment of carelessness, and the abuse has already reached this point. That is why I could not restrain my words."
entries.literal: One moment of carelessness, and the flowing abuse has already reached this point—this is why your official could not restrain his words."

entries.zh: 詔切責，降主事。
entries.en: An edict sharply rebuked him and demoted him to secretary.
entries.literal: An edict sharply rebuked him and demoted him to secretary.

entries.zh: 乞終養歸。
entries.en: He begged leave to retire and care for his parents at home.
entries.literal: He begged leave to retire and care for his parents at home.

entries.zh: 十五年，太后歸政，仁守慮僉人讒構兩宮，易生嫌隙，疏請依高宗訓政往事：「凡部院題本、尋常奏事，如常例；
entries.en: In 1889 the empress dowager returned power. Renshou feared that malicious men would sow discord between the two palaces and easily breed suspicion. He memorialized asking that the precedent of the Gaozong Emperor's regency be followed: "All routine memorials from ministries and boards and ordinary reports shall follow usual practice;
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year the empress dowager returned power; Renshou feared that malicious men would sow discord between the two palaces and easily breed suspicion, and memorialized asking that the precedent of the Gaozong Emperor's regency be followed: "All routine memorials from ministries and boards and ordinary reports shall follow usual practice;

entries.zh: 外省密摺、廷臣封奏，仍書皇太后、皇上聖鑒，俟慈覽後施行。」
entries.en: secret memorials from the provinces and sealed reports from court ministers shall still be addressed For the Sacred View of the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, to be carried out after her gracious perusal."
entries.literal: secret memorials from the provinces and sealed reports from court ministers shall still be addressed For the Sacred View of the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, to be carried out after her gracious perusal."

entries.zh: 並請太后居慈寧宮，節遊觀。
entries.en: He also asked that the empress dowager reside at Cining Palace and moderate excursions and sightseeing.
entries.literal: He also asked that the empress dowager reside at Cining Palace and moderate excursions and sightseeing.

entries.zh: 詔嚴責，革職永不敘用。
entries.en: An edict sternly rebuked him, stripped him of office, and barred him forever from reappointment.
entries.literal: An edict sternly rebuked him, stripped him of office, and barred him forever from reappointment.

entries.zh: 既歸，主講山西令德堂。
entries.en: After returning home he became head lecturer at Lingde Hall in Shanxi.
entries.literal: After returning home he became head lecturer at Lingde Hall in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 二十六年，兩宮西狩，起用五品京堂，授光祿寺少卿。
entries.en: In 1900, when the two palaces fled west, he was recalled as a fifth-rank capital official and appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went west on campaign, he was recalled as a fifth-rank capital official and appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 尋卒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he died.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he died.

entries.zh: 列傳二百三十二
entries.en: Biographies 232
entries.literal: Biographies 232

entries.zh: 馥既膺疆寄，則益欲大有為，凡所以阜民財、瀹民智者，次第興舉，天子嘉之，擢署兩江總督，移督兩廣。
entries.en: Entrusted with a frontier post, Zhou Fu sought larger achievements, launching programs to enrich the people's wealth and enlighten their understanding in turn. The emperor commended him, appointed him acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs, then transferred him to govern the Two Guangs.
entries.literal: Once Fu received frontier trust, he wished all the more to achieve great things; whatever could enrich popular wealth and enlighten popular wisdom he launched in sequence; the Son of Heaven praised him, promoted him to act as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, then transferred him to govern the Two Guangs.

entries.zh: 三十三年，請告歸。
entries.en: In 1907 he asked to retire.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he requested leave to return home.

entries.zh: 越十四年，卒，諡愨慎。
entries.en: Fourteen years later he died; his posthumous title was Queshen (Respectful Caution).
entries.literal: After fourteen years he died; posthumous title Que Shen.

entries.zh: 直隸、山東、江南士民皆祠祀之。
entries.en: Communities in Zhili, Shandong, and the lower Yangzi region all erected shrines in his honor.
entries.literal: Officials and people of Zhili, Shandong, and Jiangnan all erected shrines to worship him.

entries.zh: 兩江總督劉坤一疏薦元鼎才任方面，二十一年，授惠潮嘉道，調江蘇糧道，遷按察使。
entries.en: Governor-General Liu Kunyi recommended Lu Yuanding for higher office; in 1895 he was appointed intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaying Circuit, then grain intendant of Jiangsu, and promoted to judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi of the Two Jiangs memorialized recommending Yuanding's talent for frontier responsibility; in the twenty-first year he was appointed Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaying Circuit intendant, transferred to Jiangsu grain transport intendant, and promoted judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 陛見，溫語移時。
entries.en: At audience with the emperor he was addressed warmly for a long time.
entries.literal: At imperial audience, warm words extended for a long while.

entries.zh: 論及前歲日本構戰，我軍槍彈多與口徑不合，以故敗。
entries.en: The conversation turned to the recent war with Japan: many army rifles and ammunition were mismatched in caliber, which was one reason for defeat.
entries.literal: Discussion turned to the previous year's Japanese war-making: our army's rifle bullets mostly did not match the bore caliber, and for this reason they were defeated.

entries.zh: 帝因諭樞臣戒督撫審軍實，且曰：「毋謂語由元鼎，使督撫生芥蒂也。」
entries.en: The emperor told the Grand Council to warn governors to inspect their armies honestly, adding: "Do not let them think this came from Lu Yuanding and breed resentment."
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon instructed Grand Council members to warn governors to examine military realities, and said: 'Do not say these words came from Yuanding and make governors bear a grudge.'

entries.zh: 江陰焚教堂，縣吏捕首事者上之按察使。
entries.en: When a church was burned at Jiangyin, county officials arrested the ringleaders and sent them to the judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: At Jiangyin a church was burned; county officials arrested the ringleaders and sent them up to the judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 上海領事謂逮捕者非首犯，駐京公使言於總署，令領事往會鞫。
entries.en: The Shanghai consul claimed the wrong men had been arrested; the minister in Beijing pressed the Zongli Yamen to let the consul join the trial.
entries.literal: The Shanghai consul said those arrested were not the chief culprits; the minister in Beijing spoke to the Zongli Yamen, ordering the consul to go for joint trial.

entries.zh: 元鼎曰：「會鞫有專官，按察使署非會鞫所。」
entries.en: Lu Yuanding replied: "Joint trials have designated officers; a judicial commissioner's yamen is not the place for them."
entries.literal: Yuanding said: 'Joint trial has specialized officials; the judicial commissioner's office is not a joint-trial venue.'

entries.zh: 領事言：「不會鞫，當觀讞也。」
entries.en: The consul said: "If there is no joint trial, I must at least see the verdict."
entries.literal: The consul said: 'If there is no joint trial, I should observe the judgment record.'

entries.zh: 元鼎持不可，領事曰：「其如總署指揮何？」
entries.en: Lu Yuanding refused. The consul asked: "What about orders from the Zongli Yamen?"
entries.literal: Yuanding held firm that it could not be done; the consul said: 'But what of the Zongli Yamen's orders?'

entries.zh: 元鼎曰：「慎守國憲。
entries.en: Lu Yuanding answered: "Uphold the laws of the realm.
entries.literal: Yuanding said: 'Carefully uphold the laws of the state.

entries.zh: 官可辭，法不可撓！」
entries.en: An official may resign; the law cannot be bent!"
entries.literal: Office may be resigned; law cannot be bent!'

entries.zh: 領事怏怏去。
entries.en: The consul withdrew in annoyance.
entries.literal: The consul left displeased.

entries.zh: 樞臣聞而嘉之，曰：「不爾，又為故事矣。」
entries.en: Grand Council members praised him, saying: "Otherwise we would have yielded as usual."
entries.literal: Grand Council members heard and praised it, saying: 'Otherwise, it would again become an old story.'

entries.zh: 尋署布政使，護巡撫。
entries.en: He soon served as acting treasurer and acting governor.
entries.literal: Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer and served as acting governor.

entries.zh: 宣統元年，德宗梓宮奉移西陵，詔所需不得攤派民間。
entries.en: In 1909, when Emperor Guangxu's coffin was moved to the Western Tombs, an edict forbade levying the costs on the people.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Emperor Dezong's coffin was moved in honor to the Western Tombs; an edict declared required expenses must not be apportioned to the populace.

entries.zh: 士驤慨然思革百年之弊，疏曰：「國初因明季加派紛繁，民生彫敝，屢降旨申禁科累。
entries.en: Yang resolved to reform abuses of a century and memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty, the many surcharges of the late Ming had exhausted the people, and repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions.
entries.literal: Shixiang, moved with resolve to reform a century's abuses, memorialized: 'At the dynasty's founding, because of the late Ming's many added levies, popular livelihood was carved and exhausted—repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions.

entries.zh: 近畿繁劇，供億多，不能盡革，故田賦較各省輕，而歲出差徭逾於糧銀之數。
entries.en: The capital region remained complex and costly, so land tax stayed lighter than in other provinces, yet annual labor levies exceeded the grain tax in silver.
entries.literal: The metropolitan region is busy and complex, supplies numerous—could not fully reform; therefore land tax is lighter than other provinces, yet yearly corvée levies exceed the grain-tax silver amount.

entries.zh: 新政迭興，學堂、巡警諸費，無不取給於民，輸納之艱，日以加甚。
entries.en: With successive new policies, school and police costs and more were all levied on the people, and payment grew harder by the day.
entries.literal: New policies arose in succession—schools, constabulary, and other expenses all drew supply from the people; the hardship of payment daily grew worse.

entries.zh: 擬官紳合查常年應官差徭，實係公用者，酌定數目，折交州縣自辦，不得濫派折錢；
entries.en: He proposed that officials and gentry audit annual public corvée, fix the amounts truly needed for public use, pay a cash commutation to prefectures and counties to handle themselves, and forbid reckless surcharges;
entries.literal: It is proposed that officials and gentry jointly investigate yearly corvée due to government, what is truly for public use—fix the amount, convert and hand to prefectures and counties to manage themselves, and not permit reckless apportionment of cash conversion;

entries.zh: 胥役書差，官給津貼。
entries.en: with yamen runners and clerks paid official allowances.
entries.literal: runners, clerks, and document handlers—officials should provide allowances.

entries.zh: 庶積弊一清，上下交益。」
entries.en: Thus long-standing abuses might be cleared and both government and people would benefit."
entries.literal: Thus accumulated abuses may be cleared at once, and above and below mutually benefit.'

entries.zh: 疏入，優詔答之。
entries.en: The memorial was answered with a commendatory edict.
entries.literal: The memorial entered and received a favorable edict in reply.

entries.zh: 五月，卒，贈太子少保，諡文敬。
entries.en: He died in the fifth month and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenjing (Cultivated Respect).
entries.literal: In the fifth month he died; posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Wenjing.

entries.zh: 馮煦，字夢華，江蘇金壇人。
entries.en: Feng Xu, whose courtesy name was Menghua, came from Jintan in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Feng Xu, courtesy name Menghua, was a native of Jintan, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 光緒十二年一甲三名進士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1886 he placed among the top three metropolitan graduates of the first class and was appointed Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he was metropolitan graduate of the first class, top three, and appointed Hanlin compiler.

entries.zh: 疊上疏代奏，請圖自強，敦大本，行實政，德宗嘉納。
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized for national self-strengthening, sound fundamentals, and practical government; Emperor Guangxu approved.
entries.literal: Repeatedly he submitted memorials for presentation, requesting plans for self-strengthening, honoring the great foundation, and carrying out practical government—Emperor Dezong commended and accepted.

entries.zh: 典湖南鄉試，稱得士。
entries.en: As chief examiner of the Hunan provincial examinations, he was praised for selecting able candidates.
entries.literal: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination and was said to have obtained worthy scholars.

entries.zh: 二十一年，以京察一等授安徽鳳陽知府。
entries.en: In 1895, rated first class in the metropolitan personnel review, he was appointed prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, through metropolitan personnel review of the first grade he was appointed Fengyang prefect of Anhui.

entries.zh: 鳳屬連年水澇，煦單騎按部，逐一履勘，以被災之重輕，定給賑之多寡，人霑實惠。
entries.en: Fengyang suffered floods year after year; Feng rode alone through the district, inspected each area, and scaled relief to the severity of damage so that people received real help.
entries.literal: Fengyang territory suffered flood and waterlogging year after year; Xu rode alone on inspection, examined each place in turn, and according to the severity of disaster fixed the amount of relief—people received real benefit.

entries.zh: 並屢平反疑獄。
entries.en: He also repeatedly overturned wrongful convictions in doubtful cases.
entries.literal: He also repeatedly reversed doubtful cases.

entries.zh: 總督劉坤一以心存利濟、政切先勞疏保，兩攝鳳潁六泗道。
entries.en: Governor-General Liu Kunyi recommended him for devoted public service and twice had him act as intendant of the Fengying-Liusi Circuit.
entries.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi memorialized to recommend him for mind set on benefiting others and government earnest in taking hardship first; twice he acted as Fengying-Liusi Circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 二十七年，遷山西按察使，調四川。
entries.en: In 1901 he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Shanxi, then to Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Shanxi judicial commissioner, then to Sichuan.

entries.zh: 廣安州有聚眾謀毀學堂者，獲四人，擬照土匪例正法。
entries.en: At Guang'an Prefecture a crowd plotted to destroy a school; four were arrested and the provincial government proposed executing them under the bandit law.
entries.literal: In Guang'an Prefecture men gathered plotting to destroy a school; four were seized and it was proposed to execute them by the bandit precedent.

entries.zh: 煦白大府，請按而後誅，以去就爭，至免冠抵幾，不得請不止。
entries.en: Feng appealed to the provincial government for trial before execution, staking his office on the point, even removing his cap and pounding the desk until his request was granted.
entries.literal: Xu informed the superior office, requesting trial before execution; he contested with his post at stake, even removing his cap and striking the desk—he would not stop until his request was granted.

entries.zh: 旋署布政使，復調安徽，兼署提學使。
entries.en: He soon served as acting provincial treasurer, returned to Anhui, and also acted as education commissioner.
entries.literal: Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer, again transferred to Anhui, concurrently acting as education commissioner.

entries.zh: 列傳二百三十六
entries.en: Biographies 236
entries.literal: Biographies 236

entries.zh: 鶴年有知人鑑，少與文祥同學相淬厲。
entries.en: Henian had a keen eye for talent; as a young man he studied alongside Wen Xiang, and the two pushed each other to excel.
entries.literal: Henian had a discerning eye for talent; in youth he studied together with Wen Xiang and they spurred each other on.

entries.zh: 及居言職，嚴疏劾肅順跋扈，而奏起曾國籓於家，謂必能辦賊。
entries.en: While serving as a remonstrating official he submitted stern memorials impeaching Sushun for arrogance and power, and urged the court to recall Zeng Guofan from retirement, declaring that Zeng alone could defeat the rebels.
entries.literal: When he held a remonstrating office he sternly memorialized impeaching Sushun's overbearing conduct, and memorialized to recall Zeng Guofan from retirement at home, saying he would surely be able to handle the bandits.

entries.zh: 拔宋慶、張曜統豫軍，後皆為名將。
entries.en: He elevated Song Qing and Zhang Yao to lead the Henan armies, and both later became celebrated generals.
entries.literal: He promoted Song Qing and Zhang Yao to command the Henan armies; both later became famous generals.

entries.zh: 治豫久，多善政，豫人刻石頌之。
entries.en: After long service in Henan he left behind many policies that benefited the people, and locals erected stone inscriptions in his praise.
entries.literal: He governed Henan for a long time with many benevolent policies, and the people of Henan carved stone inscriptions to praise him.

entries.zh: 始任河督，黑岡堤潰，不絕如縷。
entries.en: When he first became river commissioner, the Heigang dike burst and hung together by a thread.
entries.literal: When he first took up the river commission, the Heigang dike breached and hung by a thread.

entries.zh: 鶴年親督工二十餘晝夜，險工克濟。
entries.en: Henian personally oversaw the repairs for more than twenty days and nights until the perilous stretch was secured.
entries.literal: Henian personally supervised the work for more than twenty days and nights, and the dangerous project was successfully completed.

entries.zh: 德宗嘗詢李鴻藻以善治河者，鴻藻舉鶴年，上亦識前事之枉也，故再任河督。
entries.en: Emperor Guangxu once asked Li Hongzao who best understood river control; Hongzao named Henian, and the emperor, recognizing that Henian had been wronged before, appointed him river commissioner again.
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong once asked Li Hongzao who was good at managing rivers; Hongzao recommended Henian, and the emperor also recognized that the earlier affair had been unjust, so Henian was again appointed river commissioner.

entries.zh: 其卒也，豫民有流涕者。
entries.en: When he died, some among the people of Henan wept openly.
entries.literal: At his death, there were people of Henan who wept.

entries.zh: 三子葆恂博學多文，尤知名。
entries.en: His third son Bao Xun was widely learned and literary and became especially well known.
entries.literal: His third son Bao Xun was learned and literary and was especially well known.

entries.zh: 十年，擢閩浙總督。
entries.en: In 1871 he was promoted to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 明年，陛見，賜紫禁城騎馬。
entries.en: The following year he was received in audience and granted the rare privilege of riding a horse inside the Forbidden City.
entries.literal: The next year he had an audience with the emperor and was granted the privilege of riding a horse within the Forbidden City.

entries.zh: 旋署福州將軍，兼署巡撫。
entries.en: He was soon made acting Fuzhou general while also serving as acting governor.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed acting Fuzhou general and additionally acted as governor.

entries.zh: 詔詢海防事宜，覆奏言：「海防之策，莫重於練兵、籌餉、制器、用人四端。
entries.en: When the court asked about coastal defense, he answered in a memorial: "Coastal defense depends above all on four things: training troops, securing funds, manufacturing weapons, and appointing the right men.
entries.literal: The throne inquired about coastal defense; in reply he memorialized: "Of policies for coastal defense, nothing is more important than the four points of training troops, securing funds, manufacturing weapons, and employing men.

entries.zh: 四者之中，以用人為急務，而尤在專其責成。
entries.en: Of these four, staffing is the most urgent, and what matters most is to assign clear responsibility.
entries.literal: Among the four, employing men is the urgent task, and above all one must assign clear responsibility.

entries.zh: 沿海疆臣固責無旁貸，第無統率大員，仍恐意見紛歧，臨事推諉。」
