entries.en: The coastal governors cannot evade their duty, but without a senior commander in overall charge, opinions will split and officials will pass blame when crisis comes."
entries.literal: Coastal governors and viceroys are indeed without excuse from their responsibility, but without a supreme commanding officer there is still fear of divergent opinions and shirking at the critical moment."

entries.zh: 上韙其議。
entries.en: The emperor endorsed his proposal.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his plan.

entries.zh: 十四年，鄭州河再決，上震怒，褫河督李鶴年職，以大澂代之。
entries.en: In 1888 the Zhengzhou breach opened again; the emperor was furious, dismissed river commissioner Li Henian, and replaced him with Dacheng.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year the Zhengzhou river breached again; the emperor was greatly angered, stripped river commissioner Li Henian of office, and replaced him with Dacheng.

entries.zh: 是年冬，河工合龍，大澂力居多。
entries.en: That winter the breach was closed, and Dacheng's contribution was the largest.
entries.literal: That winter the river works were closed; Dacheng's effort was foremost.

entries.zh: 大澂盛負時譽，會海軍議起，以醇親王奕枻為總理。
entries.en: Dacheng enjoyed great contemporary renown; when plans for a navy were raised, Prince Chun Yixuan was placed in charge.
entries.literal: Dacheng bore great contemporary reputation; when discussion of a navy arose, Prince Chun Yixuan was made superintendent.

entries.zh: 大澂素與王善，治河功成，實授河道總督，加頭品頂戴。
entries.en: Dacheng had long been on good terms with the prince; after the river works succeeded he was formally appointed Yellow River commissioner and granted the first-rank hat finial.
entries.literal: Dacheng had long been on good terms with the prince; when river control was successfully completed he was substantively appointed Yellow River commissioner and granted the first-rank hat finial.

entries.zh: 大澂遂疏請尊崇醇親王稱號禮節。
entries.en: Dacheng then memorialized requesting elevated titles and ceremonial honors for Prince Chun.
entries.literal: Dacheng then memorialized requesting elevated titles and ceremonial honors for Prince Chun.

entries.zh: 疏入，孝欽顯皇后震怒，出醇親王元年所上預杜妄論疏頒示天下。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, Empress Dowager Cixi was furious and had Prince Chun's own memorial from his first year in office — written to forestall reckless speculation — published throughout the empire.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Dowager Cixi was greatly angered and issued for publication throughout the realm the memorial Prince Chun had submitted in his first year to forestall reckless talk.

entries.zh: 大澂幾得嚴譴，以母喪歸，乃已。
entries.en: Dacheng nearly faced severe punishment, but returned home for his mother's mourning, and the affair ended there.
entries.literal: Dacheng nearly received severe punishment, but returned home on his mother's death, and the matter then ended.

entries.zh: 李鶴年，字子和，奉天義州人。
entries.en: Li Henian, styled Zihe, was a native of Yizhou in Fengtian.
entries.literal: Li Henian, styled Zihe, was a native of Yizhou in Fengtian.

entries.zh: 道光二十五年進士，由編修改御史，轉給事中。
entries.en: He became a jinshi in 1845, moved from a Hanlin compiler's post to the Censorate, and was later appointed a supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, was transferred from compiler in the Hanlin Academy to censor, and then to supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 父憂歸，服除，命赴河南襄辦軍務。
entries.en: After returning home for his father's mourning and completing the prescribed period, he was sent to Henan to help manage military affairs.
entries.literal: He returned home upon his father's death; after the mourning period ended, he was ordered to proceed to Henan to assist in military affairs.

entries.zh: 同治元年，授常鎮通海道，署河南按察使，調直隸，授布政使。
entries.en: In 1862 he was made intendant of the Chang-Zhen-Tong-Hai Circuit, served as acting Henan judicial commissioner, transferred to Zhili, and received appointment as provincial treasurer.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed intendant of the Chang-Zhen-Tong-Hai Circuit, acted as Henan provincial judicial commissioner, was transferred to Zhili, and was appointed provincial treasurer.

entries.zh: 四年，擢湖北巡撫，調河南。
entries.en: In 1865 he was promoted to governor of Hubei and shortly afterward transferred to Henan.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to governor of Hubei, then transferred to Henan.

entries.zh: 硃其昂，字云甫，江蘇寶山人。
entries.en: Zhu Qiang, styled Yunfu, came from Baoshan in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Zhu Qiang, courtesy name Yunfu, was a native of Baoshan, Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 同治初，從軍攻南匯。
entries.en: Early in Tongzhi he joined the campaign against Nanhui.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he joined the army to attack Nanhui.

entries.zh: 城賊原降，要一人入盟，無敢往者，其昂毅然請入受其降，城始下。
entries.en: The besieged rebels offered to surrender on condition that someone enter the city to seal the pact; no one dared go until Qiang volunteered, entered, accepted their surrender, and the city then fell.
entries.literal: The rebels in the city wished to surrender but required one person to enter and conclude the pact; no one dared go; Qiang resolutely volunteered to enter and accept their surrender, and only then did the city fall.

entries.zh: 旋納貲為通判，累至道員。
entries.en: He soon purchased a subprefect post and rose step by step to circuit intendant.
entries.literal: Soon he purchased office as subprefect and rose through accumulation to circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 北洋大臣李鴻章頗奇其才。
entries.en: Li Hongzhang, minister for the northern coast, took a strong interest in his abilities.
entries.literal: Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang greatly admired his talent.

entries.zh: 福州船政造軍艦不適用，奏改商船。
entries.en: Warships built at the Fuzhou Naval Yard proved unsuitable, and the court was asked to shift to merchant shipping instead.
entries.literal: The Fuzhou Naval Yard built warships that proved unsuitable, and a memorial was submitted to change to merchant vessels.

entries.zh: 其昂與其弟其詔創議官商合辦，請設輪船招商局，鴻章上其事，遂檄為總辦。
entries.en: Qiang and his younger brother Qizhao proposed a joint official-merchant steamship company; Li Hongzhang memorialized the plan and appointed Qiang general manager.
entries.literal: Qiang and his younger brother Qizhao originated the proposal for joint official-merchant operation and requested establishment of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company; Hongzhang reported the matter and then ordered him as general manager.

entries.zh: 御史董俊翰劾以力小任重，下鴻章查覆，仍力贊其成。
entries.en: Censor Dong Junhan impeached him for taking on more than he could manage; Li Hongzhang was ordered to investigate but still strongly backed the venture.
entries.literal: Censor Dong Junhan impeached him for bearing too great a burden with too little strength; the matter was referred to Hongzhang for investigation, yet he still strongly supported its completion.

entries.zh: 於是官商合力開局集股，並收並外人所設旗昌輪船公司以保航權。
entries.en: Officials and merchants then opened the company, sold shares, and bought out the foreign-run Russell & Company steamship line to protect China's shipping interests.
entries.literal: Thereupon officials and merchants combined to open the bureau and collect shares, and also acquired and merged the Qichang steamship company set up by foreigners to protect navigation rights.

entries.zh: 數年，成效大著。
entries.en: Within a few years the results were striking.
entries.literal: Within several years the results were greatly evident.

entries.zh: 光緒初，直、晉災，其昂輸私財力任賑撫，以勞致疾。
entries.en: Early in Guangxu, when Zhili and Shanxi were stricken by famine, he spent his own fortune on relief work until illness overtook him.
entries.literal: Early in Guangxu, when Zhili and Shanxi suffered disaster, Qiang contributed private wealth and took full charge of relief, falling ill from overwork.

entries.zh: 鴻章特委權津海關道，越三日卒，詔優恤，贈光祿寺卿。
entries.en: Li Hongzhang specially appointed him acting Tianjin customs intendant; he died three days later. The throne granted generous posthumous honors and the rank of vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Hongzhang specially entrusted him with acting as Tianjin customs intendant; three days later he died; an edict granted generous condolence and posthumously awarded him as Chamberlain of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 其詔，字翼甫。
entries.en: His younger brother Qizhao, styled Yifu.
entries.literal: Qizhao, courtesy name Yifu.

entries.zh: 納貲為知縣，累至道員。
entries.en: He purchased a magistracy and rose step by step to circuit intendant.
entries.literal: He purchased office as magistrate and rose through accumulation to circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 歷充江、浙漕運事。
entries.en: He served repeatedly in Jiangsu and Zhejiang grain transport.
entries.literal: He successively served in grain transport affairs for Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 輪船招商局既成，復請以額定漕運費給輪船代為海運，局基始固。
entries.en: Once the China Merchants Company was running, he secured the fixed grain-transport subsidy for steamship carriage by sea, giving the company a firm financial base.
entries.literal: After the China Merchants Company was established, he again requested that the fixed grain-transport quota be paid to steamships for sea transport in its place, and the company's foundation was then secured.

entries.zh: 再權永定河道，時出巡河堤上下，務盡其利弊。
entries.en: He again served as acting Yongding River intendant, touring the dikes up and down the river to learn every advantage and defect.
entries.literal: He again acted as Yongding River intendant, often going out to inspect dikes up and down the river, striving to ascertain all advantages and disadvantages.

entries.zh: 遇伏汛暴漲，嘗三晝夜不交睫，親督弁兵搶護，始免潰決，民皆德之。
entries.en: During a sudden summer flood he once went three days and nights without sleep, personally directing emergency repairs, and averted a breach; the people were deeply grateful.
entries.literal: When the summer flood season brought sudden rise, he once went three days and nights without sleep, personally directing officers and soldiers in emergency defense, and only thus avoided breach; the people all thanked him.

entries.zh: 擴充天津電報學堂，成材益廣。
entries.en: He expanded the Tianjin Telegraph School and turned out more graduates than ever.
entries.literal: He expanded the Tianjin Telegraph School and produced talent in ever greater numbers.

entries.zh: 時方議辦海軍醫學堂，其詔复捐自置天津法租界地四十畝為校址以成之，其急公好義類如此。
entries.en: When a naval medical school was being planned, Qizhao donated forty mu he had bought in the Tianjin French concession as its site—typical of his public spirit.
entries.literal: At that time a naval medical school was under discussion; Qizhao again donated forty mu of land he had purchased in the Tianjin French concession as the school site to bring it into being; his public spirit and love of righteousness were of this sort.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒，贈內閣學士。
entries.en: He died soon afterward and was posthumously made a Grand Secretariat bachelor.
entries.literal: Before long he died and was posthumously awarded Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

entries.zh: 洪汝奎，字琴西，湖北漢陽人。
entries.en: Hong Rukui, styled Qinxi, came from Hanyang in Hubei.
entries.literal: Hong Rukui, courtesy name Qinxi, was a native of Hanyang, Hubei.

entries.zh: 道光二十四年舉人。
entries.en: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-fourth year of the Daoguang reign (1844).
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate.

entries.zh: 咸豐初，考取官學教習，期滿以知縣用。
entries.en: Early in the Xianfeng period he qualified as an Imperial College instructor and, upon completing his term, was selected for a county magistracy.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he passed the examination for Imperial College instructor; when his term ended he was appointed as a magistrate.

entries.zh: 參曾國籓軍事。
entries.en: He joined Zeng Guofan's military staff.
entries.literal: He participated in Zeng Guofan's military affairs.

entries.zh: 同治初，洊保至江南道員。
entries.en: In the early Tongzhi years successive commendations advanced him to a Jiangnan circuit-intendant post.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, through repeated recommendations he rose to circuit intendant of Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 總理糧台，供應防軍及他省協餉。
entries.en: As superintendent of the grain bureau, he supplied provisions for garrison troops and inter-provincial military assistance funds.
entries.literal: He superintended the grain bureau, supplying defense forces and assistance funds from other provinces.

entries.zh: 又籌還西征洋債，出入逾二千萬，綜核名實，不避嫌忌。
entries.en: He also managed repayment of the foreign loans raised for the Western campaigns, handling more than twenty million taels in turnover while reconciling accounts rigorously and refusing to evade controversy.
entries.literal: He also arranged repayment of Western-expedition foreign loans; receipts and disbursements exceeded twenty million; he audited names against facts and did not shun suspicion.

entries.zh: 光緒中，沈葆楨為兩江總督，尤倚任之。
entries.en: Under Guangxu, when Shen Baozhen governed the Two Jiangs, he leaned on him more than anyone else.
entries.literal: During Guangxu, Shen Baozhen served as governor-general of the Two Jiangs and especially relied upon him.

entries.zh: 葆楨治尚威猛，因疾在告，輒疏請汝奎代治事，聲望益起。
entries.en: Shen governed in a stern, forceful style; whenever illness kept him on leave he repeatedly asked the throne to let Rukui act for him, and Rukui's standing grew accordingly.
entries.literal: Baozhen's governance favored stern severity; when illness obliged him to request leave, he repeatedly memorialized asking Rukui to administer affairs in his stead, and Rukui's reputation rose further.

entries.zh: 會詔求人才，大臣交章論薦。
entries.en: When the court called for talent, senior officials lined up to recommend him.
entries.literal: When an edict sought talented men, ministers submitted memorials one after another commending him.

entries.zh: 五年，特擢廣東鹽運使。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was specially promoted to salt transport commissioner of Guangdong.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was specially promoted to Guangdong salt transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 調兩淮，裁冗費，建義倉，濬揚州城河。
entries.en: Transferred to the Two Huai salt administration, he pruned waste, founded charity granaries, and dredged Yangzhou's city canal.
entries.literal: Transferred to the Two Huai, he cut redundant expenses, established benevolent granaries, and dredged the Yangzhou city canal.

entries.zh: 方欲大有為，而江寧三牌樓之獄起。
entries.en: He was on the verge of major achievements when the Three Pailou case broke out in Nanjing.
entries.literal: Just as he intended great undertakings, the Nanjing Three Pailou case arose.

entries.zh: 其冬，力疾再出關，駐諒山，趣軍進取，分襲海陽、嘉林綴敵勢；
entries.en: That winter, ill as he was, he crossed the border again and took post at Lang Son. He pressed the army to advance and sent columns to strike Hai Duong and Gia Lam and tie down the enemy.
entries.literal: That winter, forcing himself despite illness, he again went through the pass, stationed himself at Lang Son, urged the army forward, and sent detachments to raid Hai Duong and Gia Lam to pin down the enemy;

entries.zh: 並請撥船嚴扼海口，斷其出入：諭仍力守北寧。
entries.en: He also asked for vessels to block the river mouth and cut the enemy's lines of supply. The court told him nonetheless to hold Bac Ninh at all costs.
entries.literal: he also asked that ships be assigned to block the estuary strictly and cut off enemy movement in and out: the court instructed him still to hold Bac Ninh firmly.

entries.zh: 於是令左軍黃桂蘭、右軍趙沃協防其地。
entries.en: He then ordered Huang Guilan's left wing and Zhao Wo's right wing to defend the place together.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered Huang Guilan of the left army and Zhao Wo of the right army to defend the place jointly.

entries.zh: 適山西陷，延旭猶慮兵力薄，復遣使入關募勇，通舊五十餘營，厚集於此。
entries.en: Son Tay had just fallen, and Yanxu still feared his forces were too few. He sent men back through the pass to raise troops and gathered more than fifty former battalions in strength there.
entries.literal: Just then Son Tay fell; Yanxu still feared his forces were thin, and again sent envoys back through the pass to raise braves, mustering more than fifty old battalions in strength at this point.

entries.zh: 隨令廣間諜，安地營，禁擾民，嚴冒餉；
entries.en: He spread spies widely, ordered camps properly sited, forbade harassment of civilians, and cracked down hard on padded payrolls.
entries.literal: He then ordered extensive use of spies, proper siting of camps, prohibition of harassment of the people, and strict punishment of false muster rolls;

entries.zh: 然沃等皆寡識，桂蘭尤侈汰，與越官張登壇日事宴樂。
entries.en: Yet Zhao Wo and his fellows were shallow men, and Huang Guilan was especially extravagant. He and the Vietnamese official Zhang Dengtan spent their days in feasting and pleasure.
entries.literal: Yet Zhao Wo and the others were all men of little judgment; Huang Guilan was especially extravagant and wasteful, and with the Vietnamese official Zhang Dengtan feasted and made merry every day.

entries.zh: 登壇故通法，嗣以有郤洩其事。
entries.en: Dengtan had long been in touch with the French; later, after a falling-out, he betrayed the fact.
entries.literal: Dengtan had formerly been in contact with the French; later, because of a rift, he leaked the matter.

entries.zh: 上命延旭罷登壇，或囚而殺之，延旭以力不能制而止。
entries.en: The throne ordered Yanxu to remove Dengtan, or to imprison and execute him, but Yanxu desisted because he lacked the power to enforce it.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Yanxu to dismiss Dengtan, or imprison and execute him; Yanxu stopped because he had not the power to control him.

entries.zh: 日唯籌軍火濟師，以為兵力厚，可恃以無恐。
entries.en: He spent his days only arranging arms and supplies for the troops, convinced that with so large a force he had nothing to fear.
entries.literal: Day after day he only planned arms and supplies to support the army, thinking that with thick forces he could rely on them without fear.

entries.zh: 桂蘭復希風指，侈談部下能戰，延旭益信之，遂六上書請戰。
entries.en: Huang Guilan again tried to read his commander's mind and boasted of his men's fighting power. Yanxu believed him all the more and six times memorialized asking permission to give battle.
entries.literal: Huang Guilan again sought to read his superior's wishes and boasted that his subordinates could fight; Yanxu believed him all the more and six times submitted memorials requesting battle.

entries.zh: 上不許，敕保守未失陷地，毋貪功。
entries.en: The emperor refused and ordered him to hold whatever ground had not yet been lost and not court glory recklessly.
entries.literal: The emperor did not permit it and ordered him to hold what had not yet fallen and not seek merit greedily.

entries.zh: 十年，法軍陷扶良，三路攻北寧，桂蘭潰奔太原。
entries.en: In the tenth year the French took Phu Luong and attacked Bac Ninh on three fronts. Huang Guilan's force collapsed and fled toward Thai Nguyen.
entries.literal: In the tenth year the French army took Phu Luong, attacked Bac Ninh on three routes, and Huang Guilan broke and fled to Thai Nguyen.

entries.zh: 李鴻章電奏失守，延旭猶上言：「西聯滇軍，東防江口，北寧斷無他虞。」
entries.en: Li Hongzhang telegraphed that the position had been lost, yet Yanxu still reported: 'With the Yunnan army on our west and the river mouth guarded on the east, Bac Ninh is surely in no danger.'
entries.literal: Li Hongzhang telegraphed reporting the loss of the position; Yanxu still memorialized: 'In the west we are linked with the Yunnan army, in the east we guard the river mouth; Bac Ninh certainly has no other worry.'

entries.zh: 上責其飾詞。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him for dressing up the truth.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him for glossing over the facts.

entries.zh: 會岑毓英抵保勝，部署邊外各軍，遂命延旭軍屬之。
entries.en: When Cen Yuying reached Baosheng and took charge of the frontier armies, Yanxu's forces were placed under his command.
entries.literal: When Cen Yuying reached Baosheng and deployed the various armies beyond the border, the court then placed Yanxu's army under his command.

entries.zh: 初，延旭之任西撫也，未及兩月，亦知桂蘭等未可恃。
entries.en: When Yanxu first took up the governorship of the western provinces, he had known within two months that Huang Guilan and his like were not to be trusted.
entries.literal: At first, when Yanxu took office as governor of the western provinces, before two months had passed he too knew that Huang Guilan and the others could not be relied on.

entries.zh: 嗣以臨敵易將，操之急，易生變，以故誥誡備至；
entries.en: Later, knowing that replacing commanders on the eve of battle or driving them too hard could easily spark mutiny, he issued repeated stern admonitions.
entries.literal: Later, because replacing generals on the eve of battle and pressing them too hard easily produced mutiny, for that reason he admonished them at length in edicts;

entries.zh: 而桂蘭等且縱兵剽奪，越民不堪命，忿滋甚。
entries.en: Yet Huang Guilan and his men still let their troops loot and pillage until the Vietnamese could bear no more and their anger grew fierce.
entries.literal: yet Huang Guilan and the others also let their troops plunder and seize; the Vietnamese people could not bear it and their resentment grew ever worse.

entries.zh: 是役也，群反噬，城乃陷。
entries.en: In that battle the populace turned on them, and the city fell.
entries.literal: In this campaign the masses turned on them in retaliation, and the city then fell.

entries.zh: 延旭上其欺飾狀，並自糾請治罪。
entries.en: Yanxu reported their deceit and filed a confession of his own, asking to be punished.
entries.literal: Yanxu reported their deception and concealment and also impeached himself, requesting punishment.

entries.zh: 上怒，詔革職留任。
entries.en: The emperor was furious and stripped him of rank while leaving him in his post.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him dismissed from office but retained in his post.

entries.zh: 法人奪我越南，被命赴開化防守，即於軍前除巡撫。
entries.en: When the French seized Vietnam from China, he was ordered to Kaihua on defense duty and was appointed governor on the spot before the army.
entries.literal: The French seized our Vietnam; he was ordered to go to Kaihua to defend, and was at once appointed governor before the army.

entries.zh: 誤聞將議和，亟還省履任。
entries.en: Mistakenly hearing that peace talks were imminent, he hurried back to the provincial capital to take up his duties.
entries.literal: Mistakenly hearing that peace was about to be negotiated, he hurried back to the province to take up his post.

entries.zh: 上大怒，褫職逮問，刑部定讞斬監候。
entries.en: The emperor was furious, stripped him of rank, and ordered his arrest. The Ministry of Justice sentenced him to decapitation after imprisonment.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, stripped him of office and ordered arrest and trial; the Ministry of Justice fixed the sentence as decapitation after imprisonment.

entries.zh: 久之，上意解，三歷秋審，赦歸。
entries.en: In time the emperor relented. After three autumn sentence reviews he was pardoned and sent home.
entries.literal: After a long time the emperor's anger eased; through three autumn reviews he was pardoned and returned home.

entries.zh: 左宗棠臚其治行上於朝，命戍雲南，交岑毓英差序。
entries.en: Zuo Zongtang memorialized the court on his administrative record. He was ordered to serve in Yunnan and placed at Cen Yuying's disposal.
entries.literal: Zuo Zongtang set forth his record of administration and submitted it to the court; he was ordered to serve exile in Yunnan and placed under Cen Yuying's assignment.

entries.zh: 十三年，賞巡撫銜，督辦雲南礦務，偕日本礦師躬履昭通、東川、威寧銅鉛各廠，疏陳變通章程，又歷請減免貴州鉛課，豁免雲南礦廠官欠民欠，並報可。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was given governor's rank and put in charge of Yunnan mining. With Japanese mining engineers he personally inspected the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining, submitted revised regulations, and repeatedly asked for cuts in Guizhou lead taxes and cancellation of official and private debts at Yunnan mines—all approved.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted the rank of governor, supervised Yunnan mining affairs, and together with Japanese mining engineers personally inspected the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining; he memorialized in detail revised regulations, and also repeatedly requested reduction of Guizhou lead levies and exemption of official and private debts owed by Yunnan mines, all of which were approved.

entries.zh: 惟經營十五年，僅歲解京銅百萬斤，為時論所譏。
entries.en: Yet after fifteen years of management he forwarded only a million jin of copper a year to the capital, and contemporary opinion mocked the result.
entries.literal: Yet in fifteen years of management he forwarded only a million jin of copper annually to the capital, and was ridiculed in contemporary opinion.

entries.zh: 三十一年，謝病歸。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year he retired on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 三十四年，以鄉舉重逢，晉太子少保。
entries.en: In the thirty-fourth year, on the fiftieth anniversary of his provincial examination, he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, because he had passed the provincial examination fifty years earlier, he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 逾歲卒，年八十，卹如製。
entries.en: He died the following year at eighty, and state mourning was granted according to regulation.
entries.literal: The following year he died at the age of eighty; mourning rites were granted according to regulation.

entries.zh: 九年，法越事起，海防戒嚴。
entries.en: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out and coastal defenses were placed on alert.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose and coastal defense was placed on alert.

entries.zh: 璟令總兵張得勝等分扼諸郡，提督孫開華等分扼台、澎，並檄楊在元署台灣鎮，助防守。
entries.en: Jing ordered Brigadier Zhang Desheng and others to hold the prefectures and Brigadier Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu. He also put Yang Zaiyuan in acting command of the Taiwan garrison to assist in the defense.
entries.literal: Jing ordered Brigadier Zhang Desheng and others to hold the various prefectures in separate detachments, and Brigadier Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu; he also dispatched Yang Zaiyuan to act as Taiwan commander to assist in defense.

entries.zh: 明年，又上福、廈、台益船募卒狀，上皆勗勵之。
entries.en: The next year he memorialized again on adding ships and recruiting troops for Fujian, Xiamen, and Taiwan, and the emperor commended him warmly.
entries.literal: The next year he again submitted a memorial on increasing ships and recruiting soldiers for Fujian, Xiamen, and Taiwan; the emperor encouraged him in all respects.

entries.zh: 已而會辦軍務，張佩綸至，事皆專決，視璟等若屬吏；
entries.en: Soon he was assigned to joint management of military affairs. Zhang Peilun arrived, decided everything himself, and treated Jing and the others as mere subordinates.
entries.literal: Before long he was assigned to joint management of military affairs; Zhang Peilun arrived, decided everything on his own authority, and treated Jing and the others as subordinate officials;

entries.zh: 又嚴劾在元貪謬，璟坐疏忽，幹吏議。
entries.en: He also impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and incompetence. Jing was held negligent and referred to the personnel office for deliberation.
entries.literal: he also sternly impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and folly; Jing was implicated for negligence and referred to the personnel office for deliberation.

entries.zh: 以是益畏事之，不敢為異同。
entries.en: Jing feared him all the more and dared not disagree.
entries.literal: For this reason Jing feared him all the more in affairs and did not dare to differ.

entries.zh: 佩綸調舟師砲船局，璟亦以砲布衙署自衛。
entries.en: Peilun transferred the fleet to the gunboat bureau. Jing also posted cannon around his yamen for self-defense.
entries.literal: Peilun transferred the naval force to the gunboat bureau; Jing also placed cannon around his yamen for self-defense.

entries.zh: 廷旨以閩事亟，諄諄諭固守。
entries.en: Because Fujian affairs were urgent, the court repeatedly ordered him to hold firm.
entries.literal: Court edicts, because Fujian affairs were urgent, repeatedly instructed him to hold firm.

entries.zh: 逮戰書至，璟告佩綸曰：「明日法人將乘潮攻馬尾矣！」
entries.en: When war was declared, Jing told Peilun: 'Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!'
entries.literal: When the declaration of war arrived, Jing told Peilun: 'Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!'

entries.zh: 佩綸弗聽。
entries.en: Peilun would not listen.
entries.literal: Peilun would not listen.

entries.zh: 舟師大挫，璟欲馳援，而臨浦無舟可濟，株守省城，卒致閩事日壞；
entries.en: The fleet was crushed. Jing wanted to rush to reinforce them, but there were no boats at Linpu to cross the river. He stayed fixed in the provincial capital, and Fujian affairs grew worse by the day.
entries.literal: The fleet suffered a great defeat; Jing wished to rush to reinforce but at Linpu there were no boats to cross, and he remained fixed at the provincial capital, until Fujian affairs grew worse day by day;

entries.zh: 然猶左袒廣勇，雖逃不問，頗為時訾議。
entries.en: He still favored the Guangdong braves and did not punish deserters, which drew considerable public censure.
entries.literal: yet he still favored the Guangdong braves and did not inquire into deserters, which drew considerable censure in contemporary opinion.

entries.zh: 乃飛章自劾，而廷旨已先召還京。
entries.en: He sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself, but the court had already ordered him back to the capital.
entries.literal: He then sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself, but a court edict had already recalled him to the capital.

entries.zh: 尋御史亦劾其闒冗，部議褫職。
entries.en: Soon a censor impeached him for slackness and incompetence, and the ministry recommended stripping him of office.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward a censor also impeached him for slackness and incompetence, and the ministry recommended stripping him of office.

entries.zh: 十四年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the fourteenth year.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 何璟，字小宋，廣東香山人。
entries.en: He Jing, whose courtesy name was Xiaosong, came from Xiangshan in Guangdong.
entries.literal: He Jing, style name Xiaosong, was a man of Xiangshan in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 父曰愈，見循吏傳。
entries.en: His father Yu is treated in the biographies of model officials.
entries.literal: His father was named Yu and appears in the biographies of model officials.

entries.zh: 璟，道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，轉御史。
entries.en: Jing passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and later became a censor.
entries.literal: Jing, a jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and transferred to censor.

entries.zh: 咸豐七年，英人陷廣州，總督葉名琛獲譴罷，而巡撫柏貴等罪相埒，譴弗及，時論譁然，璟乃分別上其謬誤狀。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the British took Guangzhou. Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed, yet Governor Bai Gui and others were equally guilty yet went unpunished, and public opinion was outraged. Jing memorialized separately on each man's errors.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the English took Guangzhou; Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed, yet Governor Bai Gui and others were guilty to the same degree but were not punished, and public opinion was in an uproar; Jing thereupon submitted separate memorials on their errors.

entries.zh: 明年，英艦入津沽，疏陳戰守要略，先後抗論外務，疏凡八上。
entries.en: The next year, when British ships entered Tientsin, he memorialized on the essentials of war and defense and argued repeatedly against foreign-policy concessions, submitting eight memorials in all.
entries.literal: The next year, when British ships entered Tientsin, he memorialized on essentials of war and defense, and successively argued against foreign affairs policy, submitting eight memorials in all.

entries.zh: 遷給事中。
entries.en: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary.

entries.zh: 十年，出為安徽廬鳳道。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed Lu-Feng circuit intendant in Anhui.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he went out as Lu-Feng circuit intendant of Anhui.

entries.zh: 同治二年，遷按察使。
entries.en: In the second year of Tongzhi he was made provincial judge.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he was transferred to provincial judge.

entries.zh: 捻至，與總兵喻吉三隨方應禦，寇不得逞。
entries.en: When the Nian rebels appeared, he and Brigadier Yu Jisan met them wherever they struck, and the rebels could not break through.
entries.literal: When the Nian arrived, together with Brigadier Yu Jisan he responded wherever needed and the bandits could not prevail.

entries.zh: 四年，晉湖北布政使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was promoted to treasurer of Hubei.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Hubei provincial treasurer.

entries.zh: 逾歲，到官，值黃陂飢嗛，民就食江、漢，便宜發帑金濟之。
entries.en: A year later he took up his post. Huangpi was in famine, and people were fleeing to the Yangzi and Han for food. He promptly disbursed treasury funds for relief.
entries.literal: After a year he reached his post; it happened that Huangpi suffered famine, and the people sought food along the Yangzi and Han rivers; he promptly disbursed treasury funds to relieve them.

entries.zh: 九年，擢福建巡撫，歷山西、江蘇。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was made governor of Fujian and later served in Shanxi and Jiangsu.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian, and served successively in Shanxi and Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 遭父憂，服闋，起閩浙總督。
entries.en: After his father's death and the mourning period, he was recalled as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was recalled as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 徐延旭，字曉山，山東臨清人。
entries.en: Xu Yanxu, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshan, came from Linqing in Shandong.
entries.literal: Xu Yanxu, style name Xiaoshan, was a man of Linqing in Shandong.

entries.zh: 咸豐十年進士，出知廣西容縣。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign and was appointed magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he became a jinshi and was sent out as magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 師克潯州，與有功，累晉知府。
entries.en: When government forces took Xunzhou, he distinguished himself in the campaign and rose step by step to the rank of prefect.
entries.literal: When the army captured Xunzhou he had a share in the merit and was repeatedly promoted to prefect.

entries.zh: 同治九年，除知梧州。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Tongzhi he was made prefect of Wuzhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Tongzhi he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 光緒三年，遷安襄荊鄖道。
entries.en: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Yun circuit.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Yun circuit intendancy.

entries.zh: 八年，晉廣西布政使，命督辦海防，得專奏事。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to treasurer of Guangxi, put in charge of coastal defense, and allowed to memorialize the throne directly.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Guangxi provincial treasurer, ordered to supervise coastal defense, and granted the right to submit memorials on his own authority.

entries.zh: 時法人謀佔全越，巡撫張之洞、侍讀張佩綸先後疏薦堪軍事。
entries.en: The French were then seeking to occupy all of Vietnam, and Governor Zhang Zhidong and Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun both memorialized the court in turn, commending him as capable in military matters.
entries.literal: At the time the French were plotting to seize all of Vietnam; Governor Zhang Zhidong and Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun successively memorialized recommending him as fit for military affairs.

entries.zh: 會南定陷，朝命出鎮南關，與提督黃桂蘭、道員趙沃籌防，未行，越官劉永福戰勝懷德府紙橋，狀其績以上。
entries.en: When Nam Dinh fell, the court ordered him to take command at Zhennan Pass and work out defenses with Brigadier Huang Guilan and Circuit Intendant Zhao Wo. Before he marched, the Vietnamese commander Liu Yongfu defeated the enemy at Paper Bridge in Hoa Duc prefecture and sent up a report of his victory.
entries.literal: When Nam Dinh fell, the court ordered him out to guard Zhennan Pass and plan defense with Brigadier Huang Guilan and circuit intendant Zhao Wo; before he set out, the Vietnamese official Liu Yongfu won a battle at Paper Bridge in Hoa Duc prefecture and reported his achievements upward.

entries.zh: 左寶貴弟寶賢等永山鄧世昌劉步蟾林泰曾等戴宗騫
entries.en: Zuo Baogui (and his younger brother Bao Xian and others), Yong Shan, Deng Shichang, Liu Buchan, Lin Taiceng and others, and Dai Zongqian
entries.literal: Zuo Baogui; his younger brother Bao Xian and others; Yong Shan; Deng Shichang; Liu Buchan; Lin Taiceng and others; Dai Zongqian.

entries.zh: 永山，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子，黑龍江將軍壽山弟。
entries.en: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner, stationed in the Heilongjiang garrison; he was the son of Jilin General Fuming'a and the younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.
entries.literal: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, a Hanjun of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Heilongjiang; son of Jilin General Fuming'a and younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.

entries.zh: 以廕授侍衛，歸東三省練軍。
entries.en: By hereditary privilege he was appointed an Imperial Bodyguard and returned to serve with the training army of the Three Eastern Provinces.
entries.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed an Imperial Bodyguard and returned to the Three Eastern Provinces training army.

entries.zh: 中日戰起，從將軍依克唐阿軍，率黑龍江騎旅駐摩天嶺。
entries.en: When war broke out between China and Japan, he served under General Yiketang'a, commanding the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade posted at Motianling.
entries.literal: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out, he followed General Yiketang'a's army, leading the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade stationed at Motianling.

entries.zh: 永山臨敵輒深入，為士卒先。
entries.en: Whenever he met the enemy Yong Shan drove deep into the fight, always ahead of his men.
entries.literal: Whenever Yong Shan faced the enemy he would press deep into the line, going ahead of his soldiers.

entries.zh: 與日軍戰數有功，連殲其將。
entries.en: In repeated clashes with the Japanese he distinguished himself and killed several of their officers in succession.
entries.literal: In several engagements with the Japanese army he won merit and successively killed many of their officers.

entries.zh: 既克龍灣，乘勝渡草河，規鳳凰，依克唐阿策襲其城，檄永山為軍鋒，偕壽山分率馬步隊深入攻之。
entries.en: After taking Longwan they pressed the advantage across the Cao River toward Fengcheng; Yiketang'a planned a surprise on the city and named Yong Shan the vanguard, while he and Shoushan each led mixed cavalry and infantry columns in a deep strike.
entries.literal: After capturing Longwan, they took advantage of the victory to cross the Cao River and aimed at Fengcheng; Yiketang'a planned a surprise assault on the city and ordered Yong Shan as the vanguard, together with Shoushan each leading mixed horse and foot columns in a deep attack.

entries.zh: 抵一面山，距城八里，張左右翼，各據一坡以待。
entries.en: They reached Yimianshan, eight li from the city, and deployed left and right wings, each holding a slope in readiness.
entries.literal: They reached Yimianshan, eight li from the city, deployed left and right wings, each occupying a slope in wait.

entries.zh: 永山為右翼，尤得地勢。
entries.en: Yong Shan held the right wing, which had the better ground.
entries.literal: Yong Shan commanded the right wing and especially held the superior terrain.

entries.zh: 敵作散隊，伍伍什什冒死前，復以大隊橫沖我左翼。
entries.en: The enemy came on in open order, advancing in small groups at the risk of their lives, then threw a large column in a slashing charge against our left wing.
entries.literal: The enemy formed skirmish lines, advancing in fives and tens risking death, then sent a large column to charge straight across our left wing.

entries.zh: 左翼潰，右翼亦不支，乃相繼退。
entries.en: The left wing broke, the right could not hold, and the whole line fell back in turn.
entries.literal: The left wing collapsed and the right wing could not hold either, so they withdrew in succession.

entries.zh: 永山獨為殿，遇伏，連受槍傷，洞胸踣，復強起督戰，大呼殺賊而逝。
entries.en: Yong Shan alone covered the retreat; ambushed, he took shot after shot, was pierced through the chest and fell; he dragged himself up to rally the fight, cried "Kill the bandits!" and died.
entries.literal: Yong Shan alone served as rearguard; ambushed, he received gunshot wounds one after another, was struck through the chest and fell; he forced himself up again to direct the battle, shouted "Kill the bandits!" and died.

entries.zh: 事聞，諡壯愍，予建祠奉天。
entries.en: When the court learned of his death, he was given the posthumous name Zhuangmin (Stalwart and Sorrowful), and a temple was built for him in Fengtian.
entries.literal: When word reached the court, he was given the posthumous name Zhuangmin and a temple was erected for him in Fengtian.

entries.zh: 二十年，朝鮮亂起，日本進兵。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, turmoil broke out in Korea and Japan sent troops.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, disorder arose in Korea and Japan advanced troops.

entries.zh: 朝議既決戰，衛汝貴、馬玉昆、丰紳阿各率所部往御之，寶貴自奉天來會，是為四大軍。
entries.en: Once the court resolved on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'e each led their commands to resist the invader; Baogui came down from Fengtian to join them — the force known as the Four Great Armies.
entries.literal: Once the court had decided on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'e each led their units to resist; Baogui came from Fengtian to join them — these were the Four Great Armies.

entries.zh: 慮海道梗，乃繞道自遼東行，渡鴨綠江入平壤。
entries.en: Fearing the sea lanes would be cut, they marched overland through eastern Liaodong, crossed the Yalu, and entered Pyongyang.
entries.literal: Fearing the sea route would be blocked, they took a detour through eastern Liaodong, crossed the Yalu River, and entered Pyongyang.

entries.zh: 是時葉志超虛飾戰胜狀，電李鴻章入告，遂拜總統諸軍命。
entries.en: At that time Ye Zhichao dressed up false reports of victory and telegraphed Li Hongzhang with the news, and was accordingly appointed commander-in-chief of all forces.
entries.literal: At that time Ye Zhichao falsely reported victories and telegraphed Li Hongzhang; he was then appointed commander-in-chief of all forces.
